result.submission_requirements:
Sources: the Fall 2026 "ACS PRF Grant Application Components" PDF (direct read of the local copy at C:\MyData\Cowork\Funding\research\sources\acs-prf-application-components-fall-2026.pdf) and the UNI knowledge-base article (direct read). Only the deviations matter here; the funder-wide norm is recorded elsewhere.

**FIRST, THE THING PEOPLE GET WRONG: there is no page limit. PRF works in WORD counts.** Narrative max 4,000 words, single PDF containing title, abstract, narrative, references and all figures/tables, double-spaced 12-point with 1-inch margins, word count stated at the end. Title, abstract, references and figure/table captions do not count. References go in the SAME PDF, listing ALL authors and complete article titles — "Truncated author lists or shortened titles are not acceptable" (and "Do not use 'et al.'"). Enforcement is absolute.

**WHERE UNI DEVIATES FROM THE OTHER PRF MECHANISMS:**
- **Complete publication AND presentation lists** — not the five-year lists ND and UR file. "For ND and UR grants, publications during the past five years are required. For DNI and UNI grants, complete publication lists are required." Same split for presentations.
- **Teaching Information section is REQUIRED (UR and UNI only):** typical teaching duties in the academic year; % of time dedicated to research in the academic year; % in summer; number of undergraduates who performed research with the PI in the past 12 months.
- **No Co-PI.** The Co-PI block is "[optional; ND and UR grants only]", and the UNI page says "no co-PI can be involved but one or more collaborators can participate on the project."
- **Postdoctoral Fellow Salary Support is not an allowable budget line** — that line is "[ND and DNI grants only]".
- **A different new-direction test.** For ND/UR the PI must have no publications in the area; for UNI "the project must be distinct from the PI's graduate or postdoctoral research." UNI page: "Excluded from consideration are proposals which are a mere extension of research from the PI's graduate or postdoctoral experience."
- **Student-support floor is 40%, NOT the 60% that binds ND and DNI:** "The PRF Committee requires that at least 40 percent of the total budget be devoted to support the education and training of students." Undergraduates must be supported in EACH year of the grant; M.S.-level students "can be supported with salaries or stipends, only if undergraduates are also supported by this grant." Student field-work expenses count as student support if described in the justification.
- **Budget is fixed at $55,000 over 2 years.** Requesting the wrong total is a listed failure mode on PRF's own error checklist.
- **Excluded charges (UNI):** no overhead, no secretarial/administrative salaries, and "Funds may not be used for Tuition or to support post-doctoral associates, doctoral students, laboratory technicians, contractors, consultants, or visiting faculty."
- **PI summer stipend** ≤$8,000 per grant year including fringe, "to a maximum of $16,000. This limit does NOT change as a result of time extensions."
- **Travel** ≤$2,000 per grant year "or $4,000 total"; field work budgeted separately; student travel to meetings encouraged; "There are no restrictions on foreign travel."
- **Capital equipment is specifically DISCOURAGED for UNI** but ≤$5,000 is allowed "with justification and description of institutional cost-matching (if provided)."
- **Publication costs** ≤$2,000 over the project (open access fees, language editing, covers).
- **EXTRA DOCUMENT IF NOT TENURE-TRACK:** "attach a brief statement to your application describing your appointment and include a Department Chair's letter affirming that you meet all three of the above criteria" (institutional PI certification; eligibility to serve as formal official supervisor of undergraduates; appointment continuing at least through the funding period). This is a slow-to-obtain item and is additional to the signature sheet.

**Shared with all PRF mechanisms, worth restating because they are word-capped portal fields, not parts of the PDF:** abstract 250 words (and it must also open the uploaded PDF); Petroleum Relevance Statement 100; New Research Direction Statement 500; Scientific Education Impact and Mentoring Statement 500; Available Facilities and Instrumentation 500; Safety Statement; optional Collaborations (collaborator letters upload under "All Other Documents"); optional keywords (≤5) and UN SDG alignment; Similarity Check Acknowledgement; Description of AI Tools Used if disclosed. Reviewers: minimum 6 with name, institution, email, optional 150-character justification, plus reviewers to exclude; conflicts barred include collaborators or co-authors within 48 months, former advisors or advisees, institutional colleagues, family and financial relationships.

**DRIFT WARNING — the funder's own pages contradict each other.** The proposal-submission help page on acs.org still says the new-direction and mentoring statements must be "no longer than 1 page." The Fall 2026 components PDF replaces both with 500-word portal fields. Use the PDF — it is the current cycle's document. Likewise the ND Application Instructions PDF is Rev 02/2024 and predates the AI-disclosure and UN-SDG fields. And take dollar figures from acs.org, never an aggregator: Duke's listing carries the right deadlines but states ND at "$110,000 over 2 years" where the funder says $125,000.

3. Does my budget clear the 40% student-support floor, and is my capital-equipment request defensible given that UNI "discourages" it?
4. Am I eligible — non-tenure-track appointment, five-year clock, department genuinely without a doctoral programme?
5. Which PRF Panel should I select? You choose it yourself, and it determines who judges you.

Note: UNI (like DNI) is US-only, so the eligible-countries question that matters for ND and UR does not arise here.
result.examples_or_samples:
**There is no NIH-RePORTER equivalent, and PRF publishes no sample applications and no reviewer summary statements.** What exists instead is the grantees' own narrative progress reports.

**1. ACS PRF Annual Report on Research — https://acswebcontent.acs.org/prfar/<year>/** (2016 = the 61st report; confirmed reachable). Structure: "Grants Awarded" at media/grants.html (round summary, per-mechanism counts and amounts, plus a downloadable PDF list of grants awarded that year); reports browsable By Title (REPORT.html), By Institution (affiliationa.html), By Principal Investigator (authora.html), and a Table of Contents (media/TOC.html) organised by grant type and panel — **UNI1 through UNI10**, alongside DNI1–10, ND1–10, UR1–10 and SE. Individual pages carry grant number, grant type, PI, institution, title and the full narrative. Verified example: https://acswebcontent.acs.org/prfar/2016/Paper13837.html — grant 54824-DNI1, Jennifer L. Roizen (Duke), "Site- and Enantioselective Electrophilic Halogen-Transfer Processes." Also "Researcher Stories" (media/stories.html) and "Featured Reports" (media/features.html). Full-report PDF e.g. media/ACS_PRF_61st.pdf.

**How a UNI applicant should use it:** find three funded grants whose numbers end in -UNI1 … -UNI10 **in your own panel**, at primarily-undergraduate institutions resembling yours, and read them for calibration on what PRF's scope filter actually lets through and what "distinct from graduate or postdoctoral research" looks like in practice at a PUI with undergraduate labour. The grant number itself encodes mechanism and panel, so the numbering tells you which panel judged the work.

**CAVEAT, flagged honestly:** these are progress reports on FUNDED work, not the applications that won. And availability is patchy — only the 2016 year responded to me; 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2023 returned 403, and acs.org's own annual-report.html index returns a genuine ACS 403. I could not establish whether recent years are still published or where their index lives. See unresolved.

**2. The funder's own craft materials — better value than hunting for sample applications, and the closest thing PRF offers to a worked example:**
- "What Makes a Proposal a New Direction?" — vimeo.com/132978944 (pair with the FAQ's acceptable/not-acceptable worked examples; this is the filter that kills UNI proposals pre-review)
- "What makes a competitive proposal?" — vimeo.com/41306667
- "The PRF Program Manager as a Resource" — vimeo.com/172902103
- "What makes a good ACS PRF grant proposal reviewer?" — vimeo.com/64588132
- The 14-item **"Checklist of Common Errors"** reproduced in full in the ND Application Instructions PDF — effectively PRF telling you its rejection reasons in rank order, and it applies across mechanisms.
- An "Eligibility Self-check" tool and a "PRF quiz" on the PRF homepage.

**3. C&EN round announcements** — e.g. "ACS Board approves 113 new PRF projects" (June 2026) and "Petroleum Research Fund grant submissions open for 2026" (Jan 2026); spring 2026 round totalled $12,295,000. VIA SEARCH INDEX ONLY — cen.acs.org returned HTTP 406 to both a plain fetch and a rendering browser, so I could not read the articles themselves.

**4. JACS 65th-anniversary open-access virtual issue** — retrospective of JACS papers by chemists who held PRF funding, linked from the PRF homepage. Shows what PRF seed money grew into; not useful for application craft.

**5. Your own research office — the most realistic route to reading a real UNI application.** Every PRF proposal requires an institutional endorsing official's signature, so your campus's sponsored-programmes office holds copies of prior PRF submissions, quite possibly UNI ones from colleagues at your own institution type.
result.resubmission_note:
**Allowed, but hard-capped — and at UNI the cap is unusually punishing because it coincides with the career limit.**

**The cap, verbatim** (ACS PRF Grant Application Components, Fall 2026, direct read): "Resubmission Justification / Statement of Modifications – If the research topic was previously denied by the PRF Committee, a statement describing what has been changed in the revised version is required. [Note: Applicants are limited to an initial application and a maximum of two resubmissions on the same topic.]" So 1 original + 2 resubmissions = 3 attempts on a topic.

**THE UNI-SPECIFIC TRAP (my inference, flagged):** UNI's career limit is also three — "only three (3) UNI grant applications considered and/or one (1) UNI grant funded in their career" — and a denied application still counts as considered. Spending all three attempts on a single topic therefore exhausts your entire UNI career allowance, not merely that topic's. Budget your attempts across topics accordingly.

**No NIH-style Introduction page — and putting one in is an error.** The statement of changes is a WEB-FORM FIELD in the portal, and the funder is explicit it must stay out of the document: "If this is a resubmission of a previously denied proposal, you will need to answer the question, 'What has been changed in this revised version?' in the online submission form. This information is just for the use of the Program Manager and the PRF Science Panel members, so it is not to be included in the proposal document." Putting it in the PDF would also eat your 4,000 words.

**Fresh reviewers — the trap that catches people.** "'Revised and resubmitted' proposals are sent to a different set of reviewers than those asked to evaluate the initial proposal," and correspondingly: "Resubmissions: If the proposal is a resubmission, reviewers listed on a prior submission may not be included." You need a second slate of six clean, conflict-free names ready — and note the separate standing rule that "a PI may not suggest a reviewer whom the PI has suggested to PRF in the last 4 years."

**Timing — no forced skip, apparently, unlike ND and UR.** ND imposes one ("may not submit another ND proposal until the PRF Committee meeting one year later") and UR carries the same rule. The UNI Limitations block I read directly is complete and contains no such rule, so a denied UNI applicant appears able to return at the very next meeting, subject to the standing "one research proposal per meeting" limit. INFERENCE FROM ABSENCE — confirm with a Program Manager before planning around it. Deadlines are identical for new and resubmitted proposals either way.

**What must actually change.** PRF's own checklist names failure to revise as a top rejection reason: "No outline of revisions. For a previously denied proposal, which has been revised and resubmitted, the PI did not address reviewers' concerns/comments and did not include, with the application, a summary of major changes." Note the tension with the instruction above: address reviewer comments substantively in the science, but put the summary of changes in the portal field, not the PDF.
result.deadline_pattern:
Two fixed windows per year, identical across all four PRF mechanisms (ND, DNI, UR, UNI), with the same date for new and resubmitted proposals. Not rolling and not per-solicitation.

- FALL: window opens ≈ mid-September, closes ≈ early/mid-October at 5:00 pm ET → reviewed at the May PRF Committee meeting of the FOLLOWING year → earliest award start 1 July.
- SPRING: window opens ≈ mid-February, closes ≈ mid-March → reviewed at the October PRF Committee meeting of the SAME year → earliest award start 1 January of the following year.

Funder's words (ND Application Instructions, Rev 02/2024): "Proposals submitted in February-March will be considered at the October PRF Committee meeting; submissions in September-October will be considered in May of the next year." And on starts (FAQ): "For proposals to be considered in October, the earliest start date is January 1 of the following year. For proposals to be considered in May, the earliest start date is July 1. If you are unsure when a proposal will be considered, this is noted in the footer of the application form."

Current instance: fall window 14 Sept – 9 Oct 2026 (5:00 pm ET); spring window 15 Feb – 12 Mar 2027.

Add ~1–2 weeks ahead of any window for pre-registration approval plus institutional signatures — neither is inside your control.

result.next_deadline:
NOT FOUND for the next cycle — and the reason matters, so record it rather than a pattern.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED (funder's own FY26 NOFO, Table 2 and Table 8): the FY2026 A7201 deadline was "Thursday, April 30, 2026 (5:00 p.m. Eastern Time)". That date has PASSED (today 2026-09-18). Predoctoral (A7101) was two weeks earlier, "Thursday, April 16, 2026".

NO FY2027 NOFO IS POSTED as of 2026-09-18. A Grants.gov API search (agency USDA-NIFA, statuses posted+forecasted) returns exactly one AFRI EWD record: USDA-NIFA-AFRI-011596, posted 2026-01-20, close 2026-12-31 — the FY26 NOFO. Its 2026-12-31 close date is the NOFO-wide envelope, NOT the A7201 date: the NOFO says "Applicants must respond to the Program Area Priorities and deadlines found in Part I, C." Reading 12/31/2026 off the Grants.gov card as the postdoc deadline is the single easiest error to make here, and it is wrong by eight months.

WHY NO PATTERN IS SAFE TO PROJECT — the A7201 date genuinely moves. Read from each year's own NOFO:
- FY2023: "6. Postdoctoral Fellowships (A7201) September 7, 2023"
- FY2024: "6. Postdoctoral Fellowships (A7201) Thursday, September 5, 2024"
- FY2025: no AFRI EWD NOFO found on Grants.gov at all (gap between the FY24 NOFO closing 2024-12-05 and the FY26 NOFO posting 2026-01-20)
- FY2026: "Thursday, April 30, 2026"
The deadline moved roughly four months earlier in the calendar and the predoc/postdoc order flipped (FY24: postdoc Sept 5 BEFORE predoc Oct 24; FY26: predoc Apr 16 BEFORE postdoc Apr 30).

ON THE DATED-DEADLINE QUESTION: the dated deadline is NOT unfindable and should not be suppressed — it is printed in the NOFO in two places and is the only operative date. What is unsafe is recording it bare, as though it recurs. The correct form for this mechanism is a date carrying its fiscal-year scope ("FY2026: Thursday, April 30, 2026, 5:00 p.m. ET — passed"), plus the instruction to re-read Table 2 of each new NOFO. This mechanism is the counter-example to the corpus's "citations rot, programmes don't" finding: the programme persists, and the DATE is what rots.

ACTIONABLE WATCH ROUTE: NIFA posted the FY26 NOFO on 2026-01-20 and the FY24 NOFO on 2024-03-15, so the NOFO drops in the Jan–Mar window. Watch https://www.nifa.usda.gov/grants/funding-opportunities/agriculture-food-research-initiative-education-workforce-development and Grants.gov for a successor to USDA-NIFA-AFRI-011596; when it appears, go straight to Table 2 "Program Area Priorities and Deadlines" for the A7201 row.
result.deadline_pattern:
Nominally annual, one cycle per fiscal year, one dated deadline per program area published inside that year's NOFO — but NOT a stable recurring calendar, and with at least one skipped year (no FY2025 EWD NOFO found on Grants.gov). Observed A7201 dates: Sept 7 2023 (FY23), Sept 5 2024 (FY24), [none found] (FY25), Apr 30 2026 (FY26).

Hard time-of-day rule, and it deviates from NIH: NOFO footnote 1 — "All applications must be received by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the deadline date." That is EASTERN time, not the applicant organization's local time as under the NIH norm. A West Coast applicant loses three hours relative to what they may expect.

No weekend/federal-holiday rollover provision and no NIH-style late-submission window were found anywhere in the FY26 NOFO — treat the deadline as hard. (Recorded as not found, not as an assertion that none exists.)

Note the separate A7001 Workshop Grant track in the same NOFO is "Continuous throughout the year" — it is the only rolling item in this NOFO and is a different mechanism; do not read its cadence onto A7201.
result.loi_deadline:
Not applicable — no LOI or pre-proposal stage for A7201. The funder is explicit and exclusive about this. FY26 NOFO Table 1 (Key Dates and Deadlines): "Letter of Intent: Only required for A7001, 5:00 P.M. Eastern Time, on the LOI deadline dates indicated in Part I § C.7". A7001 is Education and Workforce Development Workshop Grants, a different program area in the same NOFO.

This is worth stating positively because the adjacent LOI requirement is easy to mis-apply: the Workshop LOI is due "a minimum of 255 days before the workshop begins," with the full application "a minimum of 210 days before the start of the workshop." Those numbers belong to A7001 only. For A7201 you go straight to a full application on the single dated deadline; there is no invitation gate and no pre-proposal.
result.review_to_award:
Much faster and more sharply bounded than the NIH norm — roughly 5 months from deadline to award, versus NIH's ~9.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT (FY26 NOFO, Part VI.A Award Administration): "The date specified by the NIFA awarding official as the effective date of the grant must be no later than September 30 of the Federal fiscal year in which the project is approved for support and funds are appropriated for such purpose, unless otherwise permitted by law." For the FY26 cycle that puts deadline 2026-04-30 → award effective on or before 2026-09-30, i.e. a ceiling of about five months. The FY23/FY24 early-September deadlines compressed this much further, which is likely part of why the date moved earlier.

Start date is flexible after award: "The project need not be initiated on the grant effective date, but as soon thereafter as practical so that project goals may be attained within the funded project period."

REVIEW ARC — two stages, not NIH's three (there is no advisory-council second level):
1. Administrative screen. "First, we screen each application to ensure that it meets the administrative requirements set forth in this NOFO. All administrative requirements must be met in order for the application to proceed to the next level of review."
2. Scientific peer review panel. "Second, a scientific peer-review process will be used to technically evaluate applications that have met the administrative requirements using a review panel." Panels are deliberately mixed beyond academics — NIFA selects for "the need to include other experts (e.g., agricultural producers, range or forest managers/operators, researchers, educators, evaluators, and consumers) who can assess relevance of the applications to audiences and to program needs," and for balance across geography and entity type. Write for a panel that includes practitioners, not only specialists.
3. Program staff recommend "either approved for support from currently available funds or declined due to insufficient funds or unfavorable review." NIFA "reserves the right to negotiate with the PD/PI and/or the submitting organization or institution regarding project revisions (e.g., reductions in the scope of work, funding level, period, or method of support) prior to recommending any project for funding."
4. Feedback: "After the review process has been completed, NIFA sends copies of reviews, not including the identity of reviewers, and a summary (if applicable) of the review panel comments to the PD." Reviews go to the PD — here, the postdoc themselves, since the postdoc is sole PD.

WHICH PANEL REVIEWS YOU — the analogue of picking an NIH study section, and it is not obvious: "Postdoctoral proposals will be reviewed within a respective AFRI FAS Program Area." You signal the panel in the Project Summary/Abstract, where the applicant "should indicate the Farm Bill Priority Area name (Part I, A), Program Area name, and Program Area Priority Code from the AFRI FAS NOFO that most closely matches the topic of the proposed postdoctoral project plan." So you must read a second document — the AFRI Foundational and Applied Science NOFO — to choose your review home, even though you apply under EWD.

A POST-SUBMISSION TRAP WITH TEETH, absent from the NIH norm because eRA Commons tracks automatically and NIFA does not: "If the AR has not received correspondence from NIFA regarding a submitted application within 30 days of the established deadline, contact the Program Contact identified in Part I, C and request the proposal number assigned to the application. Failure to do so may result in the application not being considered for funding by the peer review panel." Diarise deadline + 30 days and confirm your institution's Authorized Representative actually received a proposal number.
result.submission_requirements:
PORTAL — simpler than NIH. Grants.gov Workspace only. eRA Commons does NOT apply to this mechanism: the phrase "eRA Commons" appears zero times in the FY26 EWD NOFO, and the NIFA Grants Application Guide (April 2026) makes it conditional — "Some NIFA funding opportunities are managed through the eRA Commons grants management system... The NOFO or RFP will outline whether registration in eRA Commons is required." Registration chain is SAM.gov (UEI/EIN) → Grants.gov. NIFA's own lead-time warning: "Some steps, like registering your organization on SAM.gov, can take 4-6 weeks to complete." As with NIH, the institution submits, not the postdoc.

PAGE LIMIT — the headline deviation. Project Narrative for a Postdoctoral Fellowship is 10 pages (predoctoral is 6). Source: NIFA, "Part II, C(2) AFRI Grant Types," updated November 2025 — "Project Narrative page limit for Predoctoral Fellowship Grant applications is 6 pages and for Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant applications is 10 pages." The NOFO's Table 8 routes you there ("See Part II C.2 for requirements specific to FASE Grant applications") and adds that page limits and narrative font sizes live "on the AFRI NOFO Resources webpage. Proposals that do not comply with these instructions may be excluded from review and consideration of funding."

THE THREE DOCUMENTS THAT KILL AN APPLICATION IF MISSING (NOFO, Part IV): "Failure to include any of the three critical required documents of Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, or Bibliography & References Cited sections as PDF attachment will result in the application not being reviewed or considered for funding by NIFA."

FULL REQUIRED-ITEMS LIST (NOFO, "not an exhaustive list... it only serves to highlight items that may be overlooked"): 1 Project Summary/Abstract; 2 Project Narrative; 3 Bibliography & References Cited; 4 Logic Model (integrated projects only); 5 Management Plan (integrated only); 6 Data Management Plan; 7 Mentoring Plan (if not in the narrative); 8 Facilities & Other Resources; 9 Curriculum Vitae; 10 Conflict of Interest Lists; 11 Current and Pending Support; 12 Budget; 13 Budget Justification. Plus the SF-424 (R&R) and the NIFA Supplemental Information Form.

MENTORING PLAN — fellowships are carved out of the general rule. AFRI Part IV C: "The guidelines below apply to all grant types except Predoctoral Fellowships and Postdoctoral Fellowships, which have their own unique mentoring requirements." The fellowship-specific mentoring requirements sit on the AFRI NOFO Resources webpage, which I could not retrieve this session (see unresolved).

WHO IS THE APPLICANT — a hard formatting rule people get wrong: "The postdoctoral scholar must be the sole PD listed on the Key Personnel form of the application. The mentor should not be listed as a Co-PD. Select 'Post-Doctoral' for the Postdoctoral Fellowship applicant. Select 'Other (Specify)' for the corresponding scientific mentor(s). Enter 'Mentor' for corresponding scientific mentor(s) in the Other Project Role Category Field."

PROGRAM CODE — a return-without-review risk: "postdoctoral proposals must indicate program code A7201 in the NIFA Supplemental Information Form (application package)... Do not use a FAS program code in the NIFA Supplemental Information Form, or the application is at risk of being returned without review." The FAS code goes in the Project Summary/Abstract as your review-panel signal; A7201 goes in the Supplemental Information Form. Two codes, two different places, and swapping them is fatal.

ELIGIBILITY DOCUMENTATION — due WITH the application, not later: "Documentation from the graduate advisor, graduate committee, or the institution must be provided by the application deadline." This is the postdoc analogue of an NIH sponsor letter and there is no grace period.

WHAT THE NARRATIVE MUST DO — the review-defining sentence: "Although a proposed project may fit in the context of the mentor's existing scientific area, the Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant should initiate an independent scientific program, rather than serve as an extension of ongoing projects in the mentor's laboratory." A project that reads as the mentor's next aim is the characteristic failure mode.

REQUIRED CONTENT: the project "must include all of the following: a. Objectives that are aligned with one or more of the six AFRI Farm Bill Priority Areas (Part I, A); b. Well-developed academic experiences and global competencies; c. Productive and interactive mentoring; d. Appropriate and applicable training/career development activities; and e. Substantive evaluation plans." Items b–e are graded content, not boilerplate.

BUDGET — note this corrects the existing row's "~$165,000". FY26 Table 8: "Maximum Award Amount(s): a. Including institutional allowance: $244,000"; grant duration "Up to 24 months"; "Funds must be requested primarily for salary or stipend and be properly justified"; "Other expenditures (e.g., fringe benefits, supplies, travel, workshops, publications, etc.) may not exceed $60,000 per year and must be itemized and properly justified"; "Up to $3,000 per year institutional allowance, in lieu of indirect costs which are not permitted on Postdoctoral Fellowship Grants." And a bright line: "Requests exceeding budgetary guidelines will not be reviewed."

EFFORT: "At the time of the award and release of funds from NIFA to sponsoring institution, Fellows are required to carry out their projects on a full-time basis (i.e., 100% effort)."

BUDGET LINE PEOPLE FORGET: "If organized by the program, the PD will be required to attend one NIFA AFRI EWD PD meeting during the performance period of the award. Reasonable travel expenses must be included as part of the project budget."

NOT RENEWABLE: "Unless otherwise stated, grants are not renewable."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves, and the good news is much larger than the bad news.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU — remarkably little. The governing regulation, 7 CFR 3430.303(c)(2), imposes exactly two conditions on pre- and postdoctoral fellowship applicants, and NEITHER is a prior-award bar:
"(i) The doctoral degree of the applicant must be received not earlier than January 1 of the calendar year three years prior to the submission of the proposal and not later than nine months after the proposal due date; and (ii) For pre-doctoral applications, the applicant must have advanced to candidacy by the application deadline."
There is no clause excluding applicants who hold or have held other federal awards. I searched the FY26 NOFO for prior-fellowship, repeat-application and concurrent-award restrictions and found none. So: holding an NSF GRFP, an institutional postdoc, or having been supported on someone else's federal grant does not gate you here.

THE ONE REAL EXCLUSION is about duplicate applications, not prior funding: "submission of duplicate or predominantly overlapping applications is not allowed. NIFA will disqualify both applications if an applicant submits multiple applications that are duplicative or substantially overlapping to NIFA programs within the same fiscal year." Note the penalty falls on BOTH applications, and the scope is all NIFA programs in the same fiscal year — not just AFRI.

THE DEGREE WINDOW IS THE ACTUAL GATE, and it is two-sided and generative. Applying the regulation to FY26 (deadline 2026-04-30) yields exactly what the NOFO prints: "all doctoral degree requirements must be satisfied by: a. Fiscal Year 2026 competition: no earlier than January 1, 2023, and no later than January 30, 2027." Backward edge = Jan 1 of the calendar year three years before submission; forward edge = nine months after the due date. Because the rule is in the CFR rather than the NOFO, you can compute any future cycle's window yourself once the date is announced — which is the durable thing to carry, given how much the date moves.

THE FORWARD HALF IS THE MOST UNDER-USED FACT HERE: the degree may be received up to NINE MONTHS AFTER the due date. A final-year PhD student who has not yet defended is eligible to apply for this POSTDOCTORAL fellowship. Most applicants assume a postdoc fellowship requires the PhD in hand and self-select out a year too early.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half that is usually omitted, and it is at regulation level, not merely guidance. 7 CFR 3430.303(c)(1), on AFRI New Investigator awards: "To be eligible to receive a grant, the new investigator may not have received competitively awarded Federal funds, with the exception of pre- or postdoctoral awards or NRI/AFRI Seed Grants." NIFA's "AFRI Grant Types" (Nov 2025) says the same operationally: "The new investigator may not have received competitively awarded Federal research funds as Project Director (PD) with the exception of pre- or postdoctoral grants, equipment grants, and AFRI Seed Grants. Federal funding received by the applicant as Co-PD of previously awarded competitive grants does not count against New Investigator eligibility."
Plain meaning for a postdoc: taking this fellowship does NOT burn your AFRI New Investigator eligibility later. It is a designed stepping stone, not a one-way door. This is the structural opposite of the NIH K→R01 interaction, where prior independent funding is the thing that disqualifies. Serving as Co-PD on someone else's federal grant is likewise preserved.

ALSO PRESERVED — institutional reach. Although A7201 sits inside the FASE grant family, "the applicant fellow need not be from or planning to carry out the fellowship project at a Strengthening Grant eligible institution to be eligible for a Postdoctoral Fellowship grant." You are not confined to EPSCoR states, small institutions or MSIs, even though sibling FASE categories are.

CITIZENSHIP (an eligibility gate rather than a funding conflict): "The postdoctoral PD must be a citizen, national, or permanent resident of the United States."

A FORWARD-LOOKING LEVER — fellowship-to-Standard-Grant conversion. The NOFO's postdoc section states "Note that the Program Area Priority Additional Information identified for Predoctoral Fellowships also applies to Postdoctoral Fellowships," and that predoctoral block contains: "Consistent with the program goal of fostering career independence, NIFA Predoctoral Fellowships can be converted to Standard Grants under certain circumstances (e.g., if the Fellow obtains a faculty position). One condition is that the Fellow substantively completes at least 50% of the fellowship performance period (e.g., 12 months for a 24-month award)." Conversion needs a PD letter countersigned by the Authorized Representative, a mentor letter, and National Program Leader agreement; NIFA "reserves the right to approve or deny." CAVEAT: the conversion paragraph names Predoctoral Fellowships by name, and the incorporation clause is blanket — so whether it reaches A7201 by that clause or is predoc-only is genuinely ambiguous on the page. Confirm with nifafellows@usda.gov before relying on it. One thing is stated flatly either way: "Predoctoral Fellowships cannot be converted into Postdoctoral Fellowships."
result.program_officer_contact:
NAMED ROUTE, MECHANISM-SPECIFIC: nifafellows@usda.gov — a dedicated mailbox serving both fellowship program areas. FY26 NOFO Table 8 lists it as the "Program Area Priority Contact(s)" for A7201, and Appendix I (Agency Contact) repeats it: "Predoctoral Fellowships (A7101) nifafellows@usda.gov / Postdoctoral Fellowships (A7201) nifafellows@usda.gov". Note it is a shared functional mailbox, not a named officer — so the NIH habit of emailing a specific PO by name does not transfer; write to the mailbox.

OTHER ROUTES, AND USING THE RIGHT ONE MATTERS:
- grantapplicationquestions@usda.gov — "Other NOFO or application questions" (NIFA Support, Mon–Fri 7am–5pm ET, tel. 202-445-5402)
- awards@usda.gov — "Awards under this NOFO"
- support@grants.gov — Grants.gov technical failures only
- Named EWD staff appear on the NIFA programme overview page (Kellyann Jones-Jamtgaard, Christopher Green, Jeff Sallee, Michelle Schelske-Santos, Ray A. Ali) but that page publishes no direct emails, so the mailbox is the practical entry point.

IS PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT EXPECTED? Yes, and NIFA says so in its own Application Guide's "Top Tips for Grant Applicants": "Questions about applicant eligibility or the specific funding program that you are interested in should be directed to the NIFA program staff listed in the NOFO or RFP." It is, however, a weaker and less ritualised norm than NIH's — NIFA publishes no Matchmaker equivalent, no specific-aims-page convention, and no guidance on what to ask. Expect a narrower service: eligibility and fit, not project shaping.

THE BETTER-VALUE CHANNEL IS THE WEBINAR, which has no NIH equivalent: "For a program informational webinar please visit the NIFA calendar for dates, event registration, and link. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in any of the informational webinars listed, please contact the event host listed no later than 10 days prior to the event." NIFA runs these per program area after a NOFO drops. For a first-time applicant this is the highest-yield hour available, and it is where the current cycle's date and any changed requirements get stated aloud.

HIGHEST-VALUE QUESTIONS FOR THIS MECHANISM SPECIFICALLY (each maps to a real ambiguity documented above): which AFRI FAS Program Area code should I name in the Project Summary/Abstract, i.e. which panel will review me; does my degree date fall inside this cycle's two-sided window; what exactly satisfies the advisor/institution eligibility documentation; where are the fellowship-specific mentoring requirements; and does the Standard Grant conversion provision apply to postdoctoral fellowships or only predoctoral.

WHO YOU DO NOT CONTACT: there is no Scientific Review Officer analogue and no reviewer contact route. Reviewer identities are withheld — reviews come back "not including the identity of reviewers."

MANDATORY CONTACT, NOT OPTIONAL: if your Authorized Representative has heard nothing from NIFA within 30 days of the deadline, you must email the program contact for your proposal number or risk the application not reaching the panel (quoted in full under review_to_award).

ALLOWED, with no cap found — a materially more permissive regime than NIH's single-A1 rule, and the existing row's "unspecified" can be replaced.

FY26 NOFO, Part III § B "Application Restrictions," which limits this NOFO to two application types: "2. Resubmitted application: Resubmitted applications must include the one-page 'Response to Previous Review' and are subject to the same criteria and due dates herein. Resubmitted applicants must enter the NIFA-assigned proposal number of the previously submitted application in the Federal Field (Field 4) on the application form."

Three consequences worth drawing out:
- NO A1 LIMIT AND NO TIME WINDOW. I found no equivalent of NIH's "only a single resubmission" or its 37-month clock anywhere in the NOFO. Recorded as not found rather than as an affirmative grant of unlimited attempts — but nothing restricts repeat attempts, and the practical brake is the degree-date window closing, not a resubmission cap.
- SAME DEADLINE, SAME CRITERIA. There is no separate later resubmission date as at NIH (where R/K renewals move one month out). A resubmission competes on the one annual A7201 date.
- THE PROPOSAL NUMBER IS MANDATORY, in SF-424 R&R Field 4. This is why the 30-day post-submission rule above matters twice over: if you never chased down your proposal number, you cannot correctly file a resubmission next cycle.

THE "RESPONSE TO PREVIOUS REVIEW" — mechanics, from AFRI Part IV C: it goes inside the Project Narrative attachment as its FIRST page, "containing the previous proposal number in the first line," titled "Response to Previous Review," followed by the Project Narrative itself. Critically: "The one-page 'Response to Previous Review' does not count against the ... page limit of the Project Narrative." So a resubmitted A7201 application is 1 + 10 pages, not 10 inclusive. (The Part IV C copy available to me is the Foundational and Applied Science edition, which cites "7- or 18-page" narratives; the structural rule is what transfers, while the page figure for A7201 is the 10 pages from AFRI Grant Types. Flagged in unresolved.)

ONE HARD INTERACTION: do not hedge by submitting a resubmission alongside a near-identical new application. "NIFA will disqualify both applications if an applicant submits multiple applications that are duplicative or substantially overlapping to NIFA programs within the same fiscal year."

Renewals are effectively moot here: "Unless otherwise stated, grants are not renewable."

result.review_to_award:
Much shorter and much less instrumented than NIH; there is no council round, no published review calendar, and no score/summary-statement release schedule.

HARD OUTER BOUND (the one firm date rule, NOFO Part VI, A): "The date specified by the NIFA awarding official as the effective date of the grant must be no later than September 30 of the Federal fiscal year in which the project is approved for support and funds are appropriated for such purpose, unless otherwise permitted by law." For FY2026 that is 16 April 2026 deadline -> award effective no later than 30 September 2026: a maximum of about 5.5 months from submission to award start, versus NIH's ~9 months.

REVIEW PATH (Part V, A): two parts — (1) an administrative screen ("All administrative requirements must be met in order for the application to proceed to the next level of review"), then (2) "a scientific peer-review process ... using a review panel". Panels are assembled to mix scientific/extension/education expertise with producers and non-academic experts. After deliberation NIFA staff recommend approval or decline. Feedback: "After the review process has been completed, NIFA sends copies of reviews, not including the identity of reviewers, and a summary (if applicable) of the review panel comments to the PD." Note "if applicable" — a panel summary is not guaranteed, unlike NIH's mandatory summary statement.

THE 30-DAY TRAP (Part IV, C — genuinely catches people, no NIH equivalent): "If the AR has not received correspondence from NIFA regarding a submitted application within 30 days of the established deadline, contact the Program Contact identified in Part I, C and request the proposal number assigned to the application. Failure to do so may result in the application not being considered for funding by the peer review panel." The burden is on the applicant's institution to chase NIFA within 30 days, or the application can drop out of review. Diary this for ~16 May in a 16 April cycle.

TRACKING: no eRA Commons equivalent. NIFA runs an Application Status Dashboard that anyone can query with the Grants.gov tracking number (entered as GRANT99999999 or 999999999); questions to electronic@usda.gov. Once assigned, the NIFA proposal number must be cited on all correspondence.

NOT FOUND: NIFA publishes no target/median time-to-award, no panel meeting dates, and no notification date for A7101. Only the 30 September statutory outer bound is stated.
result.submission_requirements:
PORTAL — no NIH-style triple route: Grants.gov ONLY. "Applicants must apply to this NOFO electronically; no other method or response is accepted." There is no eRA Commons/ASSIST analogue. Find the package by opportunity number USDA-NIFA-AFRI-011596. The NIFA Grants Application Guide bundled in the package governs form-filling, but "The NOFO overrides the NIFA Grants Application Guide if there is a discrepancy." Institution's Authorized Representative (AR) submits, not the student — "Contact an AR prior to starting an application to assess the organization's readiness to submit an electronic application." So the real internal deadline is the research office's, as with NIH.

WHO IS THE APPLICANT (a structural quirk worth getting right): "The predoctoral candidate must be the sole PD listed on the Key Personnel form of the application. The mentor should not be listed as a Co-PD. Select 'Graduate Student' for the Predoctoral Fellowship applicant and 'Other (Specify)' for the corresponding scientific mentor(s). We highly recommend that applications be submitted through the mentor's institution with the mentor institution listed as the applicant."

PAGE LIMIT — THE KEY DEVIATION: Project Narrative is SIX pages, the shortest in the whole EWD NOFO. Verbatim (FY 2026 AFRI EWD NOFO Additional Information for Part IV, C): "For Predoctoral Grant applications, the Project Narrative section may not exceed a total of six-pages using 12-point font with single line spacing (i.e., no more than six lines per vertical inch), including all figures and tables. Margins must be 1-inch on all sides. Do not use a condensed or narrow font (e.g., Arial Narrow)." Postdoctoral A7201 gets ten. Independently confirmed in FY 2026 AFRI Grant Types: "The Education and Workforce Development project narrative page limit is 10 pages for all programs, except for the Predoctoral Fellowship program which has a 6-page limit." Enforcement is automatic: "applications exceeding the applicable page limitation or violating the limitations on margins or font size will be returned without review."

WHAT MUST FIT IN THOSE SIX PAGES — four plans, not one: "The project narrative attachment includes: Response to Previous Review (for resubmitted applications ONLY); Training/Career Development Plan; Mentoring Plan; Project Plan; and Evaluation Plan." NOTE THE DEVIATION: for every other AFRI grant type the Mentoring Plan is a separate 2-page attachment; for pre/postdoc fellowships it is folded INSIDE the narrative — "The guidelines below apply to all grant types except Predoctoral Fellowships and Postdoctoral Fellowships, which have their own unique mentoring requirements within the Field 8. Project Narrative attachment." Required content: career goals personal statement, fellowship activities, transition-to-independence plan; mentor role and specific mentoring activities; a project plan scoped "within the 3-year timeframe of the fellowship"; and an evaluation plan with milestones, measurable indicators and a dissemination plan.

PROJECT SUMMARY: "maximum of one page and approximately 250 words", and it must state PD and Primary Mentor names/institutions, that it is a Predoctoral (A7101) application, the project type, the primary AFRI Farm Bill Priority Area, and relevance to the fellowship programme goals.

LETTERS — heavier than NIH F31 in one respect: THREE reference letters, and they may not come from your mentors. "Three reference letters are required. Letters should not come from identified mentor(s) but must be obtained from other individuals who know the applicant well to substantially speak towards the applicant's academic and research accomplishments and ability to complete the doctoral degree program... Reference letters should be no longer than one-page." Separately: a Primary Mentor Letter of Commitment, submitted "as an attachment to Field 12, Other Attachments, of the Other Project Information form", explicitly stating responsibilities; and collaborating-mentor letters "limited to one page".

ELIGIBILITY DOCUMENTATION (slow item — start early): "For predoctoral applications, documentation from the graduate advisor, graduate committee or the institution indicating that the applicant has advanced to candidacy, as per institutional requirements, by the date specified in the EWD NOFO." Must be in hand BY the deadline.

THE THREE THAT KILL AN APPLICATION OUTRIGHT: "Failure to include any of the three critical required documents of Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, or Bibliography & References Cited sections as PDF attachment will result in the application not being reviewed or considered for funding by NIFA." Full checklist is 13 items: Project Summary/Abstract; Project Narrative; Bibliography & References Cited; Logic Model and Management Plan (integrated projects only); Data Management Plan; Mentoring Plan (if not in the narrative); Facilities & Other Resources; Curriculum Vitae; Conflict of Interest Lists; Current and Pending Support; Budget; Budget Justification.

BUDGET DEVIATIONS: $180,000 total over up to 36 months, capped at $60,000/yr — up to $35,000 salary/stipend, up to $22,000 other costs, up to $3,000 institutional allowance. "indirect costs ... are not permitted on Predoctoral Fellowship Grants" (the $3,000 allowance is in lieu). Only the stipend cannot be carried over year to year. "Requests exceeding budgetary guidelines will not be reviewed." Budget in a required PD meeting: "If a Predoctoral fellowship grant application is funded, the Project Director will be required to attend one AFRI Fellows Project Directors' meeting during the performance period of the award." 100% effort required at award. Cost-share: dollar-for-dollar match applies only to applied research that "is commodity-specific and not of national scope"; "If the applied research or integrated project with an applied research component is not commodity specific or is national in scope, then no match is required."

FORMAT: all attachments PDF; "Check the manifest of submitted files to verify attachments are in the correct format."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, and the disqualifying half is mostly EMPTY — which is itself the finding.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES: I searched the full FY26 EWD NOFO (49 pp.), the FY 2026 Part IV, C instructions (39 pp.) and 7 CFR 3430.303 for prior-award language ("concurrent", "only one", "previously held", "already received", "another fellowship", "simultaneous"). There is NO prior-award or concurrent-award exclusion for A7101 in any of them. Unlike NIH F31 (no prior PD/PI on an NIH research grant; 5-year aggregate NRSA cap) and unlike NIH K awards (the R01/K interaction), an AFRI predoctoral fellowship carries no prior-funding disqualifier that NIFA states. The only submission-conduct bar is duplication, verbatim: "Duplicate or Multiple Submissions – submission of duplicate or predominantly overlapping applications is not allowed. NIFA will disqualify both applications if an applicant submits multiple applications that are duplicative or substantially overlapping to NIFA programs within the same fiscal year." Note it disqualifies BOTH applications, not just the later one. The real gates are structural, not prior-funding: US citizen/national/permanent resident; advanced to candidacy by the deadline (7 CFR 3430.303: "the applicant must have advanced to candidacy by the application deadline"); and still pre-degree.

CAUTION FOR THE EXISTING ROW: the row currently asserts "one active AFRI predoctoral fellowship per fellow". I could not source that in any FY2026 NIFA document. It may be true, stale, or inferred. It needs a citation or removal — do not carry it forward unsourced.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the high-value half, and the direct analogue of NIH's K/R01 carve-outs:
(1) Taking this fellowship does NOT burn your later AFRI New Investigator status. Verbatim, FY 2026 AFRI Grant Types: an individual who "has not received competitively awarded Federal research funds as Project Director (PD) with the exception of pre- or postdoctoral grants, equipment grants, and AFRI Seed Grants is eligible to submit an application for a New Investigator Standard Grant". Corroborated by 7 CFR 3430.303, which says New Investigator applicants "may not have received competitively awarded Federal funds, with the exception of pre- or postdoctoral awards or NRI/AFRI Seed Grants." So the predoc fellowship is carved out by name — it is a free move with respect to the next rung of the AFRI ladder.
(2) Co-PD money never counts: "Federal funding received by the applicant as Co-PD of previously awarded competitive grants does not count against New Investigator eligibility."
(3) Your institution's wealth does not gate you: "While the Predoctoral Fellowships Program Area Priority is a component of the AFRI Food and Agriculture Science Enhancement (FASE) grant types, the applicant fellow need not be from, or planning to carry out the fellowship project at, a Strengthening Grant eligible institution to be eligible for a Predoctoral Fellowship grant." Also "New Investigator Grant applications do not need to adhere to the eligibility requirements described for Strengthening Grants."
(4) The award can be upgraded rather than surrendered if your career moves fast: "NIFA Predoctoral Fellowships can be converted to Standard Grants under certain circumstances (e.g., if the Fellow obtains a faculty position)", provided "the Fellow substantively completes at least 50% of the fellowship performance period (e.g., ... 18 months for a 36-month award)", via letters from the PD (AR-signed) and the mentor to the National Program Leader. But: "Predoctoral Fellowships cannot be converted into Postdoctoral Fellowships."
(5) Grants are not renewable ("Unless otherwise stated, grants are not renewable"), so the successor is a postdoctoral fellowship (A7201) or a New Investigator grant, not a renewal.
result.resubmission_note:
ALLOWED, with no stated cap on attempts — materially more permissive than NIH's single-A1 rule. FY26 EWD NOFO Part II, B limits the FY26 competition to two application types: "1. New application ... 2. Resubmitted application: Resubmitted applications must include the one-page 'Response to Previous Review' and are subject to the same criteria and due dates herein. Resubmitted applicants must enter the NIFA-assigned proposal number of the previously submitted application in the Federal Field (Field 4) on the application form."

Mechanics of the Response to Previous Review (Part IV, C instructions): "A maximum one-page response to the previous review", which must include "Previous proposal number" and carry "'Response to Previous Review' as the title on the first page of the project narrative attachment". "The 'Response to Previous Review' is not applicable to new applications."

No 37-month window, no A1 suffix system, no ban on a further attempt after a failed resubmission is stated by NIFA. There is only one cycle a year, so each attempt costs a full year. The overlap bar still applies: duplicate or substantially overlapping applications to NIFA programmes within the same fiscal year disqualify both. This fills the existing row's `resubmission_allowed`/`resubmission_policy` fields, which are currently `unspecified`.

Ali — but publishes no email addresses beside them and does not say which covers A7101. NIFA also refers to a "National Program Leader" as the post-award point of contact, identified on the Notice of Award, not in advance.

IS PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT EXPECTED? Permitted and sanctioned, but NOT framed as expected — NIFA publishes nothing resembling NIH's "one of the best times to contact a PO is when you are thinking about applying". Do not build a strategy around cultivating an individual PO here, as you would at NIH. NIFA's flagged pre-submission step is institutional, not scientific: "Contact an AR prior to starting an application."
result.examples_or_samples:
NO FUNDED SAMPLE APPLICATIONS ARE PUBLISHED — a real gap, and the sharpest contrast with NIH. NIFA has no equivalent of the NIH/NIAID/NHGRI/NIA sample-application libraries with summary statements. I searched NIFA's own site and the AFRI NOFO Resources page and found no sample or annotated application for A7101 or any AFRI mechanism. Record as "not found", not as "none exists" — but plan on writing without a model application from the funder.

WHAT NIFA DOES GIVE YOU, best first:

1. THE SCORING RUBRIC — closest substitute for a sample, and most applicants never open it. "FY 2026 AFRI Review Criteria" (PDF, AFRI NOFO Resources page) has a section "8. Predoctoral and Postdoctoral Fellowship Applications" with the three scored headings and their sub-bullets: (a) Merit of the Application; (b) Qualifications of Project Personnel, Adequacy of Facilities, and Project Management; (c) Project Relevance. It tells you reviewers are asked to assess the applicant's "critical thinking and analytical skills based on organization and details provided in the application", "level of maturity of thought", and "alignment between career goals and objectives and appropriate activities" — i.e. the narrative is judged as evidence of the candidate, not only of the project. Write the six pages against this list.

2. FUNDED PROJECT ABSTRACTS — the NIFA Data Gateway is the RePORTER analogue: "The Data Gateway enables users to find funding data, metrics, and information about research, education, and extension projects that have received grant awards from NIFA", covering FY2002 to the present. Two entry points: NIFA Enterprise Search (portal.nifa.usda.gov/enterprise-search/, filterable by project type, knowledge area, field of science, award year, state, grantee type) and Recent Awards (portal.nifa.usda.gov/lmd4/recent_awards). Search prior A7101 awards to see funded abstracts, host institutions and mentors — and to identify mentors who have carried fellows before. Progress reports on funded projects surface through REEport / the NIFA Reporting System.

3. BASE RATES NIFA PUBLISHES AND ALMOST NO FUNDER DOES — "Most Successful Institutions FY 26" and "Least Successful Institutions FY 26" PDFs sit in the Related Documents list on the AFRI NOFO Resources page (alongside FY 24 versions). These let an applicant calibrate how their institution has actually fared in AFRI competitions before investing three months.

4. THE DENOMINATOR — the FY26 NOFO sets the money aside explicitly: "no less than 15 percent of the funds will be made available for Food and Agricultural Science Enhancement (FASE) Grants", and "no less than 11.25% will be made available for Strengthening grant types under the FASE program." The residual, 15% - 11.25% = 3.75%, is the pre- and postdoctoral fellowship share — which independently corroborates the 3.75% FASE figure already recorded in the row from the January 2026 AFRI FAQ. Against ~$39.7M for the whole EWD NOFO, that is roughly $1.5M, or about eight $180K fellowships across predoc and postdoc combined. Treat this as a very small programme.

5. STRUCTURAL GUIDES — "FY 2026 AFRI Grant Types" and "FY 2026 AFRI Project Types" PDFs (Related Documents, AFRI NOFO Resources) explain the Research/Education/Extension/Integrated choice the Project Summary forces you to declare; the "AFRI New Investigator Decision Tree" PDF maps the next rung. The repo already holds NIFA's "AFRI Project and Grant Types FAQ" (January 2026) at research/sources/nifa-afri-project-and-grant-types-faq-2026-01.pdf.

6. WHO TO TALK TO INSTEAD OF READING A SAMPLE — because no sample exists, the highest-value substitute is a mentor who has held or supervised an AFRI fellowship; find them via Data Gateway searches on prior A7101 awards at your institution, then ask to read their funded narrative directly.

result.review_to_award:
Unusually fast decision, then a very long wait for money — the two halves differ sharply and both matter for planning.

- Submission to notification: 9 days in the last cycle. Close 8 Dec 2025 → "Applicants will be notified if they are selected to receive an award by Wednesday, Dec. 17." 
- Notification to meeting: about 6 months (mid-Dec 2025 → June 2026 meeting).
- Notification to cash: LONGER STILL, and this is the highest-practical-impact finding. The award is a post-meeting reimbursement, not an up-front payment: "Travel award funds are non-transferable and will be provided following the conclusion of ASM Microbe 2026 upon confirming awardee's attendance at the meeting." The applicant must front the full travel cost and is repaid after attending — roughly 6 months after being told they won. Registration is separate and is provided complimentary.
- Continuing condition: membership must be held "at the time of application and remain active through the 2026 meeting" [i.e. through the meeting], so a lapsed membership between December and June puts the award at risk.
result.submission_requirements:
Four components plus a membership condition, submitted through the ASM awards portal. Quoted from the funder's page:

1. "Scientific abstract not previously published or presented at another conference."
2. "Curriculum vitae (CV), including scientific focus area."
3. "Two letters of nominations on institution letterhead written by the department chair and principal investigator or immediate director."
4. "Applicant statement providing a brief overview (limit 500 words) of qualifications and how the travel award supports scientific research."
Plus: "A current ASM member at the time of application and remain active through the [June] meeting."

WHERE IT DEVIATES from a normal society travel award:
- TWO letters, and not two of your choosing: one must come from the DEPARTMENT CHAIR and one from the PI/immediate director, both "on institution letterhead". That is an institutional sign-off in practice and is the main scheduling risk — a chair's letter typically needs weeks of notice.
- The abstract must be UNPUBLISHED AND UNPRESENTED elsewhere. A poster already shown at a regional or institutional meeting can disqualify the abstract, so reserve fresh data for this.
- The only free-text advocacy space is 500 words; there is no research plan, no budget, no biosketch.
- Selection is on the science: judged "by the Travel Award Committee on the basis of the scientific quality of submitted abstracts", with the award "determined by the ASM Microbe Program Committee". The abstract carries the decision; the statement is secondary.
- No page limits, budget justification, or institutional certification beyond the letterhead letters.

SUBMISSION ROUTE: a per-award solicitation in ASM's portal — this award is https://asm.secure-platform.com/a/solicitations/241/home — which redirects to ASM Single Sign On (app.asm.org). I did not log in or create an account, so the in-portal form fields and any additional in-form requirements are unverified. Each sibling award is a SEPARATE solicitation (Halde 240, this award 241, Finkelstein 242, Clinical Virology 245), so each is its own submission rather than one common form.

result.submission_requirements:
Mechanism-specific mechanics, all from the funder's own application form (GTFC-application.docx) — these are NOT on the programme page and are where this mechanism deviates:

ROUTE — email, not a portal. "Email submission to: ASME Engineering Education, c/o Manager, Engineering Education and Outreach, EngineeringEducation@asme.org". The form prescribes the exact subject line: "Subject: Graduate Teaching Fellowship Application – [your name here]". The GTF explicitly does NOT go through ASME's online scholarship application system used by other ASME student awards.

FORMAT — one file. "In ONE Complete PDF: Please include the following information with your fully completed application form." The completed form plus every component must be merged into a single PDF; this is the commonest way to fail on technicality.

PACKET CONTENTS — the ASME form itself (12 numbered items), undergraduate cumulative GPA, resume/CV, transcripts of all academic work, "Two letters of recommendation from faculty members, especially from M.S. Committee, if appropriate", a statement about the anticipated faculty career, and — critically — "Certification from department head of a commitment to a lecture-responsibility teaching assistantship and the lecture assignment anticipated." The department-head certification is a component of the submitted packet, not merely a pre-award condition; the form also collects the dept head/chair's name, email and phone (items 4).

SIGNATURE — item 12 requires the applicant's signature under "I verify that all the information contained and included in my application is accurate and true to the best of my knowledge." No institutional research-office or sponsored-programs sign-off is required; the department head's certification is the only institutional endorsement.

REFERENCE LETTERS — two, and they travel inside the applicant's single PDF. There is no separate referee portal or independent-submission route, so the applicant must collect them before the deadline.

ELIGIBILITY ITEM PRESENT ONLY ON THE FORM: "Applicant must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, have an undergraduate degree from an ABET accredited program, and be an ASME student member." The ABET-accredited-undergraduate-degree requirement does not appear in the programme page's eligibility list — the two ASME sources disagree, and this matters for internationally-educated applicants who hold permanent residency.

MEMBERSHIP — ASME student membership is required but need not precede the application: "If you're not yet an ASME member, you may apply for membership while also applying for a loan, scholarship, or fellowship. (ASME student membership fee is $25 a year.)"

PAGE LIMITS — none stated anywhere, for the career statement or any other component.

The form also asks the applicant to check a Male/Female box (item 10).
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
No prior or concurrent award is stated as disqualifying anywhere on the programme page or the application form. What matters here is the opposite of the usual pattern, and it is the single most misunderstood feature of this mechanism:

WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (and is in fact mandatory):
- Holding a teaching assistantship is REQUIRED, not disqualifying. "A lecture-responsibility teaching assistantship commitment from the applicant's department is required" and "In the term of the fellowship, the awardee must teach at least one lecture course with full responsibility for the course." Unlike most doctoral fellowships, which bar or limit concurrent employment and assistantship support, the GTF is a $5,000/yr top-up that is designed to sit on top of a departmental TA line. An applicant already carrying TA support is the intended candidate.
- Prior receipt of the GTF itself does not bar a second year. "The fellowships may be renewed for a second year though it is not guaranteed", and the form states "Renewal for a second year is possible, and renewal applications will be assessed alongside new applications" — i.e. a current fellow re-competes in the same pool rather than being excluded, but also is not entitled to year two.
- Master's-stage funding and prior degrees are irrelevant to eligibility; the M.S. (or passed qualifying exam) is a prerequisite, not a conflict.

WHAT LIMITS OR EXCLUDES:
- A hard lifetime cap of two years: "Fellowship awards in the amount of $5,000 a year are made, for a maximum of two years." Two prior GTF years exhaust eligibility permanently.
- Year two is conditional on compliance, not on a new competition alone: the fellow must file mid-year (31 Oct) and year-end (4 Apr) reports, one from the student and one from the department head, or renewal eligibility lapses.
- Non-funding gates that function as exclusions: US citizenship or permanent residency, ASME student membership, ME (or related) PhD candidacy, and — per the form only — an ABET-accredited undergraduate degree.

THE REAL-WORLD CONFLICT ASME DOES NOT ADDRESS (flagged, not asserted): a major full-support fellowship whose terms prohibit teaching during the tenure year — an NSF GRFP tenure year is the obvious case — would collide with the GTF's mandatory full-responsibility lecture course. ASME publishes no rule either way, so this is a practical incompatibility, not a stated ineligibility. It is the single best question to put to the Manager, Engineering Education and Outreach before applying; see unresolved.
result.program_officer_contact:
Role-based contact, no named individual published. Route: EngineeringEducation@asme.org, addressed "c/o Manager, Engineering Education and Outreach", ASME Engineering Education. This same address receives the application, the applicant's questions, and (for fellows) the renewal reports.

Pre-submission contact is invited but not required or expected — the form closes: "If you have any questions or need additional information let us know at the email above." There is no stated expectation of contacting a program officer before applying, and no pre-submission concept-check stage, so the email is a logistics/eligibility channel rather than a scientific-fit conversation.

I could not find a named staff member: the ASME engineering-education page carries no staff directory, and the general Contact Us page offers only headquarters routes (CustomerCare@asme.org; US/Canada (800) 843-2763; outside North America (646) 616-3100; Two Park Avenue, Suite 1600, New York, NY 10016-5990) with nothing specific to student programmes. Selection is by a committee, not an officer: "Fellows are selected/renewed annually by the ASME Selection Committee", under the Committee on Engineering Education.

Highest-value human route is not ASME staff but the applicant's own department head, whose teaching-assistantship certification is a required packet component — that conversation must happen well before 15 February.
result.examples_or_samples:
ASME publishes no funded sample application, successful abstract, annotated example, or reviewer guidance for this mechanism. Two concrete substitutes exist, both on the funder's own page:

1. THE FUNDER'S OWN APPLICATION GUIDE — page 1 of GTFC-application.docx (https://www.asme.org/getmedia/<session-id>/GTFC-application.docx) is a genuine instruction sheet, not just a form: it restates the criteria, the packet contents, the one-PDF rule, the email address and the required subject line. Downloading it is the correct first action for anyone considering this award; it is the "material to get started".

2. A PUBLIC, CONTACTABLE ALUMNI ROSTER — the programme page lists current and past fellows continuously from 1992 through 2026, with name, fellowship years, institution, and for recent cohorts a working email address (46 unique non-ASME addresses on the page as fetched). Current/recent fellows include Anna Alvarez (2025-27, UC Santa Barbara), Daniella Walter (2026-27, UC Santa Barbara), Samantha Splendido (2025-26, Penn State), Nafiseh Mohammadianaftah (2025-26, University of Kansas), Myia Dickens (2024-25, Notre Dame), Jordan D. result.resubmission_note: No resubmission or reapplication restriction is stated. There is no "one resubmission only" rule, no A0/A1 concept, and no required response-to-reviewers: the mechanism runs a single annual round with no published feedback to respond to. By the FY2027 pattern it should launch in early July 2027 and close mid-August 2027. That is a pattern extrapolation, NOT a found date — treat as expected, not confirmed.
