result.deadline_pattern:
Annual, single cycle per fiscal year, four fixed stages. FY2027 as published: LOI launch "By July 6, 2026" → LOI deadline "August 14, 2026, at 5:00 pm ET" → application deadline "October 20, 2026, at 5:00 pm ET" (Oct 22 ISTAART) → "Application Review: October–December, 2026" → award notifications by end of January 2027.

So the working rule: LOI opens early July, closes mid-August, full application late October, decision end of January. AARFA shares this exact clock with its two sibling mechanisms AARGA (Research Grant for All) and AACSFA (Clinician Scientist Fellowship for All) — which matters because you may only apply to ONE of the three per cycle.

Hard cutoff: "Letter of intent (LOI) and application submissions must be received by 5 p.m. Eastern time (ET) by their respective deadlines. Late submissions will not be accepted - no exceptions."

ISTAART membership buys a 2-day extension at the full-application stage only, not at LOI.
result.loi_deadline:
"August 14, 2026, at 5:00 pm ET" for the FY2027 cycle — CLOSED as of 2026-09-18. LOI launched "By July 6, 2026", giving roughly a six-week window.

The LOI is a hard gate, not a formality: "LOIs are a required component of the application process. No application will be considered without an approved LOI, including resubmitted applications." It is also a real cut — "only a fraction of LOIs will be invited for full application" — reviewed by "two or three reviewers with expertise in the area of the application," with no feedback given ("Due to the high number of submissions, specific feedback and reviewer comments are not provided at the letter of intent (LOI) stage").

Two features that trip people up:
1. The LOI is BLIND-reviewed. "Applicants must not include any personally identifiable information (e.g., names, institutions, locations, or other identifiers) within the body of the LOI. Any submission containing such information may be disqualified or returned for revision."
2. LOI content is tightly capped: four narrative sections (project summary incl. methodology; specific aims; innovation/novelty; overall impact), "EACH SECTION IS LIMITED TO 1,000 CHARACTERS, INCLUDING SPACES." Plus PI + primary mentor biosketches and non-profit documentation (W-9 US / W-8-BEN non-US, signed within the past five years).

LOI review criteria (blinded, so they are all about the science, not the person): innovation/novelty; alignment with Association research priorities; impact on Alzheimer's and related dementia research; evidence of methodological rigor.

No penalty for submitting an LOI while awaiting a prior decision: "There is no penalty for submitting an LOI to a new cycle while awaiting results from a current submission; if you are awarded in the current cycle, we will administratively withdraw the new LOI."
result.review_to_award:
Full timeline, ~5.5 months from LOI to decision and up to ~8.5 months from LOI to money:

LOI deadline 14 Aug 2026 → LOI review and invitation (unspecified interval; invitation arrives by email from Association staff) → full application 20 Oct 2026 → "Application Review: October–December, 2026" → award notification "By Jan. 30, 2027" (funder web pages) / "By January 31, 2027" (RFA PDF — a one-day discrepancy between the site and its own RFA) → "After the notification email, you will receive official award documentation within 5-10 business days."

EARLIEST START: applicant-chosen but bounded. "You choose your own start date within 3 months of the award notification, and it must begin on the first of the month (for example, it cannot start on January 17)." So earliest realistic start is 1 Feb 2027 for the FY2027 cycle, and the outer bound is ~end of April 2027. The RFA makes the outer bound binding: "awards will begin the period of performance within three months of the award notification. Failure to initiate an award within the stated period may result in cancellation." Extensions to that window "are only granted if requested prior to application submission, in writing, by contacting grantsapp@alz.org" — i.e. you must foresee the delay BEFORE you submit, which is unusual and easy to miss.

ETHICS APPROVAL IS A START-DATE GATE, NOT A SUBMISSION GATE: "animal welfare and human volunteer ethical assurances are not required at the time of application, investigators have until their chosen start date (within 3 months or less of award notification) to submit these approved documents." The RFA warns that "IRB/IACUC approval at many institutions can take more than 90 days" — so a fellow with human/animal work should start IRB in parallel with the full application, not after notification. For fellowships specifically, if the approval sits on the mentor's protocol, the Fellow must supply "a signed letter stating that the ethical approval ... covers the awarded project with the Fellow's name and award number included."

REVIEW STRUCTURE (three stages): (1) peer scientists with subject expertise score the application; applicants may nominate recommended reviewers and exclude conflicted ones (conflict definitions include trained with/by the reviewer, co-published within 4 years excluding large consortia such as ADNI/IGAP, co-investigator within 4 years, conceptual bias, financial benefit); (2) normalisation and discussion by the IRGP Council plus invited committee members; (3) final recommendations to the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG), then to the Association.

APPEALS: within 10 business days of outcome notification, two-page double-spaced letter to grantsappeals@alz.org; decision "usually within 90 days of the appeal deadline." Only for undeclared conflict of interest, egregious error, or malfeasance — "not intended to provide a mechanism for routine protest." No appeals at the LOI stage.
result.submission_requirements:
Submitted through ProposalCentral (proposalcentral.com). Templates and instructions only become visible AFTER the LOI is approved — you cannot see the full application requirements in advance except via the RFA.

FULL APPLICATION COMPONENTS AND PAGE LIMITS (verbatim from the RFA):
- Statement of Mentorship (2 to 3 pages) — written by the mentor: "commitment, background, and plan to support the applicant's training and development." The RFA states "This statement will be a significant part of the application review."
- Statement of Commitment (3 pages) — written by the applicant: interest in the field, a timeline, how the mentor's training plan maps to the research project and career development.
- Area of Research (3 pages) — background, scientific rationale, research strategy, alternative approach, impact. Note: only 3 pages of actual science.
- Data Analysis plan (1 page) — including statistical and power analyses.
- References/Citations (1 page)
- Recruitment Plan (1 page) — human-subjects studies only.
- Plan for Data Sharing (2 pages)
- Letters of Support/Reference (1 page) — "up to 3 letters are permitted."
- Biosketch(es) (5 pages each) — PI, mentor, and key personnel as applicable. "We do not require a specific biosketch format -- NIH, NIH Common Forms, SciENcv, or another format are all acceptable. The binding requirement is length."
- Environmental Context (1 page) — an unusual component: community relationships, specialised institutional features, rural/urban setting, limited infrastructure, or personal context. It is explicitly fed into scoring (reviewers are told to consider it under two of the three criteria).
- Resubmission Statement (1 page, optional)
- Available Resources and Budget Justification (2 pages)
- Non-profit documentation (W-9 US / W-8 or W-8BEN non-US, signed and dated within the past five years by a signing official, carrying EIN/TIN/VAT).

WHERE IT DEVIATES FROM THE NORM — four things worth flagging:
1. NO INSTITUTIONAL SIGNATURE AT SUBMISSION. "Institutional signatures are not required at the time of submission by the Association. Should your institution/organization require it, a signature page is provided for use... Please do not submit the signature page with your application." This is the opposite of NIH practice and removes the usual sponsored-programs bottleneck — though your own office may still impose one.
2. EFFORT IS MEASURED AGAINST RESEARCH, NOT SALARY. "Effort should be listed as a percentage of their overall total commitment to research, not as the percentage of salary covered by the grant's budget." And: "The Principal Investigator must commit to maintaining at least 50% of their full-time effort to research during the funding period. This requirement INCLUDES research efforts beyond the AARFA-funded project." So the 50% is 50% of your time on research generally, not 50% on this project.
3. GENERATIVE AI IS EXPLICITLY PERMITTED. "Applicants may use LLMs and other generative AI tools in the preparation of their LOIs and full applications... Using one of these tools will not affect the review of your application." (Applicant remains responsible for content.)
4. MENTOR NEED NOT BE LOCAL, AND THERE IS ONLY ONE. "The mentor does not need to be at the same institution." Only one primary mentor is allowed and only that mentor is stipend-eligible; co-mentors go in as key personnel/consultants. A required element is "a plan for an evaluation strategy of the mentoring process."

SCORING WEIGHTS (stage one): applicant's ability and promise as a scientist, from record of achievement, career plan, letters of support and CV — 30%; "Quality and emphasis of applicant and originality of the research plan" — 40%; significance of the question, quality of work plan, impact-risk, impact on the AD/ADRD ecosystem — 30%.

BUDGET RULES THAT SHAPE THE APPLICATION: indirect costs capped at 10% of total direct costs, inclusive of subcontracts; no salary cap; travel ≤$12,500 across the award and ≤$7,000 in any year, and must cover AAIC attendance; up to $2,500 per budget period for licensed childcare. NOT allowed: computer hardware and standard software, major lab equipment (freezers, ultracentrifuges, RT-PCR, imaging), service contracts, construction, tuition, rent, visa costs and fees, general liability insurance, currency-exchange fees, institutional overheads on staff time.

FUNDED BENCHMARKS (obligations, not application content, but they change who should apply): required benchmarks include AAIC attendance with an accepted abstract and at least one Association networking event, documented face-to-face mentoring hours, reviewing grant applications, documented networking facilitation, and submission of funding proposals to other agencies (NIH, NSF, MRC, CIHR are named). The $20,000 dissemination stipend ($10k PI + $10k mentor) is paid only on successful completion and is not guaranteed.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves. The headline finding: unlike an NIH K award, AARFA does NOT bar you for holding or winning NIH funding — the conflict rules are scoped almost entirely to other Alzheimer's Association awards.

WHAT MAKES YOU INELIGIBLE:
- Rank. "Individuals who have a position at or above Assistant Professor (or the equivalent, including Research Assistant Professor) are not eligible." Research Assistant Professor counts as above the line here (and is explicitly eligible for the sibling AARGA instead). Also barred: current undergraduate/master's/doctoral students "regardless of prior degree status," and "Temporary, part-time, or acting faculty."
- Timing of the rank test is two-pronged: within 10 years of terminal degree AT LOI SUBMISSION, and not holding an independent faculty position AT THE TIME OF AWARD. The FAQ spells out the trap: "if your LOI is invited, your full application is within funding range, and it is funded, you will not be able to accept the award if you are by then in an Assistant Professor position." A postdoc on the faculty market should know this before investing in the application.
- One application per cycle across the three sibling programmes. "Applicants are not allowed to submit to more than one of the following programs in any given cycle: Alzheimer's Association Research Grants for All, Alzheimer's Association Research Fellowship for All, or Alzheimer's Association Clinician Scientist Fellowship for All. Duplicative submissions will be withdrawn administratively. This stipulation holds regardless of whether the topics are distinct areas or projects."
- "Overlapping funding of more than one Alzheimer's Association grant is not allowed," and specifically "Overlap with Alzheimer's Association Clinician Scientist Fellowship for All or the Alzheimer's Association Research Grant for All programs are not allowed."
- Delinquency. "Investigators/organizations who are delinquent in required reporting to the Alzheimer's Association are not eligible to apply."
- The absolute bar: "Investigators that have previous Alzheimer's Association awards closed as 'Incomplete' are not eligible to apply without exception. This policy will be strictly adhered to."
- Governance: current MSAG and IRGP Council members cannot be PI on any award.
- Institutional: for-profit entities, and state/federal government-appropriated laboratories in the US and abroad, cannot be the applicant institution (VA hospitals are carved out as eligible). Also barred if the institutional official with fiscal oversight is the PI, or is a familial relation of the PI.
- US sanctions law: no awards to sanctioned individuals/entities or those on the SDN list.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half applicants usually cannot find:
- NIH K AND R AWARDS DO NOT DISQUALIFY YOU, during the award: "I received an NIH (K and/or R) award or other funding during my fellowship. Can I keep my fellowship? ... It depends on your fellowship's mandatory effort requirement and your institution's policies. Contact grantsapp@alz.org, and the Grants Team will work with you and your grants office to keep both awards wherever the effort requirements allow." This is a negotiated effort question, not an eligibility bar.
- Other funders' awards likewise: "I received an award from another organization. Can I maintain my Alzheimer's Association award? In most cases, yes -- provided there is no scientific or funding overlap... if there are overlapping aims, we will need updated aims for review."
- Holding a PRIOR Association award from a different call is fine: "Investigators with Alzheimer's Association awards in programs from specific program announcements may still apply to a program listed in this call, but the project must be distinct from their current award."
- You can be on someone else's application while submitting your own: "Can I be part of another LOI (as a collaborator or Co-I) even if I submit my own LOI? Yes, as long as the projects are distinct and do not overlap."
- Lab-mates may both apply: "Members of the same team/lab may submit proposals on distinct areas of a larger, overarching line of study provided there is no budgetary or technical overlap."
- The 10-year clock can be extended: "Adjustments to this eligibility period may be considered for documented career interruptions such as family leave, military service, or major illness or injury." CRITICAL PROCEDURAL CATCH — "The approval of any exemptions must be obtained prior to submitting a LOI," and the FAQ adds that requests are not "considered once the deadline has passed." Email grantsapp@alz.org well before mid-August.
- Not yet in post at LOI time: "If you have not yet begun an eligible position as listed in the RFA at the time of LOI submission, we encourage you to apply once you" are in post (i.e. apply in the cycle where you will meet criteria at LOI).
- MSAG/IRGP members may still be your MENTOR — they simply "must forfeit their mentor stipend" — and may serve as key personnel or collaborators without salary.
- Awaiting a decision does not block a new LOI (see LOI field).

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether holding a concurrent NIH F32/K99 AT THE TIME OF APPLICATION is permitted. The FAQ answers only the during-award case. The 50%-research-effort commitment is the operative constraint, and the funder routes this to grantsapp@alz.org case by case.
result.program_officer_contact:
No named program officer. The Association runs a shared grants inbox rather than assigning POs, so there is no individual to build a relationship with — this is a real difference from NIH and worth telling postdocs explicitly.

- grantsapp@alz.org — the Alzheimer's Association Grants staff, the single route for all pre-submission and post-award questions. Named as the contact on the AARFA page, in the RFA's Contact Information section, and throughout the FAQ.
- grantsappeals@alz.org — appeals of funding decisions only.
- 24/7 Helpline 800-272-3900 is a general Association line, not a grants line.

IS PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT EXPECTED? Not routinely — there is no required pre-submission inquiry stage for AARFA (unlike the sibling ALZ-RWD and ALZ WW-FNFP programmes, which state "Pre-submission inquiries accepted at any time"). But contact is MANDATORY, before the LOI deadline, in four situations, and each is a case where silence costs you the cycle:
1. Any eligibility exemption — the >10-years-post-degree exception for career interruption. "Email grantsapp@alz.org before you submit your LOI and describe your situation clearly."
2. Ambiguity about your rank/track — the FAQ invites contact where an institution has no Assistant Professor track, where clinical duties complicate the clock, or where you are an Instructor/Research Associate unsure whether to target AARFA or AARGA: "the recommendation would be to apply to AARFA. If you have questions, contact grantsapp@alz.org."
3. Questions about overlap with an existing Association award — "There are some exceptions so please contact grantsapp@alz.org if you have questions."
4. Any need to extend the 3-month award-start window — must be "requested prior to application submission, in writing."
Also scope questions: "I have a question about whether my project is within scope. Who can I talk to? ... If you still have questions, contact grantsapp@alz.org."

WHO ELSE TO TALK TO: reviewers are IRGP Council and MSAG members, and the Association publishes the full membership list (alz.org/grants, and /research/for_researchers/grants/the-international-research-grant-program-irgp-co). That list is the closest thing to knowing your review panel. ISTAART — the Association's professional society — is the other route in: membership also buys the 2-day full-application extension, and AAIC is where funded fellows are required to present.
result.examples_or_samples:
Honest answer: the Association publishes funded ABSTRACTS but no sample or annotated APPLICATION. Do not send someone looking for the latter.

WHAT EXISTS:
1. Funded studies database — https://www.alz.org/research/for_researchers/grants/funded-studies-search — "View abstracts of studies supported by our research funding." Filterable by Year (2008–2026), State, Country, and Program, and the Program list carries 50+ mechanisms including AARF and its variants. This is the usable route: filter Program to the Research Fellowship line and read several years of funded abstracts. Because the LOI is the real cut and is itself four 1,000-character sections, these abstracts are the closest published analogue to a winning LOI — arguably the single most useful preparation material for this mechanism.
2. Portfolio summaries by year — /research/for_researchers/grants/portfolio_summaries — the shape of what the Association actually funds.
3. Example award documents (not applications) — on the About Our Grants page: "including the example standard award letter, the current standard conditions of award, and the example Part the Cloud (PTC) award letter and conditions." The FAQ stresses the conditions "are non-negotiable" and should be checked with your institution BEFORE applying. For partnership programmes, "contact grantsapp@alz.org for those examples."
4. The RFA itself (https://www.alz.org/getmedia/<session-id>/aarfa-rfa.pdf) and the grants FAQ PDF (https://www.alz.org/getmedia/<session-id>/alzheimers-association-grants-faq.pdf) — the FAQ in particular reads like accumulated applicant questions and is the best single orientation document.
5. Published review criteria PDF — /getmedia/<session-id>/Alzheimers-Association-Review-criteria.pdf.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: no sample application, no annotated proposal, no mock LOI, no published success rate. Searched the FAQ and About Our Grants specifically; neither mentions sample applications, and neither gives application-to-award ratios. The only quantitative statement of scale is "more than $450 million invested in over 1,200 active projects in 59 countries." The RFA says only that "a fraction of projects are invited to submit full applications."
result.resubmission_note:
Permitted and structurally supported, but the LOI gate resets every time.

"Applicants may revise and resubmit an application that was previously submitted for an earlier grant cycle; however, a new LOI is required each cycle. A current LOI corresponding to the application year must accompany each application. Revisions of previous submissions will be treated as new applications. Efforts will be made to provide some continuity in reviews. The resubmission of an approved LOI does not guarantee that you will be invited to resubmit a full application in a future cycle. Resubmissions may be submitted to a different program in this call and still be a resubmission."

The warning worth quoting to any applicant: "Resubmissions are reviewed holistically again, and merely responding to reviewer critiques is not enough to be funded on resubmission." This is the opposite of the NIH A1 habit of writing to the critique.

Support offered: an optional 1-page Resubmission Statement — "Resubmissions are granted a one-page summary addressing comments raised by reviewers in a prior review cycle(s). It is up to the investigator whether they wish to declare their application a resubmission, even if it is a similar application to a prior submission." Declaring is optional, and stage-one criteria note "Resubmissions will have the opportunity to provide a response to prior reviews."

Prior invitation carries nothing forward: "I was invited to submit a full application last cycle but was not funded (or did not submit). Do I have to submit another LOI? Yes. All applicants must submit an LOI for the current open cycle. Previously approved LOIs from a different cycle are not eligible."

No stated cap on the number of resubmissions.
unresolved: FY2028 LOI launch and deadline dates — not published as of 2026-09-18. The early-July-launch / mid-August-close pattern is extrapolated from the single published FY2027 cycle, not found. Re-check the AARFA page from ~June 2027.

LOI-to-invitation rate and overall success rate — never published. The RFA says only 'only a fraction of LOIs will be invited for full application'. Not in the FAQ, not on About Our Grants. Do not estimate.

Whether an applicant may hold a concurrent NIH F32/K99 or other fellowship AT THE TIME OF APPLICATION. The FAQ answers only the during-award case (permitted subject to effort and institutional policy). The 50%-research-effort commitment is the operative constraint; the funder routes this to grantsapp@alz.org case by case.

result.review_to_award:
Funder's own statement (FAQ): "Project proposals are reviewed by an internal awards panel and the results are communicated approximately three months after the submission deadline." Decisions go "via email to all applicants".

Observed, close -> decision letters: Spring 2026 (closed 13 May 2026) -> August 2026 (~3 mo). Fall 2025 (closed 12 Nov 2025) -> March 2026 (~4 mo). Fall 2023 (closed 13 Nov) -> "Decision letters were sent out March 2024". Spring 2023 (closed 26 Apr) -> August 2023. Fall 2022 (closed 26 Oct) -> March 2023. EARLIEST START: no project start date is set by Amazon, because the cash is "a one-time unrestricted gift to your Principal Investigator's academic institution or organization" rather than a grant with a performance period. The outer bound is in the rules: "If you do not fulfill the administrative requirements for processing cash Awards within two years of your receipt of an Award notification, Amazon reserves the right to withhold payment." result.submission_requirements:
Submitted by the PI directly to Amazon's submission site — NOT through the university sponsored-programs office, and no institutional sign-off, cost-share, or authorised-organisational-representative approval is required at application. (Institutional involvement comes only after award, when the gift is processed.) This is the single biggest deviation from federal practice and the reason ARA is fast to apply to.

From the official ARA Proposal Template (PDF, version dated 03.19.2025, text extracted directly), verbatim:

(Individual CFPs may raise this — the Spring 2026 Agentic AI call said "a maximum of 4 pages, not including Appendices", the Spring 2026 AI for Information Security call said "encouraged to be a maximum of 3 pages". Always take the page limit from the specific CFP.)
- "Formatting: 11-point with commonly used legible font (e.g. Calibri, Times New Roman, or Arial); 1-inch margins on all sides."
- "Final document: All components should be saved as a single PDF and uploaded to submission site."
- "If you have been funded directly or indirectly by Amazon in the last three years, please include Appendix C."

Required body sections, in template order: Project Title; PI (name, title, department, university); Co-PI (optional, one only); "Cash funding needed:"; "AWS Promotional Credits needed:"; "Amazon contact (optional)"; Abstract; Keywords; Introduction ("Significance of the research and prior work"); Methods ("Your technical approach"); Expected results ("Please include milestones with timeline estimates, such as for datasets, code releases, technical reports, publications, applications, presentations, etc."); Funds needed; Additional information (answers to the extra questions posed by the specific CFP).

Appendices (do not count toward the page limit):
- "Appendix A - Reference ... Limit two pages."
- "Appendix B - CV of PI ... One-page CV of PI (professional title, experience, etc.), only to include the 5-6 most relevant papers to this proposal. One-page CV of Co-PI (optional)." NOTE: a one-page CV capped at 5-6 papers — much tighter than an NIH biosketch or NSF 2-page CV.
- "Appendix C - Previously Funded Project Summary" — see prior_funding_conflicts.

NO letters of reference, NO letters of support, NO sponsor/mentor statement, NO institutional letter, NO data-management plan, NO broader-impacts section. There is no reference-letter machinery at all.

BUDGET — two deviations that catch people:
- No indirect costs. Template: "For cash funding, please do not include indirect expenses which are not incurred solely for your project." The Spring 2026 Amazon 2030 CFP: the budget "should not include administrative overhead costs."
- Scope is prescribed by the FAQ: "A proposed cash budget is generally expected to support one to two graduate students (or a post-doctoral researcher) for one year, plus some conference travel and equipment. The budget should include a list of expected costs specified in USD."
- AWS Promotional Credits are requested separately and need "the requested amount, a short justification, a list of AWS products and any AWS Public Datasets to be used."

Team structure (FAQ): "Each proposal has a single faculty member, who will serve as the Primary PI. One co-PI per proposal can be included in the application form." Other team members may be named inside the proposal text but not on the form.

Award sizes are set per CFP, e.g. Spring 2026: Amazon 2030 "Unrestricted cash funds, up to $100,000 USD" plus "AWS Promotional Credits, no more than $70,000 USD on average"; Agentic AI "no more than $70,000 USD on average" cash plus "no more than $50,000 USD on average" credits; AI for Information Security ~$80,000 cash plus ~$40,000 credits on average.

Review criteria are stated per call and are short, e.g. Agentic AI: "potential impact to the research community and the quality of the scientific content"; Think Big: "transformative potential of the research, quality of the scientific content and the timeliness/readiness of the research to deliver breakthrough outcomes."

Template file: https://www.amazon.science/_attachment/ara-proposal-template-2025?id=<session-id> — downloadable now, even between cycles, so a first-time applicant can draft against it during the quiet period.

Not captured: the submission-portal URL itself. The "apply" link appears on a CFP page only while that call is open, so it could not be recorded on 2026-09-18.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
ARA HAS NO PRIOR-FUNDING EXCLUSION. Nothing about holding or having held other grants — federal, foundation, industry, or a previous ARA award — makes an applicant ineligible. This is the opposite of the NIH K/R01 interaction and is worth stating plainly to anyone used to federal mechanisms.

WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (explicitly):
- Previous ARA recipients may apply again. Program rules: "you may submit new proposals for subsequent ARA Program calls". FAQ, on award structure: awards are not extendable, "though applicants can submit new proposals for subsequent calls." So the route to continued Amazon support is a fresh proposal to the next cycle, not a renewal.
- Prior Amazon money does not disqualify — it triggers DISCLOSURE, not exclusion. Template rule: "If you have been funded directly or indirectly by Amazon in the last three years, please include Appendix C." Appendix C: "If you or someone on your project team has received cash funding or AWS Promotional Credits directly or indirectly from Amazon within the past 3 years, please answer the questions below. (Include funding from Amazon through your institution or from the NSF-Amazon Fairness in AI funding grant.)" It then asks for: "Project title: / Funding amount and time: / Funding source: / Who was this funding for? / If AWS Promotional Credits were provided, how much is left? / Please provide a brief summary of the results, papers, and open-source software enabled:". Note the 3-year lookback reaches ANY team member, counts credits as well as cash, and counts money routed through your institution or through the NSF-Amazon Fairness in AI programme. Unspent AWS credits must be declared.
- Holding concurrent non-Amazon funding on related work: no restriction stated anywhere in the rules, FAQ or template.
- International applicants: FAQ, "Researchers from around the world are encouraged to apply" (subject to the sanctions/export-control bar below).
- A PI who has already used their one proposal may still appear as co-PI on one other proposal: "A Primary PI can be listed as a co-PI on an additional proposal, but must withdraw if the other proposal is selected."

WHAT MAKES SOMEONE INELIGIBLE (program rules, last updated 26 March 2025) — all Amazon-relationship or status bars, none about grants:
Positive requirement: the PI must be "(1) either a full-time faculty member at an accredited academic institution or a permanent researcher at a non-governmental organization with recognized legal status in its country (equivalent to 501(c)(3) status under the United States Internal Revenue Code) and (2) at or above the age of majority in their jurisdiction of residence at the time of application." Postdocs and PhD students therefore CANNOT be the PI — they are funded as budget lines on a faculty member's proposal. This is the practical gate for early-career people: it is open to newly appointed faculty from day one (no years-since-PhD limit, no prior-award requirement), and closed to anyone not yet in a faculty or permanent-researcher post.
Representations required at submission, verbatim, that the PI:
"(a) is not a paid employee of a government entity (other than an accredited academic institution);
(b) is not under US export controls or sanctions;
(c) has not been a director, officer, employee, intern or contractor of Amazon within the 12 months preceding submission of your proposal to the ARA Program ("Ineligible Personnel");
(d) is not a member of the immediate family or household of Ineligible Personnel; and
(e) has not participated in or had decision-making authority over any cloud infrastructure procurements involving Amazon."
Watch (c) and (e): a recent Amazon internship or contract, or sitting on your university's cloud-procurement committee, is disqualifying where a competing grant would not be.

VOLUME LIMIT (not a funding conflict but the rule people trip on): "Each Principal Investigator is permitted to submit only one proposal to the ARA Program per call for proposal period." A cycle runs 5-8 topic CFPs sharing one deadline, so you must pick ONE call, not shotgun the cycle.
result.program_officer_contact:
No assigned program officer, and pre-submission contact is NOT expected or required.

Programme mailbox: research-awards@amazon.com. The FAQ is candid about its limits: "We provide limited email support via research-awards@amazon.com." The same address is the way to be added to the future-call announcement list, which is the most useful thing an applicant can do between cycles.

No feedback on rejection: "Unfortunately, due to the number of proposals we receive, we are unable to provide detailed reasons a proposal was not accepted."

The nearest thing to a program officer is the OPTIONAL "Amazon contact" — a distinctive and under-used feature. The template has a field "Amazon contact (optional): <Amazon contact name>, <email>". The FAQ defines it: an Amazon contact is "an Amazon employee who is aware of the proposal, familiar with the Principal Investigator's research and may be willing to serve as an Amazon research contact." It is not required, and "all funded proposals receive an Amazon research contact assigned by the review panel." Practical implication for an early-career applicant: you cannot ring a program officer, but you CAN cultivate an Amazon scientist in your area (via conferences, co-authorship, or the Amazon Science publication pages) and name them on the form. Reviewing is done by "an internal awards panel" of Amazon scientists, so a named internal contact who knows the work is the closest available substitute for pre-submission guidance.

After award, contact becomes the point: "Each project receives an Amazon research contact. The researchers are encouraged to maintain regular communication with their Amazon contact to discuss ongoing research and project progress."
result.examples_or_samples:
No funded full proposals or funded abstracts are published. Amazon does not release application text. What IS available, in descending order of usefulness:

1. THE OFFICIAL PROPOSAL TEMPLATE (closest thing to an annotated sample, and downloadable right now between cycles): https://www.amazon.science/_attachment/ara-proposal-template-2025?id=<session-id> — a section-by-section skeleton with inline instructions for each part (Abstract, Keywords, Introduction, Methods, Expected results with milestones, Funds needed, Appendices A/B/C). Drafting straight into this is the single best starting move.

2. FUNDED PROJECT TITLES BY CYCLE, with PI name and institution, in the recipient announcement posts. Format is "Name | Institution | Project title", e.g. "Jonathan Aldrich | Carnegie Mellon University | A Visual Debugger for Program Verification" and "Dalal Alrajeh | Imperial College London | SOLAR: Symbolic Learning for Automated Requirements Consistency" (Fall 2025, 70 awardees across 49 universities in 11 countries, published 27 May 2026). Reading a cycle's title list is the fastest way to calibrate scope and how narrow a fundable project is. https://www.amazon.science/research-awards/latest-news

3. RECIPIENT DIRECTORY, ~915 entries filterable by year 2015-2025 and research area, giving name, institution and topic (no abstracts): https://www.amazon.science/research-awards/recipients — use it to find a funded PI in your own subfield, then read their subsequent papers (ARA recipients are asked to acknowledge ARA support, so the resulting publications are traceable) or approach them directly. A funded peer is the realistic source of a sample proposal, since Amazon publishes none.

4. SUCCESS STORIES, narrative write-ups of what funded projects did: https://www.amazon.science/research-awards/success-stories

5. THE CFP ARCHIVE itself, which is unusually valuable here: every past call page stays live with its full requirements, extra questions, award sizes and dates — so you can read the exact Fall 2025 call to draft against while waiting for Fall 2026 to post. https://www.amazon.science/research-awards/call-for-proposals

Also relevant to the same audience: Amazon runs separate programmes for people who cannot be an ARA PI — the Amazon Postdoctoral Science Program (https://www.amazon.science/postdoctoral-science-program) and Amazon Scholars (https://www.amazon.science/scholars). Postdocs and PhD students should be pointed there, or to a faculty PI's budget line.
result.resubmission_note:
No formal resubmission mechanism and no penalty for reapplying. Awards are one-time and cannot be extended or renewed; the stated route for continuing is a new proposal to a later call — program rules: "you may submit new proposals for subsequent ARA Program calls"; FAQ: this funding "is not extendable," though "applicants can submit new proposals for subsequent calls."

A declined proposal can simply be resubmitted to the next cycle, subject to the one-proposal-per-call limit, but there is no resubmission cover letter, no introduction-to-resubmission page, and no response-to-reviewers step — because there are no reviewer comments: "we are unable to provide detailed reasons a proposal was not accepted." Practically: revise blind, or better, retarget to whichever of the next cycle's topic CFPs fits best, since the call list changes each cycle (Spring 2026 ran 7 calls, Fall 2025 ran 8, and topics such as Automated Reasoning, Sustainability and Robotics come and go).

A previously funded PI reapplying must add Appendix C disclosing the earlier Amazon funding and what it produced — so results from a prior ARA award effectively become part of the new application.

Annual, single cycle per year, anchored to the northern autumn.

- Internal calls posted: late June – mid July (Harvard HMS 30 Jun 2026; Michigan 13 Jul 2026)

result.loi_required: no (Apple side) — but a mandatory university internal nomination competition functions as the pre-proposal stage, and it is the stage that actually eliminates people
result.loi_deadline:
There is no Apple-run LOI. The functional equivalent is the institutional internal competition, which is compulsory because Apple caps each invited university at 3 nominees and "requires each of [the university's] nominees to represent a unique research area" (Purdue packet) — Harvard states the same, "limited to one nominee from these research areas".

Internal deadlines in the 2026 cycle, i.e. how far ahead of Apple's 8 September you actually had to be finished:
- Harvard GSAS: noon, 21 July 2026 (7 weeks early) — CV, 2-page research statement, 1-page confidential advisor letter, as a single PDF to gsasacademicprograms@fas.harvard.edu
- UCL: 23:59, 28 July 2026 (6 weeks early) — via Jotform
- Purdue: 23:59 ET, 31 July 2026 (5.5 weeks early) — via InfoReady, plus a signed Review Panel Commitment Form from the Director of Graduate Programs by the same date
- Michigan: 17:00, 3 August 2026 (5 weeks early) — via InfoReady; "Application materials and recommendation letters will not be accepted beyond the internal deadline"
- Técnico Lisbon: 5 September 2026 (internal, only 3 days before Apple's)

Note the second-order trap: the internal packet is usually SMALLER than the Apple packet (Harvard asks for a 2-page statement internally; Apple wants 4 pages). Harvard warns explicitly: "if you are nominated, the full application -- due on September 8 -- requires additional, more extensive materials than the internal submission." Purdue's nominees get "approximately two weeks" after 21 August to expand the statement and secure a second reference letter.
result.review_to_award:
Long, and longer than the announcement dates suggest.

- Apple's deadline: 8 September 2026
- Outcome to the university: "Apple will then run their own application evaluation process and nominating universities will hear back regarding the status of their students' applications by December 2026" (UCL) — roughly 3 months from submission
- Public announcement of the cohort: the following spring. Apple published the 2025 cohort on 26 March 2025 and the 2026 cohort on 21 April 2026, both on machinelearning.apple.com. Individual notification therefore precedes the public post by ~3–4 months
- Earliest start: **Fall 2027** for the cycle that closed 8 Sep 2026 — ~12 months after submission. Award period is stated as "Fall 2027 to Summer 2029", two academic years

Review is two-phase and partly blinded: "Personally identifiable information is redacted for phase one reviewers" (UCL, describing Apple's specification), which is why applicants are told to keep PII out of the statement body. Inside the university, Purdue's reviewers are departmental faculty who "will have three weeks to score and rank nominee applications using a rubric-survey" and may not sit on the applicant's dissertation committee.
result.submission_requirements:
The student never submits to Apple; the university uploads to Apple's portal. Two packets exist.

APPLE-STAGE PACKET (UCL reproduces it as "in line with Apple's specifications"; Técnico Lisbon and Purdue list the same components):
- Up to 2 of Apple's research areas, ranked primary/secondary
- Research proposal title
- Research abstract, **200 words maximum**
- Student CV and publication list (PDF)
- Research statement, **4 pages maximum including citations, in a legible font size**, "clearly stating the hypothesis and expected contributions to the chosen research area"
- **2 letters of recommendation, one from current advisor, 1 page maximum per letter**, combined into a single PDF
- Link to most recent published work / arXiv (optional)
- PhD advisor name and email; estimated tuition and fees for the academic year
- File-naming convention enforced: "Last name, First name - Research Statement", "- Resume", "- Letters of recommendation"
- Redact birth date, photographs and other PII; "Nomination materials should not contain confidential or proprietary research"

DRIFT WARNING: the research statement was **5 pages** in the Fall-2025-start cycle (Purdue packet, and Purdue's older ECE page: "5 page maximum including citations") and is **4 pages** now. The research-area list was also rewritten this cycle from 12 areas to 13 — the old set (Privacy Preserving ML, Human Centered AI, AI for Ethics and Fairness, AI for Accessibility, AI for Health and Wellness, ML Theory, ML Algorithms and Architectures, Embodied ML, Speech and Natural Language, Computer Vision, Information Retrieval and Knowledge, Data-Centric AI) is the one still shown on the 2026 cohort page; the live set is On-Device and Efficient AI; AI Security, Agent Safety & Assurance; Evaluation, Reliability & Measurement for AI Systems; Computer Use Agents & AI-Assisted Software Development; Human Centered AI; AI Ethics, Inclusion & Social Responsibility; AI for Accessibility; Data-Centric AI; Privacy Preserving ML; AI for Science, Health Signals & Biological/Physical Modeling; ML Theory; ML Algorithms and Architectures; Spatial, Embodied & World-Model AI. Do not write to last year's areas.

INTERNAL-STAGE ADDITIONS (vary by school, and these are the ones people miss):
- A **confidential** letter from the thesis advisor, not shared with the applicant — Michigan flags this as a change: "some changes to the internal application, including a required 1-page confidential letter from thesis advisor(s). Applicants should start drafting their applications early in order to request this letter through the InfoReady platform"
- Purdue: a Review Panel Commitment Form, signed by the Director of Graduate Programs, naming a departmental faculty reviewer — "This form must be emailed to trainee-funding@purdue.edu by the application deadline"; a second reference letter is only requested after internal selection
- Harvard: single combined PDF, confidential letter sent separately
- Institutional sign-off is intrinsic: the nomination itself is the institutional act

REVIEW CRITERIA, in Apple's own words as quoted in Purdue's packet from the non-public official nomination guide: "Nominations are reviewed and selected based on the strength of the research proposal, the impact the nominee has had on the field thus far (both as a researcher and community citizen), and their demonstrated potential as a leader and collaborator in the field"; and for the proposal, "Novelty of the proposal, scientific merit of the proposed approach, potential for impact, and alignment with research areas highlighted by Apple."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
EXCLUDES — one rule, stated verbatim and identically by Michigan, UCL and Purdue: "Nominee must not hold another industry-sponsored full fellowship while they are an Apple Scholar in AI/ML (Fall 2027 to Summer 2029)."

Two limits are doing real work in that sentence: **industry-sponsored**, and **while they are** an Apple Scholar. So the bar is concurrent holding of a competing corporate fellowship during the award window only.

PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — Purdue's nomination packet glosses the same rule in its screening question, and this is the load-bearing half: "Do you/will you hold another industry-sponsored fellowship beginning Fall 2025? **This does not refer to Purdue funding, or funding from government or non-profit agencies.**"

On that gloss, none of the following disqualify you:
- Government fellowships — NSF GRFP, NDSEG, DOE CSGF, NIH training grants
- Non-profit / foundation fellowships
- University or departmental funding, RA/TA support, endowed internal fellowships
- An industry fellowship that has already ended, or ends before the Fall 2027 award start — the clause is about concurrency, not history
Nothing in any source excludes someone for having previously held any award, Apple's own included.

CAVEAT, stated because it matters: the carve-out sentence is a nominating university's paraphrase, not Apple's published words, and Apple's official nomination guide is explicitly not public. A student holding, say, a Google or NVIDIA fellowship overlapping Fall 2027–Summer 2029 should confirm directly — Michigan routes exactly this question: "If you are still uncertain about your eligibility please contact the sponsor directly: aiml_scholars@apple.com."

SEPARATE, NON-FUNDING BARS that disqualify more people than the funding rule does:
- Must be enrolled full time and "expect to be enrolled through the end of the 2028/2029 academic year"; anticipated graduation ~May–August 2029
- "Nominee should be entering their last two to three (2-3) years of study as of Fall 2026" — Harvard adds bluntly, "G1s are not eligible"
- Michigan: "Students attending universities in the United States who are starting the first year of their PhD at the time of nomination may not be nominated. The program is targeted towards mid-to-late career PhD students with an established research and publication record"
- Your institution must be on Apple's invited list; students at non-invited institutions cannot enter at all
- Internally, you compete only against others in your own research area, because each of a university's three nominees must represent a unique area
result.program_officer_contact:
No named program officer. Apple's single published route is a shared mailbox: **aiml_scholars@apple.com** — "For more information, please contact aiml_scholars@apple.com" (Apple's 2026 cohort page). Michigan directs eligibility questions there: "please contact the sponsor directly."

Pre-submission contact with Apple is NOT expected and is not part of the process — this is not an NIH-style programme-officer conversation. Apple deals with universities, not students. UCL is explicit: "The fellowship is run externally by Apple and we are unable to answer questions about the fellowship programme itself beyond what's available on this webpage."

The contact that actually matters to an applicant is their own institution's fellowship or limited-submission office, and pre-submission contact with THEM is essentially mandatory, since they control the internal deadline and the nomination. Real examples, useful as a model for what to look for at your own school:
- Michigan: fellowshipLSO@umich.edu (Office of the VP for Research, limited-submission)
- Purdue: trainee-funding@purdue.edu — staffed by Rachelle Swan, PhD, Trainee Funding Specialist, Office of the Vice Provost for Graduate Students and Postdoctoral Scholars, rachelle@purdue.edu — and they offer a Fellowship Writing Coach
- Harvard: gsasacademicprograms@fas.harvard.edu (submissions), gsas-fwc@fas.harvard.edu (process questions)
- UCL: docschool@ucl.ac.uk
result.examples_or_samples:
No funded application is published, and Apple's own guidance is closed: Purdue quotes Apple's criteria "taken from the official nomination guide, which is not publically available". What does exist, in descending order of usefulness:

1. **Purdue's "Apple Scholars in AI/ML Nomination Application Packet" (9-page PDF, publicly downloadable)** — the single best artefact for someone starting cold. It contains an "Example Layout for Research Statement" with a section-by-section page budget (Introduction ½–1 p; Past Research Projects ½–1 p; Background ½–1 p; Hypothesis 1 para–½ p; Methods and Evaluation 1½–2 p; Expected Contributions 1–2 paras; Relevancy to Apple 1–2 paras; Conclusion optional; References ≤1 p), an "Advisor's Guide for Writing Letter of Recommendation" listing Apple's values for the letter writer, the Review Panel Commitment Form, and Apple's verbatim review criteria. Written for the 5-page cycle, so rescale to 4 pages. URL in source list (tokenised REDCap link — may expire; the same packet is linked from Purdue's InfoReady competition).
2. **Harvard HMS Career Navigator page** — reproduces all 13 of Apple's current research areas with full prose definitions AND sub-topic lists. This is effectively Apple's own rubric text in public, and is what you should mirror keywords from when naming your area.
3. **Apple's cohort pages, 2020–2026** — each scholar listed with institution, research area and a "Read bio". Seven cohorts, 120+ scholars; the closest thing to reading winning abstracts. Cross-read with machinelearning.apple.com/research: Purdue's guide says to "see which keywords and research emphases are ongoing at Apple within your research area category. Incorporate key words and main ideas."
4. **Institutional coaching** — Purdue reviews drafts if emailed to trainee-funding@purdue.edu by 15 July, and runs "Fellowship Help Office Hours", a "Computational Research PhD Fellowships Info Session" and "How to Find and Prepare Fellowship Applications" workshops in June–July. Ask whether your own graduate school runs the equivalent; most limited-submission offices do.
5. Apple's 2026 announcement also names four Spotlight papers co-authored by Scholars during internships (NeurIPS/ICLR/ICML 2025), which shows what the mentorship+internship arm is expected to produce.
result.resubmission_note: Not found. No source — Apple's or any university's — states a resubmission policy, a cap on attempts, or whether prior unsuccessful nomination helps or hurts. Treat any claim about resubmission advantage as unsourced.

LOI close (31 Jul 2026) → LOI outcome (16 Nov 2026) ≈ 3.5 months. Full application close (11 Jan 2027) → interview invitation (7 Apr 2027) ≈ 3 months → interviews (20–21 Apr 2027) → award notification (22 May 2027). Total ≈ 10 months from LOI submission to award notice.

EARLIEST START: on or about 1 August 2027, i.e. ~10 weeks after notification. This is pinned by the funder's own eligibility wording, which defines the award year: applicants may hold no more than $225,000 "at the time of application for either this year (Aug 2026-July 2027) or year one of the BYI award (Aug 2027-July 2028)." So BYI award years run August–July.

Award is 4 years at ~$150,000/yr, but not unconditionally: "contingent upon demonstrated progress after the second year of the award." No indirect costs — "The Foundation does not provide for overhead or for indirect costs," which materially changes what the institution nets versus a federal grant.
result.submission_requirements:
LOI STAGE (all through the SM Apply portal; PDF unless stated, single-spaced, 1-inch margins, 11 pt Arial with 10 pt captions/references OR 12 pt Times New Roman with 11 pt captions/references, 2 MB max per file):

1. Technical pre-proposal — REQUIRED, "4 pages total including all references, diagrams, and drawings (no template)". The page repeats the point because people get it wrong: "the 2027 Program pre-proposal must be no more than four pages, including figures and references." Must carry a title at the top of page 1.
2. Proof of citizenship/permanent residency — required, no page limit. Accepted: valid US passport; OR certified birth certificate AND driver's license; OR permanent resident card (front and back); OR US passport card; OR green card; OR enhanced driver's license (not a REAL ID). Form I-797 holders have a specific carve-out.
3. BYI Biosketch — required, 4 pages max, MANDATORY TEMPLATE from the portal. Not seen by reviewers at LOI stage: "At the LOI stage, this document is not distributed to reviewers. Rather, it is used internally by the Beckman Foundation to determine eligibility."
4. Current Funding chart — required, e-form in the portal. Must list every current grant, direct funding for this year and award year one, AND "the amount of overlap that each grant has with your proposed BYI project."
5. Stop-the-clock / leave documentation — optional, no page limit.
6. Names of three "independent evaluators" — NOT reference letters: "these are not Letters of Recommendation, nor will they be called to review for the current application cycle."
7. Two institutional endorsements — electronic signatures from (a) Chief Academic Officer (President/Chancellor/Provost) and (b) Dean of the College/School/Division. Explicitly "NOT letters of recommendation and no documentation is required to be uploaded."

WHERE THIS DEVIATES FROM THE USUAL NORM — five traps:

A. BLIND REVIEW, ENFORCED BY DISQUALIFICATION. This is the single biggest deviation from NIH/NSF practice. "Failure to follow the guidelines below for blinding your pre-proposal will result in your proposal being deemed ineligible." No name, gender, pronouns, institution, collaborators, mentors, postdoc advisors or lab members anywhere in the pre-proposal. Third person encouraged. Self-citations must carry no asterisk/bold/italic marking, and you must avoid "in our preliminary work" or "my group has shown". Unpublished work is cited as "(Applicant name withheld). Unpublished work, 2026." Filename must not contain your name, initials or institution — "Inclusion of your name, initials, or institution in the file name will render your application administratively ineligible." Reviewers see ONLY the pre-proposal.

B. ENDORSEMENTS ARE A HARD GATE WITH A 14-DAY FUSE. "Your application cannot be submitted until you have received and accepted both Institutional Endorsements." Endorser links "will be valid for 14 days from when you request it," and after each endorsement lands the applicant must return and click "Mark as Complete" — "BOTH endorsements must be received and finalized by the application deadline." FAQ Q14: missing one endorsement means you cannot submit. Request these first, not last.

C. NO SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL AT ALL. FAQ Q22 → "No. Applicants are only permitted to upload the required documentation."

D. ONE PI ONLY. "Only one principal investigator is allowed on the application, but if awarded, grant money can be used to fund collaborations." Portal collaborators can help draft but the application must be submitted under the PI's name.

E. AI-USE DISCLOSURE IS MANDATORY IF USED. "If AI tools are used in producing any parts of your application or in assisting with the writing process, a brief statement describing this use must be included with the references." Conversely, reviewers "are NOT allowed to use or upload your materials into an AI tool."

Also worth knowing: no minimum effort commitment (FAQ Q18 — 5% research time is acceptable); institutions may submit unlimited LOIs; an institution with a currently funded BYI remains eligible; submission is final ("no changes can be made"); write for a multidisciplinary panel — "it is unlikely that the whole committee will be experts in your specific field."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Two SEPARATE and independently disqualifying rules. Applicants routinely miss that the second exists.

RULE 1 — THE $225,000 ANNUALIZED CAP (a test on the person's total funding).
DISQUALIFIES: "Applicants can have no more than $225,000 in direct, annualized external funding grants at the time of application for either this year (Aug 2026-July 2027) or year one of the BYI award (Aug 2027-July 2028)." Tested TWICE — FAQ Q9: "Applicants must have annual funding of no more than $225,000 at the time of the Letter of Intent and Full Application deadlines," and the LOI Instructions add that you remain eligible for the full proposal only if still under the cap. Counting rules that catch people out:
- Co-PI and Co-I money COUNTS. "Please count only the direct funds your lab receives from all PI, Co-PI, and Co-I awards." Being a mere Co-I is not a shelter.
- Signed-but-not-yet-received money COUNTS. "The Foundation defines CURRENT Funding as funds that your lab has received, or funds that your lab will receive after signing a funding agreement."
- Funding that expires partway through the BYI award does NOT rescue you (FAQ Q9A: an award ending one year into BYI still counts → "No").
- Only DIRECT costs count, annualized.

PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the carve-outs — these do NOT count toward the $225k):
- Start-up funds/packages, including large equipment purchases, lab renovations and recruitment money.
- Department-wide instrumentation grants.
- "Transition" grants received as a postdoc, explicitly including NIH K99/R00. FAQ Q10 is unambiguous: an R00 that pushes the total over $225k still leaves you eligible — "Yes. Transition grants (grants received as a postdoc), department wide instrumentation grants, and start-up funds do not count toward the $225,000 annual limit."
- NOTE: all three must still be REPORTED in the funding table — excluded from the count, not from the disclosure.

RULE 2 — PROJECT EXCLUSIVITY (a test on the proposed project, separate from the cap).
DISQUALIFIES: "The BYI program requires that the project be solely funded by the Beckman Foundation." So a project already carried on another award is out even if you are far under $225k.
PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY: "Minimal overlap is allowed." You may have submitted a similar proposal elsewhere (FAQ Q21 answers "Can I still apply?" without a bar), but the Foundation warns "most NIH funding mechanisms would not meet the innovative, novel aims of the BYI program." Per-grant overlap with the BYI project must be declared in the Current Funding table.

BACKGROUND POSTURE: "The BYI program funds promising young scientists early in their careers who have not yet received a major award from another organization. Proposals that already have substantial funding will not be considered."

ADJACENT DISQUALIFIERS that behave like prior-funding conflicts:
- LIFETIME CAP OF TWO ATTEMPTS: "No individual may apply for a Beckman Young Investigator award more than two times (including submitting a Letter of Intent)." An LOI that goes nowhere burns one of only two lifetime shots — so timing the first attempt matters more here than at most funders.
- NIH ESI STATUS DOES NOT HELP. Explicitly non-transferable (FAQ Q6): "The Foundation's requirements for the BYI program do not align with NIH ESI status. You must meet the Foundation's requirements to be eligible." Holding ESI while past 4 years in post or 10 years post-PhD does not preserve eligibility.
- STOP-THE-CLOCK PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY, generously: a full year extension per child added by birth or adoption "regardless of the length of your leave," plus leave for a sick family member, personal illness, or a family move. Leave taken during the POSTDOC also counts, not just as PI. Rule of thumb from FAQ Q2: "If your 'stop-the-clock' event(s) equal at least as much time as you are beyond 4 years, then yes, you are likely eligible to apply."
- Government labs (NIH intramural, federally funded national labs) are ineligible institutions; 501(c)(3) or similar nonprofit with an FEIN required. If your institution does not qualify but has an affiliated Foundation that does, you may list the Foundation instead.
- No clinical research, clinical trials, or single-target drug discovery; those with strictly clinical appointments are ineligible. Social sciences are out of scope.

PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT IS SPLIT — and the split is the useful part:

result.resubmission_note:
HARD LIFETIME CAP OF TWO ATTEMPTS, and an LOI counts as an attempt. Programme page: "No individual may apply for a Beckman Young Investigator award more than two times (including submitting a Letter of Intent)." FAQ Q13 confirms from the other direction: "I still meet the eligibility requirements but have submitted twice. Am I eligible to apply? No. Applicants may only submit a maximum of two letters of intent."

Practical consequence worth flagging to any applicant: because eligibility is capped at 4 years into the appointment, most people get at most 3–4 cycles of eligibility but only 2 permitted submissions — so a speculative early LOI is expensive. No formal resubmission/response-to-reviewers mechanism is described, and no reviewer feedback is mentioned as being returned on an unsuccessful LOI.
unresolved: FUNDER CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE INTERVIEW DATE. The 2027 FAQ (Q8) calls March 16, 2027 the interview: 'official US citizenship or permanent residency documents are required by the BYI Interview (March 16, 2027)', and the programme page's eligibility section repeats that label. But the programme page's own Program Timeline lists '7 Apr 2027 — Applicants notified of Interview' and '20 Apr 2027 / 21 Apr 2027 — Interview Day One / Day Two'. The LOI Instructions resolve it in favour of the timeline by treating March 16 as a DOCUMENT deadline, not the interview: 'you must submit a copy of your United States permanent residency card by March 16, 2027' and 'A copy of your United States permanent resident card must be submitted prior to the BYI Interview'. Most consistent reading: 16 Mar 2027 = citizenship/PR documentation deadline; 20-21 Apr 2027 = interviews. Not stated authoritatively by the funder in one place — an applicant relying on the FAQ alone would mis-date this. Worth a direct question to byi@beckman-foundation.org.

FILE-NAMING INSTRUCTION CONFLICTS BETWEEN SOURCES. The programme web page says: 'Title the document “Proposal” when uploading.' The 2027 LOI Instructions say: 'save file as “pre-proposal”' and 'Name your document “Pre-Proposal”.' Both agree no name/initials/institution may appear in the filename (that part is disqualifying). The 2027 Instructions are the more specific and more recent source, but the discrepancy is unresolved and the stakes are administrative ineligibility.

2028 CYCLE DATES NOT PUBLISHED. As of 2026-09-18 only the 2027 cycle is dated. The June-open/July-close pattern is precedent plus the funder's own 'generally ... June – August timeframe' hedge, not a posted 2028 date. Anyone planning for 2028 should re-check the portal from ~May 2027.

NUMBER OF AWARDS PER CYCLE NOT STATED. The FAQ gives the LOI-to-full-application funnel ('about 100 top candidates advance to the Full Application round') but neither the page nor the FAQ states how many awards are made annually, so an overall success rate cannot be computed from funder sources. It could be derived by counting a recent year in the awardee database, which I did not do.

DEADLINE TIME ZONE STATED INCONSISTENTLY. The LOI Instructions say '5pm PT' on p.1 and '5 PM PST' on p.6; the FAQ (Q24) also says 'PST'. A 31 July deadline falls in Pacific Daylight Time, so 'PST' is loose usage. Treat as 5 p.m. Pacific local and submit early — the funder makes no late exceptions.

FULL-PROPOSAL AND INTERVIEW STAGE REQUIREMENTS NOT ESTABLISHED. All published component/page-limit detail covers the LOI stage only. What the invited full proposal requires (length, budget format, whether reference letters appear at that stage, whether review remains blind) is not on the public pages — it is presumably released in the portal to invited applicants in November. Formal written review criteria for either later stage were not found; the closest public proxy is the prose guidance in the LOI Guidance Document.

TOOLING NOTE, not a finding: beckman-foundation.org returns HTTP 403 to a plain text fetch, so the programme page was read with a rendering browser. The PDFs were retrieved directly (they 302-redirect to website-media.beckman-foundation.org) and parsed locally. NO SEARCH INDEX WAS USED — this session's web-search budget was exhausted before I began, so every claim above comes from the funder's own pages and PDFs, which is the preferred source anyway.

result.deadline_pattern:
Annual, but per programme per fiscal year — there is no single CDMRP-wide date. Each of the ~34 disease programmes issues its own announcement when its congressional appropriation lands, so the family's deadlines are scattered across the calendar (observed FY26 career-stage pre-application dates: PCRP Aug 12, MRP Sept 22, PRP Oct 23). A career-stage mechanism also appears and disappears between fiscal years: BCRP's Era of Hope Scholar Award is not among FY26 BCRP's open mechanisms, and no FY26 mechanism named literally "Career Development Award" was found in any of the six open programmes checked.

Two-step shape, constant across the family: mandatory pre-application (LOI) first, full application 2-3 weeks later (PCRP 3 weeks, MRP 3 weeks, PRP 2 weeks), then a short post-deadline verification window (~6-7 days). Pre-application always at 5:00 p.m. ET; full application always at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Hard rule: "There are no grace periods for deadlines; failure to meet submission deadlines will result in application rejection. The DHACA cannot make allowances/exceptions for submission problems encountered by the applicant." SAM.gov, eBRAP and Grants.gov registration "can take several weeks or longer" and must be active before you start.

Practical watch route: the programme's own funding page (cdmrp.health.mil/funding/<prog>) carries release date, pre-application date and application date for each open mechanism.
result.loi_deadline:
Mandatory, and its role is the opposite of NIH's. Dates above (MRP 2026-09-22; PRP 2026-10-23; PCRP FY26 was 2026-08-12, ~3 weeks before the full application).

Three things that catch applicants out:

1. It is a rejection gate, not a screening gate. Missing pre-application is one of only three grounds for automatic rejection: "The following will result in administrative rejection of the full application: The Project Narrative is missing. The Budget is missing. Pre-application was not submitted."

2. There is no invitation and no triage. "Pre-applications submitted to this funding opportunity are used for program planning purposes only (e.g., reviewer recruitment) and will not be screened" and "CDMRP will NOT provide an invitation to submit a full application after pre-application submission. Applicants are encouraged to develop pre-application and full application components concurrently". So do NOT wait for a reply — build both in parallel.

3. The pre-application issues the key that unlocks the full application: "eBRAP assigns each submission a unique log number. This unique log number is required during the full application submission process" and must be typed into SF424 R&R Block 4a. Identifiers must match exactly across both steps or submission breaks.

Pre-application content is thin — PCRP: "LOI (one-page limit): Provide a brief description of the research to be conducted. Include the FY26 PCRP Overarching Challenge the research will address." PRP EIRA adds a real task at this stage: the LOI must also carry the "List of Individuals Providing Confidential Letters of Recommendation" — "a minimum of two and maximum of three individuals (including the Mentor, if applicable)", who are then emailed by eBRAP. So referees must be lined up by the LOI date, three weeks before their letters are due.

Pre-application goes through eBRAP in every case, by the PI, regardless of where the full application goes.
result.review_to_award: See review_to_award content above.
result.submission_requirements:
Where it deviates from a generic federal application (PCRP EIRA FY26, HT942526PCRPEIRA, read from the PA itself):

SPLIT PORTALS. Pre-application: eBRAP, always, submitted by the PI. Full application: Grants.gov Workspace for extramural organisations; eBRAP only for intramural DoD/DOW. An extramural full application sent through eBRAP is administratively withdrawn. Read alongside the General Application Instructions version CD26_01 (https://ebrap.org/eBRAP/public/gai.htm?version=CD26_01).

PAGE LIMITS — PCRP EIRA: Project Narrative 6 pp; Technical Abstract 1 p; Lay Abstract 1 p; Statement of Work 3 pp; Researcher Development Plan 2 pp; Impact Statement 1 p; Eligibility Statement 1 p; Inclusion of Women and Minorities 4 pp (clinical research only); Transition Plan 1 p; Supporting Documentation no page limit. These vary across the family — PRP EIRA's Project Narrative is 8 pp with a different attachment set (Research Outcomes Plan, Animal Research Plan 5 pp, Sex as a Biological Variable strategy). Check the specific PA; do not reuse a page budget across programmes.

Over-length is silently truncated, not returned: "Pages exceeding the specified limits will be removed prior to reviewing all documents. Documents not requested will be removed."

FILENAMES ARE PRESCRIBED. Each attachment uploads under an exact name — "ProjectNarrative.pdf", "Support.pdf", "TechAbs.pdf", "LayAbs.pdf", "SOW.pdf", "ResearchDev.pdf", "Impact.pdf", "Eligibility.pdf", "Inclusion.pdf", "Transition.pdf", "RequiredReps.pdf". Appendix 1 of the PA is a submission checklist.

NO URLs ANYWHERE except in References Cited and the publications/patents list — a stray link elsewhere is grounds for administrative withdrawal.

INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF IS A SPECIFIC LETTER, not a routine form: "Attachment 8: Eligibility Statement (one-page limit) ... Provide a letter, signed by the PI and the Department Chair, Dean or equivalent official, to verify that the eligibility requirements have been met by the application submission deadline. The letter should provide the date (month/year) the PI completed/will complete requirements for their doctoral degree, and the date (month/year) the PI began/will begin postdoctoral research".

MENTOR/SPONSOR MATERIAL. At least one mentor with prostate-cancer research and mentoring track record; "Letter(s) from the Mentor(s): Provide letter(s) of recommendation from the mentor(s)" plus letters of collaboration and, if military/VA resources are used, a letter "signed by the lowest-ranking person with approval authority". A 2-page Researcher Development Plan is a separate scored attachment. The PI must write the narrative: "The Project Narrative must be written by the PI while also showing evidence of appropriate direction from the mentor(s)."

THE TRAP IN THE PRP VARIANT: confidential letters of recommendation (2-3) are uploaded by the referees directly into eBRAP and are due 2026-11-13 — a week AFTER the 2026-11-06 application deadline. "The PI should monitor whether the letters have been received in eBRAP ... The PI will not be able to view the letters." Referees are named at LOI stage.

ALSO REQUIRED: Research Sharing Plan (named repositories, milestones, rationale for anything withheld); Transition Plan (1 p, named potential industry partners and named follow-on funding opportunities); biosketch and Current/Pending Support per senior/key person; Required Representations; a budget honouring the direct-cost bars — no equipment, no clinical trial costs, and "Salary support for the mentor(s) or any other senior/key personnel except the PI" is not allowed.

AFTER THE DEADLINE: transmission to eBRAP "may take up to 48 hours", then a verification window. "The Project Narrative and Research & Related Budget Form cannot be changed after the application submission deadline. Other application components ... may be changed until the application verification period ends." Verifying in eBRAP is the applicant's job.

SCOPE BARS for EIRA: no clinical trials, no prospective recruitment of human subjects; must address one of the named FY26 Overarching Challenges or it is withdrawn.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES. The headline: CDMRP career-stage awards have NO NIH-style prior-award test. There is no R01-equivalent bar, no dollar threshold, no "must not have held independent funding" clause anywhere in the FY26 PCRP EIRA or PRP EIRA announcements.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES OR GETS YOU WITHDRAWN
1. Career-stage clock, not funding history. PCRP EIRA: "Have three years or less of postdoctoral research experience. Postdoctoral research experience is calculated from the date of doctoral degree conferral to the application submission deadline." Miss it and "The PI does not meet the eligibility criteria" is a withdrawal ground. PRP EIRA instead uses within 10 years of advanced degree or residency training completion.
2. One application per PI per announcement: "An investigator may be named as a PI on a single application to this program announcement. If an investigator is named multiple times as a PI, only the first application received will be accepted; additional applications will be administratively withdrawn."
3. Same project twice in one programme-year: "Submitting applications that propose essentially the same research project to different funding opportunities within the same program and fiscal year is prohibited and will result in administrative withdrawal of the duplicative application(s)."
4. Double-dipping on money: "duplication of funding or accepting funding from more than one source for the same research is prohibited" (CDMRP Directive on Research Duplication, https://cdmrp.health.mil/funding/researchDup).
5. Concurrent career award — but only in the MASA variant, and only at award time: "If recommended for funding, must not have a concurrent career-development-like award at the time this award is made." Note "at the time this award is made", not at application.
6. Mentored status blocks the independent variant: for MASA, "An investigator in a mentored position (e.g., postdoctoral fellow, clinical fellow) at the time of full application submission is NOT considered an independent investigator and is NOT eligible to be named as the PI".
7. Panel entanglement: any involvement of an FY26 programmatic panel member in the application — concept, drafting, budget, or a personal letter of support — is a withdrawal ground. Check the published panel list first (e.g. https://cdmrp.health.mil/pcrp/panels/PCRP%20FY26%20Programmatic%20Panel%20List.pdf).
8. Institutional, not personal: "If there are delinquencies in technical reporting requirements for any existing DHA or U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command awards at the applicant organization, DHACA will not issue any new awards to the applicant organization until all delinquent reports have been submitted." A colleague's late report can block your award.
9. Repeat-mentor bar in MASA: the Career Guide "Must not be the named Career Guide on any previously funded (FY21-FY25) MASA applications."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY
1. Holding other federal or NIH funding does not disqualify you — only funding the SAME research twice does. And in terms: "While it is allowable to propose similar research projects to different programs within the CDMRP or to other organizations..." You disclose via Current/Pending Support; there is no exclusion attached.
2. Clinical training does not burn the postdoc clock: "For physician investigators (M.D., D.O., or equivalent), exclude time spent in clinical residency or clinical fellowship training that is not primarily research focused."
3. Family medical leave does not burn the faculty clock (MASA): "no more than seven years from obtaining their first faculty-level appointment as of the full application submission deadline, excluding time spent on family medical leave."
4. No topic track record needed: "the PI need not have previous prostate cancer research experience."
5. No preliminary data required (PCRP EIRA, MASA, PRP EIRA Level 1). PRP Level 2 does require it.
6. No citizenship or nationality gate: PIs are eligible "regardless of ethnicity, nationality or citizenship status", and foreign organisations may apply.
7. Non-tenure-track is fine (MASA): "May be in a non-tenure track or tenure track position."
8. Narrow carve-out on the panel bar: "Programmatic panel members may provide letters to confirm PI eligibility and access to laboratory space, equipment and other resources necessary for the project if that is part of their regular roles and responsibilities (e.g., as Department Chair)."
9. No cost sharing: "Cost sharing is not an eligibility requirement."

Routes that do exist:

When you do write, quote the version code: "Questions related to this program announcement should refer to the program name, the program announcement name and the program announcement version code CD26_01d".

And there is a hard bar in the other direction — approaching reviewers is a withdrawal offence: "Personnel from applicant or collaborating organizations are found to have contacted persons involved in the review or approval process to gain protected evaluation information or to influence the evaluation process."

So "who to talk to" for this mechanism is: your mentor and prospective Career Guide, your institution's sponsored-programs office (SAM/Grants.gov registration, weeks of lead time), prior awardees in the same programme (named on the programme's awards pages), and the eBRAP help desk for mechanics. Not a program officer.
