result.resubmission_note:
No formal resubmission track, and no penalty for re-applying. The word "resubmission" does not appear anywhere in any of the three FY26 career-stage announcements read in full (PCRP EIRA, PRP EIRA, MRP MASA). There is no A0/A1 designation, no introduction-to-resubmission attachment, no limit on the number of cycles, and no requirement to flag that an application was submitted before.

What does constrain reuse is within-cycle only: the same project may not go to two funding opportunities inside the same programme in the same fiscal year, and one investigator may be PI on only one application per announcement.

Practical consequence: an unfunded applicant re-enters as a fresh application in the next fiscal year's announcement, against that year's Overarching Challenges/Focus Areas (which change annually) — but must still clear the career-stage clock at the new deadline, which is the real limit on how many times a postdoc can try a PCRP EIRA.

Every compliant applicant receives a peer review summary statement of strengths and weaknesses, so there is substantive feedback to revise against even though there is no formal resubmission mechanism.

Suggested value for resubmission_allowed: "yes" (unlimited across fiscal years, no formal resubmission designation), with the within-cycle duplicate bar in resubmission_policy.

result.next_deadline:
DATED ANCHORS FOUND — but there is no single CIRM date, because this mechanism has TWO deadline layers and the one that matters to a predoc/postdoc is set by the host institution, not by CIRM.

LAYER 1 — trainee applies to a host program (this is the layer a PhD student/postdoc acts on). Each of the 18 CIRM Scholars programs "has its own eligibility criteria and application process" (cirm.ca.gov/scholars). Documented dated cycles:
• UC San Francisco (grant EDUC4-12812): applications due "no later than 11:59 pm on September 21, 2025", for an award period "December 1, 2025, through November 30, 2026". Annual.
• UC Santa Cruz: "the standard Application Deadline for that Program Year (i.e August 31st)".
• UC Irvine (grant EDUC4-12822): "June 17, 2024 (11:59 PM)", cohort confirmed by December, program start January 1.
• Gladstone Institutes: "Requests for applications will be announced once a year." Not open as of 2026-09-18.

PATTERN: annual, host-set, closing roughly June–September for a December 1 or January 1 start. A candidate should therefore be talking to a host program director in spring for that year's autumn deadline.

STATUS AS OF 2026-09-18: no 2026 trainee round is posted at UCSF (no Fall 2026 RFA linked from ctp.ucsf.edu) or at Gladstone. UCSC's Aug 31 date would have just passed.

LAYER 2 — CIRM's institutional competition (the university applies; trainees never see this): next competition date NOT FOUND. No current education RFA is published on cirm.ca.gov; the only reachable CIRM education RFA documents are 2008-vintage (see loi_deadline). Relevant signal, flagged as inference not funder statement: the current EDUC4 grants look to be in their final year — UCSC states "Our current CIRM Scholars Program Funding expires in December 2026", UCSF's award period ends November 30 2026, and CIRM's own award record for EDUC4-12822 says it is "currently in Year 4". result.deadline_pattern:

result.loi_deadline:
Trainee layer: no LOI or pre-proposal. Application is direct to the host program (UCSF uses a single Qualtrics form).

Institutional layer: an LOI is REQUIRED and is gating — CIRM's education RFAs state that "Applications will only be accepted from institutions that have submitted a Letter of Intent (LOI) that is accepted by CIRM". LOI falls roughly six to seven weeks before the full application: in both reachable education RFAs the LOI was due "5:00 PM (PDT), July 31, 2008" and the full application "5:00 PM (PDT), September 16, 2008". "Each eligible applicant institution may submit only a single application."

CAVEAT: both RFA documents on cirm.ca.gov (Research Training II, Bridges) are from 2008. The current EDUC4-era RFA was not retrievable, so treat the LOI requirement as CIRM's established practice for education RFAs rather than as confirmed current text.
result.review_to_award:
Trainee layer (the applicant's real timeline): UCSF closes Sept 21 and starts the fellowship Dec 1 — about 10 weeks from submission to start. UC Irvine closes mid-June, confirms the cohort "by December" and starts January 1 — about six months. Neither publishes a named review committee or a notification date; UCSF states only that selection weighs "applicant's previous scholarly record, proposed research, potential translational value".

Institutional layer — this is where CIRM deviates sharply from a federal funder. Review is by CIRM's Grants Working Group (GWG), and an award is not final until CIRM's governing board (the ICOC) approves it in a public meeting. Archived RFA timeline: application mid-September → GWG review "November, 2008" → "ICOC review and approval: Early 2009" → "Earliest funding: Spring, 2009". So roughly two months to review, four to five months to board approval, six to seven months to money. For Bridges, "Fifteen scientists on the GWG together with select specialists with expertise in undergraduate and Master's level educational programs will review the applications."
result.submission_requirements:
THE STRUCTURAL DEVIATION THAT MATTERS MOST: an individual cannot apply to CIRM. CIRM funds California host institutions through an institutional training grant (EDUC4 series, "CIRM Scholars Comprehensive Research Training Program"); the trainee competes for a slot at one of 18 host programs. At UC Irvine the trainee route is explicitly a mentor-initiated NOMINATION — "Nominations are requested for postdoctoral students" / "for pre-doctoral students" — so the mentor, not the candidate, opens the process. Budget time for securing a mentor first.

TRAINEE-LEVEL COMPONENTS (UC Irvine, the most fully documented host):
• Mentor nomination letter, 2-page limit, confirming active participation commitment
• Biosketches for BOTH candidate and mentor, "NIH or CIRM format"
• Career statement from the candidate, under 1 page, confirming willingness to take the required courses
• Research project plan in NIH Specific Aims format — 2 pages for postdoctoral, 1 page for predoctoral applicants
• Mentor's current and pending research funding documentation
• Previous applicants must address prior feedback, 1-page limit
• Completed online application form
Mentor must have active, securely funded research in a stem-cell-related area.

OTHER HOST DEVIATIONS:
• UCSF: applicant must have "at least one remaining year of training in their selected lab as of the fellowship start date."
• Gladstone clinical scholars: "Clinical trainees may not spend more than 25 percent of their appointment time on clinical duties independent of the CIRM training program."
• All programs carry a mandatory training/curriculum load beyond the research — didactic courses on responsible conduct and reproducibility, an ELSI course, monthly seminars, journal clubs, patient-engagement activities and an annual retreat. CIRM states all Scholars "have opportunities to participate in community and patient engagement activities and serve as mentors" — outreach is part of the deal, not optional garnish.

INSTITUTIONAL-LEVEL COMPONENTS (archived education RFAs, 2008): Part A application information form with abstract up to 3000 characters and a separate public abstract up to 3000 characters; Part B program proposal with "Overall Program Design (up to 4 pages)" and remaining sections at 1–2 pages each; Part C host lab summary; Part D biosketches; Part E institutional letter of commitment. One application per institution.

STIPENDS (trainee, for planning): UC Irvine predoc $42,000 stipend + up to $16,000 tuition/fees + up to $2,000 research/travel. UCSC postdoc ~$79,767 salary and benefits + $5,000 health insurance + $12,000 supplies/travel; UCSC predoc ~$44,000 GSR-ship + $9,600 tuition/fees + $6,000 supplies/travel. Gladstone adds $12,000 for core facility and project costs.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, and the preserving half is the headline.

WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (strongly evidenced, three independent host programs):
• NO CITIZENSHIP OR PERMANENT-RESIDENCY REQUIREMENT. UCSF: "There are no citizenship requirements." UC Irvine: "There is no requirement for US citizenship or permanent residency." UC Santa Cruz: "Both U.S. and international postdocs are encouraged to apply", and the same for graduate students. This is the decisive carve-out versus the NIH NRSA family — F31, F32 and T32 slots require US citizenship or permanent residency. For an international predoc or postdoc in California, CIRM Scholars is one of very few substantial mentored training fellowships they can actually hold. Any adviser steering an international trainee away from "training grants" by NIH reflex is giving wrong advice here.
• A PRIOR UNSUCCESSFUL APPLICATION DOES NOT DISQUALIFY — resubmission is structured and expected: "Previous applicants must address prior feedback (1-page limit)".
• NON-BENCH AND NON-BIOLOGY BACKGROUNDS ARE NOT EXCLUDED. CIRM supports "diverse individuals drawn from a wide variety of scientific backgrounds, including fundamental biology, engineering, clinical programs, and other relevant areas like manufacturing process development, data science, bioethics, and more."
• THE MENTOR'S OTHER FUNDING IS AN ASSET, NOT A CONFLICT — the mentor is required to hold active, securely funded research, and must document current and pending support.

WHAT RESTRICTS OR DISQUALIFIES (weaker than an applicant might fear; all host-specific, none funder-wide):
• UC Santa Cruz: "Postdocs currently participating in a training program (i.e. IRACDA) are discouraged from applying due to conflicts with resources provided." Discouraged, not barred, and only at UCSC.
• UC Irvine: "Any supplementation to stipends and fees should come from unrestricted funds." You cannot top up a CIRM stipend from another restricted grant.
• Gladstone clinical scholars: clinical duties independent of the programme capped at 25 percent of appointment time.
• The real gate is career stage, not prior money: UCI postdoctoral nominees must be 1–3 years post-PhD; UCI predoctoral nominees must have completed at least one year of graduate study with 2nd- and 3rd-years prioritised; UCSF requires at least one remaining year of training in the chosen lab at the start date.

NOT FOUND — and do not read the silence as permission: no CIRM-level rule barring concurrent NIH F31/F32/T32 or NSF GRFP support appears in either reachable CIRM education RFA or on any of the six host pages read. NIH's own rules forbid holding an NRSA fellowship and an NRSA training-grant appointment simultaneously, so a candidate holding an F31/F32 must clear the interaction with both the host program and their NIH programme officer before assuming they can stack. Treat as unverified rather than absent.

The chain (RFA §10.1): CPRIT Scientific Review Council scores -> recommended applications go to the Program Integration Committee (PIC) for "review, prioritization, and recommendation" -> CPRIT Oversight Committee approves. "Approval is based on an application receiving a positive vote from at least two-thirds of the members of the Oversight Committee."

Two timing facts that matter operationally and differ from a normal funder norm:
1. There is an EARLY signal before formal approval. Because recruits hold competing offers, "CPRIT's Academic Research program staff will notify the nominating institution of the Scientific Review Council's review decision following the Scientific Review Council meeting." But "No award is final until it has been approved by the Oversight Committee at a public meeting," and if the institution makes an offer in that gap "the institution does so at its own risk. There is no guarantee that the recruitment award will be approved by the Oversight Committee."
2. Notification goes to the NOMINATOR, not the recruit: "Notification of the review decision is sent to the nominator."

Earliest start / award year: FY27 award period is September 1, 2026 – August 31, 2027. The funder warns the award may slip a fiscal year: recommended nominations "may be announced and awarded either in the current fiscal year (prior to August 31, 2027) or in the first quarter of the next fiscal year (starting September 1, 2027)." CPRIT's opportunity listing shows RFT "Award Notification: Continuous" and "Application Review: September 2026 - July 2027."

Post-award clock: "it is expected that the nominating institution provides CPRIT with a status of the award acceptance within 60 days of the award notification." Before funds disburse, the institution must demonstrate matching funds equal to half the CPRIT award (at contract execution and annually thereafter, "not when the application is submitted") and must have a tobacco-free workplace policy.
result.submission_requirements:
THE BIGGEST DEVIATION: the individual cannot apply. This is an institutional nomination. "PIs must be nominated by the president, provost, vice president for research, or appropriate dean of a Texas-based public or private institution of higher education... The application must be submitted on behalf of a specific PI." Only the Authorized Signing Official (ASO) can actually submit. Nominator, ASO, and the Grants Contract/Office of Sponsored Projects Official must each hold a CARS user account. A postdoc's real task is therefore to get a Texas department/dean to nominate them — not to write a submission themselves.

Portal: CPRIT Application Receipt System (CARS), https://CPRITGrants.org. "Only applications submitted through this portal will be considered eligible for evaluation." Migration note: the RFA says "Cycle 27.4 is expected to be the first application cycle in the new system" (new Grant Management Platform), and CPRIT's website says recruitment applications transition to the new GMP "in November" — consistent, since 27.4 opens 11/23/2026. Check which system applies for a 27.3 submission.

Required components with limits (RFA §9.2):
- Summary of Nomination — 2,000 characters
- Layperson's Summary — 2,000 characters
- Summary of Specific Aims and Subaims — 2,000 characters
- Specific Aims and Subaims — CPRIT template provided in CARS
- Institutional Commitment — 3 pages (see prior_funding_conflicts; carries the mandatory K99/R00 clause and a salary-source table)
- Letter of Support from Department Chair — up to 2 pages; must (1) "Describe how the PI will be independent and autonomous in developing his or her research program" and (2) "Present a plan for mentoring that includes the design and execution of a faculty career development plan for the PI"; must also certify the 70% research effort
- Curriculum Vitae — published or "in press" only
- Research — 4 pages, "must be prepared by the PI"
- Publications/References — 1 page
- Research Collaboration/Synergy Plan — 2 pages, PLUS collaborator biographical sketches uploaded "in addition to the 2-page synergy plan"
- Publications — the 3 most significant, as full-text PDFs
- Timeline — 1 page ("If the application is approved for funding, this section will be included in the award contract")
- Current and Pending Support — MUST use the provided "Recruitment - Current and Pending Support" template (.doc and .pdf, posted under the CARS Summary tab). "If the PI has no current or pending funding, a document stating this must be submitted."
- Letters of Recommendation — exactly 3, "from individuals who are in a position to detail the PI's academic and scientific research accomplishments"
- Research Environment — 1 page
- Descriptive Biography — up to 2 pages, "must be prepared by the PI"; becomes public if funded

TRAP that returns an application unread: the Research section must end with a signed verbatim statement — "Applications that do not contain this signed statement will be returned without review." The statement reads: "I understand that I do not need to have made a commitment to <nominating institution> before this application has been submitted. However, I also understand that only 1 Texas institution may nominate me for a CPRIT Recruitment Award, and this is the nomination that I have endorsed. I understand that requests to change the recruiting institution during the recruitment process are not allowed after the application is submitted to CPRIT."

Formatting (IFA §19): Arial 11 pt or Times New Roman 12 pt main text; figure legends Arial 7 pt / TNR 8 pt minimum; single spacing; 8.5 x 11 in; 0.50-inch margins all directions. References must give the full article title and at least the first 3 authors.

Hard administrative gate: "Applications that are missing 1 or more of these components; exceed the specified page, word, or budget limits; or do not meet the eligibility requirements listed above will be administratively withdrawn without review."

Budget rules that deviate from the norm: up to $2,000,000 total costs over 5 years; indirect costs capped at 5% of total award (5.263% of direct); FY27 salary cap $225,000 — but note "Funds from this CPRIT award may not be used for salary support of this PI or to construct or renovate laboratory space." No international travel. Institutional financial commitment to the PI "must equal or exceed 50% of the proposed CPRIT award for the full duration of the award," and "a federal indirect cost rate credit cannot be used to demonstrate an institutional commitment to the PI." Applications from emerging research institutions requesting $1,000,000 or less "will be considered separately." No cap on applications per institution: "No annual limit on the number of grant application submissions per institution has been set at this time."

AI disclosure stance: CPRIT permits AI for "limited aspects of application preparation" but holds "the investigator and the institution... responsible for all content generated by AI."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
The decisive point: for RFT the gate is CAREER STAGE AND APPOINTMENT, not grant history. No prior or current research grant disqualifies an applicant. What disqualifies is already having the job.

WHAT MAKES SOMEONE INELIGIBLE:
- Holding a faculty appointment at or above assistant professor at submission: "At the time of application submission, the PI must not hold an appointment at the rank of assistant professor or above (or equivalent) at an accredited academic institution, for-profit company, health care organization, government agency, or non-profit organization."
- Holding a NON-tenure-track assistant professorship — a frequent and costly surprise for senior postdocs: "PIs holding non-tenure-track appointments at the rank of assistant professor are not eligible for this award. Examples of such appointments include research assistant professor, adjunct research assistant professor, assistant professor (non-tenure track)."
- Accepting the offer too early: "A PI who has accepted a position as a tenure-track assistant professor at the recruiting institution prior to the time that the Scientific Review Council meets to review the recruitment application is not eligible for a recruitment award."
- Being nominated by more than one Texas institution: "A PI may be nominated by only 1 institution."
- Effort/role: PI "must devote at least 70% effort to research activities. PIs whose major responsibilities are clinical care, teaching, or administration are not eligible."
- Resubmission is a permanent bar: "Resubmissions will not be accepted for the RFTTFM Award mechanism. Any nomination for the RFTTFM Award that was previously submitted to CPRIT and reviewed but was not recommended for funding may not be resubmitted." "The decision of the Scientific Review Council not to recommend an application is final."
- Donation and kinship conflicts: ineligible if the institution, nominator, senior/key personnel, officers or directors (or relatives within the second degree) "has not made and will not make a contribution to CPRIT or to any foundation specifically created to benefit CPRIT" cannot be certified; and ineligible if any of them "is related to a CPRIT Oversight Committee member."
- Disclosure duty: applicants must report whether the institution, nominator or substantive contributors "are currently ineligible to receive federal grant funds or have had a grant terminated for cause within 5 years prior to the submission date."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half that is usually missing):
- An NIH K99/R00 career transition award or an investigator-initiated award does NOT disqualify — the RFA anticipates it and PROTECTS its value. The institutional commitment letter must contain this verbatim statement: "This institutional financial commitment will not be offset by funds from a career transition award (K99/R00) or an investigator-initiated award received by the PI. If an award dictates that such funds must be used for salary, the corresponding amount of institutional funds committed to pay the PI's salary will be redirected to allow the PI to use them for program support." So a K99/R00 is additive: the institution cannot shrink its 50% match because the recruit brought money. Reinforced by the rule that CPRIT funds "may not be used for salary support of this PI," so the two awards do not overlap on salary.
- Having NO funding at all is fine: "If the PI has no current or pending funding, a document stating this must be submitted."
- Not yet being in Texas is fine: "The PI may or may not reside in Texas at the time the application is submitted."
- Being nominated by your own current postdoc institution is allowed, with a caution: a PI "may be nominated for a faculty position at the Texas institution where he or she is completing postdoctoral training or at another Texas institution" — but such nominations "that do not clearly demonstrate a subsequent career pathway to independence for the PI will not be looked upon favorably."
- Not having committed to the institution is fine and expected: "It is not necessary that a PI agrees to accept the recruitment offer at the time an application is submitted."
- Non-cancer disciplinary background is fine and actively courted — extra institutional material is "highly encouraged when proposing a PI with exceptional expertise and/or talent that can be directed to cancer research such as a computational biologist, chemist, etc, whose prior experience has not been directly focused on cancer research."
- An administrative rejection is not fatal: "If a nomination was administratively rejected prior to review, it may be resubmitted in the following cycles." A Deferred application pending at fiscal year end "may be resubmitted... Such resubmission will not count against the resubmission limit."
- Future CPRIT funding stays open: the award "is not renewable, although individuals may apply for other future CPRIT funding as appropriate."
- Degree requirement is broad: MD, PhD, DDS, DMD, DrPH, DO, or DVM held at time of submission.
- Note: this RFA "does not allow Coinvestigators," and non-Texas collaborating organizations may participate but "are not eligible to receive CPRIT funds."
result.program_officer_contact:
No named individual program officer is published for this mechanism — CPRIT routes to program mailboxes (RFA §14).

- Scientific and programmatic questions: Research@cprit.texas.gov ("Scientific and programmatic questions should be directed to the CPRIT Academic Research Program. Before contacting CPRIT, please refer to the IFA document and contact the Helpdesk for any items related to CARS, page limitations, formatting, etc.")
- Helpdesk (registration, CARS mechanics, page limits, formatting, uploads): Help@CPRITGrants.org, Tel 866-941-7146, Monday–Friday 8 AM to 6 PM central time; "The Helpdesk will answer queries submitted via email within 1 business day." Helpdesk "staff cannot answer scientific or programmatic questions."

PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT IS NOT THE NORM HERE — AND PART OF IT IS PROHIBITED. Unlike NIH, there is no expectation of courting a program officer about fit, and contact with reviewers is banned: "Communication regarding the substance of a pending application is prohibited between the grant applicant (or someone on the grant applicant's behalf) and the following individuals: an Oversight Committee member, a PIC member, or a Scientific Review Council member." The ban "begins on the first day that grant applications for the particular grant mechanism are accepted by CPRIT and extends until the grant applicant receives notice regarding a final decision," and "Intentional, serious, or frequent violations of this rule may result in the disqualification of the grant applicant." All Scientific Review Council members are non-Texas residents. The only reconsideration route is "limited to an undisclosed conflict of interest."

WHO A CANDIDATE SHOULD ACTUALLY TALK TO: because the institution is the applicant of record, the productive conversation is with the prospective Texas department chair, dean, or VP for research who would nominate you, and with that institution's Office of Sponsored Projects — not with CPRIT. Institutional contact page: https://cprit.texas.gov/about-us/contact-us

PIs are encouraged to refer to and use these templates." These require a CARS account at https://CPRITGrants.org, so in practice the nominating institution's research office pulls them.

NOT available: CPRIT does not publish full funded applications, annotated samples, reviewer summary statements, or score distributions for RFT.
result.resubmission_note:
Effectively one shot per nomination — the strictest resubmission rule among comparable recruitment mechanisms. RFA §8: "Resubmissions will not be accepted for the RFTTFM Award mechanism. Any nomination for the RFTTFM Award that was previously submitted to CPRIT and reviewed but was not recommended for funding may not be resubmitted." Reinforced in §10.1: "The decision of the Scientific Review Council not to recommend an application is final, and such applications may not be resubmitted for a recruitment award."

Two carve-outs preserve a second attempt: (1) "If a nomination was administratively rejected prior to review, it may be resubmitted in the following cycles" — which is why the administrative-withdrawal traps (missing component, over page limit, missing signed single-nomination statement) matter so much; a clean administrative rejection is survivable, a substantive rejection is not. (2) "A Grant Application that is Deferred and pending a final Grant Award recommendation at the end of the state fiscal year may be resubmitted by the Grant Applicant in a subsequent review cycle. Such resubmission will not count against the resubmission limit, if any."

Practical consequence: the institution should not "test the water" with a weak nomination in an early cycle, because a non-recommendation permanently burns that candidate for recruitment awards.

IF YOU ARE ALREADY IN THE 2027 CYCLE (invited at LOI stage): the next live deadline is the invited full proposal, quoted verbatim: "Full proposal due January 11, 2027, 3:00 pm (EST)". Invitation-only — "Only invited applicants can access the full proposal application."

IF YOU ARE A NEW APPLICANT: you cannot enter now. The 2027-cycle LOI closed "August 14, 2026, 3:00 pm (EDT)". The next LOI (2028 cycle) is NOT YET PUBLISHED — this is a verified absence, not a failed fetch: the CASI programme page shows Status "Not Open to Applications", and https://www.bwfund.org/grants/ lists CASI as "Closed" with "Application Deadline: not set" (both retrieved 2026-09-18, direct fetch of the funder's pages, no search index used).

PLAN AGAINST THE PATTERN: the cycle repeats in the same calendar slot, so expect the portal to open on or about 1 June 2027, and the 2028-cycle LOI to fall in mid-August 2027 at 3:00 pm ET. Treat that as a planning pattern, not a published date — re-check the programme page's live Status field before acting.

result.deadline_pattern:
Annual, two-stage, same calendar slot each year. Full cycle as published for 2027 (RFP p.3, verbatim): portal available "On or before June 1, 2026" → LOI "August 14, 2026, 3:00 pm (EDT)" → "Invitation to submit a full proposal By November 13, 2026" → "Full proposal due January 11, 2027, 3:00 pm (EST)" → "Invitation for finalist interview March 22, 2027" → "Finalist interviews April 20-21, 2027" → "Notice of award By June 1, 2027" → "Award start date July 1, 2027" → "New Awardees Convening TBD, September/October 2027" → "Award end date June 30, 2032".

Planner's shorthand: portal opens ~1 June; LOI mid-August; invitations mid-November; invited full proposal mid-January; interviews late April; award start 1 July, running five years.

Hard-cutoff behaviour: "LOIs will not be accepted after 3:00 pm EDT on August 14, 2026. The online application system shuts down automatically at the deadline... NO EXCEPTIONS OR EXTENSIONS WILL BE GRANTED." For the full proposal: "The submit button will disappear after that time."
result.loi_deadline:
REQUIRED, and it is the only door in — full proposals are invitation-only. 2027 cycle: "August 14, 2026, 3:00 pm (EDT)" (now closed). Next cycle's LOI not yet published; expect mid-August 2027 by pattern.

LEAD TIME THAT MATTERS: the LOI sits ~5 months ahead of the full proposal (14 Aug → 11 Jan) and ~10.5 months ahead of money. Invitations land ~3 months after the LOI ("By November 13, 2026").

WHAT THE LOI ACTUALLY IS (lighter than most people expect — mostly a web form, one attachment):
Completed online: title (150 characters with spaces); applicant/PI info (the postdoc is the PI); list of up to five publications; demographics; institutional info; mentor/graduate-advisor/key-personnel contacts; mentor certification; the essay; discipline, biological areas and methodology.
Uploaded as PDF: exactly one item — the confidential recommendation letter from the primary postdoctoral mentor.

The essay: "An essay of no more than 4,000 characters (including spaces) should be entered in the webform field provided." Addressed "to a group of well-educated scientists, who are not necessarily experts in the field." It must cover six points in the RFP's order: the unanswered biological question; the larger objective plus specific aims with some experimental detail; your ability to carry out the work; interdisciplinary and innovation aspects; future career goals and the transition to independence ("Emphasize how your interdisciplinary training positions you to be the one to answer the research question"); and broad impact.

LOI TRAPS:
- The mentor letter gates submission: "The recommendation letter is REQUIRED to submit the application. No late applications will be accepted due to letters not being uploaded by the mentor." BWF asks for it a week early — "at least a week early, August 7, 2026".
- Only one mentor letter is allowed. A second postdoc mentor may co-sign a single joint letter uploaded by the primary mentor; secondary mentors do not submit separately.
- You must supply your GRADUATE ADVISOR's contact details at LOI stage even though their letter is only needed if you are invited. Easy to miss.
- Referees must be contacted at institutional addresses: "The use of personal email accounts is prohibited, unless prior approval has been granted from BWF."
- No extras: "Do not include a cover letter or supplemental materials. If extra materials are included, the LOI will be rejected out of fairness to all candidates."
- No budget at LOI (or at full proposal).
- LOCK-IN AT LOI: "Institutions may not be changed after submitting a LOI. Candidates moving to a new institution after submitting the LOI will not be able to submit a full application, even if invited to do so." Likewise "Mentors may not be changed after submitting a LOI."
- You may unsubmit and edit, but only if the deadline has not passed and BWF has not already routed the LOI to committee.
result.review_to_award:
~10.5 months from LOI to first dollar; ~5 months from invited full proposal to award start. Measured from the 2027 cycle's published dates (RFP p.3):

- LOI due 14 Aug 2026 — month 0.
- Invitation to submit a full proposal, by 13 Nov 2026 — ~3.0 months.
- Invited full proposal due 11 Jan 2027 — ~4.9 months.
- Invitation for finalist interview, 22 Mar 2027 — ~7.3 months.
- Finalist interviews, 20-21 Apr 2027 — ~8.2 months.
- Notice of award, by 1 Jun 2027 — ~9.6 months.
- Award start, 1 Jul 2027 — ~10.6 months. Award end 30 Jun 2032.
- New Awardees Convening: "TBD, September/October 2027".

THREE STAGES, NOT TWO. The RFP is explicit: "Applying for this award is a three-stage process" — LOI, invited full proposal, then interview. The interview is a real gate: "a selected group of applicants will be invited to participate in an approximately 20-minute interview with the CASI Advisory Committee and BWF staff, conducted virtually over Zoom."

WHO DECIDES: "The Interfaces in Science Advisory Committee will review all LOIs, select candidates to invite for submission of full applications, interview finalists, and make recommendations for awards to the BWF Board of Directors." Named external academics, roster published on the programme page (#committee). No study section, no scores, no written critiques at any stage.

CASH FLOW ONCE AWARDED (matters for negotiating a faculty offer): $560,000 over five years, front-loaded to the postdoc phase then the faculty phase — "Year 1: $100,000; Year 2: $100,000" during the postdoc portion (minimum one year, maximum two), then "Year 3: $120,000; Year 4: $120,000; Year 5: $120,000" for the faculty portion. Unspent postdoc balance rolls into the faculty portion if you move in under two years. No-cost extensions of 12-24 months are available, and "Awardees demonstrating adequate progress may be granted no-cost extensions up to the time they are reviewed for tenure."

SUCCESS RATE: BWF publishes none. The only public funnel found is third-party (an awardee's guide, 2017-18 cycle): 287 LOIs → 85 invited full proposals → 23 interviews → 11 awards (~3.8% overall; ~48% once you reach interview). Treat as indicative, not current.
result.submission_requirements:
Portal: ProposalCentral (https://proposalcentral.com) — register via "Need an account?", build a professional profile, attach your institution from the registry (if your institution is absent, Altum support must create it — start weeks out), then Home tab → red "Create New Proposal" → "Filter by Grantmaker" → Burroughs Wellcome Fund → CASI → "Apply Now". ORCID optional but "highly suggested". Work can be saved and reopened.

WHERE CASI DEVIATES FROM THE BWF NORM — check these first:

1. RESEARCH PLAN = 6 PAGES, and the RFP words it two ways. The upload instruction says "no more than six pages, including figures, tables, images, graphs, and references" and "Do not include a table of contents, appendices, or bibliography"; the next bullet says the optional Bibliography (up to four pages) "is not included in the six-page limit for the research plan". Read together: keep everything except the separate bibliography attachment inside six pages. Format: "standard 11- or 12-point font for the text, and no smaller than a 10-point font for figures, legends, and tables. Text must be single-spaced, with one-inch or larger margins on all sides. Number the pages."
   Required content, in the RFP's stated order: (1) scope and significance of your postdoctoral research, highlighting your personal involvement in interdisciplinary work; (2) your work plan for the faculty years; (3) career objectives and how the award helps (including any planned biology coursework); (4) "Why you are the best person to do the work you are proposing."

2. TWO REQUIRED CONFIDENTIAL LETTERS, FROM TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE, AT TWO DIFFERENT STAGES — this is the CASI-specific shape. LOI: primary postdoc mentor (one only; joint letter permitted if co-mentored). Full proposal: "at least one letter of recommendation from the applicant's PhD Advisor is required" — plus one optional third from someone who knows your work. Do not resend the mentor letter; BWF already holds it. If your graduate advisor is unavailable, BWF allows your thesis committee chair or another committee member. FAQ on length: "most letters typically range from 2 to 4 pages". Upload target: "at least a week early, by January 4, 2027".

3. SIGNING OFFICIAL IS REQUIRED ONLY AT FULL-PROPOSAL STAGE (not at LOI) — and it is the classic sinker. From the institution where the postdoc portion occurs (where your mentor is appointed), "an official responsible for sponsored programs (generally from the institution's grants and contract office, office of research, or sponsored program office)". They certify three things: you are eligible, the institution approves submission, and the institution can receive the award. "Applications cannot be submitted without both signatures [applicant + Signing Official]. Signatures must be obtained prior to the application deadline. Extensions will not be given for missing institutional signatures." Adding them grants them administrator access. BWF's own warning: "Lead times for obtaining approval may range from a few days to several weeks. Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact their grants or sponsored research office early."

4. NO BUDGET AT EITHER STAGE — unusual and worth knowing: "an itemized budget and budget justification are not required for the submission of an LOI and full proposal. Consequently, there is no input field or attachment available for submitting these elements." Budget is prepared only after award. "Indirect costs may not be charged against the grants." No tuition or fees.

5. REPRINT CAP IS ABSOLUTE: one required, up to three total, each uploaded as its own PDF. "Only THREE reprints will be allowed. If more are included, the application will be rejected out of fairness to all candidates." Preprints (bioRxiv/arXiv) may be one of the three but "will not count towards fulfilling the requirement to submit at least one reprint."

OTHER FULL-PROPOSAL COMPONENTS: lay abstract 3,000 characters incl. spaces; scientific abstract 3,000 characters incl. spaces; Personal Statement 4,500 characters incl. spaces — and note CASI's framing, "Describe your activities and interests outside of science to give the CASI Advisory Committee a sense of your individuality beyond your scientific accomplishments"; NIH-style biosketch, 5-page limit, "non-fellowship format that excludes scholastic performance"; optional letters of collaboration from up to two collaborators, each with a biosketch (up to five pages), letter "typically not exceeding two pages" — and if included, "the relevant collaborative situations should be described in the six-page research plan". All attachments must be PDF.

CARRY-OVER RULE: "All responses provided on the LOI should remain as is and not be updated" and "Contact BWF staff before changing pre-populated data fields as your eligibility may be impacted."

FINISH SEQUENCE: click "Validate" → "Sign and Print" (type name, click Sign) → "Submit". Nothing is submitted until Submit is clicked; expect a confirmation email. "After the deadline, applicants with incomplete proposals and those not adhering to instructions will be disqualified without prior notice."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, quoted from the 2027 RFP (p.6 "Holding Other Awards", p.4-5 eligibility, p.10 supplemental funds) and the CASI FAQ.

DISQUALIFYING:
- NIH K99: "Candidates must not hold nor have accepted a K99 award from the U.S. National Institutes of Health." The application carries a declaration field for it ("NIH K99 Application: Indicate if you have applied or plan to apply").
- Any other postdoc-to-faculty transition award: "Candidates must not hold nor have accepted a career transition award supporting both a postdoctoral and faculty phase, such as through the HHMI Hannah Gray Fellows program." FAQ restates it as a flat No.
- A tenure-track assistant professorship held OR accepted, "either in writing or verbally", at any point — "both LOI, full application, and interview. This award cannot be made to a tenure-track faculty member because it is a transition award." If you accept one after the interview, "the candidate may not start the new position until after the start date of the award."
- Any role that already makes you independent: "candidates are ineligible if they currently hold a position type (e.g., early independence; probationary tenure-track-like role) that permits them to function as an independent investigator in a role analogous to that of an assistant professor."
- Concurrent BWF awards: "Candidates may not hold concurrent BWF awards." Post-award this hardens to "Award recipients may not hold concurrent BWF awards or NIH K99/R00 awards."

PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half most applicants never find:
- **NIH K01 is explicitly compatible, with a funding split**: "Candidates with a K01 award from the NIH may apply for this award as long as they meet all the remaining criteria, however, if granted a CASI award, the NIH will need to fund the postdoc portion and BWF will only fund the faculty portion of the award." This is the single most valuable carve-out in the mechanism.
- **Having applied for a K99 and not been funded does not bar you.** The bar is holding or accepting one; applying is a disclosure, not a disqualification. (FAQ; and the portal asks you to declare it.)
- **You may run a CASI LOI alongside another BWF competition**: "Candidates are permitted to submit an LOI and/or application for other BWF competitive programs simultaneously. If a candidate is selected as a finalist for both awards, they will need to decide which award to accept."
- **NIH intramural and HHMI Janelia postdocs may apply** — a named exception to the federal-facility ban: "Candidates may apply from the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH) or HHMI's Janelia Research Campus. The NIH/HHMI will support these award recipients during the postdoctoral years. With the exception of eligible postdoctoral fellows at the NIH, LOIs will not be accepted from federal facilities."
- **Stacking other funding after award is fine**: "Award recipients may obtain funds from other sources for research in the same or similar areas as that conducted under these grants, so long as there is no conflict with meeting the terms of BWF's award."
- Nothing in the RFP or FAQ excludes K08, K23, DP5, NSF or other standard fellowships — only K99/R00 and dual-phase transition awards are named. Absence of a named bar is not a grant of permission: if your award has a faculty phase, ask casi@bwfund.org before the LOI deadline.

THE REAL LIMIT IS THE CLOCK, NOT A COUNTER. Eligibility window: "at least 12 months but not more than 60 months of postdoctoral research by the date of the full invited application deadline", and "Post-PhD work experience in any scientific research field (including outside academia) cannot exceed 60 months." For the 2027 cycle BWF spelled the window out: "generally the applicant would need to have received their doctoral degree no earlier than January 11, 2022, and no later than January 11, 2026." Two written carve-outs: non-science time in the post-PhD timeline may be excluded but "must gain prior approval from the BWF program officer. No exceptions to this requirement will be made"; and "Parental or other well-justified family/medical/military leave does not count against the 60-month clock. An automatic 1-year extension will be granted for the birth or adoption of a child." Submitting outside the window without written prior approval is fatal: "their application will be considered ineligible for review."

ALSO GATING (non-funding): PhD must be in mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer science, statistics or engineering — a biology-side PhD needs a pre-approved exception (see officer field). MD alone is ineligible; MD/PhD qualifies if the PhD is in a qualifying field. At least one first-author peer-reviewed publication (shared first authorship counts; accepted/in press counts; preprints do not). Must be at a US/Canadian 501(c)(3) or equivalent. Citizens, permanent residents and temporary residents legally qualified to work in the US/Canada, with named visa classes (J-1, H1B, F-1, O-1; Canadian Study Permit, C-43, C-44, C-10, C-20). Primary postdoc mentor must hold an appointment at the same institution as you. If awarded, ≥75% time on research-related activities.
result.program_officer_contact:
NAMED, PUBLISHED, AND FOR CASI THERE ARE TWO SITUATIONS WHERE CONTACT IS MANDATORY.

Route in priority order:
- Programme mailbox first: casi@bwfund.org — "For eligibility and programmatic questions related to the Career Awards at the Scientific Interface, please contact casi@bwfund.org."
- Program Officer: Dr. Tammy Collins — tcollins@bwfund.org, 919-991-5120.
- Program Associate: Eliza Gary — egary@bwfund.org, 919-991-5107.
- Program Coordinator: Lama Haidar — lhaidar@bwfund.org, 919-991-5115 (award management, progress and financial reporting).
- Portal/software problems go to Altum, never BWF: pcsupport@altum.com, 1-800-875-2562, "8:30am to 5:00 pm ET, Monday - Friday except holidays".

IS PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT EXPECTED? No — and this is the sharpest contrast with NIH practice. There is no "does my aim fit your portfolio" call, and no post-decision debrief, because there are no critiques. FAQ: "It is the responsibility of applicants to read the published Request for Proposals guidelines and FAQs to determine eligibility" and "Please do not contact BWF to ask if we can make an exception to clearly stated guidelines."

BUT CONTACT IS MANDATORY IN THESE CASES, AND SKIPPING IT VOIDS THE APPLICATION:
1. Biology-side PhD: "Candidates whose PhD is in a biological field must have this exception approved by the BWF Program Officer before applying. No exceptions to this requirement will be made." (Eligible if you can show real competence in maths/physics/chemistry/CS/statistics/engineering via papers, advanced coursework or undergraduate major, and the proposal draws on it.)
2. Outside the 12-60 month postdoc window because part of your post-PhD time was not in science research: you "may be eligible but must gain prior approval from the BWF program officer. No exceptions to this requirement will be made." The portal has a field for the date that approval was granted plus a brief explanation.
Also requiring prior approval: using a referee's personal rather than institutional email, and changing any pre-populated field between LOI and full proposal ("Contact BWF staff before changing pre-populated data fields as your eligibility may be impacted").

WHEN: before the LOI deadline, without exception — "Candidates with questions about their eligibility must contact BWF in advance of the LOI application deadline. BWF will make no exceptions to its policies."

WHAT TO ASK ABOUT: narrow eligibility-window questions — degree field, the 60-month clock, visa class, institutional status, interaction with an existing award. Not whether an idea is fundable; BWF routes that question to the published selection criteria, the Advisory Committee roster and its own webinar instead.
result.examples_or_samples:
There is no BWF sample-application library, no public abstract database and no summary statements — "BWF does not provide critiques of unfunded proposals." What exists, best first:

1. THE FUNDER'S OWN HOW-TO WEBINAR — the best single starting point, and most applicants miss it because it is only linked from inside the RFP: "Career Awards at the Scientific Interface – Tips for Writing a Successful Application - A recording of Dr. Tammy Collins, Program Officer, providing an overview of the CASI grant award and the application process." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rifIr2iJEVc
2. PAST CASI GRANT RECIPIENTS — https://www.bwfund.org/funding-opportunities/interfaces-in-science/career-awards-at-the-scientific-interface/grant-recipients/ — cohorts 2012-2026 with name, institution and project title (titles only, no abstracts); roughly 9-12 awardees a year (2026: 12; 2025: 10; 2024: 12; 2023: 9). Example entries: "Green Ahn, Ph.D.", University of Washington, "Leveraging de novo protein design to remodel the cell-surface proteome"; "Juncal Arbelaiz, Ph.D.", Princeton University, "From anatomical to functional connectomics: a control-theoretic framework to investigate how brain structure relates to brain function and dysfunction". Use it to calibrate scope and to find someone in your field to ask for their funded application — the cohort is small enough that recipients are findable and are routinely approached this way.
3. THE CASI ADVISORY COMMITTEE ROSTER — https://www.bwfund.org/grants/interfaces-in-science/career-awards-at-the-scientific-interface/#committee — these are your actual reviewers and interviewers. Reading their fields is the practical substitute for a programme-officer fit conversation.
4. THE PUBLISHED SELECTION CRITERIA (RFP p.8) — effectively the scoring rubric, in three blocks: Project Plan (importance of the biological question and innovation of approach — "Candidates should present clear evidence of already beginning to tackle a biological problem"; interdisciplinarity and degree to which non-biological methods are integrated; potential for large impact); Investigator (depth and rigour of training in a discipline other than biology; productivity during the postdoc; quality of collaborations, recommendations and personal statement); and Impact of person on the BWF CASI community. Two stated priority areas worth naming explicitly if they fit: "Proposals that include deep or machine learning applications of artificial intelligence are particularly encouraged. Special consideration will also be given to proposals that investigate the connection between climate change and human health."
5. AWARDEE PROFILES AND THE "FOCUS IN SOUND" PODCAST — https://www.bwfund.org/awardee-profiles/ — awardees describing funded work in their own words, organised by programme including CASI (e.g. 2018 CASI awardee Markita Landry, UC Berkeley, on functionalising nanoparticles for imaging and gene editing). Closest thing to "what a funded person actually proposed".
6. THIRD-PARTY WALK-THROUGH (verified to exist this session; cycle-specific details are from 2017-18 and may be stale): Calin Plesa, "Guide to the BWF CASI application process", https://www.calinplesa.com/guide-to-the-bwf-casi-application-process/ — gives the 287 → 85 → 23 → 11 funnel, a section-by-section page budget for the six-page research plan (≈1 page background, 2.5 pages postdoctoral scope and significance, 1 page faculty-phase plan, 0.5 page career objectives, 0.5 page competitive advantage, 0.25 page conclusion), and interview mechanics (author reports five slides maximum, a five-minute presentation then ~fifteen minutes of questions — the current RFP says only "approximately 20-minute interview... conducted virtually over Zoom", so treat the slide format as unconfirmed for 2027). He does not post the documents themselves.
7. Also linked from the RFP: the CASI FAQ, and BWF's Direct and Indirect Costs Policy (https://www.bwfund.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/BWF_Direct_Indirect_Costs_PolicyDocument_2026_v4.pdf).

Not verified this session (web-search budget was exhausted, so I could not confirm it): the IRS Form 990-PF route via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer for an exhaustive grantee/amount list. Flagging rather than asserting.
result.resubmission_note:
No resubmission mechanism in the NIH sense — no A1, no resubmission track, no introduction page, no response to reviewers, because there is nothing to respond to. RFP p.8: "Candidates not selected may reapply in the next award cycle, provided they meet the eligibility requirements. BWF does not provide critiques of unfunded proposals." Re-entry is simply a brand-new application in a later cycle: "Candidates can re-apply in subsequent years as long as they remain eligible."

No cap on attempts is stated for CASI, and one application per cycle: "Candidates may not submit more than one CASI LOI per application cycle."

The binding constraint is therefore the eligibility clock, not an attempt counter: the 12-60 month postdoctoral window (measured at the full-proposal deadline) plus the bar on holding or having accepted a tenure-track assistant professorship. In practice that allows a small number of attempts before ageing out — with zero feedback in between. Since BWF issues no critiques and no scores, the only substitutes for a summary statement are peer review of your own draft, the published selection criteria, the Advisory Committee roster and the programme officer's recorded webinar.

Within a cycle you may unsubmit and edit, but only if the deadline has not passed and BWF has not already routed the application to committee. Two irreversible lock-ins at LOI: institution and mentor cannot change afterwards, and moving institutions after the LOI ends the application even if you are invited.

result.review_to_award:
Long by career-award standards: ~11 months from submission to first dollar, and ~8 months to any binding news. All dates from the RFP key-dates table, corroborated by the programme page.

- Sep 30, 2026 — full proposal submitted (month 0)
- Jan 20, 2027 — "Notice of Application Status" (~3.7 months). This is the cut; most applicants learn nothing more.
- Mar 9-10, 2027 — "Finalist Interviews" (~5.3 months), before the CAMS Advisory Committee
- May 28, 2027 — "Notice of Award" (~8 months)
- Sep 1, 2027 — Award Start Date (~11 months)
- Aug 31, 2032 — Award End Date (5-year term)

Deviations from the funder norm worth planning around:
1. The Sep 1 start is the LATEST start-to-deadline gap of BWF's career programmes (CASI and PATH start Jul 1; NGPI Oct 1), so the gap between submitting and being paid spans a full academic year. Anyone using CAMS to bridge a fellowship-to-faculty transition has to survive ~11 months on other funds.
2. Decision-making is a named, published advisory committee, not a study section: "The CAMS Advisory Committee will review proposals, interview finalists and make CAMS award recommendations subject to approval by BWF's Board of Directors." There are no scores, no percentiles, no summary statements and no written critique at any stage — "BWF does not provide critiques or written comments of unfunded proposals."
3. Institutional mobility is frozen during review: "The institution for the proposal may not be changed."
4. Selectivity, stated by BWF on the programme page for the most recent completed cycle: "Based on the number of eligible applicants in the 2025-2026 cycle (156) and awards given (12), the funding rate was 7.7 percent." NOTE FOR THE CORPUS: the existing CSV row carries "~12% success rate (funder-reported historical)" — the funder's current published figure is 7.7%, so that cell is stale.
result.submission_requirements:
Submitted through ProposalCentral (Altum). All attachments must be PDF. Where CAMS DEVIATES from the BWF-wide norm is flagged.

RESEARCH PLAN — 6 pages: "Research Plan (PDF upload; 6-page limit including figures, tables, images, graphs. Bibliography/References list not included in page count.)" Formatting is prescriptive: "Use Times New Roman 11-point font for all text, and no smaller than a 9-point font for figures, legends, and tables. Text must be single-spaced, with one inch or larger margins on all sides. Page numbers for the research plan are required. Do NOT include a table of contents or appendices." (DEVIATION: PATH is 5 pages with half-inch margins; PDEP is 3 pages including references. Do not reuse a sibling programme's page budget.)

BIOSKETCH — "NIH-style Biosketch (PDF upload, 5-page limit, Times New Roman 11-point font, 0.5in margins)." SciENcv is NOT required: "BWF asks that you submit an NIH-style biosketch, but it is not a requirement to make and certify the biosketch in SciENcv."

CHARACTER-LIMITED NARRATIVES (these are character, not page, limits):
- Lay Abstract — 3,000 characters including spaces
- Scientific Abstract — 3,000 characters including spaces
- Personal Statement — 3,000 characters including spaces. CAMS-SPECIFIC AND COUNTERINTUITIVE: "This statement should describe your motivations, activities, and/or interests outside of science. This statement is intended to give the CAMS Advisory Committee a sense of who you are, NOT to reshare your scientific accomplishments."
- Career Development Plan — 6,000 characters including spaces, describing "the anticipated steps to becoming an independent investigator" and "how you anticipate the BWF CAMS award aiding in achieving that goal."

FOUR CONFIDENTIAL LETTERS (more than any BWF sibling — CASI needs one at LOI, PDEP one): "Four recommendation letters are required: one letter from the applicant's sponsor/mentor, and three additional letters from individuals who know the applicant and their work well." Only one mentor letter is permitted; co-mentors may co-sign one letter, or a co-mentor may instead write one of the three others. Mechanics: add all four under "Mentor and Key Personnel" (roles "Mentor" and "Recommender"), then request each letter by email from the "Request Recommender/Graduate Advisor Letter" section; referees upload directly. "Applications cannot be submitted without the required letters." Target date: "It is recommended all letters of recommendation are uploaded by September 20, 2026."

INSTITUTIONAL SIGNING OFFICIAL — the classic sinker. A web-form signature from "an official responsible for sponsored programs (generally from the institution's grants and contract's office, office of research, or sponsored program's office)". Adding them grants them administrator (edit and submit) access automatically. They must personally log into ProposalCentral, open the proposal, go to Sign and Print and sign BEFORE the deadline. "Applications cannot be submitted without both signatures. Signatures must be obtained prior to the application deadline. Extensions will not be given for missing institutional signatures." The Signing Official certifies eligibility, institutional approval, and that the institution can receive the award. If applicable they must also "verify candidate's immigration status as part of the application."

BUDGET IS REQUIRED — DEVIATION: "Complete the budget and justification that explains how this research grant will be spent annually." (CASI requires no budget at all until after award.) No indirect costs may be charged. Internal caps: postdoc phase max $80,000 salary + $11,000 fringe in year 1, $85,000 + $11,000 in year 2; faculty phase max $59,500/yr salary and fringe combined; up to $5,000/yr may go to caregiving expenses; equipment >$50,000/yr or travel >$15,000/yr needs written BWF authorization.

PUBLICATIONS — HARD DISQUALIFIER: up to three reprints, each uploaded as its own PDF. "Only THREE reprints will be allowed. If more than three are listed and/or are uploaded as a combined PDF, your application will be ruled ineligible for review." Preprints (bioRxiv/arXiv) count as one of the three; "accepted with revisions" is permitted.

IRS DETERMINATION LETTER — "Upload a copy of the institution's most recent IRS determination letter that indicates the institution is recognized as a 501(c)(3) organization. Applicants from Canadian institutions should include a US IRS letter." Obtain from your research office; allow lead time.

NOTHING EXTRA: "Do not include a cover letter or supplemental materials. If extra materials are included, the application will be rejected out of fairness to all applicants." And: "After the deadline, applicants with incomplete proposals and those not adhering to instructions will be disqualified without prior notice." Use the "Validate" link before submitting; submission is not complete until the blue SUBMIT button is clicked and a confirmation email arrives.

ORCID optional but recommended. Project work may be saved and reopened repeatedly before submission.

TRAP TO AVOID: the "CAMS Sponsor Letter Fillable Form" PDF linked from the programme page (https://www.bwfund.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/CAMS-Sponsor-Letter_Fillable-Form.pdf) is NOT an application component. I extracted it: it is the "Sponsor's Annual Letter of Evaluation", a POST-AWARD progress-reporting form for existing awardees ("Progress reports must be received by November 1 or the awardee's payments will be delayed"). Applicants should not send it to their mentor.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, verbatim. The decisive point: CAMS is blocked by INDEPENDENCE-CONFERRING awards, not by mentored ones — the opposite of the reflex most K-award applicants bring from NIH.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU:
- RFP, eligibility requirements: "Candidates who hold non-tenure track faculty appointments and have been awarded an NIH R01 or Early Independence Investigator award(s), including NIH K99/R00 or NIH DP5 award, are ineligible." Note the scope: this clause is written for candidates who ALREADY hold a non-tenure-track faculty appointment, and it names the R01 explicitly. (NEW RELATIVE TO THE EXISTING CSV ROW, which lists only K99/R00 and DP5 — the R01 limb is not captured there.)
- FAQ, asked directly about K99/R00 eligibility: "No."
- RFP, terms of grant: "Award recipients may not concurrently hold other BWF awards, NIH DP5 or NIH K99/R00 awards."
- FAQ, general concurrency: "Award recipients may not hold concurrent BWF awards or NIH K99/R00, NIH DP5, or similar Early Independence awards." — "or similar" is doing real work; a non-NIH independence award may be read across.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES YOUR ELIGIBILITY:
- Mentored K awards are fine. FAQ: "Yes. Applicants are allowed to hold a National Institutes of Health K series award (except K99/R00) as long as there is no significant overlap in research aims or conflict with meeting the terms of BWF's award." This covers K08, K12, K21 and K23 — the standard physician-scientist path — and is the single most useful sentence in the FAQ for this audience.
- A PENDING K99 or DP5 application does not block you. FAQ, on applying while a K99/DP5 is in play: "Yes. However, awardees cannot receive funding simultaneously from both a K99 or DP5 and a CAMS award." So you may run both competitions in parallel and choose later; only simultaneous receipt is barred.
- Other research funding is fine. RFP: "Award recipients may obtain funds from other sources for research in the same or similar areas as that conducted under these grants. There should be no significant overlap in research aim(s) and no conflict with meeting the terms of BWF's award."
- NIH intramural postdocs may apply, and transition out to an eligible U.S./Canada institution for the faculty phase to draw the full award.
- You may hold a junior faculty title and still qualify: "Candidates who hold a junior faculty appointment (Lecturer, Clinical Lecturer, Assistant Professor nontenure track, etc.) may be eligible and are required to determine eligibility via the eligibility check quiz prior to applying."

THE REAL BINDING GATE IS CAREER STAGE, NOT GRANT HISTORY. Two independent tripwires, both in the RFP:
1. "At the time of application, candidates cannot hold nor have accepted, either in writing or verbally, a faculty appointment as a tenure track Assistant Professor." A verbal yes counts. 
2. "Candidates holding a junior faculty appointment with substantial institutional start up packages are also ineligible. A substantial institutional start up package is determined based on the terms of candidates offer letter." (BWF's FAQ frames substantial as a package over ~$500K and/or including independent lab space; exceptions are rare and must be argued to cams@bwfund.org by the eligibility-check deadline.)

Other non-funding bars to check in the same pass: degree must be M.D., D.D.S., D.V.M., V.M.D. or D.O. (PhD-only, PharmD and PharmD/PhD are ineligible — CASI is the analogue for those); clinical training complete and board-eligible by the award start date; at least 75% research effort; U.S./Canada citizen, permanent or temporary resident legally qualified to work, temporary residents holding J-1, H1B, F-1 or O-1 (U.S.) or Study Permit / C-43 / C-44 / C-10 / C-20 (Canada); primary mentor must hold an appointment at the same institution as the applicant; health services research and large-scale clinical trials are out of scope.

2. Startup-package exception for a junior-faculty candidate — argued to cams@bwfund.org, also by the eligibility-check deadline, and granted rarely.

BOTH WINDOWS ARE NOW SHUT FOR THE OPEN CYCLE: "BWF recommends completing the eligibility check by September 15, 3:00pm EDT. Beyond this date, BWF will not be responding to eligibility inquiries." That date passed on 2026-09-15; today is 2026-09-18. There is no BWF equivalent of the NIH "is my aim a fit for your portfolio" call, and no post-decision debrief, because no critiques are issued. The fit conversation happens through three public channels instead: the RFP's own selection criteria (Project Plan: innovation and appropriateness of methods, significance of the biological questions, potential for large impact, creative and original approaches; Investigator: scientific experience, potential for independence and career development plan, strong publication history, positive reference letters and personal statement; plus "Impact of the Investigator on the BWF CAMS Community"); the published CAMS Advisory Committee roster, which names your actual reviewers; and BWF's recorded CAMS webinar with PO Dr. Paige Cooper Byas, linked from the programme page (the page notes the recording is from an earlier cycle, so treat its dates as stale).
result.examples_or_samples:
No BWF RePORTER, no public abstract database, no summary statements, and no BWF-published sample CAMS applications. What actually exists, most useful first:

1. GRANT RECIPIENTS SECTION on the CAMS programme page — the best starting point. Fifteen cohorts, 2012 through 2026, each awardee listed with name and degree(s), institution, and project title. Titles only; I confirmed no abstracts are published. Use it to find someone in your subfield, ideally at your own or a peer institution.
2. AWARDEE PROFILES — https://www.bwfund.org/awardee-profiles/ — narrative profiles and "FOCUS in Sound" podcast transcripts in which awardees describe their funded work in their own words, covering CAMS, CASI, PDEP and CAST. CAMS example confirmed live: Alice Chen-Plotkin, MD, at /awardee-profiles/2018-alice-chen-plotkin-md/. This is the closest published thing to "what a funded CAMS person actually proposed", though still not an application.
3. CAMS ADVISORY COMMITTEE ROSTER, linked from the RFP as "CAMS Advisory Committee Members" — your named reviewers. Reading their fields is the practical substitute for a programme-officer fit conversation, since BWF offers none.
4. PAST CAMS AWARD RECIPIENTS, linked from the RFP alongside the FAQ and advisory committee links.
5. BWF NEWS (https://www.bwfund.org/news/) and ANNUAL REPORTS (https://www.bwfund.org/about/annual-report/) — cohort announcements with names, institutions, titles and amounts; programme narratives and summarized financials.
6. THE ODDS, stated by BWF itself on the programme page: "Based on the number of eligible applicants in the 2025-2026 cycle (156) and awards given (12), the funding rate was 7.7 percent." This is the only CAMS funnel number BWF publishes, and it supersedes the ~12% figure currently in the corpus row.
7. WHAT PEOPLE ACTUALLY DO: ask a past recipient for their funded application. Twelve awards a year makes recipients findable and they are routinely approached. Many university research-development offices also keep local copies of successful BWF applications — ask yours before assuming none exist.

CAUTION ON CROSS-PROGRAMME GUIDANCE: the one detailed public walk-through of a successful BWF application that circulates (Calin Plesa's guide) is for CASI, not CAMS. CASI is two-stage with an LOI, a different page budget and no budget document; its advice does not map onto a single-stage 6-page CAMS submission with four letters and a required budget. I did not independently verify that guide in this run. Likewise the ProPublica Form 990-PF route (EIN 23-7225395) for exhaustive grants-paid data was not verified in this run.
result.resubmission_note:
Unlimited reapplication, zero feedback. There is no resubmission mechanism in the NIH sense — no A1, no resubmission track, no introduction page, no response to reviewers — because nothing is issued to respond to.

RFP, selection process: "BWF does not provide critiques or written comments of unfunded proposals." and "Provided they continue to meet the eligibility requirements, candidates who are not selected for interview or final award may reapply in a future cycle(s)."

FAQ, the only place a count is stated: "BWF does not currently have a cap on reapplying. As long as a candidate remains eligible, they can reapply in a future cycle(s) an unlimited number of times."

So the real limit is not a resubmission counter, it is the ELIGIBILITY WINDOW. CAMS has hard career-stage gates — no accepted tenure-track Assistant Professorship (verbal offers count), no junior faculty post with a substantial startup package, no R01 or Early Independence award for non-tenure-track faculty holders. Applicants typically age out after one to three attempts, and receive no feedback between them. Peer review of your own draft, the RFP's published selection criteria, and the named Advisory Committee roster are the only substitutes for a summary statement.

WITHIN A SINGLE CYCLE: FAQ — "You can submit only one application per cycle." You may apply simultaneously to another BWF programme if you meet its criteria, but awardees may not hold more than one BWF award at once, so a double finalist must choose. You may edit and re-save the application repeatedly before the deadline ("The application may be accessed and changed multiple times as needed prior to submission"), but nothing changes after it: the SUBMIT button greys out at 3:00 p.m. EDT and "will NOT be reactivated". Your institution is locked for the cycle — "The institution for the proposal may not be changed."
result.deadline_pattern:
Annual, single-stage, one round per year, anchored to the last week of September. For the open 2027 cycle: portal opened July 1, 2026 → eligibility check September 15, 2026 (3:00 p.m. EDT) → full proposal September 30, 2026 (3:00 p.m. EDT) → status January 20, 2027 → interviews March 9-10, 2027 → award notice May 28, 2027 → start September 1, 2027 → end August 31, 2032.

So the planning rhythm is: portal opens ~July 1, eligibility quiz ~mid-September, proposal ~end of September, decision ~8 months later, money ~11 months later. Working backwards from a late-September deadline, a first-time applicant should start the ProposalCentral account, the institution registration, the Signing Official conversation and the four referees in July, not September.

Every deadline is 3:00 p.m. Eastern on a named date and is enforced by the portal, not by staff. Next-cycle (2028) dates are not yet published; re-check the live "Status" field on the programme page and the Grant Status filter at https://www.bwfund.org/grants/ before acting. Note that BWF's dedicated /upcoming-deadlines/ page is less complete than the individual programme pages, so trust the programme page.

The RFP bars those who 'have been awarded' an R01; it is silent on pending applications, and the FAQ's parallel carve-out for pending K99/DP5 applications is not repeated for the R01.

Whether any funded CAMS application text, successful abstract or annotated sample exists publicly anywhere. None found on bwfund.org; recipient titles and narrative awardee profiles are the closest published artefacts.
