result.loi_deadline:
FY27: July 29, 2026, by 1 p.m. Eastern Time. Decision August 17, 2026 — 19 days later — and the full Application was then due October 5, 2026, i.e. 7 weeks after the invitation.

But the LOI is NOT the first gate, and this is the easiest thing to miss on this mechanism. There is a prior institutional step: the applicant's institution must opt in by emailing missiongrantsadmin@komen.org (FY27: by June 10, 2026), ~7 weeks before the LOI is due, and then name its nominees to Komen before the LOI deadline. An eligible PI whose institution never opted in cannot apply at all. Working backward from the LOI, an applicant needs to be talking to their Office of Sponsored Programs by roughly April/May.

The LOI is a hard eligibility screen, not a courtesy: "Any Applicant/PI who will not meet ALL eligibility criteria, as listed on pages 3 and 4 of this Announcement, will be administratively withdrawn at the Letter of Intent stage and WILL NOT be invited to submit an Application." Withdrawal carries "no opportunity for appeal."
result.review_to_award:
LOI due July 29, 2026 to LOI decision August 17, 2026 = 19 days. Invitation to full Application due October 5, 2026 = ~7 weeks to write an 8-page research plan, assemble a 3-5 member Mentor Committee including a Patient Advocate Mentor, and collect letters of support.

Application to award notification: October 5, 2026 to "on or around April 15, 2027" = ~6.4 months. Whole pipeline, institutional opt-in (June 10, 2026) to notification = ~10 months; LOI to notification = ~8.5 months.

Earliest project start: NOT STATED. I searched the full 13-page RFA for start date / grant term / project period / commence language; it gives the 3-year term and the $150,000/yr cap but never names a start date. The funded-grants page says only that approved projects "will be funded once the Grant Agreements between Komen and the Grantee institution(s) are fully-executed." So budget an unknown gap after ~April 15 notification.

Note a drift signal: the RFA's own page 12 says notification is "on or around April 15, 2026" while its Key Dates page and page 4 both say April 15, 2027. The 2026 instance is a stale-year typo carried over from the prior cycle — see prior_funding_conflicts, where the same paragraph is internally inconsistent in a way that actually matters.
result.submission_requirements:
All via proposalCENTRAL (https://proposalcentral.altum.com), committee "FY27CCR". PDF uploads only, named e.g. Smith_LOI, Smith_Biosketch, Smith_OtherSupport, Smith_Letter of Institutional Support. Must pass "Validate" before Submit. Materials in English. One LOI per applicant.

WHERE IT DEVIATES MOST — this is an institution-nominated limited submission, not an open call:
- "This is a limited submission opportunity: each institution may submit up to two nominees to apply for this funding. Applicants/PIs cannot self-nominate. The Institution's Office of Sponsored Programs, Grants Office, or equivalent must select the nominees."
- Institution emails missiongrantsadmin@komen.org by June 10, 2026 to opt in; Komen then sends the institution a submission link for its nominees. No opt-in, no route in.
- NEW in FY27 and easy to miss: a "Required: Institutional Nomination Process and Selection Criteria Disclosure" — the institution must describe in writing how it solicited, reviewed and selected nominees, who ran the process, evaluation criteria and weighting, selection-committee composition, and "measures taken to mitigate conflicts of interest or bias." It goes inside the Letter of Institutional Support, on letterhead, signed by an authorized representative.

LOI components (July 29, 2026):
- LOI Narrative, Komen template mandatory, "not to exceed one-page in total length" covering ALL THREE of A. Title (lay-friendly, <=81 characters incl. spaces, no abbreviations or all-caps), B. Research Plan (question, hypotheses, specific aims, scoped to the full 3-year term), C. Impact and Innovation. The title counts inside the one page.
- Applicant/PI Biosketch, NIH format, <=5 pages. Biosketches for mentors/other personnel are NOT wanted at LOI.
- Other Support, NIH format, signed by the PI, "may be as long as necessary"; required even if the applicant has none.
- Letter of Recommendation/Institutional Support from Dean, department chair or equivalent, on letterhead, confirming eligibility in writing, plus a statement on a pathway to independence if the applicant does not yet run their own lab. "The Lead Mentor may not provide this letter."
- Name the Lead Mentor (same institution as the PI; may be Lead Mentor on only one application per Komen mechanism; must do breast cancer research, or at least one Mentor Committee member must). A Lead Mentor letter is NOT required at LOI.
- Cited publications, institutional support letter, biosketch and other support are excluded from the one-page limit.
- Budget NOT required at LOI.

Added at full Application (October 5, 2026):
- Research Plan Narrative <=8 pages, sections A-I: Title; Research Questions/Hypotheses/Specific Aims; Background; Approach; Impact and Innovation; **Patient Advocate Involvement Plan**; Applicant Potential and Career Development Plan; Research Timeline; Statistical Plan.
- Mentor Committee "typically consisting of 3-5 mentors", including the Lead Mentor and a **Patient Advocate Mentor** — the advocate becomes mandatory Key Personnel at application stage.
- Data Sharing Plan (Komen policy aligned to NIH 2023 data sharing, genomic data sharing and clinical trial reporting), applies regardless of award size.
- Letters of Support from Institution, Lead Mentor, Patient Advocate Mentor(s), other Mentor Committee members, resource availability, collaborators/consultants.
- Signed Statement of Commitment from the PI on institutional letterhead.
- Biosketches (<=5 pp, NIH format) for PI, Lead Mentor and other Key Personnel.
- Cited Publications; Budget and Budget Justification; Institution Payment Verification form; Institution W-9; Clinical Trial Protocol and Contract/Consortium Budget if applicable.
- **ORCID identifier required** at submission.

Other binding conditions: >=75% of full-time effort protected for breast cancer research; indirect costs <=15% of total direct (including via subcontracts); equipment <=25% of total direct; personnel base salary cap $250,000/yr; no degree-granting tuition, no professional membership/subscription dues, no visa costs; patient advocate compensation IS allowed. Institution must be a U.S. non-profit and "may not be a governmental agency (i.e., NIH, NCI, etc.)". Single PI only — "Co-Principal Investigators (Co-PIs) are not allowed."

Format failure is fatal, not correctable: "Failure to adhere to these instructions will result in the Letter of Intent being administratively withdrawn from consideration, without appeal."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
The RFA states this TWICE, in two places, and the two versions do not agree. An applicant near the boundary must resolve it with Komen before investing in an LOI. Both halves below.

EXCLUDES — narrow version, RFA page 4 (Eligible Applicants):
- "Must not simultaneously hold any other Grant awarded by Susan G. Komen."
- "Must not currently be or have been a Principal Investigator on an existing NIH R01 grant or their equivalent as of the date of Award Notification (on or around April 15, 2027)." Note "or have been" — this is a lifetime bar on R01 PI status, not merely a concurrency bar, and it is tested at notification, not at submission. So an R01 that starts between October 2026 and April 2027 disqualifies a pending application.

EXCLUDES — broad version, RFA page 12 (Other Support at Application):
- "Applicant/PI may not currently hold another career transition award, training award (K-type award) or R-type award at time of notification of intent to fund (on or around April 15, 2026). If Applicant previously held an R-type award at any point, they are not eligible to apply for this award."

The conflict: page 4 bars only R01-or-equivalent PI status; page 12 additionally bars holding ANY K-type award or ANY R-type award at notification, and makes ever having held any R-type award a permanent bar. Under page 12 an R21 or an R00 would disqualify; under page 4 arguably neither does. The page-12 paragraph also carries the wrong year (2026 for 2027) and refers to "the Komen Career Transition Grant" in the adjacent Statement of Commitment paragraph — both signs it was copy-pasted from Komen's sibling Career Transition Award. That makes page 4 the likelier governing text, but the applicant carries the risk, and the K99/R00 case in particular is genuinely unresolved. Ask the help desk in writing and keep the answer.

PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — explicitly:
- Past Komen grants do NOT disqualify. Only simultaneous ones do. The requirement is compliance: "Must ensure that all past and current Komen-funded Grants are up to date and in compliance with all Komen requirements; e.g., progress and financial report submissions, IRB approvals, etc. by the Letter of Intent due date."
- Citizenship is not a gate: "Is not required to be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident" — stated for the Applicant/PI and, separately, for the Lead Mentor. The U.S. requirement attaches to the institution, not the person.
- Not having started the faculty job yet is fine: a "formal offer letter from the Institution that confirms position and start date by the Application due date (October 5, 2026)" is sufficient.
- Non-tenure-track and junior faculty titles do not disqualify — but they do burn the clock. Cap is 6 years total faculty appointment by October 5, 2026, and "All positions that are considered as 'Faculty' positions by the Applicant/PI's institution (or prior institution) count towards the 6-year limit. This may include positions such as Instructor, Research Fellow, or other non-tenure track faculty positions."
- Not yet running an independent lab is acceptable, provided the Letter of Institutional Support documents "a pathway to independence."
- Doctoral degree (M.D., Ph.D., Dr.P.H., D.O., or equivalent) required; no specific years-since-degree cap — the clock is faculty years, not post-degree years.
result.program_officer_contact:

- Programmatic (eligibility, program requirements, Komen policies): Komen Research Programs Help Desk at www.komen.org/researchhelpdesk — this resolves to a triage web form (https://www.tfaforms.com/327935) whose first question is "What is your question related to?" with options "I am applying for a Komen Research Grant" / "I already have a Komen Research Grant" / "Other". The RFA warns replies "could take up to 2 business days" — so do not leave a boundary-eligibility question until deadline week.

Pre-submission contact with Komen is NOT expected or required, and there is no scientific pre-review. result.examples_or_samples:
No sample application, successful LOI, or annotated example is published for this mechanism. What exists:

1. Funded-project abstracts, by fiscal year, free and public: https://www.komen.org/grants/funded/FY26/index.html — a sortable, searchable table with Investigator, Organization, State/Country, Grant Mechanism, Project Title and a plain-language Project Summary. This is a positive finding from three independent AHA sources, not an absence of evidence:
1. The CDA Key Dates block has no pre-proposal row — only RFP posted / ProposalCentral open / proposal deadline / award notification / award start.
2. The CDA entry on the Required Application Documents page lists no pre-proposal or LOI item.
3. AHA's published Research Plan page-limit table gives the CDA a single figure ("8"), whereas every two-stage AHA mechanism carries a paired figure: Innovative Project Award "1 pre-proposal / 5", Collaborative Sciences Award "3 / 10", Established Investigator Award "2 / 8", Merit Award "2 / 6", ASA/Bugher "5 pre-proposal / 17".

Practical consequence: unlike the AHA Innovative Project Award (pre-proposal due Dec 9, 2026; invitation Jan 21, 2027; invited full proposal Mar 4, 2027), the CDA gives you no staged entry and no early "no". You build the entire package — including four third-party document sets — for one deadline.
result.review_to_award:
Submission Tues., Dec. 1, 2026 → notification March 2027 → earliest start April 1, 2027. That is ~3 months deadline-to-notification and ~4 months deadline-to-money, roughly one month faster than the funder's Aug/Sept training cycle (Aug 4-5 deadline → Dec notification → Jan 1 start) and much faster than NIH's ~9-10 months for a K.

Arc between those two dates: assignment to a peer review committee (driven by the FIRST major science classification/keyword YOU pick) → initial triage → written critiques from 2 assigned scientist reviewers plus a 3rd reader → committee meeting, private scoring, averaged priority score, percentile ranking → AHA Research Committee funding decision (AHA's single post-review body; there is no NIH-style second Advisory Council step) → email to applicant, mentors AND grants officer directing you to log in to ProposalCentral for status.

TRIAGE — mechanism-specific wording, and it CONFLICTS with the funder-wide instructions. The CDA page's own Peer Review section says: "The Association reserves the right to an initial triage, whereby a minimum of half of the submissions may be triaged." Note "a minimum of half" — the CDA page sets a floor, not a ceiling, and unlike the 57-page Application Instructions it says nothing about whether a triaged CDA receives written comments. Plan on a better-than-even chance of never reaching committee discussion.

DELAY OF START — allowed, with a mechanism-specific carve-out REMOVED. Funder-wide, a delay of up to six months is allowable in limited cases, and intent must be declared in the Personal Statement of your biosketch at submission. For the CDA, the one reason you might most want it is explicitly forbidden: "Proposals will not be accepted with the intent to delay the award start date to accommodate the faculty appointment. It must be guaranteed by the award start date and stated explicitly by the Department in the requisite letter." So a postdoc may apply, but the faculty post must be guaranteed for April 1, 2027 in writing by the Department Head — you cannot buy time with the delay provision.
result.submission_requirements:
$231,000 over 3 years ($77,000/yr incl. 10% institutional indirect), non-renewable. Minimum 10% effort — note how far that is below NIH's 75% for a mentored K; the low floor is deliberate, "Recognizing the unique challenges that clinicians, in particular, experience in balancing research and clinical activity."

APPLICANT UPLOADS (page limits are AHA's published figures):
• Research Plan — 8 pages
• Career Development Plan — 3 pages (CDA-only document; see below)
• Literature Cited — 4 pages
• Research Project Environment — 2 pages, MANDATORY DOCX TEMPLATE
• Budget Justification Form — 2 pages, MANDATORY DOCX TEMPLATE
• Biosketch — NIH format accepted as-is, "It is not necessary to reformat to American Heart Association page specifications"
• Vertebrate Animal Subjects — if applicable, no page limit
• Resubmission Modifications — if applicable, 2 pages

THIRD-PARTY DOCUMENTS (Department Head Letter 5 pages; Primary Mentor: Training Plan for the Applicant 4 pages + Past and Current Trainees 3 pages + Biosketch; Secondary Mentor: Past and Current Trainees 3 pages + Biosketch + Mentor's Letter 3 pages; up to two Additional Mentors: Biosketch + Mentor's Letter 3 pages each).

SEVEN PLACES THIS MECHANISM DEVIATES FROM THE AHA NORM:

1. NO REFERENCE LETTERS — and this is a trap if you are coming from the fellowship side. Verbatim: "Only letters of support required from members of the mentoring team will be accepted. No other reference reports/letters are required or accepted." Fellowships need 3 reference reports at 4 pages each; the CDA needs zero.

2. THIRD PARTIES DO NOT UPLOAD — YOU DO. Fellowship referees upload via a system-generated email link. For the CDA, both the mentoring-team page ("Send your documents electronically to the applicant. The applicant will upload the documents to the application.") and the Department Head Letter page ("Complete the letter and return it to the applicant by e-mail. The applicant will upload it to the electronic application.") put the burden on you. Chase these yourself; nothing in ProposalCentral will chase them for you.

3. A MENTORING TEAM OF AT LEAST TWO, WITH STRUCTURAL CONSTRAINTS. Minimum primary + secondary, up to two more. "At least one mentor must be from outside of the applicant's department, division or institution." "One mentor should be committed to guiding the applicant's future grant writing endeavors (such as, how to write an R01 or equivalent)." A mentor contingency plan is a scored criterion: "Is there a contingency plan for mentors, if they cannot fulfill their contract for mentorship?"

4. CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN, 3 pages, with a prescribed skeleton: primary career intention; long-term goals; explicit short-term goals plus the challenges to overcome; timeline and "2-3 metrics that will define success" per goal; what you will DELEGATE to free the time; skills/knowledge gaps and how you will close them; and "Specifically delineate when and how progress assessments/checkpoints will occur, particularly with each member of your mentoring team." Unusually, AHA disclaims the academic default: "The Association does not require this to be a traditional academic research or health profession track. For example, an applicant might wish to pursue a career in industry, technology, teaching, or public health."

5. THE PRIMARY MENTOR'S TRAINING PLAN NEEDS TWO LITERALLY-TITLED SECTIONS. AHA asks for a section titled "Instruction in responsible conduct of research and rigor and reproducibility" and another titled "Mentor's Qualifications" (special skills offered, how they will support the applicant's academic growth, plus a personal testimonial about mentorship). "The American Heart Association does not require submission of the NIH RCE form."

6. THE DEPARTMENT HEAD LETTER ASKS FOR SALARY DATA. Beyond appointment, accomplishments, commitment and institutional support, the letter must give the "Date of applicant's last salary review" and place you in a band: "The salary for this applicant falls within the following percentile range for faculty at the same level in my department: 0-25th, 26th-50th, 51st-75th, 76th-100th". It also carries the faculty-appointment guarantee. AHA instructs the writer to avoid bias: "Please avoid referring to personal circumstances or attributes of the applicant: Marital status, age or gender... child care or illness... (e.g. mother, husband, father)."

7. NO HYPERLINKS AT ALL — which kills the funder's own Precision Medicine Platform route for this mechanism. Verbatim: "Hyperlinks to data/figures/additional information are not permitted in the Research Plan nor any other proposal documents. This includes use of the Precision Medicine Platform for applications and peer review purposes."

BIOSKETCH PERSONAL STATEMENT — two mandatory, scored insertions (page updated 4/27/2026). The applicant must "include a statement that explicitly states how you will contribute to a safe and inclusive work environment." And "mentors on Fellowships and Career Development Awards should complete recognized training specific to sexual and gender-based harassment" — the review criteria check for it: "Have the mentors included a statement in the Personal Statement section of their biosketch noting they have completed recognized training specific to sexual and gender-based harassment?" Any intent to delay the start date also goes here.

FORMATTING (funder-wide, enforced by administrative withdrawal, not a warning): single-spaced; ≤15 characters per inch incl. symbols/punctuation/spaces; margins ≥¾" all four sides; ≤50 lines per page; Arial 12pt (Windows) / Helvetica 12pt (Mac); PDF only; documents as separate files.

SIGN-OFF: "All submissions require the signature of a designated institutional representative." Two-step — PI submits to the Grants Officer, who e-signs and releases to AHA, and who can decline it back to you for revisions.

ALSO SCORED: sex/age as biological variables must be addressed for any vertebrate-animal or human-subjects application, with "strong justification" for studying only one sex or age group. AI/LLM use is permitted but must be disclosed at submission; undisclosed use is grounds for administrative withdrawal.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, verbatim from AHA's CDA page.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU:
• "Investigators who have been awarded NIH K99/R00 or R01 grants are not eligible to apply." Read the tense: "have been awarded" — a past R01 or K99/R00 bars you permanently, not just a currently active one.
• "The applicant may not be a current or prior recipient of a Career Development Award or Scientist Development Grant." One CDA per lifetime; the retired Scientist Development Grant (the CDA's predecessor) counts against you too.
• Submitting the same or similar application a fourth time → administratively withdrawn.
• More than one CDA application in a single cycle: "The applicant may submit only one Career Development Award application per deadline."
• The clock gates, which function as eligibility exclusions: at award activation you must hold "a faculty/staff position up to and including the rank of assistant professor (or equivalent)", and "No more than six years may have elapsed since the first faculty/staff appointment (after receipt of doctoral degree) at the assistant professor level or equivalent (including, but not limited to, instructor, research assistant professor, research scientist, staff scientist, etc.)."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half most applicants never find:
• THE BIG ONE: "A Career Development Awardee may concurrently hold an NIH K award (other than K99/R00) if there is no budgetary overlap." So a live K01, K08, K23, K25 or K76 does NOT bar you, and you can hold both simultaneously. The test is budgetary overlap, not the existence of the award. This is the exact inverse of NIH's own mentored-K rules, where holding another K generally excludes you — an AHA CDA is the standard way to add pilot money and a second mentoring structure on top of an NIH K.
• "A Career Development awardee may also hold a Collaborative Sciences Award, Innovative Project Award, Transformational Project Award, and may be the program director or sponsor on an Institutional Award for Undergraduate Training."
• "Strategically Focused Research Network personnel may hold individual Association awards."
• INSTRUCTOR TIME IS NOT CHARGED TO YOUR SIX YEARS: "If the candidate held the title of instructor during postdoctoral fellowship or residency years due to clinical or teaching responsibilities, that period of time does not count against the eligibility period for applying for the Career Development Award." For clinician-scientists this can be the difference between eligible and not.
• CAREER INTERRUPTIONS COUNT IN YOUR FAVOUR: "The Association will consider interruptions of work experience due to extenuating circumstances and clinical training."
• POSTDOCS MAY APPLY: "Postdoctoral fellows are eligible to apply but must have attained faculty appointment by the time of award activation" — but the Department Head must guarantee the April 1 appointment in the letter, and you may NOT use the six-month delay-of-start provision to wait for it.
• Resubmission preserved: original plus two resubmissions.
• No NIH salary cap: "The Heart Association does not require use of the NIH salary cap."

THE PRACTICAL ORDERING RULE: apply for the AHA CDA BEFORE your first R01 or K99/R00, and you keep both doors open; land either of those first and the AHA CDA is closed to you forever. Institutions: US-based non-profit only. Citizenship/visa list and required AHA Professional Membership at submission are already in the row.

result.resubmission_note:
ALLOWED. The CDA is on AHA's enumerated list of resubmission-eligible programmes, and the CDA page repeats the cap in its own words: "The applicant may submit the same or similar application three times (the original plus two resubmissions). The same or similar application submitted the fourth time will be administratively withdrawn."

THE INTRODUCTION-EQUIVALENT: a separate "Resubmission Modifications" upload, 2-page limit, specifying significant changes made in response to major comments from the scientific critiques and how the proposal was strengthened. AHA warns it "complies exactly with the association's Page Setup/Formatting Requirements" — format non-compliance is an administrative-withdrawal ground.

WHY RESUBMITTING IS WORTH IT HERE: "when possible, a resubmitted proposal will be assigned to at least one of the previous primary reviewers. Reviewers of resubmitted proposals will be provided with the critiques and scores from the previous round for reference." Your revision is read against your last round by someone who read it — answer the critiques point by point and say where.

MECHANISM-SPECIFIC CONSTRAINT THAT BITES HARDER THAN THE CAP: the resubmission counter is not what will run out first. Your six-years-since-first-faculty-appointment window and the assistant-professor rank ceiling keep running, and the deadline is annual — so in practice you get one attempt per year against a fixed faculty clock. A first submission in year 5 of the window leaves room for at most one resubmission before you age out, regardless of the three-try allowance.

WHAT COUNTS: "A resubmission is the same or similar proposal (similar aims)... If major changes are made to the proposal or if this is a different/new project, it is not considered a resubmission." You tick a resubmission box in Section 1 (Project Title) of ProposalCentral and indicate whether the prior application sat in ProposalCentral or the legacy Grants@Heart system.

NOT ALLOWED: "It is not acceptable to resubmit a proposal previously submitted by another investigator."

Materials are customarily due 1 month prior to the anticipated grant start date"; the PI completes Contacts, Other Support, Ethical Certifications, Milestones and the Year 1 budget and clicks "Validate and Submit Activation Materials to RO", then the RO approves the Year 1 budget and adds payment details. So allow at least a month between notification and first funds, and get the RO diarised. REVIEW PATH for a single-stage CDA (handbook §3, steps 4–8, LOI steps not applicable): full proposal submitted → administrative triage (a real and frequently invoked gate — incomplete application, missing budget or biosketch, over-length research plan, formatting violation, or poor fit to the Research Strategy eliminates it before review) → internal and/or external scientific review, "at the discretion of Breakthrough T1D Scientific Staff and Breakthrough T1D Senior Management", reviewers "provide qualitative critiques and quantitative scores" → Scientific Staff make a funding recommendation to Senior Management → "Breakthrough T1D Senior Management and/or a committee of the International Board of Directors make final funding decision" (the board-committee step is the NIH-Council analogue applicants forget) → written notification → activation. Human-subjects CDAs add an unquantified clinical-review step before award. There is no standing named study section and no published reviewer roster. INFERENCE, FLAGGED, NOT A FINDING: the funder-wide pattern from dated topic RFAs runs ~4–5 months from full proposal to notification and 1–3 months more to earliest start, which against a 2 July deadline would imply notification around Nov–Dec and a start early the following year. Do not print that as a CDA date — ask smukerjee@breakthrought1d.org for the FY28 cycle's expected notification and start dates.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, AND THE ANSWER IS UNUSUAL — THE "EXCLUDED" HALF IS NEARLY EMPTY.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU (the complete list — it is a career clock and a job title, nothing else):
1. The 3-year faculty clock, verbatim: "Researchers who have received their first faculty-level appointment less than 3 years before the submission date are eligible to apply for this award." Measured from FIRST faculty appointment to SUBMISSION DATE — not from degree, not from current appointment.
2. Position at submission: "The applicant must hold an academic faculty-level position (including assistant professor or equivalent) at the time of submission of the proposal, at a university, health science center, or comparable institution with strong, well-established research and training programs for the chosen area of interest."
3. Degree, required at activation not submission — the CDA checklist reads "Has a PhD/MD/DMD/DVM/DO or the equivalent from an accredited institution at award activation". The RFA and handbook brief-description lines also list PsyD: "MD, DMD, DVM, DO, PsyD, PhD, or equivalent".
4. Effort floor: "Awardees must spend at least 75% of time and effort on type 1 diabetes-related research projects during the period of the award."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — everything else. THERE IS NO PRIOR-FUNDING EXCLUSION OF ANY KIND. I read the FY27 CDA RFA in full (4pp) and the Grant Handbook in full (95pp) and searched both for R01, NIH, prior/previous award, ineligible, not eligible, only one, per cycle, concurrent, duplicate, already hold. Findings: "R01" appears nowhere in either document. There is no NIH-style exclusion clause, no "must not already hold independent research support", no bar on a prior or current K award, no bar on other foundation funding, no bar on a previous Breakthrough T1D award, no cap on number of resubmissions, and no limit on applications per cycle. The phrase "not eligible" occurs exactly once in the entire 95-page handbook and is unrelated — "Postdoctoral Fellowships are not eligible for transfers." So an applicant holding an NIH R01, a K08/K23/K99-R00, an AHA or other foundation grant, or who previously held a Breakthrough T1D postdoctoral fellowship, is NOT barred from a CDA on that basis. THIS IS A STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE FROM THE K-ANALOGUE ROWS IN THIS CORPUS and should not be assumed away: NIH mentored Ks exclude current/former R01 PIs with a named carve-out list, and the AHA Career Development Award excludes prior AHA CDA/SDG recipients and NIH K99/R00 or R01 awardees outright. Breakthrough T1D does neither.

WHAT REPLACES THE EXCLUSION — an effort-and-overlap test, not an award-type test. This is what actually catches people:
- Disclosure, and note the CDA-specific twist: "Applicants must include accurate and complete information regarding all other sources of grant support from the main PI (current and pending), including title, abstract, annual and total amount of the grant, inclusive funding period, and percent effort of the applicant. For Postdoctoral and Advanced Postdoctoral Fellowships, Other Support information should be provided for the Sponsor/Mentor only." Read the second sentence carefully — for the two fellowships the disclosure is the mentor's; for the CDA it is YOUR OWN, because you are the PI. Entered in the RMS360 "My Profile" section at application and revised at Activation and each Renewal.
- The ceiling: "Personnel contributing to a Breakthrough T1D grant are expected to monitor their total percent effort across all funding (Breakthrough T1D or other) which may not exceed 100%."
- The arithmetic that binds: 75% of your effort must sit on T1D-related research for the whole award, and total effort across all funding cannot exceed 100%. A concurrently held non-T1D R01 at substantial effort is therefore what breaks a CDA — through effort accounting at activation, not through an eligibility rule at submission. Conversely a T1D-relevant concurrent award can often be made to fit. This is the question to put to the program administrator in writing before you write.

THE WAIVER — a written invitation, and asking is the only way to get it: "Breakthrough T1D is sensitive to personal and COVID-related matters that impact career trajectories. Applicants who have taken leave from their career (e.g. parenting of a child, childbirth, long-term care of a parent/spouse/child/dependent, personal health issues) or experienced a delay due to COVID shutdowns that puts them outside of the eligibility time frame for the award mechanism should reach out to Breakthrough T1D staff ahead of their application submission. Breakthrough T1D aims to be flexible and adjust these time frames if necessary and appropriate." If you are at 3 years and 4 months post-first-appointment with a parental leave in between, you are plausibly still in — but only if you ask BEFORE submitting.

CONTRADICTION ON THE FACE OF THE FUNDER'S OWN TWO DOCUMENTS — flag, do not resolve: the RFA and handbook CDA sections both say "Career Development Award research may be conducted at foreign and domestic, for-profit and nonprofit, and public and private organizations", while the handbook's own Career Development Awards Application Checklist requires "The applicant's institution is a nonprofit or academic entity". A for-profit-based applicant should email preawardsupport@BreakthroughT1D.org before investing any writing time.

SCOPE EXPANSIONS THAT PRESERVE ELIGIBILITY FOR PEOPLE WHO WOULD PREVIOUSLY HAVE BEEN OUT — two, both new and both easy to miss: (1) FY27 RFA opening line, "Important: In a change from previous years, applicants proposing human subject research on long-term complications covered by the Breakthrough T1D research strategy (specifically diabetic eye, kidney, and cardiovascular disease) are eligible to apply for training awards. Human subject research includes interventional or observational trials as well as analysis of clinical bio-samples or data." (2) The handbook CDA section carries a line the RFA omits: "Applications in Psychosocial and Behavioral Health will be accepted."
result.submission_requirements:
Single-stage full proposal through RMS360 (https://breakthrought1d.smartsimple.us/). Below, only what is CDA-SPECIFIC or deviates from the funder-wide norm.

PAGE LIMITS — the CDA numbers, which differ from the fellowships:
- Research Plan: "The research plan may not exceed 12 pages, including figures and tables" — 12, not the fellowships' 7. Enforcement is absolute: "Proposals with research plans exceeding the page limit will not be considered."
- It must describe a FIVE-YEAR project: "The Career Development Award research plan should describe a five-year project."
- Fixed headings: "a) Specific Aims; b) Background and Significance of this work to type 1 diabetes; c) Preliminary Studies (if applicable); d) Research Design and Methods; e) Literature Cited (no page limit)."
- Future Career Plans Statement: 2 pages. Placement is CDA-specific — "At the end of the Research Plan section, the applicant must include a Future Career Plans statement, which is limited to 2 pages. The applicant must include a statement of career goals and indicate the relevance of these goals to type 1 diabetes-related research."
- Introduction to Revised Application (resubmissions only): 2 pages maximum.

THE PAGE-LIMIT AMBIGUITY, WORTH AN EMAIL BEFORE YOU WRITE: the RFA places the 2-page Future Career Plans statement "at the end of the Research Plan section", while the CDA Application Checklist lists three separate line items under "Proposal Research Plan" — "Introduction to Revised Application (2 pages maximum) / Research Plan (12 pages maximum) / Future Plans (2 pages maximum)". Whether the 2-page career statement (and, on a resubmission, the 2-page introduction) counts inside or outside the 12 is not stated unambiguously. Over-length is automatic administrative triage, so ask preawardsupport@BreakthroughT1D.org and get the answer in writing.

TWO COMPONENTS THAT ARE OTHER PEOPLE'S WORK AND SIT ON YOUR CRITICAL PATH:
1. Three confidential references, submitted BY the referee, not by you: "Three (3) recommendation references assessing the scientific abilities and potential of the applicant must be submitted. Please note that the recommendation references are confidential and will not be released to the applicant. The recommendation references must be submitted directly through RMS360 by the referee. Please note proposals cannot be successfully validated until all references are submitted." The checklist lists them under Contacts — "Recommendation References (blind) 3 required" — i.e. you name the referees on the Contacts tab and RMS360 invites them. A missing reference blocks validation, which blocks submission. Brief referees the day the RFA posts.
2. Department Head Statement (the CDA's institutional sign-off, and its substitute for a mentor letter): "The applicant's institution must, through the departmental supervisor, provide assurance of an academic commitment to the applicant and to the research project. This Department Head Statement must be included as a Supporting Document and uploaded as a proposal attachment." "Department Head" is also a required entry on the Contacts tab.

WHAT THE CDA DOES **NOT** REQUIRE — the deviation people over-prepare for: NO sponsor, NO mentor, NO Training Plan Statement. The Postdoctoral and Advanced Postdoctoral Fellowships require a sponsor plus a 2-page sponsor-written Training Plan Statement, and the Kellogg ECPODRA requires a sponsor plus a 4-page one. The CDA requires none of these, because the applicant is already the independent investigator. Its institutional-commitment evidence is the Department Head Statement instead.

FULL CHECKLIST ITEMS beyond the above: PI biosketch up to date IN THE RMS360 PROFILE (auto-appended, not an attachment; Breakthrough T1D or NIH format both accepted) and the "My Biosketch is up to date" box ticked on Contacts; Co-PI, Research Delegate, Key Personnel, RO and FO contacts; a research priority area AND an alternate priority area; resubmission yes/no; an explicit yes/no on "allow Breakthrough T1D to share this application with The Leona M. and Harry B. Helmsley Charitable Trust for potential co-funding"; clinical classification if applicable; Other Support (see prior_funding_conflicts); two abstracts, one scientific and one lay, the lay one in six named categories (General Audience Summary, Technical Abstract, Objective, Background/Rationale, Anticipated Outcome, Relevance to type 1 diabetes) with a 600-word limit EACH; human subjects / vertebrate animals assurances; biosketches for Key Personnel and other faculty-level investigators as attachments; optional Collaboration Letters, Protocol Synopsis, Resources, Supporting Documents, Diversity & Inclusion Resource Sheet; budget not exceeding $200,000/yr including 10% indirect.

FORMATTING — violations are grounds for triage, not a request to fix: "Use 10-point size font only"; "Margins, in all directions, must be at least 1/2 inch"; no text boxes; figures as .jpg or .gif, not .tif; each attachment 3–4 MB; English only; "Do not include your social security number or passport number in your Breakthrough T1D application." And: "Please note that if the guidelines outlined above are not followed, the application will be administratively triaged and will not receive a review."

INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF — the reason a 5:00pm deadline is really an earlier deadline: submission is two-step and the second step is not yours. The PI clicks Validate & Submit to route the proposal to the Research Office; the RO then approves the budget and formally submits from the "Pending RO Approval" tab. A PI who validates at 4:55pm has not submitted. Start the RMS360 setup 4–6 weeks out: PI self-registration, a new-organisation request if your institution is not in the dropdown, RO and FO accounts (a newly created RO/FO must be approved by an already-registered research officer at your institution, or by preawardsupport@BreakthroughT1D.org if none exists or none replies), and any Co-PI registered with a current profile biosketch. Use Chrome or Firefox; attachments must be unlocked, non-password-protected PDFs.

TERMS, WITH AN INTERNAL CONTRADICTION WORTH RESOLVING BEFORE YOU BUDGET: "200,000 USD maximum/year for up to 5 years, including up to 10% for indirect costs and generally not renewable after 5 years", and the research plan "should describe a five-year project" — yet the same RFA says twice "The awards are renewable pending satisfactory progress up to a maximum of four years" and "Awards are renewable each year for a maximum of four years after submission and approval of a renewal proposal." Most likely four renewal years after year one (= five total), but the document states both 5 and 4 on its face. Confirm with the program administrator. Research allowance may include a technician, supplies, equipment and travel up to USD 2,000/yr; equipment after year 1 must be strongly justified; indirect costs (excluding equipment) may not exceed 10% of subtotal direct costs; annual progress report required to renew.
result.resubmission_note: Allowed, same policy as the funder norm — no CDA-specific variation, and no cap. Grant Handbook §3 verbatim: "Breakthrough T1D accepts applications resubmitted after rejection by the Breakthrough T1D review committee(s) discussed above. All resubmitted applications must include: A copy of the summary statement for the original application if provided for rejected submission. An introduction (limited to two pages) addressing each of the reviewer's concerns if provided for the rejected submission. These documents must be included in the Resubmission section of the Research Plan." The CDA checklist mirrors this in RMS360: "Is the application a resubmission? Select YES or NO — If yes, please include Summary Statement from the previous application; Rebuttal Letter (included in the research plan and does not exceed 2 pages)", and names the same document a third way under Proposal Research Plan as "Introduction to Revised Application (2 pages maximum)". Introduction / rebuttal letter / Introduction to Revised Application are one and the same 2-page document. NUMBER OF RESUBMISSIONS: no published cap — not found; nothing in the handbook or the FY27 CDA RFA states an NIH-style A1 limit. TIME WINDOW: none published — not found. But for the CDA the effective clock is set by two calendars, and for this mechanism the second one is brutal: (1) the call recurs only once a year, so a resubmission waits ~12 months; and (2) the 3-year first-faculty-appointment window keeps running while you wait. A CDA rejected in your third faculty year may leave no eligible cycle to resubmit into — check your own clock before planning a resubmission, and if a career gap is in play, ask about the waiver. NOTE THE CONDITIONALS: both required items are qualified "if provided for the rejected submission", and critiques are not guaranteed — "Generally, applications undergo a pre-review process. For applications receiving a full review, critiques containing the reviewers' comments may be provided." A CDA killed at administrative triage generates no summary statement, so there is nothing to attach and nothing to answer; you are submitting fresh. WHAT MUST CHANGE: not specified beyond "addressing each of the reviewer's concerns" — no change-marking convention, no percentage rule. NO APPEAL: the handbook's "Grant Appeals Procedure/Rebuttal" (§5.9) is post-award only, governing a Grantee Institution's response to probation or corrective action. The reviewer rebuttal offered on SRAs and IDDP is a mid-review right of reply and is not part of the single-stage CDA process at all. There is no route to contest a CDA rejection.
result.program_officer_contact: NAMED, SINGLE, AND ADMINISTRATIVE. The FY27 CDA RFA names exactly one contact: "Program Contact — Sanjukta Mukerjee, Program Administrator, Breakthrough T1D, Email: smukerjee@breakthrought1d.org", followed by "If you have any grant-specific questions as you work within RMS360, please contact the administrative contact listed above." The same administrator covers all four FY27 Training Awards. DEVIATION FROM THE FUNDER NORM, AND IT MATTERS: topic RFAs at this funder print a named Scientist / Senior Scientist / Associate Director of Research alongside the administrator, for scientific-fit conversations. The FY27 CDA RFA names NO scientific contact. So there is no designated programme scientist for this mechanism and no informational webinar in the training-award cycle — the two cheapest routes to scientific steer at this funder are both absent here. IS PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT EXPECTED? Not mandatory, unlike the SRA (which "requires permission from Breakthrough T1D") and IDDP (applicants "must contact Breakthrough T1D Research staff prior to submitting an LOI"). But it is explicitly invited for the one thing that decides whether you can apply at all: applicants outside the 3-year window for caregiving, childbirth, personal health or COVID reasons "should reach out to Breakthrough T1D staff ahead of their application submission", and flexibility is only available to those who ask. WHO TO EMAIL FOR WHAT — mixing these up wastes a week: eligibility-clock waivers, forms, attachments, RMS360 mechanics, and the page-limit question → smukerjee@breakthrought1d.org or preawardsupport@BreakthroughT1D.org (the handbook's general pre-award inbox, also the fallback that approves an RO/FO account when nobody at your institution is registered, and the inbox the handbook nominates for training-award human-subjects queries); active-award questions after you win → postawardsupport@BreakthroughT1D.org; human-subjects design that may trigger clinical review → your assigned Breakthrough T1D scientific manager via the Clinical Trial Management group. WHEN: May–June for a 1–2 July deadline, i.e. as soon as the RFA posts in April–May and before you commit to writing. Once submitted, contact is over — "status of an application will not be given by phone." WHAT TO ASK, given no scientific contact is named: which of the eight research priority areas your project maps to and which alternate to list (alignment with priority areas "will be given priority consideration in the review process"); whether the work duplicates the existing portfolio (staff weigh "relevance of the proposed research in complementing the existing Breakthrough T1D project portfolio"); whether your career gap extends the 3-year window; whether the 2-page Future Career Plans statement counts inside the 12 pages; whether 4 or 5 years is the correct project length to budget; and — if you hold other grants — whether your effort split clears the 75% T1D floor and the 100% ceiling. Do not ask for a draft pre-review; staff co-develop invited SRA proposals but do not pre-review unsolicited drafts.

BEST AVAILABLE, AND IT IS MECHANISM-FILTERABLE: the Breakthrough T1D Global Research Portfolio, https://www.breakthrought1d.org/explore-research/funded-research/ — verified 2026-09-18 that "Career Development Award" is a SELECTABLE Funding Mechanism filter (alongside Strategic Research Agreement, Industry Development and Discovery Program, Innovative Grants, Postdoctoral Fellowship, Advanced Postdoctoral Fellowship, Early Career Patient-Oriented Diabetes Research, High Priority Short Term Award, Special Grant Partnerships). Cross-filter by Research Priority Area (Beta Cell Replacement, Beta Cell Regeneration, Immunotherapies, Prevention, Artificial Pancreas, Metabolic Control, Complications, Psychosocial), Grant Status (Active / Complete), institution and geography. Each record shows Grant Key, Principal Investigator, Project Title, Grant Duration, Institution Name and Address, Award Amount, Contract Amount and LAY ABSTRACT. Search conventions, verbatim: "Geographic (US-based): State abbreviation followed by country (no commas) Example: FL United States or MI United States; Geographic (non-US): Country (no abbreviations) Example: United Kingdom; Institution: Keyword only (collaborating institutions may pull into results) Example: Harvard". A map view lets you click a state for institutions and abstracts. (The page 403s a plain curl behind Cloudflare; it read fine through this session's rendering fetch and renders normally in a browser.)

THE HONEST LIMIT — DO NOT PROMISE A READER A FUNDED CDA APPLICATION. Handbook §5.3.2: "Most grant materials submitted to Breakthrough T1D are for internal Breakthrough T1D use only. Exceptions include the Lay Abstract submitted at the time of Application and the Web Progress Reports, submitted on an annual basis with the Annual and Final Progress Report." So lay abstracts and annual/final lay progress reports are public; full applications, research plans, budgets, reviewer critiques and summary statements are not. There is no NIH-RePORTER equivalent exposing Specific Aims pages, and I found no published sample-application library for this funder from Breakthrough T1D or from any university research office.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, IN DESCENDING ORDER OF VALUE FOR A CDA APPLICANT:
1. Filter the portfolio to Funding Mechanism = Career Development Award + your priority area, and read 10–20 lay abstracts. This is the strongest proxy available, and for the CDA it is unusually direct: the lay abstract is written by a funded CDA PI to the very six-category, 600-words-each template you must fill in yourself, on a project the reviewers accepted at the same career stage.
2. Read the annual Web Progress Reports on COMPLETE CDA grants in your area — they show what five-year trajectory the funder actually accepted and what the awardee delivered, which is the question the CDA's "ability and potential for a career in type 1 diabetes research" criterion really asks.
3. Use the portfolio's institution filter on your own institution to find current and former Breakthrough T1D awardees down the hall. For an early-career applicant this is the intended use of that filter, and it is the only realistic route to seeing an actual funded CDA narrative — an awardee can show you theirs even though the funder will not.
4. Affiliate results pages publish named awardees per competition, e.g. https://breakthrought1d.ca/research/grant-opportunities/ carries a "Results" link for each past round.
5. Trace the papers: grantees must acknowledge Breakthrough T1D with the grant number, so a literature search on the acknowledgement string surfaces what a given CDA produced.
6. For co-funded work, the Leona M. and Harry B. Helmsley Charitable Trust's grants listing overlaps this portfolio — the CDA application itself asks permission to share with Helmsley.

CALIBRATION AID, NOT A SAMPLE: the RFA states the evaluation criteria in the funder's own words, and the weighting is explicit and unusual — "Awards will be made on the basis of the applicant's perceived ability and potential for a career in type 1 diabetes research, the caliber of the proposed research, and the quality and commitment of the institution. The applicant's professional ability and promise will hold the highest priority in selection and will be assessed on the basis of items such as letters of recommendation, publications, career plans, and prior clinical and research training." The candidate outranks the project here. That is why the three blind references and the 2-page career statement carry more weight in a CDA than their page count suggests.

November 1, 2026, 3:00 PM (ET) — published (a Sunday; by BCU's own weekend rule this should become Mon 2 Nov 2026).

But the LOI is the SECOND of three gates, and the first one is the one people miss. CDP runs Eligibility → Letter of Intent → Full Application, each submitted separately through the portal.

How CDP's LOI differs from BCU's other mechanisms: for TRP/ACT/DGP the LOI is a competitive triage gate ("We will only be inviting full applications that will be competitive"). For CDP it is NOT — every applicant whose eligibility is approved proceeds. The CDP LOI is instead a LOCKING gate, and that is the trap: "Information collected in the Letter of Intent Phase will automatically populate fields in the Full Application Phase. Carefully and thoughtfully complete these sections as the fields are locked after the Letter of Intent Phase is completed." And: "applicants must place some of that LOI information on the full application template. This information must exactly match... starting this year, any changes may result in disqualification."

LOI Phase components: reference letter-writer requests, ORCiD, first-author publications, research information, collaborator/mentor information — plus the public-facing Summary (500 char), Title (150 char), research focus details.

TIMING SQUEEZE: LOI closes 1 Nov, full application closes 15 Nov — only 14 days apart, and the LOI cannot open until eligibility is approved. Eligibility approval is rolling but can take up to 10 business days, and BCU states plainly: "The LOI phase deadline will not be changed based on an eligibility form being returned to the applicant for incomplete and/or unclear information." Submitting eligibility in, say, early October rather than on 15 October is the single highest-leverage scheduling decision in this mechanism.
result.review_to_award:
Full application 15 Nov 2026 → notification July 2027 (~8 months) → earliest start 1 Oct 2027 (~10.5 months after submission). From the first gate (eligibility opens July 2026) to money, roughly 12-15 months.

Where CDP deviates from the funder-wide norm:
- BCU publishes NO review panel month for CDP. (TRP publishes a March 2027 panel meeting; CDP does not.) Treat the CDP panel month as unconfirmed.
- Eligibility review is a distinct, staff-run, rolling stage with its own clock — "typically within 2 business days," up to 10. "Contact researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org if you have not received notification within 10 business days." Historically "~20-30% of eligibility requests were rejected," though BCU says it has "updated the eligibility form to make rejections far less likely, but it takes much more time to complete."

Scoring: "CDP applications are reviewed by an independent, voluntary panel of experts." The application "receives a Priority Score based on the NIH scoring system," plus a separate Mission Score (1-5) for blood-cancer relevance. Then: "After the review panel meeting, Mission-relevant applications (Mission Scores 1, 2, and some 3) will be rank-ordered based on their Priority Scores and those within or near the payline will be presented to Blood Cancer United's oversight committees for approval."

Two pre-review kill screens worth planning against, in BCU's numbers: ">10% of Career Development Program (CDP) applications submitted (from all non-clinical subcategories) were disqualified without full review based on non-compliance with the Mission Relevance"; and "approximately 10-15% of all full applications had serious structural flaws" (section lengths, font size, missing Sponsor Letter or biosketch, incomplete data attribution). Mission Score 4 or 5 = "eliminated without full review." A Fellow whose Sponsor lacks a blood-cancer publication/funding record "will be disqualified without full review."

Outcome states in the portal: "Under Review" → "Awarded" or "Waitlist," or "Not Funded." Waitlist is a real, distinct outcome, not a soft no. "Funding status is relayed by email only and is not available by phone." Payline and success rate are not published.
result.submission_requirements:
NO overall page limit is published for CDP Fellow. Length is enforced by a LOCKED Word template plus hard character limits — this is the main deviation from mechanisms that quote a page count (BCU's own TRP, by contrast, runs real page limits).

CHARACTER LIMITS (all "including spaces", strictly enforced on the web form and template):
- Summary (public-facing, 3-5 sentences): max 500
- Title: max 150
- Lay Description: MINIMUM 2,000 and maximum 2,500 — the minimum is the one people miss
- Scientific Abstract: max 1,500
- Brief Biography: max 1,000
- Clinical Protocol Summary (rare for Fellows): up to 2 pages; "Do not attach a full clinical protocol."

FORMAT RULES THAT DISQUALIFY:
- "Font must be black Arial 11 pt., including figure legends, which must be text boxes separate from the figure itself." Tables too. Figures themselves may use smaller text.
- "Outside of the figures themselves, should any font be smaller than Arial 11 pt. (including shrunken figure legend text boxes, which will appear smaller), the application may be administratively disqualified without review."
- "Line spacing is preset in the Word document. Do not change the setting... Any modifications in line spacing, particularly if the change allows for more text to fit into the page, may result in administrative rejection." Extra space BETWEEN paragraphs is allowed.
- ONE combined PDF in the template's exact order: "Failure to submit as a single PDF in the order above may result in disqualification." Nothing may precede the template — no cover letters. "Applications that include additional documents besides those requested may be administratively disqualified."

REFERENCE LETTERS (Fellow-specific, and a hard disqualifier):
- "Three letters are required"; "No more than four letters will be accepted."
- "If there are not at least 3 letters of reference received by the full application deadline, the application will be administratively disqualified."
- Blind: "Letters are blinded to the applicant and must be uploaded directly by the writer." You register writers in the portal during the LOI phase ("Request Blind Reference Letters", green "+" button); each gets a unique auto-emailed link. "The email may end up in the letter-writer's spam" — if not received in 2 business days, email BCU for a re-send. A name added in error cannot be deleted.
- "Though not required, it is beneficial to have two of the letters coming from outside your institution."
- The Sponsor may NOT write one: "Sponsors may not write a reference letter." "Blood Cancer United does not allow co-Sponsors for CDP applicants."

SPONSOR LETTER (separate, critical, scored): signed, on institutional letterhead, and must contain: the applicant's position and how their research integrates into the lab; "a brief description of how much of the application was written by the applicant," including certification that the Preliminary Data and Experimental Design sections contain only applicant-generated data; the Sponsor's mentorship experience; source of funding for the applicant's research; a "training plan to develop the applicant into an independent researcher"; description of any co-mentor/mentoring team; signature. "Applicants with Sponsor Letters that follow the rules and clearly outline appropriate mentorship will have a better chance of funding."

TWO-OF-EVERYTHING RULE (a named disqualifier): separate NIH-format biosketches for applicant AND Sponsor, and separate Other Support documents for each — Sponsor uses the NIH Other Support form, applicant uses BCU's own form in the template. "Failure to provide separate Other Support Documents for the applicant and for the Sponsor may result in administrative disqualification." The applicant's biosketch "must not be the fellowship format"; no eRA Commons username needed; omit undergrad/grad courses and grades.

OTHER REQUIRED COMPONENTS: Sections 1-6 = Abstracts and Brief Biography; Application Template; Budget; Assurances; Research Tags; Attachments. Plus ORCiD (mandatory, supplied at LOI phase, https://orcid.org/); a Graphical Abstract (up to two, "must not be professionally developed"); Description of Models, Drugs/Reagents and Trials tables; Data Attribution tables ("Applications without appropriate and clear attribution... will be unfavorably reviewed and may be administratively disqualified"); an Access to Non-Commercially Available Reagents section; a Sponsor Mentor Table; a Signature Page (electronic signatures acceptable); collaboration/support letters where access to patient samples, models or specialised equipment is needed.

NEW AND SCORED: "Disease Demographics and Equitable Research Models and Approaches" sections are now required — "Reviewers will give a score boost to those with clear information on demographics and thoughtful discussions about equitable research models and approaches while those with little information... will get a score reduction." Also an Age Focus (pediatric %) item.

AI DISCLOSURE: "Substantial copying/pasting from other sources is not allowed (the exceptions are similar applications submitted by the applicant to other funders); excessive use of artificial intelligence/large language models is not allowed. Indicate how much if any use of either approach was used in your application."

INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF: every applicable assurance (human subjects/IRB, IACUC + Animal Welfare Assurance number, recombinant DNA, biohazards) "must be accompanied by a signed letter from the appropriate institutional official, including assurances that are pending. Do not send letters signed by yourself nor from anyone outside of the designated institutional offices." "Any application without these letters attached will not be reviewed." Pending IRB is acceptable at submission but must be approved before the award start date.

BUDGET: max $70,000/yr including a minimum $65,000 applicant salary/stipend; indirect costs ≤5% of total, capped at $3,500/yr; remainder to fringe; "Expenditures for laboratory costs/equipment, travel, tuition, etc. are not permitted (some exceptions to this rule apply in the case of K99 recipients)"; "Carry forward of unspent dollars is not permitted for any reason." Childcare stipend up to $3,600/yr for Fellows in mentored positions. No percent-effort requirement.

PORTAL MECHANICS: clicking "Submit" locks that phase; you must self-identify status from two portal indicators ("It is the applicant's responsibility to determine their status"); confirmation emails arrive within 2 business days and often land in spam. Submitted in error or wrong PDF uploaded — BCU staff will help, but the email and correct file must arrive "at least one hour before the deadline" and "there are no exceptions to this rule." After the deadline only two updates are accepted by email: newly accepted manuscripts (with the acceptance letter) and institution transfers.

LONG-LEAD ITEM: you cannot self-register for the portal. First-time applicants must complete the intake form (https://www.llsform.org/ho0999SER/qm43km6adu/index.html) and wait for BCU staff to create the account. Returning applicants reuse their login; password reset is self-service. Portal: https://bloodcancerunited.fluxx.io/ (the legacy https://lls.fluxx.io/ link is still published on the page and reaches the same system).
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
This is the field most often got wrong for CDP Fellow, because the rule is about what you may HOLD, not what you may APPLY with. Both halves, verbatim.

=== WHAT DISQUALIFIES (all about concurrent holding at/after the award start) ===
- "No career development-type award or research grant with a higher total award amount (compared to the Fellow Award) may be held at the time of the award start date. If such an award/grant is activated after receiving a Fellow Award, the Blood Cancer United award must be relinquished."
- Eligibility criterion: applicants must "Not plan to concurrently hold a Fellow award (should it be awarded) together with any career development-type award nor any research grant that has a total value higher than the total value of the Fellow award (the exception is the K99)."
- Non-blood-cancer funders are excluded outright: "an absolute requirement is that the other funding must support blood cancer research. Funding from organizations that are focused on diseases other than blood cancer may not be held concurrently with the Fellow award."
- Independence ends it: "Fellow awardees cannot be independent faculty members and hold the Fellow award within the first year of funding... those already funded must terminate their award at the time they transition to independence if within the first year of funding." BCU "reserves the right to require the return of any funds given after the start of an independent position if this change occurs within the first year."

=== WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half that is usually missing) ===
- PRIOR big awards never block you, and CURRENT ones do not block you from APPLYING: "Those who have previously held any award with a higher total funding amount compared to the Fellow award may apply for a CDP Award. Those who currently hold such an award can apply as well, but they cannot hold that award should they accept the CDP award." So a larger fellowship in hand is a choice to make at acceptance, not a bar at application.
- THE K99 CARVE-OUT (this mechanism's R01/K equivalent): "The exception to this rule is when an applicant has a K99 award. Current K99 awardees may apply for a Fellow award, and current Fellow awardees may accept a K99 award and keep the CDP Award, pending Blood Cancer United approval." Conditions: the K99 aims must be supplied; "An absolute requirement is that the K99 must be directly focused on blood cancer research for it to be compatible with holding the CDP award," with BCU scientific staff having final say; "Note that the NIH/NCI has its own approval process." Reporting duty: "It is required that Fellow applicants and Fellow awardees notify Blood Cancer United of any developments in the K99 application process." Bonus: K99 holders escape the salary-only spending restriction — Fellow funds "may be used for any purpose related to the CDP application/award, whether it be awardee salary, technician salary, or research supplies, pending Blood Cancer United approval."
- SMALLER awards may be held concurrently: "If a career development-type award or research grant (of lower total value compared to the Fellow award) is held by the applicant, this funding may be held concurrently with the Blood Cancer United award at Blood Cancer United's discretion" — but then "the Blood Cancer United funding may only be used to support the applicant/awardee's salary." Note "at Blood Cancer United's discretion," and "Blood Cancer United will not change any aspect of the Fellow award to accommodate other awards (with the exception of the K99 award)."
- SALARY TOP-UP IS EXPRESSLY ALLOWED: "A Fellow's salary/stipend may be supplemented by funds from another source." There is also no effort floor: "there are no requirements for a certain percent effort in our budget template."
- SPONSOR OVERLAP IS EXPECTED, NOT A CONFLICT: "It is expected that there will be overlap of CDP applications with their Sponsor's currently funded grants." Where the overlap is with the Sponsor's OWN BCU application in the same cycle, you must show independent funding exists for your research "(since CDP is salary only)"; such proposals "will have a higher bar" — "Contact researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org for questions about specific proposals."

=== THE REAL LIMITER IS THE CLOCK, NOT A FUNDING COUNTER ===
"Not have more than 3 years of total postdoctoral experience as of July 1 in the year of the award start date." For this cycle (start 1 Oct 2027) the measuring date is 1 July 2027, and the Eligibility Outline sets, for PhD-only applicants, earliest oral thesis defence 30 June 2024 and most recent = the Eligibility Phase due date. All postdoctoral experience counts, in any lab, including time between positions — "the eligibility clock does not start with the start date in your current laboratory." MD: the clock starts when post-MD research exceeds 50% time (typically Hem/Onc fellowship year 2-3); clinical training under 50% research does not start it. Only three pauses exist: parental leave (max 1 year), military service, and government-caused visa delays (visa claims require the application filed within 90 days of thesis defence or end of clinical training, extendable another 90 days). "There are no other acceptable pauses to the eligibility clock." Practical effect: a Fellow applicant realistically gets one or two attempts, ever.

ALSO: "Applicants may only submit one application" per cycle. Sponsor-side limits: any one Sponsor may have one fully-mentored Fellow applicant plus one co-mentored Fellow applicant, and may separately sponsor one Special Fellow and multiple Scholars in the same cycle. Applicant must also hold a PhD/MD/DVM by the Eligibility Phase due date, have ≥1 first-author primary research publication by that date, be at a non-profit academic institution, have no unexplained gaps in training, and not be in a graduate programme taking >20% of their time at the award start date.
result.resubmission_note:
Allowed, uncapped and informal — nothing like NIH's A1 machinery. No numeric limit, no time window, no A0/A1 renumbering, and no "Introduction to Resubmission" page. A resubmission is simply a new application in the next cycle that discloses the prior one.

What is actually required, verbatim from the full application template component list: "Previous CDP Applications (if applicable): If you previously submitted a CDP application that was not funded, briefly describe what has changed from that application. Your prior application may be shared with the current review committee."

So the change narrative is a short template field, not a page — but because reviewers may be handed your previous application, the changes have to be real.

The binding constraints are elsewhere: (1) the 3-year postdoctoral clock, which for most Fellow applicants permits only one or two cycles ever; (2) "Applicants may only submit one application" per cycle; (3) within a cycle, an eligibility submission rejected on administrative grounds may be revised once before the eligibility deadline, but "Submissions rejected based on eligibility criteria may not be resubmitted."

THE HARD PART: you usually cannot learn what went wrong. "Brief, anonymous feedback from the review panel may be provided but only when available." There is no summary statement equivalent, and "All Priority Scores are confidential and are available only to Blood Cancer United oversight committees and staff." No appeals process is described in the CDP guidelines — treat "Not Funded" as final for that cycle. A "Waitlist" status is the strongest available signal to return next cycle.
result.program_officer_contact:
No named program officer, and no phone route. One shared mailbox for everything: **researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org** (note: the stale newsroom page still gives the dead-branded researchprograms@lls.org).

PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT IS EXPECTED, and BCU says when: "it is imperative that any questions be posed to Blood Cancer United as far ahead as possible," because "Blood Cancer United's response time to questions may be delayed by the high volume received near the deadline." Practical translation for this cycle: email in July-September, not in the first half of October.

HIGHEST-VALUE QUESTION TO ASK, and BCU invites it: "Am I in the right subcategory?" — "You may be contacted by a Blood Cancer United staff member if the information provided on your eligibility request suggests that you may be better suited for a different award category." With ~20-30% of eligibility requests historically rejected, asking first is far cheaper than being rejected (and an eligibility-criteria rejection cannot be resubmitted). Fellow vs Special Fellow turns purely on the postdoc clock (≤3 years vs 3-5), so it is exactly the kind of thing staff can settle in one email.

Other things they will answer: eligibility-clock edge cases (parental leave, military service, visa delays, non-US training structures, gaps in training); unusual position titles — "Applicants whose titles significantly differ from the above examples must have a letter submitted by the full application deadline explaining the position," from an institutional representative such as HR; overlap between your proposal and your Sponsor's own BCU application ("Contact researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org for questions about specific proposals"); K99 concurrency approval; a reference letter-writer who never received their link after 2 business days; a missing confirmation email after 2 business days; a missing eligibility decision after 10 business days; submitted-in-error or wrong-PDF fixes (at least one hour before the deadline); institution/lab transfers (notify at least 30 days ahead).

WHAT IS REFUSED: status and results. "Please do not call or email regarding status updates." "Funding status is relayed by email only and is not available by phone." And special treatment: "To create a fair process for all applicants... Do not ask for exceptions to these policies, including but not limited to exceptions to deadlines or making corrections to your document past the deadline."

WHO ELSE TO TALK TO — the mailbox is not your mentor, and for Fellow the Sponsor IS an eligibility criterion. Your prospective Sponsor must have ≥3 first/last-author blood-cancer publications in the last 10 years and, if >5 years independent, "at least one peer-reviewed, nationally competitive research grant providing at least a total of $200,000/year (USD) for at least 3 years" active past the award start date. If your Sponsor has ≤5 years of independence, funding may come from "an R00, institutional startup funds, or other grants" totalling ≥$200,000/yr of blood-cancer-focused funding, plus "at least one competitively awarded grant from outside their institution that has a major blood cancer focus." For junior Sponsors BCU adds: "the competitiveness of applicants with these Sponsors may be lower. Therefore, it is highly recommended that applicants having junior Sponsors assemble a mentorship team." So the real pre-submission conversations are (a) with your Sponsor, to confirm their record clears the bar and to plan the Sponsor Letter and training plan, and (b) with previously funded BCU investigators in your department, whom you can identify by name and institution from the Research We Fund database.
result.examples_or_samples:
BCU publishes NO sample full applications, NO reviewer critiques and NO summary statements for CDP, and there is no RePORTER-style API. Say that plainly to any applicant. What does exist:

1. **The funded portfolio — https://bloodcancerunited.org/research/research-we-fund**, CDP-filtered at https://bloodcancerunited.org/research/research-we-fund?sort_bef_combine=created_DESC&search=&grant_program%5B72006%5D=72006 (the programme page links this as "See our active CDP awardee portfolio"). I verified this filter returns live records, each carrying: PI name, institution, city/state/country, programme, project title, a several-sentence awardee-written summary, and the project term — e.g. Hannah Maul-Newby (Yale), "Revisiting splicing factor mutations in MDS/AML"; Subha Saha (Massachusetts General Hospital), "Leveraging p53 to Improve Menin Inhibition in Leukemia Therapy"; both "Project Term: July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2028".
   CAVEAT I CONFIRMED: records are labelled only "Career Development Program" with NO subcategory, so you cannot filter to Fellow alone — infer from career stage and institution.
   HOW TO USE IT AS A GRANT-WRITER: read 10-15 summaries in a row and calibrate two things: (a) how explicitly funded work ties to blood cancer, patient samples and blood-cancer models — this is the Mission Score in practice, and Mission Score 4-5 is eliminated without review; (b) the register of the public summary, which is a real scored deliverable here (Lay Description min 2,000/max 2,500 characters, Summary max 500).

2. **Named Fellow awardees to approach**, from the CDP page's own testimonials: Annamaria Gulla, MD, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute — "CDP Fellow", project "Optimizing mechanisms for induction of immunogenic cell death to improve clinical outcome in high risk multiple myeloma patients". Also Kasey Leger, MD, Seattle Children's Hospital (CDP Scholar in Clinical Research). Companion investigator view: https://bloodcancerunited.org/research/who-we-fund.

3. **The templates themselves are the closest thing to an annotated sample.** The eligibility template and full application template are downloadable from the Application Document section of the web form inside the portal, and the guidelines say detailed per-element instructions sit on the template itself. The public documents are the 2026-2027 Fellow Guidelines & Instructions (https://llsorg.widen.net/s/zzmvfjzhwm/en-guidelines-and-instructions-cdp-fellow) and the CDP Funding Agreement Template FY27 — read the funding agreement BEFORE applying, since BCU agreements are non-negotiable.

4. **The only route to a real funded application** is a person: find an awardee in your subfield or institution via Research We Fund and ask them directly. Some US university research offices circulate successful LLS/BCU applications internally — ask your research development office. Your own feedback is conditional at best ("Brief, anonymous feedback from the review panel may be provided but only when available").

5. The CDP Achievement Awards page ("See awardees from previous years", linked from the CDP page) highlights the standout awardee in each subcategory including Fellow — useful for identifying exemplars.
