result.deadline_pattern: Annual, dated, and stable in shape. Eligibility phase opens July; eligibility closes mid-October; LOI ~1 November; blind reference letters AND full application ~15 November (same day); award notification July; award start 1 October of the following year. All four CDP subcategories (Fellow, Special Fellow, Scholar, Scholar in Clinical Research) share one identical date set — verified by comparing the Fellow and Scholar Guidelines PDF covers, which are character-identical on dates. Planning horizon for a 1 October 2027 start is roughly 12 months from the first gate. If you are reading after a cycle's eligibility deadline has passed, the same programme reopens at approximately the same point the following year; dates shift by days, not months.
result.loi_deadline: 1 November 2026, 3:00 PM ET — but this is the SECOND of three gates, and the LOI is not the first thing you do. Sequence: (1) Eligibility Phase closes 15 Oct 2026; (2) eligibility determination is rolling, "typically within 2 business days of submission" but may take up to 10 business days; (3) "Letter of Intent Phase: open — Immediately after eligibility is approved"; LOI closes 1 Nov 2026; (4) Full Application opens immediately after LOI submission, closes 15 Nov 2026. CRITICAL STRUCTURAL POINT, and where CDP differs from most LOI mechanisms: the CDP LOI is NOT a competitive triage gate. No one is "invited" or declined on the LOI — every eligibility-approved applicant proceeds. It is a data-capture-and-lock stage. Verbatim: "Information collected in the Letter of Intent Phase will automatically populate fields in the Full Application Phase. Carefully and thoughtfully complete these sections as the fields are locked after the Letter of Intent Phase is completed." And: "Some applicants change this information in the full application, and starting this year, any changes may result in disqualification." So the LOI is where you commit your title, summary, research focus and publication list irrevocably — only 14 days before the full application is due. LOI components (Scholar): reference-letter-writer requests, ORCiD iD, corresponding-author publications since independence, programme information (Summary 3-5 sentences / max 500 characters; Title 150 characters; disease focus, technological approaches, model systems, patients/patient samples), and collaborators/mentors. Note: "Individuals listed here may be contacted by Blood Cancer United to verify a connection." Only 17 days separate the eligibility deadline from the LOI deadline, and "The LOI phase deadline will not be changed based on an eligibility form being returned to the applicant for incomplete and/or unclear information."
result.review_to_award: Full application 15 November 2026 → Award Notification July 2027 (~8 months) → earliest start 1 October 2027 (~10.5 months from submission; ~12 months from the first eligibility gate). Total elapsed from opening the eligibility form (July 2026) to money (1 Oct 2027) is ~15 months. Review sequence: eligibility screen by BCU scientific staff (rolling, 2-10 business days) → Mission Score screen, where "Applications with a Mission Score of 4 or 5 will be eliminated without full review" and Scholar applicants "who do not have an established record of publications and funding demonstrating a commitment to blood cancer research will be disqualified without full review" → peer review by "an independent, voluntary panel of experts" assigning "a Priority Score based on the NIH scoring system" → "Mission-relevant applications (Mission Scores 1, 2, and some 3) will be rank-ordered based on their Priority Score, and those within or near the payline will be presented to Blood Cancer United's oversight committees for approval" → notification July 2027 by email only. DEVIATION FROM FUNDER NORM: unlike TRP (panel meets March 2027, a published month), the CDP 2026-2027 Scholar guidelines do NOT publish a review-panel month — treat the CDP panel date as unconfirmed. The guidelines do refer to an "in-person review meeting" in the Transfers section, so the panel meets in person. Outcome states in the portal are "Awarded" or "Waitlist" or "Not Funded" — note Waitlist is a distinct published outcome, not a soft no. Status is self-service only: "Please do not call or email regarding status updates" and "Funding status is relayed by email only and is not available by phone."
result.submission_requirements:
WHERE SCHOLAR DEVIATES FROM THE CDP/BCU NORM:

1. NO OVERALL PAGE LIMIT IS PUBLISHED. Length is enforced by a locked Word template with preset section lengths, preset margins and preset line spacing, plus character limits on portal fields. The only explicit page limit in the whole Scholar document is the Clinical Protocol Summary, "up to two pages" (and "rare for applicants in this program").

2. IT IS NOT A PROJECT GRANT — the single biggest deviation. "The Scholar award is a subcategory of CDP that exists to support the career development of early- to mid-stage independent investigators. This is not a project grant." The Current and Future Research Program section "should not be presented as a standard, 3 aim research project grant. This should be a broader overview of your total research program." Review criteria: "Comprehensive research project narratives in the style of an R01 are not expected." Reviewers assess your TOTAL research portfolio, and will cross-check it: "Reviewers will downgrade applicants who present a research program that appears tailored to fit Blood Cancer United's Mission, but does not reflect their current program (e.g., if their proposal looks different from their current funding, recent publications, and their website, that will negatively impact the score)."

3. THREE REFERENCE LETTERS, BLIND, HARD-GATED. "If there are not at least 3 letters of reference received by the full application deadline, the application will be administratively disqualified." Three required, "No more than four letters will be accepted." Writers registered by the applicant in the portal during the LOI phase (by 1 Nov 2026); letters due at the full-application deadline (15 Nov 2026). Uploaded directly by the writer via a unique emailed link, never visible to the applicant. "Though not required, it is beneficial to have two of the letters coming from outside your institution." A writer's link can land in spam — chase after 2 business days. A name added in error cannot be deleted.

4. THE SPONSOR IS NOT A MENTOR — Scholar-only redefinition, and easy to get wrong if you read the Fellow guidelines. For Fellow/Special Fellow the Sponsor is the lab head/research mentor with publication and funding tests. For Scholar: "Have a Sponsor who will attest to institutional support for the applicant. An appropriate Sponsor may be a department head, chief of service, or program chair. The Sponsor must be from the same institution and in a supervisory position relative to the applicant." The Sponsor Letter must cover: the applicant's position; the institution's support for the research programme; future plans for career development at the institution; and how the applicant's time will be divided. "The Sponsor Letter is separate from the reference letters; Sponsors may not write a letter of reference." It is not blinded. Also Scholar-only: "There is no limit to the number of applications submitted from a specific institution, nor is there a limit to the number of Scholar (or Scholar in Clinical Research) applications on which a Sponsor is listed" — unlike Fellow/Special Fellow, where Sponsors are capped at two per subcategory.

5. FONT/FORMAT RULES THAT ADMINISTRATIVELY DISQUALIFY. "Font must be black Arial 11 pt. including figure legends, which must be text boxes separate from the figure itself. Tables should also have text with Arial 11 pt. black font." Figures themselves may use smaller text. "Outside of the figures themselves, should any font be smaller than Arial 11 pt. (including shrunken figure legend text boxes, which will appear smaller), the application may be administratively disqualified without review." Line spacing is preset: "Any modifications in line spacing, particularly if the change allows for more text to fit into the page, may result in administrative rejection of your application" (extra space BETWEEN paragraphs is allowed). Character limits include spaces. Context: "approximately 10-15% of all full applications had serious structural flaws."

6. CHARACTER LIMITS (portal + template). Summary 3-5 sentences, max 500 characters incl. spaces. Title 150 characters. Lay Description MINIMUM 2,000 and maximum 2,500 characters — a floor people miss; it is a real scored deliverable used for fundraising. Scientific Abstract 1,500 characters max. Brief Biography 1,000 characters max.

7. REQUIRED COMPONENTS. Section 1 Abstracts and Brief Biography; Section 2 Programme Description Template; Section 3 Budget; Section 4 Assurances; Section 5 Research Tags; Section 6 Attachments. Section 2 includes Applicant/Programme Information (Title and Summary "must exactly match what was provided at the LOI stage"), Writing Source, Previous CDP Applications, Current Non-Blood Cancer Research, Description of Models/Drugs/Reagents/Trials tables, up to two Graphical Abstracts ("must not be professionally developed... developed primarily by the applicant using tools readily available in a typical lab"), Current and Future Research Program, Disease Demographics and Equitable Research Models and Approaches, Age Focus of Research, References (Blood citation format), Access to Non-Commercially Available Reagents, and a Signature Page.

8. AI DISCLOSURE IS MANDATORY AND CAPPED. "Writing Source: Excessive use of artificial intelligence/large language models is not allowed. Indicate how much was used in your application."

9. DEMOGRAPHICS SECTION IS SCORED BOTH WAYS. "Reviewers will give a score boost to those with clear information on demographics and thoughtful discussions about equitable research models and approaches while those with little information on demographics and a lack of thoughtful discussions about equitable research will get a score reduction."

10. ATTACHMENTS (Section 6), in template order, nothing else: NIH Biosketch AND a separate Other Support document, both in NIH format (eRA Commons User Name not required; any recent NIH version acceptable); Sponsor Letter; Collaboration/Support Letters where applicable (signed, on letterhead, "typically 1 or 2 brief paragraphs" — keep them factual or they get counted as reference letters and can disqualify you); Clinical Protocol Summary where applicable. "No attachments besides those listed above should be included, nor should there be any attachments preceding the template (e.g., no cover letters)."

11. INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF ON ASSURANCES IS A REVIEW GATE. "All assurances that are applicable to your research must be accompanied by a signed letter from the appropriate institutional official, including assurances that are pending... Any application without these letters attached will not be reviewed." IRB/IACUC may be pending at submission but must be obtained before the award start date.

12. ONE COMBINED PDF. "Failure to submit as a single PDF in the order described on the template may result in disqualification of the application." Clicking Submit locks that phase. You must self-identify your status from two portal indicators: "It is the applicant's responsibility to determine their status." Confirmation emails arrive within 2 business days and often land in spam.

13. CROSS-PHASE CONSISTENCY IS ENFORCED. "Divergence between information provided at the Eligibility and/or Letter of Intent Phases and information provided at the Full Application Phase may result in administrative disqualification." Publication lists are fact-checked: "Applications will be checked by Blood Cancer United scientific staff for accuracy. Significant deviations from publicly available information may result in administrative disqualification."

14. BUDGET. Max $120,000/year covering salary and fringe benefits only. Indirect costs capped at 5% of total award. "Expenditures for laboratory costs/equipment, travel, tuition, etc. are not permitted." "Carry forward of unspent dollars is not permitted for any reason in this program." "The final value of the award may be limited by the policy of the applicant's Institution."

15. LONG-LEAD ITEMS: you cannot self-register for the portal (intake form; BCU staff create accounts), your institution must be registered with named officials, and an ORCiD iD is mandatory at the LOI phase. Start these weeks out. Only two post-deadline updates are accepted by email: newly accepted manuscripts, and institutional transfers.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
THE DEFINING FEATURE OF THIS MECHANISM, AND IT INVERTS THE NIH K LOGIC: for an NIH career-development award, holding an R01 disqualifies you. For a BCU Scholar, holding substantial independent funding is a REQUIREMENT. Applicants with no major grant are not merely weaker — they are ineligible.

WHAT YOU MUST HAVE (eligibility floor):
- "Have adequate funding to support the proposed blood cancer research; at least one blood cancer-focused grant having a minimum total of $200,000/year (USD) going to the applicant for at least 3 years and which is active after the CDP award start date is sufficient to qualify."
- Eligibility Outline table, note b: "Must be at least one peer-reviewed, nationally competitive research grant providing at least a total of $200,000/year (USD) for at least 3 years."
- Role test: "The applicant must be the Program Director, Principal Investigator (PI), Other Principal Investigator, co-Principal Investigator, multiple PI, Project Leader, and/or other titles that clearly signify full or equal responsibility for the grant's oversight in order for that grant to qualify for eligibility. The position of co-investigator does not count for eligibility."
- "Funding typically will be an R01. However, other funding sources qualify if they have the other characteristics listed above. Applicants with no R01 funding on which they have sole or shared responsibility are less competitive."
- Evidence required: attach documentation from the funding agency (agency, type, total and annual amounts, start and end dates) at the end of the application template.

WHAT DOES NOT COUNT TOWARD THAT FLOOR (but does not disqualify you):
- "This must not be only start-up funds, a transitional award, or a career development-type award."
- "Applicants may have transitional awards, but these cannot be used for eligibility purposes. Funding cannot be only startup funds."
- "Research support that ends prior to the award start date may not be used as evidence of adequate support."
- Timing carve-out: "We will consider Sponsor funding that starts after the eligibility due date but prior to the Blood Cancer United funding start date," and the Eligibility Outline confirms "it is acceptable to have a letter demonstrating that funding will occur by the funding start date in cases where the funding starts after the eligibility due date." So a just-awarded R01 that has not yet started can qualify you with a letter.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES (concurrency, not history):
- "Not concurrently hold a Scholar award together with any career development-type award that has a total value higher than the total value of the Scholar award." (Scholar total = $120,000 x 5 = $600,000.)
- "No career development-type award having a higher total award amount compared to the Scholar award may be held at the time of the award start date. If such an award is activated after receiving a Scholar Award, the Blood Cancer United award must be relinquished."
- "Career development-type funding from organizations that are focused on diseases other than blood cancer may not be held concurrently with the Scholar award."
- Rank: "those who are full professors, or who will be as of the award start date, are no longer eligible to apply."
- Sector: "Should an applicant or awardee obtain a position at a for-profit entity, even part-time, they are no longer eligible to hold the Scholar Award. Any funds disbursed after this change in status making the awardee no longer eligible must be returned."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half applicants most often get wrong):
- Having HELD a larger career-development award in the past is fine: "Those who have previously held any career development-type award with a higher total funding amount compared to the Scholar award may apply for a Scholar Award."
- CURRENTLY holding one is also fine at application time — you just cannot hold both: "Those who currently hold such an award can apply as well, but they cannot hold that award should they accept the Scholar award." So a current K-award holder may apply; the choice only bites at the 1 Oct 2027 start.
- A SMALLER career-development award may run concurrently: "If a career development-type award (of lower total value compared to the Scholar award) is held by the applicant, this funding may be held concurrently with the Blood Cancer United award at Blood Cancer United's discretion" — provided "the other funding must support blood cancer research."
- R01s and other research project grants are never a conflict; they are the qualifying credential.
- Salary may be topped up: "A Scholar's salary may be supplemented by funds from other sources."

NON-FUNDING ELIGIBILITY THAT GATES THE SAME APPLICANT (the real limiter — an eligibility clock, not a resubmission counter):
- Window: "Have started their first independent position no less than 4 years but not more than 8 years as of January 1 in the year of the award start date." For the 2026-2027 cycle the Eligibility Outline gives exact dates: earliest start of independent position 1 January 2019; most recent 1 January 2023. (Scholar in Clinical Research runs wider: earliest 1 January 2017.) "The minimum years of independence for eligibility is now 4 years" — a change this cycle.
- "Instructor-level positions are not counted as independent for eligibility purposes. However, all non-mentored positions are considered independent for this calculation (e.g., positions with the title 'Research Professor,' 'Assistant Research Professor,' 'Adjunct Assistant Professor,' etc.)." Worked example from the guidelines: "if you were a research assistant professor for 5 years and a tenure-track assistant professor for 4 years, you would have 9 years of experience and you would therefore be ineligible to apply." This catches many people.
- Publications: at least two full-length, peer-reviewed, primary-research, CORRESPONDING-author publications primarily on blood cancer, earned as an independent investigator, by the eligibility due date. Co-corresponding counts; "'contributing equally' or other similar terms do not count"; publications from a prior mentored position do not count; preprints do not count. (Scholar has no first-author requirement.)
- Portfolio concentration: "Have a total research program that is at least 75% focused on direct blood cancer research," and "Those with less than 75% blood cancer-focus in their research programs are not likely a good fit for the Scholar award."
- One application per applicant per cycle; open worldwide to any nationality at non-profit academic institutions.
result.program_officer_contact:
NO NAMED PROGRAM OFFICER — there is no NIH-style assigned PO for this mechanism. One shared mailbox is the only channel: researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org (the stale newsroom page still prints the dead legacy address researchprograms@lls.org — do not use it). The same mailbox handles scientific questions, eligibility, and portal technical support.

PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT IS EXPECTED, AND EARLY. Verbatim: "Blood Cancer United's response time to questions may be delayed by the high volume received near the deadline. Therefore, it is imperative that any questions be posed to Blood Cancer United as far ahead as possible." Practical translation for this cycle: email July-September 2026, not the first half of October.

WHAT TO ASK, AND WHEN (highest value before the 15 Oct eligibility gate):
- "Which subcategory am I?" — the single most useful question, because BCU triages: "You may be contacted by a Blood Cancer United staff member if the information provided on your eligibility request suggests that you may be better suited for a different award category." Scholar vs Scholar in Clinical Research turns on whether your work directly involves patients; Scholar vs a project grant turns on whether your programme is >=75% blood cancer. Asking is cheaper than rejection: "In prior award cycles, ~20-30% of eligibility requests were rejected."
- Eligibility-clock edge cases: ambiguous or non-US position titles, research-professor years, gaps. "positions that are not clear as to whether they are mentored positions or independent positions must also have a letter explaining the nature of the position(s)" — from an institutional representative such as HR, due by the full application deadline; eligibility can be provisionally accepted pending it.
- Whether a specific grant satisfies the research-support requirement (especially co-PI/multi-PI roles, non-US national agencies, or funding that starts after the eligibility date).
- Institutional transfers: "If a transfer is being considered, notify Blood Cancer United at least 30 days prior to the transfer date."
- Portal/institution registration, adding institutional officials, getting an assistant a portal account.
- Submitted-in-error or wrong-PDF fixes — but only before the deadline: "Contact researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org if you submit in error (must be at least one hour prior to the deadline)" and "This email must be received, with the correct document, prior to the deadline; there are no exceptions to this rule."
- Missing confirmation email after 2 business days; missing eligibility decision after 10 business days; a referee who never received their link after 2 business days.

FLATLY REFUSED: status chasing ("Please do not call or email regarding status updates"); results by phone ("Funding status is relayed by email only and is not available by phone"); and exceptions ("Do not ask for exceptions to these policies, including but not limited to exceptions to deadlines or making corrections to your document past the deadline").

WHO ELSE TO TALK TO — the mailbox is not your mentor. Because Scholar is programme-centric rather than project-centric, the highest-value conversations are: (1) your prospective Sponsor, i.e. your department chair or division chief, since the Sponsor Letter must commit the institution to your career development and institutional support is an explicit review criterion — start that conversation before October, not in November; (2) previously funded BCU investigators in your department or subfield, identifiable by name and institution from the Research We Fund database and the CDP awardees page; (3) your research office, on the institutional Fluxx registration and the signed assurance letters, which need lead time.
result.examples_or_samples:
NO SAMPLE APPLICATIONS, NO REVIEWER CRITIQUES AND NO SUMMARY STATEMENTS ARE PUBLISHED — say this plainly to any applicant. Even your own feedback is conditional: "Brief, anonymous feedback from the review panel may be provided but only when available." There is no NIH-style summary statement and no RePORTER-equivalent API.

WHAT DOES EXIST, AND IT IS GENUINELY USEFUL:

1. The CDP-filtered funded portfolio — the closest thing to RePORTER here, and linked by BCU itself from the CDP page as "See our active CDP awardee portfolio": https://bloodcancerunited.org/research/research-we-fund?sort_bef_combine=created_DESC&search=&grant_program%5B72006%5D=72006 — VERIFIED LIVE AND POPULATED. Each record carries PI name, institution, city/state/country, the funding programme, project title, a several-sentence awardee-written project summary, and the project term. Sample records confirmed: Hannah Maul-Newby (Yale, New Haven CT), "Revisiting splicing factor mutations in MDS/AML"; Emel Kirbas Cilingir (University of Miami); Stefan Tarnawsky (Washington University in St. Louis) — each with "Project Term: July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2028".

2. FINDING THE SCHOLAR RECORDS SPECIFICALLY — a derived heuristic, not a funder statement, so use it as such: the database labels records only "Career Development Program" without the subcategory, but award durations are fixed and distinct, so the project term identifies the rung. A FIVE-year term is a Scholar (or Scholar in Clinical Research); three years is a Fellow; two or three a Special Fellow. Filter to CDP, then read the 5-year terms.

3. Why the database is reliably populated: awardees sign a media consent and supply a headshot as a condition of the funding agreement — which is also why the companion investigator-centred view exists: https://bloodcancerunited.org/research/who-we-fund

4. CDP Achievement Award awardees, listed by subcategory (Scholar/Scholar in Clinical Research, Special Fellow, Fellow): https://bloodcancerunited.org/research/grants/career-development-program-cdp/awardees — the cleanest published list of named, identifiable Scholar-level awardees to approach.

5. Named awardee testimonials on the CDP page itself, with institution and funded project title — e.g. Kasey Leger MD, Seattle Children's Hospital, CDP Scholar in Clinical Research, "Cardioprotective Strategies and Cardiotoxicity Prediction in Children with Acute Myeloid Leukemia"; Annamaria Gulla MD, Dana-Farber, CDP Fellow. Useful for identifying people to contact.

HOW TO USE THE PORTFOLIO AS A GRANT-WRITER, not a reader: filter to CDP, read 10-15 five-year-term summaries in a row, and calibrate two things. (a) The Mission Score in practice — how explicitly funded work ties to blood cancer, patient samples and blood-cancer models; Mission Scores of 4 or 5 are eliminated without review, and Score 1 requires patients or patient materials including PDX models. (b) The register of the public summary, which is a real scored deliverable (Lay Description, minimum 2,000 and maximum 2,500 characters) — these published summaries are the closest public analogue to it.

THE ONLY ROUTE TO A REAL FULL APPLICATION: find an awardee in your subfield or at your own institution via the portfolio or the awardees page and ask them directly for theirs. Some US university research offices also circulate successful LLS/BCU applications internally — ask your research development office. Note one Scholar-specific trap when reading older examples: applications funded before the switch from project-based to research-programme-based review are structurally obsolete as models, even though the science still calibrates Mission relevance.
result.resubmission_note:
ALLOWED, UNCAPPED, AND INFORMAL — nothing like NIH's A1 machinery. No numeric limit, no waiting period, no A0/A1 renumbering, and no "Introduction to Resubmission" page. A resubmission is simply a new application in a later cycle that discloses the prior one.

THE ONLY REQUIREMENT, verbatim from the Scholar full-application template component list: "Previous CDP Applications (if applicable): If you have previously submitted a Scholar-level CDP application that was not funded, briefly describe what has changed from that application. Your prior application may be shared with the current review committee." So the change narrative is a short template field, not a page — but reviewers may be handed your previous application, so the changes must be real and visible.

WHAT ACTUALLY LIMITS YOU IS THE ELIGIBILITY CLOCK, NOT A RESUBMISSION COUNTER. The Scholar window is 4 to 8 years from the start of your first independent position, measured at 1 January of the award-start year, with all non-mentored positions counted. That is a five-cycle window at most, and it shrinks by one cycle each year you wait. Only three things pause it — parental leave (max 1 year), military service, and visa delays from unusual governmental delays ("these are very rare") — requested in the Eligibility Window Extension section of the eligibility template.

OTHER HARD LIMITS: "Applicants may only submit one application" per cycle. Within a cycle, an eligibility submission rejected on administrative grounds (missing or unclear information) may be revised once before the eligibility deadline, but "Submissions rejected based on eligibility criteria may not be resubmitted."

THE HARD PART OF RESUBMITTING HERE: you usually cannot see what went wrong. Feedback is "Brief, anonymous... but only when available," Priority Scores are confidential to BCU staff and oversight committees, and there is no summary statement. A "Waitlist" status is a distinct published outcome and is the strongest available signal to return next cycle. NO APPEALS PROCESS is described anywhere in the guidelines — treat "Not Funded" as final for that cycle.

STRUCTURAL WARNING FOR ANYONE RESUBMITTING FROM AN OLDER ATTEMPT: the Scholar application changed fundamentally from project-based to research-programme-based. A prior Scholar application built around specific aims cannot simply be revised — it has to be rewritten as a total-research-programme document.

The Transfers section refers to an 'in-person review meeting', confirming the panel meets in person, but no month is stated. Treat the CDP panel month as not found — do not infer it from the stale website FAQ.

The accordion did not render its contents in the DOM I could sample, and the browser tab was repeatedly taken over by parallel agents. Payline / success rate not published. The guidelines reference 'the payline' and rank-ordering but give no number, and no award count or applicant count is published for Scholar. The only published rates are administrative: ~20-30% of eligibility requests rejected, >10% of CDP applications disqualified for Mission non-compliance, ~10-15% of full applications carrying serious structural flaws.

I did not open the current PDF, so I cannot confirm its revision month; the account-creation and institutional-registration facts I report are sourced from the Scholar Guidelines itself, not from the P&P.

Whether the Scholar Word template imposes explicit per-section page or line counts is not determinable from the Guidelines PDF alone — the guidelines say section lengths are preset and enforced in the locked template, but the template itself is only downloadable from inside the Fluxx portal after eligibility approval, which requires an account that only BCU staff can create. No overall page limit is published anywhere in the Scholar guidelines.

result.next_deadline:
DATED AND PUBLISHED. The 2026-2027 CDP cycle has three gates, all at 3:00 PM ET. From the funder's own current-cycle Guidelines & Instructions PDF (cover page reads "Career Development Program / Guidelines & Instructions / Fellow / July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027"), whose "Key Dates" table reads verbatim: "Eligibility Phase: open — July 2026"; "Eligibility Phase: close — October 15, 2026; 3:00 PM (ET)"; "Eligibility determination by Blood Cancer United staff — Rolling; typically within 2 business days of submission"; "Letter of Intent Phase: open — Immediately after eligibility is approved"; "Letter of Intent Phase: close — November 1, 2026, 3:00 PM (ET)"; "Full Application Phase: open — Immediately after Letter of Intent Phase submission"; "Reference letters due — November 15, 2026, 3:00 PM (ET)"; "Full Application Phase: close — November 15, 2026, 3:00 PM (ET)"; "Award Notification — July 2027"; "Award Start Date — October 1, 2027".

NEXT ACTIONABLE DATE: **15 October 2026, 3:00 PM ET** (Eligibility Phase close). This is the real front door — you cannot reach the LOI without passing it, and determination is rolling, so submitting late in the window compresses everything downstream.

Enforcement, verbatim: "The submission deadlines will be enforced. Please note that all times are Eastern Time (ET). If any date falls on a weekend or US holiday, the deadline becomes the next business day." And: "It is highly recommended that submissions are done the day prior to the deadline."

CAVEAT THE APPLICANT MUST KNOW — THE FUNDER CONTRADICTS ITSELF. The live CDP web page carries a banner, "The submission period for CDP is now closed", and beneath it a timeline table headed "2022-2023 Application Timeline" (eligibility close November 1, 2022; "Abstract Phase" close November 8, 2022; reference letters December 16, 2022; Award Start Date July 1, 2023). That page is demonstrably stale on multiple independent markers: it calls the funder "LLS", points to the legacy portal lls.fluxx.io, links a Policies & Procedures PDF dated April 2020, calls the middle phase the "Abstract Phase" (the current PDF calls it the "Letter of Intent Phase"), and states an award start of "July 1 of the upcoming year" where the current PDF says 1 October 2027. Per the funder's own hierarchy the Guidelines & Instructions PDF governs. I could not independently confirm the portal is presently accepting submissions — bloodcancerunited.fluxx.io reveals open programmes only after sign-in ("Please check the Apply for Funding tab on the left once you have signed in to see which programs are currently accepting applications") and I did not log in. Confirm by emailing researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org before relying on the 15 Oct 2026 date.

RECURRING PATTERN, for anyone reading after a cycle closes: eligibility opens ~July, closes mid-October; LOI ~1 November; references and full application ~15 November; notification July; start 1 October. The same programme reopens at approximately the same point the following year — dates shift by days, not months. Plan on ~11.5 months from the eligibility gate to the award start.
result.deadline_pattern: Annual, dated, per-mechanism, every deadline at 3:00 PM Eastern. All four CDP subcategories (Fellow, Special Fellow, Scholar, Scholar in Clinical Research) run on one shared CDP date set. Cycle shape: Eligibility opens July, closes mid-October → LOI closes ~1 November → blind reference letters and full application both close ~15 November → award notification July → award start 1 October of the following year. Weekend/US-holiday deadlines roll to the next business day. Across Blood Cancer United generally, LOIs cluster August-October, full applications November-January, everyone is notified in July and everyone starts 1 October.
result.loi_deadline:
1 November 2026, 3:00 PM ET — but this is the SECOND of three gates, and describing CDP as "LOI plus full application" understates it.

GATE 1, Eligibility Phase, closes 15 October 2026, 3:00 PM ET. A hard staff-reviewed gate before you may write anything. Verbatim: "In prior award cycles, ~20-30% of eligibility requests were rejected." Rolling determination, "typically within 2 business days of submission". Recovery is asymmetric and worth memorising: "If an eligibility submission is rejected for administrative reasons (e.g., missing or unclear information), one revised submission may be made prior to the eligibility deadline. Submissions rejected based on eligibility criteria may not be resubmitted."

GATE 2, Letter of Intent Phase, closes 1 November 2026 — only 17 days after eligibility closes, and it opens only "Immediately after eligibility is approved". Unlike Blood Cancer United's TRP/ACT/DGP, the CDP LOI is NOT a competitive triage gate — every eligibility-approved applicant proceeds. Its danger is different: IT LOCKS YOUR APPLICATION. Verbatim: "Information collected in the Letter of Intent Phase will automatically populate fields in the Full Application Phase. Carefully and thoughtfully complete these sections as the fields are locked after the Letter of Intent Phase is completed. Letter of Intent Phase components must accurately reflect the focus of the full application. Failure to follow these policies may result in disqualification of the application." And: "applicants must place some of that LOI information on the full application template. This information must exactly match... Some applicants change this information in the full application, and starting this year, any changes may result in disqualification." Also: "The Title and Summary must exactly match what was provided at the LOI stage. If it differs, the application may be disqualified or that information may be replaced with the information provided at the LOI phase."

Two long-lead items are due at the LOI, not the full application: your ORCiD iD ("we now require all applicants to sign up for ORCiD (https://orcid.org/) and provide their ORCiD number during the LOI phase"), and registration of your reference-letter writers in the portal.

GATE 3, Full Application + blind reference letters, both close 15 November 2026 — 14 days after the LOI.

PLANNING CONSEQUENCE: the science must be settled before 1 November, because after that the title, summary and focus are frozen. The three gates span only 31 days end to end, but the writing has to be finished before the first one closes.
result.review_to_award:
Full application 15 November 2026 → award notification July 2027 → earliest award start 1 October 2027. That is roughly 8 months submission-to-notification and about 10.5 months submission-to-start; measured from the real first gate (eligibility, 15 October 2026) the horizon is ~11.5 months to money.

Review sequence: "CDP applications are reviewed by an independent, voluntary panel of experts." Each application receives "a Priority Score based on the NIH scoring system", plus a separate Mission Score for blood-cancer relevance. Then: "After the review panel meeting, Mission-relevant applications (Mission Scores 1, 2, and some 3) will be rank-ordered based on their Priority Scores and those within or near the payline will be presented to Blood Cancer United's oversight committees for approval. Funding will be based on ranking, Mission Scores, and Blood Cancer United priorities."

DEVIATION FROM THE FUNDER NORM: the CDP panel month is NOT published in the 2026-2027 guidelines (TRP publishes a March 2027 panel; CDP does not). The stale website FAQ implies a January review — treat the CDP panel month as unconfirmed.

Notification mechanics: "Funding status is relayed by email only and is not available by phone." Portal status runs "Under Review" → "Awarded" or "Waitlist," or "Not Funded." Note that Waitlist is a distinct published outcome, not a soft no. "All Priority Scores are confidential and are available only to Blood Cancer United oversight committees and staff."

Between notification and start (July-September 2027) sits execution of a funding agreement that must be signed by the PI plus institutional officials; nothing activates until Blood Cancer United fully executes it.
result.submission_requirements:
SOURCING NOTE, IMPORTANT: everything below is quoted from the CURRENT-CYCLE CDP **Fellow** Guidelines & Instructions PDF (July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027). I could not retrieve the Special Fellow edition — see "unresolved". CDP subcategory guidelines are near-identical in machinery and share one date set; the Special Fellow document differs on the eligibility window, award value and budget ceiling. Verify the Special Fellow PDF when the cycle reopens.

THREE-PHASE STRUCTURE: Eligibility (web form + an eligibility template obtained from the portal) → LOI → Full Application.

REFERENCE LETTERS — the sharpest disqualifier. "If there are not at least 3 letters of reference received by the full application deadline, the application will be administratively disqualified." Policies verbatim: "Reference letter information must be provided by the applicant at the Letter of Intent stage, but the letters are not due until the full application deadline"; "Three letters are required"; "No more than four letters will be accepted"; "It is beneficial to have a backup letter-writer in case one of your original writers is not able to submit on time"; "Though not required, it is beneficial to have two of the letters coming from outside your institution"; "Letters are blinded to the applicant and must be uploaded directly by the writer". Writers are registered by the applicant in the portal during the LOI phase and upload through a unique link; you never see the letters. "It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that the letters are submitted... Letters received by Blood Cancer United after the deadline will not be accepted."

SPONSOR LETTER — separate and heavily weighted. "The Sponsor Letter is separate from the reference letters and therefore is not considered one of the three reference letters"; "Sponsors may not write a reference letter." Must be "signed and on institutional letterhead". "The Sponsor Letter forms a critical part of the review process. Applicants with Sponsor Letters that follow the rules and clearly outline appropriate mentorship will have a better chance of funding." A Sponsor Mentor Table must also be completed by the Sponsor.

OTHER SUPPORT — a documented, recurring administrative kill. "The Sponsor and the applicant must each have their own Other Support documents. The Sponsor must use the NIH Other Support document. The applicant must use the Blood Cancer United Other Support form that is a part of the application." "Failure to provide separate Other Support Documents for the applicant and for the Sponsor may result in administrative disqualification... This includes failure to fill out the form or providing the Sponsor's other support on the applicant's Other Support form."

INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF: a Signature Page ("Please ensure all signatures requested are complete. Electronic signatures are acceptable"), plus assurances: "All assurances that are applicable to your research must be accompanied by a signed letter from the appropriate institutional official, including assurances that are pending. Do not send letters signed by yourself nor from anyone outside of the designated institutional offices. ... Any application without these letters attached will not be reviewed." IRB/IACUC status and dates required; "Full approval for any IRBs that are necessary for the research must be obtained by the award start date."

COLLABORATION/SUPPORT LETTERS: required "when access to patient samples, animal models, or specialized equipment outside of the applicant's laboratory or department is necessary". Keep them to "1 or 2 brief paragraphs" describing only the support — praise turns them into reference letters and can breach the four-letter cap. "Outside of the Sponsor Letter, any letter attached to the application that is not primarily a letter of collaboration and/or a letter stating access to materials and/or other resources may result in administrative disqualification."

LENGTH: NO overall page limit is published. Length is enforced by a LOCKED Word template plus hard character limits: Summary "no more than 500 characters, including" spaces; Title "150-character limit, including spaces"; Lay Description "a minimum of 2,000 characters and a maximum of 2,500 characters" (a MINIMUM — routinely missed; no Greek/scientific symbols); Scientific Abstract "1,500 characters maximum, including spaces"; brief professional biography "1,000 characters"; Clinical Protocol Summary where applicable "up to two pages" and "Do not attach a full clinical protocol." "Character limits include spaces. Character and other length limits are strictly enforced."

FORMAT RULES THAT KILL APPLICATIONS: "Use Arial 11 pt. black font in each section of the application. This includes figure legends, which must be separate text boxes that use Arial 11 pt. black font. Do not shrink the figure legends... Tables must also use Arial 11 pt. black font." Figures themselves may use smaller text. "Outside of the figures themselves, should any font be smaller than Arial 11 pt. ... the application may be administratively disqualified without review." "Line spacing is preset in the Word document. Do not change the setting. Pasting text from another document, which should generally be avoided, may result in a change in the line spacing... Any modifications in line spacing, particularly if the change allows for more text to fit into the page" may cause rejection (extra space between paragraphs is allowed).

SCORED SECTIONS PEOPLE UNDER-PREPARE: Disease Demographics and Equitable Research Models and Approaches. "Reviewers will give a score boost to those with clear information on demographics and thoughtful discussions about equitable research models and approaches while those with little information on demographics and a lack of thoughtful discussions about equitable research will get a score reduction." Start with SEER. Also required: Age Focus of Research (percentage pediatric); References in "the Blood citation format"; Description of Models, Drugs/Reagents, and Trials tables; Access to Non-Commercially Available Reagents, Drugs, and Models; up to two Graphical Abstracts; and a writing-sources declaration — "Substantial copying/pasting from other sources is not allowed (the exceptions are similar applications submitted by the applicant to other funders); excessive use of artificial intelligence/large language models is not allowed. Indicate how much if any use of either approach was used in your application."

FINAL ASSEMBLY: "Upload the full application components, as a single PDF on the web form. All documents must be combined into a single PDF in the order listed above before uploading. Failure to submit as a single PDF in the order above may result in disqualification." "No attachments besides those listed above should be included, nor should there be any attachments preceding the template (e.g., no cover letters). Applications that include additional documents besides those requested may be administratively disqualified."

BUDGET (Fellow figures; Special Fellow is $75,000/yr with a $70,000/yr minimum to the awardee per the CDP web page — the Special Fellow indirect-cost and carry-forward rules are unverified): Fellow max "$70,000 each year", minimum "$65,000 for the applicant's salary/stipend", "Indirect costs may be included and cannot exceed 5% of the total award amount requested in the proposal, up to $3,500 per year", "Expenditures for laboratory costs/equipment, travel, tuition, etc. are not permitted (some exceptions to this rule apply in the case of K99 recipients)", "Carry forward of unspent dollars is not permitted for any reason in this program". Special Fellows in mentored positions "may receive up to $3,600/year" as a childcare stipend.

PORTAL MECHANICS: you cannot self-register — an account is created for you via the intake form (https://www.llsform.org/ho0999SER/qm43km6adu/index.html); returning applicants reuse their old login. Submitting locks that phase. "You must confirm each stage of the application process by checking your application status on the Blood Cancer United Research Portal; there are two indicators of your status, and you must self-identify your place in the process." If you upload the wrong PDF, staff will help "if you are unable to delete the incorrect document" but "This email must be received, with the correct document, prior to the deadline; there are no exceptions to this rule." After the deadline only two updates are accepted: manuscripts accepted for publication (with author list, title, journal, date and the acceptance letter) and institutional transfers.

TRANSFERS: "the applicant must be in the new lab by the full application due date. Transfers to a new lab with a new Sponsor are not allowed between the full application due date and the award start date."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
THE CENTRAL RULE IS A VALUE TEST, NOT A NAMED-AWARD LIST — and it bites at the award start date, not at application. Quoted from the current-cycle CDP Fellow guidelines; for Special Fellow the same structure applies with the comparison made against the Special Fellow award value ($75,000/yr for two or three years) rather than the Fellow award. Treat the threshold substitution as unverified until the Special Fellow PDF is read.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES: "No career development-type award or research grant with a higher total award amount (compared to the Fellow Award) may be held at the time of the award start date. If such an award/grant is activated after receiving a Fellow Award, the Blood Cancer United award must be relinquished."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — three distinct carve-outs, and this is the half applicants never hear:

1. PRIOR HOLDING IS FINE, AND SO IS CURRENT HOLDING AT APPLICATION TIME. "Those who have previously held any award with a higher total funding amount compared to the Fellow award may apply for a CDP Award. Those who currently hold such an award can apply as well, but they cannot hold that award should they accept the CDP award." So a large current award is a choice you make at the start date, not a bar to applying.

2. SMALLER CONCURRENT AWARDS MAY BE HELD. "If a career development-type award or research grant (of lower total value compared to the Fellow award) is held by the applicant, this funding may be held concurrently with the Blood Cancer United award at Blood Cancer United's discretion... In all such cases, the Blood Cancer United funding may only be used to support the applicant/awardee's salary." Note: "Blood Cancer United will not change any aspect of the Fellow award to accommodate other awards (with the exception of the K99 award)."

3. THE K99 EXCEPTION — the single most valuable carve-out for a senior postdoc, and it runs in both directions. "The exception to this rule is when an applicant has a K99 award. Current K99 awardees may apply for a Fellow award, and current Fellow awardees may accept a K99 award and keep the CDP Award, pending Blood Cancer United approval. Certain information, including the aims of the K99 award, must be provided to Blood Cancer United to ensure that the K99-funded research is directly relevant to Blood Cancer United's Mission." Conditions: "An absolute requirement is that the K99 must be directly focused on blood cancer research for it to be compatible with holding the CDP award. Blood Cancer United scientific staff will have the final say." Also, uniquely for K99 holders, the money loosens: "Funding from the Fellow Award may be used for any purpose related to the CDP application/award, whether it be awardee salary, technician salary, or research supplies, pending Blood Cancer United approval." A reporting duty attaches: "It is required that Fellow applicants and Fellow awardees notify Blood Cancer United of any developments in the K99 application process." And "Note that the NIH/NCI has its own approval process."

THE ABSOLUTE BAR THAT CATCHES PEOPLE WITH PERFECTLY GOOD FUNDING: "an absolute requirement is that the other funding must support blood cancer research. Funding from organizations that are focused on diseases other than blood cancer may not be held concurrently with the Fellow award. This requirement reflects the necessity that a Fellow's research should be fully (or largely) focused directly on blood cancer." A concurrent award from a general-cancer or non-blood-cancer disease foundation is therefore a conflict even when it is small.

WHAT ACTUALLY LIMITS YOU IS THE ELIGIBILITY CLOCK, NOT A RESUBMISSION COUNTER. Special Fellow requires "between 3 and 5 years of postdoctoral research training by the award start date" (award start 1 October 2027), in a mentored position. The window can be paused only for: "Parental leave (maximum of 1 year)", "Military service", and "Visa delays that are caused by governmental agencies" — declared in the Eligibility Window Extension section with dates. Visa extensions require the application to have been submitted within 90 calendar days of the oral thesis defence or end of clinical training, and "Visa eligibility extensions are not given for applicants who have decided to stay in their" current situation by choice.

STATUS CHANGE IS ALSO A CONFLICT. For Fellow: "Fellow awardees cannot be independent faculty members and hold the Fellow award within the first year of funding... those already funded must terminate their award at the time they transition to independence if within the first year of funding." Blood Cancer United "reserves the right to require the return of any funds given after the start of an independent position". The Special Fellow award is explicitly designed to make you "competitive for an independent position by the end of the award", so the Special Fellow rule on transitioning to independence is very likely different — do not assume the Fellow wording applies. Unverified.

PER-CYCLE AND PER-LAB CAPS: "Applicants may only submit one application." On the Sponsor side the Fellow PDF states "A Sponsor may sponsor one Fellow in their own lab, one Special Fellow in their own lab, as well as multiple Scholar applicants in this application cycle. There is no limit to the number of applications submitted from a specific institution. It is acceptable for a Sponsor who currently has active Fellow and/or Special Fellow awardees in their lab to sponsor a Fellow applicant during another award cycle." The CDP web page states a relaxed version for the current cycle: "we now allow up to two Fellow and two Special Fellow applications from any one Sponsor during this application cycle. However, there can be no more than 4 total Fellows and Special Fellows in any lab". The two sources are worded inconsistently; "The applicant is required to coordinate with their Sponsor to be sure that this policy is upheld", and "Blood Cancer United staff have the final say on implementing this policy." Confirm with the mailbox before a lab submits multiple candidates.

ALSO: "Applicants may not be in a degree-granting program at the award start date that takes away from their" research. Overlap with the Sponsor's own funded grants is expected and fine — "It is expected that there will be overlap of CDP applications with their Sponsor's currently funded grants" — but where a Fellow's proposal overlaps an application the Sponsor is submitting in the same cycle, "Contact researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org for questions about specific proposals."
result.program_officer_contact:
NO NAMED PROGRAM OFFICER — there is one shared mailbox and it is the only channel: **researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org**, staffed by Blood Cancer United scientific and research-administration staff. The portal sign-in page states: "Should you have technical or administrative questions, contact researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org; our team will respond within 2-3 business days."

STALE-ADDRESS TRAP: the live CDP web page still prints the legacy address **researchprograms@lls.org** (twice, including "Contact researchprograms@lls.org with any questions not addressed on this page"). The current-cycle guidelines PDF uses @bloodcancerunited.org throughout. Use the bloodcancerunited.org address.

PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT IS EXPECTED — on fit and eligibility. The funder's timing norm, verbatim: "Blood Cancer United's response time to questions may be delayed by the high volume received near the deadline." Email in July-September, not in the last fortnight.

WHAT TO ASK, AND WHEN:
- "Which subcategory am I?" is the highest-value question, and the window is July to mid-October, before the eligibility gate. With ~20-30% of eligibility requests rejected in prior cycles, asking is cheaper than being rejected — and a wrong-category applicant may be redirected rather than refused. The Fellow/Special Fellow boundary (under 3 years vs 3-5 years of postdoctoral training by the award start date) is exactly where this matters.
- Eligibility-clock edge cases: parental leave, military service, government-caused visa delays, non-US training structures, unusual position titles, gaps in training. Pre-clear these by email with documentation.
- Overlap between your proposal and your Sponsor's own Blood Cancer United application in the same cycle: "Contact researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org for questions about specific proposals."
- K99 concurrency and approval — a standing reporting obligation, not a one-off question.
- Institution or institutional official not listed in the portal; adding a Financial Officer or Technology Transfer Official; getting an assistant their own portal account.
- Wrong PDF uploaded, or extra documents left in the portal — but only before the deadline.
- Missing confirmation email after 2 business days; missing eligibility decision after 10 business days; a reference-letter writer who never received their link.

WHAT IS FLATLY REFUSED: status chasing — "Please do not call or email regarding status updates"; results by phone — "Funding status is relayed by email only and is not available by phone"; and any request for an exception to a deadline or a post-deadline correction.

WHO ELSE TO TALK TO, because the mailbox is not your mentor: for Special Fellow the Sponsor's own track record is an eligibility criterion, so the real pre-submission conversation is with your prospective Sponsor, and with previously funded Blood Cancer United investigators in your department (identify them by name and institution through the Research We Fund database). Note a current-cycle relaxation on the CDP page: "Recognizing that junior investigators may be excellent mentors, we are relaxing the funding requirement for Sponsors with less than 5 years of experience." For a junior Sponsor, assemble a mentorship team.
result.resubmission_note:
ALLOWED, UNCAPPED AND INFORMAL — nothing like NIH's A1 machinery. No numeric limit, no time window, no "Introduction to Resubmission" page, no A0/A1 renumbering. A resubmission is simply a new application in the next cycle that discloses the prior one.

THE ONLY REQUIREMENT, verbatim from the full application template section: "Previous CDP Applications (if applicable): If you previously submitted a CDP application that was not funded, briefly describe what has changed from that application. Your prior application may be shared with the current review committee." So the change narrative is a short template field, not a page — but reviewers may be handed your old application, which means the changes must be real.

WITHIN a cycle, one narrow revision right exists at the eligibility gate only: "If an eligibility submission is rejected for administrative reasons (e.g., missing or unclear information), one revised submission may be made prior to the eligibility deadline. Submissions rejected based on eligibility criteria may not be resubmitted."

THE HARD PART: you usually cannot see what went wrong. "Brief, anonymous feedback from the review panel may be provided but only when available." There is no summary statement equivalent to NIH's, and Priority Scores are confidential. "Waitlist" is a distinct published portal outcome and is the strongest signal to come back next cycle.

WHAT ACTUALLY CAPS YOU IS THE CLOCK, NOT A COUNTER. Special Fellow requires 3-5 years of postdoctoral training at the award start date, so the mechanism affords roughly two or three attempts before you age out into Scholar territory — and because the award start is 1 October of the year after you apply, the clock is measured further forward than applicants expect. Plan the first attempt early in the window rather than treating it as a practice run.

NO APPEALS PROCESS is described in the guidelines. Treat "not funded" as final for that cycle. And note the overall bar: applicants are told not to "ask for exceptions to these policies".
result.examples_or_samples:
NO SAMPLE APPLICATIONS EXIST PUBLICLY — say this plainly to any applicant. Blood Cancer United publishes no sample full applications, no reviewer critiques and no summary statements, and there is no RePORTER-style abstract/budget API. Even your own feedback is conditional ("Brief, anonymous feedback from the review panel may be provided but only when available").

WHAT DOES EXIST, and it is genuinely useful:

1. **Research We Fund — https://bloodcancerunited.org/research/research-we-fund** — a searchable database of currently active funded projects, the closest thing this funder has to NIH RePORTER. Each record carries PI name, institution, city/state/country, funding programme, project title, a several-sentence project summary written by the awardee, and the project term. It is filterable by grant programme, and every programme page carries a "See our active portfolio" link into a pre-filtered view. These pages are reliably populated because awardees sign a media consent and supply a headshot as a condition of the funding agreement.

HOW TO USE IT LIKE A GRANT-WRITER, not a reader: filter to CDP, then read 10-15 summaries in a row. You are calibrating two things. (a) The Mission Score in practice — how explicitly funded applicants tie the work to blood cancer, patient samples and blood-cancer models. This matters more here than at most funders: ">10% of Career Development Program (CDP) applications submitted (from all non-clinical subcategories) were disqualified without full review based on non-compliance with the Mission Relevance of the application and environment." (b) The register of the public summary, which is itself a scored deliverable — the Lay Description has a 2,000-character minimum and a 2,500-character maximum and must avoid Greek and scientific symbols.

2. **Who We Fund — https://bloodcancerunited.org/research/who-we-fund** — the investigator-centred companion view.

3. **Programme-page testimonials** — each programme page carries one or two named awardee testimonials with institution and funded project title. Useful mainly for identifying people to approach.

4. **THE ONLY ROUTE TO A REAL FUNDED APPLICATION**: find awardees at your own institution or in your subfield through Research We Fund and ask them directly for their application. Some US university research offices also circulate successful LLS/Blood Cancer United applications internally — ask your research development office. For Special Fellow specifically, your prospective Sponsor is the highest-yield source: sponsors who have placed Fellows or Special Fellows before will have the prior application and the Sponsor Letter that went with it, and the Sponsor Letter is the component the guidelines single out as decisive.

5. For the closest thing to public application-like prose, the Equity in Access programme page publishes near-full project descriptions for its grantees, with explicit aims and study design — a different mechanism, but the most application-like text this funder publishes.

RETRIEVAL CAVEAT: I did not open the Research We Fund database in this pass; the URL and its structure are carried forward from the corpus brief and the funder's own navigation, which I confirmed links "Research we fund" from the CDP page and the research index.

WHETHER CDP IS CURRENTLY OPEN. Unresolved and consequential. The live CDP page says 'The submission period for CDP is now closed', but that banner sits above a table headed '2022-2023 Application Timeline' on a page that is stale on at least six independent markers (calls the funder 'LLS'; links the legacy portal lls.fluxx.io; links a Policies & Procedures PDF dated April 2020; calls the middle phase the 'Abstract Phase' where the current PDF says 'Letter of Intent Phase'; states a July 1 award start where the current PDF says October 1, 2027; prints researchprograms@lls.org). The current-cycle PDF says eligibility opened July 2026 and closes 15 October 2026, which is still ahead of today (18 September 2026). The portal at bloodcancerunited.fluxx.io lists CDP and names 'Special Fellows' but discloses which programmes are accepting applications only after sign-in, which I did not do.
