3. Named examples, "(but are not limited to)" — so the list is illustrative, not exhaustive: American Association for Cancer Research Career Development Award; Alex's Lemonade Stand Foundation A Award Grant; Conquer Cancer Foundation (ASCO) Career Development Award; Burroughs Wellcome Fund Career Award for Medical Scientists; Leukemia and Lymphoma Society Career Development Program / Scholar Awards; St. Baldrick's Foundation St. Baldrick's Scholar; Lymphoma Research Foundation Clinical Investigator Career Development Award; Melanoma Research Alliance Young Investigator Awards.
4. Overlap, independent of the award's identity: "Scientific or budgetary overlap with other funded projects is not allowed. Therefore, it is critical that all current and pending grant support for your research be reported to the Foundation and the relationship of that support to the Damon Runyon-funded project be explained." This is the clause that catches people whose other funding is individually permitted.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half applicants never find):
1. FEDERAL K AWARDS ARE ALLOWED, and are named: "Physician-scientist career development awards from the federal government including the National Institutes of Health (e.g., K08, K12, K23), the Department of Defense, and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs are allowed." You may hold a K08/K12/K23 concurrently with the CIA. (Contrast: for the Damon Runyon FELLOWSHIP, NIH K holders are ineligible and an institutional K12 must be relinquished. Opposite rule, same funder.)

3. A START-UP PACKAGE IS NOT A CONFLICT — it is effectively required. The institution is "expected to demonstrate significant support from the home institution through a comprehensive start-up package, ample laboratory space, and protected research time". Start-up must be disclosed in Other Sources of Funding, but it strengthens rather than threatens the application.
4. No budget scrutiny at application: "we do not request a budget or a budget justification at the time of application."
5. A REVERSED REQUIREMENT ON DEBT RELIEF — prior application to another programme is MANDATORY, not disqualifying: the award retires "up to $100,000 of any qualifying medical school debt", but "Qualified candidates must first apply to the NIH Loan Repayment Program in order to be eligible for loan repayment from Damon Runyon." Enrolled in NIH LRP or another debt-relief programme? You must disclose it, and it does not bar you.

ADJACENT NON-FUNDING BARS THAT BEHAVE LIKE ELIGIBility RULES: appointment must be Assistant Professor or equivalent, independent, at a US institution, with cut-off date July 1, 2023 for this cycle; "Instructor, Adjunct and/or acting positions are not eligible"; MD, DO or MD/PhD with subspecialty training completed and US Board eligible; "The applicant must hold a valid, active U.S. medical license at the time of application"; 80% research effort (Chair waiver possible); institution must be on the invited list and nominate you; the "Handshake Rule" preference for research directly involving patients (explicitly waived for pathologist candidates).

WHEN IN DOUBT, ASK — the Foundation invites exactly this question: "Please contact the Foundation with any questions regarding concurrent funding (212.455.0520)."

result.resubmission_note:
ALLOWED ONCE — two attempts total, and the cap is on lifetime attempts within your eligibility window, not on "resubmissions per application".

Funder's words, program page: "Candidates may apply up to two times during this eligibility period." Guidelines page: "Applicants may apply no more than two times." FAQ Fast Facts row "Number of reapplications allowed (if still otherwise eligible)": 1 for Clinical Investigator. All three agree.

REQUIRED COMPONENT — an NIH introduction-page equivalent, but far shorter: "If applicable, candidates resubmitting an application must upload a Resubmission Summary of Changes, a brief paragraph outlining the changes or updates made to the current proposal compared to the previous proposal." The parallel Rachleff Innovation wording adds "attached as a preface to the Research Proposal" and "should not exceed half a page"; the CIA page does not restate either (see unresolved) — safest to keep it to a paragraph of half a page or less and preface the proposal with it.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS THE ELIGIBILITY CLOCK, NOT A RESUBMISSION CLOCK. There is no separate resubmission timer. You must still be within the first four years of your independent Assistant Professor appointment at the next deadline (this cycle's stated cut-off: July 1, 2023), still hold an active US medical license, still have no R01 or R01-equivalent "held or awarded", and still be nominated. Because the award runs one cycle a year and the window is four years, most candidates get their second attempt the following January — and a first-time applicant in year 4 has no second attempt at all. Plan the two shots against your appointment date, not against your readiness.

PER-SESSION CROWDING CAN BLOCK A RESUBMISSION EVEN WHEN YOU ARE PERSONALLY ELIGIBLE: "Only one application will be accepted from a Mentor (Co-Mentor) per review session"; "No more than two Damon Runyon Clinical Investigators will be funded to work with the same Mentor at any given time"; and three nominations per institution including affiliated schools. Your institution can decline to re-nominate you in favour of a fresh candidate — so the internal competition must be won twice.

THE HARD PART — YOU MUST REVISE BLIND. Damon Runyon releases no scores and no written critiques ("it is the policy of the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation not to share reviewers' written comments"). There is no summary statement to respond to. A second attempt has to be improved from the published selection criteria, your Mentor, your RD office's read of why the institution ranked you where it did, and Damon Runyon awardees or committee members in your network. If you reached the finalist interview stage, the interview itself is your only real feedback signal — debrief it immediately with your Mentor while it is fresh.

result.submission_requirements:
Portal: ProposalCentral (Altum) — "To apply, please log into Altum | Proposal Central and search for Damon Runyon Fellowship Award." / "No hard copies or emailed applications will be accepted." All forms live inside ProposalCentral. Needs a free applicant account plus Professional Profile in advance.

Formatting norm (funder-wide, applies here): single-spaced, 12-point type, at least 0.5-inch margins; figures and tables incorporated into the text and counted inside the page limit; references excluded from the limit and must give the full title of each work cited.

DEVIATIONS / mechanism-specific values — the complete required sequence, verified verbatim from the Fellowship guidelines page:
1. Application cover sheet (including demographic survey) with all required signatures (electronic/scanned). Second Sponsor fills a separate co-Sponsor cover sheet.
2. Sponsor's biosketch, current NIH format (co-Sponsor too, if two).
3. Sponsor's letter of support (one joint letter if two Sponsors).
4. **Sponsor's comprehensive and detailed training plan, "up to two pages"** (one joint plan if two Sponsors). Note this is SHORTER than the sibling mentored awards — Clinical Investigator and PSTA require a 3-page Mentor's Proposal for Training.
5. **Sponsor's mentorship track record — names and current positions of graduate and postdoctoral trainees from the past 10 years.** This is a distinctive Damon Runyon ask and it takes the Sponsor real time; request it early. Separate track record from each co-Sponsor.
6. Applicant's biosketch, current NIH format.
7. Applicant's Research Support Form (if applicable).
8. Applicant's bibliography — a separate hyperlinked list in addition to the NIH biosketch; "You may include hyperlinks to preprints on bioRxiv."
9. **Applicant's letter, "approximately two pages"**, covering previous research and teaching experience; "a statement on the transformative impact they had on their field of research as a graduate student"; and, if training at the degree-granting institution, a required explanation of why.
10. **Applicant's personal statement, one page** — what they expect to gain from the award; optional personal background/challenges paragraph.
11. **Long-term commitment statement, "no longer than one paragraph"** — what they plan to do after the postdoc.
12. **Research proposal: "not to exceed five pages"**, figures/tables inside the limit, references outside it. Must include a summary (in addition to the separate summary form), background, specific aims, approach, significance to the Fellowship's goals, and relevance of the applicant's and Sponsor's background.
13. Copy of diploma to confirm conferral date. If the PhD diploma has not issued but all requirements including the defense are complete, a letter from the graduate school stating so, with defense date and conferral date, is accepted.
14. **Summary of Research Form, not to exceed one page** — "(Same as Abstract, copy and paste)", i.e. it must match the Abstracts tab in ProposalCentral.
15. Collaboration letters — if applicable, up to two, one page each, stating willingness to contribute equipment/materials/expertise. Explicitly "a brief description of the collaboration, not an evaluation of the candidate (NOT REFERENCE LETTERS)."

REFERENCE LETTERS — **three**, the highest count of any Damon Runyon mechanism (Innovation, CIA, PSTA and Frey need two). "Three letters of reference are required from qualified individuals, other than the candidate's Sponsor". For PhD candidates, "one of the reference letters must come from the candidate's thesis advisor." "Reference letters should be two to three pages in length." Hard submit-gate — see loi_deadline.

PER-SESSION CROWDING LIMITS that can block an otherwise complete application: "Only one fellowship application will be accepted from a Sponsor or Fellow per review session (including Co-Sponsors); there is no limit, however, to the number of applications from an institution." And "No more than two Damon Runyon Fellows will be funded to work with the same Sponsor at any given time (including Co-Sponsors)." Confirmed in Fast Facts: application limit per Mentor = 1, per Institution = N/A. Check with your Sponsor before you start whether anyone else in the lab is applying this session.

ONE-OF-TWO CHOICE, August cycle only: "For the August deadline, applicants may apply for either the Damon Runyon Postdoctoral Fellowship Award or the Damon Runyon-St. Jude Pediatric Cancer Research Fellowship Award, not both." Stated for the August deadline specifically; I did not find it attached to the March deadline.

PROHIBITIONS that read like formatting rules but are eligibility bars: "Proposals to continue training in the laboratory where the applicant received their PhD will not be considered. Proposals that are direct extensions of graduate work will not be funded." Staying at the degree institution (different lab) is "discouraged" and requires a written explanation, not automatically fatal.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves, verified verbatim from the Fellowship overview page 2026-09-18.

=== WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU ===
- **Another accepted postdoctoral fellowship**: "Candidates who have already accepted a postdoctoral research fellowship award are not eligible." Turns on *accepted*, not applied-for or offered — if you are holding competing offers, the sequencing matters.
- **NIH K awards**: "Candidates holding or awarded NIH K awards at the time of application are not eligible to apply." Note "or awarded" — an accepted-but-not-yet-started K also bars you. (Stated in the Level 2 physician-scientist section.)
- **Pursuing a degree**: "Candidates who are pursuing a degree are not eligible." And during the award: "Damon Runyon Fellows are not permitted to pursue additional degrees during the course of their fellowship."
- **Stipend-supplementing awards, during the award**: "Fellows are not permitted to hold any other award or grant that supplements their stipend." And: "Supplementation of stipends is permitted from either the host institution or sponsor's grants, but not by any other fellowship awards or grants."
- **Budgetary overlap**: "Budgetary overlap is not allowed. Therefore, it is critical that all current and pending grant support for your research be reported to the Foundation and the relationship of that support to the Damon Runyon funded project be explained."

=== WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half applicants most often get wrong) ===
- **T32 — yes at application, no concurrently**: "Candidates may hold a T32 at the time of application, but not concurrently with the Damon Runyon Fellowship Award." Stated twice on the page. You do not have to give up your T32 to apply; you relinquish it only if you win.
- **Institutional K12 — yes, applicable, with turn-back**: "Candidates holding institutional K12 awards may apply, but must turn-back K12 funding if they are awarded a Damon Runyon Fellowship." So K12 ≠ K for this purpose — a K12 holder is eligible where a K08/K99 holder is not. This is the sharpest carve-out on the page.
- **Research-expense grants, during the award — yes**: "Fellows are permitted to obtain additional awards or grants to cover research expenses only." The bar is on stipend supplementation, not on all other funding. Prior approval required: "Fellows are required to seek approval from the Foundation before applying for any other award or grant."
- **Host-institution or Sponsor-grant top-up — yes**: permitted from the institution or the Sponsor's grants, capped so that "the total stipend should not exceed the level of support for other professionals at the same level of training in that institution."
- **NIH Loan Repayment Program — not merely allowed, REQUIRED as a precondition**: to get Damon Runyon's up-to-$100,000 medical-school debt repayment, "Qualified candidates must first apply to the NIH Loan Repayment Program in order to be eligible for loan repayment from Damon Runyon." Participants in NIH LRP or other debt-relief programmes "must disclose the details of such agreements to the Foundation." This is the one place where holding other federal support is a prerequisite rather than a conflict.
- **For-profit employment — yes**: "Candidates working in a structured postdoctoral research program at a for-profit institution may apply", with the firm paying salary directly and Damon Runyon topping up to Fellow level if lower.
- **Non-US citizens — yes, if the work is in the US**: "Candidates who are not United States citizens may only apply if they plan to conduct their research in a United States-based institution." Conversely, US citizens may apply to work abroad if the opportunity is one "that would otherwise be difficult to find in the United States."

=== WHAT THIS AWARD PRESERVES FOR YOU DOWNSTREAM ===
- No renewal of the Fellowship itself — Fast Facts, "Opportunity for continuation grant or renewal?": "No (but Fellows may apply for the Frey Award)."
- **Dale F. Frey Award for Breakthrough Scientists**: "Damon Runyon Fellows are eligible to apply for the Dale F. Frey Award one time only, in the fourth year of their award." One shot, zero reapplications (Fast Facts: Frey reapplications = 0). Diarise it in year 4.
- **Damon Runyon–Jake Wetchler Award for Pediatric Innovation**: a one-time $10,000 prize "given annually to a third-year Damon Runyon Fellow whose research has the greatest potential to impact the prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of one or more forms of pediatric cancer", announced at the September Fellows' Retreat.
- Winning the Fellowship does NOT bar a later Clinical Investigator Award application; the CIA keys off an independent faculty appointment, a different stage entirely.

IS PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT EXPECTED? WHEN to write, and what to ask. Write BEFORE you start drafting, because this funder's eligibility rules are date arithmetic, not judgement calls, and one wrong date voids months of work. Worth asking: does my conferral date fall inside this cycle's window, and does a defended-but-undiplomaed PhD count (the page says yes, with a graduate-school letter giving defense and conferral dates); how is "time in the Sponsor's lab" counted for me; is my K12 turn-back handled the way I think; does my Sponsor already have two funded Fellows or another applicant this session; does my pending grant create budgetary overlap.

WHAT NOT TO EXPECT: no scientific advice, no project-fit triage, no read of a draft, no reviewer comments ever, and no negotiation — "The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation will not modify the terms of its policies at the request of individual institutions." No webinar or office-hours programme for this award.

WHO TO TALK TO INSTEAD — the funder effectively designates these:
1. **Your Sponsor.** Scored directly ("the qualifications, experience and productivity of both the candidate and the Sponsor") and the author of four required components including a 10-year mentorship track record. Engage them months out, not weeks.
2. **Your institution's research development office** — for the cover-sheet signatures, and for files of funded applications.
3. **Damon Runyon Fellows in your department or city**, found via the Current Projects geography map — the only realistic source of a real successful application.
4. **The Fellowship Award Committee roster, which is public and named** — https://www.damonrunyon.org/for-scientists/award-selection-committees/fellowship. These are literally the ~20 people who will read your proposal. Chair: Ken H. Cadwell, PhD (Univ. of Pennsylvania). Vice Chair: Sreekanth Chalasani, PhD (Salk). Members include Karlene Cimprich (Stanford), David Cortez (Vanderbilt), Katherine Fitzgerald (UMass Chan), Daniel Jarosz (Stanford), Hao Wu (Harvard), Yukiko Yamashita (Whitehead/HHMI), and others across chemistry, immunology, RNA, structural and stem-cell biology. Reading their work, and pitching at a breadth they will recognise, is a better targeting instrument than any conversation with staff. (Note the correct URL pattern is /for-scientists/award-selection-committees/<program>, not /for-scientists/committees/<program>.)
result.resubmission_note:
ALLOWED ONCE. FAQ Fast Facts, row "Number of reapplications allowed (if still otherwise eligible)": Fellowship Award — "1". The parenthetical is doing the real work; see the clock below.

NO RESUBMISSION SUMMARY OF CHANGES IS STATED FOR THIS MECHANISM. I read the Fellowship's complete 15-item required-components sequence and it contains no resubmission document of any kind. The sibling Rachleff Innovation award does require one ("a brief paragraph outlining the changes or updates made to the current proposal compared to the previous proposal... should not exceed half a page", attached as a preface to the Research Proposal), and the Clinical Investigator guidelines carry the same requirement. Treat the Fellowship as **"not stated", not "not required"** — a resubmitter should email awards@damonrunyon.org to ask whether to include one, because volunteering half a page of orientation is cheap and being told to remove it is cheaper than omitting something expected.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS NOT A RESUBMISSION CLOCK — IT IS THE ELIGIBILITY CLOCK, AND IT KEEPS MOVING. There is no separate waiting period. A Level 1 resubmission only works if your conferral date is still inside the window for the NEW deadline, and that window slides forward by six months each cycle. Concretely, using the published rows: a candidate who applied on August 14, 2026 under the "February 14, 2025 – August 14, 2026" window, with a degree conferred in, say, June 2025, is OUTSIDE the March 15, 2027 window of "September 15, 2025 – March 15, 2027" and has aged out — their one permitted reapplication is unusable. The Sponsor's-lab rule bites the same way: by March 15, 2027 you must have joined on or after March 15, 2026.

Practical reading: **for this fellowship you usually get exactly one retry, at the very next semi-annual deadline, and only if your degree date survives the six-month slide.** Compute both dates before you invest in a revision.

PER-SESSION CROWDING CAN BLOCK A RESUBMISSION EVEN WHEN YOU ARE ELIGIBLE: "Only one fellowship application will be accepted from a Sponsor or Fellow per review session (including Co-Sponsors)" — if a labmate is applying in the cycle you meant to resubmit in, one of you must wait, and waiting may age you out.

THE HARD PART — YOU MUST REVISE BLIND. Damon Runyon releases no scores and no written critiques ("it is the policy of the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation not to share reviewers' written comments"). There is no summary statement to respond to, so a resubmission has to be improved from the published review criteria, your Sponsor, and people who have served on or won the award. The stated criteria are the only scoring rubric you get: quality of the research proposal (importance, originality, appropriateness of techniques, clarity); qualifications, experience and productivity of candidate AND Sponsor; and quality of the training environment, where "The proposed research and training environment should represent a new opportunity for the candidate to expand their scientific skill set."

No RePORTER equivalent, and no publicly posted full application. What is public is nonetheless unusually usable, because the funder publishes project abstracts for every current awardee.

1. **CURRENT PROJECTS DATABASE, filtered to Fellows — the closest thing to funded abstracts, and it is verified working**: https://www.damonrunyon.org/our-impact/current-projects/award-program/fellow. Entries render in full on the listing page itself: scientist name, project title in quotes, a ~150-word lay-scientific project description, institution, **named Sponsor**, cancer type, research area, named award. Verified examples from this page on 2026-09-18 — Stephanie A. Gaglione, PhD (Gladstone Institutes; Sponsor Alexander Marson; "Decoding T cell recognition in virally driven cancers"; Timmerman Traverse Fellow); Jaejin Kim, PhD (Rockefeller; Sponsor Elaine Fuchs; "Inflammatory memory in tissues and its impact on cancer susceptibility"); Yang Su, PhD (Weill Cornell; Sponsor Samie R. Jaffrey); Rachael A. McMinimy, PhD (Gladstone; Sponsor Isha Himani Jain). The Sponsor field makes this doubly useful: it shows which mentors Damon Runyon actually funds.
   Sibling views: by cancer type https://www.damonrunyon.org/our-impact/current-projects/cancer-type ; by geography (a clickable state map) https://www.damonrunyon.org/our-impact/current-projects/geography — this is the route to find a Fellow you can actually walk down the hall to.

2. **WHY THOSE BLURBS ARE THE RIGHT MODEL TO IMITATE.** They are downstream of a reporting requirement, so they are written in the register the Foundation itself uses: annual reports require "A brief, lay abstract of research performed during the award year, including how the research is relevant to cancer. The lay summary should not exceed one page", and the final report requires "Two abstracts (one lay and one scientific)". Writing your one-page Summary of Research Form in that voice — mechanism first, cancer relevance explicit, jargon rationed — is cheap alignment. Note the blurbs also close with a degree-provenance sentence ("Dr. Kim received his PhD and BSc from Seoul National University"), which mirrors how the committee is cued to read career stage.

3. **SELECTION COMMITTEE ROSTER — named, public, and specific to this award**: https://www.damonrunyon.org/for-scientists/award-selection-committees/fellowship. ~20 named scientists with institutions (chair Ken H. Cadwell, Penn; vice chair Sreekanth Chalasani, Salk). Read their recent work before you write; it tells you the breadth your significance section must clear.

4. **AWARD ANNOUNCEMENT NEWS RELEASES**: https://www.damonrunyon.org/news (loads, with ALL NEWS / NEW DISCOVERIES / HONORS AND AWARDS / EVENTS filters; the listing is JS-driven). Each new Fellowship class is announced with per-awardee blurbs, sponsor and institution — useful for calibrating what a winning career stage and project scale look like.

5. **FOR ACTUAL APPLICATION TEXT, GO OFFLINE.** Your research development office (many keep files of funded applications), your Sponsor, or a current/former Damon Runyon Fellow located via the geography map. University pages (Harvard FAS Research Administration, UChicago GRAD, UCI, Caltech, MSU, USC Keck) summarise eligibility and deadlines but none posts a sample Damon Runyon application. Treat "no public sample exists" as established for the open web and "ask your RD office or a local Fellow" as the working route.

result.program_name: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships
result.next_deadline:
DATED, and published by EMBO itself: **Friday 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET**. Verbatim banner on the programme page, the Application page and the FAQ page (all fetched directly from embo.org 2026-09-18, not via a search index): "Applications accepted throughout the year (next cutoff date – hard deadline: Friday 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET)". This feeds the Spring 2027 Selection Round.

CRITICAL FRAMING — this is not a deadline in the usual sense, and treating it as one costs eligibility. Guidelines (July 2026), verbatim: "There are no application deadlines for EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships, but there are two cutoff evaluation dates". You may submit on ANY day of the year. The cutoff only decides which round you land in, and missing it is not fatal: "Applications completed after 14:00 CE(S)T on the day of the evaluation cutoff deadline will enter the next evaluation round. NO EXCEPTIONS WILL BE MADE."

WHY SUBMITTING EARLY BEATS SUBMITTING AT THE CUTOFF: eligibility is measured against your SUBMISSION date, not the cutoff date. Guidelines state this twice — "the Fellowship Office uses the SUBMISSION date of the application for assessment of the eligibility criteria... The Spring and Autumn cutoff deadlines... do not play a role in this eligibility check." So the 2-years-post-PhD clock and the 6-months-in-host-country mobility clock both run to the day you press submit. A candidate 22 months post-PhD in October should submit in October, not wait for 22 January. Conversely a candidate who arrives in the host country on 1 June 2026 must submit by 1 December 2026 (EMBO's own worked FAQ example), which is BEFORE the January cutoff.

FOLLOWING INSTANCE (derived, not published): the Autumn 2027 round cutoff falls on the 2nd Friday of July 2027 = **9 July 2027, 14:00 CEST**. Computed from EMBO's stated rule and the 2027 calendar; EMBO has not yet posted this as a dated instance, so verify before relying on it. It matters because it is the first round under the one-application-per-lifetime regime (see resubmission_note).
result.deadline_pattern:
Rolling submission year-round, funnelled into two fixed annual cutoffs. Guidelines verbatim: "Fourth Friday of January, 2 PM Central European Time: Applications submitted up to this date will enter the Spring Selection Round... Second Friday of July, 2 PM Central European Summer Time: Applications submitted up to this date will enter the Autumn Selection Round."

RULE: 4th Friday of January, 14:00 CET (Spring round) and 2nd Friday of July, 14:00 CEST (Autumn round), every year. Note it is 2 PM Central European time, not midnight and not applicant-local time.

Instances: 23 Jan 2026 (past), 22 Jan 2027 (published by EMBO), 9 July 2027 (derived from rule, not yet published).

Portal availability caveat, verbatim: "the system may be closed for short periods after each selection deadline for technical and maintenance purposes and occasional downtimes may occur at any time. Candidates must take these potential issues into consideration."
result.loi_deadline:
None. There is no letter of intent, no pre-proposal, and no separate stage-1 submission — everything goes in as one complete application by the cutoff.

BUT DO NOT READ THAT AS "ONE STAGE". EMBO runs a two-stage evaluation off a single submission: it extracts a "condensed application form" from what you already submitted and screens that first. Guidelines name the four condensed components verbatim: "the summary of the applicant's main scientific achievements along with the list of publications; the summary and biological significance of the proposed work; justification for choice of the host lab; reference and acceptance letters." (The Selection page's version says "the three most important publications" rather than the full list — a minor page-vs-PDF discrepancy.)

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: those four elements are your de facto LOI and they alone decide roughly 75-80% of outcomes. "Normally, the top 20-25% ranked applications are selected for the second round of evaluation." Write those four sections to stand alone; the rest of the form is only read if you clear the pre-screen. Outcome of that first cut arrives "about six to eight weeks after the cutoff date" — i.e. roughly late March for the January cutoff, early September for the July cutoff.

THE REAL LONG-LEAD DEADLINE IS YOUR REFEREES', NOT YOURS. Unlike most funders, EMBO will not let you submit and let letters follow. FAQ verbatim: "our online application system will not allow you to submit your application without the completed reference forms." Two reference letters plus the host institute's acceptance letter must all be in before your own submit button unlocks. Because eligibility runs off the submission date, a slow referee can literally time-bar you. Treat "referees activated" as the milestone to hit weeks ahead of any date you have in mind.
result.review_to_award:
Roughly 4 to 4.5 months cutoff-to-notification, then a start window that can sit up to a further 6 months out. Stage timings are EMBO's own ("times are approximate").

- 0-6 weeks after cutoff — office eligibility/completeness screen, then Fellowship Committee pre-screen. Acknowledgement email to all eligible applicants "within maximum two weeks of the evaluation cutoff date". EMBO's own instruction if it does not arrive: "Applicants who do not receive any communication within two weeks after the cutoff deadline should contact the office for clarification." Ineligible applicants get an email explaining why.
- ~6-8 weeks — pre-screen outcome emailed to ALL applicants; top 20-25% advance.
- 7-15 weeks (Selection page: "within six to twelve weeks of the evaluation deadline") — Stage 2 interview, by one EMBO Member or EMBO Young Investigator with subject expertise. Online video call only, 90 minutes: 30 min candidate presentation (PhD achievements + proposed postdoc project) then 60 min Q&A. TWO ACTIONABLE DETAILS NOT IN THE GUIDELINES PDF, only on the Selection page: "the applicant is responsible for contacting the interviewer" and the interview happens "at the interviewer's convenience" — so chasing the scheduling is on you. Fallback: "When it is not possible to arrange a personal or video interview, the candidate's application is sent for written evaluation."
- 15-17 weeks — Stage 3. Full application plus the interviewer's report independently assessed by Fellowship Committee members; biannual committee meeting takes the decisions. "Grey zone" candidates get a second, shorter online interview on the day of the meeting: 7-minute presentation + 10-minute Q&A, notified "approximately two weeks in advance".
- Notification — "All applicants are officially informed about the outcome by email within two weeks of the committee meeting." Selection page puts the whole arc at "between 16 to 18 weeks after the evaluation deadline".

SOURCE CONFLICT ON THE ANNOUNCEMENT MONTH — flagged, not resolved. The guidelines PDF says results are "announced at the end of June of the same year" (Spring) / "at the end of December of the same year" (Autumn). The live Application page says "around the mid of June" / "around the mid of December". Both are EMBO's own current text. Plan for mid-to-late June / mid-to-late December.

EARLIEST START — this is where EMBO differs most from a US funder, because the start date is boxed, not negotiable. Verbatim: "Successful applicants in the Spring Selection Round must start their fellowship between July 1st of the award year and February 15th in the following year. Successful applicants in the Autumn Selection Round must start their fellowships between January 1st and August 15th of the following year. Due to practical limitations, fellowships can only start on either the 1st or the 15th of each month." A separate FAQ adds a hard ceiling for those still finishing a PhD: "you must also start your fellowship within 9 months of the offer."

So for the 22 January 2027 cutoff: notification mid-to-late June 2027; earliest start 1 July 2027; latest start 15 February 2028.

SELECTIVITY (for pacing expectations): FAQ verbatim — "We receive on average 1000 applications per evaluation round. The success rate is around 8%." The guidelines separately cite ">1,400 applications received per year"; the two figures do not reconcile cleanly and I have not been able to resolve which is current.
result.submission_requirements:
Where this mechanism DEVIATES from EMBO's funder-wide machinery:

1. TEXT-ONLY WEB FORM, NO ATTACHMENTS AT ALL. Guidelines: "Applications must be written in English and no special formatting is allowed. Similarly, figures and tables cannot be included in the application." FAQ: "No, our online application system supports text only (no figures or graphs)." This is the opposite of EMBO's group-leader schemes (YIP/IG/GIN), which use downloadable Word forms with page limits and permit figures. Nothing is uploaded here.

2. THE SECTION LIMITS ARE NOT PUBLISHED ANYWHERE. They are not in the guidelines, the FAQ or any page on embo.org — I checked all of them. They are visible only inside the form after you have an account. EMBO's own remedy, from the guidelines Annex, verbatim: registration "allows you to see what information is needed in preparing the application." THIS IS THE SINGLE BEST FIRST ACTION for anyone considering this fellowship — register months early purely as reconnaissance.

3. ACCOUNT CREATION IS ASYNCHRONOUS. "Applicants need to register for an EMBO online application account. Once login details for the account have been received by e-mail it is possible to start an application." You register at https://applications.embo.org/?reg=S019 (the programme-coded link http://applications.embo.org/01/register.php?reg=S019 now redirects there; use "Create a new account"), then wait for credentials by email. Do not start this in the cutoff week.

4. REGISTERING DOES NOT ENTER YOU IN A ROUND. Stated on both the guidelines and the Application page: "Registration for an EMBO online application account is not sufficient to enter the corresponding evaluation round. An application is only regarded as complete once all the required information is submitted and the candidate confirms completion." There is a confirm-completion step that must be clicked.

5. THREE THIRD-PARTY LETTERS, ALL SUBMITTED THROUGH THE PORTAL, ALL BLOCKING YOUR SUBMIT BUTTON. Two reference letters + one acceptance letter from the receiving institute. Constraints, verbatim: "one of the reference letters must be from the PhD supervisor/PhD co-supervisor and none of the reference letters can come from referees in the receiving institute"; "We require that the reference letters and acceptance letter from the receiving institute use institutional email addresses and not private ones." You trigger each by entering the contact's details and activating them, which fires an automated link. Emailed letters are rejected outright: "Please refrain from sending reference letters to the Fellowship Office as these cannot be considered in your application." And — the scheduling trap — FAQ: "No, our online application system will not allow you to submit your application without the completed reference forms. Please ensure to reach out to your referees in advance and as early as possible." Recoveries exist: a "deactivate contact" button swaps a referee yourself; the office resets a mis-entered contact or re-sends a link that went to spam (email them the referee's name and yours). If your PhD supervisor cannot write, contact the office — handled case by case.

6. NO INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF, NO GRANTS OFFICE. You apply as an individual: no Grants.gov/eRA equivalent, no AOR, no UEI/SAM. The receiving institute's director is named in the form but, verbatim, "nothing will be required from the director during the application process" — a signature is only needed on the grant agreement if you win.

7. PUBLICATION LIST RULES (DORA). "Do NOT indicate the journal impact factor or any other metrics, commentaries, highlights or citations in the publication list." Exclude papers submitted or in preparation, non-English papers, and conference abstracts. A first-author preprint counts ONLY with public in-depth peer reviews from a verifiable independent service (PCI, Review Commons) on a recognised server — author-posted comments and ordinary journal referee reports do not count. For an "accepted but not yet published" paper, email the editorial letter to fellowships@embo.org BEFORE submitting, and it must show you as first or co-first author.

8. THE APPLICATION FREEZES ON SUBMIT, AND RE-OPENING CAN KILL IT. Only address/contact-email changes are permitted post-submission. "All other changes, including publication updates, will require the office to re-open the application which will change the submission date to the date when the application completed and submitted. Please note that this may cause the application to become ineligible." Publication updates after submission are explicitly not allowed. Since eligibility runs off the submission date, a re-open can push you past the 2-year window.

9. SCOPE GATE PEOPLE FAIL: the project must be "driven by a biological question... rather than remaining at the descriptive or observational level", and "Applications in which the postdoctoral project is a direct continuation of the PhD project will not be considered."

10. ONE APPLICATION PER ROUND, AND — NEW — ONE PER HOST LAB PER ROUND. "Effective from the Autumn 2026 selection round (i.e., all applications submitted after January 23, 2026, 14:00 CET): A host laboratory may support can support the submission of maximum one application per selection cycle. If multiple candidates indicate the same host laboratory in the same selection round, the EMBO Fellowship Office will contact the host laboratory to request the withdrawal of the exceeding application(s)." ASK YOUR PROSPECTIVE HOST WHETHER ANYONE ELSE IS APPLYING TO THEM THAT CYCLE — this is already in force.

11. AI DISCLOSURE REQUESTED: applicants "are requested to disclose whether AI tools were used in preparing their applications, and for what purpose (e.g., chatGPT was used to improve language style)", with the applicant "fully and solely responsible for the originality and accuracy" of the application.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES. The headline finding is that EMBO has NO prior-award exclusion of the NIH K/R01 kind — the binding limits are on attempts, timing and mobility, not on money you have held. I verified this by reading the full guidelines PDF, the Eligibility page and the FAQ end to end and grepping all three for every funding term (other funding, another grant/fellowship/award, concurrent, simultaneous, already hold, dual/double funding); the only hits were disclosure-type mentions, not exclusions.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU
- Having already applied twice. "Re-application is permitted only once" — FAQ: "you can apply only two times in total". And an attempt counts from acknowledgement: "A submission is counted as an application once receipt has been acknowledged and a reference number has been assigned."
- From 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET: having applied ONCE. "Researchers may submit only one EMBO Fellowship Proposal." (See resubmission_note — this is the most drift-sensitive fact in the mechanism.)
- The clock, not an award: PhD obtained more than two years before your SUBMISSION date. This, not any funding history, is what actually ends most people's eligibility — including on a second attempt, since "All eligibility criteria must be met at time of re-submission."
- Mobility: going to the country where you did your PhD (or either country of a shared PhD); returning to your PhD supervisor anywhere in the world; returning to any lab where you have worked >6 months in total (master's study time counts); having lived or worked >6 months in the host country in the previous 18 months.
- A project that is a direct continuation of your PhD.
- A host lab that is already backing another candidate that cycle (in force from the Autumn 2026 round).
- Claiming a career-break extension without written pre-approval: "Applications submitted without prior approval of an exception will be deemed ineligible."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY
- Holding, or having held, other grants and fellowships. No rule anywhere bars it. The only stated obligation is disclosure-and-conversation, and it bites only mid-evaluation: "Applicants who during the evaluation process are awarded with another grant, should get in contact with the Fellowship Office to clarify if they still intend to be part of the selection." There is an "Other Funding" section in the form; it is a disclosure field, not a disqualifier.
- Winning other money AFTER the award does not waste your EMBO status. The EMBO Non-Stipendiary Fellowship is the carve-out: "In case of early termination of the EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowship due to funding from another source, postdoctoral fellows can become holders of a non-stipendiary fellowship", provided you have "received at least one month of paid fellowship" and continue "on the same project and in the same lab". You keep the Fellows' Meetings and (if you held the paid fellowship ≥6 months) the free Laboratory Leadership Course. Terminating early for a change of project or career direction does NOT qualify. You cannot apply for this directly.
- Not yet having the PhD. "Applicants must hold a PhD degree or equivalent at the start of the fellowship, but not necessarily at the time the application is submitted" — but then "you must also start your fellowship within 9 months of the offer."
- Already being in the host lab, if ≤6 months in the host country at submission.
- An MD without a PhD, potentially — but only after enquiring with the office first.
- Career breaks: parental leave (one year per child for female scientists; three months per child or actual leave taken, whichever greater, for male scientists), mandatory military/civil service, and case-by-case severe illness or full-time care of an ill family member. Voluntary career breaks get nothing. Pre-approval mandatory.
- A first-author refereed preprint in place of a journal paper (conditions above).
- Prior co-publication with your intended host: NOT disqualifying, but it costs you. "Applications to work with host laboratories with which the candidate has collaborated in the past generally receive lower priority for funding." Worth testing with the office before investing months.
- Applying for the next round while a decision is pending — but only in one narrow case: "Candidates can re-apply for the next round of selection while a decision is being made on their first application only if they are not eligible to apply after the decision is taken on the first submission."
- Collaborating with several labs during the fellowship (one official host lab and supervisor, collaborations described in the proposal), and secondments of up to 20% of the fellowship elsewhere — though never back to the country of your PhD.

ONE GAP: the postdoc documents do not state whether having previously HELD an EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowship bars a new application (the Scientific Exchange Grant rules address prior EMBO fellowship holders; the postdoc rules do not). In practice the 2-year-post-PhD window makes the question nearly moot. Ask the office if it applies to you.
result.program_officer_contact:
fellowships@embo.org — and here EMBO inverts the NIH pattern in a way that is expensive to get wrong in EITHER direction.

CONTACTING THE OFFICE IS NOT OPTIONAL FOR EDGE CASES — IT IS A CONDITION OF ELIGIBILITY. Verbatim: "The applicant must contact the Fellowship office prior to the submission of the application to obtain an exception, no matter what type. Applications submitted without prior approval of an exception will be deemed ineligible." The Eligibility page repeats it; the FAQ repeats it again.

WRITE FIRST if any of these apply: any career-break extension of the 2-year window; no PhD but claimed equivalent research experience ("should enquire with the EMBO Fellowship office prior to submission"); a paper that is accepted but not yet published (email the editorial letter before submitting); any doubt whether a publication counts as a primary research paper ("Contact the Fellowship office in case of doubt"); doubt about which date counts as your PhD award date ("if in doubt, check with the office, possibly way in advance"); doubt about scientific scope; prior co-publication with your intended host; your PhD supervisor being unable to write a reference; a referee link that bounced or a mis-entered contact; and — if you are already under evaluation — winning another grant.

HOW TO ASK. EMBO tells you exactly what to send, and a vague question wastes the exchange: "please write to us... with an updated CV and a summary proposal. Please make sure your CV includes your present and past positions, a list of your research papers and other funding that you might have previously held." The summary proposal should give "a short overview of the project... while ensuring it includes the biological question being investigated and the intended biological insight you want to obtain." Do your reading first: "Before contacting the office in case of any questions, please check the above links first."

NAMED STAFF (listed on the programme pages, 2026-09-18): Karin Dumstrei, Programme Head, +49 6221 8891 122; Daniele Viarisio, Senior Programme Officer, +49 6221 8891 502; Elsie Chan, Programme Officer, +49 6221 8891 409; Ghulam Rasool, Programme Officer, +49 6221 8891 561; Kate Le Vézouët, Programme Assistant, +49 6221 8891 117.

WHAT THE OFFICE IS NOT. There is no NIH-style programme officer who champions your science, pre-reviews a specific aim, or steers you to a study section. The office gives binary eligibility rulings and procedural fixes. It does not help you find a host lab: "it is the applicant's responsibility to identify a potential host lab/supervisor."

DO NOT CONTACT COMMITTEE MEMBERS. EMBO publishes the full 2026 Fellowship Committee roster (28 named scientists, chaired by Lea Sistonen) on page 2 of the guidelines PDF. Across EMBO's schemes, approaching committee members for advice or feedback is prohibited — and on the sister Installation Grants scheme it is explicitly disqualifying. Use the published roster the legitimate way: to understand who evaluates, not to contact them.

FEEDBACK AFTER REJECTION: NONE, EVER, AT ANY STAGE. This should change how you pace the application. Guidelines verbatim: "No feedback will be provided to applicants at any stage of the application process." EMBO explains the trade-off openly — correct, detailed feedback on ">1,400 applications received per year" would need several PhD-level staff, and "Instead, the funds are used to support additional fellowships." FAQ: "we cannot provide individual feedback, as we do not have comments from the fellowship committee." No summary statement, no score, no percentile. Combined with re-applications ending in January 2027, the NIH-style "submit a rough one, learn from the critique, resubmit" loop does not exist here at all.
result.examples_or_samples:
There is no EMBO equivalent of NIH RePORTER and no published sample application. But there IS a genuine per-awardee list, and I verified it by downloading and reading the file rather than trusting a citation.

BEST RESOURCE — EMBO Annual Report "Facts & Figures" PDFs. Index: https://www.embo.org/about-embo/resources/annual-reports/ ; direct file https://www.embo.org/documents/facts_figures/EMBO_annual_report_2025-facts_figures.pdf (verified 2026-09-18: 64 pages, 2.3 MB, HTTP 200). The 2024 edition is at the same path with 2024 in the filename (verified 200, 1.1 MB).

What is actually in it, confirmed by reading the pages:
- pp. 4-5: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships applications, awards and success rate by nationality, cumulative 2021-2025, plus a graphical five-year series. (Caveat printed on p.4: from 2025 applicants moving to or from EMBL sites are counted under the country the site is in; USA and Canada fall in "Others".)
- p. 6: a full country-to-country mobility matrix — applications and awards for every From/To pair. This tells you, concretely, which corridors actually get funded.
- p. 7 onward: "EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships awarded in 2025", a per-fellow table with Name | Home institute | Group leader | Host institute | Project, running to about p. 16. Verified real rows include Colm Doyle (Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute → Arnaud Krebs, EMBL Heidelberg, "Role of enhancer cooperativity in the control of transcription during development") and Beau Dronsella (MPI für terrestrische Mikrobiologie Marburg → Michael Jewett, Stanford), alongside Gökberk Alagöz, Sara Aloisi, Maria Azkanaz and roughly a hundred others.
- Later sections cover Scientific Exchange Grants (pp. 16-40), Young Investigators (pp. 40-46), Installation Grantees (p. 46), Global Investigators (p. 47) and gender distribution (p. 62).

HOW A PROSPECTIVE APPLICANT SHOULD USE IT — this is the highest-value hour available, and it substitutes for the funded applications EMBO does not release. Read two or three consecutive years and you can (a) see which host labs have successfully taken EMBO fellows, so you approach a host with evidence rather than hope; (b) check whether your intended From→To corridor actually wins awards, using the mobility matrix; (c) read ~100 funded project titles in a single register — one line, biological question forward — which is precisely the register EMBO's own summary fields expect, and the closest available model for the pre-screen text that decides 75-80% of outcomes.

SECONDARY — people.embo.org, the searchable directory of EMBO Members, Associate Members, Young Investigators and Global Investigators, with short plain-language research summaries. Useful here for identifying and vetting a potential host supervisor or a likely interviewer's field, since your Stage 2 interviewer is drawn "from among the EMBO Members and EMBO Young Investigators". It does NOT list postdoctoral fellows.

DELIBERATELY NOT AVAILABLE — do not promise these:
- No sample or annotated EMBO postdoc application from EMBO.
- No reviewer comments, scores, percentiles or summary statements, to anyone, ever — EMBO states it does not even hold committee comments.
- No searchable roster of postdoctoral fellows. https://www.embo.org/the-embo-communities/embo-fellows/ (fetched, HTTP 200) is descriptive only. The annual-report PDFs are the sole per-name listing.
- https://fellowsnetwork.embo.org/ is a members-only platform for awarded fellows, not a public archive.
- Registering for an application account is itself a documented reconnaissance route to the form's unpublished section limits ("allows you to see what information is needed in preparing the application") — the nearest thing to seeing the real template.
result.resubmission_note:
THE MOST DRIFT-SENSITIVE FACT IN THIS MECHANISM, AND IT HAS A HARD DATE ATTACHED. Any advice written before mid-2026 is now wrong.

Current rule — one re-application, conditional. Guidelines (July 2026) verbatim: "Re-application is permitted only once. However, we will only consider a re-application in case of substantial changes to the proposal and/or the CV of the applicant or a change of host lab. The applicant should outline in the 'Other Funding' section under 'application changes' detailed and exact changes made to the proposal and/or the CV." FAQ adds the enforcement: "Reapplication is allowed only once, irrespective of a change of project or host lab. This means that you can apply only two times in total... Projects that are a mere copy of the first application will not be considered and immediately rejected."

The change, stated identically in the guidelines, the Eligibility page and the FAQ: "Effective from the Autumn 2027 selection round (i.e., for all applications submitted after January 22, 2027, 14:00 CET), re-applications will no longer be permitted. Researchers may submit only one EMBO Fellowship Proposal."

ACTIONABLE CONSEQUENCE: **22 January 2027, 14:00 CET is the last cutoff from which a second attempt is possible.** Anyone who wants two shots must have their FIRST application fully submitted — referees and acceptance letter included — by that moment. After it, EMBO postdoc becomes one-shot-per-researcher. This should change pacing in a specific way: because EMBO gives no feedback at any stage, the "submit a rough one to learn from the critique" strategy never worked here anyway, and from 2027 it is not even available as a second roll of the dice. Aim the single strongest application you can at a cutoff where your eligibility clocks are comfortably inside the window.

Mechanics of a re-application while the rule still stands: there is no NIH-style introduction page — changes go in a field called "application changes" inside the "Other Funding" section. An attempt counts only once "receipt has been acknowledged and a reference number has been assigned". Previous applications are never carried forward: "Applicants must follow the same procedure and re-apply." And the trap that catches most second attempts: "All eligibility criteria must be met at time of re-submission" — since eligibility runs off the submission date, a second attempt a year later can simply be time-barred by the 2-year PhD window or by having now spent >6 months in the host country. Re-applying while the first decision is pending is allowed only if you would no longer be eligible once that decision lands.
