result.funder: U.S. Department of Energy — Office of Science (SC)
result.next_deadline:
NO FY2027 DATE IS PUBLISHED YET — verified, not withheld. Checked the funder's own open-NOFO list (science.osti.gov/grants/FOAs/Open) on 2026-09-18: the only open SC NOFOs are DE-FOA-0003657, DE-FOA-0003612 and the Open Call DE-FOA-0003600. No ECRP NOFO is open. DE-FOA-0003602 (FY2026) now sits on the CLOSED list, so that cycle is finished.

THE FY2026 CYCLE'S ACTUAL DATES (closed; use as the template for FY2027), quoted from the NOFO cover:
- "NOFO Issue Date: March 3, 2026"
- "Submission Deadline for Pre-Applications: March 24, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET" — "A Pre-Application is required."
- "Pre-Application Response Date: April 21, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET" (encourage/discourage)
- "Submission Deadline for Applications: June 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET"

THE PRIOR CYCLE (FY2025, DE-FOA-0003450), from the same closed list: issued 1/17/2025, pre-app 18 Feb 2025 5:00 PM ET, application 4/22/2025 11:59 PM ET.

WHY YOU CANNOT JUST ASSUME "MARCH": the cycle drifts substantially year to year. FY2025 opened mid-January with a February pre-app; FY2026 opened in March with a March pre-app — roughly a five-week slip in one year. Treat March/June as the FY2026 dates, not a rule.

STALE-PAGE TRAP: on 2026-09-18, science.osti.gov/early-career still read as though the 2026 competition were open and still displayed the 24 March / 2 June dates, more than three months after the application deadline. The landing page is not a live status source; the Open and Closed NOFO lists are. Anyone watching for FY2027 should watch science.osti.gov/grants/FOAs/Open, not the programme page.

The programme is expected to recur: FAQ Q117 — "Our intention is to continue this program on an annual basis, subject to availability of funds." It has run 16 consecutive years, FY2010–FY2025 (NOFO: "The program has been offered in 16 previous years, FY 2010 - FY 2025").
result.deadline_pattern:
Annual competition, one cycle per fiscal year, with a three-gate internal structure. Shape (from the two most recent cycles):

NOFO issued (Jan–Mar) → mandatory pre-application ~3 weeks later → encourage/discourage email ~4 weeks after that → full application ~6 weeks after the response → selections announced ~1 month after the application deadline → suggested start ~3 months after the application deadline.

FY2026: 3 Mar → 24 Mar → 21 Apr → 2 Jun → selection "by July 2026" → suggested start 1 Sept 2026.
FY2025: 17 Jan → 18 Feb → (response) → 22 Apr.

All times Eastern. PAMS closes at 5:00 PM ET for pre-applications; Grants.gov at 11:59 PM ET for applications. Late submissions: the NOFO allows them only for "widespread technological disruptions or significant natural disasters", incapacitating/life-threatening illness, or death of an immediate family member — and lists unacceptable justifications explicitly.

PRACTICAL PLANNING WINDOW: the gap between NOFO issue and pre-application close was only 21 days in FY2026. That is not enough time to do the long-lead registrations (SAM.gov, Grants.gov AOR, PAMS institutional registration) from a standing start. Those must be done before the NOFO drops.
result.loi_required: yes — but not called an LOI
result.loi_deadline:
FY2026: pre-application due "March 24, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET"; encourage/discourage response "April 21, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET"; full application "June 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET". So the pre-application sat 70 days ahead of the full application, with the verdict arriving 42 days before it.

TERMINOLOGY TRAP — the single easiest thing to get wrong here. The NOFO's Section IV.A.1 and Section V.D.1 both say, literally: "Letter of Intent (LOI) — Not applicable." If you search the NOFO for "LOI" you will conclude there is no gate. There is. The gate is called a PRE-APPLICATION, it is mandatory, and it is hard:
- NOFO cover: "A Pre-Application is required."
- FAQ Q106: "I did not submit a pre-application. May I submit a full application?" — "No."
- FAQ Q57: "Only those applicants that receive notification from DOE encouraging a formal application may submit full applications. No other formal applications will be considered."
- NOFO body (the controlling text, slightly softer): "Applications that have not been encouraged by DOE may be declined without merit review."

IT IS A COMPETITIVE CUT, NOT A HEADCOUNT. Pre-applications are scored against four criteria — responsiveness, scientific and technical merit, appropriateness of approach, likelihood of scientific impact — by "no less than three federal program managers". "Applicants with the highest rated pre-applications will be encouraged to submit applications; others will be discouraged."

YOU ARGUE IN THE DARK: "Written feedback about pre-applications will be provided after the deadline for the receipt of applications." You learn only encouraged/discouraged before you must commit to writing the full application; the reasoning arrives after the full application is already due.

PRE-APPLICATION MECHANICS (deviates from the full application in every respect):
- Portal: PAMS only (https://pamspublic.science.energy.gov/), never Grants.gov or FedConnect. "You cannot draft or edit a pre-application in PAMS" — compose elsewhere, upload.
- Length: "Not including the title page, the pre-application may not exceed three pages" — 8.5x11, 1-inch margins, body text ≥11 pt. "Figures and references, if included, must fit within the three-page limit" (FAQ Q65, Q66 confirm both).
- Title page: excluded from the three pages, may run to two pages if needed (FAQ Q111). Mandated fields include Year Doctorate Awarded, "Number of Times Previously Applied", Multiple Program Scope (Yes/No), and "Eligibility Extension Requested: (Yes/No)". "The material listed here defines the acceptable information on a title page."
- Also required, not counted against the three pages: a listing of senior/key personnel, and a listing of individuals who should NOT serve as merit reviewers, attached as an "Additional Attachment" in PAMS. The NOFO warns this list "is rarely empty because the instructions contain mandatory inclusions requirements."
- Two extra PAMS questions unique to ECRP: whether the PI is PECASE-eligible, and year doctorate awarded.
- Any eligibility-extension request for a major life event must be IN THE PRE-APPLICATION (see prior_funding_conflicts). There is no second chance at the full-application stage, and no advance ruling (FAQ Q8).
- YOU CANNOT SUBMIT IT YOURSELF: "Pre-applications may only be submitted by a user at the PI's institution with the 'Submit to DOE' privilege in PAMS. A PI may draft a pre-application but will only be able to submit the pre-application for institutional countersignature." Cover page: "Pre-Applications must be submitted by an authorized institutional representative."
- One only: FAQ Q63 — may you submit more than one pre-application, or the same one to multiple programmes? "No."
- Notification arrives from PAMS.Autoreply@science.doe.gov; status also updates in PAMS. If nothing arrives by the response date, "Applicants ... are responsible for contacting the program to confirm this status."
- Late pre-application relief exists only if you contacted the PAMS help desk "well before" the deadline and have a tracking number (FAQ Q73).

CARRY-OVER INTO THE FULL APPLICATION: the DOE Title Page of the full application requires the "PAMS Pre-application tracking number", so the pre-application is structurally welded to the application. Title/topic may not change: "Our preference is that you keep the same or a very similar title. A slight change in the title is allowed, but the topic may not change" (FAQ Q91).
result.review_to_award:
MUCH FASTER THAN THE SC NORM — this is the biggest timing deviation. The Open Call promises decisions "within six months" of receipt, with a regulatory backstop of 12 months under 10 CFR 605.10. ECRP compresses that to about one month.

- NOFO Section VII.B: "It is anticipated that the award selection will be completed by July 2026. It is expected that awards will be made in Fiscal Year 2026." Application deadline was 2 June 2026 — so roughly 4 weeks from submission to selection.
- Earliest start, FAQ Q116: "We suggest a start date of September 1, 2026. Please feel free to indicate any desired date: We can always negotiate a different date after merit review and award selection. The date mentioned in an application is not binding." That is ~3 months from application deadline to money.
- Whole cycle, pre-application to start: 24 Mar 2026 → 1 Sept 2026, about five months.

WHY IT IS COMPRESSED: ECRP is fiscal-year-bound in a way the rolling Open Call is not. Awards must land inside FY2026, which ends 30 September. The pre-application cut is what makes the short review possible — the panel only ever sees a filtered pool.

REVIEW MECHANICS:
- Method is not fixed: FAQ Q115 — "Applications may be reviewed by either mail review or panel review or some combination of both. Each program will decide individually on its review method."
- Non-selection notice: "Organizations whose applications have not been selected will be advised as promptly as possible. This notice will explain why the application was not selected."
- Reviewer comments, FAQ Q119: "Principal Investigators will have access to the reviewer comments in PAMS at the time or shortly after the application is recommended for funding or declined."
- Not score-ranked, FAQ Q120: "No, the Selection Official will consider the merit review scores and written recommendations, program policy factors, and the amount of funding available." Programme policy factors named include "ensuring opportunities to investigators not currently supported by DOE, and increasing participation of institutions historically underrepresented in the SC research portfolio."
- National labs only: do NOT submit a Field Work Proposal with the application — "The program office will request submission of Field Work Proposals later only from those applicants who are selected for possible funding" (FAQ Q77). Do not use Searchable FWP (Q76).

SCALE: FY2026 NOFO expected 100 awards from $145M ($79M FY2026 + $66M outyear). Award period 5 years; $875,000 for an Institution of Higher Education, $2,750,000 for a DOE/NNSA National Laboratory or SC Scientific User Facility.
result.submission_requirements:
DEVIATIONS FROM THE SC-WIDE NORM — the things that get ECRP applications killed:

PAGE LIMIT (SC sets this per programme office; ECRP sets its own): "The Project Narrative must not exceed a page limit of 15 pages of technical information, including charts, graphs, maps, photographs, and other pictorial presentations ... Merit reviewers will only consider the number of pages specified." Optional table of contents excluded (FAQ Q96); the required header block may go on a separate cover page outside the narrative (FAQ Q84).

NO CO-PIs — hard structural rule, unlike most SC mechanisms: "Awards under the Early Career Research Program must be under the sole and indivisible leadership of the PI ... There can be no co-PIs. Applications including co-PIs may be declined without review." Other senior/key personnel "must commit less time and effort and request less support than the PI." FAQ Q99 refuses multi-investigator team proposals outright.

NO LETTERS OF RECOMMENDATION OR SUPPORT — the trap for anyone arriving from NSF CAREER, where a departmental letter is expected: "Letters of recommendation and department chair letters are not allowed. Applications that include recommendations or department chair letters will be subject to elimination from consideration during DOE's initial review." FAQ Q83 ("Do you require a letter from my department chair?" — "No.") and Q101 ("Are letters of recommendation, endorsement, or support allowed?" — "No.").

COLLABORATION LETTERS ARE A FILL-IN-THE-BLANK FORM: allowed in Appendix 7, not counted against the narrative, and "Each letter of collaboration or access may contain two and only two sentences" on the mandated template ("If your application entitled, '<Application Name>,' is selected for funding ... it is my intent to collaborate in this research by ..."). May be addressed "To Whom It May Concern:". They "must not be written as recommendation or endorsement letters." DIII-D work additionally requires a Record of Discussion from the facility.

DATA MANAGEMENT PLAN IS A KILL SWITCH: FAQ Q79 — "The DOE Office of Science will decline without review any application that does not include a data management and sharing plan." It goes in Appendix 4, and it must meet the requirements of the specific programme office that encouraged you (FAQ Q113).

NO EDUCATION OR OUTREACH COMPONENT: FAQ Q82 — "Do you require an educational or outreach component in the application?" — "No." The opposite of NSF CAREER. Do not import a Broader Impacts plan.

TWO EXTRA REVIEW CRITERIA: beyond the four in 10 CFR 605.10(d), "Merit reviewers will be asked to evaluate two additional criteria of equal significance to the fourth criterion established by SC: Appropriateness of the Data Management and Sharing Plan [and] Potential for leadership within the scientific community." Criterion 6 asks "How has the PI been recognized as a leader in the scientific community?" — evidence naturally lands in the biosketch and in Appendix 5 Synergistic Activities (optional; one page per senior/key person, "no more than five distinct examples").

PROGRAMME OFFICE IS LOCKED AFTER ENCOURAGEMENT: FAQ Q113/Q100 — pre-applications may be moved between topics within one office by DOE, but "Once a pre-application is encouraged by a particular program office, the application must be submitted to and reviewed in that program office ... applications will not be moved between program offices after they arrive."

AI-WRITTEN NARRATIVES — stricter than the Open Call's disclose-if-used rule: "Submission of a Project Narrative that is not the work of the proposed researchers, including machine-generated Project Narratives, may constitute academic dishonesty or research misconduct."

ASSEMBLY (shared with SC generally, still the top cause of rejection): one single machine-readable PDF containing DOE Title Page + Project Narrative + all appendices, attached to Field 8 on the Grants.gov form. "Do not attach any of the requested appendices ... as files for Fields 9, 10, 11, and 12" — if you do, "these additional attachments will not become part of the application in PAMS." No PDF portfolios or binders, no scanned images, no editable fields or signatures. Filenames ≤50 characters. Biosketches and current & pending attach instead to the Research and Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) form, using SciENcv Common Forms — the NOFO states "there is no page limitation for the Biosketch, though some fields in SciENcv have character limitations". Startup funds are NOT listed in current and pending (FAQ Q92).

DOE TITLE PAGE mandatory fields include: DOE/SC Program Office, research area, DOE/SC Program Office Technical Contact, Year Doctorate Awarded, "If at a University, is the PI in a tenure-track appointment?", "Does the PI have tenure:", "Number of Times Previously Applied:", "PAMS Pre-application tracking number:", and "Application Contains Data Management Plan in Appendix 4: (Yes or No)?".

APPENDICES: 1 Bibliography; 2 Facilities & Other Resources; 3 Equipment; 4 Data Management and Sharing Plan (mandatory); 5 Synergistic Activities (optional); 6 Transparency of Foreign Connections (mandatory, per applicant and each subrecipient); 7 Other Attachments (where collaboration/access letters go). None count against the 15 pages.

FIXING MISTAKES: before the deadline, resubmit through Grants.gov with "Changed/Corrected Application" ticked and email SC.Early@science.doe.gov (FAQ Q107); submitted twice with no word from you, "we will consider the application that arrived last" (Q109). After the deadline: "Changes after the deadline are not allowed for any reason" (Q108).

WHO CANNOT USE THIS MECHANISM AT ALL: postdocs may not apply directly ("However, a PI may include postdoctoral support for the project in the proposed budget", FAQ Q5), and research (non-tenure-track) professors are excluded (FAQ Q12). PhD students and postdocs wanting a DOE route should look at SCGSR, a separate mechanism, not ECRP. A PhD candidate who already holds an eligible faculty or lab appointment IS eligible even before the degree is conferred (FAQ Q10).
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU:

1. A PRIOR DOE SC ECRP AWARD — permanent, no exceptions. NOFO: "PIs who have received awards previously under the SC ECRP are not eligible." FAQ Q13: "If I received an Office of Science Early Career Research Program award previously, am I eligible?" — "No."
2. THREE PRIOR COMPLETED ATTEMPTS — a lifetime cap, unusual for DOE: "Only one pre-application on behalf of a PI may be submitted in any given SC ECRP competition. A PI may not submit an application in more than three SC ECRP competitions. Participation in the competition is defined as submission of a full application that completed the review/decision process."
3. DUPLICATING WORK YOU ARE ALREADY FUNDED FOR — from any funder. FAQ Q97: "The application may not duplicate your currently funded research, regardless of the agency funding it. You should propose new research."
4. Being tenured, or a research (non-tenure-track) professor, or a postdoc, or outside the 10-year window. "NOFO: eligibility exemptions will not be granted."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half applicants get wrong and self-reject over:

1. EARLY-CAREER AWARDS FROM OTHER FUNDERS DO NOT DISQUALIFY YOU. FAQ Q11: "If I have previously won an early career award from another agency or a nonprofit organization, am I eligible?" — "Yes." The NOFO adds the one condition: "PIs of early career awards funded by other agencies or entities are eligible, but the proposed research must have a scope different from that already funded by the other organization." So an NSF CAREER, NIH K, ONR YIP, ARO ECP or foundation early-career award holder is eligible — with a distinct scope.
2. A PRIOR PECASE DOES NOT DISQUALIFY YOU. FAQ Q19: "Yes. Previous winners of PECASE are eligible for the Early Career Research Program." NOFO: "PECASE eligibility is not required for an award under this NOFO." Note the two senses of "PECASE eligible" — a previous PECASE bars you from being NOMINATED for PECASE again through ECRP (the PAMS pre-application asks whether you are PECASE-eligible: US citizen/national/PR as of the closing date AND no prior PECASE from any agency, FAQ Q85), but it does not touch your ECRP eligibility. PECASE nominees are drawn from ECRP winners after the fact (FAQ Q86); non-citizens simply win ECRP without the PECASE track.
3. YOU MAY SUBMIT THE SAME IDEA TO ANOTHER AGENCY AT THE SAME TIME. FAQ Q98, which names the exact case: "Can I submit the same proposal to two federal agencies simultaneously (e.g., can I submit the same proposal to the NSF CAREER program and the DOE Early Career Research Program)?" — "Yes, but you can only be funded once by the federal government for a given scope of work. Thus, if both are selected for funding, you will only be able to accept one award. To avoid this situation, you can submit proposals for completely different scopes of work to the two agencies."
4. YOU MAY HOLD BOTH AWARDS if the scopes are distinct. FAQ Q114: "You may be allowed to receive both awards. However, you will not be funded twice for the same work. Make sure you keep the ideas you propose to the two agencies distinct if you want to accept both awards."
5. STARTUP FUNDS ARE NOT A CONFLICT and are not even disclosed: FAQ Q92 — should current and pending include university startup funds? "No."
6. FAILED ATTEMPTS MOSTLY DO NOT BURN AN ATTEMPT against the cap of three. A discouraged pre-application does not count (FAQ Q67). An encouraged pre-application you choose not to act on does not count (FAQ Q68: you are not obliged to submit; Q69: it does not count). An application withdrawn before official declination does not count (Q74, and the NOFO). An application "declined without merit review by the DOE SC will not count as a submission." Only a full application that ran the whole review/decision process counts (Q3).
7. TENURE TIMING IS A DEADLINE TEST, NOT A TRAJECTORY TEST. FAQ Q14: "You are eligible if you are untenured but still on the tenure track as of the application due date ... If tenure is granted prior to the application due date, you will be ineligible. If tenure is granted after the application due date but before an award is made, you are eligible." And once you hold the award, FAQ Q118: "you will not have to give up the award when you receive tenure."
8. NOT-YET-STARTED APPOINTMENTS ARE WORKABLE. You must be employed in the eligible position on the APPLICATION due date, not the pre-application date (FAQ Q16, Q17); at the pre-application stage you list your current title with a footnote naming the incoming position and expected start (FAQ Q60/61). Part-time converting to full-time at a lab works the same way (Q15).
9. CITIZENSHIP IS NOT REQUIRED. "SC does not require that individuals be U.S. citizens or permanent residents to be proposed as a PI"; FAQ Q4 confirms. Students and postdocs you fund need not be US citizens either (Q105). Only the employing institution must be US.
10. NO INSTITUTIONAL CAP: FAQ Q94 — is there a limit on applications per institution? "No." (Labs and user facilities likewise have no pre-application cap, though each must vouch for scope fit.)
11. NO NATIONAL LAB COLLABORATION REQUIRED: FAQ Q104 — "No. Your application will be evaluated using the merit review criteria in the announcement, and collaboration or contact with a national laboratory is not required."

THE 10-YEAR CLOCK AND ITS EXTENSION — the highest-value carve-out:
"No more than 10 years can have passed between the year the PI's Ph.D. was awarded and the calendar year at the start of the Federal fiscal year in which this NOFO is released. For the present competition, those who received doctorates on or after January 1, 2015, are eligible." It is measured in whole calendar years off the fiscal-year start, not months from your defence — and conferment date governs, not defence date (FAQ Q6: defended 2014, conferred 2015 → eligible).
EXTENSION: "Extensions to eligibility due to major life events (three months or longer) must be validated by a letter from the university dean, research vice president, laboratory division director, or equivalent official. The letter must be included in the pre-application." Three procedural traps: (a) it goes in the PRE-application, not the application, and the pre-application title page has a dedicated "Eligibility Extension Requested: (Yes/No)" field; (b) no advance ruling — FAQ Q8: "No, the letter requesting an eligibility extension will be evaluated as part of the pre-application process"; (c) it does not carry over — FAQ Q9: "No. We intend to continue allowing eligibility extensions in future years ... but we will not maintain records of approved extensions from prior years", so you re-request every year.
MULTIPLE DOCTORATES: the one inside the window must be relevant to the proposed research (FAQ Q18).
LAB APPOINTMENT TYPES: named fellowships (ANL Maria Goeppert Mayer, BNL Goldhaber-era fellows, FNAL Wilson/Peoples, LANL, LBNL Divisional Fellows, ORNL Wigner/Shull/Russell/Householder/Weinberg, SLAC Panofsky, SNL FNITS and others) have pre-cleared eligible/ineligible determinations tabulated in the FAQ, with dates. "Note that limited term employees are not eligible for this program unless their position types appear in the first chart"; if in any doubt, email SC.Early@science.doe.gov and have the institution clear the position type in advance (FAQ Q20, Q21).
result.program_officer_contact:
YES — named individuals, and contact is explicitly blessed before the pre-application.

STRUCTURE: the FY2026 NOFO names a Technical Contact against each of its 54 numbered research topics across the seven participating offices (ASCR, BES, BER, FES, HEP, NP, DOE IP), in the form "Technical Contact: Amanda Haes, Amanda.Haes@science.doe.gov" directly beneath the topic description — 64 distinct @science.doe.gov addresses in the document. You pick the topic's programme manager from a dropdown when you submit the pre-application in PAMS, and you name them again on the full application's DOE Title Page ("DOE/SC Program Office Technical Contact"). There is no way to apply without choosing a person.

WHAT CONTACT IS FOR, in the funder's own words (FAQ Q58): "May I contact the program manager before I submit my pre-application for feedback?" — "Yes. Feel free to contact a program manager if you are uncertain about which topic from the solicitation is the best fit for your idea. The program manager can provide informal feedback on your idea and suggest other program areas if the idea does not fit within his or her area."

THE LIMIT ON WHAT THAT BUYS YOU, same answer: "Please note that you may formally submit any pre-application you believe fits within the topics described in the solicitation, regardless of the informal feedback you may receive from a program manager. A formal encourage/discourage decision based on topical fit with the solicitation will be issued for every pre-application we receive." A warm conversation is not permission; a cool one is not a veto.

WHEN CONTACT ACTUALLY MATTERS MOST — a cross-topic idea, because the programme-office choice becomes irreversible: FAQ Q100 — "You should select a single topical area to be the primary one ... You may also contact the Technical Contact prior to the pre-application deadline to discuss whether your idea fits within their topical area. Once a pre-application is encouraged by a particular program office, the application must be submitted to that program office and cannot be moved to another program office by DOE." Ask before the pre-application, or live with the answer for the whole cycle.

ROUTING — send the right question to the right place:
- Scientific/technical, topic fit, "is this in scope": the named Technical Contact for the topic.
- Budget and eligibility questions: SC.Early@science.doe.gov (the NOFO's designated Administrative Contact; the programme landing page prints it as SC.Early@doe.gov).
- Position-type eligibility at a lab or user facility: SC.Early@science.doe.gov, ideally cleared by the institution in advance.

I opened the FY2025 file and counted it: 99 funded abstracts, each roughly one page, giving project title, PI name and academic rank, department, institution, city, a ~400-word structured abstract, and a closing line naming the funding office. First entry is "Optical Quantum Sensing in Molecular Assemblies", Dr. Ashok Ajoy, Assistant Professor of Chemistry, UC Berkeley, "selected for funding by the Office of Basic Energy Sciences."
WHERE THE MONEY ACTUALLY WENT in FY2025, counted from that file — this is the aiming information nobody publishes as a table: Basic Energy Sciences 53 (plus 6 more as joint/lead), High Energy Physics 12, Nuclear Physics 8, Advanced Scientific Computing Research 8, Biological and Environmental Research 6, Fusion Energy Sciences 3, Accelerator R&D and Production 1. BES alone takes well over half the programme. Read five years of abstracts in the office you are aiming at, not across the whole programme.

2. PAMS PUBLIC AWARD SEARCH — no account needed: https://pamspublic.science.energy.gov/WebPAMSExternal/interface/awards/AwardSearchExternal.aspx. DOE SC grants, cooperative agreements and interagency awards back to 2014, searchable by PI, institution, sponsoring SC programme office, and free text across the abstracts. This is how you find out who your specific programme manager already funds, at what size, and in what language — the DOE analogue of NIH RePORTER.

3. TOPICAL FOA AWARD LISTS: https://science.osti.gov/Funding-Opportunities/Award — filterable by programme and year, each entry linking a PDF of selected projects with titles, PIs and institutions.

4. YOUR OWN REVIEWER COMMENTS, and your colleagues'. FAQ Q119: "Principal Investigators will have access to the reviewer comments in PAMS at the time or shortly after the application is recommended for funding or declined." Since a discouraged pre-application costs you nothing against the three-competition cap, a first pre-application is a cheap way to buy a real read on topical fit. Asking a colleague in your department to show you their ECRP reviews is the closest DOE analogue to an NIH summary statement.

5. THE NOFO AND FAQ THEMSELVES are unusually instructive and should be read as samples: the FY2026 FAQ runs 127 questions over 21 pages, including DOE's own tabulated counts of applications received and awards made per programme office since FY2010 (Q123/Q124 — those two tables are embedded as images and did not extract as text; open the PDF to read them).

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: DOE SC publishes no full funded ECRP application texts and maintains no official sample-proposal library. For a complete narrative, go to your university's research development office (many keep internal libraries of submitted DOE proposals) or file a FOIA request — the NOFO notes applications "may be made publicly available if an award is made", so funded narratives are FOIA-reachable in principle. Also useful downstream: DOE PAGES/OSTI for publications from funded awards, and USAspending for dollar figures.
result.resubmission_note:
NO NIH-STYLE RESUBMISSION, and none is needed — but ECRP is the one SC mechanism with a hard lifetime cap, so attempts are a scarce resource.

FORM MECHANICS: SC does not use the Resubmission or Continuation options on SF-424 (R&R) Field 8. There is no introduction page, no "A1" numbering, and no mandated waiting period. A previously declined ECRP application simply comes back as a new application in the next annual competition.

THE CAP, verbatim from DE-FOA-0003602: "Only one pre-application on behalf of a PI may be submitted in any given SC ECRP competition. A PI may not submit an application in more than three SC ECRP competitions. Participation in the competition is defined as submission of a full application that completed the review/decision process. In rare cases, it is necessary to withdraw an application; an application withdrawn prior to it being officially declined will not count as a submission. Likewise, an application declined without merit review by the DOE SC will not count as a submission." The pre-application title page requires you to self-declare "Number of Times Previously Applied", and "A PI who has participated in three past SC ECRP competitions is not eligible."

WHAT DOES NOT BURN AN ATTEMPT (from the FAQ — this is what makes an early, exploratory try rational):
- a discouraged pre-application (Q67);
- an encouraged pre-application you decide not to act on (Q68, Q69);
- an application withdrawn before official declination (Q74);
- an application declined without merit review (Q3).
Only a full application that went the distance through review and decision counts.

STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE: three real attempts, inside a ten-year eligibility window that also requires you to stay untenured. A discouraged pre-application is free intelligence. A full application submitted into a poorly fitting programme office is expensive — and since the office is locked once it encourages you, the fit decision is made at the pre-application, not later.

WITHDRAWAL is the escape hatch and the one place the cap interacts with SC's general machinery: applications may be withdrawn through PAMS at any time between submission and the moment DOE releases them to merit reviewers; such withdrawals "take effect immediately and cannot be reversed"; after release to reviewers you must ask the programme office. A withdrawal before official declination preserves the attempt.

THE SUBSTANTIVE CONSTRAINT ON COMING BACK: several SC programmes state that "Previously declined applications that have not been substantially revised in light of merit reviewer comments may be declined without additional merit review." Get your reviews from PAMS, rewrite visibly against them — and note that under the ECRP rules a decline without merit review does not consume an attempt, so an unchanged resubmission wastes a year rather than an attempt.

NOT A RESUBMISSION ISSUE BUT THE SAME FAMILY — CHANGING THE PROPOSAL MID-CYCLE: the topic may not change between pre-application and application ("A slight change in the title is allowed, but the topic may not change", FAQ Q91); typos may be fixed before the deadline by resubmitting with "Changed/Corrected Application" ticked plus an email to SC.Early@science.doe.gov (Q107); and after the deadline, "Changes after the deadline are not allowed for any reason" (Q108).

NEXT CYCLE (FINESST-26): **date not yet published as of 2026-09-18** — and NASA says so itself rather than leaving it blank. Q76 of the official FINESST-25 Q&A: "The release date of the next FINESST is hard to predict. Plus not every part of SMD participates in every call/solicitation. Due to budget limitations, one or more a part of SMD may choose to skip the next FINESST competition. Normally, two FINESST NOFOs (competitions) are not open at the same time. Barring circumstances beyond NASA's control, the FINESST-2025 decisions will be in January 2027, or 6 months after the July 2026 due date."

WHAT TO PUT IN FRONT OF A STUDENT (dated, defensible, all NASA-sourced):
- Watch for the next NOFO from **January 2027 onward** — it is gated on FINESST-25 decisions, which NASA expects in January 2027.
- Once released, intake runs "an approximate minimum of 60 days from the release" (NASA's wording in the FINESST-21 selections document), so expect roughly a 2–3 month writing window, not a year.

- Monitor point: https://go.nasa.gov/FINESST25 (the NSPIRES element page — NASA states "Any FINESST updates will be posted on the NSPIRES page for this program element"), plus the ROSES due-date tables.

WHY THE MONTH MOVES (state this to the user, don't hide it): the cycle is annual but the calendar month is NOT stable. Verified anchors — FINESST-24 "opened November 5, 2024 and closed February 26, 2025"; FINESST-25 opened July 10, 2025 and closed July 14, 2026. NASA moved the whole ROSES release month from February to July with ROSES-2025. As of 2026-09-18 ROSES-2026 has not appeared and the SARA page still describes "The current opportunities (in ROSES-2025)"; ROSES-2025 amendments have reached No. 74 with no FINESST-26 announcement.

SHUTDOWN RISK, in NASA's own words: "Because NASA is funded only through September 30, 2026, the end of the federal fiscal year, should there be a new lapse, that will impact the timing of decisions and the next NOFO release." Precedent: the 2025 lapse pushed some FINESST-24 decisions to April 10, 2026 — NASA calls it "an 18-month year!"
result.loi_deadline: Not applicable — there is no LOI, NOI, pre-proposal or Step-1 stage at any point. This is definitive and quotable twice over. Amendment 52 / F.5 header notice: "Neither notices of intent nor Step-1 proposals are requested nor accepted. Proposals are due July 14, 2026." F.5 Section 11 Summary of Key Information, row "Due date for Notice of Intent to propose (NOI)": "Not Applicable. Notices of Intent are not requested/accepted for this program element." ROSES-2025 Table 2 prints the F.5 NOI/Step-1 column as N/A. FINESST is therefore a single-step competition — useful to say plainly, because the ROSES-wide norm (NOI ~90 days out, or Step-1 → Step-2) does NOT apply here and students who read the general ROSES guidance often expect one.
result.deadline_pattern: Annual, single-step, one due date per competition, cut-off 11:59 pm Eastern Time. F.5 Section 11: "Proposals may be submitted at any time until 11:59 pm Eastern Time on the due date given in Tables 2 and 3 of ROSES." Not a rolling, no-due-date or flexible-due-date element. The cadence is reliable; the MONTH is not — it has ranged from late February (FINESST-24, closed 2025-02-26) to mid-July (FINESST-25, closed 2026-07-14) in consecutive cycles because of the ROSES release-month shift. No extensions should be assumed: Q77 of the FINESST-25 Q&A states "There are no plans to reopen/extend the FINESST due date. Such an action requires a formal amendment to the F.5 file." Live dates live in ROSES Table 2 (https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table2, by due date) and Table 3 (https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table3, by division); both were last amended September 2, 2026.
result.review_to_award:
TARGET: notification within ~6 months of the due date. FINESST-25 Q&A Q54: "Typically, all programs in ROSES, including FINESST aim to notify proposers within 6 months of the due date. However, the formal notification of award sent from the NASA Shared Services Center (NSSC) may take an additional 60 days." Applied to this cycle (Q76): "the FINESST-2025 decisions will be in January 2027, or 6 months after the July 2026 due date."

EARLIEST START: F.5 Section 7 — "The start date for new awards normally is no earlier than January 2027 and no later than one year after the proposal due date." Section 11 adds that proposers "may request an earlier start date, subject to NASA's 90-day pre-award spending policy." All new awards get an automatic 90 days of pre-award spending approval; costs incurred more than 90 days before the award need prior written approval from an NSSC Grants Officer, and any pre-award costs are at the proposer's risk.

MONEY IN HAND: later than notification. Q&A Q29: "All dates are estimates. It may be 60 days or longer after initial notification that the funds will be available." NASA pays through HHS's Payment Management System; "Normally, neither the PI nor FI access PMS."

HISTORICAL ACTUALS (FINESST-21, a February-2022 due date): selections communicated "late May through late July"; "Selection documents are released first, followed by non-selections. Non-selections may not be available until August 15, 2022, or later." So ~3.5–5.5 months to a yes, ~6 months to a no. Per-division NSPIRES publication dates in that cycle spanned May 26 to September 26, 2022 — i.e. divisions do not announce together, and Planetary Science deliberately releases selections and declines simultaneously.

DEVIATION FROM THE NASA NORM (worth flagging): the ROSES-wide goal of 150 days is aspirational here and has been missed badly. Some FINESST-24 decisions (Feb 2025 close) were not announced until April 10, 2026 — roughly 13.5 months — because of the 2025 federal funding lapse.

THE FI-SPECIFIC TRAP, and the single most practical thing to tell a student: the Future Investigator cannot see their own result. FINESST-21 selections document: "FIs, however, cannot receive or access FINESST decisions or review results directly via NSPIRES. If by August 15, the PI or AOR have not contacted the FI, then the FI should ask them to log in to NSPIRES to see if the proposal status has changed and download and share the results." NSPIRES emails only the PI and the AOR. Students should agree with their PI in advance who will check and forward the review. Post-award grant processing moves to the NSSC and cannot be tracked in NSPIRES — track it by a web search on the PI's name (not the FI's name or proposal number) at https://www.nasa.gov/centers/nssc/forms/grant-status-form, or call 1-877-NSSC123.
result.submission_requirements:
FINESST deviates sharply from the ROSES-wide norms. The deviations, not the norms:

PAGE LIMIT — 6 pages, not 15. F.5 §5.1.1.1: "The S/T/M section, excluding citations, may total no more than six (6) pages." Section 11 confirms "6 pages". This is the single biggest departure from the ROSES default.

FILE STRUCTURE — exactly two required PDFs plus one optional, and nothing else. §5.1: "No additional components or files are permitted."
 1. ANONYMIZED technical proposal (DAPR-compliant): S/T/M (6 pp) + References (no page limit, must directly follow S/T/M, excluded from the 6 pp) + Open Science and Data Management Plan (up to 2 pp) + Mentoring Plan or Agreement ("should not exceed two pages"; "Due to DAPR, the mentoring plan must not be signed"; prepared jointly by FI and mentor; reviewed under Scientific Merit).
 2. "EXPERTISE AND RESOURCES NOT ANONYMIZED" PDF: Research Readiness Statement (limit 1 page, "authored by the FI", must give a graduate-study timeline incl. degree type, subject area, time enrolled and estimated graduation month/year) + Biosketches for PI and FI (no page limit; NASA Grants Policy template required; optional for Co-I/collaborator mentors; none for non-mentors) + Current and Pending Support (no page limit; NASA template mandatory "Even if the FI and/or PI have no C&P other than the FINESST proposal to report") + Statements, Letters, Facilities/Equipment/Other Resources + Acknowledgements (limit 150 words, must affirm the FI was primary author) + Budget and Narrative.
 3. Optional High-End Computing appendix.

NO LETTERS OF RECOMMENDATION, NO TRANSCRIPTS — and this is enforced, not merely unrequested. §6.1: "Do not include academic transcripts or letters of recommendation anywhere within the proposal." Q&A Q65, asked about mentorship/recommendation letters from NASA-centre collaborators: "No. Including such letters or other documents FINESST does not request can lead to your proposal being returned without review for non-compliance." §6.1 also: "Proposals containing unsolicited appendices or attachments may be returned without review." Statements of Commitment are likewise not wanted — NSPIRES click-confirmation replaces them (they are required only on the Grants.gov route). Letters of Resource Support are needed only if the team lacks regular access to a required facility.

DUAL-ANONYMOUS REVIEW is mandatory here and catches people: reference callouts "must be numerical (e.g. [1], [2], etc.) rather than using author's names" — the Q&A calls name-based callouts "a serious DAPR violation" that "may result in your proposal being declared non-compliant." A named common error: citing your own institution's repository in the OSDMP instead of writing something like "will be archived at the PI/FI institution's repository." The NSPIRES cover-page Project Summary must also be anonymized. Review order: anonymized sections are graded first, then the non-anonymized E&R document.

ROLES AND SIGN-OFF — the student writes it, the advisor is PI, the institution submits. §1: the FI "shall have the primary initiative to define the proposed FINESST research project and must be the primary author." The FI is listed on the NSPIRES cover page as a Team Member with role "Graduate/Undergraduate Student"; the mentor appears as PI or Co-I. Submission is by the institution's Authorized Organizational Representative. Hard blocker: "A proposal cannot be submitted if any listed team member, including unfunded collaborators, does not log into NSPIRES and confirm their role on the proposal." Any additional named mentors must also be added as team members and confirm.

OTHER GOTCHAS: ORCID (or other digital persistent identifier) required in NSPIRES for PI, FI and Co-Is "To be eligible to receive funding." SciENcv-generated biosketches and C&P forms are NOT accepted. Formatting is enforceable grounds for return: 8.5x11, one-inch margins, no technical content in margins, max 15 characters/horizontal inch (~12 pt), max 5.5 lines/vertical inch. Budget: ≤$50,000 per 12-month budget year, ≤$150,000 over ≤36 months; no salary, travel or other costs for PIs, Co-Is or Collaborators ("FINESST awards are intended to support only student projects"); SMD suggested a student stipend of $40,000 per 12 months in the FINESST-21 cycle. Grants.gov funding opportunity number for this cycle: NNH25ZDA001N-FINESST.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves, from F.5 §4 (Eligibility), §7 (Award Information and Restrictions) and the FINESST-25 Q&A.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES OR LIMITS:
- One proposal per student per competition: "A principal investigator (PI) may submit one or more FINESST proposals, but a student shall be named as a Future Investigator (FI) on only one FINESST proposal."
- NASA civil servants may not be the FI (they may serve as mentors if listed on the cover page).
- NASA Centers and other non-degree-granting Federal entities are not eligible institutions; nor are degree-granting Federal entities that cannot accept federal financial assistance.
- Already-funded FIs face a budget constraint rather than a bar: "Past or currently funded FIs, including those who were a successor FI to the original student, are eligible to apply but they are subject to budget limitations."
- Overlapping support must be declared and can force a rewrite: §7 — "During the period that a FINESST proposal is under consideration or during the period of performance of a FINESST grant, the funded institution's Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) must inform NASA if the student has accepted any Federal or non-Federal fellowship or traineeship that 1) provides stipend and other costs, e.g., tuition that overlap with the FINESST award, and 2) is longer than three months in duration ... NASA may require a revised budget before award, and, if appropriate, a revised proposal for any active award." And flatly: "NASA will not fund duplicative work."
- Scope overlap with an existing NASA award must be addressed in the text: §5.1.1.1 — "In cases when the PI already has an ongoing research award from NASA, the research proposed under FINESST may address a similar topic, but the proposal must make clear, anonymously, how the proposed research goes beyond what NASA has already funded or recommended for potential funding."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half applicants most often get wrong):
- Prior unsuccessful applications never count against you: "FIs who previously proposed to, but are not funded by, a prior FINESST or any another NASA opportunity such as the NASA Earth and Space Sciences Fellowship (NESSF), the NASA Space Technology Graduate Research Opportunities (NSTGRO) etc., are eligible."
- Turning NASA down does not burn eligibility: "FIs who previously proposed to FINESST, were selected and declined the NASA funding also are eligible."
- Having held a FINESST award does not bar reapplication: "Past or currently funded FIs ... are eligible to apply but they are subject to budget limitations."
- Applying elsewhere at the same time is fine, it just has to be disclosed: "FIs who are applying concurrently for NSTRGO, the National Science Foundation's Graduate Research Fellowship (GRF), or any other federal funding, must list those proposals in the current and pending section." Disclosure goes in Current & Pending, not a bar.
- Stacking other money for uncovered costs is allowed: §7 — "Students funded by a FINESST grant may receive funding from other sources for any expenses not covered by this award."
- No citizenship or residency bar: a student "who is NOT a U.S. citizen or permanent resident" is eligible; international students (US visa or temporary protected status, enrolled at a US university, residing in the US) "are FI-eligible only through the university where they are enrolled."
- You do not have to be enrolled yet: an eligible FI is someone who by the proposal due date "has applied to, or has been admitted to, or is enrolled as a graduate student."
- No discipline or degree-type restriction — Master's, PhD, or both; the Q&A confirms Doctor of Engineering students are normally eligible if the project is relevant.
- On the PI side there is no cap at all: "A principal investigator (PI) may submit one or more FINESST proposals," and Q35 — "PIs with current FIs are eligible to propose with a new FI. In fact, in past competitions some PIs have one more than one FI awarded in that same FINESST year." An advisor already carrying a FINESST student is not a reason to hold back.
- The mentor need not be at the proposing institution: "Unless the submitting institution has a requirement, NASA has no requirement that the mentor be at the proposing institution."

CORRECTION NEEDED IN THE EXISTING ROW (not applied — data only): data/mechanisms.csv currently states "a student may hold only one FINESST/NESSF award tied to a single degree pursuit; prior recipients for the same degree are ineligible (per FINESST NOFO)." The second clause is contradicted by the current NOFO, which says past and currently funded FIs ARE eligible to apply, subject to budget limitations. The accurate restriction is one FI role per proposal per competition, not a lifetime/per-degree bar.
result.program_officer_contact:
Pre-submission contact is expected for scope and eligibility, and NASA names a route rather than leaving you to guess. F.5 §2: "If proposers, have research eligibility questions, then they should email HQ-FINESST@mail.nasa.gov and one or more of the Points of Contact in Section 11 well in advance of the proposal due date." §10: "Email questions to the relevant division(s) Funding POC(s) listed in Section 11 and HQ-FINESST@mail.nasa.gov."

COORDINATING MAILBOX: HQ-FINESST@mail.nasa.gov

FINESST PROGRAM SCIENTISTS BY DIVISION (ROSES-25 F.5 §11):
- Earth Science: yaitza.luna-cruz@nasa.gov and cynthia.r.hall@nasa.gov
- Planetary Science: Nick Lang and Henry Throop — shared mailbox HQ-PSDFINESST@mail.nasa.gov
- Astrophysics: antonino.cucchiara@nasa.gov and roopesh.ojha@nasa.gov
- Heliophysics: jared.m.bell@nasa.gov
- Biological & Physical Sciences: ursula.m.koniges@nasa.gov

THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE QUESTION is which division to submit to — the student picks one division at proposal creation, and §6.1 warns that a proposal whose "research scope is beyond the reviewing division's specifications ... may be returned without peer review" (though SMD may offer to move or share it between divisions "when it is practical to do so"). Cross-divisional work should be flagged on the cover page. Ask this one early.

THE OTHER TWO PEOPLE TO TALK TO, and NASA insists on them: your PI/mentor and your institution's AOR / sponsored programs office. Q&A Q2: "An FI should not try and prepare a budget alone. The FI must talk to their Principal Investigator (PI) and Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) about the submitting organization's budget policies and practices." NASA will not pre-approve budgets — "Grants Officers (GO) at NASA Shared Services Center, not the FINESST Team, will have the final word on all and any costs."

SYSTEMS vs CONTENT: NSPIRES Help Desk nspires-help@nasaprs.com / (202) 479-9376, Mon–Fri 8 am–6 pm ET, and Grants.gov support@grants.gov / (800) 518-4726, handle the systems only; content and policy go to the program officers above.

ANONYMITY NORM WORTH KNOWING: because FINESST is dual-anonymous, the public pre-proposal events are run anonymously — "To preserve anonymity of callers, callers should not disclose their names or institutions," with anonymous questions taken via a public board. A conversation with a program scientist cannot influence how the panel grades you (the panel does not know who you are until after grading); it influences whether you are in the right division, at the right scale, with an eligible project. Questions asked publicly get answered publicly in the cycle's Q&A document.

NOT ESTABLISHED: no NASA statement was found that FINESST program scientists will or will not read draft proposals or summaries. There is no documented NASA equivalent of NIH's "send me your specific aims." Treat draft review as not found rather than as available.
result.examples_or_samples:
FUNDED ABSTRACTS: yes, published per cycle per division, and they name the PI–FI pair — which is how a student finds the people in their subfield NASA just funded. Verified example (fetched and read): the FINESST-21 selections document, NNH21ZDA001N-FINESST, https://nspires.nasaprs.com/external/viewrepositorydocument?cmdocumentid=890512 — it opens with SMD-wide statistics (927 proposals reviewed, 139 selected across six divisions, i.e. roughly a 15% success rate), gives per-division NSPIRES publication dates, then lists each selection alphabetically by PI last name in the form "Mitchell Begelman (PI) / Hannalore Gerling-Dunsmore (FI), University of Colorado, Boulder" followed by the project title and a paragraph abstract.

HOW TO FIND THEM FOR ANY CYCLE: go to https://nspires.nasaprs.com, click "CLOSED/PAST", filter by keyword "FINESST", open the cycle's program-element page, and download the PDF linked under the heading "Selections". FINESST-25 selections are NOT yet posted — decisions are expected January 2027, so the most recent published sets are the earlier cycles.

THE BEST "GET STARTED" MATERIALS, all on the FINESST-25 NSPIRES page (https://go.nasa.gov/FINESST25) under Announcement Documents / Other Documents:
- **FINESST-25 Questions and Answers**, posted June 23, 2026 and updated July 9, 2026 to add Questions 74–77 — 77 real questions from actual applicants with NASA's answers, covering budgets, DAPR anonymization, eligibility, multiple mentors, project duration, and what happens after submission. https://nspires.nasaprs.com/external/viewrepositorydocument?cmdocumentid=1139140&solicitationId=%7bF9C7B701-6405-FD55-6705-EB4B190646B8%7d&viewSolicitationDocument=1 — this is the single most useful document for a first-time applicant, more so than the NOFO.
- FINESST25 Webinar Slides (May 28, 2026 pre-proposal webinar): cmdocumentid=1133449. NOTE: NASA posted a separate file, "28 May Webinar Recording Not Available," explaining the recording was not released — so the slides are the only artefact from that event.
- F.5 FINESST Earth Office Hours Slides (Earth Science Division, June 23–24, 2026).
- Guidelines for Proposers to ROSES Dual-Anonymous Peer Review Programs: https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/dual-anonymous-peer-review/
- Mandatory NASA Grants Policy templates for the Biographical Sketch and Current & Pending Support (linked from F.5 §5.1.2.2–5.1.2.3), plus NASA's Grants Policy and Compliance Team video explaining both.
- SMD Open-Source Science Guidance and division-specific OSDMP templates (via ROSES-2025 F.1 Cross Division Research Overview).
- Optional FINESST RPPR progress-report template: https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/faqs/#faq-11

SELECTION STATISTICS: https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/grant-stats/ publishes "July 2025 ROSES Selection Stats" as PDF and Excel (ROSESGrantStats_072825_TAGGED.pdf / ROSESGrantStats_072825.xlsx). NASA states "Our current graduate student research program ... is part of ROSES and data for that program is part of the grant stats spreadsheet above" — FINESST is inside the workbook, not broken out on the page, so the per-cycle selections PDFs remain the better source for FINESST-specific rates.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST — say so plainly so nobody hunts: NASA does not publish full funded proposals, does not publish summary statements, and has no NIH-RePORTER-style searchable abstract database covering SMD. NASA's disclosure commitment is limited to PI name, team member names, title, abstract and keywords, and "It is NASA's policy not to release any information about proposals that are not selected for funding." To read a complete funded FINESST proposal you have to get it from a person — your PI, your department, your division's analysis group, or a recent awardee found via the selections PDFs. Community-curated FINESST example collections are reported to exist on GitHub and personal sites; I did not verify any, so treat that as a lead, not a citation.
result.resubmission_note:
Allowed, unrestricted, and — importantly for morale — carries neither penalty nor credit. FINESST-25 Q&A Q9: "Each submission to FINESST, including a resubmission, is considered to be an ENTIRELY new proposal. NASA does not compare prior and current year proposals from the same FI." There is no A1/A2 designation, no Introduction page, no required response-to-reviewers, and no cap on attempts.

NASA actively warns against writing the resubmission as a reply to last year's panel: "It is always a good idea to consider reviewer's advice, but saying that you are only addressing reviewer comments may or may not make the proposal competitive. Last year's reviewers may not be reviewers again this year, so addressing your proposal to last year's reviewers may confuse the new reviewers." Under dual-anonymous review the new panel has no idea it is a resubmission, so the proposal must stand alone.

Eligibility after a decline is explicitly preserved (F.5 §4): FIs who previously proposed and were not funded are eligible; so are FIs who were selected and declined the funding. The FINESST-21 selections document told non-selected teams directly: "A non-selected 2021 FINESST proposal may be eligible to be revised and resubmitted to the 2022 competition. Entirely new, eligible proposals also are welcome."

Practical constraint on timing: because "Normally, two FINESST NOFOs (competitions) are not open at the same time" and the next NOFO is released only after the current cycle's decisions, a declined applicant generally cannot resubmit until the following annual competition — and must still be an eligible graduate student at that point.

Reviews come back to the PI and AOR through NSPIRES, not to the student directly, so a student planning to resubmit must ask their PI to download and share the evaluation. The ROSES-wide debriefing and reconsideration track (SPD-09D: debrief requestable within 30 days of the evaluation; written reconsideration limited to factual errors or inconsistencies, judged only on material in the original proposal) applies to FINESST as a ROSES element, but nothing FINESST-specific about debriefs was found in the F.5 element or the Q&A.
unresolved: FINESST-26 due date: not published as of 2026-09-18. NASA states the next NOFO will likely follow the FINESST-25 decisions expected January 2027, but no date, and no ROSES-2026 has been released (SARA still lists ROSES-2025 as the current opportunities; ROSES-2025 amendments have reached No. 74 with no FINESST-26 notice). Re-check https://go.nasa.gov/FINESST25 and the ROSES tables after January 2027.

Whether all six SMD divisions will participate in the next cycle: NASA explicitly warns they may not — 'not every part of SMD participates in every call/solicitation' and 'one or more a part of SMD may choose to skip the next FINESST competition.' Division participation must be re-checked per cycle, not assumed from FINESST-25.

Per-division selection counts for FINESST-21 could not be read reliably: the two-column table in the selections PDF was mangled by text extraction and the division labels are offset from their numbers (the document's own header notice further revises the Astrophysics figure to 28, while a later section heading reads 29). Only the SMD-wide total is safe to publish: 927 reviewed, 139 selected (~15%). Do not display a per-division breakdown from this extraction without re-reading the PDF visually.

FINESST selection rates for the 2022-2025 cycles: not established. The SARA grant-stats workbook (ROSESGrantStats_072825.xlsx) reportedly contains FINESST data but was not opened this pass; the FINESST-only rate would have to be computed from it or from each cycle's selections PDF.
Whether FINESST program scientists will review draft proposals or pre-proposal summaries: no NASA statement found either way. Recorded as not found, not as unavailable.

Actual FINESST-25 decision date: expected January 2027 per NASA, but contingent on there being no federal funding lapse after September 30, 2026. The FINESST-24 precedent (some decisions delayed to April 10, 2026) shows this slipping by many months is a live scenario.

F.5 Section 12.23 ('How do I know NASA got the proposal? What if my proposal is marked late?') is cited by the Q&A but did not appear in the extracted text of the F.5 PDF, which runs 12.19 then to Section 13. Possible extraction gap or a later-amended element version; confirmation-of-receipt mechanics were therefore taken from the ROSES-wide norm rather than from F.5 directly.
