No search index was used for any claim. This is a coverage limit, not a gap in what was found - but it means I could not cross-check the funder's text against third-party reporting of an extension or a cancelled cycle.

result.program_name: Fulbright U.S. Student Program
result.funder: Fulbright Program (U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs); administered for ECA by the Institute of International Education (IIE)
result.next_deadline:
NATIONAL DEADLINE: Tuesday, October 6, 2026 at 5:00 pm Eastern Time, for the 2027-2028 competition. The funder's wording, repeated on every page of the site: "The 2027-2028 Competition is now open. The national deadline is Tuesday October 6, 2026 at 5 pm Eastern Time". That is 18 days from today (2026-09-18).

BUT THE NATIONAL DEADLINE IS NOT THE ONE MOST APPLICANTS FACE. If you are currently enrolled at a U.S. college or university, you go through your campus first, and: "The Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA) will set a campus application deadline for the institution's students, which is typically 4-6 weeks earlier than the final October deadline." For this cycle that puts campus deadlines roughly late August to mid September 2026 — i.e. for most campuses, ALREADY PASSED as of today. A currently-enrolled student reading this in mid-September 2026 has most likely missed their campus route for 2027-2028 and should contact their FPA immediately to ask whether a late campus review is possible; the realistic target is the 2028-2029 cycle.

THIRD DATE, easy to miss: "The deadline to request a letter be un-submitted is Friday, October 2, 2026 at 5:00pm Eastern Time." — four days before the national deadline, and the last moment to fix a recommendation problem.

PATTERN (annual, one cycle a year): competition opens early April; national deadline falls on a Tuesday in early October at 5 pm ET; campus deadlines 4-6 weeks earlier, set individually by each institution's FPA. The 2028-2029 competition should therefore open early April 2027 with an early-October 2027 national deadline, but that date is not yet published — do not treat it as fixed.
result.deadline_pattern: Annual, single competition cycle. Application opens early April, national deadline a Tuesday in early October at 5:00 pm ET, decisions the following spring, grant start the following academic year. Layered deadlines: (1) campus deadline, set per institution by the FPA, 4-6 weeks before the national deadline; (2) recommendation un-submit request deadline, ~4 days before the national deadline; (3) national deadline, by which the applicant's own submission AND all three recommendations AND the Foreign Language Evaluation AND (where required) the Letter of Affiliation must all be in. Every supporting item is due at the national deadline, not after it.
result.loi_deadline:
No formal letter of intent or pre-proposal exists. But there are TWO de facto pre-stages, and both are where first-timers fail:

(1) THE CAMPUS ROUTE (enrolled students and, where the institution accommodates them, recent alumni). You apply through your campus FPA, meet a campus deadline 4-6 weeks before the national one, and go before a "Campus Interview Committee". The funder's own instruction: "Make any necessary revisions based on feedback from the Campus Interview Committee (pertains only to candidates applying through a U.S. institution)." The FPA then uploads a Campus Committee Evaluation (CCE) form into your application — described by the funder as giving "constructive feedback to applicants about their proposal" and giving the National Screening Committee insight into the candidate. FPA-facing webinars this cycle were "FPA Webinar: CCE Form Overview" (3 Sept 2026), "FPA Office Hours: CCE Form" (15 Sept 2026) and "FPA Webinar: Final Steps (including uploading CCE Form)" (24 Sept 2026), which brackets the real campus calendar. Skipping the campus route is allowed — "If your institution is not listed or does not currently have a Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA), you are welcome to apply as an At-Large applicant" — and carries no penalty: "At-Large applicants are at no disadvantage during the selection process and are regularly selected to receive Fulbright grants." But an enrolled student is "strongly encouraged" to go through their institution.

(2) THE LETTER OF AFFILIATION (Study/Research awards). For awards that require one it must be IN HAND at the national deadline: "Failure to submit a letter of affiliation for an award which requires one at the national deadline may result in an application being deemed ineligible. Late affiliation letters are not accepted." Securing it means finding and persuading a host institution abroad months in advance. This is the single longest lead item in the whole application and functionally a pre-stage even though nothing is filed with IIE. The funder runs a dedicated session on it: "Application Tips: Study/Research Award - Finding a Letter of Affiliation".

Net: start 9-12 months before the national deadline. Nothing is filed early, but the campus review and the host-country affiliation both have to be finished before you can submit.
result.review_to_award:
Published stage by stage on the funder's Competition & Selection page, and materially slower and more layered than the DOE norm because a foreign government or binational commission gets a second, independent say.

- OCTOBER — technical review: IIE staff screen for eligibility and completeness. (Purely administrative; the URL, transcript and language-form rules kill applications here.)
- NOVEMBER - DECEMBER — National Screening Committee review: discipline-based faculty reviewers read and rate.
- BY THE END OF JANUARY — first notification: you learn whether you are "Recommended" or "Non-Recommended". Binary, ~3.5 months after the deadline. A "Recommended" is not an award; it is forwarding to the host country.
- JANUARY - APRIL — host country review: "Embassies and Fulbright Commissions conduct interviews and request materials". This is a second competition, run abroad, with its own criteria and its own interview. Recommended candidates should expect to be contacted for an interview and for extra documents in this window.
- MARCH - JUNE — final selections, released "on a rolling basis in the spring". Your country's post decides when; there is no single announcement date, so two applicants to different countries can hear five months apart.
- GRANT START — for the 2027-2028 award year, grants begin "no later than June 1, 2028"; most start with the host country's academic year, so typically Aug-Oct 2027 for northern-hemisphere placements.

END TO END: ~4 months deadline-to-first-word, 5-8 months deadline-to-final-answer, and 10-20 months deadline-to-departure. From first drafting to boarding a plane is close to two years. Plan finances and any degree-completion timing around the rolling spring answer, not around a fixed date.
result.submission_requirements:
DEVIATES SHARPLY FROM THE FUNDER-WIDE/DOE NORM IN THREE WAYS: the applicant of record is the individual, not an institution (no SAM.gov, no UEI, no AOR, no Grants.gov — you submit yourself at https://apply.iie.org/fulbrightusstudent); limits are CHARACTER counts, not page counts; and there is no post-submission fix of any kind.

ESSAYS — count characters, not pages:
- Study/Research (Academic): Statement of Grant Purpose "6,000 characters in length including spaces and punctuation". No bibliographies, citations or URLs. No personal contact information.
- English Teaching Assistant: Statement of Grant Purpose "limited to a maximum of 3,000 characters, including spaces and punctuation", plus an abstract with a "1750-character limit".
- Short answers, three, both award types: Flexibility & Adaptability "2,000 character limit"; Community Engagement "2,000 character limit"; Impact of Fulbright Award "1,000 character limit".
- URLs are fatal, not merely ignored: "Do not include links to websites or external files/materials. Adding any URLs to external websites may result in your application being deemed ineligible."

RECOMMENDATIONS — three, and the ETA variant is a form, not a letter:
- "You must submit three recommendation letters." You register recommenders in the system and they upload directly.
- "All recommendations must be submitted by the application deadline, Tuesday October 6, 2026." And: "Late recommendation submissions are not accepted under any circumstances."
- ETA only: "Recommenders for English Teaching Assistant Program applicants do not submit written letters of recommendation and must complete this recommendation form in full." Tell ETA recommenders this early — many will otherwise write a letter that cannot be used.
- Un-submit request deadline: "Friday, October 2, 2026 at 5:00pm Eastern Time."

LANGUAGE FORMS — two, one of them external:
- Language Self-Evaluation inside the application, PLUS a Foreign Language Evaluation form completed by a professional language teacher or native speaker. "Submission of both the Language Self-Evaluation portion of the application and Foreign Language Evaluation form is mandatory ... Failure to submit required language forms may result in your application being deemed ineligible." Whether it is Not Required / Recommended / Required is set per country award and is a filter in Award Search.

LETTER OF AFFILIATION (Study/Research): required where the award requires it, on institutional letterhead, signed, in English, and not from a relative. "Late affiliation letters are not accepted."

TRANSCRIPTS: "You must provide transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions from which you received degrees. Transcripts must also be submitted from other institutions where you studied and received 12 or more credits for coursework where the credits are not reflected as transfer credits on your undergraduate transcript." Must be registrar-produced and show your name and the institution; screenshots are rejected; graduate students must still include undergraduate transcripts. "Failure to submit at minimum the required transcripts will result in your application being declared ineligible."

ARTS APPLICANTS add a discipline-specific portfolio, all due at the same national deadline: creative writing "maximum of ten pages of double-spaced text" (exceeding it renders the application ineligible); visual arts "no more than twenty images of current work"; theater design "no more than twenty images"; architecture "no more than twenty pages of design content"; dance video "no longer than ten minutes in total"; theater acting "totaling no longer than six minutes"; voice up to four unedited videos, max six minutes each; music composition three manuscript scores with recordings. File caps: 64 MB documents/images, 5 GB audio, 5 GB video.

CAMPUS ROUTE adds the Campus Interview Committee and the FPA-uploaded CCE form.

TWO RULES THAT CATCH PEOPLE: "You are responsible for submitting your own application before the National Deadline; your Fulbright Program Adviser cannot do this on your behalf." And: "Application submissions are final. Applications cannot be unsubmitted for any reason." There is no DOE-style PAMS withdrawal, no Changed/Corrected resubmission, no last-timestamp-wins. Preview the PDF proof before you submit — the funder's own checklist tells you to, because text that overruns is cut off rather than flagged.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES. The half people get wrong is the second one: a prior Fulbright is a PREFERENCE against you, not a bar, and this program has no two-year waiting rule (that rule belongs to the Fulbright U.S. Scholar Program, a different mechanism).

WHAT MAKES YOU INELIGIBLE
- A conferred doctorate: ineligible are "Applicants who currently hold or will hold a doctoral degree (Ph.D.) by the national application deadline." The test is conferral by the deadline, not enrolment.
- Medical degree enrolment abroad: ineligible are "Applicants seeking enrollment in a medical degree program abroad."
- MDs are restricted, not excluded: "Doctors of Medicine may receive grants for advanced academic study, but not for internships or residencies." Advanced research by an MD belongs in the Fulbright Scholar Program instead.
- Long residence abroad: ineligible if you "resided abroad for five or more years in the six-year period preceding" the deadline, where anyone who "has lived outside the United States for nine months or more during a calendar year is deemed to have resided abroad for that year."
- Federal/Fulbright-agency employment, for you and your immediate family: ineligible "for a period ending one year following the termination of such employment, association, or service" — covering U.S. Department of State, USAID, agencies under State Department contract, exchange-program selection officers, Fulbright Commission board members and staff, and Foreign Scholarship Board members. "Immediate family members (i.e., spouses and dependent children)" are caught too, though "self-supporting children who live apart from their parents" are not. Carve-out: "This provision does not apply to interns" — but taking employment afterwards triggers it.
- Concurrent applications: you "may not apply to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program and the Fulbright Scholar Program in the same competition cycle" and "may not apply for more than one Fulbright U.S. Student grant in each competition cycle." One country, one award, one cycle.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half that matters
- A PRIOR FULBRIGHT DOES NOT DISQUALIFY YOU. The funder's words: "there is a program preference for those who have not previously held a Fulbright grant." Preference, not exclusion. And for the most recent cohorts specifically, applicants from the 2024-2025, 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 programs "will be at a competitive disadvantage, but are still eligible to apply." No stated waiting period, no cap on attempts.
- SUSPENSION CARVE-OUT: "Fulbright participants whose programs in the Middle East were suspended in Spring 2026 will not be disadvantaged if they reapply." Anyone in that cohort reapplies on a clean footing.
- A J.D. IS FINE: applicants "may hold a J.D. at the time of application." The doctoral bar is the Ph.D., not every doctoral-level credential.
- DOCTORAL CANDIDACY IS FINE. Master's holders, ABD students and dissertation-stage candidates are eligible so long as the Ph.D. is not conferred by the national deadline — which is precisely the graduate_predoc window this row serves.
- APPLYING WITHOUT A CAMPUS IS FINE: "At-Large applicants are at no disadvantage during the selection process and are regularly selected to receive Fulbright grants."
- Non-degree federal funding, assistantships, NSF GRFP, teaching fellowships and the like are nowhere listed as conflicts; nothing in the published eligibility rules excludes concurrent or prior non-Fulbright awards.

DISADVANTAGE ≠ INELIGIBILITY (a third category the funder names explicitly): "Applicants whose higher education was undertaken primarily at" non-U.S. institutions, and those with "six or more months" of recent host-country experience, are at a competitive disadvantage but may still apply. If either describes you, address it head-on in the Statement of Grant Purpose rather than hoping it goes unnoticed.

DUAL NATIONALS: not barred by IIE, but must "ascertain whether they have, or are eligible to have, their host country's nationality and to address any potential consequences thereof before they accept an award" — the host country can block you even when the U.S. side clears you. Resolve this before you choose a country, not after you are Recommended.
result.program_officer_contact:
There is NO program officer in the NIH/DOE sense — nobody pre-clears your idea, and there is no named manager who decides your topic's home. The country and award you apply to is chosen by you from the published Award Search catalogue. Two contact routes, plus one that matters more than either.

1. YOUR CAMPUS FULBRIGHT PROGRAM ADVISER (FPA) — the primary route for anyone enrolled, and for alumni whose last institution will take them. Find yours at https://us.fulbrightonline.org/applicants/search-for-a-fulbright-program-adviser by institution name or state. The FPA sets the campus deadline, convenes the Campus Interview Committee, uploads the CCE form, and in practice holds a file of past successful applications from your campus. Contact is not merely expected, it is structurally required if you use the campus route. If your institution has no FPA, you apply At-Large with no penalty.

2. IIE PROGRAM STAFF — general: FBstudent@iie.org, 1-800-272-6994 (9am-5pm Eastern). By region: East Asia-Pacific FBstudent.EAP@iie.org; Europe & Eurasia FBstudent.EUR@iie.org; Middle East & North Africa FBstudent.MENA@iie.org; South & Central Asia FBstudent.SCA@iie.org; Sub-Saharan Africa FBstudent.AF@iie.org; Western Hemisphere FBstudent.WHA@iie.org. Sub-programs: Fulbright-Fogarty FBstudent.fogarty@iie.org; Fulbright-National Geographic FBstudent.natgeo@iie.org. Application technical support: FBstudentsupport@iie.org. FPA support (advisers only): FPA@iie.org. Media: Fulbright.Press@iie.org. Use the regional address for questions about a specific country's award, its language requirement, or whether it requires an affiliation letter.

3. THE CONVERSATION THAT ACTUALLY DECIDES YOUR APPLICATION is with your prospective host abroad, not with IIE. For Study/Research awards you need a named academic or institution willing to sign a Letter of Affiliation on letterhead, and the quality of that relationship shows in the proposal. Start cold-emailing potential hosts 6-9 months before the deadline. The funder runs a whole session on how: "Application Tips: Study/Research Award - Finding a Letter of Affiliation".

LOW-RISK WAY IN IF YOU DO NOT WANT TO COLD-EMAIL: the funder runs free live webinars and posts recordings — see https://us.fulbrightonline.org/applicants/information-sessions and https://us.fulbrightonline.org/resources/recorded-webinars — and four on-demand tutorials at https://us.fulbrightonline.org/tutorials, available 24/7.
result.examples_or_samples:
FOUR ROUTES, in order of usefulness to someone starting from zero.

1. THE OFFICIAL ANNOTATED GUIDANCE — free, on demand, and specific to the pieces people fail on. Recorded webinars at https://us.fulbrightonline.org/resources/recorded-webinars include "Application Tips: Statement of Grant Purpose", "Application Tips: Short Answers", "Application Tips: Study/Research Award - Finding a Letter of Affiliation", "Your Future with Fulbright: How to Apply for the Fulbright Study/Research Award", "Your Future with Fulbright: How to Apply for the Fulbright English Teaching Assistantship", "Your Future with Fulbright: Dissertations, Post-Doc Opportunities, and Conducting Research Abroad", "Fulbright for Medical and Public Health Research", "Your Future with Fulbright: Creative Journeys with the Arts Award", plus a "Fulbright Alumni Voices" series. Four on-demand tutorials at https://us.fulbrightonline.org/tutorials: General Overview; The Study/Research Award; Arts Study/Research Award; The ETA Program — the funder states these are accessible 24/7. Live sessions and registration at https://us.fulbrightonline.org/applicants/information-sessions.

2. FIND A REAL FUNDED PERSON AND ASK THEM — https://us.fulbrightonline.org/alumni/grantee-directory. Filterable by U.S. institution, host country (80+), year (1949-2025), field of study and U.S. state. This is how you locate someone from your own department who won in your country and field, and ask to read their Statement of Grant Purpose. It is the closest thing to a sample library that the funder itself operates.

3. YOUR FPA'S CAMPUS FILE — the de facto sample collection. Advisers at established campuses keep past successful applications and run the Campus Interview Committee that critiques yours. To find the campuses with the deepest operations, see Top Producing Institutions at https://topproducing.fulbrightonline.org/.

4. CALIBRATE YOUR ODDS — applications vs awards by country and by award type, with columns for 2024-2025, 2025-2026 and 2026-2027, at https://us.fulbrightonline.org/study-research-eta-statistics. Country-level selectivity varies enormously and this table is how you pick a realistic target. TOOLING NOTE: this table is JavaScript-rendered and a plain fetch returns the filters and column headers with empty cells — the numbers need a rendering browser. I could not read the figures, so none are recorded here.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: IIE and ECA publish no funded application texts and no official sample-essay library, and unlike DOE there is no public award-abstract database for this program. Individual campus fellowship offices are the usual source of publicly posted redacted Statements of Grant Purpose — I attempted to verify several (Carnegie Mellon, Notre Dame, Penn State, Michigan) and every URL returned 404, DNS failure or 403 within this session's fetch budget, so treat "ask your FPA" as the verified route and campus web libraries as plausible but unverified here.
result.resubmission_note:
No formal resubmission mechanism, no A1 numbering, no introduction page, no cap on attempts, and no stated waiting period for anyone who has not previously held a Fulbright grant. The competition is annual; a declined applicant simply applies again in the next cycle as a fresh application. A prior GRANTEE may also reapply — the constraint is a stated preference against them, not a bar (see prior_funding_conflicts).

TWO STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES FROM DOE/NIH THAT CHANGE HOW YOU SHOULD WORK.

(a) NO POST-SUBMISSION REPAIR. "Application submissions are final. Applications cannot be unsubmitted for any reason." There is no PAMS-style withdrawal, no Changed/Corrected version, no last-timestamp-wins rule. The only fix window is the recommendation un-submit request, "Friday, October 2, 2026 at 5:00pm Eastern Time", four days before the national deadline.

(b) NO REVIEWER COMMENTS AFTER THE FACT. The January notification is binary — "Recommended" or "Non-Recommended" — and no route to written reviewer feedback from IIE appears anywhere on the funder's pages (recorded as unresolved, not as a denial). The structured critique in this program happens BEFORE submission, not after: the Campus Committee Evaluation is described by the funder as providing "constructive feedback to applicants about their proposal". Practical consequence — if you intend to reapply, the leverage is in going through a campus review next time, not in waiting for a summary statement that does not come.

ONE PER CYCLE: you "may not apply for more than one Fulbright U.S. Student grant in each competition cycle" and cannot run a Student and a Scholar application in the same cycle. There is no hedging across two countries.
unresolved: Applications and awards by country and award type (2024-2025, 2025-2026, 2026-2027) — https://us.fulbrightonline.org/study-research-eta-statistics is JavaScript-rendered and a plain fetch returned the filters and column headers with empty data cells. Needs a rendering browser. No selectivity figures are recorded rather than estimated ones.

Whether unsuccessful applicants can obtain any written feedback or reviewer comments from IIE after the Non-Recommended notification — no such route is described anywhere on the funder's pages. Absence of a statement, not a statement of absence.

Per-country award requirements inside Award Search — specifically which countries require a Letter of Affiliation at the national deadline versus later, and which set the Foreign Language Evaluation to Required rather than Recommended. Award Search is an interactive JS tool and is not enumerable by plain fetch; the filters exist (language requirement: Not Required / Recommended / Required) but per-country values were not read.

Specific campus fellowship-office libraries of public sample Statements of Grant Purpose — attempted Carnegie Mellon, Notre Dame, Penn State and Michigan; all returned 404, DNS failure or 403. Tooling facts, not evidence that such libraries do not exist.
The 2028-2029 national deadline. The 'opens early April, closes early October' pattern is published; the 2027 date is not. Do not infer one.

Fulbright-Fogarty and Fulbright-National Geographic supplementary components and any sub-deadlines beyond the shared 6 October 2026 national deadline — the Types of Awards page states the national deadline applies to all programs, but the Nat Geo storytelling component and the Fogarty NIH-site arrangements were not examined in detail. Note Nat Geo scale: 'The National Geographic Society expects to select up to five applicants for this award.'
Exact 2026 campus deadlines — these are set individually by each institution's FPA and are not published centrally; only the '4-6 weeks earlier' guidance is funder-stated.

Grant duration as a published figure — the Award Benefits page describes stipend, travel, health benefits and language study but does not state a duration; Award Search listings show 6-24 months per award. Whether dependents are supported is an Award Search filter but is not stated program-wide.

THE DATED CHAIN (all verbatim from the Federal Register):
1. FY2025 NIA published 30 Oct 2024 (89 FR 86323): "Applications Available: October 30, 2024. Deadline for Transmittal of Applications: January 15, 2025."
2. Extended 3 Dec 2024 (FR 2024-28290): "This extension notice extends the deadline for the transmittal of applications to January 29, 2025" — "In consideration of upcoming holiday observances and academic year winter breaks at eligible institutions."
3. CANCELLED 9 May 2025 (FR 2025-08109): "The NIAs published in the Federal Register on October 25, 2024 (89 FR 85176)--GPA, October 20, 2024 (89 FR 86323)--DDRA, and January 8, 2025 (90 FR 1469)--FRA, are withdrawn and the competitions cancelled as of May 9, 2025." Reason given: "The Department is cancelling the competitions as part of a comprehensive review of recently published FY 2025 NIAs. This reevaluation seeks to ensure that all priorities and requirements for the Department's FY 2025 competitions align with the objectives established by the Trump Administration."

FOUR INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATIONS THAT NO FY2026 CYCLE RAN:
- Federal Register: a search of all documents since 2025-01-01 mentioning "Fulbright-Hays" returns 7 results, none of them a DDRA notice inviting applications.
- Grants.gov API, Assistance Listing 84.022: 17 opportunities, every one "archived" or "closed". Newest is ED-GRANTS-103024-001 (opened 10/30/2024, closed 01/29/2025). Nothing posted or forecasted.
- USAspending, ALN 84.022: award IDs run P022A18 through P022A24 only. ZERO FY2025 (P022A25) and ZERO FY2026 (P022A26) awards exist. Awards were made in FY2024 and then stop dead.
- ED's own current IFLE programme page lists only two programmes — CAANN (84.015C) and MECE (84.021C). DDRA is absent, and the DDRA page URL cited inside the FY2025 NIA itself now returns HTTP 404.

PLUS A PENDING REGULATORY KILL: on 1 July 2026 ED published an NPRM (FR 2026-13248) proposing to rescind the DDRA regulations outright: "ED proposes to rescind all regulations under parts 662, 663, and 664." Part 662 IS DDRA. ED's rationale: these regs "codify programs that are not named in statute, including program names, eligible entities, program activities, selection criteria." Comments closed 31 July 2026. As of 16 Sept 2026 (latest eCFR issue) 34 CFR part 662 is STILL IN FORCE and no final rule has published — so DDRA's regulatory basis is alive but under active proposal to be removed.

DO NOT CONFUSE WITH: the "Mutual Education and Cultural Exchange (MECE)" competition (FR 2026-12425, applications due 15 July 2026, $10,193,170, 2-4 awards, 36 months). It runs under the same Fulbright-Hays Act authority but it is NOT DDRA: eligible applicants are "Public or private nonprofit foundations, educational or other institutions", it funds "visits and study in foreign countries by teachers and prospective teachers", and its priorities are "Patriotic Education" and "Returning Education to the States". A PhD student cannot apply to it for dissertation research.
result.deadline_pattern:
Historically annual, and the dates were always published — here is the actual series from the Grants.gov API (ALN 84.022), open date → close date:
- FY2019: 2019-01-24 → 2019-03-25
- FY2020: 2019-12-17 → 2020-02-18
- FY2021: 2021-02-04 → 2021-04-05
- FY2022: 2022-02-02 → 2022-04-06
- FY2023: 2023-02-10 → 2023-04-28 (extended; FR 2023-07419 also amended selection criterion (b)(3) mid-competition)
- FY2024: 2024-01-29 → 2024-03-29
- FY2025: 2024-10-30 → 2025-01-15, extended to 2025-01-29, then CANCELLED 2025-05-09

SHAPE: notice published mid-winter (Dec–Feb, once in October), applications due roughly 8 weeks later (Feb–Apr, once in January), institutional grant starts 30 September every single year without exception. Closing time is always 11:59:59 p.m. Eastern.

This pattern is now BROKEN, not merely late. FY2026 produced no notice, no opportunity and no awards. Anyone planning fieldwork should treat DDRA as unavailable until ED publishes a new NIA, and should not hold a field season open waiting for it.
result.loi_deadline:
No ED-level letter of intent or pre-proposal has ever been required. But TWO earlier gates function like one and are the most common way a strong student misses this award entirely:

(1) THE CAMPUS DEADLINE — this is the real one. The legal applicant is the university, not the student. Per 34 CFR 662.11 the institution is responsible for "Accepting and screening applications in accordance with its own technical and academic criteria; and Forwarding screened applications to the Secretary." The FY2025 NIA: "Eligible doctoral students submit their individual research narratives and application forms to the project director at their home IHE, who then compiles all the research narratives from the doctoral students and incorporates them into the institutional grant application package." So your campus runs its own competition first, on its own date, weeks before the federal deadline. Campus dates vary by institution and are not published by ED — ask your DDRA Project Director (usually in the graduate school, area-studies centre, or fellowships office) as your first action, not your last.

(2) THE INSTITUTION'S G6 REGISTRATION — quoted from the FY2025 NIA: "IHEs must email the name of the institution and the full name and email address of the project director to [DDRA@ed.gov]. We suggest that applicant IHEs submit this information no later than 2 weeks prior to the application deadline date to ensure that they obtain access to G6 well before that date." If your campus has never run DDRA, nobody has done this, and there is no route for your application at all.

(3) A PRE-APPLICATION WEBINAR was held each cycle: "The Department will hold a pre-application meeting via webinar for prospective applicants." Details were posted on the DDRA website (that page now 404s).
result.review_to_award:
ED publishes no notification date for DDRA, but the award calendar is completely regular and can be read straight off the award data (USAspending, ALN 84.022):

EVERY cohort's institutional grant starts 30 September of the award fiscal year, with an 18-month institutional project period ending 31 March two years later: P022A20 → start 2020-09-30; P022A21 → 2021-09-30; P022A22 → 2022-09-30; P022A23 → 2023-09-30 (43 awards); P022A24 → 2024-09-30 (36 awards).

So, empirically, submission → institutional award start:
- FY2024: closed 29 Mar 2024 → started 30 Sept 2024 = ~6 months
- FY2023: closed 28 Apr 2023 → started 30 Sept 2023 = ~5 months
- FY2021: closed 5 Apr 2021 → started 30 Sept 2021 = ~6 months

The fellow's own research period (6–12 months, per 34 CFR 662.5(a)) sits INSIDE that 18-month institutional window, so realistically you can be in the field from late autumn of the award year. Budget ~5–6 months from deadline to award, and about a year from writing to boarding a plane.

NOTIFICATION MECHANICS (FY2025 NIA): "If your application is successful, we notify your U.S. Representative and U.S. Senators and send you a Grant Award Notification (GAN); or we may send you an email containing a link to access an electronic version of your GAN. We also may notify you informally. If your application is not evaluated or not selected for funding, we notify you." Note the notice goes to the INSTITUTION, not to you directly. For paper submissions: if you do not receive receipt acknowledgment "within 15 business days from the application deadline date, you should contact the person listed under FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT."

REVIEW MECHANICS: applications are split into seven geographic panels — "Foreign language and area studies experts assigned to geographic area-based panels will review the doctoral student applications. Each panel will review, score, and rank its applications separately... At the conclusion of the peer review process, however, all fellowship applications in the competition will be ranked from the highest to the lowest score for funding purposes." Ties are broken by the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board's veteran's-preference policy. Final selection formally rests with the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board (34 CFR 662.22(a)), acting on the Secretary's recommendations — an extra body most applicants do not know sits in the chain.
result.submission_requirements:
WHERE IT DEVIATES MOST FROM THE FEDERAL NORM — five traps:

1. NOT GRANTS.GOV. DDRA is submitted through ED's own G6 system at www.g6.ed.gov. "Neither the IHE nor the doctoral student applicant may email an electronic copy of a grant application to us." The Grants.gov listings for 84.022 are informational only. Confusing this with Grants.gov is the classic first-timer error here.

2. YOU ARE NOT THE APPLICANT. Your university is. "Eligible Applicants: Institutions of higher education (IHEs)." The award is a "Discretionary grant redistributed as fellowships to individual beneficiaries." Four steps, in order: (a) IHE emails its project director details to DDRA@ed.gov ≥2 weeks out; (b) "Doctoral students must complete their individual applications and submit them to their home IHE project director using G6"; (c) "Persons providing references for individual doctoral students must complete and submit reference forms for the doctoral students to the IHE project director using G6"; (d) "The IHE project director must officially submit the IHE's application, including all eligible individual doctoral student applications, reference forms, and other required forms, using G6."

3. PAGE LIMIT IS RECOMMENDED, AND DOUBLE-SPACED. "We recommend that you (1) limit the application narrative to no more than 10 pages and the bibliography to no more than two pages." Format: 8.5"x11" one side only, 1" margins; "Double-space (no more than three lines per vertical inch) all text in the application narrative, including titles, headings, footnotes, quotations, references, and captions, as well as all text in charts, tables, figures, and graphs"; 12-point or no smaller than 10 pitch; Times New Roman, Courier, Courier New, or Arial. The double-spacing rule makes 10 pages far less text than applicants expect. EXCLUDED from the limit: "the cover sheet, budget section, including the narrative budget justification; the assurance and certifications; or the one-page abstract, the resumes, the biography, or the letters of support."

4. FLATTENED READ-ONLY PDF OR YOU ARE OUT. "as files in a read-only flattened Portable Document Format (PDF), meaning any fillable documents must be saved and submitted as non-fillable PDF files... If you upload a file type other than a read-only, non-modifiable PDF (e.g., Word, Excel, WordPerfect, etc.) or submit a password-protected file, we will be unable to review that material. Please note that this will likely result in your application not being considered for funding." Transcripts also go through G6.

5. G6 IS CLOSED PART OF THE WEEK. Published hours (Eastern): unavailable Sun 15:00–23:59, Mon 00:00–06:00, Wed 21:00–23:59, Thu 00:00–06:00; available 24h Tue, Fri, Sat. "G6 will not accept an application for this competition after 11:59:59 p.m., Eastern Time, on the application deadline date." A Wednesday-night or Sunday-night final push can simply fail.

COMPONENTS: individual research narrative; one-page abstract; bibliography (≤2 pp); resume/CV; biography; transcripts; reference forms submitted directly by referees via G6; letters of support; budget and narrative budget justification; SF 424, ED Supplemental Information for SF 424, ED 524, assurances and certifications (institution side). SAM/UEI/TIN registration is the institution's burden, not the student's.

TOPIC GATE (FY2025 absolute priority, from 34 CFR 662.21(d)): "A research project that focuses on one or more of the following geographic areas: Africa, East Asia, Southeast Asia and the Pacific Islands, South Asia, the Near East, Central and Eastern Europe and Eurasia, and the Western Hemisphere (excluding the United States and its territories)." Western Europe and the US are out. Also 34 CFR 662.20(b): "The Secretary does not consider applications to carry out research in a country in which the United States has no diplomatic representation."

BONUS POINTS (FY2025): CPP1 less commonly taught languages — "any modern foreign language except French, German, or Spanish" (2 pts); CPP2 thematic focus on STEM/social-science fields (2 pts); CPP3 HBCU/MSI/TCU (2 pts). CAUTION: CPP3 derived from the 2021 Supplemental Priorities. The June 2026 MECE competition instead used "Patriotic Education" and "Returning Education to the States", so if DDRA returns its priorities will very likely differ. Do not write to the FY2025 priorities.

THE PUBLISHED SCORING RUBRIC (34 CFR 662.21) — unusually, the exact point weights are public, 100 points total: Quality of proposed project (63) = hypotheses/questions + methods (20), relationship to literature and originality (10), preliminary research already done and data availability (10), justification for overseas fieldwork and research contacts/affiliations abroad (10), plans to share results and the dissertation with host-country scholars and officials (3), guidance and supervision of the dissertation advisor or committee (10). Qualifications of the applicant (37) = graduate academic record (10), strength in area studies (10), language proficiency (10), steps taken to improve advanced language proficiency (5), ability to work in a foreign cultural context per references or prior overseas experience (2). Write section-by-section against these weights — the 20-point methods block and the 10-point advisor-supervision block are where most points move.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU:

1. A concurrent Fulbright award from the same year's money. The regulation, 34 CFR 662.22(b), verbatim: "No applicant for a fellowship may be awarded more than one graduate fellowship under the Fulbright-Hays Act from appropriations for a given fiscal year." The FY2025 NIA operationalises this against the Fulbright U.S. Student Program (FUSP): "no DDRA Fellowship Program applicant concurrently may receive a grant from the Fulbright U.S. Student Program (FUSP) and a grant from the Fulbright-Hays DDRA Fellowship Program from the same fiscal year's appropriation."

2. ACCEPTING FUSP money or training at any point mid-competition kills you instantly: "At any time during the U.S. Department of Education Fulbright-Hays DDRA Fellowship Program competition process, if a doctoral student accepts a fellowship award from the FUSP, or the FUSP disperses funds to provide training services to a doctoral student, that doctoral student is automatically deemed ineligible for consideration for a grant under the Fulbright-Hays DDRA Fellowship Program. Also, if the FUSP notifies the Fulbright-Hays DDRA Fellowship Program that it has awarded funds or provided training to a potential recipient... the Department will automatically deem the doctoral student ineligible for further consideration." Note "disperses funds to provide training services" — even pre-departure orientation can trip this.

3. No renewals. 34 CFR 662.5(b): "A fellowship may not be renewed."

4. Concurrent paid work during the fellowship. 34 CFR 662.41 requires a fellow to "Devote full time to research on the approved topic" and to "Not engage in unauthorized income-producing activities during the period of the fellowship." This, not an eligibility bar, is what constrains stacking a second stipend on top.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES YOUR ELIGIBILITY — the half applicants get wrong:

1. APPLYING to Fulbright U.S. Student in parallel is entirely permitted and is expected practice. The bar attaches to ACCEPTING, not to applying. The NIA merely requires disclosure: "when applying for a grant under the Fulbright-Hays DDRA Fellowship Program, a doctoral student must indicate in the application whether they have also applied for a FUSP grant." So run both. The NIA's own instruction is to phone first, not to withdraw: "Doctoral students thus should notify the person listed under FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT prior to accepting any grant support or training from the FUSP."

2. The bar is a same-fiscal-year CONCURRENCY rule, not a lifetime cap. Nothing bars a prior Fulbright-Hays fellow from a later appropriation year.

3. 34 CFR 662.3 states the COMPLETE individual eligibility test, and it contains no prior-funding exclusion of any kind: citizen/national or permanent resident; "graduate student in good standing"; "When the fellowship period begins, is admitted to candidacy in a doctoral degree program in modern foreign languages and area studies"; "planning a teaching career in the United States upon completion of his or her doctoral program"; "Possesses sufficient foreign language skills to carry out the dissertation research project." So prior or current FLAS, NSF GRFP, SSRC IDRF, Wenner-Gren, Mellon, ACLS or departmental funding does NOT disqualify you on its face — subject only to the full-time-research rule in §662.41 during the award period itself.

4. Note the timing carve-out in the candidacy rule: you need candidacy WHEN THE FELLOWSHIP PERIOD BEGINS, not when you apply. ABD-by-departure is enough; you may apply before advancing.

5. Prior recipients stay eligible for any future competition. The 2026 rescission NPRM says so explicitly: "ED's proposed deregulation would not affect the eligibility of prior grant recipients under these programs to compete under future competitions, as eligibility will continue to be governed by the underlying statutory framework applicable to such programs."

6. Institution side: a university's prior DDRA grants do not disqualify it, though under 34 CFR 75.217(d)(3) the Secretary may consider "the past performance of the applicant in carrying out a previous award" and whether it "failed to submit a timely performance report or submitted a report of unacceptable quality."
result.program_officer_contact:
TALK TO YOUR CAMPUS FIRST, ED SECOND. Because the university is the legal applicant and screens under its own criteria (34 CFR 662.11(b)), your DDRA Project Director — typically in the graduate school, an area-studies/Title VI centre, or the fellowships office — controls your access to the competition and sets the internal deadline. ED cannot accept anything from you directly. If your campus has no Project Director, that is the blocker to solve.

ED CONTACTS (emails decoded from the GPO/govinfo copies, since federalregister.gov obfuscates them):
- Programme contact, FY2025 DDRA NIA and its extension notice: Pamela J. Maimer, U.S. Department of Education, 400 Maryland Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20202. Telephone: (202) 453-6891. Email: DDRA@ed.gov. The generic DDRA@ed.gov box is also the address institutions use to register their Project Director for G6, so it is the most durable route.
- Contact on both the 2025 cancellation notice and the 2026 rescission NPRM: Stacey Slijepcevic, (202) 453-6150, stacey.slijepcevic@ed.gov. This is the person to ask about programme status and whether a competition is coming.
- For the separate MECE competition (not DDRA): Kurrinn Abrams, 202-987-1920, MECE@ed.gov.

IS PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT EXPECTED? Not in the DOE/NIH sense — ED does not invite topical negotiation with a programme officer, and the panel is external. What ED did offer each cycle was a group channel: "The Department will hold a pre-application meeting via webinar for prospective applicants." One point where ED directs you to call proactively is the Fulbright U.S. Student conflict: "Doctoral students thus should notify the person listed under FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT prior to accepting any grant support or training from the FUSP."

CAVEAT ON STAFFING: Maimer is named in a notice that has since been withdrawn, and Slijepcevic's details come from 2025–26 documents. Neither was independently confirmed as still in post; the ed.gov staff pages could not be fetched (403 to scripted requests, 404 on the DDRA page).
result.examples_or_samples:
RANKED BY WHAT ACTUALLY HELPS A STUDENT:

1. THE PUBLISHED POINT-WEIGHTED RUBRIC — the single best "sample" here, and free. 34 CFR 662.21 gives the exact scoring breakdown (63 points for project quality, split 20/10/10/10/3/10; 37 for applicant qualifications, split 10/10/10/5/2). Most funders publish criteria; few publish the weights. Draft your narrative with these as headings. Live text: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-34/subtitle-B/chapter-VI/part-662

2. IRIS — ED's own award database, and it is still live even though the ed.gov programme page is gone. https://iris.ed.gov/programs/ddra carries a "Browse DDRA Grants" link (https://iris.ed.gov/iris/ieps/search.cfm?type=ADV&tab=BRW&goFind=go&programs=1); the search form's own label reads "(Search grant titles, abstracts, or award numbers)" and offers a "Dissertation Research" programme filter. This is the closest DDRA analogue to NIH RePORTER — funded project titles and abstracts by institution. TOOLING CAVEAT: I confirmed the route and the form exist but could NOT retrieve a results page programmatically — it is a POST form with a CSRF token that redirected (302) my scripted request. It needs a real browser. I therefore cannot vouch for how many DDRA records it returns or how recent they are.

3. THE PERFORMANCE-REPORT TEMPLATES — an underused trick. These show exactly what ED asks a funded fellow to report, i.e. what it counts as success, which tells you what to promise: https://iris.ed.gov/iris/pdfs/DDRA_fellow.pdf (fellow) and https://iris.ed.gov/iris/pdfs/DDRA_director.pdf (project director). Both are cited in the FY2025 NIA itself. Align your narrative to the four published performance measures: language-proficiency gain of at least one level; degree completion within four years of the fellowship; employment using language/area skills within eight years; and cost per fellow so employed.

4. WHO ACTUALLY WON — USAspending, ALN 84.022, gives recipient institutions and dollar amounts per cohort (award IDs P022A18…P022A24). Useful for finding which departments on which campuses have a live DDRA pipeline, and therefore a Project Director who knows the process. Verified working via https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/ filtered on program_numbers 84.022.

5. YOUR OWN CAMPUS ARCHIVE — in practice the best source of a full narrative. Because every application is screened and bundled locally, your Project Director's office holds past submitted applications from your institution, and past fellows are identifiable from the IRIS/USAspending recipient lists. Ask. This is the only realistic route to a complete funded narrative.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: ED publishes no full funded DDRA application texts and no official annotated sample-proposal library. The ed.gov DDRA press kit (https://www.ed.gov/sites/ed/files/about/offices/list/ope/iegps/ifle-fh-ddra-press-kit.pdf) is linked from IRIS but returned HTTP 403 to a scripted fetch — it may still open in a browser.
result.resubmission_note:
No formal resubmission track, no "A1" numbering, no introduction page, no cap on attempts and no stated waiting period — because each fiscal year's competition is a fresh new-application competition. Reapplying in a later cycle was always normal and unrestricted. Note separately that the AWARD itself is non-renewable: 34 CFR 662.5(b), "A fellowship may not be renewed."

WITHIN a single competition you may replace your own submission before the deadline, and ED takes the last timely version. From the FY2025 extension notice, verbatim: "Applicants that have already timely submitted applications under the FY 2025 DDRA competition may resubmit applications on or before the extended application deadline of January 29, 2025, but are not required to do so. If a new application is not submitted, the Department will use the application that was submitted by the original deadline. If a new application is submitted, the Department will consider the application that is last submitted and timely received by 11:59:59 p.m., eastern time, on January 29, 2025."

THE WEAK SPOT vs NIH/NSF: nothing in the NIA or in 34 CFR 662 promises to release reviewer comments or panel scores to the student. There is no summary-statement equivalent and no PAMS-style "View Reviews". Feedback, if any, reaches the institution as the grantee of record, so ask your Project Director to request it. Plan to revise against the published §662.21 point weights rather than against reviewer prose you may never see.

DRIFT WARNING FOR ANY REUSED NARRATIVE: ED has changed the rules mid-competition before — FR 2023-07419 (10 Apr 2023) amended selection criterion (b)(3) AND extended the FY2023 deadline to 28 April 2023 in the same notice. Treat 5 Mar–30 Apr 2027 as a planning date, NOT a funder commitment: it is a campus projection, unconfirmed on research.google. PATTERN (what survives drift): annual; opens early March, closes end of April, decisions by end of August, public announcement by end of October, fellowship begins at the start of the following school year. Corroboration that the spring window is not new: the University of Pittsburgh's 2024-25 internal call set its institutional deadline at "Monday, April 15, 2024" with the external packet due "Monday, May 6" — i.e. an April/May close in that cycle too. THE DEADLINE THAT ACTUALLY BINDS A STUDENT IS NOT GOOGLE'S. Students cannot apply directly, so the operative date is the home university's internal nomination deadline, which runs roughly 2–6 weeks before Google's close. Verified 2026-cycle examples: Emory 17 April 2026 (12:00PM), Mines 15 March (2027 cycle). Further 2026 examples seen only as search-index snippets, not fetched directly: Purdue ECE 29 March, UW ECE 7 April, Georgia Tech mid-April, UNM 15 April.
result.deadline_pattern: Annual. Application window opens early March and closes 30 April (2026 cycle: 5 March – 30 April 2026; Mines projects the identical window for 2027). Decisions notified by 31 August; recipients publicly announced by 31 October; award begins at the start of the following school year — funder: "Google PhD Fellowships begin at the start of the upcoming school year after award notification." Institutional internal nomination deadlines fall 2–6 weeks earlier, mid-March to mid-April. Note a naming trap: institutions label the same cycle inconsistently — Emory titles the cycle closing 30 April 2026 "Application Guidelines for the 2027 Fellowship Year" while inside the same document requiring coursework completed "by Fall of the award year (Fall 2026)", and Purdue calls it "Nomination for Fall Start 2026". Confirm with your graduate school which academic year a given call refers to.
result.loi_required: no (at funder level) — but yes in practice at the institutional level
result.loi_deadline: Google requires no letter of intent or pre-proposal. However, because the fellowship is nomination-only and capped ("Canada and the United States: Universities may nominate up to four eligible students"), essentially every eligible university runs an internal competition that functions as a de facto pre-proposal stage, with a lighter materials set due weeks before the full packet. Two verified shapes: (1) Mines — initial materials due 15 March 2027 (a one-page research description plus CV), nomination decisions 30 March, then "Nominated applicants will have one month to finalize their application materials", full packet 29 April, Google closes 30 April. (2) Pittsburgh (2024-25) — internal packet (student CV, 1-page advisor CV, transcripts, advisor letter) by 15 April 2024; only if selected did the student prepare the external packet (2 further letters, 3-page proposal, both essays) for 6 May. Practical consequence: a student who first looks at this in April has already missed the stage that decides it. The internal call typically opens in the preceding autumn or early spring — funder's instruction is "Please contact your department or graduate school for more information on the internal nomination process."
result.review_to_award: Approximately 4 months from close to notification: applications close 30 April, "Notification of proposal decisions by Aug. 31" — so about 17–18 weeks. Public announcement follows up to 2 months later, "by Oct. 31". Earliest start is tight and easy to misplan: "Google PhD Fellowships begin at the start of the upcoming school year after award notification" — with notification arriving 31 August, the award effectively begins with the academic year starting almost immediately after (Fall of the same calendar year as notification; Emory's guidance for the cycle closing April 2026 names "Fall 2026" as the award year). Payment mechanics differ from a typical grant: "Any monetary awards will be paid directly to the Fellow's university for distribution. No overhead should be assessed against them." No funder-wide Google machinery was researched, so there is no funder norm to deviate from; these dates are the mechanism's own.
result.submission_requirements: Submission is by the university, not the student: "All students must be nominated by an eligible university during the application period; direct applications from students are not accepted" and "Applications must be submitted by an official representative of the university during the application window." Institutional cap for this jurisdiction: up to four nominees per university (Canada/US); three in most other regions; unlimited in Latin America. FORMAT: "Universities will need to submit the following materials in a single, flat (not portfolio) PDF file." All materials in English. REQUIRED OF ALL REGIONS: student CV with links to website and publications; "Research/dissertation proposal (maximum 3 pages, excluding references)". ADDITIONAL FOR CANADA / EAST ASIA / UNITED STATES: cover sheet signed by the Department Chair confirming the student passes eligibility requirements; short (1-page) CV of the student's primary advisor; "2-3 letters of recommendation from those familiar with the nominee's work (at least one from the thesis advisor)"; transcripts of current and previous academic records; and TWO 350-word essays unique to this region group — (a) "Describe the desired impact your research will make on the field and society, and why this is important to you. Include any personal, educational and/or professional experiences that have motivated your research interests." and (b) "Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time." The US/Canada essays are not decorative: "In Canada and the United States, East Asia and Latin America, essay responses are evaluated in addition to application materials to determine an overall recommendation." Two further funder rules: "Research should align with Google AI Principles" and "Incomplete proposals will not be considered." Also stated: "A nominee's status as a member of a historically marginalized group is not considered in the selection of award recipients." WATCH FOR INSTITUTIONAL ADD-ONS beyond Google's list — Emory additionally requires that "The thesis advisor's letter must speak to the type of supervision student has/will receive and also make specific reference to the research culture in which the student will be working", a final summary page (chair and advisor names/emails, PhD start date, graduation date, research area, proposal title, abstract), and submission "as ONE PDF file in the exact order listed"; internal caps are often tighter than Google's four (Emory forwards only the selected student; UW ECE was "limited to two nominations"; Georgia Tech allows schools "no more than two (2) nominations to the internal competition").
result.prior_funding_conflicts: BOTH HALVES, in the funder's own words — this single sentence pair is the whole rule: "Students that are already supported by a comparable industry award are not eligible. Government or non-profit organization funding is exempt." EXCLUDES: current support from a comparable INDUSTRY award — i.e. another corporate PhD fellowship (the NVIDIA, IBM, Meta/Apple-type awards sit in this class). Also excluded, absolutely and permanently: "Past awardees from the PhD Fellowship program are not eligible to apply again" — a single win ends eligibility forever, so this is a once-per-career mechanism. Also excluded: "Google employees, and their spouses, children, and members of their household are not eligible." PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half applicants most often get wrong and self-deselect on): government and non-profit funding is explicitly exempt — so an NSF GRFP, NDSEG, DOE CSGF, NIH training grant, or a private non-profit foundation fellowship does NOT block a nomination. Departmental/university funding and assistantships are not named as disqualifying. Holding this fellowship also preserves other Google routes: "Can Fellowship recipients also be considered for other Google scholarships? Yes, Fellowship recipients are eligible for these scholarships", recipients "do not become employees of Google", and "Fellowship recipients are not subject to intellectual property restrictions unless they complete an internship at Google." Continuing condition, not an entry bar: "Students must remain enrolled full-time in the PhD program for the duration of the Fellowship or forfeit the award." NOTE A GAP IN THE EXISTING CSV ROW: data/mechanisms.csv line 160 records the exclusion half only ("students already receiving a comparable industry fellowship, and past Google Fellowship recipients, are ineligible; Google employees/household members ineligible") and omits the government/non-profit exemption — the half that tells an NSF GRFP holder they may still be nominated. RESUBMISSION: Google bars only past AWARDEES. There is no stated bar on an unsuccessful nominee being nominated again in a later cycle — permitted by silence rather than by an explicit rule, so confirm with the graduate school, whose internal competition is the real gate.
result.resubmission_note: Not explicitly addressed by the funder. The only stated bar is on winners: "Past awardees from the PhD Fellowship program are not eligible to apply again." Nothing on the funder page or in the FAQ prohibits re-nomination after an unsuccessful attempt, and nothing describes a resubmission process, response-to-reviewers, or feedback to unsuccessful applicants (no critique is mentioned as being provided). Because the binding constraint is the university's internal cap rather than Google's rules, whether a student may try again is in practice a departmental decision. Treat as permitted-by-silence and verify locally; do not record as an explicit funder allowance.
result.program_officer_contact: No named program officer. The funder gives one route, a team mailbox: "please contact our global team at phdfellowship@google.com". Pre-submission contact with the funder is NOT expected and is actively damped: "We receive a high volume of emails, and to ensure we can respond to time-sensitive inquiries, we encourage you to first check our website for answers to your questions... Please note that due to the volume of inquiries, we may not be able to respond to questions already answered on the website." There is no NIH-style program-officer conversation here, and no advantage to seeking one — because students cannot apply directly, the funder has no pre-submission relationship with applicants at all. THE PERSON TO ACTUALLY TALK TO is inside your own institution, and the funder says so: "Please contact your department or graduate school for more information on the internal nomination process." In practice that is the graduate school's fellowships/nationally-competitive-scholarships office or the department's awards coordinator, and the advice on those pages is to make contact early — Mines: "Please contact [the Office of Nationally Competitive Scholarships] as early as possible to discuss your interest in applying"; Emory routes everything through LGS.profdev@emory.edu; Pittsburgh through graduate@pitt.edu. The second essential conversation is with the thesis advisor, who must write one of the letters and, at some institutions, address the supervision and research culture specifically.
result.examples_or_samples: No funded application, successful abstract, or annotated sample is published by Google for this mechanism — searched and not found; record as "none published" rather than "not found". Three usable substitutes, in descending order of value: (1) THE BEST PUBLIC TEMPLATE is an institutional guidance document, because they reproduce Google's required packet and both essay prompts verbatim with the sequencing: the Mines page (https://nationalscholarships.mines.edu/google_phd_fellowship/) lists the full materials set, both essay prompts in quotation marks, and a dated internal-to-external timeline; Emory's PDF (https://web.gs.emory.edu/_includes/documents/google-fellowship-fy27.pdf) gives the exact required order of the single PDF, the chair cover-sheet attestations item by item, and what the advisor's letter must cover; Pittsburgh's call (https://www.gradstudies.pitt.edu/sites/default/files/assets/2024-2025-Google-PhD-Fellowship.pdf) shows the two-stage internal/external split. (2) PRIOR RECIPIENTS: https://research.google/programs-and-events/phd-fellowship/recipients/ names awardees by year (2014–2025) with university and research area, filterable by area — the route to find a recent winner in your own subfield and read their published work to calibrate scope and framing. It links no proposals or abstracts. (3) THE REVIEW CRITERIA AS A CHECKLIST, since they are stated plainly and the proposal is judged against them: "strength of the research proposal, research impact, student academic achievements, and leadership potential", with proposals evaluated for "innovative concepts that are relevant to Google's research areas, as well as aspects of robustness and potential impact to the field" and an explicit instruction that "Proposals should include the direction and any plans of where your work is going in addition to a comprehensive description of the research you are pursuing." The eleven research areas on the funder page carry per-area subtopic call-outs ("we call for proposals specifically in the areas of...") which function as the real statement of fit. Ask your own graduate school whether it retains past successful internal nomination packets — several such offices do, and that is the only realistic route to a genuine funded example.

That is a rendered-page fact, not a fetch failure.

An FY2026 competition is nonetheless clearly planned: NIJ's GRF FAQ already carries live FY-specific language — "Applicants for FY 2026 must demonstrate relevance of their dissertation research to (1) supporting law enforcement operations, (2) combating violent crime, (3) protecting American children, or (4) supporting American victims of trafficking and sexual assault."

Expected window for the FY26 GRF, from NIJ's own published cadence (see deadline_pattern): posting January–March 2027, deadline roughly April–May 2027. Treat that as a pattern-derived window, NOT a date. Do not print an FY26 day-of-month: NIJ has not set one.
