result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves. This mechanism is unusual: the disqualifiers are about career stage and application structure, NOT about holding other grants.

WHAT MAKES YOU INELIGIBLE
1. Seeking renewal or top-up of an existing ARPA-E award. NOFO Section II.D: "ARPA-E will accept only new submissions under this NOFO. Applicants may not seek renewal or supplementation of their existing awards through this NOFO." When an applicant with an active ARPA-E project asked directly (2026 FAQ Q12), ARPA-E declined to pre-assess and pointed only to that sentence — i.e. the active award is not itself the bar; proposing to extend it is.
2. More than one application per person. "individual PIs may submit no more than one application to this NOFO." You also may not submit as PI on one and appear as co-PI on another (2025 FAQ Q27).
3. Any co-PI or senior oversight. "Proposals with multiple co-PIs or project oversight from senior personnel are not eligible for this program." Single PI only; standalone applicant only, no project teams and no subrecipients (2026 FAQ Q8; 2025 FAQ Q35: "This is a single PI funding opportunity with only a prime recipient").
4. Career-stage gates (the real filter): PhD conferred within eight years of the Concept Paper deadline; at a US Institution of Higher Education, must be a pre-tenure Tenure-Track Assistant/Associate Professor at the time of Concept Paper submission; must already be employed by an eligible applicant; must be a US citizen, permanent resident, or have filed Form I-485 before submitting the Concept Paper.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY
1. Having been a co-PI on a past ARPA-E project. 2025 FAQ Q11, verbatim: "Q. Can a PI be eligible if they were a co-PI on a past ARPA-E project but not the lead? ANSWER: Yes, provided all eligibility criteria are satisfied."
2. Holding other federal early-career awards. Neither NOFO contains any exclusion for current or prior NSF CAREER, DOE Early Career Research Program, DARPA Young Faculty Award, ONR YIP, NIH or any other federal award — I full-text searched both NOFOs for such clauses and found none. The NOFO in fact cites those programmes approvingly as peer efforts (footnote 5). This is an absence-of-clause finding, verified by search, not an affirmative ARPA-E statement.
3. Current and pending support is DISCLOSURE, not a bar. The CPS Common Form (via SciENcv) is a required full-application component "used to identify potential duplication, overcommitment, potential conflicts of interest or commitment" — a deconfliction instrument. Note the ARPA-E-specific deviation: "disclosure of the past five (5) years of support is required", beyond the usual current+pending.
4. Extended leave stops the eight-year clock. "excluding any periods of extended leave occurring since the time the PI obtained their Ph.D. Such leave could include personal leaves of absence, parental leave, medical leave, etc." 2026 FAQ Q14 gives the arithmetic: "only those with a graduation date on or after May 29th, 2018 are eligible, except when extended leave was taken... the duration of extended leave can be used to determine an adjusted date of eligibility by counting back from May 29th, 2018." State type and duration in the Personal Qualification Summary. Postdoc time does NOT count as leave (2025 FAQ Q24: "ANSWER: No.").
5. Green-card applicants count, not just citizens and permanent residents — provided Form I-485 is actually filed before the Concept Paper. An approved I-140 with a non-current priority date is NOT enough (2026 FAQ Q13; 2025 FAQ Q12, Q20); H-1B without I-140 approval is not enough (2025 FAQ Q22).
6. No cost share: "There is no Cost Share required for this NOFO."
7. A professor who owns a startup may apply through the LLC rather than the university (2025 FAQ Q34: "Yes, provided all eligibility criteria are met").

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE EXISTING CSV ROW
(a) career_stage "graduate_predoc, postdoc, early_career_faculty" is WRONG for 2026. 2026 FAQ Q5, verbatim: "Post-doctoral scholars are not eligible to apply." Q1: non-tenure-track research staff at an IHE — "exceptions will not be considered." Q2 extends that to research faculty with PI status. A PhD is required, so graduate students are excluded too. Correct reading: pre-tenure tenure-track faculty at IHEs, plus permanent staff at FFRDCs/national labs, for-profits and nonprofits who can self-direct the work. FFRDC PIs "can lead submissions independently without partnering with outside entities" (2026 FAQ Q3.4). An incoming assistant professor whose appointment starts after the Concept Paper date is NOT eligible (2026 FAQ Q18, Q53; 2025 FAQ Q9).
(b) award size: the CSV estimate "up to ~$500,000" should read $500,000 total across two years, inclusive of equipment and patent costs (2026 FAQ Q3.5a, Q4), plus a possible additional $250,000 "Director's Award" that is discretionary and — importantly — "only existing IGNIITE awardees are eligible; new applicants to IGNIITE 2026 should not incorporate this funding into their submissions." That explains why a 2024 project such as METAPAK shows $750,000 on its ARPA-E project page.
result.review_to_award:
For the 2026 cycle, from the NOFO's Key Dates table as revised by Modification 01 (struck-through original values shown for contrast):
- Concept Paper May 29, 2026 → invite/not-invite decision July 27, 2026 (anticipated July 14): about 2 months.
- Full Application Aug 26, 2026 → reviewer comments released Sept 16, 2026 → replies due Sept 21, 2026: about 3 weeks to see reviews, 5 days to answer them.
- Selection notifications: anticipated "September October 2026" (Mod 01 pushed September to October 2026) — about 2 months after the full application.
- Award: anticipated "December 2026 January 2027" (pushed to January 2027) — about 5 months after the full application, about 8 months after the Concept Paper.
- Period of performance: anticipated "December 2026-December 2028 January 2027 - January 2029" (pushed to January 2027 – January 2029) — 24 months.

Deviation worth flagging: the actual 2024 cohort ran longer than the 2-year nominal. The IGNIITE 2024 METAPAK project page shows Start Date Jul 18 2024, End Date Jul 18 2027 and $750,000 — i.e. a 3-year run at the Director's-Award level. So the 2-year/$500k figure is the award as offered, not necessarily as it ends up.

Two timing traps for a planner: (1) the quiet period means there is no negotiation or clarification window between submission and selection; (2) the reviewer-comment reply window is only five calendar days and lands immediately after the comments drop — an invited applicant must hold that week open.
result.submission_requirements:
CONCEPT PAPER STAGE (four components, all mandatory)
1. Concept Paper, Adobe PDF: "must not exceed 4 pages in length including images, graphics, figures, and/or tables", plus "a Personal Qualification Summary, not to exceed 2 pages, for a total document maximum of 6 pages". English; 8.5x11; margins not less than one inch; single spaced; Times New Roman, black, 12 point or larger (except figures/tables); ARPA-E Control Number, Lead Organization Name and PI's Last Name in the upper-right header of every page; page numbers in the footer. First paragraph must state Lead Organization Name and Location, PI Name, Technical Category, Proposed Funding Requested, Project Duration. One concept only. Use the eXCHANGE template — do NOT add a cover page or abstract (2026 FAQ Q3.6; 2025 FAQ Q28). A bibliography may be appended and "will not be counted against the 4-page limit" (2025 FAQ Q28).
2. Summary Slide: a single PowerPoint slide on the ARPA-E template, used in evaluation.
3. Letter of Support — the distinctive requirement: "signed by the PI's direct supervisor (1) attesting to the applicant's and PI's eligibility... and (2) expressing their commitment to support the PI in the successful completion of the project (including, but not limited to, time, space, laboratory access)." On official letterhead, signed, no page limit. Two supervisors: one joint letter signed by both is fine (2025 FAQ Q25). A founder/CEO with no supervisor still needs one — "It could be written by a board member or cofounder" (2025 FAQ Q31).
4. PhD transcript, official or unofficial, no page limit. If the university issues none, submit its official letter saying so (2025 FAQ Q15). A post-graduation legal name change requires a change-of-name verification letter (2025 FAQ Q10).

FULL APPLICATION STAGE (invited only)
- Technical Volume, PDF: Cover Page 1 page max; Executive Summary 1 page max; Sections 1–5 15 pages max; Bibliographic References no limit.
- Signed SF-424; Budget Justification Workbook/SF-424A (Excel); Summary for Public Release (250 words max); Summary Slide (1 slide, PowerPoint); completed and signed Business Assurances & Disclosures Form; ARPA-E Transparency of Foreign Connections Disclosure and Certification Form; Biosketch for each Covered Individual (all combined into one PDF, via SciENcv); CPS Common Form for each Covered Individual (all combined into one PDF, via SciENcv, past 5 years of support included).
- Reply to Reviewer Comments: optional, 3 pages max.
- Additional letters of support/collaboration are NOT required at this stage but are accepted, uploaded under the optional "Letters of Intent and/or Support" entry on the eXCHANGE "Upload and Submit" tab (2026 FAQ Q58, Q60, Q61). The project title may be changed from the Concept Paper (2026 FAQ Q59.3).

WHERE THIS DEVIATES FROM THE ARPA-E NORM
- A PhD transcript and a signed direct-supervisor eligibility letter at the concept stage — neither appears in ordinary ARPA-E NOFOs; they exist to police the individual-eligibility gates.
- Standalone applicant only, single PI, no subrecipients and no project team.
- Mandatory cohort programme: awardees "will be required to participate in the ARPA-E IGNIITE Annual Program" — a one-week session in Washington DC in each of Year 1 and Year 2, and "Applicants will need to budget up to $2,500 per year for this travel in their submission." Budget placement matters: IGNIITE Annual Program travel goes in the "c. Travel" tab, Energy Innovation Summit travel in "h. Other" (2026 FAQ Q57).
- At least 5% of federal funding must go to Technology Transfer & Outreach (TT&O) activities.
- AI use must be disclosed — see NOFO Section IV.E; a footnote in the Concept Paper is acceptable for language polishing (2026 FAQ Q7).
- Research security training per CHIPS and Science Act Section 10634 must be certified; the NSF SECURE Center consolidated module satisfies it (2026 FAQ Q70).
- Technical Areas of Interest (energy supply chain security incl. critical minerals; advanced nuclear incl. fusion and fission; geothermal; grid reliability and security; American manufacturing competitiveness) are NOT formal submission categories — the eXCHANGE dropdown exists only to match reviewers, and "if none apply, use 7. Other Energy Technologies" (2026 FAQ Q11).
- Full-application merit review weights: Impact 30%, Scientific/Technical Merit 30%, "Qualifications, Experience, and Capabilities of the Proposed PI" 30%, Soundness of Management Plan 10%. Thirty percent on the individual is the signature of this mechanism — the Personal Qualification Summary and supervisor letter are scoring material, not paperwork.
- Submission portal: ARPA-E eXCHANGE (https://arpa-e-foa.energy.gov/). Note a planned platform migration: DOE eXCHANGE consolidation expected around October 2026, with downtime Friday October 2 (8 PM ET) to Sunday October 4 (6 AM ET); accounts and applications transfer automatically.
result.program_officer_contact:
There is NO named program officer for this mechanism, and pre-submission contact is explicitly FORBIDDEN — the opposite of the NIH/NSF norm. This is the single most important expectation-setting fact for an applicant coming from another agency.

ARPA-E's own words, in the NOFO's Basic Information table: "Upon the issuance of a NOFO, only the Grants Officer via ARPA-E-CO@hq.doe.gov may communicate with applicants. This 'quiet period' remains in effect until ARPA-E's selection notification letters are distributed. Emails sent to other email addresses will be disregarded."

And on ARPA-E's standing FAQ page (last updated Dec 19 2025), to the question "Can I speak or meet with an ARPA-E Program Director or other ARPA-E personnel regarding an open NOFO?": "No. Upon the issuance of a NOFO, ARPA-E Program Directors and other ARPA-E personnel are prohibited from communicating (in writing or otherwise) with Applicants, or potential Applicants, until selections are made."

When an applicant asked whether to approach the programme manager, the answer was a flat "No" (2025 FAQ Q8). ARPA-E also refuses substantive pre-screening: "ARPA-E will not provide pre-submission assessments of eligibility or potential concepts for this NOFO" (2026 FAQ Q54), and "ARPA-E cannot comment on the merit of a specific technology through the Q&A."

THE ROUTE THAT DOES EXIST — a written, public, deadlined Q&A:
- ARPA-E-CO@hq.doe.gov for NOFO questions, with the NOFO name and number in the subject line. There is a hard cutoff per stage (2026: 5 PM ET May 19 for concept-paper questions; 5 PM ET August 17 for full-application questions).
- ExchangeHelp@hq.doe.gov for portal problems.
- Answers are published for everyone, in versioned FAQ PDFs: open NOFOs at https://arpa-e.energy.gov/about/FAQ/Apply-for-Funding/Open-NOFO-FAQs, closed at .../Closed-NOFO-FAQs. The IGNIITE 2026 file reached revision 6F with 71 questions — reading it is the substitute for a PO call, and it is where the eligibility edge cases are actually settled.
- Agency contact centre (general, non-NOFO): ARPA-E@hq.doe.gov. Press/general: ARPA-E-Comms@hq.doe.gov.

WHO YOU CAN ACTUALLY TALK TO: past IGNIITE awardees. Every ARPA-E project page publishes a named project contact with a direct email (e.g. the IGNIITE 2024 METAPAK page lists "Prof. Jun Wang, junwang@unl.edu"). With ARPA-E staff off-limits during an open NOFO, prior awardees are the legitimate and available source of tacit knowledge.
result.examples_or_samples:
Unusually good for a federal mechanism — funded work is published at the level of the individual innovator.

1. Blank forms and templates, the closest thing to an annotated sample, all on the eXCHANGE record for DE-FOA-0003624 (https://arpa-e-foa.energy.gov/Default.aspx#FoaId1704ae68-308e-4bb8-bcdc-ef39c8c69bc6): IGNIITE 2026 Concept Paper Template; Concept Paper Summary Slide Template; Full Application Technical Volume Template; Full Application Summary Slide Template; SF-424; SF-424A/Budget Justification Workbook; Summary for Public Release Template; Business Assurances & Disclosures Form; Transparency of Foreign Connections form; Replies to Reviewer Comments Template. The Concept Paper and Technical Volume templates carry the required section structure and the per-section page limits the NOFO itself does not print. The NOFO warns: use the templates for THIS NOFO, not an earlier one — "Applicants must refer to these template application documents and not templates associated with earlier NOFOs, which may cause the application to be deemed noncompliant."

2. Funded abstracts, IGNIITE 2025 cohort — a 5-page PDF of selectee descriptions: https://arpa-e.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2026-01/IGNIITE%202025%20Selectee%20Descriptions_Final%20_2.pdf. Each entry gives the innovator's name, institution and city, a one-sentence bio, a 3–5 sentence plain-language description of the funded idea, the project title and the award amount ($500,000). Example of the register that wins: "Akanksha Menon... will develop a desalination system based on air gap diffusion distillation (AGDD) that transforms brine into clean water and minerals." This is effectively a model for the Summary for Public Release, and a direct read on what ARPA-E considers fundable at this career stage.

3. Full funded portfolio, IGNIITE 2024 — 23 projects, each with its own page carrying the public abstract, PI name and email, institution, start and end dates, and award amount: https://arpa-e.energy.gov/programs-and-initiatives/search-all-projects?filter[field_reference_program]=igniite%202024. Worked example: https://arpa-e.energy.gov/programs-and-initiatives/search-all-projects/multicell-electrical-transient-accelerated-press-pack-modules-metapak. This is the best available corpus for calibrating scope and ambition, and it supplies contactable past awardees.

4. The prior-cycle FAQs are the de facto annotated guidance, since ARPA-E answers real applicants' formatting and eligibility questions in public: IGNIITE 2026 (71 Qs) https://arpa-e.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/DE-FOA-0003624%20IGNIITE%202026%20NOFO%20FAQ%20-%206F.pdf; IGNIITE 2025 (37 Qs) https://arpa-e.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2024-12/DE-FOA-0003477%20IGNITE%202025%20FOA%20FAQ%20-%201f.pdf; IGNIITE 2024 https://arpa-e.energy.gov/sites/default/files/migrated/DE-FOA-0003224%20IGNITE%20FOA%20FAQ%20-%206f.pdf.

5. Topic-level ARPA-E guidance on how to frame a submission: the standing FAQ sub-pages for Technical Volume, Summary Slide, Submitting A Concept Paper, Submitting A Full Application, Replies To Reviewer Comments and Technology-to-Market, all under https://arpa-e.energy.gov/about/FAQ/Apply-for-Funding.

NOT available: no released reviewer scoresheets, and no funded application text beyond the public abstracts. IGNIITE 2025 and 2026 program pages still show Project Count 0, so 2025 abstracts exist only in the selectee PDF above.
result.resubmission_note:
Two different things must not be conflated.

WITHIN a cycle: the "Reply to Reviewer Comments" is a built-in rebuttal step, not a resubmission — optional, 3 pages max, due 5 PM ET September 21, 2026 for this cycle. "ARPA-E has not established separate criteria to evaluate Replies to Reviewer Comments. Instead, Replies to Reviewer Comments are evaluated as an extension of the Full Application." Applicants get to see reviewer comments and answer them before selection, which is a genuine advantage over agencies that reveal reviews only after the decision.

ACROSS cycles: no resubmission policy is published for IGNIITE, in either NOFO or any FAQ. Nothing bars a previously unsuccessful applicant from applying to a later cohort, and there is no "new/resubmission" designation, no A0/A1 numbering and no requirement to mark or respond to prior reviews. The only per-cycle limit is "individual PIs may submit no more than one application to this NOFO." This is an absence-of-clause reading, verified by full-text search of both 2026 NOFOs, not an affirmative ARPA-E statement — record it as such.

The real constraint on reapplying is the eight-year PhD clock, which keeps running: a near-miss applicant may simply age out before the next cohort opens, especially given the ~6-month cycle slip between the 2025 and 2026 rounds. One 2026 applicant reported having been unable to apply in the two previous rounds for green-card reasons and returning in 2026 (2026 FAQ Q10), which at least shows repeat attempts across cohorts are ordinary.

Also note: a not-invited Concept Paper ends that cycle outright — there is no appeal and no route to submit a full application anyway.
unresolved: NEXT CYCLE: no IGNIITE 2027 NOFO, dates or announcement exists as of 2026-09-18. Verified two ways: the live ARPA-E eXCHANGE funding-opportunity list carries only IGNIITE 2026 among IGNIITE entries, and the igniite-2027 program-page slug returns 'Page not found'. A 2027 date cannot be given without guessing, and the ~6-month slip between the 2025 and 2026 cohorts makes extrapolation unsafe. Recheck eXCHANGE and FedConnect rather than predicting.

TECHNICAL VOLUME INTERNAL STRUCTURE: the NOFO defers per-section page limits to the Word templates ('must conform to the content and form requirements included within the template, including maximum page lengths'). I established the outer limits from the NOFO's required-documents checklist (Cover Page 1, Executive Summary 1, Sections 1-5 15 pages, references unlimited) but did not open the .docx templates, so the names and internal limits of Sections 1-5 are not recorded. The template URLs are in source_urls if the corpus wants that depth.

2026 OUTCOME: selections were anticipated October 2026 and had not been announced as of 2026-09-18 (the IGNIITE 2026 program page shows Project Count 0; the Replies to Reviewer Comments window was still open). Number of concept papers received, number invited, and the selection rate are not published for any IGNIITE cohort, so selectivity for this mechanism remains an estimate from cohort size (23 awardees in 2024; up to 20 planned at $500k each in 2026).

NAMED PROGRAM DIRECTOR: none is published for IGNIITE in the NOFO, the program page or the news release. This is a genuine absence rather than a gap in searching - the quiet-period rule makes a named pre-submission contact structurally impossible for ARPA-E NOFOs. Contact is role-based only (ARPA-E-CO@hq.doe.gov, ExchangeHelp@hq.doe.gov).

IGNIITE 2025 PROJECT PAGES: the 2025 program page reports Project Count 0 despite a published selectee list, so 2025 abstracts exist only in the selectee-descriptions PDF, not as individual project records. Only the 2024 cohort has per-project pages with PI contact emails.

METHOD NOTE (per house rules): no search index was used - this session's web-search budget was exhausted before research began, so every finding above comes from ARPA-E's own pages and documents. arpa-e.energy.gov and arpa-e-foa.energy.gov are client-rendered and return an empty body to a plain text fetch (confirming finding F-014 in the prior status-backfill pass); all HTML pages were read through a rendering browser. The NOFO and FAQ PDFs were fetched and extracted locally with pdftotext. One warning: the fetch tool's own PDF summariser reported 'within 12 years post-PhD' and asserted that prior ARPA-E funding creates ineligibility - BOTH are wrong. The NOFO says eight years, and no blanket prior-ARPA-E exclusion exists. Local text extraction, not the summariser, is what the quotes above rest on.

result.program_name: Investigators in the Pathogenesis of Infectious Disease (PATH)
result.next_deadline:
TWO ANSWERS — they differ by who you are, and conflating them is the main way an applicant wastes a year.

(A) NEXT DATE ON THE BOOKS — INVITED APPLICANTS ONLY: full proposal due "November 12, 2026 by 3:00 pm Eastern Time" (BWF PATH 2027 RFP, Key Dates, p.3; identical on the programme page's Award Timeline, retrieved 2026-09-18). This is closed to anyone who did not submit the July 16, 2026 LOI and receive an invitation on Oct 2, 2026. Programme page Status field reads verbatim: "Invited Applicants Only".

(B) NEXT ENTRY POINT FOR A NEW APPLICANT — the 2028-cycle LOI: NOT FOUND / not yet published as of 2026-09-18. It is not on the programme page, not on https://www.bwfund.org/upcoming-deadlines/ (which on 2026-09-18 listed only CAMS, CAST and NGPI), and ProposalCentral's opportunity list is behind a login. Expect it by the measured pattern in deadline_pattern — mid-July 2027, 3:00 pm ET — but BWF has not posted a date and I am not inferring one.

STATUS TRAP WORTH KNOWING: the funder's own two pages disagree. The master list at https://www.bwfund.org/grants/ labels PATH "Open" with "Nov 12, 2026", while the programme page itself says "Invited Applicants Only". Trust the programme page. A planner scanning the /grants/ list will otherwise believe PATH is open to new applications when it is not.

WHO THIS IS FOR: not PhD students, not postdocs, and not new assistant professors. The 2027 cycle imposes a hard floor of 36 months in post (see resubmission_note). Postdocs wanting the BWF equivalent should look at CASI; PhD students at PDEP/GDEP.
result.loi_deadline:
2027 cycle (most recent, now closed): "Letter of Intent applications due July 16, 2026 by 3:00 pm Eastern Time" (PATH 2027 RFP, Key Dates, p.3). Next cycle's LOI date: not found / not yet published as of 2026-09-18.

RELATIVE TIMING — this is the number to plan against: LOI → invitation is ~2.5 months ("Invitation to submit a full proposal October 2, 2026"); invitation → full proposal is ~6 weeks (Oct 2 → Nov 12, 2026). So an invited applicant gets roughly SIX WEEKS to produce the entire full proposal: 5-page research plan, institutional letter of support, Importance form, Facilities and Resources form, bibliography, 1-3 reprints, budget, and THREE confidential recommendation letters uploaded by the referees themselves. Six weeks is not enough time to start the letters cold — line up referees at LOI time.

LOI BURDEN IS LOW — A DEVIATION WORTH KNOWING: PATH requires NO letters of any kind at LOI stage. The complete LOI is online fields plus exactly two PDFs: "A. Candidate's CV (5-page limit)" and "B. US IRS Letter of Determination" (2027 RFP p.7). The five critical questions are 350 / 1,400 / 1,400 / 700 / 700 characters including spaces. This is materially lighter than CASI, whose LOI needs a mentor letter. The one long-lead item at LOI stage is the institutional signing official's signature — see submission_requirements.

Note BWF's own EST/EDT sloppiness: the RFP p.3 says "3:00 pm Eastern Time" for the July date while the LOI Instructions cover says "July 16, 2026, 3:00 pm EST" (July is EDT). Operatively it means 3:00 pm Eastern local time. The November date is correctly EST.
result.deadline_pattern:
Annual cycle, MEASURED across two consecutive cycles from the funder's own RFPs (not inferred from a single year):

2026 award cycle (BWF-PATH-RFP-2026_v3.pdf, Key Dates):
  LOI July 17, 2025 → invitation Oct 3, 2025 → full proposal Nov 13, 2025 → finalist interviews Apr 13-15, 2026 → notice of award by May 31, 2026 → start Jul 1, 2026 → end Jun 30, 2031.

2027 award cycle (BWF-PATH-RFP-2027_v4.pdf, Key Dates):
  LOI July 16, 2026 → invitation Oct 2, 2026 → full proposal Nov 12, 2026 → finalist interviews Mar 31-Apr 1, 2027 → notice of award by May 31, 2027 → start Jul 1, 2027 → end Jun 30, 2032.

THE RELIABLE PATTERN: LOI mid-July (both cycles fell on a Thursday: Jul 17 2025, Jul 16 2026) → invitation early October → full proposal mid-November (also both Thursdays: Nov 13 2025, Nov 12 2026) → interviews late March/mid-April → notice of award by May 31 → award starts July 1 and runs five years to June 30. Every deadline is 3:00 pm Eastern.

The anchor points that have NOT moved in either cycle are "Notice of award By May 31" and "Award start date July 1" — those two are the safest to plan around. The interview window is the least stable (Apr 13-15 in one cycle, Mar 31-Apr 1 in the next).

Enforcement is absolute and automated: "LOIs will not be accepted after 3:00 pm Eastern Time on July 16, 2026. The online application system shuts down automatically at the deadline and the SUBMIT button will no longer be available" (2027 RFP p.7), and "NO EXCEPTIONS OR EXTENSIONS WILL BE GRANTED" (p.11). PATH FAQ, in full: "Is the BWF application deadline firm? Yes."
result.prior_funding_conflicts: See the dedicated prior_funding_conflicts content above — both halves recorded: blocked by concurrent BWF career development awards and by a completed CAMS/CASI without a mandatory pre-LOI call; preserved explicitly for BWF travel, career guidance for trainees, preterm birth, regulatory science and PDEP grants, and for other funders' support of adjacent work, with an R01 effectively assumed rather than penalised. No NIH-mechanism exclusion exists in PATH's documents.
result.review_to_award:
Full arc, 2027 cycle, from the RFP Key Dates plus the programme page Award Timeline:

LOI Jul 16, 2026 (month 0) → invitation Oct 2, 2026 (~2.5 mo) → full proposal Nov 12, 2026 (~4 mo) → finalist interviews Mar 31-Apr 1, 2027 (~8.5 mo) → notice of award by May 31, 2027 (~10.5 mo) → award start Jul 1, 2027 (~11.5 mo) → award end Jun 30, 2032.

So it is ~11.5 months from first LOI keystroke to first dollar, and ~7.5 months from the full proposal to notification. Measured from the full proposal instead (the stage most people think of as "applying"), it is ~6.5 months to notification and ~8 months to start.

WHERE PATH DEVIATES FROM THE BWF NORM:
- Slightly FASTER to award than CAMS (CAMS: Sep 30 → notice May 28, ~8 months, but start Sep 1, ~11 months) and it front-loads the wait into the LOI stage rather than the post-submission stage.
- The dead zone is long: after the Nov 12 full proposal there is ~4.5 months of silence before interviews. BWF confirms no interim signal exists — "All communications, including the invitation to submit a full proposal and declinations, will be made through email" and "BWF does not provide critiques of LOIs or of full proposals."
- Interview timing is the least stable element year to year (Apr 13-15, 2026 vs Mar 31-Apr 1, 2027). Do not book unmovable travel for late March/April of the decision year.
- Award end is a fixed calendar date (Jun 30, 2032), not five years from your start — the clock does not follow you.

WHO DECIDES: "The PATH Advisory Committee will review LOIs and full proposals, interview finalists, and make recommendations to BWF's Board of Directors for funding." One committee handles all three stages — the people who screen your LOI are the people who interview you. The roster is public (see examples_or_samples); reading it is the closest PATH offers to a fit conversation.

POST-AWARD: awards pay $505,000 over five years; annual scientific progress report and institutional financial report are both due August 1 each award year, through ProposalCentral, and "Continued funding will depend on both the timely submission of these reports and their favorable review." Awardees must devote "at least 75 percent of their overall time to research-related activities", though "There is no explicit minimum percent effort that must be dedicated to the PATH award."
result.submission_requirements:
Portal is ProposalCentral, per the BWF-wide norm. Recording only PATH deviations and PATH-specific numbers.

RESEARCH PLAN IS 5 PAGES, NOT 6 (the single most important deviation — CAMS, NGPI and CASI full proposals are all 6). Verbatim: "Research Plan (5-page limit) In no more than five pages (including figures, tables, graphs, and images)". Required order: specific aims; background and significance; experimental methods and procedures; long-term objectives. Format: "standard 11- or 12-point font for the text, and no smaller than a 9 to 10-point font for figures, legends, and tables. This requirement will be strictly enforced." Single-spaced, half-inch or larger margins, pages numbered, no table of contents, no appendices. FAQ is blunt: "How serious are you about the page limit on the research plan? All applicants must stay within the set five-page limit or the application will be rejected." Bibliography is a separate attachment and excluded from the limit — but "graphs, charts, and diagrams do count toward the five-page maximum."

THREE CONFIDENTIAL RECOMMENDATION LETTERS — FULL PROPOSAL STAGE ONLY, NONE AT LOI. Rules that are easy to violate: "At least one letter should come from someone involved in training the applicant"; "One letter must be from a recommender not connected to the applicant's current institution or its affiliates"; letterhead plus signature block; referees upload directly and you never see them. Hard gate: "An application CANNOT BE SUBMITTED until the applicant's three letters of recommendation have been uploaded and attached to the application by the grant deadline." FAQ: "It is highly recommended that all Letters of Recommendation be uploaded to the application a week before the deadline date." Letters of collaboration are refused outright: "Collaborative situations can be described in the five-page Research Plan - there is no need for individual collaborative letters."

TWO INSTITUTIONAL PEOPLE, NOT ONE. Beyond the signing official that every BWF application needs, the PATH full proposal adds: "A Financial Officer must be added in this section. The Financial Officer is responsible for completing the financial report if the grant is awarded." Both must be identified inside ProposalCentral; the signing official must personally log in and sign by 3:00 pm.

TWO FORMS ON BWF TEMPLATES — download them early, they have no analogue at other funders: (C) Importance form ("describe how the aims presented here depart from or move beyond currently funded work") and (F) Facilities and Resources form.

INSTITUTIONAL LETTER OF SUPPORT is graded, not a formality. From the chair, dean or division director; must cover salary support, career-development mentoring, and "protection of 75 percent of the grantee's time for research"; on letterhead with a signature block. BWF's own warning: "Letters that lack detail, specificity, or clear enthusiasm for the applicant and his or her career can undermine an otherwise competitive proposal."

REPRINTS: "At least one reprint is required and up to three are allowed." Manuscripts in preparation are barred; preprints are allowed.

What exists is unrestricted reapplication in a later cycle as a wholly new application; declines arrive by email only.

THE REAL LIMIT IS THE ELIGIBILITY WINDOW, AND FOR THE 2027 CYCLE IT NARROWED AT BOTH ENDS.

*** DRIFT ALERT — VERIFIED BY DIFFING THE TWO RFPs. The 2027 RFP cover page is flagged "New Seniority Requirement". New hard floor: "Applicants must be 36 months or more from their start date as assistant professors by the LOI deadline of July 16, 2026" and "Applicants must have been in their faculty positions for at least 36 months to apply." The 2026 RFP contained NO such rule — only soft advice: "Very few newly appointed assistant professors are competitive for this award. Most should consider applying later in their career." Soft guidance became a hard bar in one cycle. Anyone working from last year's RFP, a mentor's memory, or a lab-wiki summary will get this wrong. ***

Ceiling, unchanged: "Candidates who will be promoted to Associate Professor by November 12, 2026 are not eligible to apply" and "Associate professors, with or without tenure, are ineligible." Note the ceiling is tested at the FULL PROPOSAL date while the floor is tested at the LOI date — a promotion landing between mid-July and mid-November disqualifies you mid-cycle. ProposalCentral asks for your "Anticipated Promotion Date", so this is checked, not assumed.

NET WINDOW: roughly from month 36 in post to promotion — commonly two to four annual attempts, with zero feedback between them. The target is stated plainly: "The ideal candidate is an accomplished investigator at the mid-to-late assistant professor level with an established record of independent research in a tenure-track position or its well-supported equivalent in non-tenure offering departments."

WHAT TO USE INSTEAD OF A SUMMARY STATEMENT: the published PATH Advisory Committee roster (these are your actual reviewers at every stage), the RFP's explicitly encouraged topics, and — uniquely for PATH — the offered call with the programme officer. Also honest self-assessment against the LOI's fifth question, which is where most LOIs fail: if the proposed work is not visibly riskier than your R01, PATH is not the mechanism.

ALSO FATAL, AND NOT A RESUBMISSION ISSUE: "It is specifically targeted toward work on the pathogenesis of infectious disease. Work not focused on pathogenesis will not be funded." And "Microbiome-related proposals must be infectious disease-focused to compete well in this program." PATH is a career development award for an individual: it "does not support collaborative teams."

ONE MORE GATE: institutions must be US or Canadian 501(c)(3) or equivalent non-profits; a Canadian institution still uploads a US IRS Letter of Determination, at BOTH LOI and full proposal stage. Get that PDF from your research office before you start. Citizenship is generously drawn — citizens plus permanent and temporary residents of the US and Canada legally qualified to work there, with named visa classes (US: J-1, H1B, F-1, O-1; Canada: Study Permit, C-43, C-44, C-10, C-20).

result.deadline_pattern: Annual. Nomination deadline noon ET second week of September (verified: Sept 10, 2026) → mandatory in-person interviews on set Wednesdays across October–November → notification by December 31 of the same year → award start the following July 1, August 1 or September 1. Applicant-selectable start date is a real feature, not drift: "Award Start Date: July 1, August 1 or September 1, 2027."
result.loi_deadline: No LOI or pre-proposal stage exists. BUT the absence of an LOI understates the timeline burden, and this is the single most missable feature of the mechanism: it is nomination-driven and the candidate is structurally barred from submitting. "Submissions by nominees will not be accepted. This is a nominator driven process, and the responsibility of submitting the nomination in SAM resides with the nominator." The functional equivalent of an LOI gate is therefore securing (a) a tenured nominator, (b) a separate tenure-track/tenured recommender, and (c) a committed NYC mentor plus a signed institutional letter — all of which must be in hand before the September deadline. The funder's only preparatory instruction is to the nominator: "At least a week in advance of the deadline, the nominator should log in to SAM or create a new account if one does not exist for the nominator."
result.review_to_award: Submission (Sept 10, 2026, noon ET) → shortlisting by Senior Fellows → MANDATORY in-person interview at the foundation on one of six fixed dates: "October 7, 14, 21 and 28 and November 4 and 11, 2026, from 1:20–5:50 PM Eastern time"; "Nominees must be available to attend an in-person interview on one of these dates." → "Notifications will be sent by December 31, 2026." → earliest start July 1, 2027. So: ~3.7 months submission-to-notification, ~9.7 months submission-to-earliest-start, and ~6 months of salary gap risk between notification and start that a candidate must bridge. Interview format is specified and is effectively a second application: 15 minutes, "approximately five minutes on the background and state of the nominee's field, five minutes on the nominee's previous work and five minutes on research plans... accessible to a general scientific audience, while providing enough specificity to allow scientists in the nominee's own field to judge the past and proposed research." Nominees are "strongly encouraged" to attend the Simons Foundation Presidential Lecture on their interview day and the dinner that follows. Selectivity: "less than 10 percent of nominees are selected."
result.submission_requirements: Portal: Simons Award Manager (SAM), https://sam.simonsfoundation.org/, under the NOMINATOR's account (Funding Opportunities → Create Application → Begin Application). DEVIATION FROM NORM: "There is no institutional sign-off involved in a Junior Fellows application" / "No institutional sign-off is required for submission" — unusual for a fellowship that nonetheless requires an institutional commitment letter. Also: "No late submissions will be permitted, and no extensions will be provided." Post-submission edits impossible; only a pre-deadline "Revise" resubmission. Six required components with hard page limits: (1) Nomination Letter, two-page limit, written and signed by the nominator; (2) Recommendation Letter, two-page limit, by "an expert that is not the nominator"; (3) Mentor Statement, one half-page limit, confirming the mentor has agreed to serve and will supply resources, plus the mentor's past mentoring experience, how they would train this specific nominee, and what professional skills they would relay; (4) Letter of support from the NYC host institution, one-page limit, signed by an institutional official, confirming space/resources and designation of a mentor, agreement to appoint the Fellow as an employee with "a postdoctoral research associate, or equivalent, title with no teaching obligations" and standard benefits, and naming a signing official and financial officer; (5) Statement of Recent Work by the nominee, "one-page limit, plus up to an additional half page for links to published work and references", summarising the PhD thesis work and the research plan and specifically addressing "the contribution of the host institution and mentor to the candidate's plan", written for a general scientific audience; (6) Nominee Biosketch, max 3 pages, mandatory SAM template — "No other template can be used", font 10pt or larger, template margins retained, plus a URL to a full publication list in a public database "such as SciENcv, My Bibliography, or Google Scholar". TWO HARD DISQUALIFIERS worth flagging to any applicant: "Any additional letters of support appended to the nomination, recommendation and host institution letters, or the mentor statement will render the nomination ineligible" and "Any uploaded documents exceeding the noted page limits below will also render the nomination ineligible." Generative-AI disclosure required: "Indicate the extent to which, if any, generative AI technology was used and how it was used to develop this proposal." ROLE-SEPARATION RULES (easy to trip): nominator must be tenured or equivalent; recommender must be tenure-track/tenured or equivalent; nominees cannot be their own nominator or recommender; "Either the nominator or the recommender must be from an institution outside the nominee's current institution"; "Active Senior Fellows of the Society of Fellows cannot nominate" and cannot write a recommendation letter; the intended mentor "cannot write the nomination letter or recommendation letter"; mentor must hold a tenure-track/tenured or equivalent post at an eligible NYC host institute; "A nominator may submit only one nomination per year"; "Only one nomination per individual is permitted." Mentor capacity limit: "A mentor can only be involved in one nomination if they are currently not mentoring a Junior Fellow or, if the Junior Fellow they are mentoring will have their award ending before the start date of nominee's award." Host institution must be an educational institution in Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, Staten Island or the Bronx (or an affiliated medical institution); "Institutions outside New York City are not eligible"; "The Flatiron Institute is not an eligible host institution, although Fellows may spend time at the institute." Residency and service obligations: Fellows must "attend weekly lectures and dinners at the foundation during the academic year, as well as an annual conference and a four-day weekend retreat", and be "in residence in New York City during the academic year" (not required outside academic terms).
result.prior_funding_conflicts: BOTH HALVES, quoted from the funder. DISQUALIFYING / TERMINATING: (1) "A Junior Fellowship cannot be held concurrently with another fellowship or a tenure-track faculty appointment." Note this bars concurrent HOLDING, not concurrent applying — a candidate may hold competing offers while nominated and must decline one on acceptance. (2) "Junior Fellows cannot hold Simons Foundation or Simons Foundation International grants during their appointment" — a same-funder bar specific to the appointment period. (3) Salary layering is barred: "Junior Fellows may not receive salary support from grants. If salary support from other sources, such as voluntary teaching, is accepted, the fellowship award amount will be correspondingly reduced." (4) Career-move termination clause: "The award will be interrupted or terminated at the foundation's discretion if the Junior Fellow takes up a primary, long-term position at a research institute, national laboratory, non–New York City or for-profit organization or accepts a major administrative responsibility that significantly reduces the time available for research." WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the carve-out, same sentence as the Simons-grant bar): Fellows "may work on research projects funded by other grants and, if permitted by their institution, may apply for or hold grants from non-foundation sources." So the rule is not "no other funding" — it is: no other FELLOWSHIP, no Simons/Simons International grant, and no SALARY from any grant; but working on other-grant-funded projects, and applying for and holding non-Simons grants with institutional permission, is expressly allowed. Practical reading for a postdoc: you can and should continue building an independent non-Simons grant record during the fellowship, and you may transfer the award between eligible NYC institutions ("Junior Fellows may transfer their award to another educational institution in New York City"). PhD-date eligibility window (drift-sensitive, restated each cycle): "For 2027, a Junior Fellow must have fulfilled the requirements of a Ph.D. no earlier than May 2025 and no later than August of 2027" — i.e. roughly a 2-year-post-PhD-to-not-yet-graduated band, which shifts annually and must be re-checked. result.review_to_award:
Submission February 1 → notification "early June" (~4 months) → earliest start July 1 (~5 months after submission). Quoted: "Fellowship awards are announced in early June." and "Awardees will receive $150,000 per year for three-years ($450,000 total) beginning July 1."

Review body: not staff and not a standing NIH-style study section — "Applications will be reviewed, and selections made, by a Scientific Advisory Committee of distinguished neuroscientists." No external ad-hoc reviewers or applicant response/rebuttal stage is mentioned; there is no interview or site-visit stage on the published timeline.

Cohort size (from the funder's Fellows directory): 16 awards in 2024, 13 in 2025, 13 in 2026. The funder does not publish application volume, so a success rate cannot be computed.

Payment mechanics worth planning for: funds go to the institution but are the Fellow's exclusively, are portable if the Fellow moves institutions (together with purchased equipment), carry NO institutional overhead (fringe benefits may be charged), and continuation is "contingent on the receipt of progress reports and determination by the Fund that the Fellow has made satisfactory progress."
result.submission_requirements:
Portal: Foundant GrantInterface at http://www.grantinterface.com/Home/Logon?urlkey=ktgf — inside it, select the proposal type "EAJK Neuroscience Application". Note the urlkey reads "ktgf" (the sibling Third Generation Foundation), so the login page will not look neuroscience-specific; that is expected.

Four required components, exactly as enumerated by the funder:
1. CONFIRMATION LETTER (institutional sign-off) — from an institutional official, e.g. an offer letter from the dean or department chair, "indicating the date of appointment and the commitment of institutional resources to establish the investigator and the prospects for long-term support by the institution."
2. ABSTRACTS — "Copies of the abstract page from four of your best papers, published in peer-reviewed journals that are representative of your work. You may include preprints."
3. RESEARCH PLAN — "no more than four double-spaced pages with 1″ margins using no smaller than 11-point font size, an outline of your research plans and the relevancy of your plans under a Klingenstein Neuroscience Fellowship. Please give specific aims. Figures and concise figure legends are allowed but must fit within the four-page limit. References are in addition to the four pages and can be single-spaced."
4. RECOMMENDATIONS — "email addresses for three or four references, including one from your department head or equivalent, who we will contact for letters"; the funder contacts them directly. Letters due February 1.

Process rule: "the Principal Investigator must initiate the application process. Once the Principal Investigator has started the application, they may invite other people (e.g., development and administrative staff) to collaborate on the request."

WHERE THIS DEVIATES FROM PEER EARLY-CAREER FOUNDATION AWARDS (the high-value deltas):
- NOT A LIMITED SUBMISSION. "More than one application may be submitted from an institution." Unlike Pew/Searle/Beckman-style awards, there is no institutional nomination cap and therefore no internal campus competition to win first. You can apply directly; you do not need your research development office's permission to be the nominee.
- The page budget is far tighter than it looks: four pages DOUBLE-SPACED at ≥11pt is roughly two single-spaced pages of prose, and figures plus legends must fit inside that. References are the only thing excluded.
- No biosketch, no NIH-style CV, no budget or budget justification is requested. Track record is evidenced by four paper abstract pages instead.
- No letters of collaboration, no sponsor/mentor statement (this is an independent-investigator award, not a mentored one), no data-management or resource-sharing plan.
- Reference letters are due WITH the application, not on a later date.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
There is NO hard prior-funding bar on this mechanism. Recording both halves, because the "excluded" half is essentially empty and the real disqualifiers are career-stage, not funding.

WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (explicitly):
- Holding other fellowships concurrently does not disqualify you — "Although there's no strict prohibition against holding more than one fellowship at one time, the Fund may take other funding into account when deciding whether to grant an Award."
- Existing research support is ASSUMED, not penalised. The award is designed as a top-up: the Fund's stated hope is that funding "will seed new directions in the fellows' research programs by providing an unencumbered addition to their regular sources of research support."
- NIH funding is nowhere named as disqualifying. There is no R01/K-style interaction rule, no "you must relinquish X", no overlap certification, and no bar on holding an R00, R01, DP2, or K award. (Stated precisely: the funder's page simply does not mention federal awards at all — this is absence of a stated bar, not an affirmative carve-out.)

WHAT ACTUALLY HURTS YOU (soft, review-stage — a scoring preference, not an eligibility screen):
- "We give priority to candidates who may not have received substantial funding from other private awards." So substantial PRIVATE foundation funding already in hand (Searle, Pew, Beckman, McKnight, Brain Research Foundation and similar) weakens competitiveness. The funder's wording is specific to private awards.
- The Fund reserves discretion to weigh your total funding picture when deciding, per the quote above.

WHAT IS MANDATORY (an eligibility condition, not a courtesy):
- Disclosure. "Applicants must inform the Esther A. & Joseph Klingenstein Fund of other sources of funding." This is listed as one of the four numbered qualifications you must meet at the deadline — so failing to disclose other funding is an eligibility defect, even though holding that funding is not.

THE REAL DISQUALIFIERS (all career-stage; these are what actually rules people out):
- More than four years between completion of your last postdoc and the application deadline — "a maximum of four years between the completion of last postdoc and the application deadline." This is measured to the deadline (Feb 1), not to the award date.
- No tenure-track appointment — "The candidate must have a tenure track appointment or equivalent."
- Primary appointment outside the US — "Applicants must have a primary tenure track position at an institution in the United States."
- Research training not yet complete — must "have completed all research training, including post-doctoral training," and hold a PhD and/or MD.
result.program_officer_contact:
No named program officer for this mechanism. The single published route is the Fund's general address: **info@klingenstein.org** — "Please contact the Fund at info@klingenstein.org with any questions." No phone number, no staff scientist, and no named grants manager is given on the neuroscience pages.

Pre-submission contact is NOT expected or required. Nothing on the page asks for a pre-submission inquiry, concept clearance, or eligibility pre-check — the framing is reactive ("with any questions"). The one thing genuinely worth emailing about is an eligibility edge case, e.g. whether your appointment counts as "tenure track or equivalent" or how a career interruption affects the four-year clock, since the page defines neither.

WHO ACTUALLY READS IT (more useful than the contact address here): the reviewers are public. The Scientific Advisory Committee is chaired by Jeremy Nathans (MD, PhD), with members Elizabeth A. Buffalo, Edward Chang, Catherine Dulac, Lily Jan, Helen S. Mayberg, Mala Murthy, Franck Polleux, Vanessa Ruta, Joshua R. Sanes, Hongjun Song, Joseph S. Takahashi, and Fan Wang; James O. McNamara is listed as Special Advisor, with Charles D. Gilbert and Eric R. Kandel as Emeritus Advisors. Strategic read: this is a small generalist panel spanning molecular, circuits, systems, and clinical/psychiatric neuroscience — not subspecialist peers. Write the four pages for an expert neuroscientist outside your subfield. Named committee members are also the people your three-to-four referees should be credible to. Source: https://klingenstein.org/esther-a-joseph-klingenstein-fund/neuroscience/scientific-advisory-committee/
result.examples_or_samples:
No full sample application, annotated proposal, or funded abstract text is published by this funder — I could not find one, and I could not extend the search (this session's web-search budget was exhausted at 200/200, so all findings here come from direct fetches of the funder's own site).

What IS available, and it is genuinely usable as a model:
- FUNDED PROJECT TITLES + PEOPLE + LABS: https://klingenstein.org/esther-a-joseph-klingenstein-fund/neuroscience/fellowship-programs/ lists three full cohorts — 2026 (13 fellows), 2025 (13), 2024 (16), 42 funded projects total — each card giving the fellow's name and degree, the funded project title, the institution, and a direct Lab Website link. Reading 42 funded titles is the best available calibration of what wins, and the lab links take you to the actual science and, usually, the researcher's publications.
- Representative 2026 titles, to show the register: "Mechanisms of Neurogenesis in the Largest Invertebrate Brain" (Caroline B. Albertin, Harvard); "Neural basis of predictive regulation of immune function" (Emilia Favuzzi, Yale); "How we learn from our mistakes: new insights from an error-signaling cell type" (Jonathan Green, Mass General); "Toward a unified logic of somatosensation and interoception" (Chen Ran, Scripps); "How to synchronize 20,000 clock neurons" (Stephen Zhang, NYU). The pattern: single crisp mechanistic question, often a novel system or an unexpected cross-domain link — matching the funder's own framing that the awards "promote high-risk, and potentially high-reward, projects."
- SELF-MODELLING SHORTCUT: since component 2 requires the abstract pages of four of your own best papers, and since fellows' lab sites are linked, current fellows' recent paper abstracts are a direct proxy for the standard of evidence the panel expects.
- WHO TO TALK TO FOR REAL ADVICE: any of the 42 listed 2024-2026 fellows is a recent, contactable successful applicant — the directory gives institution and lab site for each. Fellows attend a required annual meeting in NYC during the three-year term, so the cohort is a live network.

Note: the funder publishes no FAQ for this mechanism; I checked the neuroscience section and the funding-opportunities page and found none.
result.resubmission_note:
Resubmission is explicitly allowed, with no stated limit on attempts and no required waiting cycle: "Candidates may reapply if they continue to meet the eligibility requirements."

The binding constraint is not a resubmission rule but the eligibility clock — the four-year maximum between completion of the last postdoc and the application deadline. Because the competition runs once a year, an applicant gets at most about four shots, and in practice fewer. Plan the first application early in the window rather than treating year one as a throwaway.

The funder does not publish any "introduction to resubmission" page, response-to-reviewers component, or reviewer feedback process; there is no indication that applicants receive critiques, so a resubmission cannot be structured as a formal response to prior review.
unresolved: Whether the four-year post-postdoc eligibility clock can be extended for career interruptions (parental leave, medical leave, caregiving, visa gaps). The funder's page states the four-year maximum with no exceptions clause and no extension request process. This is the single most consequential unknown for applicants near the boundary, and the only route to an answer appears to be emailing info@klingenstein.org.

What 'tenure track appointment or equivalent' includes. The phrase 'or equivalent' is used twice and never defined — unclear whether non-tenure-track independent investigator or assistant-professor-equivalent posts at research institutes (e.g. Allen Institute, Max Planck Florida, Scripps, Dana-Farber, all of which appear in the fellows list) qualify by rule or by case-by-case judgement. Fellows at such institutes are in the 2024-2026 cohorts, which suggests they do qualify, but the rule itself is not stated.

Application volume and success rate. Only cohort size is published (16 in 2024, 13 in 2025, 13 in 2026); the number of applications received is not disclosed anywhere on the funder's site, so selectivity cannot be quantified.

Whether the literal string 'February 1, 2027' is published anywhere by the funder. It is not on the applying page — the year is derived from the funder's fixed annual pattern plus the confirmed-open portal, as documented in next_deadline. Could not be cross-checked against the application portal itself, which is behind a login (account creation is out of scope).

No funded application text, successful abstract, or annotated sample is published by the funder, and I could not search beyond the funder's own site for third-party samples (e.g. university research-development offices that sometimes post exemplars) because this session's web-search budget was exhausted at 200/200 calls. Worth one targeted search in a later session.

Funder-wide machinery was not researched and was not available for this funder. Reporting requirements beyond 'receipt of progress reports', allowable-cost detail beyond 'no provision is made for institutional overhead, but fringe benefits may be charged', and any no-cost-extension or carryover policy remain unestablished.

Whether the Simons Foundation partnership (2013-2024) leaves any residual co-branding or separate track. The neuroscience overview page still describes the former Klingenstein-Simons partnership historically, while the applying page makes no mention of it — consistent with the existing row's 2026-07-18 verification that the partnership has ended, but the overview page's wording could cause confusion for applicants searching under the old name.

result.deadline_pattern:
Fixed annual single-round deadline, late October, 5:00 PM ET. No rolling submission, no LOI round, no standard-due-date grid.

Submission is through ACLS OFA (https://ofa.acls.org). Reference letters and the institutional statement go through a SEPARATE portal (https://ofa.acls.org/reference/) that your referees and department cannot reach until you have entered them in your own application — so register and enter them weeks early.

Planning shape for a PhD student: this is the late-October cluster. If you also want the Mellon/ACLS Dissertation Innovation Fellowship, it shares this exact date, and the two have incompatible formatting (see submission_requirements) — do not reuse one packet for the other.
result.loi_deadline: n/a — no letter of intent, pre-proposal, nomination or institutional pre-screen. Single-stage full application straight into OFA. Checked the programme page and the programme-specific FAQ; neither mentions any preliminary stage. (Contrast the Graves Awards elsewhere in the ACLS calendar, which are nomination-based — this one is not.)
result.review_to_award:
FASTER than the ACLS norm — this mechanism notifies about six weeks earlier than the flagship.

- Day 0: Oct 28, 2026, 5:00 PM ET. Application must be in SUBMITTED status; letters due same moment.
- Eligibility screen: mechanical (US doctoral enrolment, dissertation topic, ABD-before-tenure, citizenship/status, not having applied twice before).
- Peer review: "Proposals submitted to the Luce/ACLS Dissertation Fellowship program are read by experts in American art history with a wide variety of specializations." Note the DEVIATION from the ACLS flagship: this is a field-specific panel of American art historians, not a two-stage disciplinary-then-multidisciplinary review. You are writing for art historians outside your subfield, not for an all-humanities panel.
- Notification: "Notifications will be sent via email by mid-March 2027" — roughly 4.5 months after the deadline, versus April/late April (~6–6.5 months) for ACLS Fellowships and Mellon/ACLS DIF.
- Earliest start: July 2027, about 8 months after the deadline. Term is "a continuous period of nine to twelve months between July 2027 and June 2028" — note this is NINE months minimum inside a 12-month window, stricter than the flagship's 6–12 months inside an 18-month window. You cannot take a short or split term.
- Reviewer feedback: available on request, but with a HARD REQUEST DEADLINE that deviates from the funder norm — "All requests for comments from the 2026-27 competition must be received by June 30, 2027", with processing beginning in the summer once the competition year closes. Miss June 30 and you get nothing. Subject to the usual limit that feedback "is made available at the discretion of each reviewer."
- No Project Development Grant consolation prize here; that is an ACLS Fellowships feature, not this one.
result.submission_requirements:
Where this DEVIATES from ACLS norms (all quotes from the programme page, fetched 2026-09-18):

1. PROPOSAL IS 8 PAGES DOUBLE-SPACED — longest dissertation proposal ACLS runs. "Proposal of no more than eight pages, double spaced, with one-inch margins, in Arial or Helvetica 11-point font, inclusive of all images and any footnotes or endnotes." Compare ACLS Fellowships (3pp SINGLE-spaced) and Mellon/ACLS DIF (7pp double). Do not port formatting between them.

2. IMAGES ARE MANDATORY AND COUNT AGAINST THE LIMIT. The proposal must include "at least three images", and the page limit is "inclusive of all images". This is unique among ACLS mechanisms and is a real design constraint: three images inside eight double-spaced pages costs you perhaps a page of prose. Budget for it from the first draft.

3. ANNOTATED BIBLIOGRAPHY, EXACTLY TEN SOURCES. "Annotated Bibliography (no more than four pages, double spaced, with one-inch margins, in Arial or Helvetica 11-point font) of ten key secondary sources." The flagship wants a plain 2-page single-spaced bibliography; here it is annotated, double-spaced, and the source count is specified.

4. TWO REFERENCE LETTERS, ONE MUST BE YOUR ADVISOR. ACLS Fellowships takes no letters at all, so this is a hard deviation. Letters due at the application deadline. NO dossier services: "No. ACLS requests that reference letters contain specific elements targeted to this fellowship program", because "Peer reviewers have expressed strong reservations about letters from dossier services since they are necessarily general and thus less helpful in assessing the merits of the proposed project." If a referee goes silent, ACLS says plainly you "can ask someone else to write for you."

5. INSTITUTIONAL STATEMENT — the sleeper long-lead item. Your department must confirm your doctoral-candidate status and that "tuition and fees for the awardee will be waived or will be provided." That is a commitment from your institution, not a form you fill in, and it is submitted through the separate reference portal. Start this conversation with your DGS early.

6. OPTIONAL: "List of publications, exhibitions, presentations, and scholarly/university service (no more than one page, single spaced, with one-inch margins, in Arial or Helvetica 11-point font)". Note "exhibitions" — curatorial work counts here in a way it does not on most ACLS forms.

7. No transcripts required. Constant with the funder norm: Arial or Helvetica 11-point, one-inch margins, page limits inclusive of notes.

EVALUATION CRITERIA (write to these three): "The quality of the proposal with regard to its methodology, scope, theoretical framework, and grounding in the relevant scholarly literature"; "The potential of the project to advance the study of American art, both generally and in the specific field(s) it engages"; and "The applicant's record of scholarly engagement and potential for scholarly achievement, taking into account the relative advantages and constraints on resources" — that last clause is an explicit instruction to reviewers to read your record against your institution's resources.

SCOPE NOTE: the programme covers "the history of art and visual culture of the United States, including all aspects of Native American art."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves. This is the strictest concurrent-funding rule in the ACLS portfolio, and it is easy to trip.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU OR THE AWARD:
- Any other stipendiary fellowship, at any level: "ACLS policy prohibits Luce/ACLS Dissertation Fellows from holding concurrent fellowships that provide a stipend of any amount." Note "of any amount" — there is no de minimis threshold. A small departmental writing stipend counts.
- The programme page's own wording: "The fellowships may not be used to defray tuition costs or be held concurrently with any other major fellowship or grant."
- Anything requiring labour: "Fellows may not accept an award that requires work of any kind, for example a teaching or research assistantship." So a TA-ship or RA-ship that funds you must be given up for the 9–12 month term. Plan the handover with your department before you accept.
- More than one ACLS award in a year: "Not more than one ACLS or ACLS-joint award may normally be accepted in any one competition year."
- HAVING APPLIED TWICE ALREADY. This is an eligibility gate, not just a resubmission cap: applicants must "have not previously applied for this fellowship more than once."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half people miss):
- Institutional tuition, fee and health-insurance support is not merely permitted — it is REQUIRED. The institutional statement must confirm "tuition and fees for the awardee will be waived or will be provided." So your university's tuition package is a precondition of the award, not a conflict with it. Do not decline it.
- Applying widely in the same cycle is fine: "Yes, an applicant to this fellowship may also apply to as many fellowship programs as are suitable." The restriction bites on HOLDING, not on applying. Apply to everything; sort out the collision only if you win twice. (Note this answers, for this mechanism specifically, the question left open at funder level about simultaneous applications across ACLS competitions.)
- The CHCI residency enhancement does not count against you and needs no separate application: fellows "have the opportunity to spend all or part of their fellowship terms in residence at selected CHCI member organizations", described as "an optional enhancement to the award for fellows and does not require a separate application."
- Non-stipendiary support (travel grants, library or museum reader fellowships with no stipend, archival access awards) is not caught by the stipend language — though I could not find a page defining "major fellowship or grant", so confirm a specific case with ACLS before assuming. See unresolved.
result.program_officer_contact:

Verbatim from the ACLS staff page: "Alison Chang is a Senior Program Officer on the US Programs Team, focusing on fellowship programs including the Getty/ACLS Postdoctoral Fellowship, the Luce/ACLS Dissertation Fellowship in American Art, and the Mellon/ACLS Dissertation Innovation Fellowship." Use the institutional routes: fellowships@acls.org for programme and eligibility questions, ofahelp@acls.org for portal/technical problems, and the reference-portal address for letter-writer problems. PROVENANCE: acls.org obfuscates every address on the rendered page (they came back as "[email protected]" placeholders in all my fetches), so those three spellings come from the funder-wide layer already established in this corpus, not from a page I read directly this pass. General switchboard, read directly: 212-697-1505, 633 Third Avenue, New York, NY 10017-6706.

WHAT CONTACT IS FOR: eligibility edge cases, not proposal feedback. Worth asking a human before you write: whether your programme or joint appointment counts as "art history or a related field"; whether your topic counts as "visual arts of the United States" (the Native American art inclusion is explicit, transnational and colonial topics are a live question); whether an interrupted degree clock affects you; and whether a specific concurrent award is caught by the stipend rule. ACLS does NOT review drafts. ACLS runs informational webinars and Zoom office hours across the open period, roughly monthly from ~3.5 months out to ~10 days before the deadline; I could not confirm the 2026-27 session dates for this competition specifically — see unresolved.
result.examples_or_samples:
Stated plainly by the funder: there are NO published funded proposals. Verbatim from this programme's own FAQ: "we do not provide examples of proposals that receive funding." ACLS instead points applicants at previous awardees. What actually exists, ranked by usefulness:

1. THE PROGRAMME'S OWN CRAFT GUIDE, linked from this page's "Supporting Documents" section — "Writing Proposals for ACLS Fellowship Competitions" by Christina M. Gillis (PDF): https://www.acls.org/competitions/acls-fellowships/writing-fellowship-proposals-2/. This is the only writing guidance ACLS endorses for this competition. It is framed around ACLS Fellowships but ACLS links it here deliberately.

2. THIS PROGRAMME'S OWN FAQ — https://www.acls.org/faqs/faq-luce-acls-dissertation-fellowships-in-american-art/. Separate from the generic ACLS FAQ, and the single densest source of rules for this mechanism (concurrency, letters, reapplication, feedback). Read it before you write anything.

3. AWARDEE LIST FILTERED TO THIS PROGRAMME — https://www.acls.org/recent-fellows/?_fellow_program=422 (20 recent fellows, 2024–2026) and the full database at https://www.acls.org/fellows-grantees/ (filter by Related Program and Fellowship Year; records run back decades). Name, year, institution and PROJECT TITLE only — no abstracts. Real examples returned: "Elise Armani, 2024, State University of New York, Stony Brook, Making Rhythms Out of Barriers: Infrastructural Interventions by Migrant Artists on the Lower East Side (1975-1989)"; "Max Bowens, 2025, Harvard University, Storing the Self: Art, Data, and Repatriation"; "Ashley Elizabeth Williams, 2024, Columbia University, Unfree Artists on the Borders of US Empire, 1850-1930". Use for calibration of scale and register, and to find named people in your subfield to email — recent fellows are the most useful humans available to you, since ACLS will not read your draft. Some entries carry an "Ellen Holtzman Fellow" designation (a named sub-award within the programme).

4. BEST VIEW OF THE ACTUAL FORM, with a caveat: the Mellon/ACLS DIF sample application PDF, https://www.acls.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/DIF-Sample-Application.pdf (48pp), is a screen-by-screen print-out of the whole OFA system. It is for a DIFFERENT competition, and its page limits and spacing are wrong for this one, but the account, demographic, education, awards, publications and reference-letter screens are the same system, so you can draft offline before creating an account. Do not copy its formatting rules.

5. Seven awards are made per year — "seven fellowships for a non-renewable, continuous nine- to twelve-month term". Useful for calibrating expectations; ACLS does not publish an application count, so no success rate can be computed.

There is no ACLS equivalent of NIH RePORTER, no abstract corpus, and no summary statements. The nearest substitute for a summary statement is the reviewer feedback you may request after a decline — and you must request it by June 30, 2027.
result.resubmission_note:
ONCE ONLY, and enforced as an eligibility gate rather than a soft norm — so a mistake here is disqualifying, not merely unhelpful.

Verbatim, FAQ: "Yes, but unsuccessful applicants may reapply to this program only once." Verbatim, eligibility: applicants must "have not previously applied for this fellowship more than once."

That is two lifetime attempts, and the ABD-before-tenure and current-enrolment requirements mean the second attempt is often not available in practice — many candidates will have defended or run out of enrolment before the next late-October deadline. Treat the first attempt as the real one.

MECHANICS: there is no introduction page, no response-to-reviewers document, no A0/A1 marking. Nothing in the application identifies you as a returning applicant and reviewers are not told. You rebuild the submission from scratch in a new cycle's application; the portal carries nothing forward, so keep your own copies of every upload.

THE ONE USABLE INPUT, and its timing — which is unusually favourable here compared with the ACLS flagship: notification lands by mid-March 2027, you must request reviewer comments by June 30, 2027 (hard cut-off), comments are processed over the summer, and the next deadline is late October 2027. That gives you a genuine summer to rewrite, rather than the flagship's month-long scramble. Request feedback the moment a decline arrives — do not wait, because the request window closes in June whether or not the comments have reached you. Caveat: "feedback is made available at the discretion of each reviewer", so comments may not arrive from everyone who read you.
unresolved: Definition of "major fellowship or grant": the programme page bars holding the award "concurrently with any other major fellowship or grant" but no ACLS page I fetched defines "major". The FAQ's stipend-based test ("fellowships that provide a stipend of any amount") is narrower and clearer; I could not establish whether a non-stipendiary award (a travel grant, an unpaid museum or library residency) is caught. An applicant with a specific competing award should email fellowships@acls.org rather than infer.

2026-27 information-session and office-hour dates for THIS competition: not found. ACLS's pattern of monthly webinars/office hours per cycle is established at funder level, but no session schedule appeared on this programme's page, its FAQ, or the OFA portals page, and I had no web-search budget left to chase the resource listing. Check https://www.acls.org/acls-resources/ before assuming none are offered.

Email addresses could not be read directly: every acls.org page renders addresses as obfuscated "[email protected]" placeholders (anti-scraping). The spellings fellowships@acls.org, ofahelp@acls.org and references@acls.org come from the corpus's funder-wide layer, not from a page I rendered this pass. The FAQ does list ACLS addresses, but in the context of a safe-sender/whitelist instruction rather than as contact routes.

Whether the applicant must remain ENROLLED during the fellowship term: eligibility requires being "a doctoral student at a university in the United States" and ABD "before beginning fellowship tenure", and the institutional statement must promise tuition is waived or provided (which implies continued enrolment), but no page states the enrolment requirement for the tenure year outright.

Advancement-to-candidacy timing: unlike the Mellon/ACLS DIF, which gates on ABD status by a fixed date, this programme says only that all PhD requirements except the dissertation must be complete "before beginning fellowship tenure" (i.e. by July 2027). I found no earlier fixed ABD date, but could not confirm from a FAQ answer that none exists.
Application success rate: seven awards per year is published; the number of applications received is not, so selectivity cannot be computed.

Exact year-range and record count of the awardee database when filtered to this programme: the recent-fellows filter returned 20 records spanning 2024-2026; the full fellows-grantees database clearly holds older records but the fetch could not confirm that the program=422 filter was applied to it.
