result.deadline_pattern: Annual in intent, but the calendar slot MOVES — do not hard-code a month. Four cycles sourced from the funder's own RFA PDFs: (1) 2022 cycle — RFA open Feb 1, 2022; LOI Mar 8, 2022, 5 p.m. ET; full proposal May 10, 2022; decision July 2022; start July 2022. (2) 2023 cycle — RFA open Feb 1, 2023; LOI Mar 8, 2023, 5 p.m. ET; full May 10, 2023; decision July 2023; start Aug 2023. (3) "FY25" cycle — RFA open Oct 17, 2023; LOI Nov 21, 2023, 5 p.m. ET; full Feb 13, 2024; decision Apr 2024; start May 2024 (pulled ~3 months earlier than the others). (4) "FY27" cycle — RFA open Jan 6, 2026; LOI Feb 10, 2026, 1 p.m. ET; full Apr 21, 2026; decision July 2026; start Aug 1, 2026. Two drift traps: the submission cut-off changed from 5 p.m. ET to 1 p.m. ET in the 2026 cycle, and no Safenowitz cycle could be sourced for 2025 (no RFA indexed, and the Fellows page stops at the 2024 cohort) — so "every year, same month" is false. Stable within a cycle: LOI to full proposal is 9-12 weeks; RFA open to LOI is ~5 weeks.
result.loi_deadline: 2026 cycle (CLOSED): February 10, 2026, 1 p.m. US ET. Next cycle's LOI date not yet published. The LOI is mandatory and gating — the full proposal is "submitted by invitation only" and the LOI sits 9-12 weeks ahead of it (2026: Feb 10 to Apr 21 = 10 weeks; 2023: Mar 8 to May 10 = 9 weeks; FY25: Nov 21 to Feb 13 = 12 weeks). Two consequences applicants miss: LOI review takes "three to four weeks", so an invitation leaves roughly 6-8 weeks to write the full proposal; and "Reviewer comments from the letter of intent phase are not provided to applicants", so a declined LOI yields no feedback. Note also that the mentor/sponsor must sign at the LOI stage, not just at full proposal.
result.review_to_award: Two review stages with published durations (FAQ): "LOI review typically takes three to four weeks"; "Full proposal review takes approximately six to eight weeks, but timing may vary depending on the number of submissions." Full path in the 2026 cycle: LOI Feb 10 -> full proposal Apr 21 -> "Anticipated Award Decision: July 2026" -> "Anticipated Earliest Start Date: August 1, 2026" — about 5 months LOI-to-decision and ~6 months LOI-to-money, ~3.5 months full-proposal-to-decision. The FY25 cycle ran the same shape (LOI Nov 21, 2023 -> start May 2024). After the Scientific Review Committee scores, the Research Committee of the Board of Trustees holds "the sole authority for approving the funding of research grants", then a pre-award check for eligibility and scientific/budgetary/commitment overlap, then contracting: "Our expectation is that contracting will be completed within 60 days of the award offer. If not, we reserve the right to rescind the award offer and redirect the funds to other projects" — so budget ~2 further months between decision and first payment, and the institution's signing official must be available in that window. Unlike the LOI stage, "Reviewer comments from the full proposal phase will be provided to applicants."
result.submission_requirements:
Portal: everything goes through ProposalCentral (proposalcentral.com; Grant Opportunities tab, Grant Maker "The ALS Association"). "Emailed documents and/or hard copies will not be accepted." The PI must submit from their OWN account — "Applications must be submitted by the principal investigator (PI) through their ProposalCentral account" — an admin may be granted access afterwards but may not own the application.
LOI: project section "approximately 2.5 pages total (see ProposalCentral for character limits for specific sections)" — scientific abstract, background and significance, rationale and goals, specific aims; administrative block naming mentor/sponsor; ATTACHMENTS: PI biosketch, and "Resubmission statement (if relevant)". DEVIATION worth flagging: "PI and mentor/sponsor signatures (required for submission)" at the LOI stage.
FULL PROPOSAL (by invitation): administrative info, lay abstract, scientific abstract, "Research plan (6 pages total, not including references)" containing scientific abstract, project roadmap with specific aims/milestones/timeline, background and significance, preliminary data, design/methods, references; budget table plus justification; ATTACHMENTS: PI biosketch, biosketch(es) for mentor(s)/sponsor(s), "Letter of recommendation from the mentor(s)", and W-9 (US organisations) or W-8BEN-E (non-US), "signed and dated within the last 12 months".
Deviations from the funder-wide norm: (a) NO external reference letters — the mentor letter is the only letter required, so there is no chasing of three referees; (b) "Indirect costs are not provided for postdoctoral fellowship awards" (the FAQ singles this programme out), and a budget claiming PI salary plus indirects "may be administratively withdrawn"; (c) no institutional sign-off at submission — the signing official enters only at pre-award, to certify IRB/IACUC and other support; (d) NO appendices: "we do not permit applicants to submit data or materials in addition to what is requested… Any additional materials or attachments will be removed from your application"; (e) "Application materials that are incomplete and/or non-compliant will not be reviewed."
Budget rules: direct costs up to $75,000/yr ($150,000 total, 2 years max); fellow salary and fringe allowed; economy travel up to $3,000/yr; computer hardware/software up to $3,000/yr; publication costs up to $4,000/project; moveable equipment not to exceed 20% of the annual budget; cost-of-living increases up to 3%; unexpended funds returned.
Post-award duty that shapes the application: fellows "will automatically become members" of the Postdoctoral Fellowship Consortium, are expected to attend quarterly 60-minute Zoom calls and present at least once; reporting is semi-annual progress plus annual expenditure, final reports within 90 days.
Eligible organisations are broad: US and non-US non-profits AND for-profit/biotech entities.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
DISQUALIFYING — the hard rule is fellowship-on-fellowship, not grant-on-grant. RFA 2.3.1: "Fellows cannot hold another postdoctoral fellowship at any point during the 2-year period of the award. Any other fellowships will need to be declined or relinquished to be eligible to receive funding through the Safenowitz Postdoctoral Fellowship Program." The FAQ repeats it as its own question: "Safenowitz Fellows cannot hold another postdoctoral fellowship at any point during the two-year period of the award." Note this bites at the award, not the application — you may apply while holding another fellowship, but you must relinquish it to accept. Also disqualifying in practice: topic overlap — "Proposals with significant overlap to previously funded work will likely not be considered. Topics of previously awarded fellowships are listed on our website"; and at pre-award the Grants Policy Statement requires other-support disclosure for all key personnel, with "Association funds shall not be used to duplicate any work supported by other funding sources" and any "scientific, budgetary, or commitment overlap" described, then "resolved and/or mitigated prior to the Association's issuance of an award" (plus an ongoing duty to report overlap arising later).
PRESERVING ELIGIBILITY — explicitly stated, and unusually generous: (1) "Yes. Awardees can have multiple active grants from the Association" — existing ALS Association funding does not block you. (2) "Yes. You can apply for multiple funding opportunities provided your proposed research project is relevant to the program(s) to which you are applying" — parallel applications are allowed. (3) The Grants Policy Statement carves out a whole class from other support: "Other support does not include training awards, prizes, or gifts." (4) This is the ONE Association mechanism a junior postdoc may lead: "junior postdoctoral fellows are not eligible to apply as principal investigators, except for the Milton Safenowitz Postdoctoral Fellowship Program." (5) No citizenship or residency bar — "Applicants can be completing their research training anywhere in the world", and non-US and for-profit institutions are eligible. (6) Fellow salary and fringe are allowable costs, so institutional salary support is not an obstacle.
THE LIVE QUESTION AN APPLICANT MUST ASK: the funder's words are "another postdoctoral fellowship" and are not defined further — whether an NIH F32 (clearly a fellowship) or a K99/R00 or other career-development award counts is nowhere resolved in the RFA, the FAQ or the Grants Policy Statement. Ask ResearchGrants@als.org before investing in the LOI; do not infer either way.
Hard gate that is not a funding conflict but disqualifies just as fast: the degree window. FY27 RFA — "Individuals who received their terminal research degree (i.e., Ph.D.) or completed their postgraduate clinical training on or after February 10, 2024, are eligible to apply" (i.e., exactly two years before that cycle's LOI deadline; the date moves with each cycle). You must also already hold a postdoctoral position with your mentor's support. Drug development studies and clinical trials are out of scope for this programme.
result.program_officer_contact: No named program officer for this mechanism — the contact route is a shared inbox, and pre-submission contact is welcomed but not required. RFA §2.7 "ALS Association Contacts": "We encourage inquiries concerning this research program and welcome the opportunity to answer questions from potential applicants. Please direct all correspondence to ResearchGrants@als.org." Same address across the site (the Funding Opportunities page and the applicant FAQ both route to ResearchGrants@als.org; the 2022 RFA used the older researchgrants@alsa-national.org, now superseded). Portal/technical problems go to ProposalCentral support, pcsubmission is handled by Altum: pcsupport@altum.com (the FAQ page prints "pcsupport@altume.com" in one place and "pcsupport@altum.com" in another — the RFA uses altum.com). Practical instruction from the funder: add ResearchGrants@als.org and pcsupport@altum.com to your safe-sender list, because LOI outcome and award notifications arrive from those addresses and otherwise land in spam; application status is also visible in ProposalCentral under the Applications tab. Kuldip Dave, Ph.D., senior vice president of research, is named publicly on the How We Fund Research page but is not offered as the applicant contact. The Scientific Review Committee roster is published (the "ALS Association Reviewers (2024-2025)" list, ~35 named reviewers), which is unusual and lets an applicant see who the reviewer pool actually is.
result.examples_or_samples: No sample application, annotated LOI, or model abstract is published for this mechanism — but three concrete, funder-hosted routes exist and are better than nothing. (1) FUNDED LAY ABSTRACTS: the ALS Association's Funded Grants Database is public and needs no login (https://proposalcentral.com/Insights/8tcJbJ1-_G4=/Public/Index) and has a "Programs" filter with an explicit "Milton Safenowitz Postdoctoral Fellowship Program" entry, searchable by PI, title, institution, country, and award start/end date. What you get is defined by the FAQ: "only the lay summary from your proposal and the final summary from your final progress report will be published in our public Funded Grants Database" — i.e., funded lay summaries plus end-of-project summaries, which is exactly the register the application's lay abstract must hit. I confirmed the database and its programme filter exist today; I did not run the search (read-only browsing, no form submission). (2) FUNDED TITLES BY COHORT: the Fellows page lists every cohort 2004-2024 with fellow name, institution and funded project title — and the RFA points there itself as the overlap check: "Topics of previously awarded fellowships are listed on our website." Reading the last three cohorts is the fastest way to see what "high scientific merit and relevance to ALS" has meant in practice (TDP-43 biology, C9orf72, iPSC models, biomarkers, EEG/digital phenotyping, assistive tech). (3) FELLOW NARRATIVES: most fellows from 2014 onward have a "Researcher Spotlight" blog post on als.org describing the funded project in lay terms. (4) The scoring rubric is published verbatim in RFA §2.4.2.2 — Fit, Impact, Scientific merit, Investigator/team/environment, Budget — and the LOI is judged on only three of those ("Review of the letter of intent emphasizes fit, impact, and investigator/team/environment"), which tells you what to front-load in 2.5 pages.
result.resubmission_note: Resubmission is permitted and routinised, though no policy text defines it. Both the current FY27 RFA and the FY25 RFA list, among required LOI attachments, a "Resubmission statement (if relevant)" — so a resubmitted LOI carries a response-to-previous-application document. No limit on the number of resubmissions is published, no page limit for the statement is given in the RFA (check ProposalCentral's form for the character limit), and the Grants Policy Statement (rev. September 2025) contains no resubmission section at all. Two practical constraints a resubmitter must plan around: the eligibility window is a fixed degree date pegged to each cycle's LOI deadline (2026 cycle: degree on or after Feb 10, 2024), so a second attempt a year later can push a candidate out of eligibility; and because LOI reviewer comments are never released, a resubmission after an LOI decline has no feedback to respond to — only a full-proposal decline yields reviewer comments to answer.
unresolved: NEXT DEADLINE: not published anywhere as of 2026-09-18. The 2027 RFA had not been posted; als.org's Funding Opportunities page shows no Safenowitz entry, and ProposalCentral's opportunity browser needs a login. Do not write a date into the row — this is precisely the case the durable/solicitation boundary (BRIEF §8, CLAUDE.md invariant 3, D-009) exists for, and it is also the case the user's utility test needs the live layer to actually carry.

WHETHER A 2025 CYCLE RAN: could not establish. No Safenowitz RFA is indexed for 2024-2025, and the Fellows page (read 2026-09-18) lists cohorts only through 2024. That is suggestive of a skipped year but is NOT evidence — the fellows page may simply be behind, and the 2026 cohort (decision July 2026) is also not yet posted. web.archive.org is blocked from this session, so the 2025 state of the page could not be checked.

WHETHER AN NIH F32, K99/R00 OR SIMILAR COUNTS AS 'another postdoctoral fellowship': undefined in the RFA, the FAQ and the Grants Policy Statement. This is the single highest-value unanswered question for an applicant and must be asked at ResearchGrants@als.org.

LOI SECTION CHARACTER LIMITS: the RFA gives only '~2.5 pages total' and defers to ProposalCentral for per-section character limits, which are visible only inside a logged-in application form for an open cycle.

SELECTIVITY: no success rate, number of LOIs received, or number of awards per cycle is published ('The number of awards is contingent upon the Association's budget and the submission of a sufficient number of meritorious applications'). Cohort sizes on the Fellows page ran 4-9 per year and 5 in 2024 — a floor, not a rate.

FUNDED-RECORD CONTENT: the Funded Grants Database programme filter was confirmed to exist, but no individual Safenowitz record was opened (would have required submitting the search form), so the richness of a published lay summary is inferred from the funder's FAQ, not observed.

TOOLING NOTE, not a finding: als.org returns HTTP 403 to a plain fetch; every als.org HTML page above was read with a rendering browser. The RFA and Grants Policy Statement PDFs fetched successfully but returned unusable compressed text, so they were extracted locally with pdftotext. result.funder: Spencer Foundation (funder) / National Academy of Education (administering body and application authority)
result.next_deadline:
**October 8, 2026, 5:00 pm ET** — a real, published, twice-confirmed date, not a pattern. Confirmed on the application platform itself: "October 8, 2026, 5:00 PM ET" (naedfellowships.secure-platform.com/a/page/dissertationfellowship) and on the NAEd programme page: "Oct 8, 2026 - 5:00 pm ET" (naeducation.org/naed-spencer-dissertation-fellowship/). This is the 2027 cycle. Fellowship start: "Earliest start date Sep 1, 2027".

IMPORTANT ROUTING NOTE FOR THE INTERFACE: the recorded source URL on this row (spencer.org/grant_types/dissertation-fellowship) does NOT carry the date. Spencer's own page says only "The deadline for this competitive program is in the fall of each year." The exact date lives on naeducation.org and on the Secure Platform page. An interface that points a PhD student at the Spencer URL sends them to the page that cannot answer "when". Point at naeducation.org.

No search index was needed — both pages were fetched directly.
result.deadline_pattern:
Annual, single round. Early October, 5:00 pm ET, with the fellowship year beginning the following 1 September (~11 months after the deadline).

Two different funder statements, at two different resolutions: Spencer publishes only the recurrence — "The deadline for this competitive program is in the fall of each year" — while NAEd publishes the dated instance. Where a future cycle's date is not yet posted, "fall of each year, early October, 5:00 pm ET; watch naeducation.org" is the honest state.

NOTE THE TIME CONVENTION DIFFERENCE FROM SPENCER'S OWN GRANTS: Spencer research grants close at 12:00pm Noon Central. This fellowship closes 5:00 pm ET. Someone applying to both in the same season is working against two different clocks.
result.loi_deadline:
Not applicable — single-stage. No letter of intent, intent-to-apply form, pre-proposal or preliminary application appears anywhere on the NAEd programme page or the application platform. The full application is the only submission an applicant makes.

THIS IS A DEVIATION FROM THE SPENCER NORM AND IT CUTS IN THE APPLICANT'S FAVOUR. Spencer's research grants are two-stage (Intent to Apply or preproposal at noon Central, then a full proposal, sometimes by invitation only). This fellowship has none of that: one deadline, one submission, everything due 8 October 2026.

One mid-process document does exist, but only for those who advance and it is not part of applying: semifinalists selected in February "submit an update on their research, timeline, budget, and other pertinent details."
result.review_to_award:
Four review stages, all dates quoted from the NAEd programme page. From the 8 Oct 2026 deadline:

STAGE 1 — staff screen, immediately after the deadline. "Staff screen applications for completness and fit (i.e., research focuses on education)." [sic, funder's own typo]

STAGE 2 — disciplinary review. "Two senior scholars in the applicants' discipline evaluates the application. About half of the applications do not move forward." Roughly half the field is gone before the selection committee ever sees an application. (Note: the postdoctoral sibling runs its disciplinary review AFTER the February cut; the dissertation competition runs it BEFORE. Do not carry the postdoc arc across.)

STAGE 3 — selection committee, first cut, FEBRUARY (~4 months out). "The selection committee reviews the remaining applications in February. Each application is reviewed by two committee members. The committee then chooses approximately 60 semifinalists. All applicants are notified of their status after this review." Semifinalists then "submit an update on their research, timeline, budget, and other pertinent details."

STAGE 4 — selection committee, finalists, APRIL (~6 months out). "The selection committee reviews the remaining applications in April. Each application is reviewed by five committee members. The committee then chooses 35 finalists. All remaining applicants are notified of their status after this review."

NOTIFICATION — MAY (~7 months out). "We will notify semi-finalists in May."

EARLIEST START — "Sep 1, 2027", ~11 months after the deadline.

FEEDBACK — new this cycle: "Beginning with the 2027 applications, we are piloting providing feedback to dissertation applicants." Previously dissertation applicants got none (the postdoc competition has long given feedback "by July"). Anyone applying to the 8 Oct 2026 round is in the pilot.

PLANNING CONSEQUENCE WORTH SURFACING: an unsuccessful applicant learns their outcome in February or April 2027 — well before the next October deadline — so a second attempt in the following cycle is genuinely possible, and now with feedback in hand. Contrast Spencer's research grants, where the one-application-at-a-time queue rule makes the practical resubmission cadence roughly annual at best.
result.submission_requirements:
DIFFERENT PORTAL ENTIRELY — the single biggest deviation. This fellowship does NOT use SmartSimple. It uses Secure Platform: https://naedfellowships.secure-platform.com/a/page/dissertationfellowship. Consequences, all good news: none of Spencer's SmartSimple machinery applies. No organization-add request. No "must be received at least 3 business days before a deadline" institutional-database step. No grants-office involvement. An applicant registers themselves and applies as an individual. The long-lead institutional trap that kills Spencer grant applications does not exist here.

NO INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF. Nothing on either page requires an authorized institutional representative, grants-and-contracts officer or finance administrator to review or sign. Spencer's full research proposals require exactly that; this does not. Applications are individual — eligibility requires applicants to "Submit individual applications only."

PAGES, NOT WORDS. Spencer research grants count words (1,250–5,000). This fellowship counts pages, and the page is the unit throughout:
- Narrative discussion: "no more than 10 double-spaced pages"
- Bibliography: "max two page" [sic], appended to the narrative
- Abstract: a single-spaced paragraph
Anyone moving between a Spencer grant and this fellowship is switching counting conventions mid-season.

FULL REQUIRED COMPONENT LIST as the funder states it:
- Background: demographic data, education history, employment history, scholarships/fellowships/assistantships, honors/awards, publications/presentations, pre-dissertation completion information, language proficiency
- Personal statement
- Work plan (with timeline)
- Abstract
- Narrative discussion with appended bibliography
- Graduate transcripts
- Two letters of recommendation

TWO LONG-LEAD ITEMS TO START EARLY:
1. GRADUATE TRANSCRIPTS. Registrar turnaround is outside the applicant's control and is the classic late-October casualty.
2. LETTERS — "one from the applicant's dissertation director/chair and one from another faculty member." One of the two is fixed by role: the chair. Referees are invited automatically by the platform once named, and NAEd issues an explicit warning worth reproducing in any interface: "Once you submit the name and email of your recommenders, the online application will send an automated request to submit. As a precaution, we recommend applicants notify reviewers that the email is forthcoming and to check their spam folder if they do not see the invitation in their inbox." Recommenders are asked to address relationship, evaluation of the student, dissertation strength, research connections, and future scholarly potential — tell them that, so the letter answers the right questions.

APPENDICES ARE PERMITTED BUT DELIBERATELY DEPRIORITISED: "You may include technical and supplemental appendices (charts, graphs, tables, questionnaires, etc.)... However, be judicious, as we do not require judges to review material in the appendices." Do not park the argument there.

THE PLATFORM SUPPORTS DRAFTING IN PLACE: applicants can "save, exit, and return to edit your application until the deadline."

ELIGIBILITY GATES THAT ARE REALLY TIMING GATES:
- "Be candidates for the doctoral degree at a graduate school within the United States" — the institution must be US; the applicant need not be a US citizen.
- "Applicants must complete all pre-dissertation requirements by June 1, 2027" — note this falls AFTER the October deadline and after the April decision, so a candidate who has not yet advanced to candidacy at application time can still qualify, provided they will clear it by 1 June 2027.
- A clear plan to finish the dissertation within one or two years.

SELECTIVITY: "As a highly competitive initiative, this fellowship annually identifies and supports 35 of the most exceptional researchers conducting dissertation studies relevant to education." With ~half cut at disciplinary review and ~60 semifinalists narrowed to 35, the shape of the funnel is published even though the application count is not.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES ARE PUBLISHED, IN THE FUNDER'S OWN WORDS, AND THE DISTINCTION IS EXTERNAL vs INTERNAL. This is the cleanest statement of this rule anywhere in the Spencer/NAEd system.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES (concurrent acceptance, not application):
"Applicants offered an external fellowship (e.g., Ford Foundation Predoctoral Fellowship or AERA Minority Dissertation Fellowship) may not accept the external award and the NAEd/Spencer Dissertation Fellowship concurrently."
Note the precise scope: the bar is on ACCEPTING BOTH AT ONCE. It is not a bar on having applied elsewhere, and it is not a bar on having held an external fellowship previously. A candidate holding offers from both is made to choose; a candidate who applied widely is not penalised for it.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the carve-out that applicants most often assume wrongly:
"Applicants offered an internal fellowship (i.e., from your department or university in which only students from the department or institution may apply and receive the award) may accept the internal award and the NAEd/Spencer Dissertation Fellowship concurrently."
So departmental and university dissertation-completion fellowships, which is what most PhD students actually hold, DO stack. The test NAEd gives is a competition-scope test, not a money test: if only students of that department or institution could apply for it, it is internal and it stacks.

THE PROCEDURAL STEP THAT APPLIES TO BOTH HALVES:
"Regardless of the award, you must contact NAEd staff for approval on a case-by-case basis."
This is mandatory and it is the one piece of pre-award contact the funder actively requires. It applies even in the permitted internal-fellowship case. Route: info@naeducation.org.

EMPLOYMENT IS NOT A PRIOR-FUNDING BAR BUT IS CAPPED BY GUIDANCE:
"The fellowship provides fellows with support for the writing phase of the dissertation and to alleviate the need for significant employment." "However, the NAEd recognizes that individuals have unique needs and circumstances, and fellows may have employment during the fellowship." "The NAEd recommends no more than 10 hours/week." A TA-ship or RA-ship is therefore not disqualifying; it is a recommended ceiling, phrased as a recommendation rather than a rule.

CROSS-PROGRAMME, SPENCER SIDE: applying to this fellowship and to a Spencer research grant with the same project idea is permitted, but it triggers a disclosure duty on the Spencer side: "If you submit applications to both the NAEd/Spencer fellowship program and a Spencer grant program with the same project idea, please email the Spencer administrative contact for the grant program to which you are applying and let them know that you are also applying to the NAEd/Spencer fellowship program." Spencer's "PIs and Co-PIs may not submit more than one application... at a time" queue rule is stated for its research grants; no equivalent queue restriction is stated for this fellowship, and I did not find one — see unresolved.
result.program_officer_contact:
NO NAMED PROGRAM OFFICER, AND NONE IS EXPECTED — a structural difference from NIH that the interface should state plainly so applicants stop looking for a person who does not exist.

THE ROUTE: info@naeducation.org — a single programme mailbox for the NAEd fellowships, dissertation and postdoctoral alike. Do NOT use the Spencer programme mailboxes (smallgrants@, largegrants@, racial-equity@, etc.) or the SmartSimple support address (mgarcia@spencer.org); those belong to the research-grant system and this fellowship is not in it.

PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT IS NOT SOLICITED FOR FIT. Neither the NAEd page nor Spencer's page invites a scientific conversation, and no named officer's address is published for this competition. There is no "email the PO your specific aims" move here.

BUT THERE IS ONE CONTACT THE FUNDER REQUIRES, and it is easy to miss because it is filed under eligibility rather than under contact: if you have been offered any other award, "Regardless of the award, you must contact NAEd staff for approval on a case-by-case basis." That is mandatory, it applies to internal awards too, and it goes to info@naeducation.org.

FOR FIT QUESTIONS, THE FUNDER POINTS AT THE AWARD RECORD RATHER THAN AT A PERSON: "Applicants should look at the listing of grants awarded during past years to assess the range of topics supported... It is the applicant's responsibility to state clearly and explicitly the connection between the proposed research and the improvement of education. If an applicant can make a case that their research is relevant to education, consider applying." That last sentence is unusually permissive for a funder and is worth surfacing to students who self-reject because their department is not a school of education — the competition is explicitly cross-disciplinary (current fellows sit in anthropology, history, research methodology, sociology and more).

result.examples_or_samples:
STRONGER THAN ALMOST ANY MECHANISM IN THIS CORPUS — for this fellowship a student can read real funded project abstracts, by discipline, at their own career stage. NAEd does not release applications ("The NAEd does not make previous applications publicly available"), but it publishes the next best thing.

1. AWARDEES DATABASE, WITH ABSTRACTS — the primary resource. https://naeducation.org/awardees/ is a searchable, filterable database of fellows "since the 1980s", filterable by Award, Year, Institution and Discipline. Individual pages at https://naeducation.org/awardee/<first-last>/ carry project title, award type, year, institution, primary discipline, a PROJECT ABSTRACT, and a biography. For a PhD student this is the closest available thing to a model application, and the discipline filter makes it answer the real question — "does work like mine get funded here?"

2. CURRENT COHORT — https://naeducation.org/current-naed-spencer-dissertation-fellows/ lists the 36-strong 2026 cohort with titles and institutions. Sample titles show the breadth: "Teaching Ethnic Studies during a Complex Time: K–12 Ethnic Studies Educators in California" (UC Irvine); "Schools, Sex & Silence: A Comparative Ethnography of the Pedagogies of Gendered Shame in Lahore, Pakistan" (Wisconsin-Madison); "Causal Machine Learning with Reflective Latent Variables" (Cincinnati). Note the Lahore project: "anywhere in the world" is real, not boilerplate — the institution must be US, the research need not be.

Anyone who starts at the recorded spencer.org source URL will never find them.

4. SSRC, "On the Art of Writing Proposals" — NAEd also recommends the Social Science Research Council classic: https://s3.amazonaws.com/ssrc-cdn1/crmuploads/new_publication_3/%7B7A9CB4F4-815F-DE11-BD80-001CC477EC70%7D.pdf

NOT USEFUL HERE: the IRS 990-PF route that works well for Spencer's research grants does not help for this fellowship. EXPLICITLY ALLOWED, AS A FRESH APPLICATION: "Applicants may reapply for the fellowship if eligible. Re-applicants must submit a new application."

Reapplication is available only while you are still a doctoral candidate with a credible one-to-two-year completion plan and can clear pre-dissertation requirements by the stated date. For most candidates that means one or two realistic attempts, and the constraint closes from the far end — finishing the dissertation ends eligibility.

AND FEEDBACK NOW ARRIVES IN TIME TO USE IT: "Beginning with the 2027 applications, we are piloting providing feedback to dissertation applicants." Applicants to the 8 Oct 2026 round are the first cohort to get this. Previously a dissertation reapplicant was revising blind.

result.program_name: NASA Postdoctoral Program (NPP) — Postdoctoral Fellowship
result.next_deadline:
**Sunday, November 1, 2026, 6:00 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time.** This is a real, showable date — verified today directly on the funder's own homepage (npp.orau.org), not from a search index. The homepage banner reads "November 2026 cycle is open. View current opportunities" and the cycle text reads verbatim: "Application deadline is Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 6 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time."

After that: **March 1, 2027**, then **July 1, 2027** (same three-per-year pattern).

IMPORTANT CONTRAST WITH THE REST OF NASA: unlike ROSES program elements — whose dates move by amendment every few weeks and which the funder-wide note correctly says must be pulled live — NPP's three dates are fixed, published as a standing annual pattern, and have held for years. NPP is the one NASA mechanism where a hard-coded date is safe to display. Show the date.

ALSO NOTE THE CUT-OFF TIME DEVIATES FROM THE NASA NORM: 6 p.m. ET, not the ROSES default of 11:59 p.m. ET. An applicant carrying over the ROSES habit loses six hours. Worth surfacing prominently.
result.deadline_pattern:
Three fixed cycles per year. Funder's own words, from two separate pages:

- apply.html: "Annual application cycle deadlines for the NASA Postdoctoral Program are typically March 1, July 1, and November 1."
- about/index.html: "Annual NASA Postdoctoral Program application deadlines are March 1, July 1, and November 1."

Cut-off time 6 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time (stated on the homepage for the current cycle). The application portal is open continuously between cycles — the catalogue of research opportunities is browsable at any time, and an application is filed against whichever cycle is currently open.

Rolling/no-due-date and NOI/Step-1/Step-2 structures from ROSES do NOT apply here.
result.loi_deadline:
No letter of intent, no pre-proposal, no Step-1. The How to Apply page describes no pre-application stage of any kind.

BUT there are two long-lead items that function as the hidden pre-deadline chain for this mechanism, and both are easy to miss:

1. **Three letters of recommendation are due AT the deadline, not after it.** tips.html: "The recommendation letter deadline is the same as the application deadline. Applicants must arrange for three letters of recommendation that must be received by the cycle deadline for the application to be considered in that cycle." apply.html: "You must arrange for three letters of recommendation that must be received by the cycle deadline." Referees submit electronically through the portal themselves. Start asking ~6 weeks out.

2. **Contacting the NASA advisor who posted the research opportunity.** tips.html: "Once the applicant has identified a research opportunity, it is _highly_ recommended that they contact the NASA advisor associated with that research opportunity by phone or email." This is nominally optional but is functionally the real first step — see PROGRAM OFFICER field for why 20% of the score depends on it.

3. Official transcripts must be ordered from the degree-granting institution (self-downloaded records are rejected), which is an institutional-turnaround item, not a same-week item.
result.review_to_award:
**Much faster than the NASA/ROSES norm.** ROSES runs ~150–220 days to selection and "rarely less than 6 months" to start; NPP runs roughly 2–3 months to notification.

From applicants/process.html (verbatim):
- Notification: "approximately two to three months after the application deadline."
- Review results: "typically available within two to three months" — i.e. applicants get their review feedback, which is usable for the next cycle.
- Offer acceptance window: awardees must accept or decline "generally within three weeks of receipt"; if not accepted in that window "it will be regarded as declined and may be offered to another applicant."

From fellows/index.html (Policies & Procedures), verbatim:
- "The Fellow's appointment start date should normally be within six (6) months of the date of the ORAU offer letter."
- Start date is "the first day the Fellow will be at the appointment facility" and must be "approved by the NPP advisor."

So for the November 1, 2026 cycle: notification ~January–February 2027, accept within ~3 weeks, start any time up to ~6 months after the offer letter (roughly mid-2027), with the exact date negotiated with the NASA advisor.

Review machinery (also from process.html): an initial **center review by the NASA Center advisor**, plus "three well-qualified, external reviewers." "Final award decisions made by the respective NASA Center" — no HQ council or second-tier body. Weighted criteria: "Scientific merit of proposed research (40%)", "References (20%)", "Academic and research record (20%)", "Laboratory/Center review (20%)". Hard threshold: "applicants must receive an overall score of 75 (out of 100) or greater to be eligible."

**Pending status** — a genuinely useful quirk: "Applications placed in pending status remain eligible for an NPP award for one (1) additional cycle from the application deadline." A near-miss carries forward one cycle automatically, with no new application.

NOTE: dual-anonymous peer review (DAPR), the SPD-09D debrief/reconsideration track, and the 150-day "you may now chase the PO" rule are ROSES machinery and I found no statement applying any of them to NPP. Do not present them on this mechanism.
result.submission_requirements:
**This mechanism deviates from almost the entire NASA funder-wide norm. Treat the NSPIRES/SAM/AOR chain as NOT APPLICABLE here.**

Portal: **Zintellect** — apply.html: "Zintellect, the applicant portal, will guide you through the application process" (https://www.zintellect.com/). NSPIRES and Grants.gov are not mentioned anywhere in the NPP application material. Consequently there is **no SAM.gov registration, no UEI, no organization registration, no AOR release-and-submit, no team-member participation confirmation, no 30-day Grants.gov enablement request**. The applicant registers as an individual and submits their own application. No institutional sign-off or sponsoring organization is required.

Required components (apply.html):
- Portal profile: contact info, citizenship, demographics, employment history, publication record, education and research experience.
- **Research proposal, PDF.** Verbatim: "The maximum length for the proposal is 15 pages, including figures and citations; double-spaced; 12-point font; one-inch margins."
  - The 15 matches the ROSES headline number but the rules are the OPPOSITE in two ways: NPP is **double-spaced** (ROSES is single-spaced, ≤5.5 lines/inch) and NPP's 15 pages **include figures and citations** (in ROSES, references are outside the page limit and unlimited). Anyone reusing a ROSES-formatted document will be badly over length.
- **Three letters of recommendation**, submitted electronically by the referees through the portal, received **by the cycle deadline**. For Postdoctoral Fellows, "one reference must be from your thesis advisor." Critical trap, tips.html verbatim: "The NPP Advisor shall not submit a letter of recommendation for the applicant, even if he or she was the applicant's thesis advisor."
- **Official doctoral transcripts** (required for Postdoctoral Fellow applicants; master's optional). "Acceptable transcripts are official reports of the academic record of the student provided by the degree granting institution" and must show institution name, student name, graduation date/degree. Verbatim: "Student academic records downloaded/obtained by the applicant or by academic advisors from internal institution systems will not be accepted." PII must be redacted.
- **Exactly one posted research opportunity.** opportunities.html: "You may select only one research opportunity for the current application cycle." FAQ: "NPP applicant may submit only ONE application for ONE research opportunity per application cycle." You cannot propose a free-standing project — you apply against an opportunity posted by a named NASA advisor at a named center, and the application links you to that advisor.
- **Opportunity-specific citizenship gate on top of the program-wide one.** tips.html: "Applicants must meet the citizenship requirements of the NPP _AND_ the specific citizenship requirements included in the opportunity description." opportunities.html: "Some research opportunities are limited to U.S. citizens only, so please pay attention to the citizenship requirements listed in the detailed view."

NOT required (all standard for ROSES, absent here): budget or budget narrative, Open Science and Data Management Plan, Table of Personnel and Work Effort, Current and Pending Support, "Expertise and Resources Not Anonymized" DAPR document, 4000-character NSPIRES cover-page abstract, Total Budget PDF.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
**WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU**

1. **A prior NPP appointment inside the last five years.** eligibility.html, verbatim: "You must not have held an NPP appointment for five years prior to applying." And: "NPP Fellows are eligible for another award five years after the end of the previous appointment." The clock runs from the END of the previous appointment, not its start — so a fellow who finished a 3-year NPP in 2024 is eligible again in 2029.

2. **Competing income during the appointment** (a condition of holding the award, not a bar on applying). eligibility.html: "Fellows may not provide services for compensation to a third party, or supplement their stipends through simultaneous employment, grants, or other sources of income that compete with the fellowship." Policies & Procedures restates it: "NPP Fellows are not allowed to supplement their stipends through simultaneous employment, grants, or other sources of income that compete with the fellowship research or management position."

3. **Non-residency / divided commitment.** eligibility.html: "Fellows must commit to resident participation at an approved NASA site for the duration of the appointment, and avoid obligations that will interrupt the research during the appointment." You must physically relocate to the center.

**WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY** (the half applicants actually need)

1. **You may apply before the PhD is in hand.** eligibility.html: "You must have completed the requirements for a Ph.D. or an equivalent doctoral degree **before beginning** the NASA Postdoctoral Program (NPP) Fellowship." The degree must exist at the start of the fellowship, not at application. ABD students in their final year are eligible to apply.

2. **Prizes, honoraria, scholarships, VA benefits and sabbatical pay are all explicitly permitted while a Fellow.** Policies & Procedures, verbatim: "Awards, prizes, review panel honoraria, scholarships, Veterans Administration benefits, sabbatical compensation, and any other payments may be accepted by an NPP Fellow, provided these payments do not represent dual payment for the same activity." The test is dual payment for the same activity — not the mere existence of other money.

3. **You never age out of the program.** Passing five years from the doctorate moves you from the Postdoctoral Fellow track to the Senior Fellow track (about/index.html: "Scientists within five years of receiving their degrees are eligible to apply as a Postdoctoral Fellow; scientists who have received their doctorates more than five years previously may apply as a Senior Fellow"), which is a reclassification, not a disqualification.

4. **A near-miss keeps its eligibility for a free extra cycle.** FAQ: "Applications placed in pending status remain eligible for an NPP award for one (1) additional cycle from the application deadline."

5. **NPP is not federal employment**, which is why it does not create an employment conflict: eligibility.html, "Fellows are stipend recipients and not employees of either NASA or ORAU or of the host institution."

6. **No rule found excluding** holders of a current or prior NASA research grant (e.g. ROSES, FINESST), a prior non-NASA postdoctoral fellowship (NSF AAPF, NRC RAP, Hubble/Sagan/Einstein), or previously declined NPP applicants. NASA's ROSES-wide posture — resubmissions considered "with neither advantage nor disadvantage" — is the general NASA stance. But I searched the eligibility, FAQ, apply, tips, process and Policies pages and found no NPP statement either way, so this is NOT FOUND rather than confirmed-permitted. See "unresolved".
result.program_officer_contact:
**There is no single named program officer, and the ROSES contact machinery does not apply** — sara@nasa.gov, the SARA program-officer list, and the NSPIRES/Grants.gov help desks are all irrelevant to NPP. Three real routes instead:

1. **The NASA advisor named on the specific research opportunity — the one that matters.** tips.html: "Once the applicant has identified a research opportunity, it is _highly_ recommended that they contact the NASA advisor associated with that research opportunity by phone or email." opportunities.html adds that before applying you should "contact the advisor listed on the opportunity to discuss it."
   **Why this is effectively mandatory rather than merely recommended:** process.html gives "Laboratory/Center review (20%)" of the total score, and the NASA Center advisor conducts the initial center review. A fifth of your score comes from the person you were invited to email. Also note the clean separation NPP enforces: the advisor scores you but may not write you a letter ("The NPP Advisor shall not submit a letter of recommendation for the applicant").

2. **NASA Center Representatives — named people with @nasa.gov addresses, one or more per center** (https://npp.orau.org/about/representatives.html). Their stated role: "Are you interested in learning more about a NASA Center or facility and have questions about its missions and research?" — they "can answer questions regarding specific Centers." Examples as listed today: Ames — Penelope J. Boston (penelope.j.boston@nasa.gov), Lawrence Lee; Astrobiology Program — Melissa Kirven-Brooks, Becky McCauley Rench; Goddard (incl. GISS and Wallops) — Katherine McKee, Ellie Jeffries, Jocelyn Lynch; JPL — Sophia Hong, Rosaly M. Lopes, Andrea Olson, Jennifer Pino; Johnson — Devin Schrader, Eve Berger; Kennedy — Rachel White; Langley — Tracy May, Neyda Abreu, John Nowak; Marshall — Cindy Upton, Elizabeth Blackwell; NASA HQ — Paulette Woods; SSERVI — Kristina Gibbs. Glenn and Stennis are currently listed as **Vacant**. This is the best "who do I talk to" surface in the whole mechanism and should be linked directly.

3. **The NPP program office at ORAU — administrative questions only.** npp@orau.org for general questions, stipend, health insurance and visa/immigration; NPPtravel@orau.org for relocation and programmatic travel; NPPreview@orau.org for reviewer matters. No phone number is published on the contact page.

Timing: advisor contact belongs well before the deadline, while the opportunity can still shape the proposal. Administrative questions to npp@orau.org any time.
result.examples_or_samples:
**NPP does not publish funded proposals or abstracts — and the NSPIRES route does not work here.** The ROSES trick of browsing NSPIRES "CLOSED/PAST" selection-abstract PDFs covers ROSES program elements; NPP is not a ROSES element and is not submitted through NSPIRES, so there are no NPP selection PDFs to download. Say this plainly in the interface so nobody hunts for them.

What DOES exist, and it is unusually good for the "who do I email" question:

1. **Current NPP Fellows table — https://npp.orau.org/experiences/current-fellows.html** — the single most useful page for an applicant. Four columns: **Center | NPP Fellow | NPP Advisor | Research Proposal Title**, roughly 157 current fellows. Real entries: "JPL | Acevedo Barroso, Javier | Daniel Stern | Launching the era of population studies for galaxy-scale strong gravitational lensing"; "Goddard | Anderson, Seamus Lon | Erika Kohler | Watch Our Future Burn: Experimental Characterization of the Volatilization Behavior of Meteorites for In Situ Resource Utilization and Secondary Exoplanet Atmospheres". Titles only, no abstracts, no search or export. Its value is the **advisor column next to the funded title** — it tells you which advisors actually win NPP slots in your subfield, so you know both what a winning topic looks like and exactly who to email. 

2. **Former NPP Fellows — https://npp.orau.org/experiences/former-fellows.html** — same table form; use it to find alumni to ask for their proposal directly.

3. **Fellow profiles / "Meet the Fellows" — https://npp.orau.org/experiences/index.html** — short narrative profiles with photos and research summaries (e.g. "Maggie Weng, Ph.D., NASA Postdoctoral Fellow, studies how life survives in super salty environments"), each with its own page: /experiences/maggie-weng.html, /vit-ruzicka.html, /tara-fetherolf.html, /gabe-grell.html, /nicky-fox.html. Useful for orientation and for a PhD student deciding whether this path fits.

4. **The opportunity descriptions themselves (Zintellect catalogue, via https://npp.orau.org/applicants/opportunities.html)** — each posting is the advisor's own statement of the project they want done. It is the closest thing to a specification of a winning proposal, because the proposal is written against one specific posting.

5. **Application Tips — https://npp.orau.org/applicants/tips.html** and **Application Process — https://npp.orau.org/applicants/process.html**, the latter carrying the published scoring weights (40/20/20/20) and the 75/100 threshold, which is the honest expectations-setter in the absence of published selection statistics.

6. Career Resources — https://npp.orau.org/news/career-resources.html — mostly post-award (Fellows Gateway training, LinkedIn Learning, required proposal-writing training and ROSES review-panel service after year one), not application samples. Note the standing NASA move still applies and is worth telling early-career users: serving on a ROSES review panel (https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/volunteer-review-panels) is how you learn what NASA rewards.

**No NPP-specific sample proposal, annotated example, applicant webinar or information-session recording was found on the funder's site.** To read a real NPP proposal you have to ask a person — a current or former fellow from the tables above is the realistic route.
result.resubmission_note:
No NPP-specific resubmission policy is published — no A1/A2 designation, no introduction page, no response-to-reviewers requirement, and no stated limit on how many times you may apply. What IS published and load-bearing:

- **One shot per cycle:** "NPP applicant may submit only ONE application for ONE research opportunity per application cycle" (FAQ); "You may select only one research opportunity for the current application cycle" (opportunities.html).
- **A near-miss carries forward automatically:** "Applications placed in pending status remain eligible for an NPP award for one (1) additional cycle from the application deadline" (FAQ) — no resubmission needed for that extra look.
- **You get your reviews:** review results are "typically available within two to three months" (process.html), so a declined applicant has concrete feedback roughly four months before the next deadline (cycles are four months apart). The practical loop is: get reviews → revise → reapply next cycle, possibly against a different opportunity or a different advisor.
- **The only hard time-bar is post-award, not post-decline:** five years from the end of a completed NPP appointment.
- NASA's ROSES-wide posture, for context only, is that resubmissions are considered "with neither advantage nor disadvantage along with new proposals" and "need not discuss how major weaknesses from previous submissions have been addressed." That is ROSES text, not NPP text — flag it as the funder's general stance, not as an NPP rule.
- The SPD-09D debrief/reconsideration appeal track is ROSES/NRA-CAN machinery; I found nothing extending it to NPP. Do not show it on this mechanism.
unresolved: Whether NASA civil servants, NASA contractors, or people already employed at the host center may apply — no statement found on eligibility.html, faq.html or the Policies & Procedures page. Not found; ask npp@orau.org.

Whether holding or concurrently applying for another postdoctoral fellowship (NSF AAPF, NRC RAP, Hubble/Sagan/Einstein) affects eligibility AT APPLICATION. The published restrictions all bite during the appointment ('supplement their stipends through simultaneous employment, grants...'), not at the application stage. Not found; treat the application-stage position as unestablished.
Whether a current or prior NASA research grant (ROSES, FINESST) affects NPP eligibility — no NPP statement either way. Not found.
Whether there is any cap on the number of times a declined applicant may reapply — not found.

The claim that the Astrobiology Program participates only in the March and November cycles: NOT CONFIRMED. I checked npp.orau.org/about/centers.html, about/index.html and about/representatives.html; the Astrobiology Program is listed as a participating program with two named representatives, but no page states a cycle restriction for it or for any other center. astrobiology.nasa.gov/research/fellowships/ returned HTTP 404. Do not display the March/November-only claim without a source.

NASA's own science.nasa.gov page for NPP: https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/nasa-postdoctoral-program/ returned HTTP 404 today. The NASA-side landing page URL is unconfirmed; npp.orau.org is the working system of record. This is a tooling/URL fact, not evidence of any change to the programme — the November 2026 cycle is open.

No named NASA Headquarters NPP program manager or program executive is published anywhere I could find, and no phone number appears on the NPP contact page. Route is npp@orau.org plus the per-center representatives.

DISCREPANCY WITH THE EXISTING CSV ROW (row 7, typical_duration): the row says '1-year appointments, renewable up to 3 years', but the Policies & Procedures page at https://npp.orau.org/fellows/index.html states verbatim 'An NPP fellowship term of appointment is initially for 24 months, reviewed annually. In most cases, appointments may be renewed for up to a total of three (3) years; however, not all NASA facilities renew appointments for a third year.' Initial term appears to be 24 months, reviewed annually — not a 1-year appointment. I did not modify the file; flagging for the row owner.

Selection rate / number of awards per cycle: NPP publishes no selection statistics (the ROSES Grant Stats page does not cover NPP). The only published expectations-setter is the 75/100 scoring threshold. Not found.

result.deadline_pattern:
Annual, one deadline, mid-to-late April (2026: April 22; 2027: April 14). Guidelines and the application open about three months ahead — "Application available January 15, 2027".

The non-obvious part of the calendar is that the **reference letters are due roughly six weeks after the application deadline, not before it.** For the 2026 cycle the Program Announcement states: "To ensure full consideration, letters of reference must be submitted online no later than June 4, 2026" — 43 days after the 22 April application deadline. The NOFO explains the mechanism: "Approximately two to three weeks after the deadline, NEH will email your letter writers, asking them to submit their letters online by the date specified in the Program Announcement." Note also that NEH amended this date mid-cycle: the 2026 announcement's revision line reads "Published / Updated (amend reference letter deadline) March 2, 2026 / April 1, 2026". Treat the letter date as the most drift-prone field in this mechanism. The 2027 letter deadline is not yet published.
result.review_to_award:
Deadline April 14, 2027 → notification "January 31, 2028" (about 9.5 months) → earliest project start **April 1, 2028**, with a permitted start window running to September 1, 2029. So from submitting to legally starting work is roughly a year, and the applicant chooses a start date inside a 17-month window.

This sits at the fast end of the funder-wide norm. The combined NOFO says NEH "will notify you of its funding decision by email by the date specified in the Program Announcement, approximately 9-12 months after the application deadline", and the 2026 cycle bears that out: deadline 22 April 2026 → "Applicants will receive notification about their application in January 2027" → "Projects must start between April 1, 2027, and September 1, 2028."

Two things that bite applicants: notification "is not an authorization to begin performance or incur related costs" — successful applicants must first complete the NEH Individual Programs Acceptance Form, from which NEH sets the payment schedule. And between notification and money there is an Office of Grant Management risk assessment that re-confirms eligibility.

Review route: NEH staff screen for eligibility/completeness/responsiveness → peer review panel → programme officers add comments → recommendations to the National Council on the Humanities (meets at least twice a year) → the NEH Chairman, who "has the sole authority to make final funding decisions". Decisions "are not appealable to any federal official or board".
result.submission_requirements:
Applicant of record is the INDIVIDUAL, via a Grants.gov "individual applicant" profile — no sponsored-programs office submits for you. Funding Opportunity Number follows the pattern YYYYMMDD-HB (2026: 20260422-HB); NEH assigns received applications a tracking number beginning "HB". Federal Assistance Listing 45.160. **No budget is required.**

Hard page limits (the announcement's own table; "citations are included in page counts"; "Attachments in non-PDF format (Word, etc.) will result in an application being automatically rejected"):
- 1 Narrative — narrative.pdf — required — **3 pages**, and "Your narrative must not exceed three single-spaced pages. Do not include an executive summary, cover page, headers, or a table of contents." Images/charts allowed inside the limit.
- 2 Work plan — workplan.pdf — required — 1 page
- 3 Bibliography — bibliography.pdf — required — 1 page
- 4 Résumé — resume.pdf — required — 2 pages; must list "awards and honors: include dates. If you have received prior support from NEH, indicate the dates of these awards and the products that resulted from them."
- 5 Confirmation of institutional support — confirmation.pdf — **"Recommended at the time of application. Required in order to receive funding."** A letter on letterhead "signed by an institutional representative, such a vice president, dean, or department head". This is the only institutional sign-off, and it is not a bar to applying.
- 6 Editions/translation sample — 2 pages (conditionally required)
- 7 Visual materials — 1 page (recommended); 8 Data sample — 1 page; 9 Data management plan — 2 pages; 10 Degree conferral; 11 Explanation of delinquent federal debt.
Forms: SF-424 Individual, NEH Supplemental Information for Individuals Form, Project/Performance Site Location(s) Form, Attachments Form. On the Supplemental form, tick "Yes" for Nominating Official and enter no name.

Two reference letters, solicited by the applicant (names, emails, affiliations go on the Supplemental form; "Ideally, they should come from different institutions"). Elected officials, NEH staff and current National Council members may not write them. "Missing reference letters will not disqualify an application from review."

Where it deviates from the NEH-wide norm: (a) the **topic gate** — "The 2026 Awards for Faculty competition will accept only projects for research in American history and culture and Western civilization... topics in the history, culture, and government of the United States in any period from the Colonial Era to the present, or topics in Western civilization from antiquity to the present", restated as a funding restriction and written into review criterion 1; (b) **course-revision projects are eligible**, unusually — eligible projects include "research leading to the improvement of a single existing undergraduate course" and "research related to institutional or community goals", and criterion 4 judges the applicant "(for course revision projects) as a teacher"; (c) conditions on your day job while funded — "forego other major activities, including teaching, while holding a full-time award", "carry a reduced teaching load when working part time", "not have course overloads or work overtime during your period of performance".

Review criteria, verbatim order: 1 intellectual significance and value to scholars/general audiences "and its potential for promoting a deeper understanding of American history and culture and Western civilization"; 2 quality of conception, definition, organization, description and "the applicant's clarity of expression"; 3 feasibility and appropriateness of the work plan; 4 quality or promise of the applicant as researcher and (course revision) teacher; 5 likelihood of completion "(not necessarily during the period of performance)".

Mechanical rejection risks: NEH "will not review... applications that exceed mandatory page limits or deviate from formatting instructions", non-PDF attachments, or unrequested attachments. eGMS catches format errors but "cannot detect other errors such as missing components or excess pages". NEH recommends submitting 48 hours early and registering on Grants.gov at least two weeks early; "NEH will not grant deadline extensions". AI rule: "you must acknowledge (by use of footnotes or other marginal notations) when you have inserted AI-generated text into your proposal." NEH estimates "on average it takes sixty hours to complete an application".
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves, quoted from NEH's combined Notice of Funding Opportunity (§C.2) and the Program Announcement.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU:
- "You may not hold any other NEH individual award, including a Chairman's Award to Individuals, in the same federal fiscal year." (Repeated verbatim in this programme's own announcement, so it is a programme rule, not just boilerplate.)
- "You may not hold two or more NEH individual awards with overlapping periods of performance or in support of the same activities. NEH will not delay the period of performance beyond the stated timelines of the Program Announcement to accommodate overlapping individual awards."
- "You may not apply for activities for which you previously received NEH funding." — the bar attaches to the ACTIVITY, not to the person.
- "You may not serve as the project director or key personnel on an NEH institutional award while working full time on an NEH individual award." (Part-time work on the individual award is not covered by this sentence.)
- One application per deadline: "You may not submit more than one application for a NEH individual award at the same deadline. For example, you may not apply for a Fellowship and Public Scholars award in the same year." This is now sharper than it looks, because Fellowships, Public Scholars, Japan and Awards for Faculty all carry the 14 April 2027 deadline — so choosing this mechanism means forgoing the other three that year. If you submit more than one, "NEH will accept only your last validated submission".
- Currently enrolled students: "you are not eligible to apply if you are currently enrolled in a degree granting program."
- NEH does not fund other federal entities, and will not process awards for anyone with delinquent federal debt or who is suspended/debarred.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half applicants usually get wrong):
- Non-NEH money, including your own institution's, on the SAME project, at the SAME time: "You may simultaneously hold fellowships or grants from institutions other than NEH — including sabbaticals and grants from your own institution — in support of the same project during your period of performance." A sabbatical does not conflict.
- Having held NEH money before does not bar you. The announcement points applicants to NOFO §C.1-C.2 "for full eligibility information, including resubmission, collaborative projects, and projects supported by previous NEH grants", and the résumé instructions actively ask you to list prior NEH awards and their products. Only re-funding the same activities is barred.
- Rejected before: "You may revise and resubmit previously rejected applications."
- Collaborators: "You are eligible to apply if you are working as part of a collaborative team but seeking funding only for yourself." Each collaborator files a separate application, each judged on its own merits.
- Degree finished but not yet conferred: eligible "if you have satisfied the requirements for a degree and are awaiting its conferral", with a letter from the dean or department chair in the degree-conferral attachment.
- Other federal entities' resources: "You may use funds from, or sites and materials controlled by, other federal entities in your project."
- Employment status is unusually permissive here: the programme "accepts applications from individuals who are full-time, part-time, adjunct, and retired faculty or staff members affiliated with Historically Black Colleges and Universities, as designated by the U.S. Department of Education at the time of application." Adjuncts, staff and retirees are in scope; no rank, tenure or years-since-PhD gate. Applicants should confirm their institution appears on the Department of Education's "Accredited HBCU listing".
result.program_officer_contact:
A programme-specific mailbox, not a named officer: **facultyawards@neh.gov** — "If you have questions about the program, contact: Division of Research, National Endowment for the Humanities, 400 Seventh Street, SW, Washington, DC 20506, 202-606-8200, facultyawards@neh.gov". Worth noting because the funder-wide NOFO gives the generic research@neh.gov; this mechanism has its own address, and the programme page shows it as "FacultyAwards@neh.gov".

Administrative/allowable-cost questions go to the Office of Grant Management (grantmanagement@neh.gov). Changing a reference after the deadline: "contact program staff at research@neh.gov". After NEH's public announcement of funded projects, "you may request copies of the peer reviewers' evaluations of your proposal by contacting research@neh.gov" — the single most useful thing to do before resubmitting.

Pre-submission contact is NOT stated as expected and there is no draft-review service: neither the Program Announcement nor the NOFO offers staff review of drafts or sets a pre-submission contact date. The substitute NEH offers is self-serve: "A pre-recorded webinar will be available on the program resource page." No named individual program officer is published for this mechanism.
result.examples_or_samples:
Unusually good for this mechanism — NEH posts funded application narratives on the programme page itself, under the heading "Sample Application Narratives":
- https://www.neh.gov/sites/default/files/Women%20at%20Odds%20%28British%20literature%29.pdf — "Women at Odds: Indifference, Antagonism and Progress in Late Victorian Literature"
- https://www.neh.gov/sites/default/files/Civil%20War%2C%20Civil%20Beings%20%28American%20History%29_0.pdf — "Civil Wars and Civil Beings: Societal Construction, Reconstruction, and Post-Reconstruction in Perry County, Alabama, 1860-1875"
- https://www.neh.gov/sites/default/files/Abolitionist%20Influence%20%28American%20History%29.pdf — "The Abolitionist Movement's Involvement in American Politics, 1750-1865"
Tooling fact, not a finding: these are AES-encrypted PDFs. They download and open normally in a PDF reader, but a plain text extractor cannot read them, so I confirmed they resolve (the Civil Wars file is a real 517KB PDF) without reading their contents. Two of the three are American-history projects, consistent with the current topic gate.

Also on the programme page: a pre-recorded applicant webinar, plus the 2026 Program Announcement PDF and the combined Individual Programs NOFO — read alongside the samples, these are the four things to hand someone starting a first application.

For funded-project precedent beyond the three samples: NEH's award search (https://awardsearch.neh.gov) and the public query (https://apps.neh.gov/publicquery/default.aspx) let you filter past Awards for Faculty recipients, institutions and project descriptions.

Realistic odds, from NEH's own page: "In the last five competitions this program received an average of 27 Applications per year", "NEH made an average of 5 Awards per year", "a 19% Funding Ratio". The 2026 announcement backs this with "Anticipated FY 2027 Funding Approximately $300,000" and "Estimated Number and Type of Awards: Approximately 5 grants". Award size "$30,000 to $60,000 ($5,000 per month for full-time work; prorated for part-time)", period of performance 2-12 months full-time equivalent, no cost share. A ~27-applicant pool is a small field by federal standards — the single most encouraging number for an early-career applicant at an HBCU.
result.resubmission_note:
Allowed, with no stated cap and no penalty: "You may revise and resubmit previously rejected applications. Resubmissions are subject to the application requirements and review criteria of the current competition." Note the deviation from mechanisms like ACS PRF: NEH requires **no** statement of changes, no summary of the previous review, and does not limit the number of attempts — but it also gives the resubmission no protected status, so it is re-reviewed cold against whatever the current announcement says. Given the 2026 topic gate, a narrative written for an earlier, unrestricted cycle may need reframing rather than polishing.

The practical loop: NEH "ordinarily will not publicly disclose the contents of applications that NEH does not select for funding", but after the public announcement of funded projects an unsuccessful applicant may request the peer reviewers' evaluations by emailing research@neh.gov. With notification at the end of January and the next deadline in mid-April, there is roughly a ten-week window to obtain reviews and turn a resubmission around — tight, so request the evaluations immediately on notification.
unresolved: Whether the topic gate carries into the 2027 competition. The restriction is written as 'The 2026 Awards for Faculty competition will accept only projects for research in American history and culture and Western civilization', and the page says 'Updated guidelines will be posted in advance of the next deadline'. Whether the April 2027 cycle keeps, widens or drops it: not found. This is the single most consequential open question for anyone planning a 2027 application.

The 2027 funding opportunity number. NEH's pattern is YYYYMMDD-HB (2026 was 20260422-HB), which would imply 20270414-HB, but that number is not published anywhere I could reach. Recorded as a pattern, not a fact. (The '361391' on the programme page is Grants.gov's internal listing id, not the FON.)

The 2027 reference-letter deadline. For 2026 it was June 4 - about six weeks after the application deadline - and NEH amended that date on 1 April 2026 after first publishing on 2 March 2026. The 2027 equivalent: not found.
Whether the 11:59 p.m. Eastern cut-off applies on 14 April 2027. Confirmed only for the 2026 cycle.

Whether a named program officer exists. Only the shared mailbox facultyawards@neh.gov and the Division of Research switchboard 202-606-8200 are published; no individual is named in the announcement, the NOFO or the programme page.

Whether the 2027 cycle keeps roughly 5 awards and about $300,000. The 'Approximately $300,000 / Approximately 5 grants' figures are FY2027 money attached to the 2026 competition; no budget figure is published for the 2027 competition.

The contents and cycle of the three sample narratives. They are AES-encrypted PDFs; I confirmed they resolve and are served under this programme's 'Sample Application Narratives' heading, but did not read them, so their award year and institutions are unverified.

result.funder: National Institutes of Health (NIH) — National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS)
result.next_deadline:
TWO SEPARATE CALENDARS. As of 2026-09-18:

**ESI MIRA (PAR-27-032) — next deadline: 2026-10-02 (14 days away; submission window opened 2026-09-02).** NOFO verbatim: "Applications are due by 5:00 p.m. local time on October 2, 2026, February 3, 2027, October 4, 2027, February 3, 2028, October 3, 2028, February 6, 2029." Open Date (Earliest Submission Date): September 2, 2026. Expiration date: February 7, 2029.

**Established/New Investigator MIRA (PAR-26-121) — next deadline: 2027-01-27.** The 2026 dates (January 27, 2026 and May 27, 2026) have both passed. Full published table: January 27, 2026; May 27, 2026; January 27, 2027; May 27, 2027; January 27, 2028; May 26, 2028. "All applications are due by 5:00 PM local time of applicant organization." Expiration Date: May 27, 2028.

These are NOT NIH standard due dates. MIRA ignores the R01 Feb/Jun/Oct 5 calendar entirely and the R35 line of the standard table does not apply — each NOFO publishes its own multi-year calendar covering every cycle to expiry. Both calendars are published in the NOFOs themselves and corroborated by the NIGMS MIRA page and by grants.gov (PAR-26-121 responseDate = May 26, 2028; PAR-27-032 responseDate = Feb 06, 2029, both matching the final row of each table).
result.deadline_pattern:
ESI MIRA: twice yearly, early February and early October (Oct 2 2026, Feb 3 2027, Oct 4 2027, Feb 3 2028, Oct 3 2028, Feb 6 2029). Established/New Investigator MIRA: twice yearly, late January and late May (Jan 27 / May 27, sliding to May 26 in 2028).

Both NOFOs enumerate every due date through expiry, so the dates above are the funder's own fixed calendar rather than a per-solicitation Key Dates table that rots. Standard NIH weekend/holiday rollover applies ("When a submission date falls on a weekend or Federal holiday, the application deadline is automatically extended to the next business day"). Neither NOFO has an AIDS/non-AIDS split — the EI/NI table lists "Not Applicable" in the AIDS column.
result.loi_deadline:
No LOI, no pre-proposal, no pre-registration stage for either NOFO. Verified by full-text search of both announcements: the string "letter of intent" appears zero times in PAR-26-121 and zero times in PAR-27-032, and neither has an LOI row in its dates table (PAR-26-121 lists "Due Dates for E.O. 12372: Not Applicable" and no LOI line).

The functional substitute is a soft, unenforced but strongly advised step: contact a NIGMS program officer ~6 weeks before the due date with a one-page summary (see program_officer_contact). For PAR-26-121 only, there IS one hard-dated pre-submission action for a narrow group: an applicant asking NIGMS to extend their MIRA eligibility time window "must contact a Scientific/Research Contact (listed in this NOFO in Section VII. Agency Contacts) at least 8 weeks before submitting the application."

- Oct 2, 2026 → March 2027 → May 2027 → July 2027 (~9 months to start)
- Feb 3, 2027 → July 2027 → October 2027 → December 2027 (~10 months)
