result.deadline_pattern:
ONE annual cycle — this mechanism does NOT use NIH's three-cycle standard due dates at all. That whole standard-due-date table (Feb/Jun/Oct etc.) is irrelevant here; L-codes appear nowhere in it.

NIH's own recurring wording (Apply page): "you may apply during the application period, which opens on September 1 and closes in mid-November annually." The Instruction Guide repeats: "The LRP application period opens on September 1 each year."

So the stable pattern is: opens September 1 → closes mid-November (Nov 19 in FY2027) → contract starts July 1 of the following year. Each fiscal year's exact close date is fixed by that year's Guide notices; FY2028 dates are not yet published.

Cap: "No individual may submit more than one LRP application to the NIH in any fiscal year" (NOT-OD-26-081) — one shot per cycle, across all subcategories.
result.loi_deadline:
Not applicable — there is no LOI or pre-proposal stage. This is a negative finding established across three independent NIH sources, not an absence of searching: (1) the three FY2027 Guide notices (NOT-OD-26-081/082/083) each enumerate the complete "Application Materials" list — applicant items, mentor items, referee items, IBO item — and none is a letter of intent; (2) the 21-page Extramural LRP Application Instruction Guide's pre-application checklist has no LOI step; (3) the Extramural Application Process Roadmap ("I'm thinking about applying. What steps should I take?") lists know the deadlines / know which LRP / determine if you qualify / obtain a Commons ID / use LRP resources — no pre-proposal.

The functional equivalent of an LOI here is informal and strongly encouraged: contacting an IC LRP Program Officer BEFORE you start the application (see program_officer_contact).
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves. For LRP the governing axes are NOT the R01/K interaction — they are employer type, funding-source purity, and competing service obligations.

WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half applicants most often get wrong):

- **You do not need any NIH grant.** Repeated verbatim on the overview page and in every notice: "Research funding from NIH is not required to participate in the Extramural LRP." And: "NIH grants and university salaries are considered eligible funding sources."
- **F32 / T32 trainees ARE eligible, with an automatic deferral.** NOT-OD-26-081: "Recipients of a Ruth L. Kirschstein National Research Service Award (NRSA) individual postdoctoral fellowship (F32) or those supported by an NRSA institutional research training grant (T32) are eligible for loan repayment. There is an NRSA service payback period during the second year of NRSA support, and fulfilling LRP and NRSA service obligations simultaneously is prohibited. Deferral of the NRSA payback obligation will be granted automatically upon acceptance of an LRP award. It is the individual's responsibility to satisfy the NRSA payback obligation immediately after the LRP award concludes." So the two obligations sequence rather than collide.
- **Holding an F or K award does not disqualify you — it classifies you.** The Instruction Guide's Mentored-vs-Independent test puts "You are receiving support and protected time from a fellowship or career development award" under "Mentored Researcher." A K99/K01/K08/K23 holder applies as Mentored (or Independent if they meet the faculty tests); either way they apply.
- **Previously rejected applicants may simply reapply.** "Individuals who have applied previously for the LRP, but did not receive an award, are eligible to apply for a new award if they meet all of the above eligibility criteria."
- **Part-time federal employees can qualify.** "Part-time federal employees (4/8ths or less) who are (a) not conducting research as a Federal employee, and (b) whose funding source is from a domestic nonprofit source, are eligible to apply for loan repayment if they meet all other eligibility requirements."
- **Renewal applicants are exempt from the debt test.** "This criterion [20 percent debt-to-income] is not applicable to applicants for a renewal award." Overview page: "Renewal applicants are not required to satisfy the 20 percent debt-to-income requirement."
- **Prior LRP awards do not bar you** — awardees "may apply for competitive renewal awards if they continue to meet eligibility requirements."

WHAT DISQUALIFIES (NOT-OD-26-081 "The following individuals are ineligible"):

- **Any for-profit money at all** — "Individuals who receive any research funding support or salary from a for-profit institution or organization." The overview page extends this explicitly to "an individual identified as a Principal Investigator (PI) or co-PI in an industry/pharma-supported Clinical Trial." This is the sharpest trap: a single industry-funded trial role or an industry salary component kills eligibility even with perfect NIH funding.
- **Federal employment over half time** — "Individuals who are employed by the federal government with work schedules of more than 20 hours per week (more than 4/8ths time)." (NIH employees use the separate Intramural LRP.)
- **Current NIH IRTA or CRTA recipients** — "Current recipients of NIH Intramural Research Training Awards (IRTA) or Cancer Research Training Awards (CRTA)."
- **A competing health-professional service obligation** — "Any individual who owes an obligation of health professional service to the federal government, a State, or other entity, unless deferrals or extensions are granted for the length of their Extramural LRP service obligation." This is what catches NHSC, IHS, military HPSP and state service-payback holders: the obligation must be deferred for the full LRP term, not merely disclosed.
- **A federal judgment lien** — "barred from receiving federal funds even if the judgment is paid in full or satisfied."
- Employment at an institution outside the United States; not a US citizen/national/permanent resident by the award start date; failing the 20% debt-to-income ratio (new applicants); research precluded by federal law or HHS/NIH policy.
- **More than one LRP application per fiscal year.**

DEBT-SIDE CONFLICTS (the analogue of prior-funding overlap): loans already covered by a service-conversion program are ineligible — "Loans, financial debts, or service obligations incurred under a program where an incurred service obligation converts to a loan upon failure to satisfy the service obligation." Also ineligible: Parent PLUS loans, loans obtained for or by anyone other than the applicant, non-educational loans, loans delinquent/in default/not current, loans paid in full, loans from unqualified lenders, and "Loans that are obtained after the start date of the initial NIH Loan Repayment Program Contract." A consolidated loan is eligible only if every loan inside it is eligible.
result.review_to_award:
Roughly 9–10 months submission → notification, on a fixed annual track, and with one genuinely counterintuitive feature: the contract start date PRECEDES notification.

Key Dates table, Extramural LRP Important Information page (FY2027 cycle):
- Online Application Period — September 1, 2026 to November 19, 2026
- Supporting Documentation Period — September 1, 2026 to November 19, 2026
- Application Assignment Period — November 2026 to December 2026
- Peer Review Period — February 2027 to May 2027
- Financial Review Period — April 2027 to July 2027
- Notification Period — August 2027 to September 2027
- Award start date — **July 1, 2027**

So: apply by Nov 19, 2026 → hear in Aug/Sept 2027 → contract runs from July 1, 2027 (i.e. retroactive to before you were told). "A new LRP award is a two-year contract that starts on July 1 in the year after the application deadline." Plan employment accordingly: "You must be at this organization at the start of the LRP contract (July 1, 2027)."

DEVIATIONS FROM THE NIH NORM:
- No study section, no impact score, no percentile, no summary statement, no Advisory Council second level, no Just-in-Time, no Notice of Award. None of the standard NIH review arc applies.
- Review IS run by CSR, but against career criteria, not project science. Stages are: DLR completeness/eligibility screen → CSR assigns to an IC ("typically takes place by the end of December", visible in the eRA Commons Grant Folder) → CSR peer review → financial review → notification.
- A second, financial gate exists that has no NIH-wide analogue: "Select applicants will be notified on a rolling basis by email to provide updated payoff quotes for all loans listed in the LRP Portal," with the account statement dated "within 30 days of DLR-email receipt."
- The current NIH emergency review modifications (NOT-OD-26-114: 30–35% discussed, three tiers, simplified summary statements) are framed around study sections and Advisory Council rounds and do not map onto this mechanism; nothing on the LRP pages references them.

UNRECONCILED DISCREPANCY (flagging rather than resolving): NOT-OD-26-081 gives "Peer Review Period: February – April" and "Anticipated Award Period: June – August", while the Important Information table gives peer review February–May 2027 and notification August–September 2027. The main LRP landing table gives a third variant, Financial Review "March - July" vs the Important Information page's "April 2027 - July 2027." Treat the Important Information table as the operative one (page last updated July 10, 2026) but do not quote a single figure as certain.
result.submission_requirements:
This mechanism deviates from the NIH funder-wide machinery more than almost any other NIH mechanism. The established portal/registration/late-policy notes largely DO NOT APPLY.

THE THREE BIGGEST DEVIATIONS:

1. **NOT Grants.gov, and NO institutional AOR submits for you.** ASSIST is the only route: "All LRP applications must be submitted electronically using the Application Submission System & Interface for Submission Tracking (ASSIST)". The applicant submits personally — Instruction Guide: "Clicking on the Submit Application button will result in changing the status to show as Submitted." There is no Signing Official step, no S2S/Cayuse pipeline, no Workspace. Your research office's internal 3–5-day deadline does not govern here; your own clock does. (The institution still participates — but as a certifier, not a submitter.)
2. **Deadline is 11:59 p.m. EST, not 5:00 PM local organization time.** No weekend/holiday auto-extension is stated. No Application Viewing Window, no Changed/Corrected application, no error-correction window, no late-submission policy (NOT-OD-26-064's two-week window is a due-date policy for NOFO-based applications and is not referenced anywhere in LRP materials). Instead ASSIST gives you Preview Application and Validate Application buttons to self-check before submitting — and the Writing Tips PDF warns that "last minute submissions are not a good idea and tend to fare poorly."
3. **Registration burden is far lighter — but not zero.** No SAM.gov, no UEI, no Grants.gov registration, no six-week runway. You need only: an eRA Commons account **with a Principal Investigator (PI) role affiliated with your current institution** ("Your institution's grants office can assist with your Commons ID, roles and affiliation"). Your mentor and your IBO each need their own Commons IDs too — collect them early.

REQUIRED COMPONENTS AND PAGE LIMITS (from the FY2027 Instruction Guide — these are LRP-specific and bear no relation to the NIH page-limit table):
- Research Project Title — 200 characters; Project Abstract — 2,000 characters. Both **uneditable after submission**.
- Research Project/Activities — **8 pages**. Note: "Literature citations, images, and bibliography are included in the eight (8) page limit." (Stricter than NIH's norm, where References Cited sits outside the limit.) Header must carry name, employer, project title, date.
- Research Environment — **1 page**.
- Personal Statement — **1 page**.
- Career Development Plan — **2 pages**, Independent Researchers ONLY.
- Training and Mentoring Plan — **2 pages**, Mentored Researchers ONLY.
- Research Accomplishments — **2 pages**, Renewal applications ONLY.
- NIH Biosketch — Biographical Sketch Common Form, **no hard page limit**, "length is controlled through the SciENcv data entry format."

NEW THIS CYCLE — the highest-risk item: "Starting on September 1, 2026, the NIH Biographical Sketch Common Form will be required for LRP. Applicants **and their mentors** must complete the forms in SciENcv, obtain an ORCID iD, and complete all parts (including the NIH Biographical Sketch Supplement form) in order to certify and download a PDF copy, before uploading the PDF to the LRP application in ASSIST." A mentored applicant therefore needs SciENcv + ORCID for themselves, their mentor, and optionally one additional lab staff member — three people's accounts, not one.

PEOPLE YOU MUST LINE UP (all due by the same Nov 19 deadline):
- **3 to 5 referees/recommenders** — "a minimum of three, but no more than five will be accepted"; each letter is limited to **2 pages** and must address previous training, commitment to a research career, potential for success, research strengths and weaknesses, and an overall recommendation. Submitted via the online LRP Reference Letter Submission portal (public.era.nih.gov/commonsplus/public/lrpreference/referenceLetter.era), using instructions in the "Welcome Email" you receive when you initiate the application in ASSIST (from era-notify@mail.nih.gov — check spam if it doesn't arrive within 24 hours).
- **Primary mentor** (if mentored) — must be one of the referees, and separately submits "Concurrence with Research Forms submitted by the Applicant (Research Activities, Research Environment, and Training/Mentoring Plan)." The mentor actively signs off on your science, so they must see the final text.
- **Research supervisor** — named by ALL applicants, mentored or independent; does not act during the application, but verifies quarterly service if you are awarded; must be employed at your institution.
- **Institutional Business Official (IBO)** — certifies eligibility, employment, citizenship, salary, and "paid, protected research time"; certifies via their own eRA Commons login; assures research "for an average of 20 hours per week (a total of 260 hours during a 13-week quarter)."

A CLASSIFICATION DECISION WITH NO NIH ANALOGUE: you must self-select **Mentored Research Scientist vs Independent Researcher**, which changes which documents you file. NIH warns this "may be different from prior applications or awards. Since the Institutes and Centers (ICs) apply varying criteria to these categories, applicants are strongly encouraged to contact the most appropriate LRP Program Officer for guidance before beginning the application." Changing it later "may result in the loss of your application data."

Also select **New vs Renewal** by a hard date test: New if you never held an LRP award or "your most recent LRP award ended before June 1, 2024"; Renewal if "Your most recent Extramural LRP award ended after June 1, 2024."

THE HIDDEN LONG-LEAD ITEM (the LRP's answer to SAM.gov): loan documentation. "While loan documents are not submitted until requested by DLR, obtaining the required documentation from lenders and servicers can take several months. You are strongly advised to begin collecting these documents well in advance... DLR will notify you when to submit your loan documents, typically between May and August." You list loans in ASSIST at application (new applicants only; the tab is blank for renewals — at least one loan must be entered), then produce documentation months later. The roadmap says to start collecting "as soon as the application is submitted."

Finally: Certifications tab requires checkbox e-signature on both the Certifications for Online Applications and the NIH LRP Contract — read the contract first, because breach costs "$7,500 for each month the contract terms are not met, with the minimum penalty set at $31,000."

STALE-DOCUMENT WARNING: NIH's own linked attachment tables (Independent-Researcher-table.pdf, Mentored-Research-Scientist-table.pdf) are out of date — they still state "An NIH Biosketch cannot exceed five (5) pages" and still describe the discontinued L32 Disadvantaged Background form. The FY2027 Instruction Guide supersedes them.

result.examples_or_samples:
IMPORTANT NEGATIVE FINDING, verified two ways: there are NO published funded sample LRP applications, and the usual NIH fallback does not work either.

- NIH's samples-and-documents page and the IC sample collections (NIAID, NHGRI, NIA, NCI, NIDCD) cover R01/R03/R21/K/F/SBIR — not L-series. No IC publishes a funded LRP application or an LRP summary statement.
- **LRP awards are not in RePORTER.** I queried the RePORTER v2 API directly for activity codes L30, L40, L50, L60 and L70: every query returned total = 0. So the "read funded abstracts in RePORTER" and "RePORTER Matchmaker" routes that work for R/K/F mechanisms are unavailable here. Do not send an applicant to RePORTER for LRP exemplars.

WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS, in descending order of usefulness:

1. **"Tips for Writing a Competitive Extramural LRP Application" (PDF, 2 pp)** — grants.nih.gov/sites/default/files/Extramural-LRP-Application-Writing-Tips.pdf. The closest thing to a rubric. It names the six criteria reviewers weigh, and closes with "Common Reasons Why LRP Applications Aren't Funded": rushed application; questionable research commitment; mismatch with IC funding priorities; poor publication record without explanation; mediocre research plan or inadequate environment; weak or lukewarm reference letters. Two lines worth quoting to any early-career applicant: "LRPs are not mentored awards in the formal sense that fellowship (F) and career development (K) awards are," and "Reviewers are not asked to re-evaluate the scientific merit of your project the way a research grant application would be judged... Focus on clarity and feasibility rather than justifying the scientific novelty of the work."
2. **Extramural LRP Application Instruction Guide (PDF, 21 pp)** — grants.nih.gov/sites/default/files/Extramural-LRP-Application-Instruction-Guide.pdf. Field-by-field walkthrough of every ASSIST screen, with a one-page pre-application checklist on p.4. This is the functional equivalent of an annotated form set.
3. **Extramural Application Process Roadmap** — grants.nih.gov/funding/funding-categories/lrp/extramural-application-process-roadmap. Structured as the three questions an applicant actually asks: "I'm thinking about applying. What steps should I take?" / "What do I need to know to prepare for my application?" / "I have submitted my application. What happens next?"
4. **Extramural LRP Technical Assistance Webinar — October 6, 2026**, registration required (linked from every LRP page). Live, and still upcoming as of today.
5. **LRP video tutorials** — era.nih.gov/era-training/era-videos.htm#LRP.
6. **LRP Ambassadors directory** — the only route to a person who has actually written a funded LRP application; request directory access on the Ambassadors page.
7. **Required-attachment tables** (Mentored-Research-Scientist-table.pdf, Independent-Researcher-table.pdf) — show exactly which documents each applicant type files for New vs Renewal. USE WITH CAUTION: both are stale (still cite a 5-page biosketch limit and the discontinued L32 subcategory).
8. **Aggregate outcome data, not samples** — NIH Data Book "Extramural Overview (2011–Present)" report.nih.gov/nihdatabook/category/29 and "Extramural Demographics" category/30; plus the Extramural LRP Trends Report and Evaluation Report PDFs. Useful for gauging competitiveness; contains no application text.
9. **FOCUS Research Areas page** — grants.nih.gov/funding/funding-categories/lrp/extramural-lrp/focus-research-areas. Not a sample, but the nearest thing to "what a fundable L70 topic looks like": each IC states its FY2027 priorities in its own words (e.g. NCI restricts L70 to ESIs in data science, computational biology, informatics, prevention, cancer control and population sciences, and human-based models; NEI lists seven vision-science priorities; NHLBI lists New Approach Methodologies and solutions-oriented health disparities research, and warns that "Applications that qualify under other existing LRP subcategories supported by NHLBI are not responsive to this subcategory").

Also worth funding: **LRP Repayment Calculator** — grants.nih.gov/funding/funding-categories/lrp/calculator — lets an applicant compute the actual benefit before investing effort. Award maths: "The amount awarded is equal to one-quarter of the total eligible debt, up to $50,000, for each year of the award. To receive the maximum amount of $100,000 for a two-year award, you must have at least $200,000 in eligible educational debt at the contract start date."
result.resubmission_note:
No A0/A1 machinery at all — none of NIH's resubmission policy applies. There is no Introduction page, no 37-month window, no single-resubmission cap, no summary statement to respond to.

An unsuccessful applicant simply applies again next cycle as a new application. NOT-OD-26-081: "Individuals who have applied previously for the LRP, but did not receive an award, are eligible to apply for a new award if they meet all of the above eligibility criteria."

The only constraint is the per-cycle cap: "No individual may submit more than one LRP application to the NIH in any fiscal year." So the practical rhythm is one attempt per year, every September–November, indefinitely, provided eligibility holds.

"Renewal" is a separate track, not a resubmission, and is decided by a hard date test rather than by outcome (Instruction Guide): select "New" if "You never received an LRP award before" or "You received an LRP award, but your most recent LRP award ended before June 1, 2024"; select "Renewal" if "Your most recent Extramural LRP award ended after June 1, 2024." Renewals require a 2-page Research Accomplishments statement covering the prior award(s) — and, NIH notes, any "time breaks" between awards. Renewal terms are one or two years (new awards are always two). Current L70 awardees "may renew under FOCUS, provided their research aligns with an IC's FOCUS research area."

Because there is no summary statement, the post-review PO conversation that drives an NIH A1 has no equivalent here; the pre-submission PO conversation carries all the weight.
unresolved: Review-schedule discrepancy across three NIH pages, not reconciled: NOT-OD-26-081 says 'Peer Review Period: February – April' and 'Anticipated Award Period: June – August'; the Important Information key-dates table says peer review February–May 2027 and notification August–September 2027; the main LRP landing table says Financial Review 'March - July' while Important Information says 'April 2027 - July 2027'. I recorded the Important Information table as operative (page last updated July 10, 2026) but NIH does not state which governs.

Whether notification genuinely postdates the contract start is not explained by NIH. The key-dates table puts Notification at August–September 2027 while the award start is July 1, 2027, implying a retroactive contract start; NIH never comments on this apparent inversion. Worth confirming with lrp@nih.gov before advising anyone to plan employment around it.

NIH's own pages disagree on the number of participating ICs: the Extramural LRP overview says 'Twenty-four NIH Institutes and Centers (IC) participate', but the Program Officers table lists 26 IC rows and 27 named officers.

NIH's linked required-attachment tables (Mentored-Research-Scientist-table.pdf, Independent-Researcher-table.pdf) are stale relative to the FY2027 Instruction Guide — they still state a 5-page biosketch limit and still describe the discontinued L32 Disadvantaged Background form. I treated the Instruction Guide as authoritative, but NIH has not withdrawn the older PDFs, so an applicant may follow the wrong one.

Selectivity / success rate not retrieved. The NIH Data Book categories 29 (Extramural Overview) and 30 (Extramural Demographics) hold 2011–present award and application counts, but I did not query them, so no funded-rate figure is recorded. The linked per-year Extramural Program Data Reports stop at FY2010.

FY2028 cycle dates are not published. Only the recurring pattern ('opens on September 1 and closes in mid-November annually') is established; the FY2028 close date will be fixed by next summer's Guide notices.

No time-of-day or weekend/holiday rule is stated on any LRP web page — the 11:59 p.m. EST cutoff appears only inside the Guide notices (NOT-OD-26-081/082/083). Whether NIH's funder-wide next-business-day extension applies if a future close date lands on a weekend is not addressed anywhere in LRP materials.

NOT-OD-26-082 (Pediatric Research, L40) was not fetched. I read NOT-OD-26-081 (Clinical Research) and NOT-OD-26-083 (FOCUS) in full and confirmed their eligibility and materials sections are identical boilerplate apart from the objective, so L40-specific deviations, if any, are unverified.

WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted (200/200) before research began, so every finding here comes from direct fetches of NIH's own pages and PDFs — no search index was used. This is a coverage limit, not a gap in NIH's publication: it means any LRP guidance NIH publishes outside grants.nih.gov, era.nih.gov and reporter.nih.gov (e.g. individual IC pages or university research-office guides) was not consulted.

result.next_deadline:
**Tuesday, October 13, 2026** for new (A0) applications — see the holiday note below. PA-24-182's own Key Dates table publishes the date as "October 12, 2026 *" (asterisk = standard NIH due date), so this is a funder-published dated deadline, not a pattern I inferred. However, October 12, 2026 is the second Monday of October = Columbus Day / Indigenous Peoples' Day, a federal holiday, and NIH's standing policy is: "When a postmark/submission date falls on a weekend, Federal holiday, or Washington, DC area Federal office closure, the application deadline is automatically extended to the next business day." Applying that policy to the published date gives Tuesday, October 13, 2026. NIH does not post a per-date confirmation notice, so record Oct 12 as the published date and Oct 13 as the operative one; the point is moot in practice because the institutional (AOR/Signing Official) internal deadline runs 3-5 business days earlier regardless.

Subsequent dates from the same NOFO table: **November 12, 2026** (resubmission/renewal/revision, a Thursday, no holiday shift); **February 12, 2027** (new); **March 12, 2027** (resubmission). 

IMPORTANT END-OF-LIFE: PA-24-182 carries "Expiration Date May 08, 2027", and February 12, 2027 / March 12, 2027 are the LAST due dates in its table. Anyone planning a June 2027 K08 needs the reissued parent announcement, which had not been posted as of 2026-09-18. NIH has historically reissued the parent K08 continuously, but no reissue notice was found — do not promise a June 2027 date.

Note also (NOT-OD-26-029, January 28, 2026, linked from the NOFO): the separate AIDS due-date column now reads "Not Applicable" for all 2026-27 rows — AIDS and non-AIDS K08 applications use the same dates.
result.deadline_pattern: K series (career development) standard due dates, three cycles per year: NEW = February 12, June 12, October 12. RENEWAL / RESUBMISSION / REVISION = March 12, July 12, November 12 (one month later than new). These are NIH's permanent published calendar, and PA-24-182 uses them unmodified (every date in its table is asterisked as a standard NIH due date). All due 5:00 PM local time of the applicant organization, with automatic extension to the next business day when the date falls on a weekend or federal holiday.
result.loi_deadline:
Not applicable. PA-24-182 states verbatim: "Letter of Intent Due Date(s) Not Applicable". There is no LOI, no pre-proposal and no pre-registration stage for the parent K08.

BUT there is a functionally equivalent parallel deadline that catches people, because it runs outside the application package entirely: the **reference letters**. They are submitted by the referees themselves directly through the eRA Commons "Submit Referee Information" link — NOT through Grants.gov, and NOT by the candidate — and they are due by the same 5:00 PM deadline. NIH counts them among "associated documents (e.g., reference letters)" subject to the same due date. The consequence of missing them is absolute: "Applications lacking the appropriate required reference letters will not be reviewed." Treat the reference-letter roster as a hidden LOI-equivalent milestone and start it 6-8 weeks out.
result.review_to_award:
Follows the NIH norm (K08 October dates sit in Cycle III), but PA-24-182 publishes the exact dated chain per receipt date, which is better than the generic cycle table:

- **October 12, 2026 receipt** → Scientific Merit Review **March 2027** → Advisory Council **May 2027** → Earliest Start Date **July 2027**. About 9 months submission-to-start.
- November 12, 2026 (resubmission) → same downstream row: March 2027 / May 2027 / July 2027.
- February 12, 2027 receipt → review July 2027 → council October 2027 → earliest start December 2027 (about 10 months).

Score and summary-statement timing follow the funder norm (scores in eRA Commons days after the meeting; summary statement typically within a month). Just-in-Time is required at least 60 days before the proposed start date.

DEVIATION WORTH KNOWING — project period is IC-dependent, not fixed at 5 years: NIMH "may limit K01, K08, and K23 support to four years. Applicants are encouraged to contact NIMH if requesting five years of support." NIDDK and NINDS support project periods up to 5 years. So the award length is a conversation with the IC, not a given.

Also in force: the current emergency review modifications (NOT-OD-26-114) reduce the share of applications discussed to 30-35%. Whether they extend to the October 2026 receipt / May 2027 council round has not been announced.
result.submission_requirements:
Where the K08 DEVIATES from the NIH-wide norm:

1. **Different instruction set.** "It is critical that applicants follow the instructions in the Career Development (K) Instructions in the How to Apply - Application Guide" — not the research-grant instructions.

2. **Reference letters — the signature K deviation and the top cause of unreviewed applications.** "At least three, but no more than five, reference letters are required unless otherwise specified in the funding opportunity." PA-24-182 sets no override, so 3-5 applies. Submitted by referees directly via the eRA Commons "Submit Referee Information" link, "not through Grants.gov" — a "separate process from submitting an application electronically." Critically: "The sponsor/co-sponsor(s) of the application cannot be counted toward the three required references" — your mentor's statement is part of the application and does NOT count as a reference letter, a distinction people get wrong every cycle. Tracking is the candidate's job: "The fellow/candidate is responsible for reviewing the status of submitted reference letters and contacting referees to ensure that letters are submitted by the due date." Failure mode: "Applications lacking the appropriate required reference letters will not be reviewed."

3. **Pick the right clinical-trial variant — all three are live, all expire May 8, 2027.** Verified from raw HTML: **PA-24-181 = Independent Clinical Trial Required**; **PA-24-182 = Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed** (PA-24-182 states "Clinical Trial? Not Allowed: Only accepting applications that do not propose clinical trials"); **PA-24-183 = Independent Basic Experimental Studies with Humans Required**. Submitting to the wrong one is a rejection, not a correction.

4. **Page limits (career-development table, differs from R-series).** Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development combined 12 pages; Specific Aims 1 page; Mentor/Co-Mentor plans and statements 6 pages; Letters of Support 6 pages; Description of Institutional Environment 1 page; Institutional Commitment to the Candidate 1 page; RCR 1 page; resubmission Introduction 1 page. There is no "Research Strategy 12 pages" line as for an R01 — the K structure is different.

5. **Effort, with surgeon carve-outs.** "Candidates are required to commit a minimum of 75% of full-time professional effort (i.e., a minimum of 9 person-months)" and "At the time of award, the candidate must have a 'full-time' appointment at the academic institution." IC exceptions that genuinely relax this: NCI — "For U.S. licensed surgeon-scientists with active surgical duties, a minimum of 6 person months (50%)" (NOT-CA-21-054); NEI — ophthalmic surgeons "may request between 6 and 9 person-months (50% to 75%)"; NIA — "allows surgeons on K01, K08, K23, K76, and K99s to commit 50-75% effort"; NIDDK — surgeon-scientist effort guidance in NOT-DK-25-002. VA appointees have separate provisions.

6. **Review criteria are the traditional five, NOT the simplified RPG framework.** The word "simplified" appears zero times in PA-24-182. Scored criteria: Candidate; Career Development Plan/Career Goals and Objectives; Research Plan; Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s); Environment & Institutional Commitment to the Candidate. Note reviewers are told explicitly to weigh the letters: "Do the reference letters address the above review criteria, and do they provide evidence that the candidate has a high potential for becoming an independent investigator?"

7. **Degree eligibility is broader than "MD".** "Candidates for the K08 award must have a clinical doctoral degree. Such degrees include, but are not limited to, the MD, DO, DDS, DMD, OD, DC, PharmD, ND (Doctor of Naturopathy), and DVM. Individuals with the PhD or other doctoral degree in clinical disciplines such as clinical psychology, nursing, clinical genetics, speech-language pathology, audiology or rehabilitation are also eligible." Non-clinical PhDs certified to perform clinical duties "should contact the appropriate Institute concerning their eligibility."

8. **Award size is set by the IC, not the NOFO** (so the corpus "varies by IC" is right, and the IC table has the actual numbers): NCI K08 salary "up to the NIH salary cap per year"; NIDDK "up to $90,000 in salary per year, plus fringe"; NCCIH "K08, K23: up to $100,000/year + fringe" with research support "up to $25,000"; NEI research support "usually $25,000, but with sufficient justification can be up to $50,000 per year"; NHGRI "research support up to $40,000 per year" plus up to $1,500 travel.

Funder-wide items that still apply: submission by the institutional AOR/Signing Official via Grants.gov (ASSIST/S2S/Workspace); SciENcv-produced Common Forms with linked ORCID for all senior/key personnel (mentors and co-mentors included — start early); no error-correction window, only a two-business-day Application Viewing Window that "does not extend the deadline."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves, verbatim from PA-24-182 Section III.

**DISQUALIFYING** — "Current and former PDs/PIs on NIH research project (R01), program project (P01), center grants (P50), or Project Leads of program project (P01), or center grants (P50), other major individual career development awards (e.g., DP5, K01, K07, K08, K22, K23, K25, K76, K99/R00), or Project Leads of program project (P01) or center grants (P50) or the equivalent are not eligible." Note "former" as well as current — a completed K99/R00 or K23 permanently closes the K08 door, and a single prior R01 does the same.

**PRESERVING ELIGIBILITY** — "Current and former PDs/PIs of an NIH Small Grant (R03), Exploratory/Developmental Grants (R21/R33), Planning Grant (R34/U34), Dissertation Award (R36), or SBIR/STTR (R41, R42, R43, R44) remain eligible, as do PD/PIs of Transition Scholar (K38) awards and individuals appointed to institutional K programs (K12, KL2)." This is the half applicants most often do not know: an R21 or an R03, or time on a K12/KL2 or a K38, does NOT burn K08 eligibility.

**CONCURRENCY — a separate trap from prior funding.** "An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently." So a K08 and a K23 cannot be under review at the same time. NIH also will not accept: "A new (A0) application that is submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of an overlapping new (A0) or resubmission (A1) application"; "A resubmission (A1) application that is submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous new (A0) application"; or an application substantially overlapping one pending appeal.

**EXPLICITLY ALLOWED ALONGSIDE** — "Candidates may submit research project grant (RPG) applications concurrently with the K application. However, any concurrent RPG application may not have substantial scientific and/or budgetary overlap with the career award application." And looking forward, holding the K08 is meant to lead to R funding, not block it: "K award recipients are encouraged to obtain funding from NIH or other Federal sources either as a PD/PI on a competing research grant award or cooperative agreement, or as project leader on a competing multi-project award as described in NOT-OD-18-157."

**AGGREGATE CAP (IC-level)** — NIMH: "Applicants initially supported by an Institutional Career Development program (e.g., K12, KL2) may be limited to six years of aggregate mentored career development support." So K12/KL2 time preserves eligibility but can shorten the K08 you can get.
result.program_officer_contact:
Pre-submission contact is expected, and for the K08 it is more load-bearing than for an R01 because the IC — not the NOFO — sets salary cap, research allowance, project period and several eligibility variants. You are not just checking fit; you are finding out what the award is worth and how long it lasts.

**The route for this mechanism specifically:** PA-24-182 does not name a single scientific contact. Section VII points to a per-NOFO table, "IC-Specific Information, Requirements and Staff Contacts", at https://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/contacts/IC-specific-information-PA-24-182.html — roughly 20 participating ICs, each with its own interest areas, salary/fringe limits, research-support limits, effort considerations and named program contacts. One Center states it "does not fund investigator-initiated individual career development awards", so checking the table before writing is not optional. Caveat: the contact email addresses on that page are obfuscated against scraping (they render as "[email protected]" to a plain fetch), so the addresses must be read in a browser — I could not extract them in this session.

ICs that put pre-submission contact in writing for career awards: **NHLBI** — "Career applicants are strongly encouraged to contact an NHLBI Scientific Program Contact below before preparing an application to discuss 1) the relevance of their proposed research to NIH's and NHLBI's priorities; 2) the program most appropriate for their career stage and career objectives; and 3) to confirm eligibility." **NHGRI** — "Prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to contact NHGRI program staff prior to submitting an application." **NIDDK** — "Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact the appropriate NIDDK program staff well in advance of applying." **NIMH** — contact if requesting five years rather than four. **NINDS** — applicants "beyond 5 years post clinical training (i.e. post consecutive residency and clinical fellowship training) are encouraged to contact the Office of Training & Workforce Development prior to applying, to discuss program priorities"; NINDS also directs applicants to "use NIH Matchmaker to find an NINDS Program Officer."

Generic fallbacks that work: RePORTER Matchmaker (https://reporter.nih.gov/matchmaker) — paste your Specific Aims, choose "Similar Program Officials", get POs with email addresses plus the likely study sections; and the per-IC career pages at https://grants.nih.gov/funding/find-a-fit-for-your-research/nih-institutes-centers-offices/{IC}?category=individual-career.

Role boundaries as usual: the PO advises on fit, mechanism and resubmission; the Scientific Review Officer handles review-stage matters only and cannot discuss funding; the Grants Management Specialist handles budget/JIT via your AOR.
result.examples_or_samples:
There ARE K08-specific funded applications published with their summary statements, which is the highest-value study material available for this mechanism.

**NIAID, Sample Applications & More** — https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications — carries a dedicated "K08 Sample Applications and Summary Statements" section. Four named K08s, each with BOTH the full application and the summary statement as PDFs:
- David Al-Adra, MD, PhD (University of Wisconsin-Madison), "Targeting Donor Regulatory Dendritic Cells During Normothermic Ex Vivo Liver Perfusion to Overcome Rejection after Liver Transplant" (Forms-F) — application /sites/default/files/1-k08-ai155816-01a1-aladra-application-508.pdf, summary statement /sites/default/files/1-k08-ai155816-01a1-aladra-summary-statement-508.pdf. Note the grant number ends **01A1** — this is a funded *resubmission*, so it shows what a successful A1 looks like, including the Introduction responding to the prior summary statement.
- Annukka Antar, MD, PhD (Johns Hopkins), "The HIV Latent Reservoir, Suboptimal Immune Response on Antiretroviral Therapy, and Exogenous Cytokine Therapies" (Forms-E) — /sites/default/files/k08-application-antar.pdf and /sites/default/files/k08-summary-statement-antar.pdf.
- Lenette Lu — /sites/default/files/k08-lenette-lu-application.pdf and /sites/default/files/k08-lenette-lu-summary-statement.pdf.
- Tuan Manh Tran — /sites/default/files/k08-tuan-manh-tran-application.pdf and /sites/default/files/k08-tuan-manh-tran-summary-statement.pdf.
(Base URL https://www.niaid.nih.gov for the relative paths above.)

Verification note per house rules: contrary to the standing note that niaid.nih.gov returns 403 to a plain fetch, the page returned HTTP 200 and full content in this session when requested with a normal browser User-Agent. The K08 listing above is my direct reading of the page as of 2026-09-18, not a second-hand description.

Two caveats on fit: all four are NIAID awards, so the science is infectious disease / immunology / transplant — read them for *structure* (how the Candidate section, career development plan and mentor statements interlock, and how reviewers scored them), not for topic. And the Forms-E and Forms-F vintages predate the current FORMS-I package, so the form furniture has changed even though the narrative architecture has not.

Secondary layers: NIH's curated index at https://grants.nih.gov/grants-process/write-application/samples-applications-and-documents; NHGRI's ELSI collection covers K99/R00 and K01 but not K08 (https://www.genome.gov/Funded-Programs-Projects/ELSI-Research-Program/Sample-Applications-and-Summary-Statements); NIH RePORTER (https://reporter.nih.gov) for funded K08 abstracts, PIs, ICs and study sections at scale — filter activity code K08 — noting RePORTER holds abstracts, not full applications, for which a FOIA request to the funding IC is the stated route.
result.resubmission_note:
One resubmission only (A1), per NIH-wide policy; PA-24-182 lists "Application Types Allowed: New, Resubmission, Revision". Resubmission dates for this mechanism are the K-series +1-month dates: **November 12, 2026**, March 12, 2027 (then the NOFO expires May 8, 2027). A1 must be submitted within 37 months of the A0. Required Introduction is 1 page, on top of the rest of the application, and must summarize changes and respond to the summary statement.

K08-specific timing trap: you cannot file the A1 "before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous new (A0) application" — so an October 12, 2026 A0 (summary statement ~April 2027, after the March 2027 review) cannot realistically make the March 12, 2027 A1 date. The A1 for an Oct 2026 A0 is in practice the June 2027 or later cycle, which falls after PA-24-182 expires and therefore depends on the reissued parent announcement. Plan the resubmission against the reissue, not against the current table.

Also binding: an individual "may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently", so you cannot hedge a K08 A1 with a simultaneous K23. After an unsuccessful A1 the idea may return as a fresh A0. Post-submission materials (30 days before the study section meeting) go through the AOR, not the candidate.
unresolved: Oct 12 -> Oct 13, 2026 holiday shift: NIH publishes the standing weekend/holiday extension policy and PA-24-182 publishes 'October 12, 2026', but NIH posts no per-date notice confirming the shift. The extension is my application of NIH's own quoted policy to a date I verified is the second Monday of October (federal Columbus Day/Indigenous Peoples' Day). High confidence in the rule; no funder page states 'October 13, 2026' explicitly.

Reissue of the parent K08 after PA-24-182 expires May 8, 2027: no reissue notice, successor PA number, or continuation announcement found as of 2026-09-18. February 12, 2027 is therefore the last confirmed new-application date. Do not assume a June 2027 cycle.

Whether the emergency peer-review modifications (NOT-OD-26-114: 30-35% of applications discussed, simplified summary statements) extend past the January 2027 council round to the October 2026 K08 receipt, whose council is May 2027. Not announced.

Named program officer emails for the K08 IC-specific contacts table: the page renders addresses as '[email protected]' to a plain fetch (anti-scraping obfuscation) and contains no mailto links, so no individual PO addresses could be extracted. The table itself must be opened in a browser. Named contact roles are visible (e.g. 'NCI K08 Program Director(s)', 'NEI Extramural Research', 'NINDS Office of Training and Workforce Development').

Exact number of reference letters for the K08: the NIH-wide rule is 'At least three, but no more than five... unless otherwise specified in the funding opportunity', and PA-24-182 states no number of its own, so the 3-5 default governs. No K08-specific override was found, but absence of an override is weaker evidence than an explicit statement.

The precise reference-letter acceptance window: PA-24-182 warns to follow 'the time period for when reference letters will be accepted' but the window's start date is defined in the Application Guide rather than the NOFO, and the guide page consulted states only that letters are due by the application due date. The opening date of the window was not established.
Current NIH salary cap dollar figure was not fetched, so 'up to the NIH salary cap' (NCI) is not converted to a number here; the salary-cap summary URL is included in sources.

result.program_name: NIH Mentored Patient-Oriented Research Career Development Award (Parent K23)
result.next_deadline:
**Monday 12 October 2026** for NEW (A0) applications — but see the holiday shift below. Read straight off the Key Dates table of the three current Parent K23 NOFOs (PA-24-185 / PA-24-184 / PA-24-186), which enumerate actual dates rather than saying "standard dates apply": "October 12, 2026 *" (New) and "November 12, 2026 *" (Renewal / Resubmission / Revision).

HOLIDAY SHIFT — the single most actionable fact here: **12 October 2026 is Columbus Day, a federal holiday** (second Monday of October). PA-24-185 Section IV.4 itself says: "When a submission date falls on a weekend or Federal holiday, the application deadline is automatically extended to the next business day." NIH's submission-policies page says the same: "When a postmark/submission date falls on a weekend, Federal holiday, or Washington, DC area Federal office closure (NOT-OD-17-041), the application deadline is automatically extended to the next business day." So the operative new-application deadline is **Tuesday 13 October 2026**. NIH does not footnote this on the due-dates table or in the NOFO — it is a policy consequence you have to apply yourself. Do not spend the extra day: there is no error-correction window, so the working target is ~9 October.

Time of day: "All applications are due by 5:00 PM local time of applicant organization" (PA-24-185). Your institution's internal research-office deadline is 3–5 business days earlier.

Subsequent dates under the current NOFOs: New **12 February 2027** (Friday); Resubmission/Renewal **12 November 2026** (Thursday) and **12 March 2027** (Friday). PA-24-185/184/186 expire **8 May 2027** ("New Date May 08, 2027 (Original Date: May 07, 2027) per issuance of NOT-OD-24-113"), so 12 Feb 2027 is the last New due date under the present parent announcements.

Note on method (per house rules): no search index was used for this — WebSearch budget was exhausted at the first call. Every date above comes from the funder's own NOFO text, read directly. The plain-fetch summariser garbled the Key Dates table, so I read the table out of the rendered DOM in a browser to get it verbatim.
result.deadline_pattern:
Three cycles a year, on the NIH K-series standard dates, stable year to year:
- NEW (A0): **February 12, June 12, October 12**
- RENEWAL / RESUBMISSION / REVISION: **March 12, July 12, November 12** (one month later)

Cycle → outcome for K23, as enumerated in PA-24-185's own table:
- June 12 dues → merit review November, council January, earliest start April
- October 12 dues → merit review March, council May, earliest start July
- February 12 dues → merit review July, council October, earliest start December

AIDS/HIV due dates: the K23 NOFO table still lists a "AIDS - New/Renewal/Resubmission/Revision" column, but it reads "Not Applicable" from the June 2026 cycle onward. NOT-OD-26-029 ("NIH Removing AIDS Application Due Dates from NOFOs", released 28 January 2026) retired them; the last separate AIDS date fed the May 2026 council round. HIV-related K23s now use the same February/June/October 12 dates as everything else.
result.loi_deadline:
Not applicable. All three Parent K23 NOFOs state under Key Dates: "Letter of Intent Due Date(s): Not Applicable". There is no LOI, no pre-proposal, and no pre-registration stage.

The thing that functionally occupies that slot — and that people miss — is the **reference-letter track**, which runs in parallel to the application and is due on the same date (see submission_requirements). A cover letter is also effectively expected: NIH's reference-letter guidance says "Make sure you include a list of referees (including name, departmental affiliation, and institution) in the cover letter of the application so NIH staff is aware of planned reference letter submissions."
result.review_to_award:
Follows the NIH norm; the K23 NOFO publishes the dates outright rather than leaving them to the standard table.

For the **12/13 October 2026** due date (PA-24-185 Key Dates, verbatim row): Scientific Merit Review **March 2027** → Advisory Council Review **May 2027** → Earliest Start Date **July 2027**. About 9 months submission-to-start.

For 12 February 2027: review July 2027 → council October 2027 → earliest start December 2027.

Deviations and cautions:
- **Assignment**: "Applications will be evaluated for scientific and technical merit by (an) appropriate Scientific Review Group(s)... Assignment to a Scientific Review Group will be shown in the eRA Commons." The NOFO does not say whether K23s go to a CSR study section or an IC special emphasis panel — it is IC-dependent and not resolvable from the NOFO (listed in unresolved).
- **Triage rate**: the NOFO carries the standing language that only "generally the top half of applications under review" will be discussed and scored. Under the current emergency review modifications that figure is 30–35%, not ~50% — the NOFO text is stale on this point. Whether those modifications reach the Cycle III applications due October 2026 (May 2027 council) has not been announced.
- **Just-in-Time / NoA**: standard. "A formal notification in the form of a Notice of Award (NoA) will be provided... The NoA signed by the grants management officer is the authorizing document" — it goes to the business official, not to you. "Any costs incurred before receipt of the NoA are at the recipient's risk."
- Project period: "The total project period may not exceed 5 years." Indirect costs are reimbursed at 8% of modified total direct costs — unusually low, and a fact your research office will want early.
result.submission_requirements:
Follow the **Career Development (K) Instructions** in the How to Apply – Application Guide (not the Research instructions), plus the **PHS 398 Career Development Award Supplemental Form**. Where the K23 deviates from the NIH norm:

**1. PICK THE RIGHT NOFO FIRST — there are three, split by clinical-trial posture, and they are not interchangeable:**
- **PA-24-185** — Parent K23, Independent Clinical Trial **Not Allowed**
- **PA-24-184** — Parent K23, Independent Clinical Trial **Required**
- **PA-24-186** — Parent K23, Independent **Basic Experimental Studies with Humans** Required
All three: posted 9 April 2024, open 10 May 2024, expire 8 May 2027.

**2. REFERENCE LETTERS — the K23's biggest deviation from research-grant practice, and a scored element.**
- 3–5 required: "At least three, but no more than five, reference letters are required unless otherwise specified in the funding opportunity."
- Submitted by the referee, not by you, and not through Grants.gov: "Reference letters are submitted directly through the eRA Commons Submit Referee Information link and not through Grants.gov" (PA-24-185). "Referees DO NOT need to login to eRA Commons."
- Deadline: "Referees must submit reference letters through the eRA Commons by the application due date." Same 12/13 October 2026 date.
- **Your mentor does not count**: "The sponsor/co-sponsor(s) of the application cannot be counted toward the three required references."
- Fatal if short: "Applications lacking the appropriate required reference letters will not be reviewed."
- You must chase them: "The fellow/candidate is responsible for reviewing the status of submitted reference letters and contacting referees to ensure that letters are submitted by the due date." You can see status but not content.
- Give referees: your eRA Commons username, your name exactly as it appears in Commons, and the NOFO number. NIH publishes a ready-made handout — "Instructions for Career Development Applicant Referees (DOCX, 17 KB) - Updated November 2024".
- They are **scored**: under the Candidate criterion, reviewers ask "Do the reference letters address the above review criteria, and do they provide evidence that the candidate has a high potential for becoming an independent investigator."

**3. PAGE LIMITS — the trap is that the research plan is not separate.**
- **Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development AND Research Strategy = 12 pages for both attachments COMBINED.** Budget these against each other; there is no separate 12-page Research Strategy.
- Specific Aims 1; Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research 1; Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-mentor(s) 6; Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants 6; Description of Institutional Environment 1; Institutional Commitment to the Candidate's Research Career Development 1; Introduction (resubmission) 1.

**4. NO MULTIPLE PIs.** "Multiple PDs/PIs are not allowed."

**5. MENTOR STATEMENT — four mandated elements plus an effort pledge.** Name a primary mentor (co-mentors optional). "The mentor should have sufficient independent research support to cover the costs of the proposed research project in excess of the allowable costs of this award." Must "Include a statement that the candidate will commit at least 9 person months (75% of full-time professional effort)". The statement must provide "1) information on his/her research qualifications and previous experience as a research supervisor; 2) a plan that describes the nature of the supervision and mentoring...; 3) a plan for career progression for the candidate to move from the mentored stage... to independent research investigator status...; and 4) a plan for monitoring the candidate's research, publications, and progression towards independence."

**6. INSTITUTIONAL COMMITMENT — one sentence decides it.** "It should be clear that the institutional commitment to the candidate is not contingent upon receipt of this career award." Plus assurances of protected effort, office and lab space. Signed off by the institution, and at time of award "the candidate must have a full-time appointment at the academic institution."

**7. TIMING OF CLINICAL TRAINING — you may apply before you finish.** "Candidates also must have completed their clinical training, including specialty and, if applicable, subspecialty training prior to receiving an award. However, candidates may submit an application prior to the completion of clinical training." This is what makes the K23 reachable from senior fellowship.

**8. EFFORT.** "Candidates are required to commit a minimum of 75% of full-time professional effort (i.e., a minimum of 9 person-months)". VA caveat: "Candidates who have VA appointments may not consider part of the VA effort toward satisfying the full time requirement... should contact the staff person in the relevant Institute or Center prior to preparing an application." Post-award adjustments exist via NOT-OD-18-156 / NIH GPS 12.3.6.4.

**9. YOU MUST READ THE IC TABLE — K23 terms are set by the institute, not the parent NOFO.** "Because of the differences in individual Institute and Center (IC) program requirements for this NOFO, prospective applicants MUST consult the Table of IC-Specific Information, Requirements, and Staff Contacts." Live examples from that table: salary cap NHLBI up to $100,000/yr + fringe; NINDS up to $125,000 + fringe; NIDDK up to $90,000; NCCIH K23 up to $100,000; NIA $100,000. Research expenses: NHLBI $30,000 (up to $50,000 with strong justification); NCCIH $25,000; NEI "usually $25,000, but with sufficient justification can be up to $50,000". Surgeon carve-outs on the 75% rule: NIA "allows surgeons on K01, K08, K23, K76, and K99s to commit 50–75% effort"; NEI "ophthalmic surgeons may request between 6 and 9 person-months (50% to 75%)"; NHLBI "applicants in medical specialties requiring significant clinical activity may request a reduced research 6 person-months (50%) effort." Career-stage gates: NIBIB supports K awards only for "junior faculty who are within 10 years of obtaining their Ph.D., fellowship or residency. Individuals with postdoctoral appointments are not eligible to apply." Cumulative caps: "NHLBI limits cumulative support on individual mentored K awards to 8 years for K08 and K23 awardees."

**10. Other:** Data Management and Sharing Plan required; RCR plan required; F&A at 8% of MTDC; "Salary for mentors, secretarial and administrative assistants, etc. is not allowed."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves, quoted verbatim from PA-24-185 Section III.1 (identical in PA-24-184 and PA-24-186):

**DISQUALIFYING — the award kills eligibility whether you hold it now or held it in the past:**
"Current and former PDs/PIs on NIH research project (R01), program project (P01), center grants (P50), Project Leads of program project (P01), or center grants (P50), other major individual career development awards (e.g., K01, K07, K08, K22, K23, K25, K76, K99/R00), or the equivalent are not eligible."
Note the two teeth: (a) **"current and former"** — a finished R01 disqualifies you as surely as an active one; (b) **Project Lead on a P01 or P50 counts**, which catches people who never thought of themselves as a PI. And one mentored K is one per career — a prior K08 or K01 blocks a K23.

**PRESERVING — the carve-outs, which are broad and which most applicants underuse:**
"Current and former PDs/PIs of an NIH Small Grant (R03), Exploratory/Developmental Grants (R21/R33), Planning Grant (R34/U34), Dissertation Award (R36), or SBIR/STTR (R41, R42, R43, R44) remain eligible, as do PD/PIs of Transition Scholar (K38) awards and individuals appointed to institutional K programs (K12, KL2)."
So: an R21 or R03 of your own, a dissertation R36, a K38, or a slot on your institution's K12/KL2 or CTSA KL2 all leave your K23 eligibility intact. The K12/KL2 → K23 path is a normal, sanctioned career sequence, not a loophole.

**WHILE THE K23 IS PENDING — you may keep applying for research grants:**
"Candidates may submit research project grant (RPG) applications concurrently with the K application. However, any concurrent RPG application may not have substantial scientific and/or budgetary overlap with the career award application."
But you may not double up on career awards: "An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently." So a K23 and a K08 cannot be in review at the same time.

**AFTER THE K23 IS AWARDED — winning an R01 is the goal, not a violation:**
"K award recipients are encouraged to obtain funding from NIH or other Federal sources either as a PD/PI on a competing research grant award or cooperative agreement, or as project leader on a competing multi-project award as described in NOT-OD-18-157." Under that notice ("Career Award (K) Policy Update: Concurrent Support from a Mentored K Award and a Research Grant", released 6 April 2018), mentored K awardees "may request to reduce effort on the K award in the final two years of the award when they compete successfully as PD/PI for peer-reviewed research awards"; "NIH will adjust the total salary support committed to the K award consistent with the adjusted level of effort"; but "NIH will continue to provide full research development support costs... as indicated on the original Notice of Award." Prior approval from the awarding IC is required.

**OTHER NON-FUNDING GATES:** health-professional doctoral degree — "the MD, DO, DDS, DMD, OD, DC, PharmD, ND (Doctor of Naturopathy), as well as a doctoral degree in nursing research or practice. Individuals with the PhD or other doctoral degree in clinical disciplines such as clinical psychology, nursing, clinical genetics, speech-language pathology, audiology or rehabilitation are also eligible. Individuals holding the PhD in a non-clinical discipline but who are certified to perform clinical duties should contact the appropriate Institute concerning their eligibility." US citizen, non-citizen national, or permanent resident **by the time of award** (not at submission).

result.examples_or_samples:
There is exactly one publicly posted **K23** application sample in NIH's own indexed collections, and it is the right one to read.

**1. NIAID K23 sample + summary statement (the only K23-specific one found):**
DeAnna Friedman-Klabanoff, M.D., University of Maryland, Baltimore — "Serological markers of natural immunity to Plasmodium falciparum infection" (Forms-F). Listed at https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications under "K23 Sample Applications and Summary Statements".
- Summary statement PDF: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/sites/default/files/k23-ai155838-01a1_friedman-klabanoff_summary-statement.pdf
- Teachable detail hiding in the filename: the grant number is **K23 AI155838-01A1** — the posted exemplar is a funded **resubmission**, so you are reading what an A1 that worked looks like.
- **Caveat, verified not assumed**: on the live page the "Full Application" text for this row is **not a hyperlink** — only the summary statement PDF is downloadable. I checked the row's DOM directly; every other sample row on the page carries a linked "Full Application PDF" and this one does not. NIAID's own banner explains the decay: "Due to current HHS and NIH restructuring, some content on niaid.nih.gov is not being updated regularly." Page last reviewed 8 September 2025.
- Method note per house rules: **niaid.nih.gov returns HTTP 403 to a plain fetch.** I read this page in a rendering browser, so the contents above are my direct reading of the live page, not NIH's description of it. The adjacent K08 and K01 collections (Al-Adra, Antar, Lu, Tran; Ross, Ambroggio, Rebeiro) are the nearest structural analogues if you want more mentored-K examples with their summary statements.

**2. Checked and negative — do not waste time here:** NIA's sample page (https://www.nia.nih.gov/research/training/sample-applications) carries only F99/K00 and K99/R00 pairs plus a Katz R01 attachment — **no K23**. NHGRI's ELSI collection covers K99/R00 and K01 — no K23. The NCI collections (Behavioral, Cancer Epidemiology, Implementation Science, Healthcare Delivery) and NIDCD are R-series only. NIH's own index is at https://grants.nih.gov/grants-process/write-application/samples-applications-and-documents. (NIA returned HTTP 405 to a plain fetch; read via browser.)

**3. Funded K23 abstracts and Specific Aims at scale — RePORTER.** https://reporter.nih.gov/advanced-search has an explicit **Activity Code** field: set it to K23 (optionally with an IC code and fiscal year) to get every funded K23 with abstract, PI, institute, study section, amount, and resulting publications. The same form exposes **Study Section** and **Program Officer** fields, so you can see which panel reviewed K23s in your area and who the POs are. Data as of 13 September 2026. RePORTER holds no full applications — for those, a FOIA request to the funding IC.

**4. Matchmaker** — https://reporter.nih.gov/matchmaker — paste your Specific Aims and get back similar funded projects, their program officials with email addresses, ICs and review panels. This is the fastest way to answer "which institute should my K23 go to" before you email anyone.

**5. Materials to hand your referees and mentor, today:** NIH's "Instructions for Career Development Applicant Referees (DOCX, 17 KB) - Updated November 2024", from https://grants.nih.gov/grants-process/write-application/advice-on-application-sections/reference-letters. Send it with your Commons username, your name as it appears in Commons, and the NOFO number the day you decide to apply.
result.resubmission_note:
Standard NIH single-A1 rule applies, with three K23-specific wrinkles that bite.

- **Next resubmission date: Thursday 12 November 2026** (no holiday shift; Veterans Day is 11 November), then 12 March 2027. Resubmissions are one month after the corresponding new date.
- **One only.** A single A1; 37 months from the A0 it follows; Introduction limited to **1 page** per the K page-limits table; after an unsuccessful A1 the idea may return as a fresh A0.
- **WRINKLE 1 — you must get brand-new reference letters.** "Resubmission applications do not need to use the same list of referees but do require new reference letters from all referees chosen." Letters do not carry over from the A0. This is the most common way a K23 resubmission dies before review, because the candidate assumes the file is still on record. Re-brief your referees the moment you decide to resubmit, and remember the mentor still cannot be one of the three.
- **WRINKLE 2 — you cannot jump the queue.** NIH "will not accept... A resubmission (A1) application that is submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous new (A0) application", nor "A new (A0) application that is submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of an overlapping new (A0) or resubmission (A1) application." With summary statements currently released later in the council round, an A0 submitted 12 October 2026 (reviewed March 2027) may not have its summary statement in hand in time for the 12 March 2027 resubmission date — plan for 12 July 2027 and confirm with your PO.
- **WRINKLE 3 — no parallel career applications.** "An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently." You cannot hedge a K23 A1 with a K08 A0.
- Also: "An application that has substantial overlap with another application pending appeal of initial peer review" is not accepted. And you may still run an RPG application alongside, provided it has no "substantial scientific and/or budgetary overlap with the career award application."
- Worth knowing: resubmission is the norm, not the exception, at this mechanism — NIAID's single posted K23 exemplar (K23 AI155838-**01A1**) is itself a funded A1, and NIA's posted K-award pairs are explicitly "initial submissions and subsequent resubmissions of applications from applicants who received an excellent score and were funded upon resubmission."
- After the summary statement, the Program Officer — not the SRO — is who you ask whether an A1 is worth it.

Derivation (every step from a funder source, no guessing): the current Parent K25 NOFOs publish their own Key Dates table, and the next New row after today (2026-09-18) reads "October 12, 2026 *" (asterisk = NIH standard due date). But October 12, 2026 is a Monday and is Columbus Day, a US federal holiday (OPM 2026 federal holiday schedule). Next business day = Tuesday, October 13, 2026. NIH's standard-due-dates page adds: "Grant applications and associated documents (e.g., reference letters) are due by 5:00 PM local time of applicant organization on the specified due date."

NOTE ON THE DATED-DEADLINE QUESTION: a date is safe to record here, and I have recorded it. This is not a scraped per-solicitation date that rots. The full recurring calendar is printed inside the NOFO itself, through the NOFO's own expiration, and it matches NIH's permanent K-series standard dates. What follows is the remaining published run, verbatim from PA-24-191's Key Dates table:

| New | Renewal/Resub/Revision | Merit review | Council | Earliest start |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 12, 2026 * (→ Oct 13, holiday) | Nov 12, 2026 * | March 2027 | May 2027 | July 2027 |
| Feb 12, 2027 * (Friday) | Mar 12, 2027 * (Friday) | July 2027 | October 2027 | December 2027 |

Nov 12, 2026 is a Thursday and is NOT a holiday (Veterans Day 2026 falls Wed Nov 11), so the resubmission date stands as printed.

HARD STOP: **February 12, 2027 is the last new-application date under the current parent NOFOs.** Both PA-24-191 and PA-24-190 carry "Expiration Date: May 08, 2027." A June 2027 or later K25 submission depends on a reissue that has not been announced. Anyone planning a 2027 K25 should treat Feb 12, 2027 as the last certain window and ask their PO about the reissue.
