result.deadline_pattern:
K-series NIH standard due dates, three cycles a year, stable year to year:
- NEW (A0): **February 12, June 12, October 12**
- RESUBMISSION / renewal / revision (A1): **March 12, July 12, November 12** — exactly one month after the corresponding new date.

Confirmed on NIH's standard-due-dates table ("K series | new | Research Career Development | February 12 | June 12 | October 12") and reproduced row-by-row inside PA-24-191's own Key Dates table, so the NOFO does not deviate from the funder norm on cadence.

Always check the printed date against the calendar: the weekend/holiday auto-extension is what makes the nominal date wrong roughly one cycle in six. October 12 is the exposed one — it collides with Columbus Day whenever it lands on the second Monday (2026, 2032, ...).
result.loi_deadline:
Not applicable. PA-24-191 and PA-24-190 both print "Letter of Intent Due Date(s): Not Applicable". There is no LOI, no pre-proposal and no pre-registration gate on the K25 — the full application is the first thing NIH sees.

Two things that are NOT an LOI but do function as real pre-deadline milestones, and are easy to mistake for "nothing to do until the deadline":
1. **Reference letters must be in eRA Commons by the same 5:00 PM deadline**, submitted by the referees themselves, through a channel you do not control. Functionally this is your LOI-equivalent long lead.
2. **A cover-letter list of your referees.** NIH: "Make sure you include a list of referees (including name, departmental affiliation, and institution) in the cover letter of the application so NIH staff is aware of planned reference letter submissions."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, quoted verbatim from PA-24-191 Section III.1.

**DISQUALIFYING — you are not eligible if you are a current or former PD/PI on:**
"Current and former PDs/PIs on NIH research project (R01), program project (P01), center grants (P50), Project Leads of program project (P01), or center grants (P50), other major individual career development awards (e.g., K01, K07, K08, K22, K23, K25, K76, K99/R00), or the equivalent are not eligible."
Read "or the equivalent" as including non-NIH independent awards of comparable scale — that judgement call belongs to the IC program officer, not to you.

**PRESERVING — these do NOT disqualify you:**
"Current and former PDs/PIs of an NIH Small Grant (R03), Exploratory/Developmental Grants (R21/R33), Planning Grant (R34/U34), Dissertation Award (R36), or SBIR/STTR (R41, R42, R43, R44) remain eligible, as do PD/PIs of Transition Scholar (K38) awards and individuals appointed to institutional K programs (K12, KL2)."
So: an R21 of your own, an R03, an SBIR, or a slot on your institution's K12/KL2 all leave your K25 eligibility intact. For a quantitative scientist this matters a lot — NSF/DOE/industry funding is not on the exclusion list at all, and a prior R21 as PI is explicitly fine.

**CONCURRENT APPLICATIONS — three separate rules, all K-specific:**
- "An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently." You cannot hedge a K25 against a K01 in the same cycle.
- "Candidates may submit research project grant (RPG) applications concurrently with the K application. However, any concurrent RPG application may not have substantial scientific and/or budgetary overlap with the career award application." A concurrent R21 is allowed if it is genuinely distinct work.
- "K award recipients are encouraged to obtain funding from NIH or other Federal sources either as a PD/PI on a competing research grant award or cooperative agreement, or as project leader on a competing multi-project award as described in NOT-OD-18-157." Once you hold the K25, winning an R01 is encouraged, not penalised — the exclusion is a gate at entry, not a ceiling during the award.
- Overlap bar: no new A0 before the summary statement from an overlapping A0/A1 issues; no A1 before the previous A0's summary statement issues; nothing with substantial overlap with an application under appeal.

**IC-LEVEL RESTRICTIONS THAT OVERRIDE THE PARENT — check before you write a word.** The parent says the K25 is for investigators "at any level of experience, from the postdoctoral level to senior faculty level." Two ICs narrow that:
- **NIBIB**: "NIBIB supports the following career development awards for junior faculty who are within 10 years of obtaining their Ph.D., fellowship or residency. **Individuals with postdoctoral appointments are not eligible to apply**" — and K25 is on that list. A postdoc cannot apply to NIBIB for a K25 at all, despite the parent NOFO's wording.
- **NHLBI**: "NHLBI limits cumulative support on individual mentored K awards to 8 years for K08 and K23 awardees and 6 years for K01 and K25 awardees."
- Project period is capped at 5 years by the parent ("The total project period may not exceed 5 years"), but **NIBIB caps K25 at 4 years** and NIDCR/NHLBI run 3–5.

**CITIZENSHIP**: "By the time of award, the individual must be a citizen or a non-citizen national of the United States or have been lawfully admitted for permanent residence." By the time of AWARD, not of application — a green card in progress is workable; a visa is not.

**Not a prior-funding rule but the same kind of trap**: "At the time of award, the candidate must have a full-time appointment at the academic institution," minimum 75% effort / 9 person-months. Multiple PDs/PIs are not allowed.
result.submission_requirements:
Machinery (Grants.gov/ASSIST/S2S, eRA Commons, SAM/UEI, ORCID, SciENcv Common Forms, the 5 PM rule, no error-correction window) is the NIH-wide norm and is not re-derived here. Where the K25 DEVIATES:

**1. REFERENCE LETTERS — the single biggest deviation, and the one that kills applications.**
The K25 activity-code page: reference letters "Required (min 3, max 5)". PA-24-191: "Applications lacking the appropriate required reference letters will not be reviewed. This is a separate process from submitting an application electronically. Reference letters are submitted directly through the eRA Commons Submit Referee Information link and not through Grants.gov."
NIH's reference-letters page adds the details that trip people:
- "At least three, but no more than five, reference letters are required unless otherwise specified in the funding opportunity."
- "Referees must submit these letters by the application deadline in order to be considered with the application. Applications that have fewer than the required numbers of reference letters will not be reviewed." Same 5 PM deadline as the application.
- "The letters should be from individuals not directly involved in the application, but who are familiar with the fellow/candidate's qualifications, training, and interests."
- **"The sponsor/co-sponsor(s) of the application cannot be counted toward the three required references."** Your K25 mentor does NOT count. Their mentor statement is a separate, required, 6-page component.
- "Referees DO NOT need to login to eRA Commons to submit their letters." Give each referee: your eRA Commons username, your name exactly as it appears in Commons, and the NOFO number (PA-24-191 or PA-24-190). Both of you get confirmation emails; you can see whether a letter arrived but never its contents.
- A ready-made handout exists: "Instructions for Career Development Applicant Referees (DOCX, 17 KB) - Updated November 2024", on the reference-letters page. Send it with your ask.
- Reference letters are SCORED, inside the Candidate criterion: "Do the reference letters address the above review criteria, and do they provide evidence that the candidate has a high potential for becoming an independent investigator."

**2. PAGE LIMITS — the K table, not the R table.** From NIH's page-limits table, "For Individual Career Development Award (K, excluding K12) Applications Including K01, ... K25, ...":
- **Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development and Research Strategy — 12 pages for both attachments combined.** This is the number people get wrong. It is not 12 pages of science plus a separate candidate section; the two share one 12-page budget, so every page of career narrative is a page of science you don't get.
- Specific Aims 1 page · Project Summary/Abstract 30 lines · Project Narrative three sentences · Introduction to Resubmission 1 page · Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research 1 page · Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-mentor(s) 6 pages · Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants 6 pages · Description of Institutional Environment 1 page · Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development 1 page · Biosketch legacy 5 pages, Common Form "No hard limit; length controlled through SciENcv data entry format".

**3. PHS 398 CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD SUPPLEMENTAL FORM** — an extra form the R-series never touches. Sections: Candidate; Research Plan; Other Candidate Information; Mentor, Co-Mentor, Consultant, Collaborators; Environment & Institutional Commitment to the Candidate; Other Research Plan Sections; Appendix.

**4. THE K25-SPECIFIC CANDIDATE NARRATIVE.** The NOFO asks you to do something no other K asks: document a quantitative track record *outside* biomedicine and then argue the bridge. Verbatim: describe accomplishments "including any publications that demonstrate the candidate's experience and interest in pursuing research (including research outside of biomedicine, behavior, bioimaging, or bioengineering). Provide a description of the candidate's commitment to a career in quantitative biomedical, bioimaging, behavioral, or bioengineering research that is relevant to the NIH mission." A pure-math or pure-CS publication record is an asset here, not a liability.

**5. THE MENTOR MUST BE FUNDED.** "The mentor should have sufficient independent research support to cover the costs of the proposed research project in excess of the allowable costs of this award." Plus a mentor statement covering: research qualifications and prior supervisory experience; the nature of the supervision; and a written commitment that you will devote at least 9 person-months (75%) to the program. Choose a mentor with active R01-scale support, and check it before you ask.

**6. SIGNED STATEMENTS, NOT JUST LETTERS.** "Signed statements must be provided by all collaborators and/or consultants confirming their participation in the project and describing their specific roles." Same for every advisory committee member if you propose one.

**7. INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF IS SUBSTANTIVE, NOT CLERICAL.** Two separate 1-page attachments — Description of Institutional Environment, and Institutional Commitment. The commitment statement must make clear "that the institutional commitment to the candidate is not contingent upon receipt of this career award," and must guarantee the 75%/9-person-month protection. Your department chair has to write and sign this. Start that conversation months out; it is the component most often still missing the week of the deadline.

**8. RCR PLAN REQUIRED** (1 page) — "All applications must include a plan to fulfill NIH requirements for instruction in the Responsible Conduct of Research."

**9. CHOOSING BETWEEN THE TWO LIVE NOFOs.**
- **PA-24-191 — Parent K25, Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed.** This is the route for almost everyone: 20 of the FY2024–26 K25 awards came through it, versus a handful through anything else. Crucially: "Applicants may propose to gain experience in a clinical trial led by a mentor/co-mentor as part of their research career development." You can get trial experience under your mentor without moving to the other NOFO.
- **PA-24-190 — Parent K25, Independent Clinical Trial Required.** Only if you will lead the trial.
- **PA-24-192 — Parent K25, Independent Basic Experimental Studies with Humans Required — HAS EXPIRED.** Its page carries "This notice has expired," following NOT-OD-26-032 ("Basic Experimental Studies With Humans (BESH) Will No Longer Be Considered Clinical Trials by the NIH," Jan 29, 2026) and NOT-OD-26-067 (April 6, 2026). If a mentor or a guide points you at PA-24-192, that advice is out of date.
- Both live NOFOs carry a March 31, 2025 banner: "This funding opportunity was updated to align with agency priorities. Carefully reread the full funding opportunity and make any needed adjustments to your application prior to submission."

**10. LATE SUBMISSION.** Under the rewritten late policy (NOT-OD-26-064, due dates on/after May 25, 2026), K awards are NOT on the exclusion list — fellowships (F30/F31/F32/F33/F99-K00), small business and international collaborative research are excluded, career development awards are not. So a documented extenuating circumstance affecting the PD/PI can in principle buy up to two calendar weeks, explained in the cover letter, where the NOFO permits. Do not plan around it: reference letters are submitted by third parties and a late application does not extend their window.
result.review_to_award:
The K25 runs on the standard NIH arc, and the NOFO prints its own cycle map. Per-cycle, verbatim from PA-24-191's Key Dates table:

- Due **Oct 12 → 13, 2026** (new) or **Nov 12, 2026** (A1) → Scientific Merit Review **March 2027** → Advisory Council **May 2027** → Earliest Start Date **July 2027**.
- Due **Feb 12, 2027** (new) or **Mar 12, 2027** (A1) → review **July 2027** → council **October 2027** → earliest start **December 2027**.

So: ~5 months submission→study section, ~7 months→council, **~9 months→earliest start.** A postdoc submitting this October should plan on money no earlier than July 2027, and should have a funded position bridging to it.

Where the K25 differs from the R01 norm is not the calendar, it is **who reviews you**. I pulled all 56 FY2026 active K25 projects from the RePORTER API and tabulated the review panels (my computation from RePORTER data, not an NIH statement):
- CSR Special Emphasis Panel (ZRG1) — 13
- **NHLBI Mentored Transition to Independence Study Section (MTI)** — 11
- **NIA Career Development for Established Investigators and Conference Grants Study Section (AGCD)** — 8 (plus 1 in AGCD Career Development For Early Career Investigators)
- **NCI Career Development Study Section (J)** — 4
- NIDDK Diabetes/Endocrine/Metabolic B (3), Kidney/Urologic/Hematologic D (2); NIAID Microbiology and Infectious Diseases B (2); then singletons.
The practical consequence: your K25 is mostly reviewed by an IC's own career-development panel, not by a CSR panel of quantitative specialists. Your reviewers are experts in judging trainees and mentoring plans, and may not be experts in your mathematics. Write the Research Strategy so a strong biomedical scientist who is not a modeller can score it.

**Current disruption — matters directly to the next deadline.** NOT-OD-26-114 (released Sept 8, 2026) continues the post-lapse modifications, but scopes them precisely: the changes "will remain in place for the January 2027 Advisory Council" — reduced discussion to 30–35% of applications, a "competitive but not discussed" middle third still considered for funding, and simplified summary statements ("a sentence describing the degree of consensus in the committee vote, plus bullets listing the main score driving points," with the three assigned reviewers' written critiques retained and impact scores only for discussed applications). NIH cites "more than 35,000 grant applications under review for the January 2027 Advisory Council."
Mapping to K25 cycles: the **June 12, 2026** deadline fed the January 2027 council and IS covered. The **Oct 12/13, 2026** deadline feeds the **May 2027** council, which is beyond the announced window — **whether the modifications extend to it has not been announced.** Treat that as open.

Post-award steps are the NIH norm: scores in eRA Commons within a few days (currently three business days) of the meeting; summary statement typically within a month of the meeting; JIT requested by IC staff after scores, with the JIT link on the Commons Status screen — you can upload, only a Signing Official can submit, required at least 60 days before the proposed start; then the Notice of Award, which PA-24-191 calls out as the only binding document: "The NoA signed by the grants management officer is the authorizing document... Selection of an application for award is not an authorization to begin performance."
result.program_officer_contact:
Pre-submission contact is not merely expected on the K25 — the NOFO makes consulting the IC a stated obligation, in bold caps in the original: "Because of the difference in individual Institute and Center (IC) program requirements for this NOFO, prospective applications **MUST** consult the Table of IC-Specific Information, Requirements, and Staff Contacts, to make sure that their application is responsive to the requirements of one of the participating NIH ICs." NIBIB adds: "Prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to discuss their plans with the NIBIB scientific program contact before preparing an application."

This is unusually consequential for the K25 because the ICs disagree with the parent NOFO about who is eligible (see prior_funding_conflicts) and differ by ~33% on what they will pay. Emailing the wrong IC wastes a cycle.

**Named contact routes for K25, decoded from the IC-specific table linked off PA-24-191.** Two ICs run a dedicated K25 mailbox:
- **NCI — NCIK25@nih.gov** (listed as "NCI K25 Program Director(s)"). Salary to $100,000/yr + fringe; research support to $50,000/yr.
- **NHLBI — NHLBI_K25@nhlbi.nih.gov.** Project periods 3–5 years; cumulative mentored-K support capped at 6 years for K25.
General K/training routes at the other participating ICs:
- NIA — NIATraining@mail.nih.gov (salary $75,000; research support $40,000)
- NIAAA — NIAAA-Training@mail.nih.gov (salary to $100,000 + fringe)
- NIAID — AITraininghelpdesk@niaid.nih.gov
- NIBIB — NIBIBKAwards@mail.nih.gov (salary to $90,000 + fringe; research support to $40,000; **junior faculty only, no postdocs**; up to 4 years)
- NIDCD — nidcd.training@mail.nih.gov (salary to $80,000; research support $30,000/yr)
- NIDCR — NIDCRtraining@nidcr.nih.gov (research support $25,000/yr; 3–5 years)
- NIDDK — by division: NIDDK_DEM@nih.gov (diabetes/endocrine/metabolic), NIDDK_DDN@nih.gov (digestive/nutrition), NIDDK_KUH@nih.gov (kidney/urologic/hematologic), NIDDK_Obesity@nih.gov (salary to $90,000 + fringe; research support to $40,000/yr; plus $1,500 travel to the NIDDK K Awardees' Workshop)
- NIEHS — NOFO.Information@niehs.nih.gov (salary to $100,000 + fringe; environmental-exposure scope, excludes alcohol/pharmaceuticals/infectious agents as primary focus)
- **NIGMS — NIGMSmentoredK@nih.gov.** Caveat, stated because it is a judgement call: the NIGMS block does not use the string "K25", but it names the K25's exact purpose as a priority area — "Quantitative scientist career development to attract investigators whose quantitative science and engineering research has not yet focused primarily on biomedical topics to integrate their expertise with NIGMS-relevant research," supported "Up to 5 years." NIGMS also "strongly encourages applications from" IDeA-eligible states, HBCUs, TCUs, and resource-limited institutions. RePORTER confirms one active NIGMS K25 in FY2026. Treat NIGMS as in scope but confirm with that mailbox first.

**Which IC actually funds K25s** (my count from the RePORTER API, 56 active FY2026 K25 projects — use it to target, not as an NIH statement): NHLBI 18, NIA 11, NCI 6, NIDDK 6, NIAID 5, NICHD 2, NIBIB 2, and one each at NIDCD, NIEHS, NIAAA, NIDA, NIGMS, NIAMS. NHLBI alone is a third of the portfolio. Median FY2026 award $144k, range $75.6k–$192k.

**How to find the individual behind the mailbox**: RePORTER Matchmaker (reporter.nih.gov/matchmaker) — paste your Specific Aims, choose "Similar Program Officials," and you get named POs with email addresses plus the panels that reviewed similar work. Then email: a 3–5 line message with a one-page Specific Aims attached, 2–3 targeted questions, no cold calls. The K25-specific questions worth asking are: does my quantitative field count as "not yet focused primarily on biomedical topics" for your IC; am I eligible at my career stage under YOUR rules (not the parent's); is the mentored-CT-experience carve-out under PA-24-191 enough for what I want to do; and given the Feb 12, 2027 expiration, is a reissue coming.

Role boundaries: the Scientific Review Officer is your contact during review only and cannot discuss funding; the PO is your contact before submission and after the summary statement; the Grants Management Specialist handles budget/JIT via your AOR. Never contact reviewers.
result.examples_or_samples:
**There is no published sample K25 application anywhere on NIH's curated index.** I checked NIH's own samples page and then NIAID's collection directly. NIH's index lists NIAID as "(R01, R03, R15, R21, R33, SBIR, STTR, K, F, G11, and U01)"; the actual NIAID page breaks that "K" down as **K01, K08, K23 and F31 only — no K25**. NHGRI's ELSI collection is K99/R00, K01, R01, R03, R21. No K25. This is a real gap, not a fetch failure, and NIH says so itself: "Samples are not available for all grant programs. Because many programs have common elements, the available samples can still be helpful."

Correction to a prior house note: **niaid.nih.gov returned HTTP 200 to a plain fetch today** and I read the page contents directly. The earlier session's 403 was transient. The K01/K08/K23/F31 breakdown above is my reading of the live page, not NIH's description of it.

**Best available proxies, in order of usefulness to a K25 applicant:**

1. **NIAID K01 full applications WITH their summary statements** — the closest structural analogue (same 12-page combined Candidate+Research Strategy, identical five scored criteria, same mentor/institutional attachments). Start with the quantitative one:
   - Jennifer M. Ross, PhD (University of Washington), "Modeling approaches to prioritize TB prevention among people with HIV in Uganda" — a modelling-led mentored K, and the filename (`k01ai138620-01a1f-...`) shows it was funded as an **A1 resubmission**, so you can read the application and the summary statement side by side. Application: niaid.nih.gov/sites/default/files/k01ai138620-01a1f-ross-application.pdf · Summary statement: niaid.nih.gov/sites/default/files/k01ai138620-01a1-ross-summary-statement.pdf
   - Lilliam Ambroggio, PhD (Cincinnati Children's), "Metabolomics Evaluation of the Etiology of Pneumonia" — k01-lilliam-ambroggio-application.pdf + -summary-statement.pdf
   - Peter Rebeiro, PhD (Vanderbilt), "The HIV Care Continuum and Health Policy: Changes through Context and Geography" — k01-rebeiro-application.pdf + -summary-statement.pdf
   Index: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications
   Reading a sample beside its summary statement is the highest-value hour a first-time K applicant can spend. NIH's caveat applies: these used the forms in effect at the time (Forms-D/E), so copy the argument structure, never the form layout.

2. **NHGRI ELSI K01 and K99/R00 applications with summary statements** — https://www.genome.gov/Funded-Programs-Projects/ELSI-Research-Program/Sample-Applications-and-Summary-Statements (returned 200; useful if your bridge is into social/ethical/informatics rather than lab science).

3. **NIH RePORTER for K25 specifically** — this is where you read real K25 science. 113 K25 projects active FY2025–26, 56 in FY2026. Every record gives the funded abstract and Specific Aims text, the PI, the IC, the study section, the amount, and resulting publications. API query that reproduces my numbers (POST to https://api.reporter.nih.gov/v2/projects/search) with `{"criteria":{"activity_codes":["K25"],"fiscal_years":[2026]}}`; the human route is reporter.nih.gov/advanced-search with activity code K25. Concrete recent examples to read: 1K25CA317042-01 (Chengyue Wu, MD Anderson, "Towards practical digital twins to optimize TNBC treatment stratification"), 1K25HD120751-01 (Nayoung Kim, Columbia), 7K25HL175222-02 (Katherine Hoff Shutta, Maryland, "Multi-omic network methods..."), 1K25AG095391-01A1 (Kellen Petersen, WashU — an A1) and 1K25HL179402-01A1 (Christopher Rock, MGH — an A1).
   RePORTER does not hold full applications. NIH's route for those: "applicants requesting complete application contents can submit a written Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request for a copy of a specific grant application to the NIH Institute or Center (IC) that funded the grant." Pick two funded K25s in your IC from the list above and FOIA them; expect months, so start now if you are aiming at Feb 2027.

4. **RePORTER Matchmaker** (reporter.nih.gov/matchmaker) — paste your aims, get similar funded projects, their POs with emails, their ICs and their review panels in one step. "The process is automated and confidential. The Matchmaker system does not track and store submitted text."

5. **Templates you can use verbatim**: the "Instructions for Career Development Applicant Referees (DOCX, 17 KB) - Updated November 2024" from https://grants.nih.gov/grants-process/write-application/advice-on-application-sections/reference-letters — hand this to each of your three-to-five referees. And the Annotated Form Sets at https://grants.nih.gov/grants-process/write-application/samples-applications-and-documents/annotated-form-sets, which show a filled-in application field by field.
result.resubmission_note:
One resubmission only (A1), on the NIH-wide rule: "Only a single resubmission (A1) of a competing new, renewal, or revision application (A0) will be accepted," within 37 months of the A0. PA-24-191 lists "Application Types Allowed: New, Resubmission, Revision." Not-discussed and (under the current modifications) "competitive but not discussed" applications remain resubmittable.

**Next A1 date: Thursday, November 12, 2026** (then March 12, 2027 — which, given the May 8, 2027 expiration, is the last A1 date under the current parents).

**Two K25/K-specific resubmission rules that do not apply to R-series work:**
1. **You must obtain entirely new reference letters.** NIH: "Resubmission applications do not need to use the same list of referees but do require new reference letters from all referees chosen." Letters do not carry over from the A0. Three to five people have to write for you again, by the 5 PM deadline. Ask them the day your summary statement lands, not a month before the A1.
2. **You cannot have two career-development applications pending at once** — "An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently" — and no A1 may be submitted before the A0's summary statement issues. With summary statements currently "released later in the Council round," the A0→A1 turnaround is tighter than the one-month gap between the new and resubmission dates suggests. Check the actual release date before committing to a cycle.

Introduction to Resubmission: 1 page (the K table's figure — the 3-page allowance applies to T/institutional training, not K25). It must summarise substantial additions, deletions and changes, and respond to the summary statement. It is an extra page, not carved out of the 12.

After a failed A1 you may submit the idea afresh as a new A0; it is reviewed as new and should not read as a rebuttal.

Evidence the A1 route works for this mechanism: two of the FY2026 K25 awards carry the A1 suffix (1K25AG095391-01A1, NIA; 1K25HL179402-01A1, NHLBI), and NIAID's most instructive published K01 sample is itself a funded A1 with its summary statement attached — read that pair before writing your Introduction.

Post-submission materials (NOT-OD-23-106) are due 30 days before the study section meeting and go through your AOR, not you directly; NIH's one-page preliminary-data update is defined for Type 1 R01/R21/R03, so do not assume it extends to a K25 — ask your PO.

K25 success rate / selectivity. NIH's per-activity-code success-rate tables were not consulted in this session; only the portfolio size (56 active FY2026, 113 across FY2025-26) and award amounts were computed from RePORTER.

result.next_deadline:
DATED, from the funder's own Key Dates table. Both live Parent K01 NOFOs (PA-24-175 Independent Clinical Trial Required; PA-24-176 Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed) print the identical table, verbatim: "October 12, 2026 *" (New) and "November 12, 2026 *" (Renewal / Resubmission / Revision). The June 12, 2026 cycle has closed, so October is next.

OPERATIVE DATE: Monday October 12, 2026 is Columbus Day, a federal holiday (OPM 2026 calendar: "Monday, October 12"). NIH's submission policy: "When a postmark/submission date falls on a weekend, Federal holiday, or Washington, DC area Federal office closure, the application deadline is automatically extended to the next business day." So the enforceable deadline is TUESDAY, OCTOBER 13, 2026, by "5:00 PM local time of applicant organization" (NOFO wording). NIH does not itself print "October 13" anywhere I found — that date is derived from NIH's own stated rule plus OPM's holiday calendar, so plan to Oct 12 and treat Oct 13 as slack, not as headroom.

Two earlier real deadlines that decide whether Oct 12 is reachable: your institution's internal research-office deadline (typically 3-5 business days earlier, i.e. roughly Oct 5-7, 2026) and the reference letters, which must be in eRA Commons from your referees by the same due date.

After that: February 12, 2027 (new, a Friday) / March 12, 2027 (resubmission, a Friday) — the last dates printed before both NOFOs expire May 8, 2027.
result.deadline_pattern:
Three cycles a year on the K-series standard dates, and the parent NOFOs enumerate them rather than saying "standard dates apply", so they are safe to read off the page.

NEW: February 12 / June 12 / October 12.
RENEWAL, RESUBMISSION, REVISION: March 12 / July 12 / November 12 (one month after new).
All by 5:00 PM local time of the applicant organization; weekend/federal-holiday dates roll to the next business day.

AIDS/HIV: the parent K01 tables show a separate AIDS column only through "May 07, 2026 *", then "Not Applicable" for the June 2026 cycle onward — consistent with NIH retiring dedicated AIDS due dates. AIDS and non-AIDS K01 applications now use the same Feb 12 / Jun 12 / Oct 12 dates.

Horizon: PA-24-175 and PA-24-176 both expire May 08, 2027, with due dates listed through February 12, 2027 (new) / March 12, 2027 (resubmission). A reissue is expected but was not posted as of 2026-09-18, so June 2027 onward is pattern, not published fact.
result.loi_deadline:
Not applicable. Both live Parent K01 NOFOs print "Letter of Intent Due Date(s): Not Applicable". I also searched the full Table of IC-Specific Information, Requirements and Staff Contacts for PA-24-176 (all ~23 participating ICs) for "letter of intent" and found zero occurrences — no participating IC adds an LOI stage for the parent K01.

What substitutes for an LOI here is pre-submission contact with IC program staff, which several ICs escalate from "encouraged" to "strongly encouraged" (see program_officer_contact). Treat that conversation as the de facto pre-proposal step: it is where you find out whether the IC will even consider your topic and career stage under K01, and it has no deadline of its own — 2-4 months out is the usable window.
result.review_to_award:
Mechanism-specific and dated, straight from the PA-24-175 / PA-24-176 Key Dates table (same for both):

- Due October 12, 2026 -> Scientific Merit Review March 2027 -> Advisory Council Review May 2027 -> Earliest Start Date July 2027.
- Due February 12, 2027 -> review July 2027 -> council October 2027 -> earliest start December 2027.
- Due June 12, 2026 (closed) -> review November 2026 -> council January 2027 -> earliest start April 2027.

So roughly 5 months to a score/summary statement and about 9 months to the earliest possible start — the same shape as the NIH-wide arc, with K cycles sitting one week after the R01 dates and landing in the same council rounds. No K01-specific deviation found.

Practical reading for a candidate: applying October 12, 2026 means you are budgeting for salary coverage that starts no earlier than July 2027, and your institution has to keep you employed through that gap. If your appointment ends before mid-2027, the February 2027 date does not help either (start December 2027) — that timing question is itself a good reason to email the IC before writing.

One caveat I could not close: NIH's current emergency review modifications (NOT-OD-26-114) reduce the share of applications discussed to 30-35% and simplify summary statements "through the January 2027 Advisory Council round". The October 12, 2026 K01 cycle goes to the MAY 2027 council, one round past what that notice covers, and I found no statement either way about whether the modifications extend to it or to career-development study sections specifically. Recorded as unresolved rather than assumed.
result.submission_requirements:
Standard NIH machinery (Grants.gov + eRA Commons, SAM/Commons/ORCID/SciENcv registrations, AOR submits, no error-correction window) applies unchanged. What is DIFFERENT about K01:

1. REFERENCE LETTERS — the single biggest deviation from the R-series, and the most common way a K application dies before review. NIH's K01 activity-code page states the requirement flatly: "Reference Letters : Required (min 3, max 5)". The NOFO: "Candidates must carefully follow the How to Apply - Application Guide, including the time period for when reference letters will be accepted. Applications lacking the appropriate required reference letters will not be reviewed. This is a separate process from submitting an application electronically. Reference letters are submitted directly through the eRA Commons Submit Referee Information link and not through Grants.gov." Letters must arrive by the application due date (the standard-due-dates page: applications "and associated documents (e.g., reference letters) are due by 5:00 PM local time of applicant organization"), and "Applications that have fewer than the required numbers of reference letters will not be reviewed." Referees do not need an eRA Commons login; give them your Commons username, your name exactly as it appears in Commons, and the NOFO number. RESUBMISSION TRAP: "Resubmission applications do not need to use the same list of referees but do require new reference letters from all referees chosen" — an A1 cannot reuse the A0's letters. Note also that these referee letters are a different object from the Letters of Support attachment inside the application; mentors write the mentor statements, not these.

2. K-ONLY ATTACHMENTS. Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development (candidate background; career goals and objectives; career development/training activities during the award); Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research; Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentor(s); Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, Consultants and advisory committee members; Description of Institutional Environment; Institutional Commitment to the Candidate's Research Career Development. Follow the "Career Development (K) Instructions" in the How to Apply - Application Guide (FORMS-I career instructions PDF verified live, 4.5 MB: grants.nih.gov/grants/how-to-apply-application-guide/forms-i/career-forms-i.pdf). K applications are NOT on the simplified RPG review framework.

3. PAGE LIMITS (Table of Page Limits, K rows) — the critical one is a COMBINED limit: "Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development and Research Strategy — 12 pages (for both attachments combined)". Every page you spend on career narrative is a page off the science. Then: Specific Aims 1; Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research 1; Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-mentor(s) 6; Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants 6; Description of Institutional Environment 1; Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development 1; Introduction to Resubmission 1; Project Summary/Abstract 30 lines. The NOFO adds no deviation ("All page limitations described in the How to Apply - Application Guide and the Table of Page Limits must be followed").

4. EFFORT AND APPOINTMENT. "At the time of award, the candidate must have a 'full-time' appointment at the academic institution. Candidates are required to commit a minimum of 75% of full-time professional effort (i.e., a minimum of 9 person-months) to their program of career development." Institutional carve-outs exist per IC — e.g. NICHD: "U.S. licensed surgeon-scientists with active surgical duties may, with prior approval and institutional justification, devote 50-75% full-time effort to K award activities". "Multiple PDs/PIs are not allowed."

5. WHICH OF THE THREE PARENT K01 NOFOs — a live routing change. PA-24-176 (Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed) is the default; mentor-led trial experience is allowed under it ("Applicants to this NOFO are permitted to propose research experience in a clinical trial led by a mentor or co-mentor"), but if you are the lead investigator on a trial you must use the companion PA-24-175 (Independent Clinical Trial Required). PA-24-177 (Basic Experimental Studies with Humans Required) is now EXPIRED: its page reads "Expiration Date: New Date May 25, 2026 per issuance of NOT-OD-26-067. (Original Expiration Date: May 08, 2027)". NOT-OD-26-067 declassifies BESH as clinical trials and anticipates "expiring all NOFOs designated as Basic Experimental Studies with Humans Required with application due dates on or after May 25, 2026"; BESH-only work now goes to Clinical Trial Not Allowed NOFOs — i.e. PA-24-176 for K01.

6. IC-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS ARE NOT OPTIONAL READING. The NOFO: "prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to consult the Table of IC-Specific Information, Requirements and Staff Contacts ... to make sure that their application is appropriate for the requirements of one of the participating NIH ICs" (grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/contacts/IC-specific-information-PA-24-176.html). That table is where the real gates live, and they vary sharply: NIBIB supports K01 only "for junior faculty who are within 10 years of obtaining their Ph.D., fellowship or residency. Individuals with postdoctoral appointments are not eligible to apply" (a hard no for postdocs); NIEHS "prioritizes applications from applicants who: Are within 3 years of starting their first independent faculty position at the time of application"; NICHD "prioritizes applications from early career individuals within 6 years of completion of postdoctoral or clinical fellowship training" and for K01 "will only consider applications in child abuse & neglect, population sciences, rehabilitation medicine, and Down Syndrome related projects"; NIAMS prioritizes K01 applicants who show "a significant change in scientific focus" or "a significant departure (greater than 1 year) from research"; NIDCD runs a separate K01 for postdoctorate Au.D./Ph.D. audiologists (3 years); NIMH caps K01/K08/K23 at four years and asks you to contact them if requesting five. Salary and research-cost ceilings differ too (roughly $75k-$100k salary; research development costs about $20k-$50k/yr; NHGRI $40k/yr plus up to $1,500 travel to its annual training meeting).
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves, quoted verbatim from PA-24-176 Section III (identical wording in PA-24-175).

DISQUALIFYING: "Current and former PDs/PIs on NIH research project (R01), program project (P01), center grants (P50), Project Leads of program project (P01), or center grants (P50), other major individual career development awards (e.g., K01, K07, K08, K22, K23, K25, K76, K99/R00), or the equivalent are not eligible." Note it bars FORMER as well as current — one prior R01 or one prior mentored K ends K01 eligibility permanently; you do not get a second mentored K.

PRESERVING ELIGIBILITY (the half that is usually omitted and is the one an applicant actually needs): "Current and former PDs/PIs of an NIH Small Grant (R03), Exploratory/Developmental Grants (R21/R33), Planning Grant (R34/U34), Dissertation Award (R36), or SBIR/STTR (R41, R42, R43, R44) remain eligible, as do PD/PIs of Transition Scholar (K38) awards and individuals appointed to institutional K programs (K12, KL2)." So an R21 or R03 in your history does not cost you the K01, and having been a scholar on an institutional K12/KL2 does not either — a very common and unnecessary self-disqualification.

CONCURRENCY, which is a separate question from eligibility:
- "An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently." Do not have a K01 and a K08/K23/K99 in review at the same time.
- "Candidates may submit research project grant (RPG) applications concurrently with the K application. However, any concurrent RPG application may not have substantial scientific and/or budgetary overlap with the career award application." A K01 and an R21 in the same cycle is allowed if the science and budget are genuinely distinct.
- "NIH will not accept duplicate or highly overlapping applications under review at the same time"; nor an A0 submitted before the summary statement of an overlapping A0/A1 issues, nor an A1 before the previous A0's summary statement issues, nor anything substantially overlapping an application pending appeal.

WINNING A GRANT WHILE ON THE K DOES NOT END IT — the opposite: "K award recipients are encouraged to obtain funding from NIH or other Federal sources either as a PD/PI on a competing research grant award or cooperative agreement, or as project leader on a competing multi-project award as described in NOT-OD-18-157." That notice ("Career Award (K) Policy Update: Concurrent Support from a Mentored K Award and a Research Grant") lets a mentored K awardee reduce K effort during the final two years of the award on successfully competing as PD/PI for a peer-reviewed research award from any federal agency, or a non-federal award of at least $100,000 direct costs, subject to the awarding entity's policy; salary support scales down with effort while NIH continues full funding of the research development costs.

IC-LEVEL ADDITIONS on top of the NOFO: NCI "will consider applications and awards from: K01 and K08 candidates who have not already been promoted to Associate Professor or an equivalent position at the time of the award"; NIMH "prioritizes mentored award applications from Early Stage Investigators prior to tenure or equivalent status at the time of award"; NIBIB excludes anyone still in a postdoctoral appointment. Rank is therefore a real constraint at some ICs even when NIH-wide eligibility is intact.
result.program_officer_contact:
Expected, and at several ICs effectively mandatory in practice. The NOFO itself lists no single scientific contact — Section VII points to the Table of IC-Specific Information, Requirements and Staff Contacts (grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/contacts/IC-specific-information-PA-24-176.html), and says "Prior consultation with NIH staff is strongly encouraged."

Verbatim from that table:
- NHGRI: "Prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to contact NHGRI program staff prior to submitting an application."
- NHLBI: "Career applicants are strongly encouraged to contact an NHLBI Scientific Program Contact below before preparing an application to discuss 1) the relevance of their proposed research to NIH's and NHLBI's priorities; 2) the program most appropriate for their career stage and career objectives; and 3) to confirm eligibility."
- NIBIB: "Prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to discuss their plans with the NIBIB scientific program contact before preparing an application."
- NIMH: "Prospective applicants are highly encouraged to contact a NIMH Program Official prior to preparing an application."
- NIDDK: applicants "are strongly encouraged to contact the appropriate NIDDK program staff well in advance of applying."

The addresses on that page are obfuscated in the HTML (Cloudflare email protection), so they do not appear in a plain fetch; decoded from the page's own data, the K-relevant mailboxes include: NCIK01@nih.gov (NCI has a K01-specific mailbox), NHLBI_K01@nhlbi.nih.gov, NIGMSmentoredK@nih.gov, NINDSKAwards@ninds.nih.gov, NIBIBKAwards@mail.nih.gov, NIMHTraining@mail.nih.gov, NHGRI_Training@mail.nih.gov, NIATraining@mail.nih.gov, NIAAA-Training@mail.nih.gov, NIAMStraining@nih.gov, NICHDextrain@mail.nih.gov, NIDA_Training@nida.nih.gov, nidcd.training@mail.nih.gov, NIDCRtraining@nidcr.nih.gov, NIEHS NOFO.Information@niehs.nih.gov, NCCIHDERFunding@nih.gov, NEI_EXTRAMURAL@NIH.GOV, NIMHDtraining@mail.nih.gov, NINRProgram@mail.nih.gov, NLMProgram@nih.gov, AITraininghelpdesk@niaid.nih.gov, orwhcareers@nih.gov.

When: at the idea stage, 2-4 months before the due date — for the October 12, 2026 cycle that means roughly June to August 2026, i.e. now or earlier for this cycle, and immediately for February 12, 2027. Three questions are worth more than a long message: does my topic sit inside your IC's K01 priorities; is my career stage/rank inside your IC's window (the NIBIB/NICHD/NIEHS/NCI limits above); and is K01 the right code for me versus K08/K23/K99-R00. Send a one-page Specific Aims plus a short email; do not cold call. The Scientific Review Officer, by contrast, is your contact only during review (expertise gaps, conflicts, study-section fit) and cannot discuss funding; after the summary statement, go back to the PO to decide whether an A1 is worth it.

Per house rules: it lists NIAID (niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications — described as covering "R01, R03, R15, R21, R33, SBIR, STTR, K, F, G11, and U01" with summary statements) and NIA (nia.nih.gov/research/training/sample-applications). I did not read either page in this session: the NIA URL returned HTTP 405 to a plain fetch and NIAID is a known 403. Those two are NIH's description of their contents, not my reading.

RePORTER does not hold full applications — those require a FOIA request to the funding IC.
result.resubmission_note:
One resubmission (A1) only, within 37 months of the A0, as NIH-wide — the parent K01 adds no deviation but adds three K-specific frictions:

1. NEW REFERENCE LETTERS ARE REQUIRED FOR THE A1. "Resubmission applications do not need to use the same list of referees but do require new reference letters from all referees chosen." Three to five fresh letters, in eRA Commons by the resubmission due date. Budget several weeks for this; it is the step that most often slips.
2. Introduction to the resubmission: 1 page, on top of the 12 combined pages for Candidate Information and Goals plus Research Strategy — it does not eat into them.
3. No parallel K applications: "An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently", and an A1 may not be submitted before the summary statement from the A0 issues. With scores at roughly 4 months and summary statements at roughly 5, a K01 submitted October 12, 2026 realistically resubmits at the July 12, 2027 or November 12, 2027 date, not March 12, 2027.

PA-24-194 repeats it: "When a submission date falls on a weekend or Federal holiday, the application deadline is automatically extended to the next business day." Not applicable. PA-24-194's Key Dates lists Letter of Intent as "Not Applicable" — no LOI, no pre-proposal, no nomination.

BUT there are three real pre-deadline milestones that function like an LOI stage and are easy to miss:

1. IC ELIGIBILITY CONFIRMATION — no fixed date, but the NOFO is emphatic: "Candidates for the K99/R00 are strongly encouraged to obtain confirmation of their eligibility from the relevant IC before they begin to prepare their applications. It is incumbent upon the candidate to provide evidence that they meet all of the eligibility criteria outlined below." This matters most for anyone whose title is not literally "postdoctoral fellow" (research scientist, staff scientist, instructor, clinical faculty) — the NOFO asks such candidates to supply "an official statement of the institution's policy (e.g. published position description in an official institutional document) which documents the position as a mentored, postdoctoral training position." Getting that letter out of an HR office takes weeks.

2. ELIGIBILITY-WINDOW EXTENSION REQUEST — a hard 12-week lead time. Verbatim (PA-24-194 and NOT-OD-20-011): applicants "must provide the child's date of birth in the extension request justification submitted to IC program officials and/or scientific/research contacts listed in the NOFO at least 12 weeks before submitting an application." For the 13 October 2026 deadline that request was due around 20 July 2026; for 12 February 2027, around 20 November 2026.

3. REFERENCE LETTERS — three to five, submitted by the referees themselves, due in eRA Commons by the application due date (see submission_requirements). Referees need 4–6 weeks of notice.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
Both halves, verbatim from PA-24-194 Section III.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU — "Individuals are NOT eligible if they: Have currently or previously held an independent research faculty or tenure-track faculty position, or its equivalent, in academia, industry or elsewhere; or Have more than 4 years of related postdoctoral research training at the time of initial application or resubmission; or Have been an independent PD/PI on NIH research grants (e.g. R01, R03, R21), NIH career development awards (e.g., K01, K07, K08, K23, K25), or other peer-reviewed NIH or non-NIH research grants over $100,000 direct costs per year, or Project Leaders on sub-projects of program project (P01) or center (P50) grants or the equivalent."

Two further disqualifiers people walk into:
- ACCEPTING A FACULTY OFFER BEFORE THE AWARD IS MADE KILLS BOTH PHASES: "If the candidate achieves independence (i.e., any faculty or non-mentored research position) before a K99 award is made, neither the K99 award, nor the R00 award, will be issued." The K99 is not a bargaining chip to hold while negotiating — it evaporates the moment you sign.
- "An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently." So you cannot hedge a K99 with a K01 in the same round. NIH also will not accept an A1 "submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous new (A0) application."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — this is the half applicants get wrong, usually by self-rejecting:
- A CURRENT NRSA FELLOWSHIP OR INSTITUTIONAL TRAINING GRANT IS FINE AND EXPECTED. The NOFO's own instructions tell you to write about it: "If currently supported by an institutional training grant or individual fellowship award (such as provided through the Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA program), describe the candidate's current research training or fellowship program." An F32 or a T32 slot is not a conflict; it is a credential.
- NON-NIH GRANTS UNDER THE MONEY LINE ARE FINE. The exclusion bites only at "over $100,000 direct costs per year." Society, foundation and pilot awards below that preserve eligibility. Note the trigger is direct costs per year, not total.
- NO CITIZENSHIP REQUIREMENT — unusual for NIH and the single most under-known fact about this mechanism: "There is no citizenship requirement for K99 candidates. A candidate may be a citizen or a non-citizen national of the United States, have been lawfully admitted for permanent residence ... or be a non-U.S. citizen." The condition is visa duration, documented by the institution: for the K99 phase the applicant institution must document "that the candidate's visa will allow them to remain in the U.S. long enough to complete the K99 phase," and separately for the R00 phase by the R00 institution. Unlike NRSA F and T awards, which are citizen/PR-only.
- CLINICAL FACULTY WHO ARE NOT RESEARCH-INDEPENDENT REMAIN ELIGIBLE: "Clinicians (including those with MD, DDS, DVM and other licensed health professionals) in a clinical faculty position that denotes independence in clinical responsibilities but not in research may also be eligible."
- TIME THAT DOES NOT COUNT AGAINST THE 4 YEARS: "parental, medical, military, or other well-justified leave for personal or family situations of generally less than 12 months duration is typically not included in the 4-year eligibility limit, nor is clinical training with no research involvement (e.g., full-time residency training). Only time dedicated to research activities counts toward the 4-year limit. Part-time postdoctoral research training ... will be pro-rated accordingly." Plus a one-year childbirth extension, automatic on request (NOT-OD-20-011), and case-by-case extensions for "medical concerns, disability, family care, extended periods of clinical training, natural disasters, and active duty military service."
- THE 4-YEAR CLOCK DOES NOT RESET FOR A RESUBMISSION, AND THIS IS THE TRAP: "K99/R00 applicants must have no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research experience as of the relevant application due date regardless of whether it is a new or resubmission application." Unlike NIH's general 37-month resubmission window, a K99 A1 must ALSO clear the eligibility bar on its own due date. Apply at year 2–3, not year 4, or you spend your only resubmission on an application you are no longer eligible to submit.

DOWNSTREAM, THE OTHER DIRECTION: the corpus's own ESI row (mechanisms.csv row 30) records that all F and K awards including K99/R00 preserve Early Stage Investigator status for a later R01 — a K99/R00 does not burn your ESI payline break. Flagged as corpus-internal; not re-verified against the ESI policy page in this session.
result.submission_requirements:
Deviations from the NIH-wide norm, in the order they bite.

PICK THE RIGHT NOFO — THERE ARE TWO PARENTS, NOT ONE (verified today on NIH's parent-announcements table):
- PA-24-193, "Parent K99/R00 Independent Clinical Trial Required" — posted 04-24-2024, expires 05-08-2027.
- PA-24-194, "Parent K99/R00 Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed" — posted 04-24-2024, expires 05-08-2027.
Their participating-IC lists differ. NIGMS, NEI, NIAID and NIDCR appear only on -194. PA-24-194 permits "a research experience in a clinical trial led by a mentor or co-mentor" but not leading one. And the NOFO warns: "ICs that do not participate in this announcement will not consider applications for funding." Confirm your IC is on your chosen NOFO before writing a word.

PAGE LIMITS — THE 12 PAGES ARE SHARED, NOT PER-SECTION (NIH page-limits table, activity codes K01/K02/K05/K07/K08/K18/K22/K23/K24/K25/K26/K32/K38/K43/K76/K99-R00):
- "Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development and Research Strategy": 12 pages COMBINED for both attachments. There is no separate 12-page Research Strategy as on an R01 — your career narrative and your science share one budget, and deciding the split (commonly ~3–4 / ~8–9) is the central craft decision of a K99.
- Specific Aims 1 page. Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research 1 page. Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-mentor(s) 6 pages. Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants 6 pages. Description of Institutional Environment 1 page. Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development 1 page. Resubmission Introduction 1 page (extra, not carved out).

REFERENCE LETTERS — THE MECHANISM'S HARDEST DEADLINE (NIH reference-letters page, updated 4 March 2026; count confirmed on the K99 activity-code page as "Minimum 3, maximum 5"):
- "At least three, but no more than five, reference letters are required unless otherwise specified in the funding opportunity."
- "Referees must submit reference letters through the eRA Commons by the application due date." Not through Grants.gov — PA-24-194: "Reference letters are submitted directly through the eRA Commons Submit Referee Information link and not through Grants.gov." Referees do not need an eRA Commons login.
- "Applications that have fewer than the required numbers of reference letters will not be reviewed." PA-24-194 repeats it: "Applications lacking the appropriate required reference letters will not be reviewed."
- "The sponsor/co-sponsor(s) of the application cannot be counted toward the three required references" — your mentor writes the 6-page Mentor Statement instead, and does not count as a referee.
- "for postdoctoral grant applications that require submission of reference letters, a letter from the fellow/candidate's predoctoral thesis advisor is not required."
- "Resubmission applications do not need to use the same list of referees but do require new reference letters from all referees chosen." An A1 cannot recycle A0 letters.
- "Make sure you include a list of referees (including name, departmental affiliation, and institution) in the cover letter of the application."
- Ready-made handout for your referees: "Instructions for Career Development Applicant Referees (DOCX, 17 KB) - Updated November 2024", linked from the reference-letters page.

OTHER MECHANISM-SPECIFIC RULES:
- Effort: "Candidates are required to commit a minimum of 75% of full-time professional effort (i.e., a minimum of 9 person-months)"; "At the time of award, the candidate must have a full-time appointment at the academic institution." Several ICs cut this to 6 person-months (50%) for surgeon-scientists with surgical duties — NIGMS, NIDCR, NIDDK, NINDS, NIA.
- "Multiple PDs/PIs are not allowed."
- Structure: "The initial (K99) phase will provide support for up to 2 years of mentored postdoctoral research training and career development. The second (R00) phase will provide up to 3 years of independent research support."
- THE R00 IS A SEPARATE SUBMISSION, NOT AN AUTOMATIC ROLLOVER. Requirements: an accepted "tenure-track, full-time assistant professor position (or equivalent) by the end of the K99 project period"; contact your program official "as soon as plans to apply for and assume an independent position develop, and not later than 6 months prior to the termination of the K99 phase"; the R00 application "should be submitted no later than 2 months prior to the proposed activation date"; "R00 funds may not be used to offset the typical startup package or to offset the usual institutional commitment to provide salary for tenure-track (or equivalent) assistant professors"; and "NIH will not activate the independent phase if the institutional commitment is deemed inadequate." Also: "except in unusual, extenuating circumstances, the awarding NIH Institute/Center will not extend the K99 phase beyond the 2-year limit." Negotiate your startup knowing NIH will audit whether the R00 is substituting for it.
- IC BUDGET CEILINGS SIT BELOW THE PARENT'S (ICO funding-considerations page; the parent's ceilings are $125k direct/yr K99 and $249k total/yr R00): NIGMS K99 salary up to $75,000 plus fringe, other program expenses up to $25,000, and K99 phase "1-2 years of mentored career development (with a minimum of one year required)"; NCI K99 salary up to $100,000/yr; NHGRI research support up to $40,000/yr plus up to $1,500 travel to the NHGRI Research Training and Career Development Annual Meeting; NLM $75,000 for postdocs. Budget to your IC, not to the parent.
- Review criteria are the traditional five-part mentored-K set, not the simplified RPG framework: Candidate; Career Development Plan/Career Goals and Objectives; Research Plan; Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s); Environment & Institutional Commitment to the Candidate.
- Institutional sign-off is the usual NIH AOR route; no mechanism-specific deviation. The Institutional Commitment attachment (1 page) must come from the department, and NIH weighs it at both phases.

result.resubmission_note:
One resubmission, on the ordinary NIH A0→A1 rule — but with a mechanism-specific trap that makes the K99 stricter than any other K.

THE TRAP: the eligibility clock does not pause for a resubmission. PA-24-194, verbatim: "K99/R00 applicants must have no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research experience as of the relevant application due date regardless of whether it is a new or resubmission application." Restated in the exclusion list: individuals are not eligible if they "Have more than 4 years of related postdoctoral research training at the time of initial application or resubmission." NIH's general rule allows an A1 within 37 months of the A0; here that window is worthless if you age out of the postdoc limit first. Since A1 falls one cycle (four months) after the A0's summary statement, a first submission at postdoc year 3.5 leaves no usable resubmission. Plan to submit the A0 by year 2.5–3.

SECOND TRAP: "Resubmission applications do not need to use the same list of referees but do require new reference letters from all referees chosen" — an A1 cannot inherit A0 letters. Re-brief your referees on the A1 timetable, not just the A0's.

THIRD: the A1 carries a 1-page Introduction on top of the shared 12 pages, which must summarise changes and respond to the summary statement.

OVERLAP RULES: "An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently." NIH also will not accept "A resubmission (A1) application that is submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous new (A0) application," nor a new A0 submitted before the summary statement from an overlapping A0 or A1, nor anything substantially overlapping an application under appeal.

AFTER A FAILED A1: the funder-wide rule permits a fresh A0 at the next new-application date — but for a K99 that only helps if you are still inside the 4-year window on that date. The realistic alternative paths when the clock runs out are K01/K08/K23 (which admit candidates further along), K22, or going straight to an ESI-flagged R01 with your new faculty appointment.

EVIDENCE THAT RESUBMISSION WORKS: both NIA K99/R00 samples are unfunded-A0/funded-A1 pairs with both summary statements published — the most directly useful artefact in existence for a K99 applicant deciding whether to resubmit.
