result.deadline_pattern:
Annual single-stage cycle. Documented 2026 cycle in full, from BWF's own RFP and application instructions (retrieved 2026-09-18):

- Portal opens: "Grant application portal available October 2025" (~3 months of lead time)
- Application deadline: January 20, 2026, 3:00 pm ET — hard
- Notice of award: "By June 2026" (RFP) / "By June 30, 2026" (instructions) / "Jun 15, 2026" (programme page)
- Award start: September 1, 2026
- Award end: August 30, 2029 (both PDFs) / August 31, 2029 (programme page)

So: October portal → late-January deadline → June notice → September 1 start → three-year term.

The deadline is enforced by the software, not by staff: "Applications will not be accepted after 3:00 pm EST on January 20, 2026. The online application system shuts down automatically at the deadline and the SUBMIT button will not process a submission." And "NO EXCEPTIONS OR EXTENSIONS WILL BE GRANTED." The FAQ puts it in one word — "Is the BWF application deadline firm?" / "Yes."

Note the deadline is stated as "3:00 pm ET" on the RFP cover and "3:00 pm EST" in the instructions; in January these are the same instant. Do not generalise the EST wording to a cycle that might land in daylight time.

Minor drift worth surfacing: the /grants/ index still lists the programme under its pre-SFFA name, "Postdoctoral Diversity Enrichment Program", while the programme page and the 2026 RFP both use "Postdoctoral Enrichment Program". Same mechanism.
result.review_to_award:
Roughly 5 months to notification, 7.5 months to money, on the documented 2026 cycle:

- Month 0 — application submitted (January 20, 2026, 3:00 pm ET)
- ~5 months — "Notice of award By June 2026" / "By June 30, 2026" (programme page shows Jun 15, 2026)
- ~7.5 months — award start September 1, 2026
- Award end August 30, 2029 (three years)

TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE BWF NORM, both in the applicant's favour:

1. NO INTERVIEW. PDEP is the only one of the major BWF mechanisms with no finalist-interview stage — CAMS, CASI, PATH and NGPI all run finalist interviews. Nothing in the PDEP RFP or instructions mentions an interview, and the selection process section describes committee review straight through to Board approval. So the whole decision is made on the written application: there is no second chance to explain yourself in person.

2. FASTEST TURNAROUND IN THE PORTFOLIO. ~5 months to notice and ~7.5 months to start, against ~8 months to notice / ~11 months to start for CAMS and ~9.5/~10.5 for CASI. A postdoc can plan on a decision inside the same academic year.

WHO DECIDES: "Selection of award recipients is made by a scientific advisory committee with final approval by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund Board of Directors." The committee is named in the FAQ as the body your mentor writes to — "The letter from the mentor should be addressed to the PDEP Advisory Committee." As with every BWF programme there are no study sections, no scores and no written critiques.

AWARD VOLUME — the RFP contradicts itself and both numbers should be shown with that caveat: p.4 says "For this cycle, up to 30 awards will be granted for enrichment activities annually"; p.6 says "Generally, up to 25 Postdoctoral Enrichment Program (PDEP) awards will be made annually." Separately, "up to five additional PDEP awards will be funded by the Charles H. Revson Foundation" for New York Metro institutions (BWF PDEP/Revson Scholars). No application counts are published, so no success rate can be computed for PDEP.

POST-AWARD CADENCE (affects whether you can carry the award): annual progress report from the awardee plus an annual financial report from the institution, "submitted (on forms that will be provided) by November 1st of each award year. Continued funding will depend on both the timely submission of these reports and their favorable review."
result.submission_requirements:
PDEP is the LIGHTEST application in the BWF portfolio, and it deviates from the funder-wide norm in several ways that matter.

THE COMPLETE COMPONENT LIST (application instructions, "Overview of Application Elements — all required ahead of deadline (no exceptions)"):

A. Completed online: 1. Lay abstract (limit of 3000 characters) 2. Budget 3. Budget Justification
B. Uploaded as PDF: 1. Personal Statement (2-page limit) 2. NIH Biosketch (5-page limit) 3. Project Plan (3-page limit, including references)
C. "Recommendation Letter from Mentor(s) — confidential (1 required — 2 allowed)"
D. Institutional Signing Official Certification

Plus, from the detail pages: project title limited to 150 characters; a publication list entered on the title page; and "NIH biosketch of Mentor (up to seven pages). Include graduate and post-graduate trainees from mentor's laboratory and their current position."

WHERE PDEP DEVIATES FROM THE BWF NORM — these are the traps:

1. REFERENCES COUNT AGAINST THE PAGE LIMIT. "Project Plan (up to three pages including references)." Everywhere else at BWF the bibliography is explicitly excluded and unlimited (CAMS: "Bibliography/References list not included in page count"; CASI allows a separate 4-page bibliography). At PDEP your citations eat your three pages. This is the single most likely place for an applicant to over-run by carrying a habit over from another BWF or NIH application.

2. THREE PAGES, NOT SIX. The research/project plan is the shortest in the portfolio (CAMS 6, NGPI 6, CASI 6, PATH 5). It must still cover three things: "i) Rationale, vision, and summary of proposed research ii) Training plan and how this relates to career goals iii) Organizational Capacity: experience, facilities, and administrative support available at proposed research institution."

3. NO FORMATTING RULES. "There are no formatting requirements, though the documents must be legible." PDEP does not impose the font/margin/spacing regime that CAMS ("Times New Roman 11-pt", 1-inch margins) and PATH ("This requirement will be strictly enforced") apply. Page counts still bind.

4. A BUDGET IS REQUIRED, AT APPLICATION. Budget and budget justification are online fields. CASI by contrast "requires no budget at all at LOI or full-proposal stage". Constraints to budget against: "Indirect costs may not be charged against BWF grants"; "The PDEP award cannot be used to support salary expenses or indirect costs"; and it "cannot be used ... to purchase reagents or equipment commonly found in the mentor's laboratory." The money is pre-split by year — Year 1 and Year 2: "$20,000 ... ($10,000 for research supplies or equipment uniquely required to enhance the postdoctoral fellow's research and $10,000 for education and training...)"; Year 3: "$20,000 ... to help the postdoctoral fellow advance research efforts towards the professoriate. The funds must be used to develop independent, innovative areas of research."

5. LAY ABSTRACT ONLY — no separate scientific abstract is listed, unlike CAMS/CASI which require both at 3,000 characters each. PDEP's is 3,000 characters and BWF tells you what it is testing: "It is important that your submitted lay abstract be written generally as evidence of good communication across various audiences."

6. ONE MENTOR LETTER, NOT FOUR. "1 required — 2 allowed", and "If there is a co-mentor, the letter should be joint." (CAMS needs four.) It is confidential, requested by you through ProposalCentral, and it has required content: the FAQ says "The mentor should explain in the letter how the applicant's stipend will be covered during the tenure of the award", and the RFP makes this mandatory — "The mentor must explicitly state how the postdoctoral fellow's stipend is being supported since the PDEP award cannot be used to support salary expenses." Address it correctly: "The letter from the mentor should be addressed to the PDEP Advisory Committee."

7. THE PERSONAL STATEMENT IS TWO PAGES AND IS SCORED. RFP p.7 lists six questions BWF wants answered (motivation and how life/professional experience led to the research focus; skills developed navigating your career; how lived experience shaped your view of a science career; using language and communication to expand access to science; your professional network and how PDEP changes it; leadership in local and scientific community). And the biosketch must not repeat it: "In the personal statement portion of the biosketch, please do not duplicate the information contained in the personal statement above and instead focus on scientific background and accomplishments."

THE LONG-LEAD ITEMS (same as funder-wide, but PDEP-specific wording):
- Institutional signing official — "The proposal may NOT be submitted without the signature of the Signing Official"; "Applications cannot be submitted without both signatures"; "Extensions will not be given for missing institutional signatures." BWF's instruction: "Be certain to add the signing official to your online application early in the process." Adding them grants them edit privileges. They must log in, edit the proposal, and sign in the "Sign and Print" section.
- Mentor letter — "No late applications will be accepted due to letters not being uploaded by the referee." "Recommendation letters sent separately or after the application due date will not be accepted."
- Institution may not exist in ProposalCentral yet — contact Altum support to have it created.
- IRS determination letter: softer here than elsewhere — "Institutional Internal Revenue Service determination letter of non-profit status may be requested by BWF staff if said letter is not on file in our database."

WHO THE APPLICANT AND INSTITUTION MUST BE (structural, and easy to get wrong): the lead institution is not necessarily your employer — "Be certain the Lead Institution is the institution where the primary postdoc mentor has an appointment." Postdocs at independent research institutes "may be eligible if the research institute is a non-profit institution (501(c)(3) or equivalent) in the U.S. or Canada and the primary postdoctoral mentor holds an appointment at an accredited, degree-granting institution... If both criteria are met, the candidate is eligible to apply but must apply through the degree-granting institution." And: "With the exception of eligible postdoctoral fellows at the National Institutes of Health, applications will not be accepted from federal facilities. These policies are non-negotiable." Once set, "The institution for the proposal may not be changed."

OVER-LIMIT IS DISQUALIFICATION: "Do not include a cover letter or supplemental materials. If extra materials are included, the application will be rejected out of fairness to all applicants." And "After the deadline, applicants with incomplete proposals and those not adhering to instructions will be disqualified without prior notice." All attachments must be PDF. Run the "Validate" link before submitting.

STALE ARTIFACT IN THE CURRENT DOCUMENT: the 2026 instructions still say the recommender "will be required to establish a BWF Grant Tracker account and upload the letter" — Grant Tracker is the retired system; the same document's step-by-step describes the ProposalCentral email-link flow. Follow the ProposalCentral flow and expect the referee to receive an emailed upload link.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
THIS MECHANISM INVERTS THE USUAL RULE: having other funding is not a conflict, it is an ENTRY REQUIREMENT. PDEP is a career-development supplement layered on top of a funded postdoc, not a stipend or a research grant.

WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half applicants most often assume wrong):

1. You must ALREADY be funded. RFP eligibility: applicants "must have secured a postdoctoral position with funding (including support by the mentor's existing research grants) at a degree-granting institution in the United States or Canada and must begin the postdoctoral position on or by the designated award commencement date." The FAQ repeats it: "Funding for the postdoc must have been secured and the position must begin on or before the award commencement date."

2. BWF says so in plain terms: "This grant is meant to supplement the training of postdocs whose research activities are already supported. It is not a research grant."

3. Concurrent research funding from other sources is EXPRESSLY ALLOWED, including in the same research area: "Award recipients may obtain funds from other sources for research in the same or similar areas as that conducted under these grants, so long as there is no conflict with meeting the terms of BWF's award." This is the operative sentence for anyone holding or applying for an F32, K99/R00, NIH T32 slot, or another foundation fellowship — nothing in the PDEP documents excludes any of them.

4. Because the award "cannot be used to support salary expenses", a salary-paying fellowship is complementary rather than duplicative — which is precisely why the mentor is required to state how the stipend is covered.

WHAT MAKES SOMEONE INELIGIBLE — and note that NONE of these is a prior-award conflict; every one is career stage, geography, citizenship or research type:

- Time in rank: "must have no more than 48 months of postdoctoral research experience (in a research laboratory) at the time of application and not be more than 5 years from his/her Ph.D." Restated as a bar: "A person with more than 48 months of postdoctoral experience (in a research laboratory) at the time of application or with more than five years from his/her Ph.D. is not eligible for this award." Both clocks must be satisfied.
- Citizenship: "must be citizens of the United States or Canada (at the time of application)." The FAQ answers the permanent-resident question by restating the citizenship rule rather than admitting PRs — treat PDEP as citizens-only and verify with staff if you hold a green card. (Flagging for the corpus: the existing row codes this `citizen_national_pr_required`; BWF's own text says citizens, and the FAQ question specifically asked about permanent residents.)
- Effort: "must devote at least 75% of time to research."
- Institution type: degree-granting US/Canadian institutions and affiliates only; federal facilities excluded except NIH postdocs.
- Research type: "Proposals in health services research or involving large-scale clinical trials are ineligible." Applications "should focus on foundational, curiosity-driven research in the biological/biomedical sciences."
- Degree: PhD in biomedical/medical sciences; MDs eligible if "secured a postdoctoral research appointment beyond clinical fellowship"; "DDS, DVM, and PharmD candidates may be eligible, but should contact BWF prior to applying."

THE ONE GENUINE AWARD CONFLICT is funder-wide, not PDEP-specific: BWF awardees "may not hold more than one BWF award simultaneously", and you may submit to a second BWF programme in the same cycle but must choose if selected for both. Nothing in the PDEP RFP, instructions or FAQ restricts holding a prior BWF award.

MOBILITY RULES THAT BEHAVE LIKE FUNDING RULES (post-award, but they change the value of the award): "Awards may not be transferred for another postdoctoral position. Award recipients who change institutions for another postdoctoral position may take with them any equipment or supplies purchased under the award." But moving up is protected: "Postdoctoral fellows securing a tenured tracked faculty position may be eligible for a transfer award, where remaining PDEP funds may be transferred to the new institution." So a mid-award faculty offer does not forfeit the balance; a lateral postdoc move forfeits the cash but not the kit.

UNRESOLVED: no BWF document I could reach names K99/R00, F32, or any specific NIH mechanism. The permissive sentence in "Terms of the Grant" is general. An applicant with an unusual stacking question should use the eligibility-inquiry route below rather than infer.
result.program_officer_contact:
PDEP REVERSES THE BWF NORM: pre-submission contact on eligibility is INVITED, in writing. The application instructions say plainly: "Eligibility inquiries should be directed in advance to BWF program staff by contacting: Alfred Mays, Senior Program Officer amays@bwfund.org / Samantha Moore, Program Associate smoore@bwfund.org."

That is a real deviation. CAMS and CASI tell applicants not to write ("Please do not contact BWF to ask if we can make an exception to clearly stated guidelines"); PDEP's own instructions route eligibility questions to staff "in advance". There is also no PDEP eligibility-check quiz and therefore no eligibility-inquiry cutoff date of the CAMS (Sep 15) / NGPI (Nov 3) kind — so the practical advice is simply: ask early, well before the January deadline.

A FIFTH MANDATORY-CONTACT TRIGGER, specific to PDEP and not in the funder-wide list: "DDS, DVM, and PharmD candidates may be eligible, but should contact BWF prior to applying." If your doctorate is not a PhD or MD, the conversation is a prerequisite, not an option.

CONTACTS — the programme page is more current than the RFP and lists four people (retrieved 2026-09-18):
- Alfred Mays, Senior Program Officer — amays@bwfund.org, 919-991-5103
- Darcy Lewandowski, Program Associate/Manager — dlewandowski@bwfund.org, 919-991-5132
- Samantha Moore, Program Associate — smoore@bwfund.org, 919-917-5137
- Kendi Kajogo, Program Coordinator — kkajogo@bwfund.org

The 2026 RFP and instructions name only Mays and Moore; Lewandowski and Kajogo appear on the live page. There is no pdep@bwfund.org programme mailbox of the cams@/casi@/ngp@ kind — PDEP is contacted through named staff.

SOFTWARE PROBLEMS GO TO ALTUM, NEVER BWF: "Technical questions regarding use of the ProposalCentral system should be directed to: ProposalCentral Support 1-800-875-2562 (8:30am to 5:00 pm ET M-F, except holidays) pcsupport@altum.com." Use this, not BWF, if your institution is missing from the ProposalCentral registry — a several-week lead item.

WHAT TO ASK ABOUT: the same narrow eligibility-window questions that dominate BWF's other programmes — does my degree qualify; does my visa/citizenship qualify; does month X count against the 48-month clock; can my independent research institute receive the funds; is my project "health services research". Not whether the science is fundable.

NO WEBINAR: unlike CAMS, the PDEP page advertises no recorded overview webinar or information session. The substitutes BWF does provide are the RFP's own selection criteria (RFP pp.6-7, which enumerate what the committee scores) and the six Personal Statement prompts on p.7 — read those as the rubric. There is no post-decision debrief, since BWF issues no critiques.

ONE OPERATIONAL CONTACT TRIGGER AFTER SUBMISSION: "Applicants should receive a confirmation email once your application is submitted. If you do not receive this email, please reach out to BWF."
result.resubmission_note:
No resubmission mechanism in the NIH sense — no A1, no introduction page, no response to reviewers, because BWF issues no critiques. What exists is unrestricted reapplication in a later cycle as a brand-new application, bounded only by the eligibility clock.

The PDEP RFP, instructions and FAQ are all SILENT on reapplication — I found no PDEP-specific statement. The governing statements are funder-wide: BWF "does not provide critiques or written comments of unfunded proposals", and the CAMS FAQ (the only place a count is stated) says "BWF does not currently have a cap on reapplying. As long as a candidate remains eligible, they can reapply in a future cycle(s) an unlimited number of times."

FOR PDEP THE EFFECTIVE LIMIT IS UNUSUALLY TIGHT, and this is the thing to tell a postdoc: the dual clock — no more than 48 months of postdoc experience AND no more than five years from the PhD, both measured at application — gives most candidates a window of at most three or four annual cycles, and in practice fewer, because you also need to have started the postdoc. Someone who defended four years ago and is 40 months into a postdoc has one attempt left. Because the deadline falls in January and the clock is measured at application, a single year's delay can close the window permanently. Plan the first attempt early rather than polishing toward a later cycle.

A PDEP-SPECIFIC DEVIATION INSIDE A CYCLE — stricter than the BWF norm: the funder-wide pattern is that you may unsubmit and resubmit up to the deadline. The PDEP FAQ says the opposite: "Can I change my application once submitted?" / "No. Once your application is submitted, it cannot be changed." Treat submission as irrevocable. Combined with the automatic 3:00 pm shutdown, the practical rule is: finish early, but do not press SUBMIT until the application is genuinely final.

Also applies within a cycle (funder-wide): one application per programme, but you may apply simultaneously to another BWF programme you are eligible for, and must choose if selected for two.

Because there is zero feedback between attempts and no interview to recover in, the only substitutes for a summary statement are peer review of your own draft, the RFP's stated selection criteria (RFP pp.6-7), and the six Personal Statement prompts on RFP p.7.
result.examples_or_samples:
PDEP IS THE EXCEPTION TO THE "BWF PUBLISHES NO SAMPLES" RULE. Correcting the funder-wide assumption: for this mechanism BWF does publish a sample document.

1. BWF'S OWN LAY ABSTRACT EXAMPLES — PDEP-SPECIFIC, AND THE BEST SINGLE ARTEFACT. https://www.bwfund.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/BWF-Lay-Abstract-Examples_10.5.20-2.pdf — a five-page BWF-produced PDF headed "POSTDOCTORAL ENRICHMENT PROGRAM (PDEP) | LAY ABSTRACT EXAMPLES", containing five complete lay abstracts (EXAMPLE 1 through EXAMPLE 5), one per page, at roughly the 3,000-character target. This is linked from the application instructions as "Here are some examples of lay abstracts you may find useful" — the link is buried in the PDF and is not surfaced on the programme page, so most applicants never see it. Surface it prominently in the interface: it is the only place BWF shows an applicant what a passing component actually reads like.

2. GRANT RECIPIENTS SECTION ON THE PROGRAMME PAGE — cohorts 2013 through 2026, each entry giving name, institution and project description. Examples seen on 2026-09-18: Mahliyah Adkins-Threats, PhD (Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center) on "molecular mechanisms that regulate development of the enteric nervous system" (2026 cohort); April Joy Aralar, PhD (UC San Diego) on "Human Anti-Staphylococcal Antibody Responses to Improve Vaccine Development" (2025); Kimberly A Kempadoo, PhD (Columbia) on "The role of dopamine in mediating hippocampal place cell stability" (2013). result.submission_requirements:
Single-stage full proposal in RMS360 (https://breakthrought1d.smartsimple.us/). Deviations from the funder-wide norm, all from the FY27 RFA and Grant Handbook:

PAGE LIMITS — the number people get wrong. Research plan "may not exceed 7 pages, including figures and tables" — roughly half the 12 pages allowed for a CDA, Kellogg or SRA. Enforced: "Proposals with research plans exceeding the page limit will not be considered." The 7 pages must absorb items a–f; only literature cited is free: a) Specific Aims; b) Background and Significance of this work to type 1 diabetes; c) Preliminary Results (if available); d) Research Designs and Methods; e) "Other aspects (formal and informal) of the program that will contribute to the total training environment"; f) "List any planned coursework"; g) references, "no page limit". Items e and f are the fellowship-only headings — training-environment and coursework narrative competes for space with your science inside the same 7 pages.

THE SPONSOR IS A CO-AUTHOR, NOT A SIGNATORY. Training Plan Statement, 2 pages, "must be written by sponsor", and must carry the sponsor's biographical sketch, a list of previous trainees, plans for "supervision, guidance, counseling", confirmation of facilities, and "accurate and complete information regarding all other sources of grant support (current and pending), including title, abstract, annual and total amount of grant, inclusive funding period, and percent effort." Plus a Future Career Plan Statement, 2 pages, written by you, at the end of the Research Plan section.

THREE REFEREES ARE ON THE CRITICAL PATH. "Three (3) recommendation references assessing the scientific abilities and potential of the applicant must be submitted… confidential and will not be released to the applicant… must be submitted directly through RMS360 by the referee. Please note proposals cannot be successfully validated until all references are submitted. Sponsors cannot be references but should complete the Training Plan Statement." Your sponsor is disqualified as a referee — so you need three others, and a late referee blocks validation, which blocks RO submission, which is the actual deadline.

OTHER SUPPORT — reversed from every other mechanism. Handbook: "For Postdoctoral and Advanced Postdoctoral Fellowships, Other Support information should be provided for the Sponsor/Mentor only." Checklist: "Completed only for the Sponsor. Indicate if any leverage." You do not file your own Other Support.

BUDGET — no indirects at all, against a 10%-of-direct-costs funder-wide cap. "There are no indirect costs allowed for fellowships and Breakthrough T1D will make no deductions for income tax, Social Security, etc." Stipend follows experience years; "Breakthrough T1D follows U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH) salary guidelines for Principal Investigators and Postdoctoral Fellows." Research allowance $5,500 per year (handbook confirms the per-year reading), justified in the Salary/Wage/Stipend/Research Allowance Justification; travel ≤$2,000/yr; personal computer ≤$2,000 in Year 1 only; health insurance allowable; and the allowance is explicitly "not to be used for laboratory supplies or equipment" — the Advanced PDF, with its $95,000/yr envelope, MAY buy supplies and Year-1 equipment. Salary support for additional staff not allowed.

NO DEPARTMENT HEAD STATEMENT. The Career Development Award requires an Institutional Assurance — "The applicant's institution must, through the departmental supervisor, provide assurance of an academic commitment… uploaded as a proposal attachment." The Postdoctoral Fellowship section and its checklist require no such letter; the sponsor's Training Plan carries the institutional commitment instead. One fewer signature to chase.

INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF is still the fatal step (funder-wide): you submit to your RO, the RO approves the budget and submits to Breakthrough T1D from the Pending RO Approval tab. Clicking Validate & Submit at 4:55pm on 2 July is not submitting.

FY27 CHANGE, quoted: "In a change from previous years, applicants proposing human subject research on long-term complications covered by the Breakthrough T1D research strategy (specifically diabetic eye, kidney, and cardiovascular disease) are eligible to apply for training awards. Human subject research includes interventional or observational trials as well as analysis of clinical bio-samples or data." If you go that route, review §7 of the Grant Handbook and expect clinical review after scientific review.

Also: 10-point font only, margins ≥1/2 inch, unlocked PDFs 3–4 MB, figures as .jpg/.gif; two abstracts (scientific + lay, lay broken into 6 named categories at 600 words each); Breakthrough T1D or NIH biosketch format both accepted; Helmsley co-funding consent is a yes/no checkbox on the Application Type page.

DOCUMENT INCONSISTENCY WORTH KNOWING: the handbook's Postdoctoral Fellowship checklist omits the recommendation-references and Mentor/Sponsor lines that the Advanced Postdoctoral checklist carries ("Recommendation References (blind) 3 required (sponsor not allowed as a reference)"). The RFA body is unambiguous that both are required. Follow the RFA; do not treat the checklist as exhaustive.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
WHAT BLOCKS YOU — four bars, and note that three bite at ACTIVATION, not at application:

1. CONCURRENT FELLOWSHIP BAR, verbatim: "Recipients of the Breakthrough T1D postdoctoral fellowship award cannot hold another postdoctoral fellowship at the same time." (RFA, Terms of Award & Stipend; identical in the Grant Handbook.) Read the wording precisely: it restricts RECIPIENTS from HOLDING two at once. It is not a bar on applying while you hold an F32 or an institutional fellowship — it is a bar on drawing both. Breakthrough T1D does not define "another postdoctoral fellowship", and whether an NIH F32, a K99/R00 phase, or a T32 slot counts is not stated anywhere. Notably the Advanced Postdoctoral Fellowship RFA contains no equivalent sentence — the bar is specific to this mechanism.
2. CLINICAL TRAINING BAR: "Must not be simultaneously serving an internship or residency", restated as an activation condition — "At the time of activating the award, the applicant must have a doctoral degree… and must not be simultaneously serving an internship or residency."
3. FACULTY APPOINTMENT BAR — in the handbook checklist, NOT in the RFA: "Does not hold a faculty appointment." This is the one that ambushes people. Accept a faculty offer between submission and activation and you fall out of the mechanism, and unlike the Advanced Postdoctoral Fellowship — which "carries an optional transition year… up to USD 110,000 total costs for 1 year… requested at any time during the 3-year fellowship period after a faculty appointment has been obtained" — the plain Postdoctoral Fellowship has NO Transition Award to carry you into the faculty year.
4. EFFORT BAR, which is where other grants actually collide: "Fellows must devote at least 75% of their effort to the project outlined in the fellowship proposal." Any concurrent award demanding more than 25% of your effort is incompatible in practice even if no rule names it.

PLUS A POST-AWARD TRAP that behaves like an eligibility rule: Handbook §5.6.9 Transfers — "**Postdoctoral and Advanced Postdoctoral Fellowships are not eligible for transfers.**" The award does not move with you. Change institutions and you terminate; you cannot carry it to a new lab.

CAREER-STAGE GATE: "Ordinarily, the most recent doctoral degree (PhD, MD, DMD, DVM, DO, or equivalent) will have been received no more than 5 years before the application is submitted." (Advanced PDF uses 6 years.) But the handbook checklist says "Has received their first degree no more than 5 years before the fellowship" — first degree vs most recent doctoral degree are materially different for MD-PhDs and second doctorates. Unresolved; ask before you write.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half applicants never get told:

1. YOU DO NOT NEED THE DEGREE YET. The doctorate is required "at award activation", not at submission (RFA and both checklists). A final-year PhD student can apply.
2. YOUR MENTOR'S GRANTS ARE NOT A CONFLICT — they are a required disclosure and nothing more. Other Support is filed for the sponsor only, and the checklist merely asks you to "Indicate if any leverage". A heavily funded sponsor is the expected case.
3. THE SPONSOR NEED NOT BE A DIABETES RESEARCHER: "The sponsor does not necessarily need to have a background in diabetes, but the research project must be type 1 diabetes related." You do not have to move to a T1D lab to be eligible.
4. NO CITIZENSHIP REQUIREMENT AND NO GEOGRAPHIC BAR: "Fellowship research may be conducted at foreign and domestic, for-profit and nonprofit, and public and private organizations." (Caveat: the handbook checklist contradicts this with "The applicant's institution is an academic or nonprofit entity" — a for-profit-based applicant must ask first.)
5. A CAREER GAP DOES NOT COST YOU THE 5-YEAR WINDOW IF YOU ASK FIRST, verbatim: applicants who took leave "(e.g. parenting of a child, childbirth, long-term care of a parent/spouse/child/dependent, personal health issues)", or were delayed by COVID shutdowns, "should reach out to Breakthrough T1D staff ahead of their application submission. Breakthrough T1D aims to be flexible and adjust these time frames if necessary and appropriate." There is no form and no published criteria — emailing ahead of submission is the only route, and it is an explicit written invitation to use it.
6. PRIOR REJECTION DOES NOT BAR YOU. Resubmission is accepted with no published cap and no waiting period.
7. HUMAN-SUBJECTS COMPLICATIONS WORK IS NOW IN, not out — new in FY27 for diabetic eye, kidney and cardiovascular disease.
8. NO STATED BAR on non-fellowship support — pilot awards, society grants, travel awards are nowhere excluded. Only "another postdoctoral fellowship" is named. Not stated is not the same as permitted; the 75% effort rule is the binding constraint in practice.
9. RENEWAL IS NOT A NEW COMPETITION: "renewable for up to two additional years pending submission and approval of a renewal proposal and progress report."
result.program_officer_contact:
NAMED, SINGLE ROUTE — and it is an administrator, not a scientist. FY27 Postdoctoral Fellowship RFA, Program Contact: **Sanjukta Mukerjee, Program Administrator, Breakthrough T1D, smukerjee@breakthrought1d.org**. Closing line of the RFA: "If you have any grant-specific questions as you work within RMS360, please contact the administrative contact listed above." The same administrator covers all four training awards.

Escalation routes: preawardsupport@BreakthroughT1D.org (RMS360 mechanics, new-organisation registration, RO/FO account approvals when nobody at your institution is registered, page-limit and eligibility questions); postawardsupport@BreakthroughT1D.org once you hold an award.

DEVIATION FROM THE FUNDER NORM — this is the mechanism where pre-submission contact is LEAST structured. Unlike the topic RFAs, the training-award RFA names no scientific contact (no Scientist / Senior Scientist / Associate Director), and there is no informational webinar in the training-award cycle. Unlike the SRA (submission "requires permission from Breakthrough T1D") and IDDP (applicants "must contact Breakthrough T1D Research staff prior to submitting an LOI"), nothing here is mandatory. So contact is genuinely optional — with two exceptions where the funder asks for it in writing:
(a) ELIGIBILITY WAIVER for a career interruption or COVID delay — "should reach out to Breakthrough T1D staff ahead of their application submission"; asking is the only mechanism, and it must be before submission.
(b) HUMAN SUBJECT RESEARCH — "It is strongly recommended that the principal investigator [PI] speaks with the Breakthrough T1D scientific manager prior to submitting the study documents."

WHEN: May–June for an early-July deadline. Independently, start the RMS360 groundwork 4–6 weeks out — a first-time applicant with no institutional history must get the organisation created, get an RO and an FO registered and approved (and if nobody from your institution is already registered, preawardsupport must approve them), and brief three referees who submit directly in RMS360. After submission, contact is over: "status of an application will not be given by phone."

WHAT TO ASK, given the documents actually contradict themselves here: does the 2-page Introduction to Revised Application count inside the 7 pages; is it "first degree" or "most recent doctoral degree" for the 5-year window; does my F32/T32/K99 count as "another postdoctoral fellowship"; is my for-profit institution eligible; does my career gap extend the window. Do not ask for a pre-review of draft text — staff co-develop invited SRA proposals, not unsolicited fellowship drafts.
result.examples_or_samples:
PRIMARY, AND IT FILTERS TO THIS EXACT MECHANISM: the Global Research Portfolio, https://www.breakthrought1d.org/explore-research/funded-research/. Verified today that "Postdoctoral Fellowship" is one of the Funding Mechanism filter options (with Advanced Postdoctoral Fellowship, Career Development Award, Early Career Patient-Oriented Diabetes Research, Strategic Research Agreement, Industry Development and Discovery Program, Innovative Grants, High Priority Short Term Award, Special Grant Partnerships). Also filterable by Research Priority Area (Beta Cell Replacement, Beta Cell Regeneration, Immunotherapies, Prevention, Artificial Pancreas, Metabolic Control, Complications, Psychosocial) and Grant Status (Active / Complete). Each record shows Grant Key, Principal Investigator, Project Title, Grant Duration, Institution Name, Institution Address, Award Amount, Contract Amount and Lay Abstract; results can be Searched, Exported and paged with Load More. Site's own search convention: "Please use one of the suggested search term formats below, to yield the best results" — state abbreviation for US, country name for non-US, keyword only for institution. (Access note: the brief records this page as 403ing a plain fetch behind Cloudflare; my rendering fetch read it today without trouble. It renders normally in a browser.)

THE HONEST LIMIT — do not promise anyone a funded application. Handbook §5.3.2, verbatim: "Most grant materials submitted to Breakthrough T1D are for internal Breakthrough T1D use only. Exceptions include the Lay Abstract submitted at the time of Application and the Web Progress Reports, submitted on an annual basis with the Annual and Final Progress Report." So lay abstracts and annual/final lay progress reports are public; research plans, budgets, reference letters, reviewer critiques and summary statements are not. There is no RePORTER equivalent and I found no sample-application library for this mechanism from Breakthrough T1D or from any university research office.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, in descending order of usefulness for a postdoc starting now:
1. Filter the portfolio to Funding Mechanism = Postdoctoral Fellowship AND your priority area, and read 10–20 lay abstracts. This is the closest available proxy, and it is closer here than for most funders: the lay abstract you will write is submitted to the same six-category template (General Audience Summary, Technical Abstract, Objective, Background/Rationale, Anticipated Outcome, Relevance to type 1 diabetes; 600 words each), so you are reading the exact artefact you must produce, written by people who won.
2. Use the institution filter to find a current or former Breakthrough T1D fellow at your own institution and ask them for their application. Person-to-person is the only realistic route to a full funded sample, and this filter is what makes it findable.
3. Read Web Progress Reports on Complete Postdoctoral Fellowships in your area — they show what the funder accepted as delivered training and science.
4. Treat the FY27 RFA as the template it is: it dictates the fixed a)–g) research-plan headings, so an outline is available even when a sample is not. https://www.breakthrought1d.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/FY27-PDF-RFA.pdf
5. Your sponsor is the real sample source. The sponsor must supply a "list of previous trainees" in the Training Plan; a mentor who has held Breakthrough T1D fellows before holds last cycle's artefacts and knows the house style.
6. Trace the papers: grantees must acknowledge Breakthrough T1D with the grant number, so searching the acknowledgement string surfaces what a given fellowship produced.
7. Affiliate results pages name awardees per round, e.g. https://breakthrought1d.ca/research/grant-opportunities/ (Canadian affiliate; separate competitions, but useful for names).
8. For co-funded work, the Leona M. and Harry B. Helmsley Charitable Trust grants listing overlaps this portfolio — the application itself asks permission to share with Helmsley for co-funding.
result.resubmission_note:
Allowed, no cap, no waiting period — the funder-wide policy applies unchanged (Handbook, Resubmissions: "Breakthrough T1D accepts applications resubmitted after rejection… All resubmitted applications must include: A copy of the summary statement for the original application if provided for rejected submission. An introduction (limited to two pages) addressing each of the reviewer's concerns if provided for the rejected submission. These documents must be included in the Resubmission section of the Research Plan.").

MECHANISM-SPECIFIC BITE — the page-limit ambiguity is much worse here than anywhere else. The Postdoctoral Fellowship checklist lists, in this order under Proposal Research Plan: "Introduction to Revised Application (2 pages maximum)" / "Research Plan (7 pages maximum)" / "Future Plans (2 pages maximum)" / "Training Plans… 2 pages maximum" — as if the introduction were separate. The Application Type page instead calls it "Rebuttal Letter (included in the research plan and does not exceed 2 pages)", and the handbook says the introduction "must be included in the Resubmission section of the Research Plan". Whether the 2 pages sit inside or outside the limit is never stated. Against a 12-page CDA or SRA that is a 17% question; against this mechanism's 7 pages it is a 29% question — and the penalty is automatic: "Proposals with research plans exceeding the page limit will not be considered." Email smukerjee@breakthrought1d.org or preawardsupport@BreakthroughT1D.org before you draft, not after.

Note also that the 2-page document travels under three names — introduction / Rebuttal Letter / Introduction to Revised Application — and they are the same thing.

BOTH REQUIRED ATTACHMENTS ARE CONDITIONAL: "if provided for the rejected submission". Handbook: "Generally, applications undergo a pre-review process. For applications receiving a full review, critiques containing the reviewers' comments may be provided." A fellowship killed at pre-review or administrative triage produces no summary statement, so there is nothing to attach and nothing to answer — you are submitting fresh, without knowing why you lost.

WHAT MUST CHANGE: nothing specified beyond "addressing each of the reviewer's concerns" — no change-marking convention, no percentage rule.

THE REAL CLOCK IS THE CALENDAR, NOT A POLICY: this mechanism runs once a year in early July, so a resubmission means waiting roughly twelve months, during which the 5-year post-doctorate window keeps running. A rejection in your year 4 may leave one attempt, or none without a career-gap adjustment.

NO APPEAL of a funding decision. The handbook's "Grant Appeals Procedure/Rebuttal" (§5.9) is post-award only, governing an institution's response to probation or corrective action; the reviewer rebuttal offered at staff discretion belongs to SRA/IDDP mid-review, not to fellowships.

result.submission_requirements:
PORTAL AND GATES (funder-wide, listed because all four are long-lead and must be done before you can press submit): ProposalCentral at https://proposalcentral.com, reached via https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/aha-proposalcentral; AHA account linked to ProposalCentral on first login; ORCID iD (not needed to log in, required to submit); AHA Professional Membership active AT SUBMISSION — this mechanism's page repeats it: "Applicants must be Professional Members at the time of proposal submission ... Membership processing may take 3-5 days; do not wait until the application deadline to renew or join. The Association expects all mentors associated with training/mentored research awards to maintain active Association Professional Membership, as well." Membership phone +1-888-242-2453 or 214-570-5935. Grants Officer e-signature required and released by them, not you: "All submissions require the signature of a designated institutional representative."

DOCUMENT SET, exactly as AHA publishes it for Predoctoral & Postdoctoral Fellowships:
APPLICANT — Proposed Research Plan (5 pages); Biosketch/Personal Statement; Literature Cited (4 pages); Vertebrate Animal Subjects (no page limit); Resubmission Modifications (if applicable, 2 pages).
THIRD PARTY — Referees: Reference Reports, 3 required (4 pages each); Mentor/Co-Mentor biosketches; and three documents from the mentor that must also cover the co-mentor: Past and Current Trainees (3 pages per mentor), Training Plan for the Fellow (3 pages), Research Project Environment (NO page limit).
OPTIONAL — Collaborating Investigator's Biosketch; Collaborating Investigator's Letter (5 pages); Consultant's Letter (5 pages).

WHERE THIS DEVIATES FROM THE FUNDER-WIDE NORM — these are the traps:
1. REFERENCES ARE A HARD SUBMISSION BLOCKER, and they are not in your hands. "Each applicant must obtain three letters of reference. Those providing the references must upload them into ProposalCentral by the deadline date. The proposal cannot be submitted without the reference reports." Who may NOT serve: "A mentor, co-mentor, department head, collaborating investigator or consultant contributing to the proposal may not serve as a referent." And do not ghost-write them: "Letters should be composed by the referent and should not originate from the applicant. Any appearance of substantially similar language in reference letters will be factored into the score for the Evaluation of the Applicant, which will impact the overall score." The Career Development Award has no equivalent requirement — this is fellowship-specific and the single most common way a postdoc application dies at 2:55 p.m.
2. NO Budget Justification Form and NO 2-page Research Project Environment DOCX. Both are required for the CDA and AIREA; for fellowships the Research Project Environment comes from the mentor with no page limit. No Department Head Letter either (that is CDA-only).
3. RESEARCH PLAN IS 5 PAGES, not the CDA's 8.
4. HYPERLINKS ARE FORBIDDEN, AND SO IS THE PRECISION MEDICINE PLATFORM LINK. This mechanism's own Restrictions section carries the prohibition verbatim: "Hyperlinks to data/figures/additional information are not permitted in the Research Plan nor any other proposal documents. This includes use of the Precision Medicine Platform for applications and peer review purposes." The PMP free workspace (60 days before deadline) may still be used to COMPUTE preliminary data, but you cannot paste the published notebook URL into this application. Contact for PMP is pmp@heart.org and the getting-started page is https://pmp.heart.org/getting-started.
5. BIOSKETCH — NIH format accepted as-is ("It is not necessary to reformat to American Heart Association page specifications"), but two AHA-specific items apply to this mechanism: a CAREER GOALS statement is required of Predoctoral and Postdoctoral Fellowship applicants ("Career goals should reflect the applicant's true plans and are not required by the Heart Association to be traditional academic or clinical research work"), and any intent to delay the start goes in the Personal Statement. Fellows are EXEMPT from the inclusive-and-safe-environment statement — AHA scopes it "All applicants (except fellows)" — but mentors on fellowships "should complete recognized training specific to sexual and gender-based harassment," and reviewers are asked to check the mentor's biosketch for it. "Scholastic Performance is no longer required for Fellowship applicants."
6. PRELIMINARY DATA MAY BE THE MENTOR'S: "A new fellow may not have had adequate time to generate preliminary data; therefore, applicants may present preliminary data generated by the mentor."
7. DUPLICATE-CONTENT BAN WITH YOUR OWN MENTOR: "the submission of an application with identical or significantly similar content from a mentor to a grant program and his/her fellow to a fellowship program is prohibited. In such cases, both applications may be removed from funding consideration." The carve-out: "If a grant application is submitted by the mentor of a fellowship application, both applications may be funded if there is no duplication of aims."

FORMATTING, enforced by administrative withdrawal rather than a warning: single-spaced; max 15 characters per inch; margins no less than 3/4 inch all four sides; max 50 lines per page; Arial 12 (Windows) or Helvetica 12 (Mac); PDF only, exported not scanned.

IN-FORM CHARACTER LIMITS: Project Title 120 characters; Summary for Non-scientists 2,500 characters with a live readability gate — "Your summary's grade level is automatically calculated in the ProposalCentral form, which uses the online editor readable.com. If your summary is written above the 12th-grade level, your proposal cannot be submitted." Lay reviewers sit on most committees and score this section into your priority score. Data Sharing Plan: Research Output 2,050 characters; limits-to-sharing 1,000 characters.

NO SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL EVER: "Only the required documents can be submitted; there is no mechanism for supplemental materials."

AI DISCLOSURE: LLM use to generate or edit proposal content is permitted "must be disclosed at the time of submission. Disclosure of this information does not impact peer review." Undisclosed use identified = administrative withdrawal.

CONFIRM AFTER SUBMITTING: log out, log back in, open the Proposals tab, confirm status reads "Submitted"; a properly submitted proposal disappears from the Home tab. "Once the application is submitted, no changes can be made." Altum (not AHA) runs technical support: pcsupport@altum.com, 1-800-875-2562 US/Canada, +1-703-964-5840 international — and keeps its own holiday calendar, distinct from AHA's.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU — all verbatim from this mechanism's own Restrictions and Eligibility sections:
1. CONCURRENT AHA AWARDS: "A Postdoctoral Fellowship awardee may hold only one Association research award at a time." and "A Postdoctoral Fellowship awardee may not hold another Association award concurrently."
2. ANOTHER FELLOWSHIP AS TOP-UP: "The awardee may not hold a comparable award (such as another fellowship) as a source of supplementation."
3. FACULTY RANK: "This award is not intended for individuals of faculty rank." And if you are promoted mid-award: "The awardee must resign the award if promoted to a staff or faculty position."
4. LIFETIME CAP ON AHA POSTDOC SUPPORT: "Maximum of four years of Association-funded postdoctoral fellowship support per individual."
5. CLOCK: at award activation, "no more than five years of research training or experience since obtaining a post-baccalaureate doctoral-level degree (excluding clinical training)" — note the exclusion of clinical training, which is what makes this reachable for MDs.
6. STILL IN A DOCTORAL PROGRAMME: "At the time of award activation, the awardee may not be pursuing a doctoral degree."
7. ONE BITE PER CYCLE: "An applicant may submit only one Postdoctoral Fellowship application per deadline."
8. YOUR MENTOR'S ROSTER CAN BLOCK YOU — the conflict that is not about you at all: "A mentor may supervise no more than four Association-funded fellows (predoctoral and/or postdoctoral) and no more than two Association-supported student fellows (undergraduate and/or medical/graduate students) at any time." Ask your prospective mentor how many AHA fellows they currently hold BEFORE you write anything.
9. OPEN-SCIENCE NON-COMPLIANCE ON A PRIOR AHA AWARD: "If you had a prior Association Research award, your eligibility to receive additional funding might depend on demonstrated compliance with our open science policies." Prior AHA money is not neutral — it has to be in good standing.
10. FEDERAL ADMINISTRATION: "Applications will not be accepted for work with funding to be administered through any federal institution or work to be performed by a federal employee, except for Veterans Administration employees."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES YOUR ELIGIBILITY — the half applicants usually never find:
1. A NON-AHA TRAINING GRANT DOES NOT DISQUALIFY YOU. It buys you a deferral instead: "An applicant who receives funding, but has an ongoing training grant from another source, may defer the start of the award up to six months to complete the existing fellowship. Prior approval is required." So an F32/T32/institutional fellowship running past January 1 is a scheduling problem, not an eligibility bar.
2. INSTITUTIONAL TOP-UP IS FINE: "The Association allows supplementation from other sources to meet the sponsoring institution's stipend and benefit levels" — the bar is only on a COMPARABLE AWARD (another fellowship) as the supplementing source.
3. THE CLINICIAN CARVE-OUT ON FACULTY RANK: "However, an awardee with a faculty position remains eligible for this award if that awardee maintains clinical responsibilities under the supervision of an instructor."
4. YOU MAY LINE UP YOUR NEXT AHA AWARD WHILE HOLDING THIS ONE: "the awardee may submit an application for a subsequent award during the last year of the project and must resign the Postdoctoral Fellowship if another Association award is activated." The ban is on HOLDING two, not on APPLYING.
5. A SECOND POSTDOC FELLOWSHIP IS AVAILABLE: "One or two years. May apply for a second two-year award. All eligibility criteria apply." — up to the four-year lifetime cap.
6. YOUR MENTOR'S OWN AHA GRANT DOES NOT BLOCK YOU: "If a grant application is submitted by the mentor of a fellowship application, both applications may be funded if there is no duplication of aims." (The bar is duplicated aims, not co-existence.)
7. CO-MENTORS AND SFRN FELLOWS DO NOT COUNT against the mentor's four-fellow cap: "This restriction does not apply to co-mentors. Fellows who are part of a Strategically Focused Research Network are excluded."
8. CITIZENSHIP IS TESTED AT SUBMISSION, NOT AT AWARD START, and no US residency is required beforehand: "Applicants are not required to reside in the United States for any period before applying for funding. However, applicants must have one of the following designations at the time of proposal submission - not award start date." F-1 and J-1 are accepted for predoctoral and postdoctoral fellowships specifically (other AHA programmes require an H-1B or equivalent by the due date) — this is a fellowship-only widening. Also accepted: US citizen, permanent resident, pending permanent resident (I-485 filed with I-797C), E-3, G-4, H-1B, O-1, TN, DACA. You must MAINTAIN the designation throughout the award.

UNRESOLVED CONFLICT IN AHA'S OWN TEXT — flagging rather than silently resolving: the funder-wide FAQ says "An individual may hold more than one American Heart Association award concurrently but may only hold one career development/recognition award (Career Development Award, Established Investigator Award, Merit Award) at a time," which is MORE permissive than this mechanism's RFP ("may not hold another Association award concurrently"). The mechanism-specific RFP governs and is the safe reading; confirm with apply@heart.org if you are near this line.
result.program_officer_contact:
THERE IS NO PROGRAMME OFFICER. AHA is not NIH on this point: no staff member will discuss whether your science fits, steer you to a mechanism, or read your aims. Review is run by volunteer scientists and the Research Committee; staff are administrative. Do not build a "talk to my PO first" step into your timeline.

FLATLY PROHIBITED, and this mechanism's own page names it as misconduct: "An applicant is prohibited from contacting peer reviewers. This is a form of scientific misconduct and will result in the removal of the application from funding consideration and institutional notification of misconduct."

WHAT IS SANCTIONED AND EXPECTED:
1. THE FREE AHA WEBINARS WITH LIVE Q&A — the closest thing to a PO conversation, and verified live on AHA's Application Resources page today (2026-09-18): "Wednesday, September 23, noon ET; Tuesday, October 6, 3 p.m. ET; Thursday, October 22, noon ET; Friday, November 13, 1 p.m. ET." Register by clicking the date on that page. A recording of the July 7, 2026 session is posted. Slides can be requested in advance by emailing apply@heart.org (offered for accessibility; the request works). Note the timing: these four sessions sit in the Career Development Award window, so a postdoc attending now is scouting the NEXT postdoc cycle and the CDA they will apply for later — that is exactly the right use of them.
2. apply@heart.org, or (214) 360-6107 option 1 — the applicant assistance team. AHA publishes the question list this mailbox handles, which doubles as a map of its limits: eligibility, level of Research Plan detail, multiple proposals, figures and legends, NIH-format biosketch, Professional Membership help, paying a collaborator from the grant, deadline extension requests, replacing a document. Scientific fit, aims feedback and study-section strategy are NOT on that list.
3. OTHER MAILBOXES, each with a real scope: awards@heart.org (post-award), peerreview@heart.org or voicemail 214-360-6108 (peer review), ResearchData@heart.org (reSEARCH@Heart portal), pmp@heart.org (Precision Medicine Platform), pcsupport@altum.com / 1-800-875-2562 (ProposalCentral technical — a different organisation with its own holiday calendar).

WHEN: ask eligibility and mechanism questions BEFORE the portal opens (the RFP posts in late April, the portal in mid-May, so April-May is the window). Once inside the portal, contact is about mechanics. AFTER SUBMISSION contact is routed through your institution: "You must first obtain consent from your grants officer before contacting the Association." And: "The program cannot be changed once a proposal has been submitted."

THE TWO MOVES EXPERIENCED APPLICANTS ACTUALLY MAKE, neither of which is a staff conversation:
(a) SERVE AS AN AHA PEER REVIEWER. AHA is publicly short-handed — its funding page carries a standing "Peer reviewers urgently needed" call, citing a "record-breaking increase" in volume — and accepts reviewers from Assistant Professor level upward. Sitting on a committee is the only legitimate way to see how AHA proposals are actually scored. Register: https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/peer-review/how-to-register
(b) CHOOSE YOUR SCIENCE KEYWORDS DELIBERATELY. They decide which committee reads you, and AHA says so: "Selecting the Science Keywords that best describe your proposed work is important for sorting your proposal to the most appropriate review group." The committee list is published at https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/peer-review/aha-science-keywords. This is AHA's substitute for an NIH assignment-request letter, and it is entirely in your hands.
result.examples_or_samples:
AHA does not publish full funded applications or summary statements. You see your own critiques in ProposalCentral and nobody else's. In descending order of usefulness for THIS mechanism:

1. reSEARCH@Heart — https://heart.dimensions.ai/discover/grant (Dimensions-powered; reached from https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/research-impact/research-at-heart-interactive-research-portal). Every AHA award since 2001, each record carrying title, PI, institution, dollar amount, start-end years and a several-hundred-word ABSTRACT behind "Show abstract," filterable by programme, start year, researcher, organisation, location and RCDC category. THE MOVE: filter programme = Postdoctoral Fellowship and sort to the current start year, and you are reading what actually got funded at your career stage this cycle. AHA's cautions: it is "not a reporting tool," publication indexing is incomplete, exports cap at 500 records, and "the portal is best used to look for EXAMPLES of funding, rather than total Association funding on a particular topic." Questions: ResearchData@heart.org. Walkthrough video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mko3FwjDtlI
2. MOST RECENT RESEARCH AWARDEES — https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/researchers-at-heart/new-aha-research-awardees. Verified today: the cohort funded July 1, 2026 contains 237 awards including 54 Postdoctoral Fellowships (and 70 Predoctoral, 31 CDA, 29 Innovative Project), filterable by award, institution and state (CA 38, OH 25, NY 21, MA 20, TX 12, CO 10). AHA explicitly invites the approach staff will not provide: "Please reach out to awardees in your institution or your field to connect and welcome them to this elite group of investigators." That is a named, recent, successful postdoc applicant at your own institution who can show you their application.
3. MECHANISM-SPECIFIC SAMPLE BIOSKETCH, free from AHA — a "Postdoctoral Fellowship biosketch sample (DOCX)" is posted on the Application Resources page alongside the non-fellowship and predoctoral samples. Use it with the biosketch instructions page, because the AHA-specific Career Goals statement is what the samples exist to show.
4. FULL APPLICATIONS WITH REVIEWER CRITIQUES, via a university library rather than AHA — UNC's TIBBS grant-examples library (https://tibbs.unc.edu/fellowship-grant-training/grant/) holds four funded AHA proposals (2012-2013), including one where "the entire proposal and reviewer comments are included," and others with personal statement and training plan. STARTER MATERIALS AHA SUPPLIES FREE, before you write anything — the Application Instructions PDF (https://professional.heart.org/-/media/PHD-Files/Research/Application-Instructions/AHA_Research_Funding_Application_Instructions_AC.pdf); the "How to Create an Application in ProposalCentral" tutorial PDF; the biosketch instructions page (updated 4/27/2026) with the NIH sample DOCX files; AHA's video on explaining your research to non-scientists, presented by Georgia Papavasiliou, PhD (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=04ZEyfM1T2s); and readable.com to pre-check your lay summary's grade level before pasting it into the form that will block submission above 12th grade.
6. PROGRAMME-LEVEL OUTCOMES, for positioning rather than craft — https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/research-impact carries Key Outcomes PDFs and narrative reports for the Strategically Focused Research Networks and initiatives such as COVID-19 Rapid Response and the AHA/Allen Initiative in Brain Health.
7. PUBLISHED SUCCESS RATES exist but were not retrieved in this pass — AHA states "The American Heart Association publishes its most recent application success rates, which are the percent of the total number of full applications submitted that received funding," with the caveat that "Past success rates should not be used to anticipate future funding rates" and that rates "are not available for all programs."
result.resubmission_note:
ALLOWED FOR THIS MECHANISM, and confirmed two ways: the Postdoctoral Fellowship is on AHA's enumerated list of programmes that accept resubmissions, and the Required Application Documents list for Predoctoral & Postdoctoral Fellowships itself includes "Resubmission Modifications (if applicable, 2 pages)."

THE CAP: original plus two resubmissions. AHA's Application Instructions: "An applicant who is unsuccessful in competition may submit the same or similar proposal three times (the original plus two resubmissions). The same or similar proposal submitted for the fourth time will be withdrawn."

WHAT COUNTS: "A resubmission is the same or similar proposal (similar aims) as one submitted previously. The project aims should be the same unless they have been modified in response to critiques or because of changes in approach that the investigator has decided to make since the original submission. If major changes are made to the proposal or if this is a different/new project, it is not considered a resubmission." You tick a resubmission box in Section 1 (Project Title) of ProposalCentral and state whether the prior application lived in ProposalCentral or in the legacy Grants@Heart system.

THE INTRODUCTION-EQUIVALENT IS MANDATORY — a separate 2-page "Resubmission Modifications" upload: "specify significant changes made in response to major comments/criticisms from the scientific critiques, and explain how the proposal has been strengthened or modified (additions, deletions, revisions). It is essential that this document complies exactly with the association's Page Setup/Formatting Requirements."

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING HERE: "To have the benefit of critiques from a previous review, when possible, a resubmitted proposal will be assigned to at least one of the previous primary reviewers. Reviewers of resubmitted proposals will be provided with the critiques and scores from the previous round for reference." Your revision is read against your last round by someone who read it — answer the critiques point by point and say where.

TIMING: with one annual cycle and "only one Postdoctoral Fellowship application per deadline," a resubmission means next August. Note the five-years-since-doctorate clock is measured AT AWARD ACTIVATION, so a postdoc at 3.5 years has room for two more attempts; one at 4.5 years may not — count your own cycles before planning a resubmission.

NOT ALLOWED: "It is not acceptable to resubmit a proposal previously submitted by another investigator."

ADMINISTRATIVE WITHDRAWAL GROUNDS: ineligibility; a fourth same-or-similar submission; failure to "comply with format requirements (type size/characters per inch, lines per page, and page limitations)"; duplication by another applicant; and undisclosed LLM/AI use.

TIME WINDOW: NOT FOUND. Neither the RFP nor the Application Instructions states an expiry (e.g. "within N cycles") on resubmission eligibility. The only time-shaped constraint located is one application per programme per cycle.

VOLUNTARY WITHDRAWAL: in writing at any time to apply@heart.org; you get an email confirmation.

result.deadline_pattern: "Fourth Tuesday in September, Annually Thereafter" — a true recurring Deadline Date (not a target date, not a submission window). Annual, one competition per year. This is the durable fact; treat any single year's date as a dated snapshot.
result.loi_deadline:
No LOI, no preliminary proposal. Solicitation, verbatim: "Letters of Intent: Not required" and "Preliminary Proposal Submission: Not required".

BUT there is a de facto pre-deadline that functions like one and is the single easiest way to lose the cycle: the TWO REFERENCE LETTERS must be in before you can submit. How to Apply doc, verbatim: "Reference letters must be submitted before you submit your proposal. Reference letter writers will need sufficient time to enter their letters prior to the deadline." Letters are submitted by the authors themselves in Research.gov's Reference Letter Submission module after the applicant nominates them and the system emails each an Invitation Code — the applicant never uploads them. So the real applicant-facing sequence is: nominate referees weeks early, referees submit, only then can you sign and submit. Unlike NSF GRFP there is no separate published letter deadline — the letters gate your own submission instead.
result.review_to_award:
Notification: "Awards are made in the Spring following the deadline" (solicitation, Section V/award info). For the 29 Sep 2026 deadline that means Spring 2027 — roughly 6 months, consistent with NSF's agency-wide "up to six months" commitment. NSF does not publish a more precise notification date for PRFB.

Earliest start / money available — this is the big PRFB deviation and it is much later than the NSF norm of ~6-9 months. Solicitation, verbatim: "Fellows must request a start date within the time frame of June 1 of the year following the deadline and September 1 of the year after that (a 15-month window)." The cover sheet start date must be "the 1st or 15th of the month" inside that window. NSF's June 2026 office-hour slides state the concrete dates for this cycle: "Fellowship Start Dates: June 1, 2027 – September 1, 2028."

So for a 29 Sep 2026 submission: notification Spring 2027, earliest money 1 June 2027 (~8 months out), latest permitted start 1 Sept 2028 (~23 months out). Duration is fixed at "24 continuous months" and is pre-populated read-only in Research.gov. Up to two months of the tenure may be used for paid leave incl. parental/family leave. "Fellowships are not renewable" and "Awards cannot be extended without prior NSF approval."
result.submission_requirements:
Submitted by the INDIVIDUAL via Research.gov — no sponsored projects office, no AOR. This is the sharpest deviation from the NSF funder-wide norm. Verbatim: "Fellowship proposals must be submitted by the Fellowship candidate, not by the Fellowship candidate's current or proposed organizational Sponsored Projects Office (SPO). The Fellowship candidate serves as his/her own SPO/Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR)." Also "Proposals must be submitted by the individual, not the host institution, and awards are made directly to Fellows." Consequence: no institutional internal deadline, no SAM.gov/UEI dependency for the applicant. Register a "Proposed Postdoctoral Fellow" role in Research.gov (My Profile > Add a New Role > Add Investigator or Authorized User Role); role can take 30 minutes to propagate. NSF advice: create the account "at least 30 days prior to the NSF deadline", fix your address 21+ days ahead, and "plan for submission at least three days prior to the NSF deadline" — "Research.gov does not allow late submissions". Slides add: set up MFA in Research.gov and use a permanent email address for the role.

PAGE LIMITS — nearly all deviate from PAPPG defaults:
- Project Description: 6-page maximum (NOT the standard 15). Must carry two headed sections, "1) Intellectual Merit and 2) Broader Impacts" — "Proposals without these separate sections with headings will be returned without review." Must cover research, training AND broader-impacts goals, explain "how this research differs from your dissertation research", justify sponsor and host choice, and give "A timetable with yearly goals".
- Project Summary: 1-page maximum, overview + separate IM and BI statements; must list sponsoring scientist(s) and host institution(s) at the start of the overview. Failure to separate IM/BI = returned without review.
- Doctoral Research Abstract: 1-page maximum — a PRFB-specific document with no PAPPG equivalent. Used to judge "the degree of overlap between your doctoral research experiences and proposed research."
- Sponsoring Scientist(s) Statement: 3-page maximum, "Regardless of the number of sponsors, one integrated statement must be developed and submitted." Must include a specific mentorship plan and how the Fellow's independence will be nurtured. NSF publishes a dedicated guidance doc for sponsors.
- Reference Letters: exactly two, "must not exceed three pages", submitted by the authors in Research.gov. "Do not submit more than two letters of reference." References "may, but are not required to, include your doctoral advisor"; "Do not use your sponsoring scientist as a reference unless they also served as your doctoral advisor" (and consult a PO if proposing to postdoc with your thesis advisor). "Your proposed sponsor should not submit a reference letter."
- Personnel documents: applicant is auto-designated PI and needs the full PAPPG set (Biographical Sketch, Current & Pending (Other) Support, COA, Synergistic Activities) — SciENcv applies as per PAPPG; slides say "Create/export personnel documents from SciEnCV (see NSF option)". ALL SPONSORING SCIENTISTS need the same four documents, submitted by the applicant, via "Add Sponsoring Scientist" (NOT "Add Mentor/Advisor"); sponsors' COA goes in "Additional Single Copy Documents" converted to PDF. "Your sponsor(s) should NOT include the PRFB proposal in their Current & Pending (Other) Support document."
- Current & Pending for the applicant must "include the active PRFB submission and any current or planned applications/proposals to other fellowship programs."
- Still required per PAPPG: References Cited, Data Management and Sharing Plan.
- NOT required: Budget (pre-populated, read-only; no budget entry at all), Budget Justification and Facilities/Equipment/Other Resources — "upload a single sheet for each stating: 'Not required for PRFB proposals'."
- DO NOT UPLOAD: "Letters of Collaboration, Letters of Support, Host Institution Letters or Research Support" and nothing under "Other Personnel Biographical Information". IACUC/IRB approvals, permits and collaboration letters "must not be included in the proposal"; flag the need in the plan and NSF may request them later.
- Cover sheet: enter host institution under Primary Place of Performance; duration is read-only.
- Voluntary committed cost sharing prohibited. PAPPG formatting (fonts, 1-inch margins, six lines/inch) still applies, including to the sponsor statement.

SCOPE GATE: a single research focus area this cycle — "Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Biological Sciences to Strengthen and Safeguard Biotechnology Innovations". Slides: "proposals with a biomedical research focus are not eligible"; if unsure, "contact a Program Officer (bio-dbi-prfb@nsf.gov)". Host may be US or international (higher-ed, nonprofit institutes/museums, government labs; for-profit only with prior PO approval).
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
WHAT DISQUALIFIES (solicitation Section IV, verbatim):
1. TIME-SINCE-DOCTORATE CLOCK, not a calendar clock: "Must not have worked in any position that requires a doctoral degree for a combined total of more than 15 full-time months prior to the deadline." Counted in full-time months actually worked in doctorate-requiring positions as of the deadline — not years since the PhD was conferred. Slides gloss it as "Graduate students, and beginning postdocs with a maximum of 15 months tenure in a position requiring a doctoral degree at the program deadline."
2. LIFETIME SUBMISSION CAP: "Must not have submitted proposals to the PRFB program more than once in previous years, i.e., you are limited to a maximum of two submissions, regardless of the outcome." And "Individuals may submit only one fellowship proposal to the Postdoctoral Fellowships in Biology program per year and may submit to the program no more than twice in total."
3. DUPLICATE-RESEARCH BAR: "Must not have submitted the same research to another NSF postdoctoral fellowship program."
4. Citizenship: US citizen, national or permanent resident "at the time of submission."
5. Post-award: "Federal supplements to this award are not permitted" and "Fellows are not allowed to serve as employers during their tenure."
Failure on any of these = "returned without review", and the applicant self-certifies under 18 U.S.C. 1001.

WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half applicants most often get wrong):
1. YOU DO NOT NEED THE PhD IN HAND TO APPLY. "Must earn the doctoral degree in an appropriate field prior to beginning the fellowship" — before the START, not before the deadline. The programme is "intended primarily for graduate students who are seeking independent support for their first postdoctoral position". A senior PhD student who defends in 2027 can submit on 29 Sep 2026.
2. PRIOR OR CURRENT NSF RESEARCH AWARDS ARE NOT A BAR. The eligibility list contains no exclusion for holding, having held, or being named on any NSF research grant. There is no NIH-style K/R01 interaction here.
3. YOU MAY APPLY TO OTHER FELLOWSHIPS IN PARALLEL — they must be disclosed, not avoided. The bar is only on the SAME RESEARCH going to another NSF postdoc fellowship programme. NSF assumes concurrent applications: Current & Pending must "include the active PRFB submission and any current or planned applications/proposals to other fellowship programs."
4. ONE PRIOR PRFB SUBMISSION DOES NOT DISQUALIFY YOU — you get two. A declined first attempt leaves exactly one more.
5. Time in non-doctoral positions, or part-time work, does not consume the 15-month clock as written (the clock counts "full-time months" in positions "that require a doctoral degree").
6. Being at an international host institution is allowed, and prior NSF GRFP tenure is not listed as an exclusion.
result.resubmission_note:
No NIH-style resubmission object (consistent with NSF-wide practice — no A1, no Introduction to Resubmission, no response-to-reviewers section). A resubmitted PRFB is a new proposal under PAPPG Ch. IV ("A declined proposal may be resubmitted, but only after it has undergone substantial revision"; treated "as a new proposal").

What is PRFB-specific and much harder than NSF's agency-wide rule: a HARD LIFETIME CAP OF TWO SUBMISSIONS, one per year — "you are limited to a maximum of two submissions, regardless of the outcome." So in practice you get one resubmission, ever. This is the opposite of NSF's uncapped agency norm and stricter than CAREER's three competitions.

Strategic contrast worth flagging to applicants: CAREER explicitly exempts unreviewed proposals from its cap ("Proposals that are not reviewed... do not count toward the three-competition limit"). PRFB publishes no such carve-out and says "regardless of the outcome" — so a proposal returned without review on a formatting or missing-section technicality most likely burns one of your two lifetime attempts. That makes PRFB's many return-without-review triggers (missing IM/BI headings, >2 reference letters, incomplete Application Form, ineligibility) unusually expensive. NSF does not state this explicitly; see unresolved.

Two cycles a year, May and December, both at 5:00 p.m. ET, submitted at awards.cff.org. CFF states the cadence plainly on its Academic Funding Opportunities page: "Deadlines: May & December".

Observed dates for this exact mechanism, from CFF's own page as archived: Dec 8 2022 (Thu), May 11 2023 (Thu), May 2 2024 (Thu), Dec 12 2024 (Thu), May 15 2025 (Thu), Dec 9 2025 (Tue), May 12 2026 (Tue). No fixed weekday or ordinal — the funder picks a Tuesday or Thursday in the first half of the month. May dates span May 2-15; December dates span Dec 8-12.

RFA-to-deadline lead time is ~2 months: Spring 2026 RFA "Published March 13, 2026" for the May 12 deadline. That is your starting gun, and it matters more than usual here because Section VI (the priority-topic list) is rewritten each cycle and the RFA itself warns that format and eligibility requirements changed.

A HARD CAP THAT COLLAPSES THE TWO CYCLES INTO ONE: "Applicants may submit only one postdoctoral fellowship application in 2026 (either spring or fall cycle)" (mechanism page). Practically this is one shot per applicant per calendar year, not two.

None. The RFA reserves a section for it and then rules it out in as many words — Section IX, "Letter of Intent Guidelines: Not applicable to this RFA."

This is a real deviation worth knowing, because CFF's clinical track (Clinical Research Award, Clinical Pilot & Feasibility) runs a mandatory LOI ~4.5 months ahead of the full application and those are invite-only. None of that applies here: you write the full application straight off, on a ~2-month runway from RFA publication. If you are routed to the Clinical Postdoctoral Research Fellowship instead (see prior_funding_conflicts), check that mechanism's own RFA — do not assume the no-LOI rule carries over.

Documented end-to-end for the Spring 2026 cycle, in the RFA's own "Key Dates" and "General Timeline" tables (identical in Sections II and VIII):

- Full Application Deadline — May 12, 2026
- Committee Review Date — August 2026 (~3 months out)
