Fall cycles run the same shape one quarter shifted: the Fall 2025 family deadline of 9 Dec 2025 carried a March 2026 review and a 1 May 2026 earliest start. So for a December 2026 submission, expect review ~March 2027, notification ~April 2027, money available ~May 2027. Budget roughly half a year of runway between submitting and spending.

WHERE IT DEVIATES FROM THE FUNDER NORM:
1. COMMITTEE. This RFA names the reviewing body explicitly, and it is not the career-award panel: "Postdoctoral Research Fellowships are reviewed by the CF Foundation's Research and Research Training Committee (RRT)". Fellowships here sit with the basic-science committee, not with a physician-scientist career panel.
2. SPEED. CFF's umbrella figure is four to eight months from submission to notification. This mechanism sits at the fast end of that range — ~4 months, every observed cycle.
3. TRIAGE RISK IS EXPLICIT AND NOTIFIED. "The CF Foundation may withdraw applications receiving low scores, and/or those deemed nonresponsive to the program announcement before the review meeting. In these cases, the CF Foundation will notify applicants if their application has been withdrawn without discussion." You will be told, but you will not get a committee discussion — and see resubmission_note for why that is more costly here than on the clinical track.
4. REVIEW IS AGAINST FOUR NAMED DOMAINS, K-award style, not just the science: Applicant (commitment to a CF research career, potential for independence, publications/presentations); Mentor(s) (established CF-related expertise, commitment for the duration, training track record); Environment (depth of CF faculty, quality of the institution's CF research and training programmes, demonstrated basic-clinical interaction, institutional commitment — and note, "For institutions without a CF research/clinical program, a description must be provided on how the applicant will be exposed to CF research and care needs"); and Training & Research Development Plan (feasibility, scientific merit, ability to build skills needed for independence, relationship to career development).
5. PAYMENT GATE AFTER THE AWARD. Money does not move until compliance paperwork is on file: IRB/IACUC/IBC approvals as applicable, plus the institution's W-9 and 501(c)(3) letter — "will not issue Award Letters to Awardees if these documents are not received and on file". Clear these during the review wait, not after notification.
result.submission_requirements:
Portal, format and the Authorized-Institution-Official countersignature are funder-wide and unchanged here (awards.cff.org; Times New Roman 12 or Arial 11; margins no less than half an inch; pre-register the profile two weeks ahead; PI clicks "Submit to Authorized Institution Official for Acceptance", the AIO enters initials on the ASSURANCE STATEMENT(S) tab and clicks "Submit to CFF"; system compiles one PDF, previewable via "Application Full Print"). What follows is what is SPECIFIC to this mechanism.

PAGE LIMITS
- Research Plan: "Page limit: Seven (7) single-sided pages, not including the Literature Cited. Applications exceeding this page limit will not be reviewed." Required subsections: Hypothesis and Specific Aims ("Do not exceed one page"); Background and Significance; Preliminary Results; Experimental Design and Methods; Limitations and Potential Pitfalls; Literature Cited.
- TRAINING PLAN — a whole second document that the research-grant mechanisms do not have: "Do not exceed four (4) pages." Written "in conjunction with the Mentor(s)", it must cover skills and techniques to be learned, CF-specific training, coursework and seminars, seminars/conferences to be attended, long-term career goals and the route to independence. Applicants are "strongly encouraged to consider the formation of a scholarly oversight/mentoring committee" and are "encouraged to attend NACFC and submit an abstract each year".
- Biosketch: NIH format, "Do not exceed five (5) pages per person" — for the applicant AND the Mentor(s).
- Other Support, Facilities Available, Critique Response: no page limit.
- Figures cannot be exiled: "Key figures and legends must be included in the Research Plan... at least 11 pt font... If uploaded as Appendices, they will NOT be reviewed."

FOUR LETTERS, AND THEY MUST LAND BEFORE YOU SUBMIT — the single biggest scheduling trap
"Letters of Support and/or Reference are weighed heavily in the review. At least four (4) letters are required": one from the Mentor(s), which "must include a description of CF-specific and other training the applicant will receive while working under the Mentor's direction (i.e., seminars, new techniques, professional development, etc.)"; plus "Letters of Reference from at least three (3) other individuals familiar with the applicant's scientific interests and abilities (with no more than two [2] referees from the same institution)". Invite them via the REFERENCES tab; they Accept or Decline by email; you are alerted on a decline, so check the tab regularly. "The applicant should inform Referees to submit the letters at least one (1) week prior to the application deadline... Once the application has been submitted, no documents can be added." Letters must not be password-protected or encrypted. You cannot see the letters.

UPLOADS UNIQUE OR NEAR-UNIQUE TO THIS MECHANISM
- Training Plan (above).
- "MENTOR'S Results of Past and Current CFF/CFFT Support" — the mentor's record, not the applicant's, for the past three to five years, itemised with CFF/CFFT award number, PI, project title, applicant's title on project, start/end dates, total award amount, and results.
- Budget Justification uploaded per year of support.
- Critique Response, if a resubmission.

PORTAL-TYPED TEXT (character-limited, not uploaded): three abstracts at "no more than 2,000 characters (including spaces)" each — Project Alignment to Research Priorities and Expected Outcomes (must "Identify up to three specific outcomes anticipated upon completion of the project"), Lay Abstract, Scientific Abstract — plus Summary of Relevance to the CF Foundation mission at "no more than 3,000 characters (including spaces)".

APPENDICES: restricted to two categories only — organisational assurance certifications (IRB/IACUC/IBC) and signed Letters of Support and/or Collaboration.

BUDGET RULES THAT BITE
- Up to $75,000 year 1 / $76,000 year 2, two years max, "Indirect costs are not allowed." Year 1 breaks down as $66,000 stipend incl. fringe + $1,500 travel + $7,500 research; year 2 as $67,000 + $1,500 + $7,500.
- "funding cannot be moved between budget categories."
- "Travel expenses may not exceed $1,500 per person per year"; conference registration goes under Other Expenses instead. Travel outside North America (including Hawaii, Puerto Rico and US territories) needs prior written GCMA approval.
- NIH salary cap applies: "salary requests may not use an institutional base salary in excess of the current federal salary cap of $228,000 (FY2026)."
- Computer hardware only if "the cost to the CF Foundation is less than 50% of the purchase price (not to exceed $1000), and the Trainee's Mentor agrees to share the costs."
- List all personnel and percent effort "whether or not salaries are requested."

NO INTERNATIONAL PATH HERE. Under tax-status verification the RFA says "International Applicants (if applicable): Not applicable." The W-8BEN-E / tax-equivalency / International Institution Form machinery that other CFF mechanisms carry does not apply, because the lab must be US-based. (Non-US citizens are still eligible — see prior_funding_conflicts.) One internal inconsistency to be aware of: that same section carries boilerplate about for-profit applicants' W-9s, while Section IV bars for-profits outright. Section IV governs.

MENTORSHIP IS A FORMAL REQUIREMENT, NOT A COURTESY: "Each fellow must have a Mentor who will be responsible for the fellow's training and research activities"; "The Mentor(s) must be at the institution where the applicant will be carrying out the work for the project"; an advisory committee is encouraged.

THE PUBLISHED REVIEWER CHECKLIST — use it as a pre-submission audit. The RFA lists "Chief causes for assigning low priority scores", verbatim: failure to address contemporary research priorities in CF; insufficient information or documentation; inadequate statement of hypothesis, experimental design or methods; failure to demonstrate awareness of and plans for coping with key problems and pitfalls; "Insufficient or improper controls"; failure to describe potential relevance to issues in CF; failure to document the necessary skills or training; failure to meet all the criteria in the policy statement; and "Failure of the applicant to describe career goals as they may be related to a long-term commitment to CF research."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half that usually goes unrecorded, and here it is unusually generous:

1. NO CLOCK. There is no years-since-PhD limit at all: "Applicants can apply for this fellowship anytime during their postdoctoral period. However, funding levels are based on the year when the award is made, not the year of the applicant's fellowship." Preference is stated for "recent graduates and those just beginning their research careers", but that is a scoring preference, not a bar. A fourth- or fifth-year postdoc is eligible.

2. NON-CITIZENS ARE ELIGIBLE. "Candidates must be U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or non-residents working in a U.S.-based laboratory." The constraint is on the lab's location, not the applicant's passport. The mechanism page says the same: "Open to U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and non-residents working in U.S.-based laboratories."

3. HOLDING A TRAINING GRANT OR ANOTHER FELLOWSHIP RIGHT NOW DOES NOT DISQUALIFY YOU. The RFA handles it as a disclosure-and-relinquish question, not an eligibility gate: "If an applicant has a current source of funding (i.e., training grant or other fellowship) that will be relinquished if this award is received, please note that in the Other Support document." The only firm limits are overlap and effort: "Scientific and budgetary overlap should be minimized. Commitment of an individual's effort greater than 100 percent, is not permitted." So an NIH F32 or a T32 slot is disclosed in Other Support with a statement that it will be given up — it is not a reason to hold off applying.

4. YOUR MENTOR'S CFF FUNDING LOAD DOES NOT BLOCK YOU. The ceilings that govern CFF's investigator awards — the $168,000/yr combined-Research-Grant ceiling and the $200,000/yr threshold requiring Program Officer approval — and the "one application per laboratory per cycle" rule do NOT appear in this RFA. I confirmed this by full-text search of the Spring 2026 Policies & Guidelines: zero occurrences of "168,000", "200,000", "per laboratory", or "Program Officer". This is consistent with CFF's own carve-out that the per-lab cap "does not apply to training awards". The mentor's past and current CFF support is disclosed and reviewed as evidence of a training track record — it is an input to scoring, not a disqualifier.

5. LANDING A FACULTY JOB MID-AWARD DOES NOT FORFEIT THE MONEY. "For awardees who obtain a faculty position before the end of their 2-year, please contact the CF Foundation Program Director to determine if part of your award may be eligible to be converted to a Pilot and Feasibility Award for the remainder of the funding period." Call before you sign the offer, not after.

WHAT MAKES YOU INELIGIBLE, OR SENDS YOU TO A DIFFERENT MECHANISM — misrouting is the common fatal error here, and four of these five are routing, not merit:

1. FOR-PROFIT EMPLOYERS ARE BARRED OUTRIGHT: "Applicants must be from a non-profit or academic institution; for-profit entities are not eligible to apply." Note this is stricter than CFF's investigator awards, where a for-profit applicant may proceed after contacting the Program Officer. There is no such door here.

2. CLINICAL FELLOWS MUST GO ELSEWHERE: "Candidates who are clinical fellows should apply to the CF Foundation Clinical Fellowship program for the appropriate year."

3. CFTR-RESTORATION AND GENE FIX/REPLACE WORK GOES TO PTAC: "Applicants seeking to submit proposals focused on topics such as restoration of CFTR protein function or approaches to fix/replace the defective CFTR gene should apply through the Path to a Cure Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Award Program." That includes rare-CFTR-mutation characterisation, nonsense modulation, gene editing/replacement, and cellular targets for CFTR correction.

4. HUMAN-SUBJECTS WORK BEYOND MINIMAL RISK GOES TO THE CLINICAL POSTDOC FELLOWSHIP: sampling is allowed here "only if the sampling method constitutes minimal patient risk (e.g., venipuncture, nasal cell brushing) and patient samples or data are anonymous". Previously obtained samples or samples from routine clinical care may be allowed if stated clearly. But "All other projects involving human subjects, including studies using data from the CF Foundation Patient Registry and interventional studies, will not be reviewed nor funded through this award mechanism" — and separately, "Interventional studies involving human subjects cannot be supported through this program."

5. THROUGHPUT CAP: "Applicants may submit only one postdoctoral fellowship application in 2026 (either spring or fall cycle)." One shot per applicant per calendar year. My reading is that "one postdoctoral fellowship application" spans the standard and the Path to a Cure postdoctoral fellowships, so you cannot hedge by submitting to both in one year — worth confirming with GCMA before you plan around it.

6. TWO UNFUNDED CYCLES ENDS IT: "Applications that have not been funded in two review cycles will not be accepted for further consideration by the CF Foundation." No tenure-track exception exists in this RFA.

Also note a documentation conflict about degrees, which I could not resolve against the RFA: CFF's Academic Funding Opportunities page files this award under "Postdoctoral Fellows (Ph.D., D.V.M., Pharm.D., or equivalent terminal degree)", while the mechanism's own page says the awards "are offered to MDs, PhDs, and MD/PhDs". The Policies & Guidelines themselves name no degree at all — they say only "Postdoctoral applicants engaged in or planning CF-related research are eligible" and route clinical fellows away. If your degree is an MD, ask GCMA which mechanism you belong in before you write anything.
result.program_officer_contact:
Expected, and cheap — but note that this mechanism does NOT carry the mandatory-PO-approval clauses that CFF's Research Grant and Pilot & Feasibility RFAs do. I searched the full Spring 2026 Postdoctoral P&G: the phrase "Program Officer" does not appear once. So pre-submission contact here is prudent rather than a stated eligibility gate — with the exception of the routing questions below, where getting it wrong is fatal and a five-minute email settles it.

NAMED CONTACTS, verbatim from Section XII of this mechanism's own RFA:
- Technical support AND content, primary: Mike Carlino, MCarlino@cff.org, 301-841-2614 (GCMA). The RFA banners his address on page 1: "For application technical support, please contact MCarlino@cff.org".
- Secondary GCMA: grants@cff.org, 301-841-2671.
- Scientific and programmatic, infection-related projects: Rebekah Dedrick, Ph.D., rdedrick@cff.org.
- Scientific and programmatic, all other projects: Katherine Tuggle, Ph.D., ktuggle@cff.org.

A THIRD ROLE THIS RFA INVOKES, WITHOUT NAMING A PERSON — the "CF Foundation Program Director", for two post-award situations: award transfers ("Awards are not transferable to other individuals or institutions unless previously approved by the CF Foundation Program Director") and the faculty-job conversion to a Pilot & Feasibility Award. Route via grants@cff.org.

WHEN TO WRITE: before you write the application, not after. The RFA publishes only ~2 months before the deadline and Section VI's priority list is rewritten each cycle, so the useful window is ~3-4 months out, while the prior cycle's RFA is still the best available guide.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WORTH ASKING, for this mechanism specifically:
(a) Routing, which is where applications die: is my project basic enough for this award, or does the human-subjects component push me to the Clinical Postdoctoral Research Fellowship? Does my CFTR angle push me to the PTAC postdoctoral fellowship? As an MD, am I a "clinical fellow" who belongs in the Clinical Fellowship programme?
(b) Priorities: is my question inside this cycle's Section VI list, or will it be deprioritised? Infection-focused applicants especially — the RFA warns that "Proposals focused solely on basic pathogen biology - without clear relevance to developing new treatments or improving outcomes for people with CF - may be deprioritized for funding," and recommends clinically relevant CF isolates, CF-lung-like models, and attention to HEMT effects on lung microbiology.
(c) Whether the once-per-calendar-year cap counts a PTAC postdoctoral application against a standard one.
(d) If your institution has no CF programme: how to satisfy the Environment criterion, which explicitly asks such applicants to describe how they will be exposed to CF research and care needs.
(e) Timing of a resubmission, given the cap (see resubmission_note).
result.resubmission_note:
ALLOWED, CAPPED AT TWO CYCLES, AND — the part that surprises people — EFFECTIVELY ANNUAL, NOT SEMIANNUAL.

The rule, verbatim from Section VII of this mechanism's RFA: "Applications that have not been funded in two review cycles will not be accepted for further consideration by the CF Foundation. In order to resubmit unfunded applications during future application cycles, applicants must indicate that the application is a resubmission and address reviewer's critiques through a response to reviewers and revisions to the research plan."

THREE MECHANISM-SPECIFIC DEVIATIONS:

1. THE COUNTER IS "NOT FUNDED", NOT "NOT DISCUSSED". CFF's Clinical Research Award says applications "that have not been discussed in two review meetings" are done — wording that arguably spares a triaged application. This RFA says "not been funded in two review cycles". Since it also warns that CFF "may withdraw applications receiving low scores... before the review meeting," a triaged postdoc application appears to burn a cycle anyway. Worth confirming with GCMA if it happens to you, but plan on the stricter reading.

2. NO PRE-TENURE THIRD BITE. The Research Grant and P&F RFAs allow an extra resubmission for pre-tenure tenure-track PIs with prior Program Officer approval. No such exception exists in this RFA — "tenure" does not appear in it. You get two cycles.

3. THE CADENCE CAP FORCES A 12-MONTH TURNAROUND. "Applicants may submit only one postdoctoral fellowship application in 2026 (either spring or fall cycle)." Chain that against the timeline: a May 2026 submission is notified in September 2026, which is before the December 2026 deadline — but a December submission would be a second postdoctoral fellowship application in the same calendar year, which the cap forbids. So a May applicant's resubmission realistically waits for the following May, not the December six months later. Confirm with GCMA when the fall RFA publishes, since the cap is worded per calendar year and is stated on the web page rather than in the RFA.

WHAT YOU MUST PRODUCE — three things, all mandatory:
(a) Flag it as a resubmission in the portal.
(b) Upload a CRITIQUE RESPONSE, from the template inside awards.cff.org: "If the application is a resubmission of a previously declined application, please provide a point-by-point response to the prior reviews. There is no page limit to your responses, but please be concise and succinct." Note what this is not: it is a separate upload, not an NIH-style one-page Introduction folded into the research plan, and it is unlimited in length.
(c) Revise the science AND mark the changes. "If the application is a resubmission of an earlier one, revisions must be clearly indicated by a change in font, bolded or underlined. The CF Foundation will not review resubmissions that have not been revised." And: "In addition to providing the response to critiques, the research plan must also be revised and clearly marked to show changes from the previous submission. Research plans that are not clearly revised may not be reviewed." A cosmetic resubmission is rejected without review.

One structural point in your favour: because CFF returns anonymised reviewer critiques to every applicant, you resubmit with the actual review in hand — this is the NIH summary-statement analogue, and the critique response is where the second attempt is won.
result.examples_or_samples:
There is no CFF equivalent of NIH RePORTER — awards.cff.org is login-gated (it is a SmartSimple instance; I confirmed the login wall today and did not register or sign in), and its Funding Opportunities list is visible only after login. Four routes work, best first, and the first one is sharper for THIS mechanism than the funder-wide advice suggests.

1. EUROPE PMC, FILTERED TO THE FELLOWSHIP AWARD CODE. CFF award IDs are shaped SURNAME + two-digit year + letter code + serial, and the letter code appears to encode the mechanism. Papers that both carry a CFF grant and mention "postdoctoral fellowship" are dominated by F0-coded awards: of the codable IDs in that result set, F0 accounted for 40 — more than every other code combined — and one record spells the convention out, reading "CFF Postdoc-to-Faculty Transition Award LIMOLI18F5" (so F5 is the Postdoc-to-Faculty Transition Award, F0 the Postdoctoral Research Fellowship). Verified live today against the Europe PMC REST API: GRANT_AGENCY:"Cystic Fibrosis Foundation" returns 3,598 records overall, and GRANT_AGENCY:"Cystic Fibrosis Foundation" AND GRANT_ID:*F0 returns 194. That is a usable list of ~194 papers written off this specific award. Real F0 examples to start from: FRANDO24F0, HSIEH21F0, MCDANI23F0, CHATTE22F0, KANG25F0, JEAN21F0, DARCH16F0. Caveat: CFF publishes no codebook, so the F0 = postdoctoral fellowship mapping is an empirical pattern I measured, not a funder statement — spot-check a record before leaning on it. Browse: https://europepmc.org/search?query=GRANT_AGENCY%3A%22Cystic%20Fibrosis%20Foundation%22 ; the same data sits in PubMed's "Grants and funding" field.

2. THE RFA'S OWN REVIEWER CHECKLIST, which is the closest thing to a published scoring rubric. Section VII of the Policies & Guidelines gives both the four review domains (Applicant / Mentor(s) / Environment / Training & Research Development Plan, each broken into named sub-criteria) and the list of "Chief causes for assigning low priority scores". Read both before you outline, and again before you submit. Free, funder-authored, mechanism-specific.

3. THE TEMPLATES ARE THE STARTER KIT, because no sample applications are published. Every uploaded component has a downloadable template inside awards.cff.org: Budget Justification, Research Plan, Training Plan, Biographical Sketches, Other Support, Facilities Available, Mentor's Results of Past and Current CFF/CFFT Support, and Critique Response. Publicly, before you have an account: the applicant how-to guide at https://www.cff.org/sites/default/files/2021-10/GMS-Guide-Applicants.pdf and the three-part video tutorial series at https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLhoQ6vyZhgqos7sBXGW1YdV1mfPtEwE17, both linked from https://www.cff.org/researchers/information-applicants-and-awardees. CAUTION: that applicant guide is filed under 2021-10, so it predates the Authorized Institution Official submission flow described in the current RFA — where they disagree, Section X of the Policies & Guidelines is authoritative. The awardee-side guide is current (2026-05), as are the Research Award Terms and Conditions at https://www.cff.org/sites/default/files/2022-03/Research-Award-Terms-and-Conditions.pdf, which tell you what you are signing up to.

4. A COLLEAGUE'S CRITIQUES AND FUNDED APPLICATION. CFF returns anonymised reviewer critiques to every applicant, funded or not. None of it is public, so the practical move — and it is how people actually calibrate for this funder — is to ask a CF-funded postdoc or PI in your department for their critiques plus the funded application. For this mechanism, ask specifically for the Training Plan and the mentor's letter: they are the two components with no NIH-equivalent muscle memory, and they are the ones "weighed heavily in the review."

5. NACFC. The RFA repeatedly nudges awardees to attend the North American CF Conference and submit an abstract each year; its abstract archive is the most direct public read on what CFF-funded postdoctoral work looks like in practice, and the meeting is where these mentors and program staff are in one room.

Institution-level funding history (ProPublica Form 990 Schedule I, CFF EIN 13-1930701) remains available as the funder-wide route, but it carries no abstracts and does not separate fellowships from grants — of little use at this mechanism's level.
unresolved: DECEMBER 2026 CALENDAR DATE NOT PUBLISHED. As of 2026-09-18 the mechanism page shows only "Spring cycle applications: May 12, 2026". The cadence ("Deadlines: May & December") is published; the fall date is not. Expect it with the fall RFA around mid-October 2026 (the Spring 2026 RFA published 13 March for a 12 May deadline). Recheck the mechanism page and the Funding Opportunities Newsletter in mid-October. The 8-12 December planning window in next_deadline is derived from seven archived cycles of this page, NOT announced by CFF.

A third-party aggregator's "December 12, 2026" is a Saturday and appears on no CFF page. The archive explains it: 12 December 2024 WAS a real deadline for this mechanism (a Thursday), so this looks like a stale date with the year rolled forward. Do not record it.

DEGREE ELIGIBILITY IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS CFF'S OWN PAGES and unresolved in the RFA. The Academic Funding Opportunities page files this award under "Postdoctoral Fellows (Ph.D., D.V.M., Pharm.D., or equivalent terminal degree)"; the mechanism page says it is "offered to MDs, PhDs, and MD/PhDs"; the Policies & Guidelines name no degree at all and only route "clinical fellows" to the Clinical Fellowship programme. The current CSV row records PhD/DVM/PharmD, which matches one CFF page and contradicts another. MD applicants should ask GCMA which mechanism they belong in.

WHETHER A TRIAGED APPLICATION BURNS A RESUBMISSION CYCLE. This RFA counts applications "not funded in two review cycles", while the Clinical Research Award counts those "not discussed in two review meetings". Since CFF may withdraw low-scoring applications before the review meeting, the stricter reading is that a triaged postdoc application still costs a cycle. Not stated explicitly; confirm with GCMA.

WHETHER THE ONCE-PER-CALENDAR-YEAR CAP SPANS THE PTAC POSTDOCTORAL FELLOWSHIP. The rule reads "only one postdoctoral fellowship application in 2026". If it spans both the standard and Path to a Cure postdoctoral fellowships, applicants cannot hedge across the two in one year. Not stated; confirm with GCMA.

WHETHER THE 2026 CADENCE CAP IS RESTATED FOR 2027. The one-application-per-year cap appears on the mechanism web page and names the year 2026; it is NOT in the Policies & Guidelines PDF. Re-verify when the fall RFA and the 2027 pages publish.

CFF AWARD-ID LETTER CODES ARE NOT DOCUMENTED BY THE FUNDER. The F0 = Postdoctoral Research Fellowship / F5 = Postdoc-to-Faculty Transition mapping in examples_or_samples is an empirical pattern I measured in Europe PMC (F0 dominant among CFF-funded papers mentioning postdoctoral fellowships; one record naming F5 as a Postdoc-to-Faculty award), corroborated but not confirmed by CFF. No codebook was found.

NO PUBLISHED SUCCESS RATE OR APPLICATION VOLUME FOR THIS MECHANISM. CFF publishes base rates only for the Clinical Research Award (~35% of LOIs invited, ~20% of full applications funded). Nothing comparable was found for the Postdoctoral Research Fellowship; do not transfer the CRA figures to it.

TOOLING FACT, NOT A FINDING: cff.org returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch and to curl, including on the Policies & Guidelines PDF (https://www.cff.org/media/11166/download?inline). All CFF content here was read from the funder's own pages through a rendering browser, with the PDF decoded in-page via pdf.js (13 pages, 352 KB). Additionally, cff.org pages render with empty innerText to the text extractor — textContent must be used. The WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted before this task began, so no search index was used at all.

NO PUBLIC SAMPLE APPLICATION, ANNOTATED EXAMPLE, OR FUNDED ABSTRACT WAS FOUND for this mechanism, from CFF or from any university research office. Established by direct examination of CFF's applicant-facing pages and the login-gated portal, not by a CFF statement to that effect.

result.deadline_pattern:
Annual, single deadline, first week of August at 3 p.m. Central Time; ProposalCentral opens exactly 8 weeks earlier (mid-May); RFP posts ~14 weeks earlier (late April). Notification December, activation January 1. 2027 cycle: RFP Apr 28, 2026 / portal May 15, 2026 / deadline Tue Aug 4, 2026 3 p.m. CT / notification Dec 2026 / start Jan 1, 2027.

This is a per-programme annual cycle, not an NIH-style standing grid: there are no three-times-a-year standard dates, and no new-vs-resubmission date offset — a resubmission goes in at the same August deadline as everything else. AHA: "The American Heart Association has rolling deadlines throughout the year... New deadline dates are generally posted with several months' notice."

One application per deadline: "An applicant may submit only one Predoctoral Fellowship application per deadline." Combined with the funder-wide one-per-programme-per-fiscal-year rule (FY = July 1 to June 30), that is one attempt per year.

Two holiday calendars sit near the December notification, not near the August deadline, so they are less dangerous here than for the CDA: AHA holidays Dec 21-25 2026, Altum/ProposalCentral holidays Dec 28-Jan 1. The August deadline is clear of both, but note AHA closes July 3 and 6 — during the final month of drafting.

This information should not be used to set expectations related to future success rates."

TRIAGE comes first and is brutal: "The American Heart Association reserves the right to an initial triage, whereby a minimum of half of the submissions may be triaged" (Predoctoral RFP page). NOTE A CONFLICT IN AHA'S OWN DOCUMENTS on what a triaged applicant receives: the public FAQ says "a minimum of half of the submissions may be triaged and not discussed in a peer review meeting. All proposals submitted will receive a written critique, unless otherwise noted," while the Application Instructions say up to half may be streamlined "with no reviewer comments and no peer review score." Do not promise a predoc student they will definitely get written feedback.

SCORING: 1-9 scale, weighted 30% Potential of the Fellow / 40% Mentor's Commitment and Research Training Plan / 30% Evaluation of the Research as a Training Vehicle. The 40% weight on the mentor is the single most important structural fact about this award — the largest share of your score is carried by documents you do not write.

A lay (non-scientist) reviewer sits on most committees and scores the Summary for Non-scientists, and that assessment feeds the priority score.

COHORT SIZE, for calibration: the most recent activation cohort (July 1, 2026) contains 70 Predoctoral Fellowships out of 237 awards — the largest single category AHA funds.

LATEST POSSIBLE START: activation can be pushed up to six months (so as late as ~July 1 for a January 1 award), but only if you declare the intent at submission — see submission_requirements. Not available for finishing coursework.
result.submission_requirements:
Portal, membership, ORCID and grants-officer e-signature are funder-wide and assumed. What follows is what is SPECIFIC to the Predoctoral Fellowship, or where it departs from the AHA norm.

A. WHAT YOU (the applicant) UPLOAD — note how short this list is:
  • Proposed Research Plan — 5 pages (vs 8 for CDA/AIREA/Transformational)
  • Biosketch/Personal Statement
  • Literature Cited — 4 pages
  • Vertebrate Animal Subjects — no page limit, if applicable
  • Resubmission Modifications — 2 pages, if applicable
DEVIATION: fellowship applicants do NOT upload a Budget Justification Form or a Research Project Environment. CDA and AIREA applicants upload both (2-page DOCX templates each). For fellowships the Research Project Environment comes from the MENTOR and has NO page limit.

B. WHAT THIRD PARTIES SUPPLY — this is the bulk of the application:
  • Referees: Reference Reports, 3 required, 4 pages each
  • Mentor (and co-mentor if named): Biosketch of Mentor; Biosketch of Co-Mentor
  • From the primary mentor, each document also covering the co-mentor: Past and Current Trainees (3 pages per mentor); Training Plan for the Fellow (3 pages); Research Project Environment (no page limit)
  • Optional: Collaborating Investigator's Biosketch and Letter (5 pages); Consultant's Letter (5 pages)

C. TWO DIFFERENT DELIVERY ROUTES — the most common mechanical error:
  • REFERENCE REPORTS are uploaded BY THE REFEREES, direct to ProposalCentral, via a system-generated email link. They are confidential: "A reference document is confidential and is not viewable by the applicant (principal investigator) or others associated with the proposal." Hard gate: "The applicant will not be able to submit the proposal until you have uploaded your reference document."
  • MENTOR DOCUMENTS go the opposite way: "Send Word or pdf documents by e-mail to the applicant. The applicant will upload the documents into the proposal." Also a gate: "The applicant will not be able to submit the application without these documents."

D. REFERENCE RULES, mechanism-specific and easy to breach:
  • Predoc/postdoc referees must use AHA's downloadable Reference Report Form (.doc), completed and saved as PDF — a structured form, not a free letter.
  • WHO CANNOT BE A REFEREE: "A mentor, co-mentor, department head, collaborating investigator or consultant contributing to the proposal may not serve as a referent." So you need three people beyond your lab's core team.
  • "Letters should be composed by the referent and should not originate from the applicant. Any appearance of substantially similar language in reference letters will be factored into the score for the Evaluation of the Applicant, which will impact the overall score." Drafting all three yourself is detected and scored against you.
  • Referees are told to "AVOID referring to personal circumstances or attributes of the applicant: Marital status, age or gender... child care or illness... roles of the applicant outside of the professional setting."

E. BIOSKETCH — predoc-specific requirements (page updated 4/27/2026):
  • NIH biosketch accepted as-is: "It is not necessary to reformat to American Heart Association page specifications."
  • REQUIRED of predoc/postdoc applicants: a Career Goals statement. "The Association requires a statement on career goals. Career goals should reflect the applicant's true plans and are not required by the Heart Association to be traditional academic or clinical research work."
  • CHANGED: "Scholastic Performance is no longer required for Fellowship applicants." Older guides and lab-recycled applications will still ask for it.
  • DEVIATION: the "safe and inclusive work environment" statement is required of "All applicants (except fellows)" — predocs are exempt.
  • Your MENTOR's biosketch must show harassment training: reviewers are asked "Did the mentor indicate in their biosketches that they have completed a recognized training specific to sexual and gender-based harassment?"
  • Delayed start, if wanted, is declared HERE: "Applicants must indicate their intent to delay the start date in the Personal Statement section of their biosketch."

F. TRAINING PLAN FOR THE FELLOW (mentor, 3 pages) — six prescribed items, including a section that must be separately titled "Instruction in responsible conduct of research and rigor and reproducibility". The mentor must also "Describe the scope and source of all funds available to the applicant" because "additional research support for the proposed project MUST come from the mentors' labs. Adequate current funding to support the fellow's project is a factor in the peer review criteria." Warning against boilerplate: "A standardized training plan will not be viewed favorably." IDPs are "not require[d] but strongly encourage[d]".

G. PAST AND CURRENT TRAINEES (mentor, 3 pages per mentor) — a prescribed table, predoctoral and postdoctoral trainees of the past five years plus current and pending, with stipend source for each; portrait or landscape allowed; co-mentor sends theirs to the primary mentor to merge.

H. AUTHORSHIP EXPECTATION, unusual and explicit: "A fellow must have primary responsibility for the writing and the preparation of the application." Reviewers are asked whether the mentor clarified "the role the applicant played in developing the proposal."

I. PRELIMINARY DATA: mentor-generated data is allowed — "A new fellow may not have had adequate time to generate preliminary data; therefore, applicants may present preliminary data generated by the mentor." (Opposite of the Innovative Project Award, where preliminary data is "not required and not accepted.")

J. HYPERLINKS BANNED — and this is a correction to a common assumption that the ban is CDA-only. The Predoctoral RFP carries it too, verbatim: "Hyperlinks to data/figures/additional information are not permitted in the Research Plan nor any other proposal documents. This includes use of the Precision Medicine Platform for applications and peer review purposes." So the PMP route of pasting a notebook URL is NOT available to predoc applicants.

K. FORMATTING, enforced by administrative withdrawal not by warning: single-spaced; max 15 characters per inch including symbols, punctuation and spaces; margins no less than ¾ inch; max 50 lines per page; Arial 12-pt (Windows) or Helvetica 12-pt (Mac); separate PDF files per document. Mentor documents must follow the same rules — the biosketch is the only exemption.

L. IN-FORM LIMITS: Project Title 120 characters; Summary for Non-scientists 2,500 characters with a live readability gate — "If your summary is written above the 12th-grade level, your proposal cannot be submitted"; Data Sharing Plan research output 2,050 characters, limits-to-sharing 1,000.

M. NO SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL, EVER: "Only the required documents can be submitted; there is no mechanism for supplemental materials."

N. AI DISCLOSURE: LLM use to generate or edit content is permitted but "must be disclosed at the time of submission. Disclosure of this information does not impact peer review." Undisclosed use, if identified, means administrative withdrawal.

O. INSTITUTIONAL: "All submissions require the signature of a designated institutional representative." Awards are limited to U.S.-based non-profit institutions. No indirect costs are paid on fellowships, and AHA "does not require use of the NIH salary cap."

P. CO-FUNDED MONEY, no separate application: the Predoctoral RFP states that "additional collaboration money has been designated through the Heart Association/Children's Heart Foundation Congenital Heart Defect Research Awards, Autism Speaks, the Barth Syndrome Foundation, the California Walnut Commission, and the Foundation for Sarcoidosis Research." You apply to the ordinary Predoctoral Fellowship; if your topic fits congenital heart defects, autism and cardiovascular/cerebrovascular health, Barth syndrome, sarcoidosis, or dietary-pattern/walnut research, designated partner funds are in play within the same competition.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES. Everything below is from AHA's own Predoctoral Fellowship page unless marked.

=== WHAT BLOCKS YOU ===

1. ONE AHA AWARD AT A TIME — and this is STRICTER than AHA's general FAQ, which is the trap. Predoctoral RFP: "A Predoctoral Fellowship student may hold only one Association research award at a time." The funder-wide FAQ says the opposite-sounding thing: "An individual may hold more than one American Heart Association award concurrently but may only hold one career development/recognition award (Career Development Award, Established Investigator Award, Merit Award) at a time." For a predoc the mechanism rule governs. Do not let a student reason from the FAQ.

2. NO COMPARABLE CONCURRENT FELLOWSHIP AS TOP-UP: "the awardee may not hold a comparable award (such as another fellowship) as a source of supplementation."

3. RANK: "This award is not for individuals of faculty/staff rank." Full-time matriculated doctoral student only.

4. ONE APPLICATION PER DEADLINE: "An applicant may submit only one Predoctoral Fellowship application per deadline."

5. YOUR MENTOR CAN DISQUALIFY YOU — the item nobody checks. "A mentor may supervise no more than four Association-funded fellows (predoctoral and/or postdoctoral) and no more than two Association-supported student fellows (undergraduate and/or medical/graduate students) at any time." Ask your prospective mentor how many AHA fellows they currently hold BEFORE you start writing.

6. DUPLICATE CONTENT WITH YOUR OWN MENTOR: "the submission of an application with identical or significantly similar content from a mentor to a grant program and his/her fellow to a fellowship program is prohibited. In such cases, both applications may be removed from funding consideration." Also: "Submission of an application with identical or significantly similar content as a submission by another investigator is prohibited."

7. RESUBMISSION CAP: original plus two resubmissions; "The same or similar proposal submitted for the fourth time will be withdrawn."

8. Other administrative-withdrawal grounds: ineligibility for the programme; non-compliance with format requirements; a proposal duplicated by another applicant; undisclosed LLM/AI use.

=== WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half applicants are never told ===

1. AN EXISTING NON-AHA TRAINING GRANT DOES NOT DISQUALIFY YOU; YOU DEFER. Verbatim: "An applicant who receives predoctoral funding, but has an ongoing training grant from another source, may defer the start of the award up to six months to complete the existing fellowship. Prior approval is required." So a current NIH F31, F30, institutional T32 or other external fellowship is NOT a bar to applying or to being funded — it shifts your start date. This is the single highest-value fact in this record for a PhD student who assumes they are ineligible.

2. THE PREDOC-TO-POSTDOC BRIDGE IS EXPLICIT: "An awardee may apply for an Association Postdoctoral Fellowship in the last year of the Predoctoral Fellowship."

3. DELAYED START UP TO SIX MONTHS generally, "This includes applicants with clinical appointments" — but you must declare it in the Personal Statement of your biosketch at submission. Carve-out on the carve-out: "The Association does not permit delayed start requests for completion of requisite coursework for the pre-doctoral program."

4. SUPPLEMENTATION IS ALLOWED: "The Association allows supplementation from other sources to meet the sponsoring institution's stipend and benefit levels" — you may be topped up to your institution's standard stipend from departmental or institutional funds; only a comparable award (another fellowship) is barred as the top-up source.

5. YOUR MENTOR APPLYING IN THE SAME CYCLE DOES NOT BLOCK YOU: "If a grant application is submitted by the sponsor of a fellowship application, both applications may be funded if there is no duplication of aims." Distinct aims, both fundable.

6. CO-MENTORS ARE EXEMPT from the four-fellow mentor cap: "This restriction does not apply to co-mentors." A mentor at the cap can still support you as co-mentor.

7. SFRN FELLOWS EXCLUDED from that cap ("Fellows who are part of an Strategic Research Network are excluded"), and funder-wide, "Strategically Focused Research Network personnel may also hold individual Heart Association awards."

8. RESUBMISSION IS ALLOWED — Predoctoral Fellowship is named on AHA's enumerated list of programmes that accept resubmissions. Original plus two resubmissions.

9. NO RESIDENCY PRE-REQUISITE: "Applicants are not required to reside in the United States for any period before applying." Visa status is judged "at the time of proposal submission – not award start date"; F-1 and J-1 are accepted for pre- and postdoctoral fellows specifically, where other AHA mechanisms require H-1B or equivalent.

10. NO INSTITUTIONAL CV BAR: awards go to any U.S.-based non-profit institution able to conduct the work, and AHA separately addresses applicants whose "lab or department is not a primarily cardiovascular or neurology discipline."

THERE IS NO PROGRAMME OFFICER. Do not build a "talk to your PO first" step into a predoc timeline — AHA's staff role is administrative; the science judgement sits with volunteer reviewers and the Research Committee. What exists instead, in the order a student should use it:

1. FREE AHA WEBINARS WITH LIVE Q&A — the closest substitute, and the sanctioned one. Confirmed live on the Application Resources page today: Wednesday September 23, noon ET; Tuesday October 6, 3 p.m. ET; Thursday October 22, noon ET; Friday November 13, 1 p.m. ET. A recording of the July 7, 2026 session is posted. Register by clicking the date. Slides can be requested in advance from apply@heart.org (offered for accessibility; the request works). These cover "upcoming research award offerings, application tips, and understanding the peer review process."

2. apply@heart.org or +1 (214) 360-6107 (option 1) — the applicant assistance team. AHA publishes the list of questions this mailbox handles, which is an honest map of its scope: eligibility for a given programme, how much detail the Research Plan needs, whether you may submit more than one proposal, figures and legends, whether an NIH-format biosketch is acceptable, membership help, paying personnel from the grant, deadline extensions, replacing a document. Note what is NOT on that list: scientific fit, feedback on aims, which committee will like your proposal.

3. FOR REFERENCE-CONTENT QUESTIONS specifically (your referees will ask): apply@heart.org or +1-214-360-6107. For ProposalCentral login or upload trouble, referees included: pcsupport@altum.com, +1-800-875-2562 US/Canada, +1-703-964-5840 international — Altum is a separate company with its own holiday calendar.

4. OTHER ROUTED MAILBOXES: awards@heart.org (post-award), peerreview@heart.org / voicemail 214-360-6108 (peer review), ResearchData@heart.org (reSEARCH@Heart portal), datascience@heart.org (Precision Medicine Platform — but see the hyperlink ban, PMP output cannot be linked in a predoc application). Membership: +1-888-242-2453 or 214-570-5935.

ABSOLUTELY PROHIBITED — say this to students plainly: "An applicant is prohibited from contacting peer reviewers. This is a form of scientific misconduct and will result in the removal of the application from funding consideration and institutional notification of misconduct."

WHEN: eligibility and mechanism questions belong BEFORE the portal opens (RFP posts late April, portal opens only 8 weeks out). Once inside ProposalCentral, contact is about mechanics. AFTER SUBMISSION it is routed through your institution — "You must first obtain consent from your grants officer before contacting the Association" — and "The program cannot be changed once a proposal has been submitted."

THE LEVER THAT IS ACTUALLY IN YOUR HANDS, in place of an NIH assignment-request letter: your Science Keywords choose your review committee. "Selecting the Science Keywords that best describe your proposed work is important for sorting your proposal to the most appropriate review group." The committee list is published at https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/peer-review/aha-science-keywords — read it and choose deliberately rather than accepting a default.

A PREDOC-SPECIFIC NOTE ON PEER-REVIEW SERVICE: AHA is publicly short of reviewers and is recruiting hard, but accepts reviewers from Assistant Professor level upward — so unlike a postdoc or new faculty member, a predoctoral student cannot use reviewer service as their route to seeing how AHA scores. For a predoc the equivalent move is to ask their MENTOR, or a recent awardee (see examples), what a funded application looked like.

AHA does not publish funded applications or summary statements. You get your own critiques in ProposalCentral, nobody else's. Ranked by what a predoc can actually act on:

1. READ FUNDED PREDOC ABSTRACTS — reSEARCH@Heart, https://heart.dimensions.ai/discover/grant (Dimensions-powered; reached from AHA at https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/aha-research-accomplishments/research-at-heart-interactive-research-portal). VERIFIED WORKING TODAY: a free-text search for "predoctoral fellowship" returns 5,699 grants and 5,933 linked publications, each record showing title, PI, institution, dollar amount, start-end years and a several-hundred-word abstract behind "Show abstract", with records labelled "(AHA Program: Predoctoral Fellowship)". Left-hand facets are START YEAR, ACTIVE YEAR, PROGRAM, RESEARCHER, RESEARCH ORGANIZATION, LOCATION and RESEARCH CATEGORIES. THE MOVE: set PROGRAM to Predoctoral Fellowship and START YEAR to the most recent year, then read twenty abstracts before drafting — that is the closest thing to a model lay/technical summary at your career stage. AHA's cautions: it is "not a reporting tool", publication indexing is incomplete, exports cap at 500 records, and "the portal is best used to look for EXAMPLES of funding, rather than total Association funding on a particular topic." Questions: ResearchData@heart.org. Walkthrough video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mko3FwjDtlI

2. FIND A LIVING PERSON WHO JUST WON ONE — https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/researchers-at-heart/new-aha-research-awardees. VERIFIED TODAY: the July 1, 2026 cohort has 237 awardees of which 70 are Predoctoral Fellowships (the largest category), filterable by award, institution and state (top institutions listed: Stanford 13, Ohio State 12, UCSF 10, Mass General 8, Michigan 7, Colorado 7; top states CA 38, OH 25, NY 21, MA 20). AHA explicitly sanctions the approach: "Please reach out to awardees in your institution or your field to connect." Filter to Predoctoral Fellowship + your own institution or state and email one. This is the route to a real, recent, successful predoc application — which AHA staff will not give you.

3. FULL APPLICATIONS WITH REVIEWER CRITIQUES, via universities rather than AHA. UNC's TIBBS grant-examples library (https://tibbs.unc.edu/fellowship-grant-training/grant/) is reported to hold four funded AHA proposals (2012-2013), one of which includes "the entire proposal and reviewer comments". CAVEATS I could not clear: access is gated behind a UNC ONYEN login so I could not verify current contents, and 2012-13 documents predate the current instructions — use them for argument and structure, never for formatting. THE GENERALISABLE MOVE: ask your own graduate school, research development office or library whether it keeps a funded-proposal bank; AHA predoc fellowships are commonly in them, and your own institution's copies will be more recent.

4. AHA'S OWN STARTER MATERIALS, free, before you write anything:
   • Application Instructions PDF, 57 pages — https://professional.heart.org/-/media/PHD-Files/Research/Application-Instructions/AHA_Research_Funding_Application_Instructions_AC.pdf ("2027 Research Funding Application Instructions Rev. 9/14/2026")
   • Reference Report Form (.doc) template your three referees must complete — from https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/application-resources/required-application-documents/reference-information. Send it to them yourself; do not assume they will find it.
   • Mentor's instruction page, with a worked example table for Past and Current Trainees — https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/application-resources/required-application-documents/sponsor-mentor-information. Send this to your mentor early; 40% of your score rides on documents they write.
   • Biosketch instructions incl. the predoc Career Goals requirement — https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/application-resources/required-application-documents/biosketch-instructions, plus NIH sample biosketch DOCX files (predoctoral version).
   • AHA video on explaining your research to non-scientists — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=04ZEyfM1T2s — and readable.com to pre-check your lay summary's grade level before pasting it in, since above 12th grade the portal blocks submission.
   • Archived Predoctoral RFPs for award-start 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 at https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/awardee-resources/past-rfps — useful for seeing what changed year to year (they 403 a plain fetch; open them in a browser).
   • Published success rate for this mechanism: 22.0% FY25-26 — https://professional.heart.org/en/research-programs/success-rates
result.resubmission_note:
ALLOWED. The Predoctoral Fellowship is on AHA's enumerated list of programmes that accept resubmissions. Cap: "the original plus two resubmissions"; "The same or similar proposal submitted for the fourth time will be withdrawn."

No separate resubmission deadline — a resubmission goes in at the same early-August deadline, and the one-application-per-deadline rule means one attempt per year. In practice a predoc has a narrow window: three tries at one per year, against a degree clock, so a first-year or second-year student who applies early has room to iterate and a fifth-year does not.

WHAT COUNTS: "A resubmission is the same or similar proposal (similar aims) as one submitted previously... If major changes are made to the proposal or if this is a different/new project, it is not considered a resubmission." You tick a box in Section 1 (Project Title) of ProposalCentral and say whether the prior application was in ProposalCentral or the legacy Grants@Heart system.

REQUIRED EXTRA DOCUMENT — the introduction-equivalent: "Resubmission Modifications", 2-page limit, confirmed on the fellowship required-documents list. AHA: "specify significant changes made in response to major comments/criticisms from the scientific critiques, and explain how the proposal has been strengthened or modified (additions, deletions, revisions). It is essential that this document complies exactly with the association's Page Setup/Formatting Requirements."

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING: "when possible, a resubmitted proposal will be assigned to at least one of the previous primary reviewers. Reviewers of resubmitted proposals will be provided with the critiques and scores from the previous round for reference." Someone who read your last version reads this one against it — answer the critiques point by point and say where you did so.

PREDOC-SPECIFIC CAUTION: if the weakness was in the mentor's 40% — training plan, mentor funding, trainee track record — the fix is in documents your mentor writes, and a resubmission that changes only your 5-page Research Plan will not move the score.

NOT ALLOWED: "It is not acceptable to resubmit a proposal previously submitted by another investigator."

TIME WINDOW: NOT FOUND. Neither the RFP nor the 57-page Application Instructions states an expiry on resubmission eligibility. The only time-shaped constraint is one application per programme per fiscal year (July 1-June 30).

VOLUNTARY WITHDRAWAL: allowed in writing at any time to apply@heart.org, with email confirmation.

TRIAGE INTERACTS WITH THIS: with a minimum of half of submissions triaged and AHA's two documents disagreeing on whether triaged proposals receive written critiques, plan for the possibility of resubmitting with no reviewer text to answer.

You may submit more than one white paper across disciplines but "must acknowledge so on each submission."
   Format: 5 pages maximum, excluding cover page, CV and references; 8.5x11, 1-inch margins, 1.5-line spacing, Times New Roman or Garamond 12 pt.
   Portal: NOT Grants.gov — a Qualtrics form, https://afosr.gov1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eKuTqm9qezoDYep . Support: afosryip@us.af.mil.

NAVY (white paper forbidden): "IMPORTANT NOTE: White Papers are NOT being solicited and will NOT be accepted. This NOFO is for proposal submissions only." ONR instead offers an optional, informal route — "A brief topic description may be submitted to facilitate these discussions but are not required," emailed to the Program Officer with ONRYIP@navy.mil cc'd.

ARMY: white paper optional/recommended — "discussions with the cognizant ARO TPOC identified for a given topic is strongly recommended before submission of a whitepaper or proposal."
result.review_to_award:
PECASE itself: the honour is conferred at a White House ceremony after agency recommendation, typically years after the underlying research award, and on no published schedule. The 14 January 2025 cohort was the most recent found. Award content: "Each Presidential award winner receives a citation, a plaque and funding from their agency for up to five years to advance his or her research" — i.e. the money rides on the nominating agency's own award, not on PECASE.

THE FEEDER AWARDS PUBLISH FULL DATED ARCS, which is what an applicant actually needs:

AIR FORCE FY2027 YIP (about 11 months end-to-end, ~5 months proposal-to-notification):
  09 Oct 2026 white paper → 06 Nov 2026 white paper determination → 04 Dec 2026 proposal → "We anticipate that we will notify proposers of selection or non-selection for award no later than 26 April 2027" → "We anticipate awards to be made by 01 May 2027, barring delays."
  Review body: internal, not external peer review — "We will evaluate proposals using an internal review panel."

NAVY FY2027 YIP (about 5 months end-to-end, ~3.5 months proposal-to-notification):
  30 Oct 2026 proposal → Notification of Selection for Award 16 Feb 2027 → Start Date of Grant 01 April 2027. The NOFO adds: "The award start date for budget purposes should be 01 April 2027." Schedule is captioned "These dates are estimates as of the date of this announcement."
  Review body: "The cognizant Program Officer and other Government scientific experts will perform the evaluation."

ARMY ECP: no published review timeline; rolling BAA, so timing is negotiated with the topic TPOC.

SELECTIVITY (Navy publishes real numbers, which is rare): "The ONR YIP is highly competitive with typically 10 percent or less of applicants receiving awards. For FY2026 more than 330 proposals were received, resulting in 23 awards (7%) with a total award value of $17M." FY2027 plan: $18.75M available, up to 25 awards, $750K each over 3 years. Air Force FY2027 plan: 37 traditional YIPs plus 3 funded with the Laboratory for Physical Sciences in Quantum Information Sciences, with "potential for an additional 37 YIPs funded from other AFOSR research funding"; $150,000/year for 3 years, $450,000 total, "No single year may exceed $150,000." Army ECP: "ECP awards will not exceed $120,000 per year for 3 years."
result.submission_requirements:
PECASE: nothing to submit. The applicant-facing work is entirely on the feeder award. Notably, NONE of the three DoD early-career solicitations mentions PECASE anywhere — I grepped all three full announcement PDFs for "PECASE" and "Presidential" and got no substantive hit. You cannot position yourself for PECASE through the paperwork; you get there by winning the underlying award.

NAVY FY2027 YIP (N0001426SF004) — deviations worth knowing:
  • Technical Proposal 20 pages. 8.5x11, 1-inch margins, SINGLE-spaced, Times New Roman 12 pt.
  • Excluded from the limit: cover page, table of contents, full CV, Data Management Plan, Letters of Support, Cited References, Current and Pending Support. "There are no page limitations for the budget."
  • Filename rule (different from DOE's 50): "The electronic file name for all documents submitted under this NOFO must not exceed 68 characters in length, including the file name extension."
  • LETTER OF SUPPORT IS MANDATORY AND SCORED — "An individual wishing to apply for the Young Investigator Program MUST submit a research proposal and at least one Letter of Support through the appropriate university officials." It is review criterion (4): "Letter of Support (required) - A long-term commitment by the University or Non-profit to the applicant and the proposed research." No prescribed format, but it must evidence "release time from teaching and/or administrative responsibilities, paid nine-month salary, other related research funding, related laboratory and/or computer investments, new faculty start-up package, support for applicant's graduate students/postdocs, and mentoring" and "must be clear that the university (or non-profit) is making a long-term commitment."
  • Single PI only: "This is a single PI award. Co-PIs are not allowed."
  • You must supply a Program Officer Code identifier — "Applicants who fail to provide a Program Officer Code identifier may receive a notice that their [proposal is rejected]."
  • CV is weighted: past performance is a stated criterion, and the NOFO warns "applicants are advised that the biographical information submitted... should list all past and present professional activities in their full curriculum vitae," including "fellowships in scientific professional organizations and national/international honors in scientific societies."

AIR FORCE FY2027 YIP (FA955026S0003) — deviations:
  • Proposal: "No more than twenty (20) single-sided pages," 1-inch margins, 1.5-LINE SPACING (not single), Times New Roman or Garamond 12 pt, PDF.
  • Excluded: cover page, table of contents, list of references, letters of support, CV, list of ongoing and pending research support. Warning: "The pages of proposals exceeding the page limit may not be included in the evaluation."
  • Data Management Plan required, explicitly modelled on NSF's.
  • Gold Standard Science attestation per Executive Order 14303 — nine listed criteria including "accepting negative results as positive outcomes" and "structured for falsifiability of hypotheses." This is new and has no DOE/NSF analogue.
  • Two different portals in one competition: white paper to Qualtrics, proposal to Grants.gov.

ARMY ECP (in ARL BAA W911NF-23-S-0001) — deviations:
  • Follows the general BAA format in Section II.D.2 — no ECP-specific page limit is stated. (Do not confuse this with the 10-page limit that applies to the Short Term Innovative Research award described immediately above it in the BAA.)
  • Institutional letter mandatory and heavily weighted: "The proposal must include a supporting letter... from the individual's Department Chairperson, Dean, Supervisor, or other official who speaks for the institution... Strong institution support for the applicant is essential." Evidence sought: "the applicant's salary, release time from administrative responsibilities, the purchase of equipment, support for the applicant's graduate students, any cost sharing, any start-up funding."
  • "Any resulting award will be made to the institution, not to the investigator."

COMMON REGISTRATION NOTE: all three run through Grants.gov, so SAM.gov/UEI and an authorised AOR are prerequisites exactly as for DOE. Cost sharing is not required and "is not an evaluation or selection criterion" (AFOSR).
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
WHAT DISQUALIFIES:
• PECASE, permanently and government-wide: "Individuals can receive only one PECASE award in their careers." (NSF and DOE PECASE pages, identical wording.) A PECASE from any agency bars a second from any other.
• PECASE citizenship: "To be eligible for a PECASE Award, an individual must be a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident."
• NAVY YIP — a prior Navy YIP is fatal: "Prior ONR YIP Award recipients are ineligible to apply." Also "Tenured faculty are ineligible to apply" and "A PI may submit only one application under this solicitation."
• NAVY YIP clock and rank: PI must be "a U.S. citizen, national, or permanent resident (on the date proposals are due), holding a first or second full-time tenure-track or tenure-track-equivalent faculty position at that university, and has received his/her PhD or equivalent degree on or after 01/01/2019."
• AIR FORCE YIP clock: "Doctorate no earlier than 01 April 2019"; PI must be a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident, and "You must have permanent residency at the time of proposal submission."
• AIR FORCE ineligible entities: "Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs)", "Department of War (DoW) Laboratories", and "Individual persons or people" (i.e. you must apply through an institution).
• ARMY ECP clock: "received Ph.D. or equivalent degrees within the last five years" — two years tighter than Navy and Air Force.
• DISCLOSURE, not funding, is the live risk: "Disclosures of current and pending support made in this application may render an applicant ineligible for funding. Prior to award and throughout the period of performance, DoW may continue to request updated continuing and pending support information, which will be reviewed and may result in discontinuation of funding" (ONR). Both services screen against NSPM-33 and DoD's countering-unwanted-influence policy. The disqualifier here is an undisclosed or adverse foreign affiliation, not a domestic grant.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — the half applicants usually get wrong:
• HOLDING OTHER FEDERAL RESEARCH GRANTS DOES NOT DISQUALIFY YOU. None of the three solicitations contains any exclusion for holding NSF CAREER, DOE Early Career Research Program, NIH, or other DoD awards. There is no NIH-style "you may not have substantial independent research support" rule anywhere in the DoD early-career stack. I searched all three PDFs specifically for this.
• A PRIOR PECASE DOES NOT BAR A DoD YIP/ECP — the one-per-career rule runs on PECASE, not on the underlying grant. (Symmetrically, DOE states prior PECASE winners remain eligible for its Early Career Research Program.)
• AIR FORCE HAS NO PRIOR-YIP EXCLUSION. The AFOSR FY2027 NOFO states no bar on previous YIP recipients — the exact opposite of ONR. Do not assume the Navy rule transfers.
• AIR FORCE ADMITS NON-TENURE-TRACK APPLICANTS VIA AN INSTITUTIONAL LETTER — the biggest carve-out in this set, and the one that opens the door to senior postdocs and research scientists: "you must hold a full-time, non-contractor permanent, career-competitive, or tenure-track position (based on your institution's definition) with your organization, OR your proposal must include a letter from your organization stating that you will be considered for a permanent, career-competitive, or tenure-track non-contractor position if you currently hold a short-term appointment." Navy has no equivalent — it demands a first or second tenure-track/TT-equivalent post and bars tenured faculty outright.
• ARMY ECP STATES NO CITIZENSHIP REQUIREMENT in the BAA — I searched the full ARL BAA text for "citizen" and "permanent resident" and found no PI citizenship gate. So a non-US-person can hold an ARO ECP award but could not be PECASE-nominated, since PECASE requires US citizen/national/PR. Worth knowing before anyone chases ECP for the honour rather than the money.
• LOSING THE NAVY YIP COMPETITION DOES NOT WASTE THE PROPOSAL: "A proposal not selected for the YIP may still be considered for an ONR grant award," though ONR is candid that "Historically, only a limited number of proposals initially submitted to the YIP NOFO, but not selected under that NOFO, have been awarded other funds," and that consideration "is at the discretion of the Program Officer."
• AFTER a Navy YIP you may re-compete: "Upon completion of the award, individuals may apply for continued support under ONR's Long Range BAA (or other research grant opportunities)... Continued support is not guaranteed."
• Cost sharing is not required and is not a selection criterion (AFOSR), so lack of institutional match does not disadvantage you.

CALIBRATION NOTE ONR offers unprompted: "The YIP is not a 'research initiation' opportunity with standards that are less demanding than ONR's other research grant programs; instead, it is intended to confer honor upon awardees beyond the funding being provided."
result.resubmission_note:
PECASE: no resubmission concept — there is nothing to resubmit. You are nominated or you are not, and you can only ever win once.

FEEDER AWARDS — no NIH-style A1 machinery at any of the three, but the rules differ:
• NAVY: one application per PI per competition. A declined proposal can be brought back in a later annual cycle while you still meet the PhD-date and first/second-TT-position tests — but the eligibility window is what closes the door, not a resubmission cap. Note the Navy's resubmission mechanic for a rejected upload: "Block 2, 'Type of Application' on the SF 424 should be marked 'New' on the resubmission." There is no introduction page, no attempt cap, no stated waiting period.
• AIR FORCE: no cap on attempts stated, but every cycle demands a fresh gating white paper — a previous white paper and PO feedback do not carry over ("No exceptions will be granted"). So a reapplication is a full restart from the October white paper, not a revision of a prior file.
• ARMY: rolling BAA, so resubmission is simply a new submission whenever you like while W911NF-23-S-0001 is open (through 20 November 2027).

The binding constraint across all three is the PhD clock, not attempt count: Navy PhD on/after 01/01/2019, Air Force doctorate no earlier than 01 April 2019, Army within the last five years. Each year you defer is a year of eligibility spent. Unlike DOE SC, none of these announcements threatens to decline an unrevised resubmission without review.
result.program_officer_contact:
FOR PECASE ITSELF: no contact route exists and none is published. The nomination is internal to each agency, and — a real finding — none of the three DoD early-career solicitations mentions PECASE at all. There is no one to lobby. Contacting anyone "about PECASE" is wasted effort; contact the feeder programme's officer about the science instead.

NAVY — contact is STRONGLY ENCOURAGED and named in caps in the NOFO: "Applicants are STRONGLY ENCOURAGED to contact the appropriate Program Officer who is the point of contact for a specific technical area to discuss their research ideas before submitting a proposal."
  • Find your PO: https://www.onr.navy.mil/our-research/our-program-officers or https://www.onr.navy.mil/our-research/onr-technology-and-research
  • How: optional brief topic description emailed to the PO with ONRYIP@navy.mil cc'd — "The ONRYIP@navy.mil need only be cc'd on the first email correspondence."
  • Why it pays: "Such discussions can clarify the content and breadth of the priority research areas and enhance the match between a subsequent proposal and Department of the Navy research needs. Please allow adequate time for such discussions."
  • Programme questions: YIP Program Manager, ONR Code 34, ONRYIP@navy.mil. Submission/administrative questions: Veronica Lacey, Grants Officer, ONR Code 253, veronica.y.lacey.civ@us.navy.mil. Question deadlines: eligibility/technical 16 Oct 2026, Grants Officer 29 Oct 2026, both 5:00 pm ET.
  • ACT NOW: with proposals due 30 October 2026, the window for a useful conversation is the next three to four weeks.

AIR FORCE — the white paper IS the structured conversation, and it is compulsory. Beyond it: "Proposers are encouraged to confer with the designated AFOSR Program Officer(s) prior to submitting a full proposal," and "The topic points of contact (POCs) will coordinate to provide feedback on the white papers."
  • Contact: AFOSR RBKR, afosryip@us.af.mil, 703-696-9517.
  • Hard limit on what a warm conversation buys you, stated plainly: "The Program Officer does not have the authority to make commitments for us. Grants and Contracting Officers acting within their warranted capacity are the only people authorized to make commitments for the Government."
  • Note the pre-proposal question window (17 September 2026) has just closed; answers are posted publicly by COB 24 September 2026 — read them before writing the white paper.

ARMY — "discussions with the cognizant ARO TPOC identified for a given topic is strongly recommended before submission of a whitepaper or proposal." TPOCs are listed per topic on the ARL BAA topics site. ARO, 800 Park Offices Drive, Durham NC 27709; (919) 549-0641 or (844) 668-2016. Because the BAA is rolling, there is no deadline pressure on this conversation — which makes ARO the lowest-risk first phone call for someone who has never approached a DoD programme officer.

PRACTICAL ORDER FOR A NEWCOMER: Army TPOC first (rolling, no clock, low stakes) to learn the register; then Navy PO if your work fits a Navy division; Air Force by white paper.
result.examples_or_samples:
HONEST ANSWER FIRST: there is no DoD equivalent of NIH RePORTER, no PAMS-style public abstract search, and no sample-proposal library for PECASE or for any of the three feeder awards. I found no published funded DoD YIP/ECP narrative or abstract collection. Defence basic-research proposals are treated as competition-sensitive — ONR states it treats white papers and proposals "as sensitive competitive information." Anyone promising you a DoD YIP sample proposal online is selling something.

WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS, ranked by usefulness:
1. PECASE RECIPIENT LISTS BY AGENCY — the honour roll is public even though the applications are not. NSF (https://www.nsf.gov/honorary-awards/pecase) and DOE (https://science.osti.gov/About/Honors-and-Awards/PECASE) both maintain current PECASE pages naming their recipients; the 14 January 2025 cohort included 55 DOE-funded recipients. Reading who wins tells you the career profile that gets nominated.
2. SERVICE PRESS RELEASES NAMING YIP/ECP COHORTS — e.g. ONR's PECASE release at https://www.onr.navy.mil/media-center/news-releases/onr-funded-young-innovators-recognized-president, which confirms the pipeline informally: "Briseno, Blei and Daraio also are past winners of ONR's Young Investigator Program (YIP)." Names plus institutions plus topic areas is enough to identify people in your field to email.
3. THE ANNOUNCEMENT PDFs THEMSELVES, which are unusually explicit about what wins. The Navy NOFO names the review criteria in order and states that past performance is scored and that the Letter of Support is criterion (4). The Air Force NOFO lists exactly what a white paper must contain: "Identification of proposed research and issues / Potential impact on DAF and DoW capabilities / Potential team members and development plans / Proposed technical approaches - hypothesis, theories, concepts, approaches, data measurements, and analysis." That list is effectively a white-paper outline — use it as the section headings.
4. THE PROGRAMME OFFICER, who is the real substitute for a sample. This is why both services push pre-submission contact so hard: the PO will tell you whether your idea fits the portfolio, which no document can.
5. YOUR OWN INSTITUTION'S RESEARCH DEVELOPMENT OFFICE — many keep internal libraries of previously submitted DoD proposals. For DoD this is the only realistic route to a full narrative, since there is no public release channel.

FOR PhD STUDENTS AND POSTDOCS SPECIFICALLY: none of these is open to you, and that is the useful finding. Navy requires a first or second tenure-track post and bars tenured faculty; Army requires PhD within five years; Air Force is the only one with a door ajar — a short-term appointment plus an institutional letter saying you will be considered for a permanent/career-competitive/tenure-track post. If you are a postdoc within a year or two of a faculty offer, the Air Force route is the one to read now, and the PhD clock (doctorate no earlier than 01 April 2019 for FY2027) is what you should be counting.
