result.program_name: Sea Grant John A. Knauss Marine Policy Fellowship (FY2027 cycle = "2027 class"; NOFO NOAA-OAR-SG-2027-32433)
result.funder: NOAA National Sea Grant College Program (DOC/NOAA/OAR; Assistance Listing 11.417)
result.next_deadline:
CLOSED for the 2027 class; no 2028-class date published as of 2026-09-18.

The most recent cycle carried three hard, dated deadlines (NOFO, Executive Summary, verbatim):
(1) STUDENT to state Sea Grant program: "Eligible students must submit application materials by 5:00 p.m. local time on July 1, 2026, to eligible Sea Grant programs."
(2) STATE PROGRAM letter of intent to NSGO: "prior to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) on August 12, 2026."
(3) STATE PROGRAM full package to Grants.gov/eRA: "by the deadline of 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) on August 26, 2026."

Funder page confirms closure verbatim: "Application Status: Closed / Application Deadline: July 1, 2026" and "THE APPLICATION PERIOD FOR THE 2027 KNAUSS FELLOWSHIP IS NOW CLOSED."

NEXT CYCLE: not found as a published date. A grants.gov API search for "Knauss" across posted|closed|archived|forecasted (81 hits, all statuses) returns NO FY2028 opportunity — not posted and not forecast as of 2026-09-18. The 2027 timeline table says the opportunity went live in March, so a repeat would open ~March 2027 with a student deadline ~July 2027 — but that is an INFERENCE from one restructured cycle, not a funder statement, and the 16-year prior pattern was just broken (see deadline_pattern). Do not treat ~July 2027 as a date; treat it as "watch the page from March 2027."
result.loi_required: yes — but the LOI is filed BY THE STATE SEA GRANT PROGRAM, not by the student. Students file no LOI. The student-side analogue is a strongly encouraged advance contact with the state program (see loi_deadline).
result.loi_deadline:
State-program LOI: 5:00 p.m. ET, August 12, 2026 — i.e. 6 weeks AFTER the student deadline and 2 weeks BEFORE the Grants.gov deadline. Verbatim: "Letters of intent from state Sea Grant Programs, including the attestation document and outlining the selection process, must be emailed to oar.sg.fellows@noaa.gov prior to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) on August 12, 2026." NSGO confirms receipt: "Programs will receive email confirmation of LOI receipt by COB August 14, 2026."

The LOI contains an 19-item attestation table on each applicant (items A-S), including item (M) "List of current and pending support for the student, specifically for any fellowships or internships" and confirmations that the CV, application questions, future-year plans and two letters comply with the NOFO. Practical consequence for the applicant: your state program certifies your compliance item by item, so a format violation is caught and attributed before national review.

STUDENT-SIDE PRE-SUBMISSION STEP (not an LOI, but expected), verbatim: "Student applicants are strongly encouraged to reach out to the Sea Grant program in their state/territory at least one to two months before the state application deadline to receive application support and provide notification of intent to apply. Following student application submission, the student should allow sufficient time to schedule an interview with the eligible Sea Grant program at the program's request."
result.deadline_pattern:
Annual, one cycle per class year — BUT the calendar was restructured for the 2027 class, so the long-run pattern cannot be extrapolated.

Grants.gov close dates (state-program deadline to NOAA) for every Knauss NOFO on record:
FY2010 04/03/2009 · FY2012 04/01/2011 · FY2013 03/30/2012 · FY2014 04/02/2013 · FY2015 03/31/2014 · FY2016 03/31/2015 · FY2017 03/31/2016 · FY2018 04/07/2017 · FY2019 04/06/2018 · FY2020 04/05/2019 · FY2021 04/17/2020 · FY2022 04/02/2021 · FY2023 04/01/2022 · FY2024 03/30/2023 · FY2025 03/28/2024 · FY2026 04/16/2025 — then FY2027 08/26/2026.

So: 16 consecutive cycles closed late-March to mid-April; FY2027 jumped ~4.5 months to late August. The fellowship year moved with it — the class year used to begin 1 February; the 2027 class runs "June 1, 2027 – May 31, 2028" (funder FAQ, verbatim: "The fellowship is one year (non-renewable). The dates of the official fellowship are June 1, 2027 – May 31, 2028."). This is a genuine structural change, not citation rot. Anyone advising from the historical "apply by late February/March" folklore will now be ~4 months wrong.

Published 2027 cadence (funder's own "2027 Timeline (subject to change)" table): March opportunity goes live · July student applications due · August LOI + national nomination · September-November national review and finalist notification · February-April placement weeks · March-May onboarding · June fellowship starts · following May fellowship ends.
result.review_to_award:
Long lead time — roughly 11 months from the student deadline to the fellowship start. This is the single most planning-relevant fact for a student in their final year.

2027 cycle, dated: student deadline 1 Jul 2026 → state review, minimum three separate written reviews per application, plus a state interview → state LOI 12 Aug 2026 → state submits to Grants.gov/eRA 26 Aug 2026 → national administrative review, paper reviews and panel Sept-Nov 2026 → NOTIFICATION: "It is anticipated that successful applicants will be notified in October 2026 that the Selecting Official is recommending them for funding to the NOAA Grants Officer" (unsuccessful applicants likewise "notified in October 2026") → finalists choose/justify executive vs legislative cohort (300-word or less justification) → placement weeks Feb-Apr 2027 → onboarding/security clearance Mar-May 2027 → START: "projects are expected to start no earlier than June 1, 2027", orientation 1-5 Jun 2027 → ends 31 May 2028.

Award terms: period of performance 13 months for a 12-month fellowship; "These awards cannot be renewed or deferred." Pre-award spending may be authorized 120 days before the start date.

CAUTION — the funder's own FAQ is stale against its own timeline table. The FAQ still says finalists are notified "mid- to late-summer" and that placement week falls "In October (executive fellows) or January (legislative fellows)" — that is the OLD (Feb-start) calendar. The 2027 timeline table and the NOFO both put notification in Sept-Nov/October 2026 and placement weeks in Feb-Apr 2027. Trust the NOFO and the timeline table.

Selectivity gate: each state program may forward at most six applications ("each eligible Sea Grant program may select and forward to the National Sea Grant Office up to six student applications from that program's state/territory", plus up to six more from each non-Sea-Grant state it handles). NOAA "anticipates funding not less than 35 applications" at $97,200 each (est. total $3,402,000; grants.gov numberOfAwards 35, awardCeiling $97,200). The binding competition for most applicants is therefore the STATE round, not the national one.
result.submission_requirements:
KEY DEVIATION FROM THE NORM: the student is NOT the applicant of record and never touches Grants.gov. "Students are not eligible to submit full application materials to Grants.gov." Eligible applicants are Sea Grant College, Institutional and Coherent Area Programs. SAM.gov + Grants.gov + eRA Commons registration (4-6 weeks) is the state program's burden, not the student's. You submit a PDF package to your state Sea Grant program; it is forwarded "unchanged beyond redacting PII", with only the director's letter added.

STUDENT PACKAGE — required order: CV, Application Questions, Future Year Plans, Director Letter, Academic Letter, Other Letter. Suggested filename format "{XXSG}_2027 Knauss_{Student's Last Name}".
1. Curriculum vitae — "not to exceed two pages". No personal contact information and no web links (LinkedIn, articles, blogs); anything included gets redacted.
2. Personal education and career development response — "should not exceed 1,500 words total", answered as SIX separate sub-responses under the funder's own section headers (headers don't count toward the limit). Section One: Career Path and Objectives (~750 words) — Prompt A: experience relating to the Sea Grant mission, emphasising distilling science for non-scientific audiences; Prompt B: why Knauss, tied to career pathway; Prompt C: transferable skills. Section Two: Career Path Experience (~750 words) — Prompt A: how you embrace public service; Prompt B: a project with collaborators/community/partners toward a common goal; Prompt C: a challenge you overcame in a leadership role, with reflection. Each subsection "Suggest 250 words".
3. Relevant Coursework and Future Year Plans — "not to exceed one page single-spaced", and must list classes/plans for the coming spring, summer and fall terms.
4. Exactly TWO letters of recommendation, each "not to exceed two pages, single-spaced", writer's name and position clearly indicated; at least one "from a faculty member associated with the student's current enrollment who has knowledge of the student's academic and research (when applicable) performance". Letters must address: self-motivation, response to setbacks, teamwork, collaborative leadership, willingness to learn a new skill or topic, academic performance and potential.
   HIGH-VALUE, COUNTERINTUITIVE: "Any letters beyond the two letters of recommendation and the eligible Sea Grant director's letter will be disregarded by the selection panel. Letters of endorsement from members of Congress, friends, or relatives will not be accepted." More letters actively cost you nothing but gain you nothing — and a congressional letter is explicitly refused.
5. A mandatory INTERVIEW with the state Sea Grant program, after which the state director writes a signed letter of recommendation (≤ two pages, single-spaced) "built from the totality of the student application package and an interview with the student", covering alignment with Knauss goals, skills, your answers on interpersonal skills and managing expectations in challenging situations, and "any gaps in the CV".
6. Transcripts are NOT a national required component; the state attests to enrollment and is "encouraged to use transcripts", so individual state programs may ask for them.
7. Feedback is built in: "Blinded reviewer comments will be provided to the students, including discussion of the LORs."

FORMATTING (state program's eRA submission, but your PDFs must comply): all attachments PDF; no "bundling"/"portfolio" combined PDFs; filenames ≤ 50 characters including spaces; ≤ 100 MB; no page larger than 8.5" x 11". NOAA points applicants at the NIH format-attachments guide and warns that "Recent applicants have encountered rejected applications for formatting issues".

NOTE A CONFLICT ON THE FUNDER'S OWN SITE: the Knauss FAQ says "Applications must be submitted to your state Sea Grant program by June 3, 2026", while the banner, the landing page, the NOFO and the timeline table all say July 1, 2026. June 3, 2026 is the enrollment-eligibility cutoff elsewhere in the NOFO, so the FAQ appears to have reused the wrong date. The NOFO Executive Summary governs: July 1, 2026.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
This mechanism has NO prior-funding exclusion in the usual sense — no rule bars holding or having held another fellowship or federal award. The bars are about prior participation in Knauss itself and about applicant conduct. Both halves below are verbatim from NOFO Section III.C "Other Criteria that Affect Eligibility" unless noted.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU:
1. Prior success in this competition: "Student applicants who have been accepted as national finalists and/or become fellows are not eligible to apply again without the written permission of the NSGO Fellowships Manager, which will only be granted in response to exceptional life events."
2. Contacting host offices early: "Prior contact/arrangements made with possible host offices before the start of the placement week will be cause for immediate disqualification from the process." (Unusual and easy to trip — normal fellowship networking behaviour is fatal here.)
3. No deferral route: "These awards cannot be renewed or deferred." You cannot bank an offer for a later year.
4. Practical, not formal: you must be able to pass a federal background security check, and must be prepared to relocate to the Washington, D.C. area.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES YOUR ELIGIBILITY:
1. Alternates keep their eligibility: "If alternates are selected, they are eligible for re-application if they withdraw prior to accepting a finalist position or are not offered a finalist position and would otherwise still be eligible to apply."
2. The exclusion is bounded by a definition: "A national finalist is defined as a student applicant who goes through the review process and is selected at the national level for the fellowship program" and "Student applicants are considered finalists until they are paired with a host office during the placement process." Applicants who competed and were NOT selected at the national level are not caught by the bar.
3. Other fellowships and internships do NOT disqualify. They must be DISCLOSED — the state program's LOI attestation requires "List of current and pending support for the student, specifically for any fellowships or internships" — but nothing in the NOFO makes current or prior support an eligibility bar. Disclosure, not exclusion.
4. Dual nationals are eligible: "while this fellowship is open to dual citizens, a significant number of participating federal host offices are unable to accept dual citizens as fellows. This may reduce the number of placement opportunities available to dual citizens. Note: Dual citizens are eligible for both the Executive and Legislative cohorts." Eligibility intact; placement pool narrower.
5. No cost share: "Standard Sea Grant cost sharing is not required for this call."

ONE SUBTLETY WORTH FLAGGING: other federal funding cannot make you ineligible, but it can affect selection. Among the Selecting Official's listed factors for awarding out of rank order is "Duplication of other projects funded or considered for funding by NOAA/Federal agencies" (also "Applicant's prior award performance"). So overlap is a selection consideration at the national stage, not an eligibility gate.
result.program_officer_contact:
No named individual program officer is published for this mechanism; NOAA uses a role mailbox.

NATIONAL (NOFO Section VII, verbatim): "Contact the Sea Grant Knauss Fellowship Program Manager, National Sea Grant College Program; Tel: (240) 507-4825; E-mail: oar.sg.fellows@noaa.gov". Mailing address: NOAA Sea Grant, 1315 East-West Highway, Silver Spring, MD 20910. The grants.gov record additionally lists a grants-management contact, Laura Hansen, tel 240-653-9028, same email.

WHO YOU SHOULD ACTUALLY TALK TO: your STATE Sea Grant program, not the national office. Pre-submission contact is explicitly expected — "Student applicants are strongly encouraged to reach out to the Sea Grant program in their state/territory at least one to two months before the state application deadline to receive application support and provide notification of intent to apply." The FAQ reinforces it: "Reach out to the Sea Grant Program in your state. Let them know you plan to apply and ask for advice on navigating the process" and "Ask questions of your local Sea Grant program and/or the National Sea Grant Office before the deadline." Directory: https://seagrant.noaa.gov/our-story/about-sea-grant/#seagrantinyourstate

IF YOUR STATE HAS NO SEA GRANT PROGRAM (funder's list: AZ, AR, CO, ID, IA, KS, KY, MO, MT, NE, NV, NM, ND, OK, SD, TN, UT, WV, WY): email oar.sg.fellows@noaa.gov to be assigned one. This is a required paperwork step, not just advice — "A written statement from the National Sea Grant Knauss Fellowship Program Manager referring the student to the most appropriate eligible Sea Grant program will be provided to the student and must be submitted to the State Sea Grant program through which they are applying." Start this early; it gates your application.

Conflict of interest on the director's letter: "If a conflict of interest exists, please contact the agency contact (Section VII)."
result.examples_or_samples:
No funded application or successful personal statement is published for this mechanism. What IS published, and is the realistic substitute (all on the funder's site; the guides are the student-facing rewrite of the NOFO):

- 2027 Knauss Applicant Guide (student guide): https://seagrant.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/2027-Sea-Grant-Knauss-Marine-Policy-Fellowship-Student-Guide_Updated-06092026.pdf
- 2027 General Student Applicant Guide to Sea Grant Fellowships: https://seagrant.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/2027-General-Student-Applicant-Guide-to-Sea-Grant-Fellowships.pdf
- Knauss factsheet/overview: https://seagrant.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/2026-Knauss-Factsheet.pdf
- FY27 applicant webinar slides: https://seagrant.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/FY27-Knauss-Fellowship-Applicant-Presentation_Updated-06092026.pdf.pdf
- Application Tips graphics, 8 images: https://seagrant.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/1_Knauss-Applicant-Tips_IG_new-logo.png through .../8_Knauss-Applicant-Tips_IG_new-logo.png
- REAL HOST-OFFICE POSITION DESCRIPTIONS — the closest thing to "what the job actually is", and the funder points applicants at them: 2023 executive positions https://seagrant.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/2023-Knauss-Executive-Positions.pdf and 2023 legislative positions https://seagrant.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/2023-Knauss-Legislative-Positions.pdf
- Current fellows and alumni, Knauss blog, alumni cards and videos, Lunch & Learns: https://seagrant.noaa.gov/communities/students/graduate-fellows/knauss-fellowship-program/knauss-current-fellows-alumni/ (the alumni network is the practical route to reading a real application — ask a current fellow from your state)
- The background-check form you will later complete, OPM OF-0306: https://www.opm.gov/forms/pdf_fill/of0306.pdf

Two further routes, both stated by the funder rather than inferred:
- Reviewer feedback on your OWN application is guaranteed: "Blinded reviewer comments will be provided to the students, including discussion of the LORs." A prior unsuccessful (non-finalist) attempt therefore yields a written critique you can apply next cycle.
- Funded applications are in principle public records: "The grant application and final report of all funded grants are public documents, except for privileged information or material that is personal, proprietary or otherwise exempt from disclosure under law." That is a FOIA route, not a download link.

The abstract template is NOT public — "the National Sea Grant Office will provide a recommended abstract template to eligible applicants" (i.e. to the state programs). Your state program is the source for it, and for sample materials generally.
result.resubmission_note:
Reapplication is allowed and is the normal path for unsuccessful applicants — the only bar is on those who already succeeded. Not eligible to reapply without written NSGO permission: anyone "accepted as national finalists and/or become fellows", permission "only be granted in response to exceptional life events". Everyone else — including alternates who withdrew before accepting a finalist position or were never offered one — "are eligible for re-application ... and would otherwise still be eligible to apply".

The real constraint on a second attempt is not a resubmission rule but the enrollment window: each cycle requires enrolment in a graduate program within that cycle's stated dates (for FY2027: "at any point between the onset of the 2025 Fall Term ... and June 3, 2026"). A student who graduates loses eligibility by that clock, not by any resubmission cap.

No "response to previous review" document is required, and there is no resubmission-specific format. Blinded reviewer comments are returned to students, so a resubmission can be revised against actual panel feedback.

TOOLING FACT, not a finding: seagrant.noaa.gov sits behind an AWS WAF (response header 'x-amzn-waf-action: challenge'). WebFetch returns HTTP 403 and curl is challenged even with a browser user-agent; only a rendering browser reaches the site, and it needs a ~3-4 second wait before the body populates (an immediate read returns an empty body, which is what defeated the previous run). All seagrant.noaa.gov content here came via the rendering browser. The NOFO text came from the grants.gov attachment, which is NOT behind the WAF.

Could not extract the TEXT of the 2027 Knauss Applicant Guide, the General Student Guide or the FY27 webinar slides — same WAF block, and the browser's PDF viewer yields no extractable text. Their URLs are verified live (they are linked from the funder page); their contents are unverified. Any page/word limit in those guides that differs from the NOFO is therefore unchecked. The NOFO limits recorded here are authoritative.

Whether individual state Sea Grant programs set their own INTERNAL deadlines earlier than the national 1 July student deadline — not verified for any specific state. This is materially important (the state round is the real competition) and highly likely to vary. WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted (200/200) before this could be checked, so no state program page was examined.

No publicly posted funded application, successful personal statement, or annotated sample was found for this mechanism. Notification: "April – All applicants for the 2027 competition are notified of their application status"; the Process & Eligibility page words it as "All applicants will be notified of competition results by the end of April of the award year." Observed confirmation: the press room item "SEARLE SCHOLARS PROGRAM NAMES 15 SCIENTISTS AS SEARLE SCHOLARS FOR 2026" is dated 29 April 2026. Planning consequence: a candidate appointed in mid-2026 who submits 30 Sept 2026 is budgeting for salary/startup coverage through June 2027.
result.submission_requirements: Where it deviates from the ordinary norm: there is no public solicitation document, no page limits, no component list and no reference-letter requirement published anywhere on the funder's site — I checked every application-information page. What the funder does publish: the application is online-only ("must be submitted online"), and access to the online system comes from the "Letter of invitation and online nomination instructions" sent to participating institutions on 1 June. So the actual application instructions are distributed through the institution, not the web, and the only way to see them before nomination is to ask your institution's named limited-submission contact. Institutional sign-off is not a formality here — it is the entry condition (award "made to tax-exempt institutions described in section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code which must be participating in our program. Awards are not made to individuals"). Two pre-submission consultations the funder explicitly requires of institutions: (a) "Institutions which do not have tenure-track appointments should consult with the Scientific Director of the Program regarding eligibility of selected applicants PRIOR to nominating such individuals"; (b) renomination of a previously unsuccessful candidate — "Institutions should consult with the Scientific Director of the Program regarding renomination of such individuals." Scope screen to apply before spending effort: fields are "biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, immunology, neuroscience, pharmacology, and related areas", and the program "does not ordinarily support purely clinical research" (mixed clinical/basic can qualify; an MD-only applicant is eligible "as long as they are researchers and not purely clinicians. Award terms to budget against: "$450,000 for a three-year period with $150,000 payable in the first year and equal sums payable in the second and third years"; publications must acknowledge the "Searle Scholars Program". All of the above is from the funder's own pages, fetched directly — no search index was needed for any claim in this record.
result.prior_funding_conflicts: Both halves, and this mechanism is unusually generous on one and unusually strict on the other. PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (funder's own FAQ, verbatim): "Are there restrictions on receiving or applying for other funding? The Searle Scholars Program does not place any restrictions on funding from other sources of support. The Searle Scholars award is meant to supplement other funding received by an investigator." That is a blanket carve-out — an NIH R01, K-award, NSF CAREER, HHMI/Pew/Packard/Beckman/Sloan money, or a pending application does NOT disqualify you and does not need to be relinquished; Searle is explicitly designed to sit on top. Nothing on the funder's site restricts concurrent or prior grants. WHAT ACTUALLY DISQUALIFIES is not funding at all — it is the appointment clock and the nomination gate: (1) "Applicants should have begun their appointment as an independent investigator at the assistant professor level on or after May 1, 2025" for the 2027 cycle (i.e. ~16 months before the deadline; the equivalent date rolls forward one year per cycle) — start earlier and you are out; (2) "The appointment must be their first tenure-track position (or its nearest equivalent)" — any prior independent-investigator appointment kills eligibility regardless of funding history; (3) not being nominated by a participating institution — "Individuals who have not been nominated by a participating institution cannot apply"; (4) purely clinical research. THE CARVE-OUT ON THE CLOCK, which is worth knowing because it is discretionary and rarely used: "The Program does consider extenuating circumstances and may make exceptions on a case by case basis. Favorable considerations include a start date very close to our stated date, an unusually short period of post doctoral training, and parental leave." That request goes to the Scientific Director before nomination. Citizenship is NOT a bar: "Are applicants required to be U.S. Citizens? No, however, awardees must be legally employed at a United States degree granting or research institution."

What IS available, and is the closest usable substitute: every awardee since at least 2020 has a public profile page with project title and a substantial lay research description (~280–300 words, written for a general reader, building from context to clinical relevance rather than an abstract's methods/results shape). One round per year, in the fall (October), single-step. Contrast for planning: Core LOIs land roughly every 3.5 months (March / July / October); Dissertation Research Grants "Next deadline: February 2027" (month only); Causal Research on the Criminal Justice System "Next deadline: April 2027" (month only). Not applicable — there is no LOI or pre-proposal stage. RSF FAQ, verbatim: "Do I have to submit a letter of inquiry before submitting an application? No, pipeline grant applications do not require an initial letter of inquiry." The review-process page confirms: "All early career grants (pipeline grants; dissertation grants; causal research on criminal justice system grants) follow a one-step application process with the direct submission of a proposal."

THE TRAP IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF AN LOI — a forced choice against the Core track in the same fall window. Deadlines page: "Note: Applicants can apply for either the Sheldon Danziger Pipeline Grants Competition or the October LOI deadline, but not both." FAQ: "Can I apply for a Pipeline Grant and a Core Research Grant at the same time? No. Applicants may apply for either a Core Research Grant or a Pipeline Grant at the fall deadlines, but not both." So the decision to take at ~2 months out is Pipeline (one step, 7 pages, decision ~March, up to $50k solo) versus Core LOI (two steps, 4-page LOI then invited 10-page proposal, ~8 months to decision, up to $200k) — you cannot hedge across both in the fall.

Also: "Can I submit multiple applications? No. Applicants may only submit one Pipeline Grant proposal per cycle." (Core, by contrast, allows multiple LOIs for different projects in one cycle.)
result.review_to_award:
SUBMISSION -> DECISION: RSF gives two figures; the mechanism-specific one is the later.
- Funder-wide early-career norm (/apply/info/process): "The full review process takes about three to four months from a proposal deadline to a final decision."
- Pipeline-specific FAQ: "How long does the application review take? We anticipate decisions by early March." Applied to the 21 Oct 2026 deadline that is ~4.5 months, i.e. decisions expected EARLY MARCH 2027. Use the FAQ figure — it is the mechanism's own.

THE STAGES (Pipeline runs the early-career one-step track, no Board of Trustees step is listed):
1. Internal staff screen — "Approximately 33-50 percent of the proposals will move to the next stage." (Kinder than Core, where only 25-35% of LOIs survive.) Screened-out applicants get no reviewer comments, but "Applicants who do not receive comments may email programs@rsage.org to request feedback from the initial screen."
2. External peer review — "At least 3-4 peer reviewers will read each proposal. PIs may be asked to respond to reviewer comments in detail before moving forward." Everyone externally reviewed receives masked reviewer comments, funded or not.
3. Standing advisory committee — "Each early career program has a standing advisory committee that reviews all proposal materials, including requested PI responses. Advisory committees recommend which proposals to fund or decline."
Note: the President/Board $75,000 threshold is stated under Core Research Grants; Pipeline budgets are capped below it ($50k individual / $65k team), and no Board stage appears in the early-career description.

No letters of reference, no mentor or sponsor statement, no dissertation-supervisor letter (that is the DRG mechanism), no institutional sign-off, no budget at submission.

PROPOSAL (deviates from Core's 10 pages): "Maximum of 7 single-spaced pages (with standard 12-point font and 1-inch margins), excluding (1) references, (2) supporting tables and figures, and (3) appendices like draft survey instruments and interview protocols." BUDGET RULES YOU MUST DESIGN TO ANYWAY (/apply/info/budget, Pipeline section) — and a correction to the existing CSV row, which records typical_award_size and typical_duration as "unspecified": "Budgets are limited to $50,000 for individuals or $65,000 for teams of eligible assistant professors." / "Project Length: Projects are limited to one year." / "Indirect Costs: No indirect costs are allowed." / "PI/co-PI salary support is limited to $15,000 per eligible PI (not including fringe benefits)"; course buyouts allowed in lieu of summer salary; conference travel capped at $3,000; equipment capped at $5,000; post-doc support up to 50% of salary but no more than $35,000; RA and participant pay at state minimum wage or $15/hour, whichever is higher; consultants max $125/hr and $10,000 total. THE FLUXX FORM FIELDS (from the published blank preview, Pipeline_application_04012026.pdf, "Last updated April 2026") — draft these offline before you open the portal:
- Eligibility gate: "Have you previously received an RSF Fellowship or Research Grant (Presidential or Trustee)?"; rank (Adjunct / Assistant Professor / Assistant Research Professor / Teaching professor-lecturer / Other); academic-year teaching load; first-generation college graduate; how you heard about the programme; consent to be contacted about your career path over 2 years.

result.prior_funding_conflicts:
WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU
- Any prior RSF research grant. Eligibility page and FAQ, identical wording: "Assistant Professor, Adjunct Assistant Professors and Lecturers who have not received an RSF research grant previously (not including Dissertation Research Grants) are eligible to apply. Applicants must meet these requirements as of the submission deadline."
- A prior RSF fellowship also counts. The early-career awards page: "Early-career faculty who have not previously received support from RSF in the form of a Trustee or Presidential research grant or a visiting fellowship from RSF are eligible to apply." The Fluxx form asks it as one question: "Have you previously received an RSF Fellowship or Research Grant (Presidential or Trustee)?"
- Rank: post-docs cannot be PI ("Post-docs are not eligible to be PIs"); associate and full professors cannot be PI. Rank and the no-prior-RSF-grant condition must both hold "as of the submission deadline" — a promotion or an RSF award landing before 21 Oct 2026 removes eligibility for that round.
- IMPLICATION (RSF does not state it in these words, but it follows from "have not received an RSF research grant previously"): a Pipeline grant is itself an RSF research grant, so winning one ends your eligibility for this competition. Treat it as once per career.

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY
- A prior RSF Dissertation Research Grant. The carve-out is written into the rule: "(not including Dissertation Research Grants)". A DRG holder who is now an assistant professor is eligible.
- Any non-RSF funding. Nothing from NSF, NIH, other foundations or your institution disqualifies you; co-funding is encouraged provided it is disclosed and non-duplicative: "Co-funding is encouraged as long as RSF is made aware of existing and/or potential co-funding and requested RSF funds are allocated to budget items that are not covered by other funders." The Fluxx form has explicit CONFIRMED and PENDING support fields.
- A senior or already-RSF-funded collaborator, as an unpaid co-PI: "Full professors and associate professors, and professors who have previously received RSF funding are eligible to be co-PIs on projects, but cannot receive funding" (eligibility page adds: "cannot receive salary support or conference travel funds"). Their RSF history does not contaminate your eligibility as PI.
- Post-docs on the team: "Post-docs are not eligible to be PIs, but can be included on and receive funding on a grant as research assistants."
- Nationality and location: "There are no restrictions on nationality or institution location." No US citizenship, no green card, no US-institution requirement (note this differs from the DRG track, which is "limited to students at institutions based in the United States"). The research itself must still be about the U.S.
- Being at an under-resourced institution or underrepresented in the social sciences is an advantage, not a bar: the programme "prioritizes disciplinary diversity and encourages applications from scholars who are underrepresented in the social sciences and/or employed at under-resourced universities." There are "no limitations on the disciplinary background of the researcher."

THE OTHER CONFLICT IS SAME-CYCLE, NOT PRIOR-AWARD: one Pipeline proposal per cycle, and no simultaneous Core application in the fall — "Applicants can apply for either the Sheldon Danziger Pipeline Grants Competition or the October LOI deadline, but not both."

- Tips & Resources: "If you're unsure, please reach out at least one month ahead of the deadline to programs@rsage.org with a short abstract and some details about the research design." For 21 Oct 2026 that means by ~21 September 2026 — this week, as of 18 Sep 2026.

Send a short abstract plus research-design specifics — not a full draft, not a call request.

result.resubmission_note:
DECLINED -> REAPPLY: allowed, with no stated cap and no waiting period, but it is not an NIH-style A1. FAQ: "An applicant may revise an application and submit during a subsequent funding round. However, the application will be processed as a new submission." There is no resubmission-specific deadline, no A0/A1 counter and no Introduction page. Practical consequences specific to Pipeline: (a) the next round is roughly a year away, since this is an annual fall competition; (b) you must still be rank-eligible and still have no RSF research grant "as of the submission deadline" of the new round, so a promotion to associate professor closes the door; (c) "Applicants may only submit one Pipeline Grant proposal per cycle."

NO INVITED-RESUBMISSION CATEGORY IS PUBLISHED FOR PIPELINE. The "invited to resubmit" route and the Board's "opportunity to revise and resubmit for a future cycle" are described on the review-process page under Core Research Grants; the early-career track ends at "Advisory committees recommend which proposals to fund or decline." Whether an early-career proposal can be invited to resubmit is not stated — not found.

THE RESPONSE-MEMO MOVE STILL APPLIES, MID-REVIEW. For Core it is a required document of the invited proposal; for Pipeline it appears inside peer review: "At least 3-4 peer reviewers will read each proposal. PIs may be asked to respond to reviewer comments in detail before moving forward", and the advisory committee "reviews all proposal materials, including requested PI responses." No page limit is published. RSF's published Core samples include real masked comments and the memos that answered them — the best available guide to the expected register.

FEEDBACK: everyone who reaches external review receives masked reviewer comments, funded or not. Those cut at the internal screen get none, but "Applicants who do not receive comments may email programs@rsage.org to request feedback from the initial screen" — worth doing before rewriting for the next year.

DEFERRAL LEVER DOES NOT APPLY HERE: the "request a deferral at least 2 weeks before the proposal deadline" rule attaches to an invited Core proposal. Pipeline has no invitation stage, so there is nothing to defer; a missed 2pm ET cut-off is simply "deferred to the next round of applications."

result.deadline_pattern: Annual and fixed to the calendar, not floating: portal opens ~July 15, nominee deadline September 15 of the nomination year, reference/nomination letters September 22, winners announced mid-February of the following (award) year, two-year term begins September 15 of the award year. The September 15 date is load-bearing beyond the deadline itself — eligibility is assessed on it ("Candidates must be tenure-track, though untenured, as of September 15 of the nomination year") and the award term starts on it. Confirmed for two consecutive cycles from the funder's own pages: 2027 cycle closed 2026-09-15, 2028 cycle closes 2027-09-15. Practical read for someone looking at this on 2026-09-18: the window just shut, you have ~10 months before the portal reopens — which is the right amount of runway to line up a nominator and three letter-writers.
result.loi_deadline: n/a — there is no letter of intent, pre-proposal, or internal-competition stage. This is the mechanism's sharpest deviation from Sloan's funder-wide machinery: for ordinary Sloan grants the route is "STEP 2: SUBMIT A LETTER OF INQUIRY by email to the appropriate program director" and "The Alfred P. Sloan Foundation does not accept or review unsolicited grant proposals" — full proposals are by invitation only, and "The Foundation does not make grants to individuals except through its Books program." The Fellowships bypass all of that: one open annual window, submitted directly by the candidate through the SM Apply (SurveyMonkey Apply) portal, awarded to the individual. What replaces the LOI is social rather than procedural, and it is what applicants miss: (a) you cannot self-nominate — "Submissions unaccompanied by a nomination letter from a senior researcher are not accepted" — so securing a nominator is a real pre-stage with no published deadline of its own; (b) "no more than three candidates may be nominated from any one department per fellowship field", so if your department has four plausible candidates an informal internal sort has to happen before July 15; (c) the nominator need not be your chair or even in your department ("Any senior researcher who can speak to the quality of your work may nominate you"), but "your department must know that you are being nominated" because of the cap.
result.review_to_award: Submission 2027-09-15 → notification mid-February 2028 → funds start 2028-09-15. About 5 months to notification and about 12 months from deadline to first dollar — the lag between "you won" and "you can spend" is the part people do not expect. Funder's words: FAQ "Q: When are the winners announced? A: Mid-February"; Terms of Awards, "Fellowships are for a two-year term, beginning on September 15th of the award year" and "Fellowships are paid in a single lump sum." The mid-February pattern is anchored by a real date: the press-release listing shows "Announcing the 2026 Sloan Research Fellows | Feb 17, 2026" (that cohort was nominated by 2025-09-15 and its term began 2026-09-15). Review is by seven field-specific independent committees; "If the committee requires external review assistance for an applicant whose research might be outside of their expertise, they may seek it." No interim contact, no interview stage, and no debrief: "Does the Foundation provide feedback to nominees not selected for fellowships? A: No. Selection committee deliberations are confidential." Fellows appear in the public Fellows Database in April, two months after the announcement.
result.submission_requirements:
Five components, all uploaded by the candidate through SM Apply (funder's list, verbatim): (1) "A letter from a department head or other senior researcher officially nominating the candidate"; (2) "The candidate's curriculum vitae (including a list of the candidates scientific publications)"; (3) "Two representative articles by the candidate that highlight his or her independent research"; (4) "A brief (one-page) statement by the candidate describing his or her significant scientific work and immediate research plans"; (5) "Three letters from other researchers (preferably not all from the same institution) written in support of the candidate's nomination." So four letters total — one nomination plus three support.
DEVIATIONS THAT MATTER: (a) No institutional sign-off, no sponsored-programs route, no budget, no biosketch format — the candidate personally creates the account and submits ("it is highly preferable for the candidate to be the one who creates the application"). Do not route this through your research office as if it were a federal proposal. (b) Page limit is one page for the research statement and the FAQ pre-empts the usual games: "Selection committees do not tend to look kindly on applications that try to skirt the one-page length limit through creative font and margin sizing. Please make text no smaller than 11pt font and margins no smaller than .5 inches." References may spill to a second page if they will not fit in footnotes. (c) CV: "no specific requirements ... but it would be helpful for the reviewers to see a full CV rather than a short biosketch" — the opposite of NIH/NSF practice. (d) Field-specific extras: physics nominees must add "your h-index and your top five cited papers (with the citations included)"; Earth system science nominees must add a one-to-two-sentence statement of how the research will impact the field, must name the primary "sphere" of investigation, and should "articulate cross-disciplinary approaches connecting two or more 'spheres'". (e) Articles need not be published, "but it is rare for successful candidates to submit papers that have not at least been accepted for publication." (f) Letters are confidential and requested through a two-step process in SM Apply (fill in the letter-writer form first, then release the request) — letter-writers no longer need an SM Apply account, and the upload link in the automated email expires every two weeks but is automatically re-sent. (g) A missing letter does not sink you on deadline day: "Submit your application without the letter. So long as you have attached all other required documents ... and so long as you have 'requested' the letter through the SM Apply system, your application will be accepted." (h) Known bug: letter uploads fail in Microsoft Edge; the Foundation says to use another browser.
STRATEGIC NOTE THE FUNDER STATES OUTRIGHT: pick letter-writers at a distance from your work — "Letters submitted by co-authors, personal associates, or professional mentors are, in this sense, less useful to Selection Committees than letters submitted by those with more professional distance from a nominee's work."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, from one FAQ answer: "Q: Can past winners apply for another Sloan Research Fellowship? A: No, past (and current) Sloan Fellows are not eligible to receive another Sloan Research Fellowship. Researchers who have received a grant from one of the Sloan Foundation's other grantmaking programs are eligible, however, so long as they meet all Sloan Research Fellowship eligibility requirements."
EXCLUDES: holding or having held a Sloan Research Fellowship — once only, no second bite.
PRESERVES: any grant from any other Sloan Foundation programme (e.g. its research or public-understanding programmes) leaves you fully eligible. Being nominated unsuccessfully in a prior year also preserves eligibility (see resubmission note).
THE REAL GATE IS TENURE, NOT MONEY. The binding disqualifier is career status, and it is absolute: "Tenured faculty are not eligible" — even if every other requirement is met — and you must be "tenure-track, though untenured, as of September 15 of the nomination year", on the faculty of a US or Canadian degree-granting institution, with "a regular teaching obligation". Not-yet-tenure-track researchers (postdocs, research-track, most soft-money positions) must wait: "If you are not yet in a tenure-track position, you will have to wait until you are to be nominated." The Foundation's test for a look-alike position is concrete: "The Foundation considers a position tenure track if someone who held the same position as the nominee has recently gone on to receive tenure without leaving that institution."
IMPORTANT LIMIT ON THIS FIELD: the funder's eligibility requirements, FAQ and terms of award are SILENT on awards from other funders. Nothing on sloan.org states that an NSF CAREER, PECASE, Packard, Beckman, DOE Early Career, or NIH K/R01 award affects eligibility, and there is no overlap or other-support disclosure in the required materials — but that is silence, not an explicit carve-out, and should not be quoted to an applicant as permission. There is also no budget and no overlap review to trigger a conflict: funds are unrestricted, paid as a lump sum, and the only stated spending bar is that "Fellowship funds may not be used for indirect costs or overhead charges." Field of degree and departmental home are likewise not disqualifiers — "it does not matter in which field you received your degree or which department your appointment is in", only that the research sits in one of the seven fellowship fields.
result.program_officer_contact: No program officer in the federal sense, and no pre-submission consultation culture — this is a named deviation from Sloan's grants side, where step 2 is a letter of inquiry "to the appropriate program director". For the Fellowships there is one published route, a shared programme mailbox: researchfellows@sloan.org, given on the Fellowships page ("Questions about how these eligibility requirements apply to you? See our FAQ page or email us at researchfellows@sloan.org"), on the FAQ page, and in the SM Apply troubleshooting answers. It is the only sloan.org address exposed anywhere on the fellowship pages. Named staff on the Fellowships page: Lauren von Eckartsberg, Grants Manager. Pre-submission contact is expected only for eligibility edge cases and portal problems, not for merit or fit discussions — the Foundation explicitly declines to advise: "The Foundation cannot advise departments on which candidates to nominate", and it gives no post-decision feedback. The people who actually judge you are public, however, and are listed by field on the Fellowships page: seven selection committees, e.g. Chemistry (Héctor D. Abruña, Cornell; Cathleen M. Crudden, Queen's; David R. Reichman, Columbia; Wilfred A. van der Donk, Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Computer Science (Moses Charikar, Stanford; Sylvia Ratnasamy, Berkeley; Kilian Weinberger, Cornell); Mathematics (Larry Guth, MIT; Amit Singer, Princeton; Karen E. Smith, Michigan); Physics (Lars Bildsten, UCSB; Sally Dawson, Stony Brook; Subir Sachdev, Harvard; Jun Ye, Colorado Boulder); plus Earth System Science, Economics and Neuroscience committees. The site also links a roster of all past committee members. Reading your field's committee is the closest thing to knowing your audience.
result.examples_or_samples: No official samples exist, and the Foundation refuses them explicitly: "Q: Can I see an example of a research statement submitted by a successful candidate? A: Unfortunately, no. Research statements submitted by nominees are confidential." There is no annotated sample, no funded-application library, and no debrief for unsuccessful nominees. What the funder does offer instead, and it is genuinely usable: (1) the Fellows Database at https://sloan.org/fellows-database — "more than five thousand outstanding early-career researchers" since 1955, filterable by year, field and institution, listing each fellow's field, award year and institution at the time of award; new cohorts are added each April. This is the practical route to "who to talk to": find two or three fellows in your field from the last three or four years, ideally one at your own institution, and ask them for their statement directly — peer-to-peer is the only channel that exists. (2) The current cohort page https://sloan.org/fellowships/2026-Fellows — 126 fellows for 2026, listed by field with institutions, showing the career stage and institutional spread that actually wins (the Foundation notes it is "quite common" for a cohort to include a department that has never had a Sloan Fellow). (3) Annual announcement press releases under https://sloan.org/about/press/press-releases (PDF; the 2026 one is dated Feb 17, 2026). No verified third-party repository of successful Sloan statements was established in this run — see unresolved.
result.resubmission_note: Re-nomination after an unsuccessful year is explicitly allowed and common: "Q: I nominated someone last year who did not receive an award. Can I re-nominate that same person this year? A: Yes, so long as they continue to meet all eligibility requirements." There is no cap on the number of attempts stated — the real limit is the tenure clock, since you must still be untenured and tenure-track on September 15 of each nomination year. Nothing carries over between cycles, and letters in particular must be rewritten: "Q: If I applied for a Sloan Research Fellowship last year and am re-applying this year, can I re-use my nomination letter and letters of support from last year? A. No. Though the same persons may nominate you or write letters of support on your behalf, they must submit new letters. This ensures that your nominator and letter-writers continue to support your candidacy." A resubmission is therefore a full rebuild of the packet, with no funder feedback to respond to and no "response to previous review" section — unlike NIH A1 resubmissions. Practical consequence: budget the same four letter-asks every year you try.

For the 2027 cycle specifically, cancer work is down-weighted unless it addresses disparities: "letters of intent submitted for cancer research that meet the eligibility requirements but do not address health disparities may not be invited to full application."

ONE LOI ONLY: "Predoctoral and Postdoctoral applicants may submit an LOI for only one project." (Other TRDRP applicants may submit up to two; trainees may not.) "No changes to PI or Co-PI may be made after LOI submission."

The LOI is submitted through RGPO's SmartSimple system (https://rgpogrants.ucop.edu). The exact LOI form fields are held inside SmartSimple and are not published in the Call document.
result.review_to_award:
Full application (Oct 29, 2026) → notification (April 2027) → earliest start (July 1, 2027). So roughly 6 months submission-to-notification and ~8 months submission-to-money; ~2-3 months from notification to start.

Counting from the true first action, the LOI (Aug 20, 2026), the whole pipeline is about 10.5 months to the award start date. A postdoc planning salary coverage needs to start this process nearly a year before they need the funds.

Intermediate step unique to this funder: LOI → invitation decision is only ~3 weeks (Aug 20 → Sep 8).

Review mechanics: "Applications will be grouped by priority area and undergo peer-review by experts from outside of California" — an explicit out-of-state reviewer rule, notable because eligibility is California-only. Scoring uses the "Standard NIH scoring system that is based on the 1-9 scale." TRDRP and its Scientific Advisory Committee then prioritize for funding, seeking "a balance across these priorities."

Waitlist: exists and does move, rarely — "Waitlisted applications may be funded only if another award in the same category is declined. This is rare but possible."

Appeals: narrow and time-boxed — only "in the case of an alleged error in, or violation of the peer review procedures and/or process"; "Appeals based on substantive disagreement with the peer review evaluation will not be considered"; "Applicant appeals must be made to the program within 30 days of funding notification."

Post-award timing note: IRB/IACUC approvals are NOT required at application, but final assurances are due "no later than six months after the award start date," and "Funds will not be released until all assurances are received by TRDRP."
result.submission_requirements:
Submitted through RGPO SmartSimple (https://rgpogrants.ucop.edu). Templates are downloaded from SmartSimple and are released only at the invited-full-application stage. Using the wrong template is fatal: "Applications failing to use the correct templates will be administratively rejected." Research Plans over length are silently cut: "Submitted Research Plans will be truncated to the page limit indicated on the template by RGPO Staff prior to peer review."

PAGE LIMITS (postdoctoral-specific; deviate from the predoctoral figures):
- Research Plan: 10 pages (predoctoral gets 6) — "Required for Postdoctoral(10-page) and Predoctoral (6-page) Award Applicants"
- Training Plan: 4 pages (predoctoral gets 6 — the postdoc allowance is SHORTER here)
- Mentor Training Experience: 2 pages
- Facilities: 1 page per institution
- Community Engagement Plan: 1 page
- Resubmission/revision statement (if applicable): 2 pages, immediately preceding the Research Plan
- Literature Cited, Vertebrate Animal Subjects, Human Subjects Accrual: no page limit

REQUIRED COMPONENTS BEYOND THE RESEARCH PLAN — this is where the mechanism deviates most:
1. Letters of reference: "A letter of support from the research advisor and a minimum of two additional references are required. Letters should address the candidate's previous training and potential for future leadership of an independent research program." Additional mentors are not obliged to write, "however, such letters may strengthen the application."
2. Individual Development Plan (IDP): mandatory, on TRDRP's template, uploaded in the Appendix. "The primary research advisor and postdoctoral applicant must complete an Individual Development Plan (IDP) using the provided template." The IDP is not the Training Plan: "the two documents must not be identical as they differ in scope and required information."
3. Formal Training Plan: developed by the primary research advisor with the applicant; must include "training on the ethical conduct of research (Required)."
4. Mentor Training Experience: mentor lists doctoral candidates/postdocs previously trained, their current positions, and whether they work in tobacco-related research.
5. Biosketches: applicant AND primary research advisor both required; mentors optional.
6. Community Engagement Plan: required of trainee applications and separately scored. Note the funder's explicit exclusion: "Presenting research findings at professional or scientific conferences is considered scholarly dissemination rather than community engagement unless the activity directly involves or engages community members."
7. Accessibility compliance (a real, unusual rejection risk): all uploads must meet "Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA standards," and RGPO will not help — "The Research Grants Program Office staff is not able to provide training or review of your documents to assist you with compliance."

OWNERSHIP OF THE SUBMISSION: unlike many mentored awards, the trainee drives it — "The applicant is responsible for preparing the application and for uploading and submitting all required research-related documents." Mentors are "encouraged to support the trainee by providing guidance and feedback."

MULTIPLE MENTORS: one must be designated "Research Advisor" in the Project Personnel List; others are listed as "Mentor."

BUDGET SPECIFICS (2027 figures): stipend up to $70,000/yr, which "must adhere to NIH experience scale, or the rates set by their institution with institutional documentation of the alternate payment scale"; institutional allowance up to $38,000/yr (fixed, not actual-cost accounted, but "should fully justify Institutional Allowance costs in their budget... broken out by year... itemized sub-category list"); a mandatory separate one-time $750 line in Year 1 labelled "Travel – TRDRP Meeting"; "Indirect Costs: Not allowed." Maximum 3 consecutive years. (3 × $108,000 + $750 = $324,750, which matches the actual 2026 postdoctoral awards in TRDRP's funded-grants database.) Employee benefits may NOT be charged: "institutions may not seek funds, or charge individual awards, for costs that normally would be associated with employee benefits (e.g., FICA, workman's compensation, life insurance, union dues, and unemployment insurance)."
Out-of-state spending is effectively discouraged: "Prop 56 does not allow funding for out-of-state research, while Prop 99 does, if justified. However, Prop 99 funds are very limited... you may not be funded at all."

EFFORT: "A minimum 75 percent time commitment on the part of the postdoctoral trainee is required."

SCORING WEIGHTS (postdoctoral): Criteria Set 1 = 40% (Responsiveness to California's tobacco control needs, Approach, Community Engagement Plan); Criteria Set 2 = 40% (Training Plan and IDP, Qualifications of the applicant); Criteria Set 3 = 20% (Mentor's qualifications and commitment, Environment). Reviewers also judge formatting: "Reviewers will evaluate to what extent the application is appropriately formatted, on the correct template, and free from errors."

INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF: UC employees must route through their campus contracts and grants office per the 1994 UC policy on submitting proposals through the University. IRB/IACUC approval not needed at submission. Human-subjects inclusion documentation IS needed: applications lacking the required description of inclusion of males, females and racially/ethnically diverse groups "are ineligible for funding and will not be evaluated."
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, because the interesting finding here is how LITTLE is disqualifying compared with an NIH K/F mechanism.

WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half usually missing):
- **No prior-award disqualifier is published at all.** I searched the full 2027 Core Call for concurrent/prior-support bars (terms: concurrent, simultaneous, supplant, another source, current and pending, other support, active grant, cost share). There is NO NIH-style rule excluding people who hold or have held a federal career-development award, a fellowship, or another grant. The TRDRP Postdoctoral Award does not key eligibility to prior funding history at all.
- **No citizenship bar**: "U.S. citizenship is not a requirement" (stated on both the mechanism page and in the Call). No visa class is specified as excluded.
- **No years-since-PhD cap is published** — no "within N years of the terminal degree" clause, which is the usual early-career gate elsewhere.
- **A previously unfunded TRDRP application does not burn you** — it can come back once as a resubmission (see resubmission_note), and a waitlisted applicant is explicitly encouraged to submit a fresh LOI in the next cycle.
- **Holding a TRDRP postdoctoral award opens further money rather than closing it**: the Cornelius Hopper Disparities Supplement and the Student Research Award Supplement (each up to $20,000) are available "to support California residents and trainees on funded grants."
- A prior pilot award is not a prerequisite anywhere in this mechanism.

WHAT ACTUALLY MAKES YOU INELIGIBLE (the real gates are institutional, role-based and overlap-based, not funding-history-based):
1. **Geography, absolutely**: "Investigators at institutions outside of California are not eligible to apply for TRDRP funding" and "TRDRP awards are only available to applicants located in the State of California." California non-profit institutions only.
2. **Role and timing**: "The candidate must be recognized by the applicant institution as a postdoctoral trainee no later than the award start date. Eligibility ends when a postdoctoral trainee moves into a non-mentored staff or faculty-level role, even if this occurs before the funding period concludes." This is the sharpest trap in the mechanism — winning the award and then being promoted to faculty mid-award TERMINATES eligibility. Anyone within ~1-3 years of a faculty start should plan around it.
3. **Scientific overlap with the mentor's portfolio** (the closest thing to a prior-funding conflict): "The application must describe an original research project and not replicate the aims of any existing grants or applications held by the research advisor or mentors, whether funded by TRDRP or another source." Note this constrains the MENTOR'S funding, not the applicant's.
4. **Overlap with any other grant, resolved before money moves**: a pre-funding requirement is "Resolution of any scientific overlap issues with other grants or pending applications." So concurrent support is managed at pre-award rather than barred at application — but a project that duplicates an existing award will be forced to change or lose funds.
5. **Effort**: the 75% minimum time commitment is the practical limiter on holding another substantial award simultaneously.
6. **One LOI**: "Predoctoral and Postdoctoral applicants may submit an LOI for only one project" — you cannot hedge across two proposals in a cycle.
7. **Scientific scope gates (2027 cycle)**: basic/preclinical work must study one of the listed commercial tobacco products or usage patterns (flavor-ban-exempt products such as hookah, loose leaf and premium cigars; non-combusted nicotine products e.g. vapes; oral nicotine; heated tobacco; addictive nicotine analogs; synthetic cooling agents; inhaled tobacco/nicotine co-used with other substances incl. cannabis/THC); clinical/translational/implementation work "must involve human subjects that have a history of commercial tobacco product use." Studies addressing only non-tobacco substances are ineligible.
8. **Missing human-subjects inclusion documentation**: "Applications without such documentation are ineligible for funding and will not be evaluated."

result.resubmission_note:
Permitted, but exactly once, and it still goes through the LOI gate.

Verbatim: "A resubmission is an unfunded application that was submitted to TRDRP as a new application in the previous cycle (i.e. 2026) and resubmitted under the current Call for Applications (i.e. 2027). Resubmitted applications are allowed to include a 2-page resubmission statement immediately preceding the Research Plan. TRDRP will accept only a single resubmission of the same or very similar project. Any additional submissions of the same or similar topic are considered new applications and may not include a revision statement."

Procedural trap: "Applicants are still required to inform TRDRP of their intent to resubmit through an LOI submission and must note it as a resubmission." A resubmission is NOT exempt from the August LOI deadline or from the capped invitation screen — a resubmitter who misses the LOI date is out for the cycle, same as a new applicant.

Content of the revision statement: "should summarize any substantial additions, deletions, and changes that have been made. It must also include responses to criticisms in the summary statement provided in response to the previous submission. These changes should be highlighted within the text of the Research Plan by appropriate bracketing, indenting, changing of typography, or use of color. The 'Preliminary Studies' section should include any relevant work done since the prior version was submitted."

Mechanism-availability trap: "resubmissions may only be submitted for those award types being competed at this time." If your original mechanism is not offered in the new cycle, TRDRP's guidance is to find an eligible mechanism that fits the topic instead. This has real teeth — the Research, Pilot, New Investigator and Tobacco Policy Research Center awards were NOT offered in the 2027 cycle, so their 2026 applicants had nowhere to resubmit. The Postdoctoral Award itself has been offered continuously and is scheduled through 2029.

Note the appeals route is not a resubmission route: appeals lie only for alleged peer-review process error, within 30 days of notification; substantive disagreement with the review is redirected to resubmission in a later cycle.

NIJ's own published cadence (funding hub page): current opportunities are "a list of notices of funding opportunity under which we are accepting applications; typically, most notices are released December through May", and forthcoming opportunities are typically posted "in the late fall". - Step 2 JustGrants deadline May 30, 2024, 8:59 p.m. ET (a full 14 days after Step 1 — this two-week gap between the two deadlines is the single most distinctive scheduling feature of OJP/NIJ and has no NIH analogue)

IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF: the NIH machinery supplied to me as "already established" does NOT apply to this mechanism in any part. There is no eRA Commons, no ASSIST, no SciENcv, no ORCID mandate, no standard tri-annual due dates, no study section, no council round, no A1 rule, no 5:00 p.m.-local rule, no Application Viewing Window. NIJ is DOJ/OJP: Grants.gov + JustGrants, a single solicitation-specific deadline pair, OJP peer review panels, and final decisions by the NIJ Director. Everything below is NIJ's own machinery, established from scratch.

(2) The LOI email address was WRONG in the original PDF and corrected by a March 19, 2024 modification notice ("The email address for submitting letters of intent, found on page 12, has been corrected. The correct address is NIJDuboisResearch@usdoj.gov."). Always re-check the modification notices stapled to the front of an NIJ NOFO.

Strategic point for early-career applicants: because NIJ publishes no program officer for this mechanism and invites no pre-submission discussion, this optional LOI — addressed to the NIJ Director — is effectively the ONLY sanctioned pre-submission contact with the agency.
