result.deadline_pattern: Annual, single dated cycle — Regime 3 of DARPA's three deadline regimes, and the only DARPA mechanism an early-career researcher can put in a calendar a year ahead. Shape: RA posts late Sept–early Nov → executive summary ~2–3 weeks later → question submittal closes ~10 days before the proposal deadline → full proposal due mid-Jan–late Feb → selections announced Aug/Sept → awards start Aug/Sept–30 Sept (start of the federal fiscal year). One RA per year; one executive summary and one full proposal per PI per RA. Every deadline is Eastern Time and in the last cycle every one of them was 4:00 p.m. ET, not 5:00 p.m. — do not assume the hour.
result.loi_required: yes — in practice, though the RA calls it "strongly encouraged" rather than mandatory
result.loi_deadline:
FY2026: "Executive summaries are due October 15, 2025, at 4:00 p.m." — 15 calendar days after the RA posted, and 97 days before the 20 January 2026 full proposal deadline. Response arrives on a published clock: "Executive summaries submitted in response to this announcement may anticipate a response within approximately 45 calendar days" — so mid-December feedback against a late-January proposal deadline, leaving roughly five weeks to write the full proposal on the strength of the answer.

THE GATE IS SOFT BUT REAL, and this is the nuance that decides whether you get a second bite. The RA preserves the DARPA-wide right to proceed anyway: "Regardless of DARPA's response to an executive summary, proposers may submit a full proposal. DARPA will review all conforming full proposals using the published evaluation criteria (Section II) and without regard to any comments resulting from the review of an executive summary." But it immediately adds a discouragement found nowhere else at DARPA: "As the YFA is considered a mentorship program, submission of a proposal is strongly discouraged if a proposal is not recommended for submission based on the executive summary." So YFA sits between the DSO model (advisory only) and the IPTO model (hard invitation-only gate) — you legally may proceed after a discouraging response, and you are told not to. Also note the ceiling on optimism: "a favorable response to an executive summary is not a guarantee that a proposal based on the executive summary will ultimately be selected for award negotiation."
result.review_to_award:
MEASURED ACROSS THREE CYCLES, not inferred. DARPA publishes no notification date for YFA, but the award records date the arc precisely.

- FY2026 (DARPARA2502): proposals due 20 Jan 2026 → RA states "A target start date of August 2026 may be assumed for planning purposes" → DARPA's news page says the 2026 class "has been selected for negotiation with formal announcements anticipated for August or September 2026." ≈ 7 months submission to start.
- FY2025 (DARPARA2501): proposals due 5 Feb 2025 → USAspending shows at least 14 YFA cooperative agreements (Michigan, Rochester, Johns Hopkins, Northeastern, MIT, Georgia Tech, Virginia, Carnegie Mellon, Florida, Illinois ×2, UT Austin, Wisconsin, Minnesota), every one starting 30 Sept 2025 and running to 29 Sept 2027. ≈ 7.8 months.
- FY2024 (DARPARA2401): proposals due 22 Feb 2024 → awards starting 1 Sept and 16 Sept 2024. ≈ 6.3–6.8 months.

So: plan on 6–8 months from full-proposal submission to money, with starts clustered at the top of the federal fiscal year. Add the executive-summary phase and the true clock from first artefact to first dollar is roughly 11–12 months.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE DARPA NORM WORTH BUDGETING FOR:
- Executive summary response is ~45 calendar days here, not the BAA Guide's 30-day abstract target.
- An extra pre-award gate the funder-wide arc does not mention: "DARPA's Fundamental Research Risk-Based Security Review Process (formerly CFIP, now FRR-BS a.k.a. 'FERBS')… DARPA will create risk assessments of all proposed Senior/Key Personnel selected for negotiation of a fundamental research grant or cooperative agreement award," run "separately from the DARPA scientific review process and adjudicated prior to final award." This is a named-personnel security screen sitting between selection and award.
- Proposal validity period required is "minimum 120 days" on the YFA cover sheet, not the 180 days the funder-wide cost-proposal norm cites.
- Cooperative agreements only: "No award type other than cooperative agreements will be issued under this RA" — so no contract/OT negotiation path, and the Grants Officer (GO), not a Contracting Officer, executes.
- After award: one No-Cost Extension to the base period of up to 12 months may be requested; longer needs GO justification.
result.submission_requirements:
SPLIT ROUTE — the trap. Executive summary goes to BAAT; full proposal goes to Grants.gov. "All executive summaries must be submitted through the Broad Agency Announcement Tool (BAAT). Each TA will have a separate announcement listing in BAAT (e.g. DARPARA2502-01, DARPARA2502-02, etc.)" and "All proposals must be submitted through Grants.gov." You must pick the right per-topic-area BAAT listing, not a single YFA listing.

DRIFT CORRECTION to the funder-wide portal note: the YFA RA states BAAT "[a]ccounts are typically disabled and eventually deleted following 75-90 days of inactivity," not 30 days. Same advice either way — "if you are unsure when the account was last used, it is recommended that you create a new account." Also: "Only one zip archive will be accepted per submission--subsequent uploads for the same submission will overwrite previous uploads."

PAGE LIMITS — far tighter than any NIH or NSF equivalent, and the numbers are published up front (unlike DARPA's office-wide BAAs, where full-proposal limits only arrive with the invitation).
- Executive summary: "Executive summaries shall not exceed a maximum of 1 page, excluding the cover sheet. The cover sheet may be expanded to 2 or more pages in order to accommodate all the requested information… Items 1 through 4 should not exceed 1 page." Items 1–4 are Summary (1–2 sentences), Intro/Background (one paragraph), Impact (one short paragraph), Methods/Approach (remainder of page).
- Full proposal Volume I: "Technical and Management Volumes shall not exceed a maximum of 8 pages." Eight pages must carry eleven sections including Statement of Work, Schedule and Milestones, Management Plan and Personnel. Technical figures, tables and charts count inside it. So do CVs: "References, technical papers, resumes are included in the page limit so proposers may wish to include these as links in the bibliography." Excluded: cover sheet, table of contents, transmittal letter, summary slide, optional bibliography. "The Government will not consider pages in excess of the page count limitations."
- Formatting: 8.5×11, 1-inch margins, ≥12 pt (8 or 10 pt permitted in figures/tables/charts); .pdf/.odx/.doc/.docx; summary slide in .ppt/.pptx.

BLIND REVIEW OF THE EXECUTIVE SUMMARY — a YFA-specific rule with no DARPA-wide equivalent, and the easiest way to be thrown out. "DARPA intends to conduct a blind review of submitted executive summaries. Institution and Key Personnel identifying information must be present on only the Executive Summary Cover Sheet, which will be separated from the remaining text prior to DARPA conducting its review. If Institution or Key Personnel identifying information is found after the Executive Summary Cover Sheet, the executive summary may be deemed non-conforming and may not be reviewed." No "our lab has shown", no self-citation by name, on the one page.

MANDATORY TEMPLATES. "Use of this template is mandatory" appears on both Attachment A and Attachment C. Four attachments: A Executive Summary Template (required if submitting one), B Proposal Summary Slide Template (required), C Volume I Technical and Management (required), D Volume II Administrative and National Policy Requirements (required).

ONE TOPIC AREA, ONE SUBMISSION. "Each submission (executive summary or full proposal) must specify ONE and only one TA… Executive summaries and full proposals that do not clearly address a specific TA may be deemed non-conforming." And: "At the executive summary phase, proposing PIs are limited to submitting only a single executive summary; at the full proposal phase… a single full proposal. Submitting more than one executive summary or full proposal may result in all of the PI's proposal submissions being determined non-conforming."

INSTITUTIONAL SIGN-OFF — exactly one letter, and it is not a reference. "Attach the official transmittal letter from the prime proposer organization. This is a brief, signed statement from an official at the submitter's organization (perhaps a Director of Research or Sponsored Programs) in support of the research proposed." NOTABLE ABSENCE, and it is a real finding: there are NO letters of reference, NO mentor or sponsor statement, NO department-chair letter and NO career-development plan anywhere in this mechanism. An ECR arriving from NIH K-award or NSF CAREER habits should not build those and should not expect them to help.

SINGLE-PI ONLY. "The PI must be from the Prime proposer's organization and must be identified as the sole Key Personnel in the proposal." Everyone else supported by the award is Senior Personnel or a team member.

COVER SHEET POLICES ELIGIBILITY. Volume I's cover sheet demands PI's Tenure Track Start Date (or Ph.D. date if at a non-profit); approved leaves of absence with type and dates; citizenship and green-card status; "Have you proposed to YFA before? [Yes or No] If yes what year"; a self-certification "I certify that the PI is eligible per Section III of the RA" (the templates say Section III, the RA puts eligibility in Section IV — a DARPA inconsistency, read Section IV); "Proposal Validity Period (minimum 120 days)"; the executive summary ID number if one was submitted; and two full disclosure tables — "List all past DARPA awards" and "List all other past federal awards" with office, solicitation number, title, amount and performance dates. That is how the funding cap is enforced.

BUDGET SPECIFICS. Budget justification is Section L of the SF-424 R&R Budget form on Grants.gov, itemised for Direct Labor, Equipment (justify anything over $5,000), Travel, Other Direct Costs and Participant/Trainee Support. Easily missed line item: "please plan for 3 two-day meetings in the Washington, D.C., area over the course of the 24-month base period and one additional meeting over the course of the 12-month option period." Publication costs are "highly discouraged"; non-DoD-sponsored travel is "highly discouraged."

STRUCTURE YOU MUST PROPOSE UP FRONT. The award is a 24-month base (max $500,000, and "Each 12-month interval of the base period shall not exceed $250,000") plus a 12-month option (max $500,000) that you must price in the original proposal — that option IS the Director's Fellowship, "reserved for a limited number of awardees who demonstrate exceptional YFA project performance over the 24-month base period," nominated later by your DARPA PM mentor. There is also an optional concurrent U.S. Person Graduate Student effort, not to exceed $350,000, which must run inside the 24-month base. Volume I "must address the full 36-month program (base and option period)." You do not apply for the Fellowship later; you either priced it at the start or you did not.

FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH ONLY. "DARPA will not select proposals for negotiation of an award if the proposal is deemed to be Applied Research, or otherwise requires Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) restrictions." All submissions anticipated unclassified; no publication restrictions expected.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, quoted from DARPARA2502 Amendment 5 Section IV.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU AS PI:
1. The money cap — "Individuals who have received funding greater than $500,000 from DARPA or $1,250,000 from all DoD sources combined as either a Prime or subawardee PI or co-PI are not eligible to be Key Personnel (i.e., PI) under the YFA program, but may serve as Senior Personnel." Note it is a career-to-date total, not an annual rate, and it counts subaward money.
2. A prior YFA — "Individuals who have previously received a YFA Award as a PI are not eligible to be a PI for this or any future YFA program, but may serve as Senior Personnel." Once, ever.
3. Former DARPA Program Managers — "not eligible to serve under this program in any capacity."
4. FFRDC / UARC / National Laboratory / other Government employees — "not eligible to serve under this program in any capacity." (Note this INVERTS the DARPA-wide norm, where FFRDCs and UARCs merely must contact the PM first. Here they are barred outright.)
5. Non-U.S. organizations cannot participate; all Key and Senior Personnel and all team members "must be employed at a U.S. institution, which includes those in U.S. states and territories."
6. Rank/clock — the PI must, by the full proposal deadline, be a "current Tenure-Track Assistant/Associate Professor", "current Tenured faculty within 3 years of their Tenure date", or "an equivalent at a non-profit research institution within 12 years of the receipt of their Ph.D."

WHAT EXPLICITLY PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY — this is the half applicants never find, and every item is load-bearing:
1. YOUR SHARE COUNTS, NOT THE AWARD TOTAL. Footnote 13: "To determine eligibility based on funding limitations, those who have served as co-PIs should include the share of the funds allocated to their contractual activity under those awards. If all PIs on an award are listed as 'co-PIs' then an equal distribution to all such identified individuals should be used." Being fifth co-PI on a $5M DoD MURI is $1M against the $1.25M ceiling, not $5M. Many people who assume they are disqualified are not.
2. LEAVES OF ABSENCE STOP THE CLOCK. The rank tests apply "(excluding any personal leaves of absence)", and both the executive summary and Volume I cover sheets provide a field — "PI's Approved Leaves of Absence, if any: Type of absence / Start date / Finish date" — to claim it. Parental, medical and family leave do not eat your window; you must declare them.
3. THE CAP BINDS ONLY THE PI. "Senior Personnel are subject to the citizenship requirements above, but not subject to tenure requirements or funding limitations." Your heavily DARPA-funded senior colleague, and any past YFA winner, and anyone over the dollar ceiling, can all join your team as Senior Personnel. The exclusion is from the PI slot, never from the project.
4. THE ceiling IS DARPA-SPECIFIC AND DoD-SPECIFIC. NSF, NIH, DOE and foundation money does not count toward either threshold. A well-funded NIH or NSF investigator with no DoD history is fully eligible.
5. NO PRIOR DARPA FUNDING IS PREFERRED, NOT REQUIRED. The programme targets rising stars "particularly those without prior DARPA funding" — a preference, not a bar; the bar is the $500,000 figure.
6. RESTRICTED-COUNTRY CITIZENSHIP HAS THREE CURE PATHS. Citizens of China, Cuba, Russia, Iran, Venezuela and North Korea are ineligible as Key or Senior Personnel "unless one of the following conditions is met: Individual is a dual citizen of the U.S. and one of the countries above; Individual is a U.S. Permanent Resident/Green Card holder; Individual is in the application process to become a U.S. Permanent Resident/Green Card holder." The third path has a hard procedural step: "please email your USCIS Form I-797 to YFA2026@darpa.mil no later than the full proposal due date" — miss it and "the proposal will be removed from consideration."
7. NON-U.S. NATIONALITY IS NOT ITSELF A BAR. "Participation is open to individuals who are U.S. Citizens, U.S. Permanent Residents, and Foreign Nationals who meet the eligibility criteria listed below," and "Non-U.S. individuals employed by U.S. institutions may participate" subject to export control and NDA compliance.
8. REAPPLYING IS FREE AND EXPECTED. There is no resubmission marking, no A1, no penalty; the cover sheet simply asks "Have you proposed to YFA before? If yes what year." Nothing carries over. The real constraint is drift, not policy: your tenure clock advances, and a successful year elsewhere can push you past the $500k/$1.25M ceiling — so YFA eligibility is a window that closes, and an ECR should apply early in it rather than polishing for a later cycle.
9. CONCURRENT SUBMISSION ELSEWHERE IS ALLOWED BUT MUST BE DISCLOSED. Volume I Capabilities section: "Identify any other solicitation(s) to which this concept has been proposed. If applicable, state whether funding or a positive funding decision has already been received, and from which agency."
result.program_officer_contact:
ROUTE, NOT A PERSON — and YFA is the documented exception to DARPA's "talk to the PM" culture.

The named contact is the RA Coordinator mailbox, which is renamed each cycle after the solicitation: FY2026 was YFA2026@darpa.mil, with phone 571-218-4565 listed on the grants.gov record under "DARPA - Defense Sciences Office". Expect YFA2027@darpa.mil for the coming cycle. The RA: "Administrative, technical, and contractual questions should be emailed to YFA2026@darpa.mil. All questions must be in English and must include the name, email address, and the telephone number of a point of contact. DARPA will post an FAQ list on the DARPA webpage." Questions close roughly ten days before the proposal deadline (9 Jan 2026 against a 20 Jan 2026 close). Technical/portal problems go to BAAT_Support@darpa.mil with a copy to the RA mailbox — sending elsewhere "may result in delayed/no response." Agency-level protests: CMO_Protests@darpa.mil; ombudsman: DARPA_Ombudsman@darpa.mil.

PRE-SUBMISSION CONTACT IS NOT THE DARPA NORM HERE. Because of volume, DARPA declines one-to-one feedback on YFA executive summaries (DARPARA2502 FAQ 82, established in the funder-wide pass: "Due to the high volume of responses to the YFA Research Announcement (RA), we are unable to accommodate such telecoms/meetings to provide additional feedback for Executive Summary submissions"). There is no Proposers Day. So the usual DARPA advice — email the PM a quad chart — does not apply to YFA the way it applies to an office-wide BAA. Your substitute for PM taste is the written Topic Area description: each TA is authored by the office that will fund it, you must name exactly one, and "DARPA reserves the right to assign a proposal or an executive summary to a different topic area than indicated by the proposer."

WHAT REPLACES THE PROGRAM OFFICER, BEFORE AND AFTER:
- Before: read current DARPA programme pages. The RA itself instructs this — "proposers are encouraged to review the DARPA mission statement and current program descriptions at the DARPA website https://www.darpa.mil to familiarize themselves with examples of current DARPA investments. This is not meant as instruction to duplicate those efforts…"
- After award, you are assigned one: "each YFA program performer will be assigned a DARPA Program Manager (PM) with interests closely related to their research topic. The PM will act as project manager and mentor to the YFA award recipients." That mentor later nominates you (or not) for the Director's Fellowship option. YFA is explicitly "considered a mentorship program" — the PM relationship is the prize, not the entry ticket.
- After notification, selected or not, the DARPA-wide informal feedback session with the PM remains available on request and is the only substitute for a summary statement.
result.resubmission_note:
No resubmission mechanism, no A1, no appeal, no limit on attempts, and nothing to disclose beyond a single cover-sheet checkbox: "Have you proposed to YFA before? [Yes or No] If yes what year." Each annual RA is a fresh competition against its own Topic Areas; nothing carries over and there is no introduction-to-resubmission page.

The YFA-specific twist is the soft gate. A discouraging executive-summary response does not bar you — "Regardless of DARPA's response to an executive summary, proposers may submit a full proposal" — but you are told that proceeding is "strongly discouraged" because this is a mentorship programme. Treat a discouraging response as intelligence about fit with that year's Topic Areas, and consider re-entering next cycle against a different TA rather than pushing a discouraged concept through.

The real constraint on coming back is eligibility drift, not policy: the tenure-track/3-years-post-tenure/12-years-post-PhD window closes, and crossing $500,000 of DARPA or $1,250,000 of total DoD funding as PI or co-PI ends PI eligibility permanently. A YFA win itself ends it — one YFA as PI, ever. So the strategic advice inverts the usual "wait and strengthen it": apply early in the window, because the window only narrows.

Note also the DARPA-wide one-way door applies once the proposal is received: all interaction routes through the Grants Officer, and neither the PM nor the GO may advise you on how to revise. Non-conformance (wrong template, un-anonymised executive summary, two submissions, more than one Topic Area, over the page limit) is never read on merit — it is the cheapest and most avoidable way to lose a year.
result.examples_or_samples:
DARPA publishes no funded YFA proposals and no summary statements. But YFA is unusually well served for a DARPA mechanism, because published templates plus award records together let you reconstruct most of what you need.

1. THE MANDATORY TEMPLATES ARE THE SAMPLE. This is the strongest answer and it is free. Attachment A (Executive Summary Template) and Attachment C (Volume I Template) are published on grants.gov with every cycle and carry DARPA's own bracketed instructional prompts for each section — literally the questions the reviewer will look for, in order. Attachment A tells you the 1-page executive summary must answer, in this sequence: a 1–2 sentence jargon-free "what are you trying to do and why does it matter", one paragraph of problem and state-of-the-art limitations, one short paragraph of impact, then methods. Attachment C gives the eleven Volume I sections. Download the prior cycle's attachments now (DARPARA2502, grants.gov opportunity 360697) and draft against them before the 2027 RA posts — they change little year to year, and the 15-day executive-summary fuse means that is the only way to be ready.

2. WHO ACTUALLY WON, WITH TITLES AND AMOUNTS — verified live this pass. USAspending's keyword search for "DARPARA" returns real YFA cooperative agreements. Working recipe: https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/ (or Advanced Search in the UI) with Awarding Agency = Department of Defense, Sub-Agency = Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, Assistance Listing 12.910, award type = grants/cooperative agreements. The FY2025 class surfaces as award IDs D25AC00347–D25AC00378 — Michigan, Rochester, Johns Hopkins, Northeastern, MIT, Georgia Tech, Virginia, Carnegie Mellon, Florida, Illinois, UT Austin, Wisconsin, Minnesota — each ~$500,000, all starting 30 Sept 2025, running 24 months. Some records carry the actual project title, e.g. HR00112410004, Ohio State, $500,000, "DEFENSE SCIENCES OFFICE RESEARCH ANNOUNCEMENT DARPARA2401 — SPATIALLY RESOLVED, NON-GENETIC OPTOELECTRONIC MODULATION OF NEURONAL ACTIVITIES"; and HR00112410003, University of Rhode Island, $749,866, "DARPARA2402 YOUNG FACULTY AWARD PROPOSAL — PRECISION IN MINIATURE: REVOLUTIONIZING MPS WITH DIGITAL ACOUSTOFLUIDICS AND NANOSCALE 3D PRINTING." Underrated use: these are named early-career PIs one or two years ahead of you who went through this exact process. Email them. They will tell you what the executive summary that worked looked like.

3. DARPACONNECT HAS A YFA-SPECIFIC MODULE. The RA names it: DARPAConnect "offers free resources to potential performers to help them navigate DARPA, including 'Fueling Innovation: Applying for the DARPA Young Faculty Award,' 'Understanding DARPA Award Vehicles and Solicitations,' 'Making the Most of Proposers Days,' and 'Tips for DARPA Proposal Success.' Join DARPAConnect at www.DARPAConnect.us." This is the closest thing to an annotated walkthrough that exists for this mechanism. CAVEAT (tooling fact, verified 18 Sept 2026): the deep link www.darpaconnect.us/learning-resources/... 302-redirects to pathfinder.theari.us and returns "Page Not Found", so the module could not be opened this pass. Reach it by registering free at the DARPAConnect root instead.

4. THE HEILMEIER CATECHISM is the frame the whole thing is scored in, and the RA points at it directly: "Proposers should also familiarize themselves with the 'Heilmeier Catechism.' Details… can be found at https://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/heilmeier-catechism." Attachment C's Executive Summary prompts are the Catechism in different words. Answer all eight questions on one page before writing anything.

5. CURRENT DARPA PROGRAMME PAGES, https://www.darpa.mil/research/programs — the RA instructs proposers to read these to calibrate ambition and to avoid duplicating funded work.

6. THE PUBLIC FAQ. The RA promises "DARPA will post an FAQ list on the DARPA webpage," and the FY2026 FAQ ran to at least 82 numbered items covering the executive summary page limit, the Grants.gov routing of full proposals, and the no-telecons rule. I could not locate its live URL this pass (flagged unresolved) — request it from the YFA mailbox, or look for it alongside the RA on sam.gov.
unresolved: YFA 2027 RA number and exact dates — not posted as of 18 Sept 2026. Verified absent from grants.gov (no DARPARA2602/2603/2701/2702/2703 record; no 2027 YFA listing under any DARPA office code) and absent from the DARPA opportunities RSS feed. DARPA's own page says early fall 2026, and the last cycle posted 30 Sept 2025, so re-check grants.gov and sam.gov from late September 2026. This is a 'not yet published' finding, not a discontinuation.

Live URL of the DARPARA2502 public FAQ list. The RA promises 'DARPA will post an FAQ list on the DARPA webpage' but gives no address, and no FAQ document was attached to the grants.gov record. The FAQ item numbers cited in the funder-wide notes (60, 81, 82) came from an earlier pass, not this one.

DARPAConnect module 'Fueling Innovation: Applying for the DARPA Young Faculty Award' — confirmed to exist by name in the RA text, but the content could not be opened: www.darpaconnect.us/learning-resources/... 302-redirects to pathfinder.theari.us, which returns 'Page Not Found'. Tooling/availability fact; the module presumably sits behind the free DARPAConnect registration.

Class size and success rate. DARPA publishes no YFA selection rate. USAspending surfaced at least 14 FY2025-class cooperative agreements all starting 30 Sept 2025, but that is a floor from one paginated query, not a class total. DARPA's anniversary page gives only a 20-year aggregate, 'over 500 rising research stars from more than 60 universities' (≈25/year if evenly spread — an inference, not a published figure).

Attachment B (Proposal Summary Slide Template) and Attachment D (Volume II, Administrative and National Policy Requirements) were identified as required but not opened this pass, so any page or content limits inside them are unverified.

sam.gov's own DARPARA2502 listing was not fetched (no API key); all solicitation content here comes from the grants.gov copy of the RA and its attachments. The two are required to match, but the sam.gov posting was not independently checked.

WebSearch was unavailable for this pass (session budget exhausted at 200/200), and DuckDuckGo's HTML endpoint returned a CAPTCHA, which I did not attempt. All findings therefore come from the funder's own documents, the grants.gov and USAspending APIs, and direct fetches — no search index was used. Nothing here rests on a search snippet.

METHOD WARNING WORTH RECORDING: a WebFetch summary of the RA PDF returned entirely fabricated content — an executive summary due 3 March 2026, full proposal 7 April 2026, 5-page executive summary, 15-page technical volume and a $3,000,000 prior-funding cap. Every one of those is false. It was caught because the invented deadlines fell after the opportunity's own archive date. The real values were obtained by extracting the PDF text locally with pdftotext and the .docx templates with zipfile. Do not let a summarizer read a binary attachment for drift-sensitive fields.

result.deadline_pattern:
Annual, single-stage. Observed FY2027 cycle: NOFO posted 17 Aug 2026 → proposals due 30 Oct 2026 → selection notice 16 Feb 2027 → grant start 1 Apr 2027. Working pattern: announcement posts mid-to-late August, proposals due late October, selection mid-February, awards start 1 April.

CAUTION ON THE PATTERN: this shape is drawn from ONE observed cycle (FY27) plus the posted date. I could not confirm it across two cycles because the search budget was spent. Treat the pattern as provisional; treat the 30 Oct 2026 date as solid.

CORPUS-RULE CONFLICT — this is the answer to "why did I or did you forbid the dated deadline". Neither of us forbade it ad hoc. It is written into the project's own brief, in four places:
- docs/BRIEF.md line 12: live solicitations with a single expiring deadline are "Out of scope (by default)".
- docs/BRIEF.md line 92, the schema: `application_cadence` takes rolling/annual/biennial/irregular "(do NOT store specific dated deadlines here)".
- docs/BRIEF.md §8: dated calls belong in a separate, disposable `live_opportunities_<country>.csv`, joined back by an FK `linked_mechanism`.
- docs/BRIEF.md line 166, acceptance criteria: "No row stores a dated deadline in `application_cadence`; standing programs only in the main file."
CLAUDE.md invariant 3 restates it: "One row = one standing programme. Dated solicitations belong to the live layer... never merged in." The rationale is staleness — dates rot, standing programmes do not (reinforced by D-009: a closed cycle "is not evidence of anything").

The rule was never a decision that applicants shouldn't see dates. It was a decision about WHICH FILE holds them. The live layer designed to carry exactly this is ROADMAP P5, which is marked "superseded by P9" and never built. Your utility test ("when to apply") is unmet not because the rule is wrong but because half the design was never implemented. Building the live layer satisfies both: durable row stays clean, viz shows "next deadline: 30 Oct 2026" via the FK. That is a P-card, not a schema change, and it needs your go.
result.loi_deadline:
No LOI, pre-proposal or white paper stage exists. The NOFO is emphatic, in bold on its own line: "IMPORTANT NOTE: White Papers are NOT being solicited and will NOT be accepted. This NOFO is for proposal submissions only."

This is a genuine deviation from ONR's house norm and worth flagging to applicants: most other current ONR announcements DO have a white-paper gate (e.g. the FY27 Communications and Networking announcement had white papers due 31 Jul 2026 before full proposals on 16 Nov 2026; the FY27 DoN HBCU/MI programme had white papers 18 Sep 2026). Someone who has applied to ONR before will expect a white-paper step here and there isn't one — it is one shot, full proposal.

There IS an optional informal route, which is NOT an LOI and has no deadline: "A brief topic description may be submitted to facilitate these discussions but are not required." It is emailed directly to the technical Program Officer with ONRYIP@navy.mil cc'd ("The ONRYIP@navy.mil need only be cc'd on the first email correspondence"). Practically it should happen well before the 16 Oct 2026 eligibility-questions cutoff.
result.review_to_award:
From the NOFO's "Anticipated Schedule of Events" table, verbatim dates:
- Proposals Due Date — 10/30/2026, 5:00 pm
- Notification of Selection for Award — 02/16/2027
- Start Date of Grant — 04/01/2027
Footnoted: "*These dates are estimates as of the date of this announcement."

So roughly **3.5 months submission → notification, 5 months submission → earliest start**. That is materially faster than NIH (which runs ~9-10 months) and should be planned for: money can land on 1 April.

Two structural cautions:
1. Everyone hears back either way — "All applicants will receive a notification email advising if their proposal has been selected or not selected for recommendation for award."
2. Selection is NOT award. A recommendation "does not ultimately guarantee an award will be made"; it then goes to ONR Contracts and Grant Awards Management for cost analysis, responsibility determination and funds availability. Budget a gap between the February notice and the April start.

Reviewing is done by "The cognizant Program Officer and other Government scientific experts" — not a standing study section. And proposals "will not be evaluated against each other since they are not submitted in accordance with a common work statement," which makes the Program Officer relationship disproportionately important compared with a panel-scored mechanism.
result.submission_requirements:
Submitted through Grants.gov Workspace by the institution's AOR (not by the PI directly), using the SF-424 (R&R) family forms.

FORMAT: 8.5x11, 1-inch margins, single-spaced, Times New Roman 12-point. **Technical Proposal page limit: 20 pages.**

EXCLUDED from the 20 pages (quoted list): Cover page; Table of contents; Full Curriculum Vitae; Data Management Plan; Letters of Support; Cited References; Current and Pending Support. "There are no page limitations for the budget."

INSIDE the 20 pages: Technical Approach (which must itself contain Future Naval Relevance naming the ONR S&T Focus Area addressed; Project Schedule and Milestones; Goals and Benchmarks; and a "Gold Standard Science" subsection — "Describe your success in implementing Gold Standard Science in accordance with Executive Order 14303"); Management Approach; Principal Investigator Qualifications; and a "Responsibility" section (six enumerated points on resources, ability to comply, record managing federal awards, integrity, eligibility, and operational controls).

WHERE IT DEVIATES FROM NORM — three traps:
1. **The letter is institutional, not academic.** At least one Letter of Support is mandatory and is a scored criterion in its own right. It is not a reference letter from a senior scientist and not an NIH-style sponsor/mentor statement. It must be "authored by the appropriate University (or Nonprofit) Official(s)" and must articulate "long-term commitment by the University... release time from teaching and/or administrative responsibilities, paid nine-month salary, other related research funding, related laboratory and/or computer investments, new faculty start-up package, support for applicant's graduate students/postdocs, and mentoring." Hard gate: "Applications received without at least one letter of support will be considered incomplete and will not be considered for award."
2. **Hidden eligibility verification inside that letter.** For anyone claiming a tenure-track-EQUIVALENT position, ONR's tenure-track-equivalent page states: "Your Department Chair (or equivalent) will verify that your position is YIP-eligible in the University Letter (letter of support)." That sentence appears on the tenure-track-equivalent page only — it is NOT repeated on the dedicated Letter of Support guidance page or in the NOFO's letter section, so it is easy to miss and it changes who must sign.
3. **Single PI, hard.** "This is a single PI award. Co-PIs are not allowed," and "A PI may submit only one application under this solicitation." The Management Approach must explicitly "explain how the proposed team fits the single PI structure" if subawardees or collaborators exist.

OTHER MECHANICS: full CV required, comprehensive, all publications/patents/chapters (SciENcv format may be used). Data Management Plan "In no more than 2 pages". Attachments must be PDF, cannot contain macros, cannot be password protected — otherwise "they will not pass ONR's automated acceptance check and will need to be resubmitted." Filenames must not exceed 68 characters including extension. Cost sharing "is not expected and will not be used as a factor during the merit review."

DOCUMENT DEFECT WORTH WARNING APPLICANTS ABOUT: the NOFO's cover-page instructions tell applicants to put "NOFO Number: N0001426SF0004" — an extra zero. The actual opportunity number everywhere else (title page, footers, grants portal) is **N0001426SF004**. Use the latter.

REVIEW CRITERIA, all equally weighted ("Criteria 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are equally important"): (1) Technical Merit; (2) Naval Science and Technology Priorities; (3) Curriculum Vitae / past performance; (4) Letter of Support; (5) Budget. Criterion 2 includes an explicit research-security risk assessment covering "Foreign Talent Recruitment Programs, Funding Sources, Patent Filings, and Associations/Affiliations" per NDAA FY2019 §1286 as amended.

SELECTIVITY (quoted, unusually specific for a funder): "The ONR YIP is highly competitive with typically 10 percent or less of applicants receiving awards. For FY2026 more than 330 proposals were received, resulting in 23 awards (7%) with a total award value of $17M." FY27 intent: "Total Amount of Funding Available: $18.75M; Anticipated Number of Awards: up to 25." Critical strategic detail: "There will be no more than five (5) awards made per S&T Department," across the five departments (31 C5ISRT; 32 Ocean Battlespace Sensing; 33 Sea Warfare and Weapons; 34 Warfighter Performance; 35 Air Warfare and Weapons). Which department you pitch into changes your odds — you compete against a 5-award cap, not the 25.
result.prior_funding_conflicts:
BOTH HALVES, as required.

WHAT DISQUALIFIES (the exclusion list is short and closed — quoted in full from Section B.1):
- "Prior ONR YIP Award recipients are ineligible to apply." One YIP per career; winning it retires you from the competition.
- "Tenured faculty are ineligible to apply." Note this is separate from the appointment test — being tenured disqualifies you even if you are still inside the PhD window.
- "A PI may submit only one application under this solicitation."
- A discretionary clause with no published threshold: "Disclosures of current and pending support made in this application may render an applicant ineligible for funding. Prior to award and throughout the period of performance, DoW may continue to request updated continuing and pending support information, which will be reviewed and may result in discontinuation of funding." So heavy existing support is a live risk, but ONR publishes no dollar line.

WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the half that is usually missing, and the useful half here):
- **No dollar cap on existing funding.** Unlike e.g. the Beckman Young Investigator ($225k direct annualized cap), ONR YIP sets no ceiling on what you already hold.
- **No other agency's early-career award disqualifies you.** I full-text searched the 41-page NOFO for CAREER, PECASE, DARPA, AFOSR, Army Research, duplicate, concurrent, simultaneous and "other agenc" — there is no exclusion for holding an NSF CAREER, AFOSR YIP, ARO ECP, DARPA YFA or PECASE. Eligibility is gated by career stage and citizenship, not award history: PI must be a US citizen, national or permanent resident on the due date, hold "a first or second full-time tenure-track or tenure-track-equivalent faculty position," and have "received his/her PhD or equivalent degree on or after 01/01/2019" (the FY27 anchoring of the 7-year window; it moves every cycle).
- **Losing does not burn the proposal.** "A proposal not selected for the YIP may still be considered for an ONR grant award," in competition with all other ONR submissions — but honestly caveated by ONR itself: "Historically, only a limited number of proposals initially submitted to the YIP NOFO, but not selected under that NOFO, have been awarded other funds." And "Consideration of any YIP proposal to another ONR research grant program is at the discretion of the Program Officer."
- **Winning does not close the door afterwards.** "Upon completion of the award, individuals may apply for continued support under ONR's Long Range BAA (or other research grant opportunities)," though "Continued support is not guaranteed."

HONESTY QUALIFIER, per house rules: the second bullet rests on verified ABSENCE across the full NOFO text, not on an affirmative carve-out sentence. ONR nowhere writes "holding an NSF CAREER preserves eligibility." The exclusion list reads as closed and enumerated, so the inference is strong, but it is an inference from absence and should be recorded as such rather than quoted as policy. An applicant in doubt has a named route to a binding answer: eligibility questions go to ONRYIP@navy.mil before 16 Oct 2026.
result.resubmission_note:
No NIH-style A0/A1 regime, and no stated bar on reapplying after a decline. The NOFO is silent on resubmitting a previously declined YIP proposal in a later cycle; eligibility is simply re-tested each year against the PhD-date window and the first-or-second-appointment test, both of which tighten annually — so the binding constraint on a second attempt is the clock, not a resubmission rule. In practice an unsuccessful applicant should check whether their PhD date still clears the next cycle's anchor (01/01/2019 for FY27, which will move forward for FY28) and whether they are still in a first or second appointment and untenured.

The only "resubmission" language in the NOFO is a mechanical one about failed format checks, not about merit: a non-PDF, macro-containing or password-protected attachment "will not pass ONR's automated acceptance check and will need to be resubmitted. Block 2, 'Type of Application' on the SF 424 should be marked 'New' on the resubmission."

Separately, and more useful than a resubmission right: a declined YIP proposal can be picked up against the ONR Long Range BAA at the Program Officer's discretion (see prior_funding_conflicts).
result.program_officer_contact:
Pre-submission contact is EXPECTED, not merely tolerated — the NOFO puts it in capitals: "Applicants are STRONGLY ENCOURAGED to contact the appropriate Program Officer who is the point of contact for a specific technical area to discuss their research ideas before submitting a proposal... Please allow adequate time for such discussions with the ONR Program Officer." Given that proposals "will not be evaluated against each other" and the cognizant Program Officer runs the evaluation, this conversation is the single highest-leverage pre-submission act for this mechanism.

Three distinct routes, deliberately separated by ONR:
1. TECHNICAL / topic fit — the Program Officer for your technical area. Directories: https://www.onr.navy.mil/our-research/our-program-officers and https://www.onr.navy.mil/our-research/onr-technology-and-research. Optional brief topic description emailed to that PO with ONRYIP@navy.mil cc'd on first contact.
2. PROGRAMMATIC / ELIGIBILITY — Reginald G. Williams, PhD, YIP Program Manager, ONR Code 34, 875 North Randolph Street, Arlington VA 22203-1995. Email: ONRYIP@navy.mil. (Program support: Ms. Paula Barden, per the ONR YIP landing page.) Cutoff for eligibility/technical questions: 16 Oct 2026, 5:00 pm ET.
3. GRANTS / SUBMISSION MECHANICS — Veronica Lacey, Grants Officer, ONR Code 253. Email: veronica.y.lacey.civ@us.navy.mil. Cutoff: 29 Oct 2026, 5:00 pm ET.

ONR asks that questions "be concise and to the point" and cite "the relevant part and paragraph" of the NOFO, and warns that "Questions submitted within 2 weeks prior to a deadline may not be answered, and the due date for submission of the full proposal will not be extended."

TARGETING TIP for the "who to talk to" question: ONR's published awardee lists name the funding Program Officer and division alongside each awardee. Find a past awardee whose topic sits near yours, and the list tells you which PO to approach — a direct, verifiable name-to-name route rather than guesswork.

result.program_name: Young Investigator Research Program (YIP)
result.funder: Air Force Office of Scientific Research (AFOSR), Air Force Research Laboratory
result.next_deadline: DATED AND LIVE as of 2026-09-18. The FY2027 competition is open under NOFO FA955026S0003 (posted 8 Sep 2026). The chain, quoted from the announcement's KEY DATES section: pre-proposal inquiries "not later than 17 September 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time" (THIS HAS JUST PASSED — one day before the check date); government answers "no later than COB on 24 September 2026"; "Whitepapers must be received by 09 October 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time" (the live, actionable deadline — 21 days out); white-paper determination returned "before COB on 06 November 2026"; "Proposals must be received electronically through Grants.gov by 04 December 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time to be considered." NOTE FOR THE ROW: the recorded source (the Oct-2023 afresearchlab.com flyer) states the OLD cadence — "Proposals Due: June/July" and "FOA posts: March/April on Grants.gov" — which is now wrong by roughly six months and omits the white-paper stage entirely. The cycle has moved; anyone working from the recorded source would miss FY2027 completely.
result.deadline_pattern: Annual, one competition per federal fiscal year. Current (FY2027) pattern: NOFO posts early September, white paper early October, invited full proposal early December, awards by 1 May. Prior (FY2024-era, per the 2023 AFOSR flyer) pattern was announcement March/April with proposals June/July — so the pattern itself is NOT stable across cycles and must be re-checked each year on Grants.gov rather than assumed. The eligibility window slides one year per cycle in step with the award start date: FY2024 required a doctorate "no earlier than 01 April 2017"; FY2027 requires "Doctorate no earlier than 01 April 2019" — i.e. roughly 7.5 years before the anticipated 1 May start. Separately, the open BAA that defines the research topics "updates annually in the March/April time frame."
result.loi_deadline: White paper (AFOSR's term; functions as a mandatory, gating pre-proposal) due 9 October 2026, 11:59 PM ET — roughly 8 weeks before the 4 December 2026 full proposal. Submitted NOT through Grants.gov but through a Qualtrics portal: https://afosr.gov1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eKuTqm9qezoDYep. It is gating in both directions, and the announcement is unusually blunt about it: "If you do not submit a white paper under this NOFO, you will be ineligible to submit a YIP proposal." Access to the full proposal is by invitation only — "Upon the PO white paper review and feedback, an invitation to submit a YIP proposal may be extended." TRAP: a white paper sent to the Program Officer in an earlier cycle does NOT carry over — "If you have previously submitted a white paper to the PO and feedback was provided you are still REQUIRED to submit under this NOFO to potentially be considered eligible for this competition. No exceptions will be granted." White paper: 5 pages max, 1-inch margins, 1.5 spacing, Times New Roman or Garamond 12pt; cover page, CV and references excluded from the count. Content must cover identification of the research and issues, potential impact on DAF/DoW capabilities, potential team members and development plans, proposed technical approaches, and all publications and presentations. You may submit more than one white paper across research disciplines but must disclose that on each submission.
result.review_to_award: Roughly 5 months from full proposal to award, and about 8 months end-to-end from the white paper. Quoted: "We anticipate that we will notify proposers of selection or non-selection for award no later than 26 April 2027. We anticipate awards to be made by 01 May 2027, barring delays." The applicant must align their own paperwork to this: "You must identify a date no later than 01 May 2027 as the anticipated start date in your" proposal. Two-stage review: programmatic review by AFOSR Program Officers and subject matter experts, plus peer review by external subject-matter experts. An interim gate exists at 6 November 2026 (white-paper determination). Note an added FY2027 screening layer: a go/no-go "Programmatic Requirements Review" applying Executive Orders 14303 ("Gold Standard Science"), 14332 and 14030 before any technical evaluation — a proposal failing it "will be removed from consideration" without full review.
result.submission_requirements: Full proposal via Grants.gov only ("We will not accept or evaluate any proposal submitted by any means other than through Grants.gov"), using the SF-424 (R&R) form family as the cover page, marked with the announcement number. Deviations worth knowing: (1) Page limit "No more than twenty (20) single-sided pages", 1-inch margins, 1.5-line spacing, Times New Roman or Garamond 12pt, PDF attachments; cover page, table of contents, references, LETTERS OF SUPPORT, CV and current/pending support are all excluded from the count. "The pages of proposals exceeding the page limit may not be included in the evaluation." (2) A separate "AFOSR Abstract" form from the Grants.gov "Related Documents" tab — 300 words / 2,000 characters max, plain text as a single block, no line breaks, tables, superscripts or special characters (& : / \ " ? are explicitly barred), marked publicly releasable, and "Your abstract header should include the Program Officer's name and office symbol" — which presupposes you have already identified your PO. (3) A Data Management Plan is required, "modeled on the National Science Foundation Data Management Plan requirement." (4) Project Narrative must open with a single-page "Statement of Objectives" written in active verbs, which AFOSR may lift verbatim into the award as the description of work. (5) Current and Pending (Other) Support (NSF common form accepted), Collaborators and Other Affiliations, Biosketch, training certifications and compliance attestation for each covered individual, plus an explicit "Statement of potential overlap." (6) Institutional sign-off is electronic — the SF-424 (R&R) "must include the signature of an authorized representative from your organization," affixed by Grants.gov at submission. (7) STRUCTURAL CONSTRAINT that catches people: "There may not be co-PIs" (sole exception: a PI moving institutions after the close date, handled as a sub-award) and "No domestic or foreign collaborators, funded or non-funded, are allowed for this single investigator award." (8) One portfolio only: "YIP proposals may be submitted for only one research portfolio area." LPS/quantum applicants must title the submission "Quantum Computing - Title of Project". (9) GenAI use is not prohibited but disclosure is "strongly encourage[d]". (10) Budget must not exceed $150,000 in any single year; proposals over the annual cap, the $450,000 total or three years "may be rejected without review." Note also an AFOSR-specific Fundamental Research Security Review (FRSR) and Section 223 NDAA disclosure regime applied before award.
result.prior_funding_conflicts: BOTH HALVES, from the FY2027 NOFO. WHAT PRESERVES ELIGIBILITY (the important half, and the reassuring one): there is NO prior-funding exclusion and NO dollar cap on existing support. Holding other federal grants — NSF CAREER, an NIH award, another DoD award — does not disqualify you. Existing awards are handled purely as a disclosure-and-overlap matter, not an eligibility gate: Current and Pending (Other) Support is used "to assess: The capacity of the individual to carry out the proposed research. Any potential scientific and budgetary overlap or duplication across projects. The potential the individual is overcommitting themselves with the proposed project." So the risk from prior funding is a scored judgement about overcommitment and duplication, manageable by writing the overlap statement well — not a bright-line bar. I found no clause barring a previous YIP winner from applying again, and no clause excluding prior or current AFOSR grantees. WHAT DOES MAKE YOU INELIGIBLE (none of it about prior awards): (a) doctorate earlier than 01 April 2019; (b) not being a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident "at time of proposal submission"; (c) employment at an FFRDC or a Department of War (DoW) Laboratory — these are named as ineligible entities, as are "Individual persons or people" applying outside an institution; (d) not holding "a full-time, non-contractor permanent, career-competitive, or tenure-track position (based on your institution's definition)" — BUT there is an explicit carve-out that rescues people on short-term appointments: "your proposal must include a letter from your organization stating that you will be considered for a permanent, career-competitive, or tenure-track non-contractor position if you currently hold a short-term appointment"; (e) inability to accept the public-release/fundamental-research publication terms; (f) PROCEDURAL, and the one that actually disqualifies most people: failing to file a white paper under this specific NOFO. PRESERVES-ELIGIBILITY BONUS ON THE BACK END: a YIP award does not foreclose follow-on money — "At the discretion of the Program Officer, and subject to the availability of fund and satisfactory progress, further effort may be identified at a later time and funded up to an additional $300,000 over a period of up to two (2) years without further competition." I searched specifically for a career-interruption waiver or extension of the degree-date window (medical/family leave) and found none: the 01 April 2019 date reads as a hard bright line.
result.program_officer_contact: Two-tier, and pre-submission contact is expected, not merely tolerated. TIER 1, administrative — YIP Program Manager, afosryip@us.af.mil, phone 703-696-9517 (per the FY2027 NOFO). The AFOSR fact sheet (rendered in a browser; it 403s a plain fetch) names the manager as Ellen M. Robinson, (703) 588-8527, DSN 425-8527, same afosryip@us.af.mil mailbox — note that fact sheet is stale on other details (it still cites the FY2025 BAA number and says "DoD Laboratory"), so treat the name as probable-current and the mailbox as authoritative. TIER 2, scientific, and this is the one that matters — the NOFO does NOT name the technical POs: "Research specific technical questions must be submitted electronically via email to the AFOSR Program Officer. Email addresses are listed in the general BAA." That general BAA is FA955026S0001, "Research Interests of the Air Force Office of Scientific Research" (status: open until superseded). Its PDF carries a named Program Officer with a direct portfolio mailbox and phone at the end of each of ~35 portfolio sections across four branches (RESA Engineering & Complex Systems, RESA Information & Networks, RESB Physical Sciences, RESC Bio-Cognitive), plus international offices. Verified examples: Dr. Amanda Chou, AFOSR/RESA, aerodynamics@us.af.mil, (703) 696-9735; Dr. Grace D. Metcalfe, AFOSR/RESB, QIS@us.af.mil, (703) 696-6204 (Quantum Information Sciences); portfolio mailboxes are topical rather than personal (comp.math@, neuroscience@, plasma@, biophysics@, networks@ ... all @us.af.mil). The expectation is explicit in both documents — NOFO: "Proposers are encouraged to confer with the designated AFOSR Program Officer(s) prior to submitting a full proposal"; BAA: "Proposers are highly encouraged to contact the Program Officer via email prior to developing a full proposal to discuss the current state of the art in their area of interest, how the proposed research would advance it, the approximate cost for a three (3) year effort, and if there are any specific submission target dates." The NOFO also warns the PO cannot bind the government: "Grants and Contracting Officers acting within their warranted capacity are the only people authorized to make commitments." PRACTICAL WARNING: match your portfolio by NAME, not by section letter. The NOFO cites Quantum Information Sciences as BAA "Section A.3.f" in one paragraph and "Section A.3.g" in another; the BAA body shows A.3.f = Quantum Information Sciences and A.3.g = Physics of Sensing, and the BAA's own index tables disagree with its body lettering in places.
result.examples_or_samples: Weak — this is the thinnest field for this mechanism, and I want to be straight about it. AFOSR publishes no sample application, no annotated example and no successful-white-paper library that I could find. What does exist: (1) FUNDED ABSTRACTS ARE PUBLIC BY MANDATE. The NOFO commits AFOSR to publishing every awardee's abstract: "If you receive an award, we must publish your abstract to a searchable website available to the general public in accordance with Public Law 113-235", pointing to DTIC (https://discover.dtic.mil/). TOOLING FACT, not a finding: DTIC Public Search was offline when checked on 2026-09-18 — the site states "DTIC Public Search is offline while we enhance the capability. It will be back online soon." So the route is real and mandated but temporarily unusable; retry later. Since abstracts are capped at 300 words and written for a public audience, they show framing and topic fit rather than proposal craft. (2) AFOSR's own YIP flyers spotlight individual winners with project titles — the Oct-2023 flyer, for instance, congratulates Professor Cheng Huang (University of Kansas) for "Generalizable Data-Driven Modeling Framework for Understanding and Modeling Turbulent Combustion", which is a usable specimen of the title-and-topic register AFOSR rewards. (3) THE FUNDER'S OWN DESIGNED SUBSTITUTE, and the one to actually use: the mandatory white paper is itself a low-cost, structured feedback round. AFOSR commits to responding — "The topic points of contact (POCs) will coordinate to provide feedback on the white papers", with determinations by 6 November 2026. Five pages buys you a Program Officer's read before you invest in a 20-page proposal. Combined with the encouraged pre-submission email to the portfolio PO, that is the intended calibration path in place of published samples. (4) The BAA's per-portfolio program descriptions are the closest thing to a statement of what a winning topic looks like, portfolio by portfolio.
result.resubmission_note: No same-cycle resubmission or revise-and-resubmit; there is no formal reconsideration or appeal route described. The NOFO instead redirects unsuccessful proposals to the open BAA: "Funding is limited under the YIP competition. As a result, otherwise meritorious proposals may not be selected. If your proposal is not selected under the YIP competition, you may resubmit your proposal under our most recent general broad agency announcement titled, 'Research Interests of the Air Force Office of Scientific Research' as published on Grants.gov." That open BAA (FA955026S0001) is open until superseded and accepts proposals throughout the year, so a declined YIP is a redirect rather than a dead end — though the BAA is not early-career-restricted and so is a different, broader competition. Re-applying to YIP in a later cycle is not barred, but the sliding degree-date window will exclude applicants as they age out (FY2027 cuts at 01 April 2019). Non-selection is not the only exit: the NOFO also warns that failing to meet reporting and due-date obligations on an existing award "could lead to being considered ineligible for future awards." An ombudsman route exists (afrl.pk.workflow@us.af.mil, subject "Ombudsman") but is explicitly not for questioning due dates or requesting solicitation copies.
unresolved: Named Program Officer per portfolio is established from the open BAA PDF (FA955026S0001), but AFOSR does not publish a consolidated web directory of POs; the BAA's own section lettering is internally inconsistent between its index tables and its body, so portfolio identification must be done by name, not section number. Whether Ellen M. Robinson is still the YIP Program Manager is not confirmed against a 2026-dated source — the fact sheet naming her is stale on other details; the afosryip@us.af.mil mailbox and the 703-696-9517 number from the FY2027 NOFO are the current-verified route.

No funded sample application, annotated example, or successful white paper is published by AFOSR for this mechanism. The mandated public-abstract repository (DTIC) exists but its public search was OFFLINE when checked on 2026-09-18 — a tooling fact, not evidence that the abstracts are unavailable. Re-check DTIC later to harvest funded YIP abstracts.

Selectivity is not stated as a rate. FY2027 volume is quantifiable but ambiguous: the NOFO anticipates 37 traditionally funded YIPs plus 3 LPS/quantum awards, with 'potential for an additional 37' core-funded; the portal summarises this as 50 expected awards. Number of applicants is not published, so an acceptance rate cannot be computed.

The grants portal lists an award range of $150,000-$650,000, which exceeds the NOFO's stated $450,000 three-year total. This is most likely the portal accommodating the discretionary follow-on (up to an additional $300,000 over two years) or the historical 'exceptional proposals' clause, but the reconciliation is not stated anywhere I could verify. The NOFO's $150,000/yr cap and $450,000 total are the figures to rely on for budgeting.

Prior AFOSR YIP receipt: no clause found either permitting or barring a second YIP award to the same PI. Absence of a bar is not the same as an explicit permission, though the sliding degree-date window makes a repeat win unlikely in practice.

No career-interruption waiver or extension of the 01 April 2019 degree-date window was found. Searched for medical/family leave and extenuating-circumstances provisions; none present in the NOFO text. Applicants near the boundary should ask the Program Manager directly rather than assume flexibility.

Prior-cycle deadline history (FY2025, FY2026) could not be reconstructed: the grants portal search surfaced only the open FY2027 opportunity, and this session's web-search budget was exhausted before alternative routes could be tried. The pattern statement therefore rests on two anchor points (FY2024 flyer, FY2027 NOFO), which is enough to show the cadence moved but not enough to date the move.
